surprises.description: Inspire’s Q2 revenue declined 7.6% year over year, a smaller drop than the preview’s expected 9%–11% decline and above its $194.72 million consensus estimate. Revenue was $200.6 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 7.6% year-over-year to $200.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 revenue was guided to a “9%–11% year-over-year decline” and cited consensus revenue of “$194.72 million.”

surprises.description: The company raised the lower end of its 2026 revenue outlook by $10 million while keeping the upper end unchanged, to $835 million–$875 million from $825 million–$875 million. The preview had flagged the existing range as the full-year outlook to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was revised to $835 million-$875 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed full-year revenue guidance of “$825M–$875M.”

surprises.description: Inspire raised its adjusted profitability outlook: adjusted operating margin is now 4%–6% rather than 2%–4%, and adjusted diluted EPS is $1.05–$1.45 rather than $0.75–$1.25.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “narrowed profitability guidance to adjusted operating margin of 4-6%” and “adjusted diluted EPS of $1.05-$1.45.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave full-year adjusted operating margin guidance of “2%–4%” and adjusted diluted EPS guidance of “$0.75–$1.25.”

surprises.description: At the same time, the GAAP diluted EPS outlook was cut below the preview’s expected range and now includes a loss: the range moved from $0.07–$0.62 to -$0.42–$0.17.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company guided diluted EPS to “-$0.42 to $0.17.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed GAAP diluted EPS guidance of “$0.07–$0.62.”

surprises.description: New Q3 guidance points to an 8%–10% year-over-year revenue decline and approximately break-even adjusted operating income. The quarter is expected to improve sequentially from Q2, but the preview had specifically raised the question of whether the reimbursement headwind would stabilize or continue into the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for an 8-10% year-over-year revenue decline (though sequentially higher than Q2) and approximately break-even adjusted operating income as marketing spend steps up.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the headwind was “stabilizing or still growing into H2 2026” and noted the company’s prior “2027 ‘return to growth’ framing”; it gave no Q3 forecast.

surprises.description: Inspire announced Project Horizon, pairing $30 million of annualized growth-investment capacity with $20 million–$25 million of pre-tax restructuring charges, most of them expected in Q3. The preview did not anticipate this restructuring program or its near-term charges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Project Horizon” is “expected to create $30 million of annualized growth investment capacity” while incurring “$20 million-$25 million of pre-tax restructuring charges (90% in Q3), including $16 million-$20 million of non-cash impairments.”

surprises.description: CMS’s proposed 2027 rates are favorable for hospital outpatient and ASC reimbursement, but would reduce physician reimbursement for CPT 64582. The preview discussed coding uncertainty and potential interim relief but did not anticipate these specific proposed rate changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: Proposed rates would “increase hospital outpatient reimbursement 12% to $35,414 and ASC reimbursement 15% to $31,722,” while “cut physician reimbursement for CPT 64582 by about 4% to roughly $699”; final rates are due in November.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “commentary on the CPT coding resolution timeline” and said “any interim relief” would be notable; it did not state an expectation for the 2027 rates.

surprises.description: Two Medicare Administrative Contractors currently require a -52 modifier for CPT 64582, leading to payment reductions of as much as 30%. This adds a specific reimbursement constraint beyond the general coding and WISeR disruption described in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two Medicare Administrative Contractors currently require the -52 modifier when billing CPT 64582, applying payment reductions ranging from 0% to 30% of the $723 national average Medicare payment.”

in_line: The estimated Q2 coding, reimbursement, and WISER impact was approximately $40 million, at the lower end of the preview’s expected $40 million–$50 million Q2 headwind.

The revised Category 1 CPT code application is scheduled for September AMA editorial-panel review, and the potential single-lead code remains on track for January 1, 2028 implementation, consistent with the preview’s stated timeline.

surprises.description: Q2 net income of $174 million and adjusted EBITDA of $314 million both exceeded the Q2 guidance ranges of $150–160 million and $295–305 million, respectively. The EBITDA result also cleared the preview’s bullish scenario threshold of $305 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $174 million” and “adjusted EBITDA rose to $314 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 company guidance was “net income $150–160M, Adjusted EBITDA $295–305M”; the preview’s bull scenario was “Adj. EBITDA ≥$305M.”

surprises.description: Gross adjusted EBITDA margin reached approximately 85%, about 10 percentage points above the company’s 75% target—an upside the preview did not flag. Management attributed some of the margin strength to OpEx shifting into the second half and minor one-time credits, so the full gap may not be recurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's gross adjusted EBITDA margin reached approximately 85% in Q2 2026, well above its 75% target, aided partly by OpEx phasing shifts into the second half and minor one-time credits.”

surprises.description: Management expects Q3 EBITDA to be roughly flat with Q2 even as revenues and volumes rise, because higher OpEx from deferred maintenance will offset that growth. The preview anticipated a second-half volume catch-up but did not flag this deferred-maintenance cost offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 net income of $165-175 million and adjusted EBITDA of $310-320 million, roughly flat with Q2 as higher revenues and volumes are offset by higher OpEx from deferred maintenance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had framed “2H 2026 as the catch-up quarter (weather normalization plus later-2026 completions).”

surprises.description: The company made no Q2 buyback and instead paid down $87 million on its revolver. That differs from the preview’s focus on buyback pace and possible sponsor repurchases, although the debt reduction also advances the deleveraging plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company did not execute a share buyback in Q2 2026, instead paying down $87 million on its revolving credit facility, reducing the drawn balance to $256 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The incremental news is buyback pace and whether another sponsor (Chevron) unit repurchase is executed”; the preview also said to “watch the actual leverage print and the split between repurchases and debt.”

surprises.description: Although the preview expected Q2 free cash flow to decline sequentially, management also said Q3 free cash flow would decline further as capital spending rises. The preview did not specify a further Q3 decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow was approximately $232 million in Q2 2026, a roughly 2% decrease from Q1, with Q3 free cash flow expected to decline further due to higher capital spending.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 free cash flow was expected to be “down sequentially on higher capex.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted free cash flow declined about 2% from Q1, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a sequential Q2 decline.
Full-year 2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance of $910–960 million was reiterated, as was the net income and EBITDA guidance that the preview expected to be reaffirmed.
Management maintained the expected second-half volume recovery, guiding to at least 5% volume growth in the second half; this matches the preview’s catch-up-quarter framing.
The expected leverage path toward approximately 2.5x by 2028 and the roughly $280 million of excess adjusted free cash flow after distribution growth were reiterated, consistent with the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $96.1 million was just below Benzinga’s $96.65 million estimate but materially below ChartMill’s $105.83 million estimate. The result was therefore around the low end of the preview’s consensus range, rather than a clear beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $96.1 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue estimates of $96.65M from Benzinga and $105.83M from ChartMill.

surprises.description: Management raised its long-term annual revenue target to $600 million from $500 million, primarily by doubling the semiconductor opportunity to $200 million annually. It also reported about $48 million of semiconductor revenue year-to-date, versus roughly $26 million for all of last year—substantial current traction alongside the higher target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised its long-term annual revenue target to $600 million from $500 million, driven primarily by doubling the semiconductor opportunity from $100 million to $200 million annually. Semiconductor revenue was about $48 million year-to-date, up from roughly $26 million for all of last year.

surprises.description: Non-Pay-TV recurring revenue grew 54% year over year and is now nearly twice the size of Pay-TV recurring revenue, providing stronger evidence of diversification than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-Pay-TV recurring revenue grew 54% year-over-year in Q2 and is now nearly double the size of Pay-TV recurring revenue.

surprises.description: The quarter brought a record 12 new customers, although the company closed six license agreements. The preview highlighted deal activity but did not anticipate the customer count or the specific RPX e-commerce opportunity, which management said could eventually reach roughly 10% of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company closed 6 license agreements and added a record 12 new customers, including a multiyear Google media portfolio renewal and a new RPX e-commerce deal. The RPX agreement licenses 10 member companies at once, and management believes e-commerce can grow to roughly 10% of total revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch the “count, new vs. renewal, and any large OTT/semiconductor names”; it did not give a Q2 deal or customer forecast.

surprises.description: Although the Fubo lawsuit itself was already known, management added that litigation timing is unpredictable and the case could pressure near-term Pay-TV results. That introduced a specific potential operating impact beyond the preview’s focus on the lawsuit’s scope and resolution path.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adeia filed claims against Fubo asserting 4 media patents; management said litigation timing is unpredictable and could pressure near-term Pay-TV results, while noting the case is separate from the Disney agreement.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the Fubo suit and said management’s “framing of scope and resolution path matters.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was 58.7%, which the company said was in line with expectations.

The company reiterated FY2026 revenue guidance of $395 million to $435 million and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of approximately 55%, as the preview identified reiteration of FY2026 guidance as the key issue.
The company continued share repurchases and debt payments and paid the $0.05 dividend, consistent with the preview’s focus on those capital-allocation actions.

surprises.description: BWXT agreed to sell just over 80% of its medical and Kinectrics stable-isotope enrichment businesses for $750 million upfront, with potential consideration of up to $800 million, while retaining a 20% stake. The preview highlighted these businesses as areas to watch but did not anticipate a sale; after closing, the businesses will no longer contribute revenue, though BWXT will receive equity income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “sale of just over 80% of its medical and Kinectrics stable isotope enrichment businesses to Nordic Capital for $750 million upfront, with shared economics allowing consideration up to $800 million, retaining a 20% minority equity stake”; the businesses “represent approximately $130 million of 2026 revenue” and “will be accounted for through equity income with no revenue post-close.”

surprises.description: BWXT raised its full-year outlook across revenue, adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow. The largest increase was in free cash flow, up $30 million from the prior guidance range; the revised EPS range also moved above the prior range at its upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raised full-year 2026 guidance: revenue to approximately $3.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $662-$672 million (up $10 million at midpoint), EPS to $4.70-$4.80, and free cash flow to $345-$360 million (up $30 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management's own FY2026 guidance (raised at Q1 report, 2026-05-04): revenue ≥$3.75B; adjusted EBITDA $650–665M; non-GAAP EPS $4.60–4.75; free cash flow $315–330M.”

surprises.description: Commercial Operations substantially outperformed the growth pace embedded in its prior outlook: revenue grew 72% and adjusted EBITDA more than doubled, while the full-year revenue-growth outlook rose to about 45% from about 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial Operations revenue grew 72% (33% organic) with adjusted EBITDA more than doubling (up 123%) to $36 million at an 11.9% margin, and full-year revenue growth guidance was raised to ~45% from ~30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “commercial nuclear components demand, Medical segment growth, and Kinectrics contribution” as themes to watch, but gave no numerical Commercial growth expectation.

surprises.description: Government Operations’ full-year revenue-growth outlook was cut from low teens to high single digits, even as its adjusted EBITDA margin outlook improved. This was a mixed change: slower expected revenue growth but a higher margin target, attributed to stronger HPDU cost performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Government Operations full-year revenue growth guidance was lowered to high single digits from low teens due to stronger HPDU cost performance, but adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was raised to ~20.5% from >19%.”

surprises.description: Backlog slipped modestly from the record level reported at Q1, rather than building further. The decline was tempered by a strong 1.7x trailing 12-month book-to-bill and backlog still being up 40% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog reached $8.4 billion, up 40% year-over-year but modestly lower sequentially, with a trailing 12-month book-to-bill of 1.7x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “record $8.65B at Q1 2026” and said to “watch for further build or any burn-down commentary.”

surprises.description: Management described a credible chance of winning at least one new-build nuclear equipment order before year-end, bringing potential order timing closer than the preview’s discussion of SMR optionality through FY2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a credible opportunity to secure at least one new-build nuclear equipment order before year-end, tied to SMR opportunities at Darlington, AP1000 projects, and X300 reactors.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “potential small-modular-reactor (SMR) optionality through FY2028.”

surprises.description: BWXT announced two new arrangements to commercialize reactor technology it had previously shelved: an exclusive land-based mPower license and a floating-platform feasibility study. The preview discussed SMR optionality but did not flag these agreements or the specific retained rights.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BWXT signed an exclusive land-based mPower licensing agreement with Applied Atomics and a floating-platform feasibility study with Core Power, retaining royalty rights, exclusive manufacturing rights, and IP to monetize technology it had shelved after spending ~$400 million.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.07 exceeded both previewed quarterly consensus estimates, though the gap was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “adjusted EPS increased 5% to $1.07.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed EPS estimates of “$1.01” and “$1.04.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $902 million was within the preview’s two consensus estimates of $891.8 million and $903.8 million.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $1.566 billion, about 4% above the preview’s roughly $1.50 billion consensus and above its $1.52 billion bull-case threshold. The preview expected the increase to be mostly inorganic, but the reported total was higher than that setup implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated net sales rose 92% year-over-year to $1.566 billion,” with Off-Highway contributing $706 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~ $1.50 bn”; the bull scenario specified “Consolidated revenue ≥$1.52 bn.”

surprises.description: The legacy Allison Transmission business grew rather than delivering the preview’s flat-to-down base case. Its $860 million of sales set a quarterly record and rose 6% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The legacy Allison Transmission business unit achieved a quarterly record of $860 million in net sales, up 6% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A flat-to-down Transmission BU print is the base case.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $2.73 exceeded the preview’s roughly $2.50 base-case expectation and both cited consensus figures, although the preview warned that the vendors’ EPS bases were unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 8% to $2.73.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave EPS consensus of “$2.48” and “$2.56,” and its base case called for “adj. EPS near $2.50.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $404 million, above the preview’s $360–380 million base-case range and also above its $385 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA reached $404 million (25.8% margin), up $91 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case projected “adj. EBITDA ~$360–380 M”; the bull case specified “adj. EBITDA ≥$385 M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted free cash flow reached a quarterly record of $281 million, a stronger Q2 conversion than the preview’s warning about the substantial back-half cash-flow requirement suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly adjusted free cash flow of $281 million rose 84% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Adj. FCF ($103 M in Q1 vs. FY $655–805 M) — a back-half-loaded conversion requirement worth stress-testing.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year sales, EBITDA, and free-cash-flow guidance instead of leaving the ranges unchanged. The sales midpoint rose about $150 million, and the EBITDA midpoint rose about $100 million versus the prior ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised 2026 guidance to “net sales of $5.8-6.0 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $1.465-1.575 billion” and “adjusted free cash flow of $745-865 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was a “third consecutive reaffirm” with “guidance reaffirmed with the range unchanged.” It listed prior ranges of “$5,575–5,925 M” sales, “$1,365–1,515 M” adjusted EBITDA, and “$655–805 M” adjusted FCF.

surprises.description: The call quantified a sharp near-term commodity-cost squeeze on legacy margins: steel and aluminum created mid-teens cost headwinds, with aluminum up nearly 25% quarter over quarter. Some recovery from customers is expected, but only with a 6-to-12-month lag, making the current margin drag more immediate than the preview’s general mix and price-cost concerns specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy business margins were compressed by rapidly rising commodity costs, with aluminum up nearly 25% quarter-over-quarter,” and “a substantial portion is recoverable from customers on a 6-to-12-month lag.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “a structural mix drag on consolidated margin” and flagged “tariff and price-cost commentary” as a checklist item, but did not quantify a near-term commodity shock or recovery lag.

surprises.description: The call said essentially no material synergies are included in 2026 EBITDA and laid out full realization only by 2029. That is a slower and more explicit realization path than the preview’s expectation that initial synergies would arrive later in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Essentially no material synergies baked into 2026 EBITDA”; the $120 million annual run-rate target is scheduled to be 40% realized by end-2027, 80% by 2028, and fully realized by 2029.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “$120 M run-rate” target had initial realization “later in 2026.”

surprises.description: The call reported wins covering more than 7,000 French tactical trucks, an award not identified in the preview’s discussion of defense orders. This adds an unanticipated defense program alongside the already-known BAE and EAGLE awards.
surprises.fact_evidence: Allison cited “wins covering 7,000+ French tactical trucks.”

in_line: The reported $250 million BAE Hägglunds CV90 MkIV contract and roughly 3,000-vehicle EAGLE award were already described in the preview; their presence in the call was not itself a new surprise.
The preview expected inorganic growth following the Off-Highway acquisition, and the call attributed $706 million of Q2 sales to that business.
The $0.29 dividend matched the preview’s note that the dividend had already been raised to $0.29.

surprises.description: AEIS reported Q2 revenue of $574 million, above both the $544.33 million consensus and the $560 million high end of company guidance. EPS was $2.74 versus the $2.20 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $574 million,” exceeding the high end of guidance; “EPS of $2.74.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue” consensus: “$544.33M”; company guidance: “$540M ± $20M.” Non-GAAP EPS consensus: “$2.20”; guidance: “$2.18 ± $0.25.”

surprises.description: Management raised its 2026 revenue-growth target from the low-to-mid-20% range to the low-to-mid-30% range, a substantial upgrade to the full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth target to the low-to-mid-30% range, up from the prior low-to-mid-20% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “FY2026 low-to-mid-20s% growth reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Data Center Computing was expected to grow 35% for the year, but management raised its full-year growth outlook to at least 50%. The Q2 result itself was slightly below Q1 sequentially, consistent with the preview’s expectation that revenue would moderate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data Center Computing revenue of $192 million grew 35% year-over-year, and full-year data center growth guidance was raised to at least 50% (from mid-30%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market was watching whether management would “reaffirm the mid-30% FY2026 data center growth target” and noted Q2 data center revenue would “moderate sequentially.”

surprises.description: Semiconductor revenue reached a record and grew 27% sequentially; more importantly, the expected second-half growth of over 30% year over year was upgraded to nearly 50%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Semiconductor revenue hit a record $278 million, up 27% sequentially and 33% year-over-year, with second-half revenue expected to grow nearly 50% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said AEIS had guided second-half semiconductor revenue “up >30% Y/Y” and flagged reaffirmation of that trajectory as a key issue.

surprises.description: Gross margin came in above the preview’s expected range even excluding tariff refunds: 40.7% excluding refunds versus an expected 40.3–40.6%. The reported margin was 41.9%, and operating margin expanded to 21.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 380 basis points year-over-year to 41.9% (40.7% excluding IEEPA tariff refunds), and operating margin expanded 730 basis points to 21.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected non-GAAP gross margin of “40.3–40.6%,” based on guidance for “+20–50bps off 40.1%.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook calls for about $640 million in revenue and $3.00 EPS, with record results expected to continue. The preview flagged the Q3 guide but did not give a specific Q3 estimate against which to compare it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of ~$640 million (±$20 million) and EPS of $3.00 (±$0.25), implying continued record results.”

surprises.description: Management moved beyond the previously stated long-term goal of gross margin above 43% by saying it now sees line of sight to that level and identifying new-product mix as the primary driver beyond volume leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company sees line of sight to gross margin above 43%, with product mix from new products cited as the primary driver beyond volume leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “a stated ‘>43%’ long-term goal” and identified whether AI-driven mix was accretive as a key debate.

surprises.description: The capacity update points to roughly $5 billion of revenue-generating capacity once the Thailand factory is fully built out, above the more than $3.5 billion of combined capacity implied by the preview’s figures for other sites and Thailand. Thailand production revenue is expected in Q4 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects roughly $5 billion of revenue-generating capacity once its new Thailand factory is fully built out, with Thailand's first production revenue expected in Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated Malaysia/Philippines/Mexico supporting “>$2.5B of revenue capacity by year-end,” plus Thailand “adding >$1B.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a 10-day inventory increase to 145 days amid the preview’s concern about cash generation and inventory, adding that the buildup is intended to support customer ramps and capture upside. The call facts do not provide the operating-cash-flow result needed to resolve the broader cash-flow concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised 2026 CapEx guidance to $180-195 million and increased inventory by 10 days to 145 days (turns at 2.5x) to support customer ramps and capture upside.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted Q1 operating cash flow of “−$6M” and a “$48M inventory build,” and flagged “operating cash flow and inventory delta” for the print.

surprises.description: Management gave a 2027 growth outlook of over 20% across all markets, adding a concrete next-year growth expectation that the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company projects over 20% revenue growth in 2027 across all markets.”

in_line: Q2 Data Center Computing revenue moderated slightly sequentially: $192 million versus $194.2 million in Q1, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q2 data-center revenue would moderate on delivery timing.
The company retained its above-43% long-term gross-margin ambition; the preview had already identified that goal.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $118.4 million, about $3.9 million above the $114.55 million consensus and above the company’s $114–115 million guidance. The preview described the revenue number as almost fully pre-announced, but the reported beat was larger than that setup implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue reached a record $118.4 million”; “the actual Q3 beat was only ~$4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sell-side consensus $114.55M”; company guidance was “$114–115M.”

surprises.description: Twist raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $456–457 million, about $12 million above the prior midpoint. The preview said consensus was sitting near the middle of the old $442–447 million range, with no raise embedded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $456-457 million (up $12 million at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026: company guides $442–447M”; consensus was “$444.69M — i.e. sitting mid-guidance, no raise embedded.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue guidance of $123–124 million is well above the preview’s implied $113.6–117.6 million, which suggested flat-to-modestly-up sequential revenue. The new range instead implies about 25% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue is guided to $123-124 million, implying ~25% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The implied Q4 FY26 is ~$113.6–117.6M — essentially flat-to-modestly-up sequentially versus Q3.”

surprises.description: Academic and government revenue sharply rebounded despite the preview’s expectation of a weak research-spending backdrop: it rose 32% year over year and 21% sequentially, after only 3% growth in the prior quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Academic and government revenue rebounded sharply to $15.5 million, up 32% year-over-year and 21% sequentially, versus just 3% growth the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Agilent noted academic & government spending –5%” and that this “argues against expecting broad-based upside.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss was about $11.3 million, worse than the preview’s base-case range of roughly $8–10 million in losses. Management nevertheless reaffirmed the expected Q4 breakeven target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss of ~$11.3 million”; management “reaffirmed its expectation to reach adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q4 fiscal 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “adj. EBITDA ~–$8M to –$10M.”

surprises.description: Management added a specific FY2027 AI-order growth outlook that the preview had not anticipated: it expressed confidence in repeating triple-digit order growth, extending the high-growth outlook beyond FY2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed confidence in repeating triple-digit order growth in fiscal 2027.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new cost and savings item: Q3 OpEx included about $2 million of employee-transition costs, which it expects to lead to more than $5 million of OpEx reduction in Q4. The preview had not flagged this one-off or the associated savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 OpEx of $98.7 million included ~$2 million in one-time employee transition costs expected to drive over $5 million in OpEx reduction in Q4.”

surprises.description: Management gave a more favorable longer-term margin indication than the preview discussed, citing 70% incremental-revenue drop-through to gross margin and a target above 60% as the business matures. The preview focused on crossing 52% in the near term and had no expectation for these longer-term margin figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “70% of incremental revenue dropping to gross margin, and management targets margins above 60% as the business matures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted an FY2026 gross-margin target of “>52%” and said gross margin “Needs to re-cross 52% to hit the FY target.”

in_line: Gross margin was 52.8%, above the preview’s 52% threshold; the preview expected it to re-cross 52%.
FY2026 AI-enabled drug-discovery order growth was expected to be on track to double; management said it expects to meet or exceed triple-digit growth, consistent with that expectation.
Management reaffirmed Q4 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA breakeven, which the preview identified as the existing target and a key issue to watch.
Therapeutics revenue growth was directionally consistent with the preview’s view that clinical and therapeutics-related demand was healthier than the academic-research channel.

surprises.description: Q2 U.S. BRIUMVI revenue was about $228 million, above the preview's $220 million company guide; global revenue exceeded $240 million, also above the roughly $230 million sell-side revenue expectation. The quarter therefore beat the revenue bar by about 4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 U.S. BRIUMVI net product revenue was approximately $228 million” and “global revenue exceeding $240 million and exceeding company guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 U.S. BRIUMVI net product revenue ≈ $220M”; revenue consensus was “$230.77M” and “$229.77M.”

surprises.description: TG raised its full-year global revenue outlook to approximately $950 million from the preview's expected $925 million. The U.S. range also moved up by $5 million at both ends, to $890 million–$905 million from $885 million–$900 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 U.S. BRIUMVI net revenue guidance to $890 million-$905 million and total global revenue to approximately $950 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guidance was “FY2026 total global revenue ≈ $925M” and “FY2026 U.S. BRIUMVI $885–900M.”

surprises.description: The company said Q2 net income included about $55 million of subcutaneous and secondary-source manufacturing charges. The preview already anticipated about $100 million of full-year subcutaneous manufacturing costs, but did not flag secondary-source charges or this specific quarterly earnings burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income was $7.8 million ($0.05 per diluted share), but excluding ~$55 million of subcutaneous and secondary-source manufacturing charges, net income would have been approximately $62 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “FY2026 opex ... ≈ $350M plus ≈ $100M subcutaneous manufacturing/start-up costs.”

surprises.description: The full-year operating expense outlook now spans $350 million–$400 million, plus about $100 million in manufacturing-related expenses, rather than the preview's approximately $350 million operating expense expectation. The upper end allows for higher spending than the preview indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year OpEx guidance of $350 million-$400 million plus ~$100 million in manufacturing-related expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY2026 opex (R&D+SG&A, ex-SBC) ≈ $350M plus ≈ $100M subcutaneous manufacturing/start-up costs.”

surprises.description: TG reported that more than 30,000 patients globally have been prescribed BRIUMVI. The preview cited more than 25,000 patients at Q1 and said it had found no Q2 patient-count datapoint or estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BRIUMVI has been prescribed to more than 30,000 patients globally.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “>25,000 patients prescribed BRIUMVI globally” at Q1 and said, “Any Q2'26 pre-announcement, buy-side whisper number, or post-Jun-30 U.S. script/patient-count datapoint. None found; none assumed.”

surprises.description: The company announced a Phase II study in treatment-resistant schizophrenia, a pipeline expansion not identified in the preview. The preview focused on BRIUMVI and the already noted MG and azer-cel programs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pipeline expansion includes ... a Phase II study in treatment-resistant schizophrenia.”

surprises.description: TG said its azer-cel program had enrolled more than 20 patients and expanded into MS, MG, CIDP, and NMO, beyond the preview's focus on a progressive-MS update. This adds indications and enrollment detail not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The azer-cel CD19 CAR-T program (over 20 patients enrolled, expanded to MS, MG, CIDP and NMO) with a clinical update expected in the second half of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned “Phase 1 azer-cel data in progressive MS guided to 2H 2026.”

surprises.description: TG described subcutaneous BRIUMVI as targeting the 35%–40% self-administered anti-CD20 segment, which it said could more than double its addressable market. The preview flagged the SC program but did not provide this market-size framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subcutaneous BRIUMVI ... targeting the 35%-40% self-administered anti-CD20 segment where TG currently does not compete, potentially more than doubling the addressable market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “SC BRIUMVI + azer-cel” and noted Phase III topline was expected “YE2026/1Q27.”

in_line: Management's plan to exit 2026 with quarterly U.S. revenue above $250 million, a $1 billion annualized run rate, was consistent with the preview's focus on the "$1B annualized run-rate before year-end" framing.

The low reported diluted EPS of $0.05 was directionally consistent with the preview's warning that vendor EPS consensus of $0.31–$0.43 was likely a low-signal comparison and that the company had repeatedly reported much lower GAAP EPS.

The positive ENHANCE findings and simplified single-infusion initiation aligned with the preview's note that Phase III topline was positive and that the single 600 mg Day-1 dose was supported; the preview also anticipated an sBLA submission in 2H 2026.
The expected timing for subcutaneous BRIUMVI Phase III topline—year-end 2026 or early 2027—was consistent with the preview's YE2026/1Q27 expectation.
The registration-directed MG study was consistent with the preview, which flagged a myasthenia gravis registration-directed trial start.
The expected second-half clinical update for azer-cel was consistent with the preview's expectation of a 2H 2026 update.

surprises.description: Reinforcement Materials EBIT was $97 million, below the preview’s implied $98–100 million from management’s expected $5–7 million sequential recovery. Global volume rose 5%, but lower gross profit per ton from the 2026 tire agreements held back the recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reinforcement Materials EBIT fell to $97 million from $128 million a year earlier,” hurt by “lower gross profit per ton from the 2026 annual tire customer agreements despite a 5% global volume increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reinforcement Materials EBIT up $5–7M sequentially on mix and yield”; applying that to Q2 actuals implied “~$98–100M RM.”

surprises.description: Performance Chemicals EBIT rose to $68 million, materially above the preview’s expectation of roughly flat sequential EBIT around $59 million. Battery Materials growth and pricing actions contributed to the stronger result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Performance Chemicals segment EBIT rose 19% year-over-year to $68 million, aided by battery materials growth and pricing actions taken ahead of rising raw material costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Performance Chemicals EBIT was expected to be “relatively consistent sequentially”; applying that to Q2 actuals implied “~$59M PC.”

surprises.description: Cabot raised the floor and lowered the ceiling of its FY26 adjusted EPS range, tightening it to $6.15–$6.45 rather than reaffirming the full $6.00–$6.50 range. The new midpoint is $6.30, close to the preview’s $6.33 analyst estimate, so the guidance action was more about narrowing uncertainty than raising the outlook overall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company tightened its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.15-$6.45 from the prior $6.00-$6.50 range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the range would narrow and said “reaffirming the full width signals unresolved Q4 risk”; its FY26 adjusted EPS estimate was “$6.33.”

surprises.description: Management announced that CEO Sean Keohane will retire on September 30, 2026, with CFO Erica McLaughlin named as his successor and a CFO search underway. The preview did not flag an impending leadership transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Sean Keohane will retire effective September 30, 2026, with CFO Erica McLaughlin appointed as the next President and CEO and a search underway for a new CFO.”

surprises.description: Cabot replaced the planned Michigan greenfield battery facility with roughly $125 million of brownfield expansions at two existing U.S. sites. The capacity is expected online in 2028 and is described as sufficient for about three years of growth; this investment-plan change was not previewed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cabot replaced its planned Michigan greenfield battery facility with brownfield expansions at two existing U.S. sites, investing roughly $125 million with capacity expected online in 2028 and sufficient for about three years of growth.”

surprises.description: The operating tax-rate outlook moved up by one percentage point at both ends, from 27–29% to 28–30%, a modest headwind relative to the preview’s stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “raised the operating tax rate range to 28%-30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed an “Operating tax rate: 27–29%.”

surprises.description: Cabot cut the high end of its FY26 capex range by $15 million, to $200–215 million from $200–230 million. The lower spending ceiling was not anticipated in the preview’s capital-allocation discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management narrowed fiscal 2026 capex guidance to $200-$215 million (cutting the high end by $15 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “capex $200–230M” and said to “Watch buyback pace against $200–230M capex.”

surprises.description: Cabot made no share repurchases in Q3 despite having repurchased about $100 million through the first half. Management expects to resume buybacks in Q4, so the pause was temporary but the quarter’s pace was below what the preview’s capital-return watchpoint might have led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cabot “repurchased $101 million of shares year-to-date with none in Q3, but expects to resume buybacks in the fourth quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$100M repurchased through H1 FY26” and said to “Watch buyback pace against $200–230M capex.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS of $1.67 was essentially in line with the preview’s $1.65–$1.66 consensus range.
Cabot reaffirmed approximately $40 million of FY26 Battery Materials EBITDA and trailing 12-month EBITDA margins of about 24%, consistent with the preview’s stated expectations.

Management warned of modest sequential EBIT declines in Q4. The preview had already highlighted Q4 downside risk and the possibility that results could trend toward the lower end of the full-year range.

surprises.description: Revenue was $1.935 billion, about 7% above the roughly $1.81 billion consensus, with year-over-year growth of 93% versus the expected 80%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 93% year-over-year to $1.935 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (consensus) | ~$1.81B, +80% YoY.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $8.15–$8.158 billion, or 80% growth—above the prior $7.650–$7.662 billion outlook and the preview’s cited bull-case expectation of growth moving toward 75% or higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $8.15–$8.158 billion (80% growth), an 11-point increase and the largest ever full-year guidance raise.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bulls (Oppenheimer) look for the ~71% growth guide to move toward 75%+.”

surprises.description: U.S. commercial revenue accelerated to 149% growth, compared with 133% in Q1, rather than merely holding up amid the preview’s concern about softer commercial spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. commercial revenue accelerated to 149% year-over-year growth (28% sequentially) reaching $764 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “US commercial momentum — whether +133% growth and $1.2B quarterly TCV hold up against Cleveland Research's softer-spend channel checks.”

surprises.description: The U.S. commercial full-year outlook rose to more than $3.424 billion and at least 134% growth, well above the prior guide of more than $3.2 billion and about 120% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. commercial guidance lifted to over $3.424 billion (at least 134% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “US commercial revenue >$3.2B (~120% growth).”

surprises.description: U.S. commercial TCV bookings reached a record $2.132 billion, far surpassing the $1.2 billion Q1 figure the preview identified as a level to watch for holding up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company closed a record $2.132 billion in U.S. commercial TCV bookings, up 153% year-over-year and nearly $800 million above the prior highest quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether +133% growth and $1.2B quarterly TCV hold up.”

surprises.description: Net dollar retention rose to 157%, up from 150% in Q1, indicating stronger expansion within existing customers than the preview’s reference point suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net dollar retention jumped 700 basis points sequentially to 157%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net dollar retention (150% in Q1).”

surprises.description: U.S. government revenue grew 90%, above the low-80% growth analysts were expecting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. government revenue grew 90% to $809 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Analysts expect low-80% growth.”

surprises.description: Adjusted free cash flow reached a record $1.22 billion, substantially exceeding the $925 million Q1 figure the preview described as setting a high bar; full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance also rose to $4.5–$4.7 billion from $4.2–$4.4 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow hit a record $1.22 billion at a 63% margin, and full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised to $4.5–$4.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1's $925M set a high bar”; “adjusted free cash flow $4.2–4.4B.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was $0.41 versus the $0.28 consensus. The reported figure included a $0.03 benefit from unrealized gains on SpaceX holdings, so part of the beat came from that non-operating tailwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income reached $1.062 billion (55% margin) with GAAP EPS of $0.41, aided by a $0.03 tailwind from unrealized SpaceX holding gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP diluted EPS (consensus) | $0.28.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin declined to 86% because Palantir took on cloud-hosting costs for a government customer, an unfavorable cost and margin development not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin declined to 86% due to costs from taking on cloud hosting for a government customer.”

surprises.description: Management warned of a significant Q3 expense ramp from new-hire seasonality, adding a near-term cost headwind that the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management warned of a significant Q3 expense ramp from new-hire seasonality.”

surprises.description: CEO Alex Karp set a specific, ambitious target for the overall business to grow at least as fast as U.S. commercial over the next 18 months; the preview did not cite this target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Alex Karp set an ambitious target to grow the overall business at a rate equal to or above U.S. commercial growth for the next 18 months.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales were about $3.5 billion, roughly 4% above the preview’s $3.36–$3.37 billion consensus range. The company also reported 6.7% sales growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 global sales grew 6.7% to $3.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: ~$3.36B (Zacks) vs ~$3.37B (MarketBeat/Yahoo cite).”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $1.27, above the preview’s $1.22 consensus estimate by about 4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS grew 15.5% to $1.27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. (non-GAAP) EPS: $1.22.”

surprises.description: Henry Schein raised its full-year sales and EPS guidance, lifting the sales-growth range from 3%–5% to 4.5%–5.5% and EPS from $5.23–$5.37 to $5.29–$5.39. The preview had described the lower EPS range and $13.6–$13.8 billion sales guidance from Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 sales guidance to 4.5%-5.5% growth (from 3%-5%) and non-GAAP EPS to $5.29-$5.39 (from $5.23-$5.37).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company raised FY2026 guidance: revenue to $13.6B–$13.8B, EPS to $5.23–$5.37.”

surprises.description: U.S. dental merchandise grew 8.3%, but growth came more from price than volume; the preview had called out expected volume and share gains. That makes the reported growth mix less volume-led than investors were primed to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. dental merchandise sales grew 8.3% (6.5% internal local currency) with growth driven more by price than volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “US dental merchandise volume/share gains.”

surprises.description: Specialty implant strength came from premium implants in Europe, whereas the preview expected value implants to outpace the premium tier. The preview’s expectation that Europe would be stronger than the U.S. was consistent with the call, which described more modest U.S. implant growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty Products Group profit grew 19.9% (mostly organic) with premium implant strength in Europe, while U.S. implant growth was more modest due to weaker consumer-driven market conditions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “implant/biomaterials demand, value implants outpacing premium tier, Europe > US.”

surprises.description: The EPS guidance increase was partly offset by much lower expected remeasurement gains: just $11 million for 2026 versus $38 million in 2025, with no further gains assumed for the rest of the year. The preview did not flag this as a factor in the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The EPS guidance raise was partially offset by lower expected remeasurement gains, now projected at just $11 million for 2026 versus $38 million in 2025, with no further gains assumed for the rest of the year.”

in_line: The preview expected cloud practice-management demand and Dentrix Ascend momentum; the call cited nearly 13,000 cloud-based platform subscribers. The preview also expected Europe to outperform the U.S. in specialty products, consistent with the call’s stronger European implant results and more modest U.S. growth.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin was 30.6%, below the preview’s expected 32–33% and below its 31% downside threshold. This was a material miss against the margin recovery the preview said was needed to support the second-half plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 30.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs ~32–33% to make the EBITDA guide” and “A sub-31% print breaks the entire 2H bridge.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance points to much slower adjusted EBITDA growth than the full-year outlook: only 8% at the midpoint. That makes the preview’s required second-half margin ramp harder to achieve, since Q3 guidance implies roughly a 21% EBITDA margin at the midpoint versus about 23% needed across the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $150-170 million (18% growth at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $32-37 million (only 8% growth at midpoint), implying decelerating EBITDA growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY guide midpoint (20.2% on $620M) requires ~23% in 2H26” and “Q2 is the first proof point that the ramp is real.”

surprises.description: Bookings and BLAO were stronger than the preview’s base case: BLAO reached a record $801 million, above the preview’s $760–790 million base range, with a 1.3 book-to-bill ratio. The preview had highlighted flat-to-down sequential BLAO as a bear trigger, while the call also said about $700 million is scheduled for delivery over the next four quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New orders of approximately $207 million produced a 1.3 book-to-bill ratio, lifting backlog and awarded orders (BLAO) to a company-record $801 million” and “Approximately $700 million of BLAO has planned delivery dates in the next four quarters through Q2 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “BLAO $760–790M”; it called “Flat-to-down q/q BLAO” the bear trigger and noted “~$628M shippable through Q1'27.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA modestly beat the preview’s roughly $30 million consensus, reaching $31.6 million. Its 28% year-over-year growth also exceeded the preview’s implied 25% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew ~28% year-over-year to $31.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$30M (guide mid)” and implied year-over-year growth of “+25%.”

surprises.description: SG&A improved sharply, falling to 17% of revenue, a 400-basis-point improvement. The preview focused on gross-margin recovery and did not flag this degree of operating-expense improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A improved 400 basis points to 17% of revenue.”

surprises.description: Net debt rose to $181.1 million and the company temporarily added $50 million of revolver capacity to fund heavy first-half inventory investment. This adds a financing and liquidity concern to the inventory-cash-flow issue the preview was watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt rose to $181.1 million with leverage at 1.6x adjusted EBITDA, and the company temporarily expanded its revolving credit facility by $50 million amid heavy first-half inventory investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Q1 burned $41.4M on inventory build” and warned that “A second consecutive burn quarter makes the FY cash guide non-credible.”

surprises.description: The call gave a timing for relief from litigation expenses: after the district court damages trial is expected to conclude in Q3, related expenses should fall away in Q4. The preview mentioned the IP victory but did not anticipate this near-term expense relief.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Shoals prevailed in its 2025 ITC case against Voltage, with the district court damages trial expected to conclude in Q3 2026, after which related legal expenses should fall away in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the “ITC IP victory (Jun 25, 2026)” but did not give a trial or legal-expense timeline.

surprises.description: The Air Link data-center product was described as differentiated and expected to command premium margins. The preview had flagged the data-center opportunity, but not the expectation of premium margins for this product.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The differentiated Air Link data-center product expected to command premium margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “AI data center opportunity” and cited “$50–60M of content per GW,” but did not mention premium margins for Air Link.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $163 million was close to the preview’s roughly $160 million consensus and within the company’s $150–170 million guide.
The company reaffirmed its FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, consistent with the preview’s stated base case.
International BLAO of $102 million was close to the preview’s approximately $100 million estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $354.7 million, below the preview’s $359.4 million consensus despite 15.2% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue rose 15.2% to $354.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $359.4M”

surprises.description: Traffic was much less negative than the buy-side expectation of roughly -2% to flat: it was -0.4%, improved 160 basis points sequentially, and turned positive in June.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-restaurant traffic was slightly negative at -0.4% but improved 160 basis points sequentially from Q1, with June turning positive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Same-restaurant traffic | ~−2% to flat (buy-side)”

surprises.description: Same-restaurant sales of 3.4% came in above the preview’s guide-anchored 1–3% expectation, even though traffic remained slightly negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “3.4% same-restaurant sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Same-restaurant sales | ~1–3% (guide-anchored)”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $34.5 million, below the preview’s derived $36–38 million bogey.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 13.5% to $34.5 million (9.7% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | ~$36–38M (our derived bogey)”

surprises.description: The company cut FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $133–136 million rather than reiterating the preview’s $133–140 million range. Management attributed the reduction entirely to higher COGS from stronger-than-expected demand for premium-beef LTOs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $133-136 million, attributing the reduction entirely to higher COGS from stronger-than-expected demand for premium beef LTO offerings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 Adjusted EBITDA guidance ($133–140M)” and the base scenario expected it to be “reiterated at $133–140M.”

surprises.description: Premium-beef LTO demand was strong enough to push beef-related costs up by just under 100 basis points year over year, an unexpected cost pressure that management said should ease substantially after the steak LTO ends in mid-August.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Beef-based menu items increased overall cost of goods by just under 100 basis points year over year, an impact expected to moderate substantially after the current steak LTO ends in mid-August.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted commodity inflation of “1–3%” but did not anticipate this beef-LTO-specific cost increase.

surprises.description: The broader commodity picture was more favorable than the preview’s 1–3% inflation assumption: Q2 had commodity deflation, and full-year guidance was revised to flat-to-up 1.5%, although management expects inflation to return in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 benefited from ~1.6% commodity deflation (eggs, avocados, bacon), but full-year commodity inflation guidance was revised to flat-to-up 1.5% with inflation expected to return in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “commodity [being] guided 1–3%.”

surprises.description: Management raised the low end of full-year same-restaurant sales guidance to 1.5% and total revenue growth guidance to 12.5%, while still warning that Q3 would be at or below the low end because of its tough comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised the low end of full-year same-restaurant sales guidance to 1.5-3% and total revenue growth to 12.5-14%, while cautioning Q3 faces the toughest comparison and will land at or below the low end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave same-restaurant sales of “~1–3% (guide-anchored)” and FY revenue consensus of “$1.38B / +13.2%.”

surprises.description: The company lowered its long-term company-owned opening target to about 50 annually starting in 2027, shifting emphasis from unit growth toward positive free cash flow and a stronger balance sheet.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its long-term unit growth target to about 50 company-owned openings annually beginning in 2027 (down from ~10% growth) to prioritize positive free cash flow starting in 2027 and strengthen the balance sheet.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a growth plan of “53–55 company” openings and said management was “prioritizing reinvestment”; it did not anticipate a lower long-term target or the stated free-cash-flow priority.

surprises.description: Management reported sizable brand-awareness gains and above-average repeat visitation among newly acquired customers, a positive customer-acquisition signal not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unaided brand awareness rose more than 50% and aided awareness increased 15% since early 2025, with 17% of newly acquired customers already returning for a second visit, tracking above average.”

in_line: Restaurant-level operating margin was broadly near the preview’s roughly 19% expectation: it improved to 18.8% from 18.5% in Q1.
Wage inflation of 4.1% was within the preview’s expected 3–5% labor-inflation range.
The warning that Q3 could be at or below the low end was consistent with the preview’s concern that the H2 pricing roll-off could leave comps at or below the low end.

surprises.description: U.S. IMCIVREE sales reached $51 million, well above the preview’s estimate of roughly $41–43 million, and drove a strong sequential rebound. The preview identified U.S. re-acceleration as the key test after Q1’s sequential decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$51 million (72%) generated in the U.S. driven by the acquired HO launch”; global sales were “up 19% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “US ~$41–43M” and said “US revenue re-acceleration” was the top metric to watch after Q1 U.S. revenue “declined 5% sequentially.”

surprises.description: Total IMCIVREE sales were $71.3 million, beating the preview’s ~$67.3 million consensus by about $4 million. The quarter’s 19% sequential growth also exceeded the preview’s 12% QoQ estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global net product sales of IMCIVREE reached $71.3 million in Q2 2026, up 19% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 consensus of “~$67.3M” and expected “+12% QoQ.”

surprises.description: International revenue was only $20.3 million versus the preview’s $25–26 million estimate. The company attributed the decline partly to an unexpected retrospective French contribution charge, including $2.3 million tied to 2025 revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International revenue declined to $20.3 million from $23.2 million, primarily due to a $3.8 million retrospective French contribution charge, of which $2.3 million related to 2025 revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “ex-US ~$25–26M.”

surprises.description: HO start forms exceeded even the preview’s bull-case threshold, and the company reported 66 clinical-trial patient conversions. However, the preview specifically sought a count of patients converted to paid or reimbursed therapy, and the reported 66 were not identified as paid conversions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the first 14 weeks since March 19 approval, Rhythm received more than 400 start forms from approximately 300 unique prescribers for acquired hypothalamic obesity, including 66 converted clinical trial patients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case called for “cumulative HO start forms ~350+ with a quantified paid-conversion cohort”; it also said the market wanted “a converted-patient number” and that “refusal to break it out will be read negatively.”

surprises.description: HO-specific coverage was already in place for roughly a quarter of Medicaid and over a third of commercial covered lives by Q2-end, with no GLP-1 step edits reported. This is encouraging progress within the preview’s policy window, though the preview did not set a coverage-percentage target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HO-specific positive coverage policies were secured for approximately 25% of Medicaid and 35% of commercial covered lives, with no GLP-1 step edits required.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “3–9 months from approval for HO-specific policies” and described movement toward the near end of that window as the bull unlock.

surprises.description: RM-718 showed a numerically stronger BMI reduction than the setmelanotide and bivamelagon figures cited on the call, rather than merely matching the preview’s competitive-efficacy bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RM-718… delivered a mean BMI reduction of 11.6% at week 16 in HO patients, favorably comparable to setmelanotide (10.1%) and bivamelagon (10.1%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “competitive BMI reduction” and framed the comparison against setmelanotide and bivamelagon as a key test.

surprises.description: Despite no generalized hyperpigmentation, RM-718 had adverse events that led 2 of 11 patients to discontinue early, including uncontrolled nausea. That falls short of the preview’s clean-tolerability expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2 of 11 enrolled patients discontinued due to adverse events (injection site reactions and uncontrolled nausea) within the first 4 weeks”; “no generalized hyperpigmentation observed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “hyperpigmentation, nausea” and described its bull case as RM-718 data with “clean tolerability.”

surprises.description: The GAAP loss per share was narrower than expected: a $0.73 loss versus the preview’s $0.82 loss consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss per share was $0.73 for Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed GAAP EPS consensus of “$(0.82).”

surprises.description: The company lowered the midpoint of its R&D expense guidance by $20 million, rather than simply reaffirming the prior spending outlook. The reduction reflects CMC work moving into early 2027, although the company said clinical timelines were unaffected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rhythm reduced the midpoint of its full-year non-GAAP R&D expense guidance by $20 million (to $175-195 million) as certain RM-718 and bivamelagon CMC activities shifted from late 2026 to early 2027, without affecting clinical timelines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 non-GAAP R&D guidance of “$197–213M” and said reaffirmation of the FY26 opex guide was a key catalyst.

surprises.description: Q2 operating cash use was far below the prior-quarter burn discussed in the preview, leaving cash at $331 million and maintaining the stated 24-month runway. That is more reassuring than the preview’s cash-exit threshold and financing concern suggested might be necessary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with approximately $331 million in cash and equivalents, expected to fund operations for at least 24 months, with cash used in operations of only ~$9 million during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$340.6M cash at 3/31/26,” “$48.3M Q1 burn,” and said cash of “≥$290M” would keep financing off the table.

in_line: Japan approval and commercial launch timing remained consistent with the preview’s expectation of a decision and launch targeted by year-end 2026.
The company reiterated an operating runway of at least 24 months, consistent with the preview’s stated runway.

surprises.description: Leidos reported non-GAAP EPS of $3.26, well above the preview’s $2.90–$2.91 consensus. The beat was much larger than the preview’s base case, which anticipated roughly $2.90–$3.00.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $3.26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS of $2.90–$2.91”; the base scenario expected “$2.90–$3.00.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $4.6 billion, above the preview’s $4.435 billion consensus, and organic growth was 4% rather than the roughly 0.5–1% the preview inferred was embedded. That indicates the result was stronger than an Entrust-driven headline beat alone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 7% year-over-year (4% organically) to a record $4.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus was “$4.435B”; the preview said consensus was “modeling organic growth of only ~0.5–1%.”

surprises.description: Management raised 2026 guidance rather than reaffirming or narrowing it: the revenue midpoint rose $100 million and the EPS midpoint rose $0.05, with larger increases at the lower ends. The preview treated a reaffirmation as the base case and a raise as the bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised the midpoint of 2026 revenue guidance by $100 million, EPS guidance by $0.05, and lifted the lower ends of ranges (revenue +$200 million, EPS +$0.10).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected FY guidance to be “reaffirmed or narrowed, not raised”; the bull case anticipated a raise.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was 13.8%, above the preview’s implied 13.3–13.6% range and its on-script estimate of about 13.3%. This was better than expected despite the preview’s warning about lost insurance reimbursement and higher growth investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin of 13.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ~13.3–13.6% (implied)”; the preview said “a ~13.3% print is on-script.”

surprises.description: Leidos produced record quarterly cash flow and improved its full-year cash outlook: it raised operating cash flow guidance by $50 million and lowered expected CapEx to roughly $250 million. The preview expected about $1.80 billion of full-year operating cash flow and flagged Q2 free cash flow as important, but did not anticipate this guidance improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2-record $793 million in operating cash flow and $761 million in free cash flow,” with full-year operating cash flow guidance raised by $50 million and CapEx expectations cut to “roughly $250 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 operating cash flow ~$1.80B”; Q2 FCF “matters for the tie-out.”

surprises.description: The VA suspended incentive payments for all medical disability exam vendors for the rest of 2026, a health-sector headwind the preview did not identify. Management said the hit was incorporated into the raised guidance, but also said the Q4 run-rate should be the baseline for 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The VA suspended incentive payments for all medical disability exam vendors for the remainder of 2026,” and the headwind is “fully incorporated into the raised guidance,” with “Q4 run-rate expected to be the baseline for 2027.”

surprises.description: Health revenue contracted as a fourth vendor was fully incorporated into the VBA contract, and management expects the segment to remain around Q2 levels with margins near 20%. That is a more pressured outlook than the preview’s expectation that Health would hold above 20% margins, though it remains around the stated floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Health segment revenue contracted due to a fourth vendor being fully incorporated into the VBA contract,” and is expected to sustain “around Q2 levels” with “non-GAAP OI margins near 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “committed to holding Health above 20%” and expected “Health low-20s” in its base case.

surprises.description: Defense bookings were much stronger than the preview’s roughly 1.0–1.1x company-wide base case: Defense posted a 2.2 book-to-bill and is expected to grow high-single-digits for the year. The 1.1 company-wide book-to-bill was in line with the base case, but the Defense result and outlook point to a stronger launch into 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense posted a 2.2 book-to-bill in Q2 (1.9 trailing-twelve-months)” and is expected to grow “high-single-digits for the year, or double digits excluding the transitioning airborne ISR business.” Total company net awards were $5 billion for a 1.1 book-to-bill.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “book-to-bill ~1.0–1.1x”; the preview said awards should “pick up significantly” through the year and flagged a second sub-1.0x quarter as a concern.

surprises.description: Despite management describing Leidos’ valuation as being at multiyear lows, the reported Q2 buyback was $66 million and the new authorization was only $20 million. That was weaker than the preview’s hoped-for accelerated repurchase signal, although the preview did not specify an expected amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: Leidos “completed its 2022 share repurchase authorization with a $66 million buyback” and the Board approved a “new $20 million” authorization; management said valuation was at “multiyear lows” and M&A targets were “currently expensive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “an accelerated repurchase is the cleanest signal management thinks the sell-off is overdone” and flagged buyback commentary as a credibility signal.

in_line: The company-wide book-to-bill was 1.1x, matching the preview’s base-case range of approximately 1.0–1.1x, even though Defense’s 2.2x was stronger than that overall result.
Leidos paid down the remaining $300 million of commercial paper, consistent with the preview’s statement that it planned to retire $300 million in 2026.

surprises.description: Trex guided Q3 sales to $305–$320 million, above the preview’s expected range of roughly $285–$300 million. The midpoint is about $20 million higher than the preview’s base-case midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net sales are guided to $305 million to $320 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (55%) | Revenue: ~$418M … Q3 ~$285–300M”; the catalyst checklist also called out “Q3 revenue guide vs. ~$285–300M.”

surprises.description: Management said Q4 revenue implied by its outlook would be flat to down year over year, a weaker signal than the preview’s expectation for H2 sales to grow about 5.7%. Management attributed the conservative outlook to geopolitical uncertainty.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The implied Q4 outlook suggesting flat-to-down year-over-year revenue that management attributed to conservatism amid geopolitical uncertainty.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY guide implies H2'26 of $454–489M (mid ~$471M, ~+5.7% vs. H2'25's ~$446M).”

surprises.description: Trex raised its full-year adjusted gross-margin outlook to approximately 38%, rather than holding the preview’s expected 37.5% guide. The 50-basis-point increase was attributed primarily to better capacity utilization as Little Rock begins production.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted gross margin guidance was raised to approximately 38% from 37.5%, primarily driven by higher capacity utilization as Little Rock begins production in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin … held ~37.5%”; the preview also asked whether the guide would be “reaffirmed at ~37.5%.”

surprises.description: Trex authorized up to another $150 million of repurchases for the rest of 2026, beyond the $150 million buyback the preview said had already been committed in H1. That is a substantially larger repurchase commitment than the preview’s stated baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to repurchase up to an additional $150 million of shares during the remainder of 2026, having already bought back approximately $51 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$150M of buyback (incl. a $100M ASR) committed in H1. Watch for a new authorization.”

surprises.description: Demand improved at the lower end of Trex’s lineup: entry-level products had their first meaningful sales increase in years, alongside a return to double-digit railing growth. That contrasts with the preview’s description of lower-price-point consumers as challenged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Railing sales returned to double-digit growth and Trex Enhanced basic (entry-level) products posted their first meaningful sales increase in years, signaling the entry-level consumer's return.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “consumer demand challenged at lower price points and premium holding up.”

surprises.description: The Little Rock ramp was accelerated by more than six months, with about half of its lines expected to be producing by year-end. The preview discussed Arkansas depreciation headwinds but did not anticipate this faster ramp schedule; most of the margin benefit is still expected later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Little Rock facility ramp-up was accelerated by over six months, with roughly 50% of lines expected in production by year-end and most margin benefits realized in 2027 and beyond.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was affected by more than 100 basis points of temporary manufacturing inefficiencies during the production ramp, an additional near-term drag not identified in the preview’s stated margin headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 37.9%, hurt by product mix shift toward lower-margin railing and entry-level decking, Little Rock depreciation, and over 100 basis points of temporary manufacturing inefficiencies from rapidly ramping production.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview framed FY margin headwinds as “~250 bps: 170–180 bps Arkansas depreciation, 70–80 bps railing mix.”

surprises.description: Trex reported a $5 million noncash obsolete-equipment write-down that reduced adjusted diluted EPS by $0.03. The preview did not flag this one-off charge, even though its EPS bridge anticipated $0.62.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.62, which included a $0.03 negative impact from a $5 million noncash write-down for obsolete equipment that was excluded from adjusted EBITDA of $112 million.”

in_line: Q2 net sales of $418 million and adjusted EBITDA of $112 million were effectively pre-announced and matched the preview’s consensus figures.
Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.62 matched the preview’s own EPS bridge and fell within its stated practical range of $0.60–$0.67.

surprises.description: Waters reported $1.645 billion of Q2 revenue, about $23 million above the $1.6223 billion consensus and above the company’s $1.616–$1.631 billion guide. The beat was modest relative to the expected headline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total company as-reported revenue was $1.645 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus” total revenue was “$1.6223B”; company guide was “$1.616–1.631B.”

surprises.description: Organic constant-currency growth was 9%, about 100 basis points above the high end of the 6%–8% guide. That exceeded the formal guide, although it was around the preview’s inferred +9% whisper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic revenue grew 9% in constant currency, beating the high end of guidance by roughly 100 basis points despite absorbing a 1% headwind from prior-year pull-forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed organic CC growth guidance of “+6.0% to +8.0%” and said the whisper was “closer to +9%.”

surprises.description: The acquired Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions businesses produced $817 million of revenue, about $15 million above the roughly $802 million guide. Their 4% reported growth (6% excluding China) also accelerated 400 basis points from flat last quarter, and management expects growth to exceed 6% by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: The acquired businesses contributed “$817 million”; they “grew 4% reported (6% ex-China), a 400 basis point acceleration versus last quarter's flat growth,” with a “greater-than-6% exit rate by year-end” target.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put acquired revenue at “~$802M” and described a second consecutive beat as a possible validation of the turnaround.

surprises.description: Waters raised its full-year organic growth outlook to 7%–9% from 6.5%–8.0%. The new high end is above the preview’s stated prior guidance and is a stronger organic outlook than a simple flow-through EPS raise alone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 organic constant currency growth guidance to 7%-9%.”
