surprises.description: Written sales growth was much stronger than the preview’s Q1-based benchmark: total written sales rose 12.6% and written comps rose 12.3%, compared with Q1 written comps of 7.0%. Growth also stayed in double digits in each month, rather than merely converting Q1’s strength into delivered sales as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total written sales rose 12.6% (comps up 12.3%), with double-digit written growth in every month: April up 10.6%, May up 15.7%, and June up 10.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comparable written business ... up 7.0% in Q1”; “Q1’s written strength is what underwrites the Q2 delivered number.”

surprises.description: The reported 61.4% gross margin topped the preview’s 60.8–61.0% base estimate, but the margin excluding about $1.5 million of tariff refunds was 60.7%, essentially flat year over year and below the base range. The headline margin outperformance therefore did not reflect underlying margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 61.4%, but excluding ~$1.5 million in IEEPA tariff refunds, margin was essentially flat at 60.7% versus 60.8% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: ~60.8–61.0% (my est.)”; base scenario: “GM 60.8–61.0%”; bull scenario: “GM holds ≥61.3%.”

surprises.description: Management gave more specific and persistent cost warnings than the preview’s general expectation of fuel-related pressure: container rates are set to rise 25–30% from mid-August, diesel is above $5 per gallon, and product input costs are expected to remain higher through year-end. Those details add pressure to the reaffirmed margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 25%-30% container rate increase starting mid-August, diesel above $5/gallon raising transportation costs, and higher product input costs through year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management also called out rising fuel costs hitting Q2 across vendor input, freight, and home delivery.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased about $16.6 million of shares year to date, including a privately negotiated purchase of roughly 600,000 shares in June, leaving only about $1.8 million of authorization. The preview noted $16.4 million of authorization remained after Q1 but did not anticipate this substantial use of it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased ~723,000 shares for $16.6 million year-to-date (including 600,000 shares for ~$13.9 million in a June privately negotiated transaction), leaving only ~$1.8 million of buyback authorization remaining.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the full-year gross-margin range of 60.5–61%, excluding additional tariff refunds, as the preview’s base case expected; the preview explicitly identified reaffirmation as a key catalyst.
Design mix increased to 36.5%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the design percentage would rise again.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $15.7 million, above the preview’s roughly $14.5 million estimate, and OIBDA was $13.7 million versus an estimated $13.3 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin was about 37.8%, also above the preview’s roughly 35% base-case level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% year-over-year to $15.7 million, while OIBDA increased 7% to $13.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA ~$14.5M (my est.; no published consensus)” and “OIBDA ~$13.3M (my est.).” The preview also described the base case as “$14.3–14.8M / ~35%.”

surprises.description: Recorded Music grew 35%, with the quarter boosted by unusually large synchronization deals. The preview discussed the segment split but did not anticipate these deals or give a Q1 Recorded Music growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recorded Music revenue surged 35% to $14.1 million,” driven partly by “outsized synchronization revenue from a couple of large sync deals closed in the quarter.”

surprises.description: Net debt rose to $448.5 million from $429.8 million at the prior quarter-end, moving materially above the preview’s $430 million watchpoint as borrowings funded acquisitions and writer signings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt increased to $448.5 million as of June 30, 2026 from $429.8 million at March 31, 2026, reflecting borrowings to fund acquisitions and writer signings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Leverage / capital deployment” and said to watch “net debt trajectory past $430M.”

surprises.description: Operating activities used $1.4 million in cash, a $7.4 million deterioration from the prior-year quarter due to royalty-payment timing and higher advances. The preview raised leverage and liquidity but did not anticipate this cash-flow decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating activities used $1.4 million in cash, a $7.4 million decline versus the prior-year quarter, driven by royalty payment timing and higher outgoing advances.”

surprises.description: The company expanded into Latin music through joint ventures with TU Publishing and the acquisition of Nacional Records, a strategic move not identified in the preview. The release cited a 17.1% growth rate for the target market in 2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reservoir expanded its Latin music footprint through joint ventures with TU Publishing and the acquisition of Nacional Records, targeting a market that grew 17.1% in 2025.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was breakeven rather than the expected $0.01 loss per share, as the net loss narrowed year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to approximately $508,000 from $644,000 a year ago, resulting in breakeven diluted EPS versus a $0.01 loss per share in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus diluted EPS was “($0.01).”

in_line: Revenue was $41.5 million, essentially matching the preview’s $41.46 million consensus estimate.
Organic revenue growth was 6%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of mid-single-digit organic growth.
Full-year fiscal 2027 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance was reiterated unchanged at $186–191 million and $75–79 million, as the preview expected.
The special committee provided no new update, matching the preview’s expectation of another quarter without a status change.
Music Publishing digital revenue grew 7%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that growth would normalize toward the prior full-year rate.

surprises.description: Pfizer reported Q2 revenue of $15 billion, above the preview’s $14.40–14.45 billion consensus range; instead of the expected year-over-year decline, revenue grew 1% operationally.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenues were $15 billion, up 1% operationally year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $14.40–14.45B” and year-over-year “‑1.4%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.77, above the preview’s $0.68 consensus and even above its estimated $0.72–0.75 functional whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.77 beat expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.68”; the preview also says the functional whisper was closer to “$0.72–0.75.”

surprises.description: Pfizer raised the midpoint of its full-year revenue outlook by $500 million, rather than reaffirming the range expected in the preview’s base case; the upper end remained unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $500 million to a range of $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected Pfizer to “Reaffirm $59.5–62.5B / $2.80–3.00”; its bull case anticipated a raise or narrowing to the upper half.

surprises.description: The revenue outlook improvement came despite Pfizer lowering its COVID-19 revenue assumption by about $1 billion, from roughly $5 billion to $4 billion—opposite the preview’s discussion of possible upside to the $5 billion assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cutting COVID-19 revenue expectations from roughly $5 billion to $4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “COVID franchise $5B” as an embedded assumption and said the market was watching whether “the $5B FY assumption is now conservative.”

surprises.description: Ex-COVID operational growth was 5%, below the preview’s 6% threshold for validating the post-pandemic growth engine and below the 6–7% base-case expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding COVID products the underlying business grew 5% operationally.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything sustaining ≥6% ex-COVID validates the post-pandemic engine”; the base case expected “ex-COVID growth ~6–7%.”

surprises.description: Pfizer recorded $4.3 billion of noncash intangible impairments and reported a GAAP loss per share, versus the preview’s expectation of about $0.45 in GAAP EPS. The preview knew about the failed sigvotatug readout, but did not anticipate the reported impairment charge or the removal of Oxbryta revenue projections.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recorded $4.3 billion in noncash intangible asset impairments in the quarter,” driven by the failed Phase III readout and “removal of Oxbryta revenue projections”; reported loss per share was “$0.04.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “GAAP EPS ~$0.45”; it noted that “sigvotatug vedotin missed OS in 2L NSCLC in June.”

surprises.description: Pfizer added an unexpected $650 million acquired in-process R&D charge tied to the Innovent transaction, an approximately $0.10 EPS impact. The company nevertheless kept its full-year adjusted EPS range unchanged, leaving the guidance outcome in line despite this new headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance was reaffirmed at $2.80 to $3.00, now absorbing an unfavorable ~$0.10 impact from a $650 million Acquired In-Process R&D charge tied to the Innovent Biologics transaction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Reaffirm $59.5–62.5B / $2.80–3.00”; it did not mention the Innovent charge.

surprises.description: Pfizer expanded its savings targets beyond the existing cost-program expectations, adding about $1 billion in productivity savings and targeting roughly $3 billion from manufacturing optimization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adding ~$1 billion to productivity savings (now $6.7 billion through 2029) and targeting ~$3 billion from manufacturing optimization, for approximately $9.7 billion in total net savings through 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said savings were “scaling through late 2026” and identified a “cost-savings target raised” as a bull-case signal.

surprises.description: Management gave unusually emphatic reassurance that it would maintain the dividend even in the most stretched scenarios and resume dividend growth after the post-2028 LOE period, directly addressing the cut concern raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Bourla “repeatedly and emphatically committed to maintaining the dividend even under the most stretched scenarios and resuming growth after the post-2028 LOE period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “dividend/deleveraging commentary given the ~131% payout ratio on GAAP earnings.”

surprises.description: CFO Dave Denton’s departure and Cecile Guegan’s appointment as interim CFO were not flagged in the preview, creating an unexpected leadership transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Dave Denton is departing Pfizer, with Cecile Guegan stepping in as interim CFO.”

in_line: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance remained at $2.80–$3.00, as the preview’s base case expected, although the company now absorbs the unexpected Innovent-related charge.
Pfizer planned 10 Phase III studies for berobenatide in 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of 10 pivotal studies launching that year.

surprises.description: IPG reported adjusted EPS of $0.58, well above the $0.40 consensus and even the $0.55 upper end of its prior guidance. The size of the earnings beat was substantially stronger than the preview’s roughly in-line base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.58” and exceeded “the top end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” adj. EPS was “$0.40”; company guidance was “$0.25–0.55.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 40.7%, above both the preview’s roughly 38.5% estimate and the 40% top end of guidance. The beat was partly helped by an unanticipated tariff-refund benefit of about 170 basis points, so the reported margin exceeded the preview’s bullish 39% threshold without that entire amount reflecting underlying operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin reached 40.7%, above the top end of guidance,” and included “a ~170 basis point benefit from $4.7 million in tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put adj. gross margin at “~38.5% (est.)” and said “39%+” would be “the single most bullish deliverable.”

surprises.description: Advanced Solutions revenue fell 9% year over year, rather than showing the inflection the preview was watching for. Semiconductor gains and 10% sequential growth were not enough to offset lower micromachining and defense sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advanced Solutions revenue declined 9% year-over-year (though up 10% sequentially)” as “semiconductor gains were offset by lower micromachining and defense sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for Advanced Solutions inflecting” and cited expected Crossbow, medical, and semiconductor traction.

surprises.description: The regional revenue picture was uneven: Asia rose 19% year over year, while North America declined 2% despite the preview noting strong bookings in both regions. The North American weakness was tied to cutting, defense, and medical applications.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Asia revenue jumped 19% year-over-year” while “North America revenue fell 2% due to weaker cutting, defense, and medical applications.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 “bookings strength was led by China, North America and Japan.”

surprises.description: The company said it expects its medical business to more than double over the next two to three years, a specific growth outlook not given in the preview’s discussion of medical backlog and the Lumibird deal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to more than double the medical business (currently ~7-8% of revenue) over the next 2-3 years.”

surprises.description: IPG said the Lumibird Medical acquisition would add about $1 billion to its addressable medical market, an opportunity detail the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The acquisition is “expected to close in Q4 2026” and would add “~$1 billion to the addressable medical market.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $49 million, just above the $48 million upper end of guidance. This was a smaller beat than the EPS outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $49 million,” exceeding the top end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance for adj. EBITDA was “$32–48M.”

in_line: Revenue of $279 million was essentially in line with the preview’s $279.98 million consensus.
Book-to-bill stayed above 1 for a third consecutive quarter, as the preview identified a third consecutive reading above 1.0 as the demand proof-point.

Q3 revenue guidance has a $280 million midpoint and adjusted EPS guidance a $0.45 midpoint, broadly matching the preview’s roughly $275–290 million revenue range and approximately $0.42–0.47 quarterly EPS bar.
The Lumibird deal remains on a path toward a Q4 close and is expected to be accretive in its first year, consistent with the preview’s expectations for Q4 timing and accretion.
IPG began shipping the Lockheed Martin CROSSBOW order in Q2, as the preview expected revenue recognition to begin this quarter.

surprises.description: Revenue was $981 million, about $7 million below the $988.47 million consensus, and Prepared Food and Beverage revenue was flat rather than inflecting: it fell roughly $20 million short because of logistics constraints and production inefficiencies. Management said the delayed revenue moves into the second half, with an estimated $5–6 million EBITDA impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenue was $981 million”; “Prepared Food and Beverage revenue fell short by roughly $20 million due to logistics constraints and production inefficiencies,” with the revenue “redistributed into the second half at an estimated $5-6 million EBITDA impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$988.47M.” The preview called Prepared Food & Beverage inflection “the single largest source of variance” and noted management had flagged “close to double-digit order improvement” in its pipeline.

surprises.description: A $17 million IEEPA tariff refund boosted adjusted EBITDA, contrary to the preview’s expectation that IEEPA relief would be offset by new tariff increases. The benefit was partly offset by $4 million of higher prior-year tariff expense and $5 million of accelerated incentive compensation; the refund also contributed about 200 basis points to Protein margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA “benefit[ted] from a $17 million IEEPA tariff refund,” partly offset by “$4 million in higher prior-year tariff expense and $5 million in accelerated incentive compensation”; Protein margins reached 24%, “about 200 basis points from tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management expected “IEEPA relief to be offset by incremental Section 122/232 increases” and guided to a “25–50 bps net tariff headwind.”

surprises.description: The company maintained the full-year outlook, but Q3 margin guidance of 17–17.5% and the stated steeper Q4 ramp leave more of the back-half margin improvement concentrated in Q4 than the preview’s roughly 18%+ required H2 margin implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA margins of “17-17.5%,” with “a steeper ramp expected in Q4”; full-year guidance was maintained.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 and Q2 results left “roughly 18%+ margin required in H2” and identified confidence in the “~18% implied H2 margin” as a key call question.

surprises.description: Facility consolidation savings were described at a much higher level than the preview’s synergy discussion indicated: the company now expects $25–30 million in annualized savings by 2028, versus an original estimate of $10–15 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Facility consolidations covering approximately 1.3 million square feet, a “15% global footprint reduction,” are expected to deliver “$25-30 million in annualized savings by 2028, up from an original estimate of $10-15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$60M targeted in 2026” and “~$150M annual run-rate targeted by end-2027,” and said any synergy pull-forward would be the cleanest path to a guidance raise; it did not identify this higher facility-savings estimate.

surprises.description: Warehouse automation added a distinct, unanticipated savings opportunity: AGV is consolidating two facilities into one for about $9 million of annual savings, even as it recorded its strongest volume quarter in six quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: AGV restructuring, “including consolidating two facilities into one,” is expected to generate “about $9 million in annual savings (~$3 million in H2 2026), following AGV's strongest volume quarter in six quarters.”

surprises.description: Leverage reached the company’s target range sooner than the preview’s Q1 leverage figure suggested, and management reported substantial year-to-date free cash flow alongside it.
surprises.fact_evidence: Leverage ended “just below 2.5x,” reaching the “2x-2.5x target range within 18 months of the combination,” with year-to-date free cash flow of “$179 million (58% EBITDA conversion).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported net debt/adjusted EBITDA of “2.6x at Q1” and listed leverage and capital returns as items to watch.

surprises.description: The company took a non-cash impairment on its 2021 Prevenio acquisition, an adverse item not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reaffirmed its 2028 adjusted EBITDA margin target while “taking a non-cash impairment on the 2021 Prevenio acquisition.”

surprises.description: Backlog coverage offered a specific reassurance for the back-half equipment revenue ramp: more than 90% of that revenue was already covered, a level the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year guidance was maintained, “supported by backlog covering over 90% of back-half equipment revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a third straight $1B+ orders quarter would “validate the H2 revenue ramp” and noted Q1 backlog of $1.49 billion, but did not give a back-half equipment revenue coverage figure.

in_line: Orders exceeded $1 billion for a third consecutive quarter, matching the preview’s highlighted marker for validating the back-half ramp; Prepared Food and Beverage orders also grew at a double-digit rate, consistent with the anticipated order improvement.

Full-year 2026 guidance was maintained at 6% revenue growth and 145 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion at the midpoint, consistent with the preview’s 5–7% revenue growth and approximately 145-basis-point margin expansion outlook.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was about 17.1% ($168 million on $981 million of revenue), within the 17.0–17.5% range in the company’s prior-quarter guidance.
The 20% adjusted EBITDA margin target for 2028 was reaffirmed, consistent with the preview’s description of that target.

surprises.description: Grainger reported diluted EPS of $12.01, above the preview’s $11.28–$11.30 consensus range by about 6% and representing growth of over 20%, versus the preview’s expected 13.1% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS up over 20% to $12.01.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $11.28 (Zacks Consensus) | +13.1%” and “EPS | $11.30 (alt. aggregator).”

surprises.description: Sales growth exceeded the preview’s expectations: reported sales grew 10.3% and daily organic constant-currency sales grew 13.7%, compared with the preview’s roughly 8.8% revenue growth and 8.5% estimated daily organic growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 reported sales grew 10.3% (13.7% on a daily organic constant currency basis).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$4.95–4.96B | +8.8%” and “Total organic daily sales growth (est.) | ~8.5%.”

surprises.description: Grainger raised full-year guidance across sales, EPS, and operating margin rather than simply reaffirming the existing outlook. The new EPS range is $45.50–$47.25 versus $44.25–$46.25, daily organic constant-currency sales growth is 11.5%–13% versus 9.5%–12%, and operating margin is 15.8%–16.2% versus 15.6%–16.0%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year EPS guidance to $45.50-$47.25 … an improvement of over $1 versus prior guidance”; “Full-year daily organic constant currency sales growth guidance was raised to 11.5%-13%, with operating margin guidance increased to 15.8%-16.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Current Full-Year FY2026 Guidance”: “daily organic constant-currency sales growth 9.5%–12.0%,” “Diluted EPS: $44.25–$46.25,” and “Adjusted operating margin: 15.6%–16.0%.” The preview also asked whether the EPS guide would be “reaffirmed, raised again, or narrowed.”

surprises.description: Endless Assortment growth was substantially faster than previewed: daily organic constant-currency sales rose 20.6%, versus the preview’s 12.2% estimate. Its operating margin also expanded 160 basis points to 11.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Endless Assortment sales rose 20.6% on a daily organic constant currency basis … and segment operating margin up 160 basis points to 11.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Endless Assortment sales | ~$1.03B (+10.8%; organic daily +12.2%).”

surprises.description: High Touch Solutions grew 11.9%, ahead of the preview’s roughly 7.4% organic daily growth estimate, and its operating margin rose 70 basis points to 17.3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “High Touch Solutions grew sales 11.9% with operating margin up 70 basis points to 17.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “High-Touch Solutions N.A. sales | ~$3.81B (+7.4% organic daily).”

surprises.description: MonotaRO’s strong growth included about $45 million of petroleum-product customer prebuying linked to the Middle East conflict. That benefit had fully subsided and was expected to slow second-half growth, an unanticipated pull-forward and future comparison headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MonotaRO's growth included roughly $45 million of customer prebuying of petroleum-related products tied to Middle East conflict, a benefit that has fully subsided and will slow second-half growth.”

surprises.description: A 90-basis-point benefit from EPA/tariff refunds on Grainger-imported products contributed to the 100-basis-point gross-margin expansion. The preview highlighted possible tariff-related margin pressure, but the reported quarter instead received this sizable refund tailwind; management said the benefit would weigh on the Q3 comparison as it laps.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 100 basis points to 39.5%, including a 90 basis point tailwind from EPA/tariff refunds on Grainger-imported products”; “Q3 operating margin expected to drop to the mid-15% range as tariff refunds lap.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s watch item was “Guidance cadence vs. tariff/cost pressure” and asked whether “tariff-related cost/price timing … resurfaces as a margin risk.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed an unexpected source of High Touch demand: data-center-related projects added about 90 basis points to growth. The revenue benefit came with gross-margin dilution, although management said it was neutral to operating margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center-related project spend added about 90 basis points to High Touch growth this year, boosting revenue but diluting gross margin while remaining neutral to operating margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Segment mix” and “margin implications given differing gross-margin profiles,” but did not identify data-center project spending as a growth driver or describe this gross-margin tradeoff.

surprises.description: Preliminary July sales above 13% daily organic constant currency supported Q3 sales guidance of over $5 billion, up more than 12%. The preview had not specified a Q3 sales outlook, so this added evidence of continuing strong near-term demand beyond the full-year guide increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Preliminary July sales are up north of 13% daily organic constant currency, supporting Q3 guidance of over $5 billion (up over 12%).”

surprises.description: Despite the strong July sales outlook, Q3 operating margin was expected to fall to the mid-15% range as tariff refunds lap, below Q2’s 16.1% margin. The preview discussed margin trajectory but did not flag this specific near-term decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 operating margin expected to drop to the mid-15% range as tariff refunds lap”; Q2 operating margin was “16.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Operating margin trajectory relative to the 15.6%–16.0% FY2026 adjusted guide band,” but gave no Q3 margin expectation.

surprises.description: CFO Deidra Merriwether was set to step down effective September 4, with the controller appointed interim CFO and an external search beginning immediately. The preview did not mention an anticipated CFO transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Deidra Merriwether is stepping down effective September 4, 2026, with VP Controller Laurie Thompson appointed interim CFO and an external search to begin immediately.”

surprises.description: Urban One reported Q2 revenue of about $85.8 million, above the preview’s $83.0 million model, and the year-over-year decline was 6.4% rather than the modeled 9.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated net revenues fell 6.4% year-over-year to approximately $85.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue … Q2'26E (base) $83.0” and “−9.4%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $11.7 million, beating the preview’s $11.0 million estimate despite falling 16% year over year; the preview treated roughly $11 million as the key quarterly hurdle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA declined 16% to $11.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … Q2'26E (base) $11.0” and “Adj. EBITDA vs. ~$11M.”

surprises.description: Cable TV revenue declined 7.4%, a substantially milder drop than the preview’s modeled 15% decline, even though Prime delivery fell 21%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cable Television revenue fell 7.4%, hurt by a 21% year-over-year decline in Prime delivery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Cable TV revenue of “$34.1” million versus “$40.1” million a year earlier, or “−15%.”

surprises.description: TV One’s linear Nielsen subscribers fell to 27.3 million, below the preview’s watch threshold of 28.5 million and down from 29.1 million at Q1; the preview flagged subscriber erosion as a major risk but expected a higher Q2 level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TV One's traditional linear Nielsen subscribers dropped to 27.3 million from 34.3 million a year earlier, reflecting accelerating cord-cutting in linear cable.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TV One subs ≥ 28.5M”; the preview also reported “29.1M Nielsen subs at Q1'26.”

surprises.description: Digital revenue fell 8.4% to $9.4 million instead of reaching the preview’s modeled $10.4 million and flat-to-positive year-over-year performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Digital segment declined 8.4% to $9.4 million, driven by reduced DEI-focused spending and broader macroeconomic caution among clients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Digital at “$10.4” million and “+1%,” and called for “Digital ≥ flat YoY.”

surprises.description: Radio revenue declined less than the preview’s modeled 6.0% overall, but local ad sales were notably weak: down 10.1% and worse than the market’s 7.8% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Radio Broadcasting revenue declined 3.9% year-over-year (down 6.6% excluding political), with local ad sales falling 10.1% and underperforming the market's 7.8% decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Radio Broadcasting at “$34.5” million versus “$36.7” million, or “−6.0%.”

surprises.description: The reported net debt and leverage were higher than the preview’s approximate balance-sheet framing: net debt was about $307.9 million and leverage was 6.66x, versus preview net debt of about $299 million and a base-case leverage estimate of roughly 6x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt stood at approximately $307.9 million against $46.2 million of LTM adjusted EBITDA, resulting in a total leverage ratio of 6.66x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview stated “Net debt ≈ $299M” and described base-case leverage as “still ~6x.”

surprises.description: Management’s political-revenue budget was $11.1 million, below the approximately $13 million achieved in 2022. The preview had highlighted midterm political revenue as a key back-half support, but gave no 2026 dollar estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management budgeted roughly $11.1 million in radio political revenue for the cycle, below the approximately $13 million achieved in 2022.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called “Midterm political (2026) into Q3/Q4 radio” a driver and said the back half was “political-driven.”

surprises.description: Urban One recognized a $3.2 million gain on the $6 million sale of KZMJ, a transaction detail and one-off gain not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sold station KZMJ for $6 million, recognizing a $3.2 million gain.”

in_line: Management lowered FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from $60 million to the mid-$50 million range, in line with the preview’s expectation of a trim to roughly $52–56 million.
The $23.5 million repurchase of 2031 second-lien notes at about 42 cents on the dollar and $4.6 million in annual interest savings were consistent with the preview’s debt-repurchase expectations.
The $22 million Dallas acquisition closed in late July, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would close in late July and contribute nothing to Q2.

surprises.description: FreightCar America cut its FY2026 outlook: deliveries are now 3,500–3,900 versus 4,000–4,500 previously, revenue is $410–$460 million versus $500–$550 million, and adjusted EBITDA is $36–$45 million versus $41–$50 million. Management attributed the reductions to a delayed second-half production ramp that shifts some deliveries into early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company revised full-year guidance downward to 3,500–3,900 deliveries, $410–$460 million revenue, and $36–$45 million adjusted EBITDA because a delayed second-half production ramp shifts some deliveries into early 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed with Q1): 4,000–4,500 deliveries, $500–$550M revenue, $41–$50M adjusted EBITDA, with a back-half-weighted delivery cadence.

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin fell to 5.5%, far below the preview’s focus on whether the exceptional 16.8% Q1 margin could be sustained. Lower deliveries, reduced fixed-cost absorption, and a realignment charge contributed to the decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin was 5.5% ($6.2 million), down from 15% ($17.8 million) a year earlier, driven by lower delivery volumes, reduced fixed cost absorption, and the $2.2 million realignment charge.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Gross margin durability after Q1's decade-high 16.8%, given mix shift toward higher-volume deliveries.

surprises.description: The reported loss was much worse than the preview’s $0.01 EPS consensus: GAAP loss was $0.94 per share, largely due to a non-cash warrant remeasurement, and adjusted results were still a loss of $0.02 per share. The preview had warned that warrant adjustments could distort GAAP results, but the adjusted loss also fell short of the EPS consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported a net loss of $30.1 million ($0.94 per diluted share), largely driven by a $24.9 million non-cash warrant remeasurement loss, versus an adjusted net loss of $0.02 per share.
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS: $0.01 (consensus, per MarketBeat preview published 2026-07-27). The preview also noted: “Warrant-liability noise: Q1 GAAP net income included a $49.1M non-cash warrant adjustment; adjusted (non-GAAP) figures are the cleaner read.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue exceeded the $110.4 million consensus at $113.1 million, and its year-over-year decline was smaller than the preview’s roughly 7% decline implied by consensus. The result was nevertheless below the $118.6 million reported a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue was $113.1 million, compared with $118.6 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue: $110.4 million; vs. $118.6M in Q2 2025 (down ~7% YoY).

surprises.description: Aftermarket revenue was still growing, but its 13% year-over-year increase was a marked slowdown from the 86% growth highlighted for Q1. That is weaker momentum than the preview’s emphasis on continued aftermarket expansion suggested, although management continues to describe it as a growth platform.
surprises.fact_evidence: Aftermarket revenue grew 13% year-over-year and represents roughly 10% of total revenue; management called it a key growth platform after the July acquisition of Southern Parts and Equipment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Aftermarket momentum (86% YoY growth in Q1; two acquisitions in twelve months).

surprises.description: The company disclosed a $2.2 million Q2 charge to structurally realign its Castaños operation, which the preview did not identify. Management expects the action to produce approximately $12 million in annualized savings beginning in Q3, making the news a near-term cost but a substantial prospective benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: A structural realignment of the Castaños operation cost $2.2 million in Q2 and is expected to generate approximately $12 million in annualized cost savings, with benefits beginning in Q3.

surprises.description: Although the approximately 3,000 Q2 orders had already been announced, the company’s reported share of those orders was not: it represented roughly 45% of industry new-railcar orders and about 56% of the addressable market excluding tank cars.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company booked approximately 3,000 units in Q2, including ~2,600 new railcars representing roughly 45% of total industry new railcar orders and about 56% of the addressable market excluding tank cars.
surprises.expectation_evidence: On 2026-07-06 the company announced that Q2 orders totaled approximately 3,000 railcars. “Backlog growth is therefore largely known; the market's focus shifts to deliveries, margin, and guidance.”

surprises.description: A shareholder exercised warrants, sharply reducing the warrant liability and turning stockholders’ equity positive. The company also said this should lower future earnings volatility without incremental EPS dilution; the preview had flagged warrant-related earnings noise but did not anticipate this balance-sheet change.
surprises.fact_evidence: A shareholder's warrant exercise reduced the warrant liability from $119.4 million to $14 million, turned stockholders' equity positive to $36.2 million, and should reduce future earnings volatility without incremental EPS dilution.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Warrant-liability noise: Q1 GAAP net income included a $49.1M non-cash warrant adjustment; adjusted (non-GAAP) figures are the cleaner read.

surprises.description: The company generated $11.3 million of free cash flow, up 43% year over year, while also reducing total debt by about $7.3 million since year-end. The preview cited prior-year operating cash flow but did not flag this level of current-quarter cash generation or debt reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company generated $12.1 million in operating cash flow and $11.3 million in free cash flow (up 43% year-over-year), ended June with $63 million in cash, and reduced total debt by approximately $7.3 million since year-end.

in_line: The approximately 3,000 Q2 orders were already pre-announced in the preview, so the order total itself was not new; the reported industry and addressable-market shares were not previously disclosed.

surprises.description: Powell’s orders and backlog were much stronger than the preview’s discussion of continuing momentum and the previously disclosed data-center award suggested: Q3 orders reached a record $934 million and backlog rose to $2.4 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly new orders of $934 million,” with a “book-to-bill ratio of 3.0x”; backlog reached “a record $2.4 billion,” up $619 million sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited backlog of “$1.8 billion as of Q2 FY2026” and said to watch “order/backlog trajectory” and “any incremental mega-project disclosures” after the previously reported >$400 million data-center award.

surprises.description: Revenue fell short of the preview’s estimate. Domestic revenue grew, but international revenue declined slightly on Canadian softness, leaving total revenue below the forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 revenue was “$312 million,” up 9% year-over-year; domestic revenue rose 12%, while international revenue “fell slightly to $61 million on Canadian softness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $318.3 million | +11.2%” year-over-year; the preview also listed an alternate estimate of “~$321.5 million.”

surprises.description: Reported diluted EPS was below the preview’s consensus estimate, rather than returning to the forecast double-digit growth pace. The comparison is imperfect because the preview specifies adjusted EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net income was $52.2 million, or “$1.42 per diluted share,” versus $48.2 million and $1.32 a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.49,” with “+12.9%” year-over-year growth expected.

surprises.description: Petrochemical revenue weakened substantially instead of showing the stabilization or improvement the preview said investors would watch for after the prior-quarter decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management warned that “petrochemical revenue fell 49%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the petrochemical trend, down 37% year-over-year last quarter, and cited “improving petrochemical activity” as a catalyst and asked whether there were “signs of stabilization.”

surprises.description: The larger backlog was less immediately convertible to revenue than the prior quarter’s mix: about 54% is due to convert over the next 12 months, versus the low-60% range last quarter. That tempers the near-term significance of the order surge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $1.3 billion (about 54%) of backlog is convertible over the next 12 months,” down from the “low 60% range last quarter,” due to the large recent order intake.

surprises.description: Powell disclosed a further capacity expansion beyond the Houston expansion highlighted in the preview: a Board-authorized leased facility of about 300,000 square feet, with total footprint expected to grow more than 20% by fiscal year-end 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Board authorized a “~300,000 sq ft leased facility” available in fiscal Q2/Q3 2027; together with the yard expansion, initiatives will grow total footprint “over 20% by end of fiscal 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “the Houston facility expansion supporting backlog execution” and continued capacity investment, but did not mention this additional leased facility or the projected footprint increase.

surprises.description: Management raised a potential labor constraint for fiscal 2027–2028, an execution risk not identified in the preview’s list of headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management warned that “craft labor availability may become a challenge in fiscal 2027-2028.”

surprises.description: Cash and short-term investments increased materially, alongside strong quarterly operating cash flow, beyond the balance-sheet level cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Powell generated “$100 million of operating cash flow” and ended with “$634 million in cash and short-term investments,” up from $476 million at fiscal year-end 2025; it carries no debt.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a debt-free balance sheet with “$433M cash” as of Q4 FY2025.

in_line: Gross margin was 30.6%, roughly flat year-over-year, consistent with the preview’s account of management expecting margins to remain consistent with prior-year performance.

surprises.description: TransDigm raised its FY26 revenue and EBITDA guidance midpoints by $150 million and $100 million, respectively, and now expects adjusted EPS of $41.04. That is above the prior adjusted-EPS guidance range of $38.83–$40.21, whose midpoint was $39.52.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance,” lifting the midpoint of revenue guidance by $150 million to $10.51 billion and EBITDA as defined by $100 million to $5.52 billion, “with adjusted EPS now expected at $41.04.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY26 company guidance was net sales of $10,300–$10,420 million, adjusted EPS of $38.83–$40.21, and EBITDA As Defined of $5,370–$5,470 million.

surprises.description: Commercial transport aftermarket revenue grew 18%, above the prior high-single-digit to low-double-digit growth outlook. TransDigm responded by raising its commercial aftermarket growth guidance to the low-double-digit range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial transport aftermarket revenue grew 18%,” prompting a raise in commercial aftermarket growth guidance “to the low-double-digit range from the prior high-single-digit to low-double-digit range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guidance assumes high-single to low-double-digit growth”; the preview identified a soft aftermarket number as a particularly damaging outcome.

surprises.description: Commercial OEM growth was stronger than the preview’s low-double-digit to mid-teens outlook, particularly for commercial transport OEM excluding business jets, which grew 25%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial OEM revenue rose ~17% in Q3, with commercial transport OEM (excluding bizjet) up 25%, driven by rising Boeing and Airbus production rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 OEM was +12% (+14% YTD) and guidance assumes low-double-digit to mid-teens.”

surprises.description: Q3 EBITDA margin came in modestly above the preview’s roughly 52.5% estimate and improved sequentially despite substantial acquisition-related dilution. The preview had highlighted margin dilution as a possible source of concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 EBITDA as defined margin was 52.8%, up sequentially from Q2 despite more than 2 percentage points of dilution from recent acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview derived Q3 EBITDA margin of “~52.5%” and described “~190bp of y/y margin dilution” as a likely source of a miss narrative.

surprises.description: The company raised full-year free cash flow guidance by $100 million, from $2.5 billion to approximately $2.6 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow guidance raised to approximately $2.6 billion from $2.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call described the prior full-year free cash flow guidance as $2.5 billion.

surprises.description: TransDigm repurchased about $980 million of shares in Q3, up from the $723 million buyback in Q2 that the preview cited as the recent pace. It also said it retained more than $10 billion of M&A firepower.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased ~800,000 shares for about $980 million” in Q3, bringing year-to-date buybacks to $1.8 billion, while retaining “over $10 billion of M&A firepower.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$723M of buybacks in the quarter” for Q2 and flagged the “Buyback pace after $723M in Q2” as a question to watch.

in_line: The Prince & Izan acquisition was already announced before the release; the call’s approximately $1.1 billion price and approximately $360 million of expected 2026 revenue were broadly consistent with the preview’s deal description.

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was $1.43, below the preview’s $1.48–$1.49 consensus estimate, even though favorable weather and sales growth partly offset cost pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS was $1.43,” down $0.15 year over year, with higher interest expense, higher depreciation/amortization, and lower transmission revenue among the drivers.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $1.48 (Barchart/Yahoo); $1.49 (Zacks).”

surprises.description: Management expects 2026 earnings at the top of the $4.55–$4.75 guidance range. The preview said consensus was already near the top and treated a reaffirmation as the base case, so this is firmer than a plain reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects full-year 2026 earnings to finish at the top end of its $4.55 to $4.75 per share guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 EPS: $4.73 consensus vs. guidance $4.55–$4.75”; the preview said a “plain reaffirm” was neutral-to-negative and highlighted “narrow to upper half” as the stronger outcome.

surprises.description: Weather-normalized sales grew 9.6%, above the preview’s 6%–8% base case and its 8% bull-case threshold. C&I growth of 12.7% was below Q1’s 14.6% pace but remained well above the preview’s bear trigger of deceleration below 8%; residential growth also improved to 5.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Weather-normalized sales grew 9.6% year-over-year, with commercial and industrial sales up 12.7% and residential up 5.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected weather-normalized sales growth of “6–8%”; its bull case required “WN sales ≥8%,” and it called deceleration toward 4% or C&I below about 8% the bear trigger.

surprises.description: Customer growth reached 2.1%, above the midpoint of guidance, and customer/sales growth added about $0.11 of quarter-over-quarter earnings benefit. The preview discussed load growth but did not set an expectation for this customer-growth result or earnings contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer growth reached 2.1%, above the midpoint of guidance,” and customer/sales growth contributed “approximately $0.11 of quarter-over-quarter earnings benefit.”

surprises.description: TSMC announced another $100 billion of Arizona investment, taking its total commitment to $265 billion and expanding plans to as many as 12 fabrication and packaging facilities. The preview discussed the large-load pipeline and semiconductor demand but did not anticipate this specific expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TSMC announced an additional $100 billion Arizona investment, raising its total commitment to $265 billion and expanding plans to up to 12 leading-edge fabrication and packaging facilities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “4.5 GW committed, ~20 GW uncommitted in queue” and said an increase in committed load or a filed tariff would be a “genuine narrative upgrade.”

surprises.description: Although the preview already knew about the planned Cholla coal-to-gas conversion, the call disclosed that it could require roughly $440 million of incremental capital not in current CapEx guidance. It could also provide about 380 MW of dispatchable generation by 2029.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The planned Cholla coal-to-gas conversion could add roughly $440 million of incremental capital investment (mostly in 2027-2028) and provide about 380 MW of dispatchable generation by 2029, and is not yet in current CapEx guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “the July 2, 2026 announcement to convert Cholla units to natural gas, targeting 2029 operation,” but did not give an incremental investment estimate.

surprises.description: Despite the expanded TSMC investment plans, TSMC’s fab electricity contribution was relatively flat year over year, with most of its more-than-1-gigawatt demand ramp still to come and expected to accelerate into next year. That puts much of the anticipated load growth further out than current consumption would suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TSMC's fab electricity contribution has been relatively flat year-over-year,” with the bulk of its “more-than-1-gigawatt demand ramp” still to come and accelerating into next year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified semiconductor and data-center demand as the driver of C&I growth and described a “1.0–1.2 GW first tranche” subscription-model filing as a key watch item, but did not flag flat current fab consumption or this ramp timing.

surprises.description: The company exhausted its existing $900 million ATM program and filed a new $500 million ATM program. The preview said 2026 equity was funded and highlighted possible 2027 equity pre-funding as a concern, but the call facts do not say the new ATM will be used or that additional equity has been issued.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company exhausted its existing $900 million ATM equity program” and “filed a new $500 million ATM program”; it also issued $500 million of senior unsecured notes to refinance maturing debt.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “All 2026 equity is funded” and flagged “2027 equity pre-funding” as something to watch.

in_line: The rate-case schedule remained broadly as previewed: hearings concluded, briefs are due in August and September, and management still expects a final commission decision before year-end, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a late-2026 decision.
The preview explicitly flagged a new all-time peak demand record as an operating metric to watch; the company reported a 9,164 MW record on August 2, more than 500 MW above the prior record.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.83, about 12% above the $1.63 consensus and above the preview’s $1.68–$1.72 whisper range. The preview described $1.63 as a low hurdle, but the reported result cleared even the higher buy-side estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased nearly 30% year-over-year to $1.83.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS **$1.63**”; “Adj. EPS vs. whisper (~$1.68–1.72)”

surprises.description: Timken raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to a $6.05–$6.35 range, with a $6.20 midpoint. That is above the preview’s preferred $6.00–$6.15 range and the existing $6.00 midpoint, rather than merely reaffirming or modestly narrowing the prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $6.05-$6.35 (up $0.20 at midpoint), now implying 16% growth versus the prior 13%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side wants the midpoint lifted toward **$6.00–6.15**”; “A simple reaffirm at $5.75–6.25 … reads as a soft signal.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 19.6%, above the preview’s estimated 18.3%–18.8% range. Organic incremental margins also exceeded 40% even excluding the tariff-refund benefit, showing stronger operating leverage than the preview’s margin estimates implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 19.6% from 17.7% a year ago, with organic incremental margins exceeding 40% even excluding the tariff refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin (my est.) ~18.3–18.8%.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales were about $1.26 billion, roughly 2% above the $1.233 billion consensus, and grew 7.5% rather than the 5.2% implied by consensus. Organic growth was 4.4%, driven by pricing and volume across both segments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total sales rose 7.5% year-over-year to $1.26 billion, with organic revenue growth of 4.4% driven by higher pricing and volume across both segments.”

surprises.description: A $0.08-per-share benefit from $8 million of IEEPA tariff refunds contributed to Q2 adjusted EPS. The preview discussed tariff costs and pricing but did not anticipate a refund benefit in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased nearly 30% year-over-year to $1.83, including an $0.08 net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds ($8 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$20M of tariff cost ate the pricing benefit”; “Price covers tariffs roughly one-for-one.”

surprises.description: Industrial Motion posted record sales of $454 million, up 14.6%, and a 23.3% EBITDA margin. The preview expected growth above Q1’s 12% and identified margins above 22% as a bull-case outcome; the reported segment result exceeded both markers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial Motion posted record quarterly sales of $454 million (up 14.6%) with EBITDA margins of 23.3%, up 500 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IM revenue growth should exceed Q1's +12%”; bull scenario: “IM >22% on full-quarter Bijur.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the belts divestiture to raise Industrial Motion’s margin but did not quantify the effect. Management said the transaction should improve pro forma Industrial Motion EBITDA margins by more than 200 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending belts divestiture, expected to close in Q3, is projected to structurally improve Industrial Motion EBITDA margins by more than 200 basis points on a pro forma basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The belts divestiture closes in Q3, removing revenue and EPS while raising margin.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year organic revenue growth outlook to 3.5% at the midpoint, up 1.5 percentage points. The preview cited full-year revenue guidance of about 5% but did not anticipate this increase in the organic-growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year organic revenue guidance was raised to 3.5% at the midpoint (up 1.5 points).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~+5% at midpoint.”

surprises.description: Second-half guidance includes a $0.10-per-share headwind, mostly for strategic investment and added aerospace and defense headcount. The preview instead identified a $0.10 inflation contingency and suggested it might be released in the bull case, so the reported use of that amount for investment was a different and less favorable earnings bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management embedded a $0.10 EPS headwind in second-half guidance, mostly tied to strategic investments in aerospace and defense operations to add operative headcount amid a growing backlog with book-to-bill well above 1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $0.10 inflation contingency embedded in guidance is released” in the bull case.

surprises.description: Management reported a growing aerospace and defense backlog with book-to-bill well above 1, providing a stronger demand signal than the preview could confirm when it asked whether backlog had grown again.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A growing backlog with book-to-bill well above 1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “What matters is whether backlog again grew sequentially and YoY (off-highway, aerospace, rail, wind led in Q1).”

surprises.description: The company raised its quarterly dividend by 3%, repurchased about 155,000 shares, and returned $45 million to shareholders. The preview said a buyback announcement alongside the belts divestiture would be a positive surprise; the call also reported a dividend increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its quarterly dividend by 3%, repurchased about 155,000 shares, returned $45 million to shareholders, and ended the quarter with net leverage at 2x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A buyback announcement alongside [the belts divestiture] would be a positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Automation and robotics grew mid-teens, while strategic verticals collectively delivered high-single-digit organic growth. The preview discussed selected end-market questions but did not anticipate this reported strength across these activities.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Automation and robotics grew mid-teens year-over-year while strategic verticals collectively delivered high-single-digit organic growth.”

in_line: The belts divestiture remained on track for an expected Q3 close.

The second-half organic-growth step-down was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of 2.5%–3% back-half organic growth; management attributed it to seasonality, tougher pricing comparisons, and ramping-down belt sales.

surprises.description: Westlake’s $3.3 billion of Q2 net sales came in above the preview’s $3.244–3.25 billion consensus range, despite the preview expecting the company to miss revenue consensus again. It also exceeded the preview’s $3.05–3.10 billion working estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Westlake reported Q2 2026 net sales of $3.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Revenue $3.244–3.25B”; the preview also modeled “~$3.05–3.10B revenue” and said Westlake had missed revenue consensus in all eight prior quarters.

surprises.description: PEM EBITDA was far stronger than the preview’s $230–290 million estimate: it reached $416 million, with a sharp sequential recovery as average sales prices rose and North American natural gas and ethane costs fell.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The PEM segment's EBITDA jumped to $416 million,” up $380 million sequentially, “driven by a 21% sequential rise in average sales price and lower North American natural gas and ethane costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled PEM at “$230–290M adj. EBITDA” and said “Anything above ~$250M validates the price-increase realization story.”

surprises.description: HIP’s Q2 revenue and EBITDA both beat the preview’s model: revenue was $1.3 billion rather than $1.10–1.15 billion, and EBITDA was $276 million rather than $225–240 million. The 22% margin was also above the preview’s modeled ~20%, although it was down from 24% a year earlier amid lower prices and freight and raw-material inflation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HIP revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $1.3 billion,” while EBITDA was “$276 million”; EBITDA margin was 22%, versus 24% a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “$1.10–1.15B sales, ~20% adj. EBITDA margin → ~$225–240M.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag an Epoxy turnaround, but Westlake said the business—previously losing more than $100 million annually—was profitable in Q2 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The formerly loss-making Epoxy business turned around from annual losses exceeding $100 million to profitability in Q2 2026.”

surprises.description: Management identified a Q3 pipe-volume headwind the preview had not anticipated: some customers pulled Q3 demand into Q2 to secure supply amid the Middle East conflict.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Some Q3 pipe demand was pulled forward into Q2 as customers secured supply amid the Middle East conflict, implying a modest headwind to Q3 pipe volumes.”

surprises.description: Westlake returned about $100 million to shareholders, including $30 million of buybacks. The preview highlighted balance-sheet and leverage concerns and expected $500 million of note repayment, but did not flag buybacks or this additional shareholder return.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company retired $500 million of 2026 notes and returned about $100 million to shareholders (dividends plus $30 million of buybacks).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Free cash flow and the balance sheet” as a key metric and said “$500M was called for Q2 repayment.”

in_line: Westlake reaffirmed its $600 million full-year profitability-plan target; the preview expected that target to be reaffirmed.

The HIP full-year guidance remained within the previously stated $4.4–4.6 billion revenue and 19–21% EBITDA-margin ranges, with management pointing toward the lower end, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the guide was already at the lower end.

The $500 million note retirement was expected in the preview, and the Wilhelmshaven acquisition had already closed before the release; its more meaningful earnings contribution beginning in 2027 was consistent with the preview’s framing.

surprises.description: Accel’s first Chicago locations are expected to open within weeks, much earlier than the preview’s base case of late 2026 or Q1 2027. The company has already been approved for 17 of 39 establishment licenses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “approved for 17 of 39 (approximately 44%) of Chicago establishment licenses” and “expects the first Chicago locations to begin operating within weeks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected Chicago to be reiterated at “late 2026 / Q1 2027”; the preview also noted an earlier “late 2026 or the first quarter of 2027” timeline.

surprises.description: Revenue was about 3% above the preview’s $356.5–356.7 million estimate, with growth of 10% rather than the expected 6.1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% year-over-year to a record $368 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $356.5–356.7M” and “+6.1%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $59 million, above the preview’s derived $55–56 million estimate, and the implied margin was about 16.0%, recovering above the expected 15.5–15.7% range. This is a stronger recovery than the base case’s expected margin stabilization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 11% to a record $59 million” on revenue of $368 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA: ~$55–56M” and “Adj. EBITDA margin ~15.5%”; its base case expected the margin to “stabilize but doesn't expand.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.15, below the preview’s $0.18 GAAP estimate despite nearly doubled net income. The call cited a $2.5 million noncash warehouse-equipment disposal charge and a $5 million noncash mark-to-market loss on earn-out shares, neither of which reduced adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS came in at $0.15”; net income was “$13 million from $7 million”; reported income included “a ~$2.5 million charge to dispose of legacy warehouse equipment and a $5 million mark-to-market loss on Class A-2 earn-out shares,” neither affecting adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s consensus table gave “GAAP diluted EPS: $0.18.”

surprises.description: Illinois hold-per-day increased 9% to $992 even as location and terminal counts declined modestly, a stronger hold result than the preview’s concern about possible hold-per-day deceleration. However, Illinois distributed gaming revenue growth excluding Fairmount was 6%, below the 8.3% growth cited for Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Illinois distributed gaming revenue (excluding Fairmount Park) grew 6% year-over-year with average location hold-per-day up 9% to $992,” despite modest declines in location and terminal counts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for any hold-per-day deceleration” and cited Illinois growth of “+8.3% in Q1.”

surprises.description: Nebraska and Georgia sustained very high growth and, according to management, became meaningful contributors to earnings growth rather than remaining only revenue-growth stories. That is better than the preview’s identified risk that their growth could normalize toward 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nebraska and Georgia posted revenue growth of 55% and 47% respectively, and are now meaningful contributors to earnings growth rather than just revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “Any sign of these normalizing to +20% resets the growth narrative.”

surprises.description: Nevada’s rapid expansion came with a sharp decline in blended hold-per-day: revenue rose 17%, but hold-per-day fell 15.8% as locations and terminals expanded by more than 50%. The preview had flagged the need to distinguish unit growth from hold, but did not anticipate this degree of hold dilution or the 6–12 month upgrade transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nevada revenue grew 17% year-over-year with locations and terminals up 54% and 53%, but blended hold-per-day fell 15.8%” due to rapid convenience-store expansion; a “6- to 12-month upgrade transition” is underway.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Distinguish price/hold from unit adds — unit-driven growth is lower quality.”

surprises.description: Reported operating cash flow was only $20 million, or 34% of EBITDA, which tempers the preview’s expectation that lower capex would produce a meaningful free-cash-flow inflection. Management said conversion would have been $37 million, or 63%, excluding a $17 million green tax credit purchase that shifts cash into Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating cash flow was $20 million (34% EBITDA conversion) but $37 million (63%) excluding a $17 million green tax credit purchase shifting cash into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the capex step-down “should be a meaningful FCF inflection” and listed “Free cash flow and buyback pace” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Management said it would detail a permanent casino development plan for Fairmount Park over the next quarter or two, an additional development initiative not anticipated in the preview. The call provided no plan details or financial estimates, so the shareholder implications are not yet clear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fairmount Park delivered its highest quarterly gross profit since acquisition,” up 33% year over year, with “a permanent casino development plan to be detailed over the next quarter or two.”

in_line: Full-year capex guidance remained $60–70 million, consistent with the preview’s stated FY26 guidance and expected step-down from approximately $89 million in 2025.
Net leverage remained about 1.4x, in line with the preview’s stated 1.4x leverage.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in at $308 million, above the preview’s $295.5 million consensus and its own roughly $288 million estimate. That is a clear top-line beat versus the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues of $308 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 2026E | $295.5M”; “My estimate: revenue ~$288M”

surprises.description: DAYBUE sales reached $125 million, well above the preview’s implied $112–115 million expectation. The company also raised its 2026 DAYBUE outlook rather than merely reaffirming it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DAYBUE net sales reached $125 million in Q2”; “raised its 2026 DAYBUE guidance to $480-510 million (from $460-490 million)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “DAYBUE net sales | ~$112–115M (implied)”; “FY26 guidance action. Reaffirm / narrow to lower half / cut”; “a narrow to the upper half would be a genuine positive surprise”

surprises.description: The company raised total 2026 revenue guidance to $1.24–1.30 billion, above the prior $1.22–1.28 billion range. The preview treated reaffirmation as the base case, so the increase is better than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “total 2026 revenue is guided at $1.24-1.3 billion”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: total revenue $1.22–1.28B”; “a reaffirm is base case”

surprises.description: DAYBUE STIX adoption showed substantial reach: about 40% of U.S. DAYBUE patients were receiving it, and it represented roughly 60% of June referrals. The preview identified STIX conversion as a key debate but did not anticipate adoption at these levels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 40% of all U.S. DAYBUE patients were receiving STIX by the end of Q2, and STIX accounted for roughly 60% of all referrals in June alone.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “DAYBUE unique patients on drug + STIX conversion”; “Look for STIX as a % of total scripts and any update to persistency curves.”

surprises.description: The pivotal RADIANT readout window moved from August–October to September–October 2026, reducing the chance of an August result and shifting the earliest expected timing later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pivotal Phase II RADIANT readout … is now expected in September to October 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Phase 2 topline in Alzheimer's disease psychosis, guided for August–October 2026”

surprises.description: ACADIA gave a more specific and earlier European commercialization timeline than the preview’s 2027 launch framing: it expects a European Commission decision in Q3 and plans a Germany launch in early Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a final European Commission decision anticipated in Q3 and a Germany launch planned for early Q4”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for 2027 launch framing and whether ex-U.S. gets folded into guidance.”

surprises.description: R&D guidance fell to $355–380 million from $385–410 million, rather than following the preview’s expected steep spending trajectory. The reduction is partly a timing shift, with a BD milestone moving to 2027, and partly portfolio prioritization, so the lower expense outlook has a mixed implication.
surprises.fact_evidence: “lowered its full-year 2026 R&D expense guidance to $355-380 million (from $385-410 million), primarily due to a BD milestone shifting to 2027 and portfolio prioritization”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 R&D was $76.9M against FY guidance of $385–410M — implying ~$103–111M per quarter for the rest of the year”; “R&D step-up quantified”

surprises.description: NUPLAZID sales were broadly in line with the preview’s implied $180–183 million range, but new-patient prescriptions rose 20% and reached their highest quarterly volume since Q1 2018. That prescription momentum was stronger than the preview’s stated expectation of a recovery and an initial contribution from the expanded sales force.
surprises.fact_evidence: “new patient prescriptions up 20% year-over-year to the highest quarterly volume since Q1 2018”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NUPLAZID net sales | ~$180–183M (implied)”; “the 30% sales-force expansion completed in Q1 should start contributing”

surprises.description: Management introduced an estimated $4 billion peak-sales opportunity for remlifanserin across Alzheimer’s disease psychosis and Lewy body dementia psychosis, split roughly 60%/40%. The preview discussed the upcoming ADP trial but did not provide or anticipate this broader commercial opportunity estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remlifanserin has estimated peak sales potential of $4 billion across Alzheimer's disease psychosis and Lewy body dementia psychosis, with management splitting the opportunity roughly 60% ADP and 40% Lewy body.”

surprises.description: Management said potential first-generation gene therapies would not affect DAYBUE’s commercial forecast in either the short or long term. This was an unanticipated reassurance about a competitive issue not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “management stated it does not expect potential first-generation gene therapies to impact DAYBUE's commercial forecast in the short or long term.”

in_line: NUPLAZID Q2 net sales of $183 million were within the preview’s implied $180–183 million range, and its 10% adjusted year-over-year growth was close to the preview’s roughly 8% growth expectation.

surprises.description: Revenue was about $75 million, far above both the preview’s $44.17 million consensus and its own $48–53 million estimate. The call attributed the increase to collaboration agreements and REDEMPLO sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net loss widened to $194.3 million ($1.36/share) from $175.2 million ($1.26/share) a year earlier, while total revenue rose to ~$75 million from $28 million driven by collaboration agreements and REDEMPLO sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FQ3 FY26 Consensus” revenue: “$44.17M”; “My estimates: Revenue $48–53M.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue beat, the loss was larger than expected: the $1.36 per-share loss was worse than the preview’s $1.2767 consensus and its own $1.15–$1.20 estimate, while the $194.3 million net loss exceeded its roughly $180 million implied estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net loss widened to $194.3 million ($1.36/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS: -$1.2767”; “Implied net loss: ~-$180M”; “My estimates: … EPS -$1.15 to -$1.20.”

surprises.description: The call reported larger and more complete SHASTA efficacy results than the preview’s broad characterization that the July topline had de-risked sHTG expansion: both Phase III studies met every prespecified endpoint, with 79% and 81% median triglyceride reductions versus about 27% for placebo.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 Phase III studies both met their primary endpoint and every prespecified secondary endpoint, with median triglyceride reductions from baseline of 79% and 81% respectively versus ~27% for placebo at month 12.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “July 22's SHASTA-3/SHASTA-4 Phase 3 topline … de-risked the sHTG expansion before the print.”

surprises.description: The call added a substantial pancreatitis outcome not highlighted in the preview: plozasiran reduced cumulative acute pancreatitis events by 78% overall and by 100% in the highest-risk subgroup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the pooled analysis, plozasiran reduced cumulative acute pancreatitis events by 78% versus placebo, and by 100% in the highest-risk subgroup.”

surprises.description: Arrowhead disclosed an unpreviewed $215 million purchase of an FDA priority review voucher, which it expects to cut sNDA review from 10 months to 6 months and support a potential accelerated launch in Q2 2027. Management projected a greater than 3x return on the investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Arrowhead acquired an FDA priority review voucher for $215 million … to shorten the sNDA review from 10 months to 6 months, with management projecting a greater than 3x return”; it “targets a potential accelerated launch in the second quarter of 2027.”

surprises.description: REDEMPLO quarterly revenue came in slightly below the preview’s $2.5–3.5 million estimate, at approximately $2.4 million. Prescriptions more than doubled quarter-on-quarter, but the stated 20–30 new prescriptions per week was at or below the preview’s roughly 30-per-week expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “REDEMPLO commercial revenue reached approximately $2.4 million for the quarter … with prescriptions more than doubling quarter-on-quarter at a run rate of 20-30 new prescriptions per week.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At ~265 average patients on therapy × $45K × ~70–75% net, I model ~$2.5–3.5M”; “At ~30 Rx/week for 13 weeks.”

surprises.description: Management put the sHTG peak-sales opportunity at $3–4 billion annually, above the preview’s roughly $3 billion market framing at the upper end, and said the overwhelming majority would be in the United States.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates the sHTG indication could drive peak sales of $3 billion to $4 billion per year, with the overwhelming majority in the United States.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “a ~$3B sHTG market” and a “~$3B sHTG opportunity.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed that the sHTG sNDA is expected before the end of 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation that filing timing would be confirmed for before year-end.
ARO-MAPT data were scheduled for September, within the preview’s expected 2H26 window.
The $45,000 per-patient annual U.S. REDEMPLO WAC was unchanged, as the preview already noted that price.

surprises.description: Alight reported Q2 revenue of $511 million, above both the $490–505 million company guide and the roughly $495–497 million consensus range. The beat was modest in percentage terms, but it cleared the top of the stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue of $511 million exceeded market expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $494.9M”; company guidance was “$490–505M.”

surprises.description: Alight reinstated full-year 2026 guidance, whereas the preview highlighted that it had withheld guidance since February and considered no reinstatement a plausible base case. Its $400–415 million adjusted EBITDA range is also above the preview’s $380–400 million estimate, though the ranges meet at $400 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $2.078-2.098 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $400-415 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Alight has withheld FY guidance since February”; the base scenario allowed “no FY26 reinstatement or only a vague FCF framework.” The preview estimated FY26 adjusted EBITDA at “~$380–400M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $92 million, above the preview’s $80–90 million company guide and its roughly $85 million midpoint. The 18% margin was also above the preview’s 17.1% midpoint estimate, although EBITDA and margin remained sharply lower year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $92 million at an 18% margin, down sharply from $127 million and a 24% margin in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is guided to $80–90M / ~16–18%”; the preview described the midpoint as an “17.1% margin.”
