surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.91 exceeded the preview’s $0.69–0.75 estimate range, despite falling substantially from the prior-year period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS dropped to $0.91 from $2.09 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.75”; the preview also cited an estimate of “$0.69” from another source.

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA is projected at only $55–61 million, below Q2’s $92 million, so Q2 was not the quarterly EBITDA trough. The preview specifically framed whether Q2 was the trough as a key question; the call attributed Q3 weakness to annual enrollment expenses and implied a Q4 rebound.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $469-479 million and adjusted EBITDA of just $55-61 million due to annual enrollment expenses, implying a significant Q4 rebound.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The single most important disclosure is whether Q2 is the trough.” The bull scenario required “Q2 confirmed as margin trough.”

surprises.description: The projected full-year free-cash-flow conversion of 40–43% of EBITDA is below the preview’s stated long-run conversion range of 44–50%. At the newly guided EBITDA level, that conversion range implies roughly $160–179 million of FCF, below the preview’s $175–195 million estimate at the upper portion of the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow conversion is expected to be roughly 40-43% of EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had framed long-run conversion at “44–50% of adj. EBITDA”; the preview said, “If FY26 FCF holds near $175–195M.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $48 million, above the preview’s $35–45 million Q2 guide, providing a positive quarterly cash-flow result even though the full-year conversion outlook was lower than the preview’s benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$101 million generated year-to-date including $48 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guide is $35–45M for Q2.”

surprises.description: Recurring revenue fell 4.3% year over year, a slight worsening from the 4% decline cited for Q1 rather than an improvement in the decline rate. The preview flagged the rate of recurring-revenue decline as a key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue fell 4.3% year-over-year due to weak commercial execution in 2025 and prior, with a 12-18 month lag before commercial activity flows through the P&L.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said recurring revenue was “−4% YoY” in Q1 and flagged whether “the rate of decline” was worsening.

surprises.description: The reported call facts provide no quantified renewal or retention rate, despite the preview identifying a hard renewal-rate disclosure as a key item investors would look for. The preview explicitly warned that silence on this issue would be read negatively.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call facts provided include no hard renewal or retention-rate figure.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Look for a hard renewal-rate number” and that “Silence here is not neutral; it will be read as bad.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was $215 million, $37 million above the $178 million cash balance cited in the preview; total liquidity was consequently $545 million versus $508 million implied by the preview’s cash and revolver figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company exited the quarter with $545 million in total liquidity ($215 million cash and $330 million undrawn revolver).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$178M cash + $330M undrawn revolver.”

surprises.description: The account-executive coverage expansion was reported as 100 to 500 clients, exceeding the preview’s stated plan of expanding coverage from the top 100 to 400 accounts. The client and account descriptions may not be perfectly comparable, but the reported coverage count is higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Account executive coverage was expanded from 100 to 500 clients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “expanded strategic account coverage (top 100 → 400 accounts covering 90%+ of ARR).”

in_line: The dividend had already been eliminated before this release, so its continued absence was not new; the preview also noted that no buybacks had occurred in Q1 and identified debt paydown and capital allocation as items to watch.

Management’s explanation that prior commercial-execution failures were still weighing on results was consistent with the preview’s expectation that those headwinds would continue to flow through the P&L.
The multi-year turnaround and AI narrative broadly matched the preview’s strategic watch list, which included whether commercial execution could support a 2027 recovery and AI-driven margin benefits.

surprises.description: EVTC reported Q2 revenue of about $275 million, above the preview’s working consensus of $262–265 million. That is a stronger result than the expected 14–15% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached approximately $275 million, up 20% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working assumption for this note: consensus revenue ≈ $262–265M (+14–15% y/y).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.05, well above the preview’s $0.95 consensus (and $0.92 alternative). The 18% year-over-year increase also exceeded the preview’s roughly 7% expected growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 18% to $1.05 from $0.89, benefiting from higher earnings and a reduced share count from buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.95 (alt. $0.92)” and “Implied y/y +6.7%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $109 million versus the preview’s estimate of about $103 million. Its 18% growth was also stronger than the preview’s modeled 11% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 18% to approximately $109 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$103M (my est.)” and “Implied y/y +11%.”

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA margin came in at 39.8%, above the preview’s modeled roughly 39.2% and the 39.0–39.5% base-case range, despite the lower-margin Latin America mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 39.8% from 40.3% a year ago due to the growing lower-margin Latin America mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ~39.2% (my est.)” and base case “39.0–39.5%.”

surprises.description: Latin America Payments and Solutions grew faster than the preview’s roughly 40% reported-growth base case: revenue rose 52%, or 42% in constant currency. The preview had identified Latin America constant-currency growth as a key debate, although the call facts do not separate organic growth from acquisition contributions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Latin America Payments and Solutions revenue surged 52% year-over-year to $131 million (42% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “LatAm +40% reported,” and the preview ranked “LatAm organic constant-currency growth” as the top metric to watch.

surprises.description: Business Solutions fell 9%, rather than improving to the roughly 5% decline the preview said Q2 needed to achieve. The Popular discount headwind is still expected to anniversary in Q4, as anticipated, but the segment’s Q2 decline was weaker than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business Solutions revenue fell 9% to $59 million due to the 10% Popular contract discount.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 must improve to ~−5%”; the preview also said the Popular 10% discount “anniversaries in October 2026.”

surprises.description: EVTC raised its FY2026 revenue range to $1.085–$1.095 billion, above the preview’s cited $1.073–$1.085 billion range. The new midpoint is higher, rather than the reaffirmation or narrowing the preview treated as the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.085–$1.095 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY26 revenue guidance of “$1.073–1.085B” and said the base case was “FY guide reaffirmed/narrowed.”

surprises.description: The new FY2026 adjusted EPS growth outlook of 8.8–11.7% implies roughly $3.94–$4.04 per share, above the preview’s modeled guide range of $3.86–$3.98 and $3.92 consensus. The raised outlook also runs counter to the preview’s concern that deal-related costs would restrain EPS growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS growth of 8.8%–11.7% from $3.62 in 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled FY26 adjusted EPS at “$3.92” consensus and an expected guide range of “$3.86–3.98.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s question about whether leverage would slow repurchases, EVTC bought back about 2 million shares for $47 million and replenished its authorization to $150 million. That was a faster quarterly repurchase pace than the Q1 pace cited in the preview, alongside a new dividend payment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately 2 million shares for $47 million during the quarter, paid $3 million in dividends, and the board replenished the buyback authorization to $150 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked, “Does buyback pace slow?” after citing Q1 repurchases of “683k shares / $20M” and $130M left on authorization.

surprises.description: EVTC disclosed a multi-year Transbank agreement, with results expected to begin being affected in the second half of 2027 and the merchant migration fully ramping in 2028. The preview did not flag this agreement or its future contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The multi-year Transbank agreement in Chile—one of the largest acquirers in Latin America—is expected to begin impacting results in the second half of 2027 and fully ramp in 2028 as a migration of the existing merchant base.”

surprises.description: Management said AI-driven efficiency benefits are expected to be incorporated into the financial outlook starting in 2027, a potential future contributor the preview did not discuss. No benefit amount was provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects AI-driven efficiency benefits to be incorporated into financial outlook starting in 2027.”

surprises.description: The preview specifically called for financial quantification of cybersecurity-related costs, but the call facts only say remediation costs were incurred and provide no amount. The incident did not disrupt operations, consistent with the preview’s expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management disclosed a June cybersecurity incident that incurred remediation costs but did not disrupt operations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Data breach financial quantification” and said this was the first quarter in which remediation and related costs would hit the P&L.

in_line: Net debt leverage was 2.55x, close to the preview’s expectation of approximately 2.5x post-Dimensa.
The Popular discount headwind is expected to anniversary in Q4 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it anniversaries in October.
The cybersecurity incident did not disrupt operations, as the preview had said no operational disruption was reported.

surprises.description: The preview treated roughly 10.6% organic growth as embedded in consensus and said growth below 11% would break the double-digit-growth thesis. Crexendo reported only 7% consolidated organic growth for Q2, although year-to-date organic growth was 11%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated organic growth was only 7% for the quarter (11% year-to-date).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus appears to embed a deceleration to ~10–11% organic”; “sub-11% breaks the ‘double-digit organic’ thesis.”

surprises.description: The preview expected gross margin to be challenged by ESI hardware mix and looked for at least 61%; instead, consolidated gross margin rose to 66%. Software solutions margin also reached 70%, above the preview’s noted 68% level, while product margin improved to 44% from 31% in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin improved 500 basis points sequentially to 66%, with software solutions at 70% … and product at 44%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side wants consolidated GM held at/above 61%”; “software solutions GM extending above 68% is the bull’s evidence.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS came in above both estimates cited in the preview: $0.12 versus consensus of $0.08 and an alternate tracked estimate of $0.10.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income reached $4.1 million ($0.12 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (non-GAAP) $0.08”; “EPS (alt. tracked estimate) $0.10.”

surprises.description: ESI contributed $6.9 million in Q2, above the preview’s roughly $6.3 million full-quarter expectation, with monthly revenue averaging $2.3 million after $2.1 million in March.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ESI acquisition contributed $6.9 million in Q2 revenue, growing from $2.1 million in March to an average of $2.3 million per month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ESI full quarter” base estimate of “$6.3M”; the preview said a full quarter materially below ~$6.2M would imply attrition.

surprises.description: Revenue was essentially in line with the stated consensus, but it fell short of the preview’s working base case and expected modest beat: $24.6 million versus a $25.2 million base estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 49% year-over-year to $24.6 million, beating top-line analyst expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s revenue bridge gave a “Base” total of “$25.2M” and said the base scenario involved a “modest revenue beat.” It also listed consensus of $24.63M.

surprises.description: The preview warned that cash was only $7.2 million and questioned whether the company could fund more M&A without an equity raise. Cash was $18.3 million at quarter-end, and year-to-date operating cash flow reached $4.8 million, up 89%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $18.3 million in cash … while generating $4.8 million in operating cash flow year-to-date, up 89%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Cash $7.2M” and said to watch for “equity-raise hints”; its bear scenario expected cash to remain “~$7M with no FCF inflection.”

surprises.description: RPO increased sequentially rather than remaining flat or declining, the trajectory the preview identified as a potential warning sign. The increase was modest relative to the year-over-year surge, but it provided a positive update on the flagged metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligation surged 97% year-over-year to $139 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Flat-to-down sequential RPO would be the first real crack” and that “Sequential direction matters more than the level.”

surprises.description: The preview said a quantified CAIRO contribution would be a positive surprise. Management gave a concrete figure: about $120 per account per month, equal to a 35% increase over a typical Telecom Services customer’s $340 average revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new CAIRO AI receptionist product added an average of ~$120 per account per month, a 35% increase over the typical Telecom Services customer's $340 average revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any hard number here is a positive surprise”; the preview also cited a claimed “25–40% ARPU uplift” and said Q2 was the first quarter where an actual dollar contribution could be quantified.

surprises.description: Crexendo reported 11 new platform logos in the first half, versus 2 in the same period of 2025, including five named migration wins. The preview flagged logos and migrations as leading indicators but did not set a numerical expectation for the first half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured 11 new platform logos in the first half of 2026 versus only 2 in the same period of 2025, with 4 of the 11 being Metaswitch migrations plus one Cisco BroadSoft migration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “New logos, Metaswitch migrations, TSD/channel bookings” as leading indicators and cited Q1’s 5 new logos, including two Metaswitch migrations.

surprises.description: Perpetual license revenue declined by $700,000 from the prior-year quarter as new licensees chose smaller initial orders and larger orders came later through upgrades. The preview discussed prior-quarter upgrade orders and strong product growth, but did not anticipate or forecast this license-revenue decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Perpetual license revenue fell $700,000 versus the prior-year quarter, as new licensees opted for smaller initial orders (~$250,000) with upgrade orders averaging 50% higher (~$300,000-$350,000).”

in_line: Headline revenue of $24.6 million was essentially equal to the stated $24.63 million consensus, despite being below the preview’s $25.2 million working base case.
GAAP EPS of $0.03 was within the preview’s modeled $0.03–$0.05 range.
Adjusted EBITDA of $4.1 million at a 17% margin was within the preview’s $4.0–$4.5 million and 16–18% base-case ranges.

Management reaffirmed the $100 million year-end 2026 revenue-run-rate goal and indicated that further M&A could occur in Q4 2026 or early 2027, broadly addressing the preview’s target and acquisition questions.

surprises.description: Marqeta guided to a much sharper Q3 slowdown than the preview’s implied H2 gross-profit path: Q3 net revenue growth is expected at 6%–8% and gross profit growth at 5%–7%, roughly a 10-point step down from Q2. The preview had estimated H2 gross profit growth at roughly 7%–9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for a sharp deceleration to 6%-8% net revenue growth and 5%-7% gross profit growth, about a 10-point step down from Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year guidance of 10–12% gross profit growth against Q2 guidance of 14–16% mathematically implies H2 gross profit growth decelerating to roughly 7–9%.”

surprises.description: The Cash App new-issuance decline is expected to become more severe and persistent than the preview’s roughly 1.5% full-year headwind framing: Marqeta expects little to no new issuance by year-end and estimates about a 2-point second-half gross-profit growth drag. Management also said the run-rate impact could exceed 2 points in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marqeta began seeing a modest decline in Cash App new issuance around mid-June (roughly 10% below expected), stepping up in July,” and expects “little to no new issuance by year-end” with an “estimated ~2 point second-half gross profit growth drag.” The diversification could “exceed a 2-point growth impact in 2027 on a run-rate basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided new issuances down in Q2 and ‘more in the second half,’ and cut the FY gross profit headwind estimate from ~2% to ~1.5%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA materially exceeded expectations, growing 31% to $37 million versus the preview’s roughly $32 million estimate and 10%–12% growth guide. The 21% net-revenue margin also contrasted with the preview’s expectation of year-over-year margin contraction to about 18.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 31% year-over-year to $37 million (21% net revenue margin, 31% gross profit margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: $29M (19.3% mgn)”; Q2 guide “+10–12% → $31.9–32.5M”; “margin contracts y/y — from 19.3% to ~18.6%.”

surprises.description: Marqeta raised its full-year profitability outlook substantially: adjusted EBITDA growth is now expected in the low 30s and GAAP net income in the high $20 millions, versus the preview’s mid-to-high-20s EBITDA growth and approximately $15 million of net income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marqeta raised its full-year outlook, now expecting adjusted EBITDA growth in the low 30s and GAAP net income in the high $20 millions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … adj. EBITDA growth mid-to-high 20s%, GAAP net income ~ $15M.”

surprises.description: The annual revenue and gross-profit outlook was mixed rather than a clear broad-based raise: revenue growth guidance was narrowed to 12%–13%, lowering its upper end from 14%, while gross-profit growth guidance moved to 11%–12%, lifting its lower end by one point but leaving the top unchanged. The preview had identified a gross-profit raise, particularly above 12%, as the bullish outcome investors wanted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Narrowing revenue growth guidance to 12%-13% and gross profit growth to 11%-12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … net revenue +12–14% … gross profit +10–12%”; “The buy-side wants management raising the FY gross profit range”; a “12%+” gross-profit guide was part of the bull scenario.

surprises.description: Q2 TPV reached $120 billion and grew 32%, above the preview’s estimated $116–118 billion and 28%–30% growth. That also delivered a fourth consecutive quarter above 30%, which the preview said would be a genuine surprise given the comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 TPV reached $120 billion, growing 32% year-over-year, marking the fourth consecutive quarter above 30% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TPV … ~$116–118B (+28–30%) est.” and “a fourth straight quarter above 30% would be a genuine surprise given the comp.”

surprises.description: Q2 net revenue and gross profit both came in above the preview’s reference points: net revenue was $176 million versus $172.9 million consensus, while gross profit was $122 million versus an estimated $119–121 million and a 14%–16% guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit grew 17% to $122 million and net revenue grew 17% to $176 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue … Consensus $172.9M (+15.0%)”; gross profit consensus “~$119–121M (derived)” and Q2 guide “+14–16%.”

surprises.description: Marqeta reported a second consecutive profitable quarter, with approximately $8 million of GAAP net income, above the preview’s approximately breakeven expectation and $0–5 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income was approximately $8 million ($0.07 EPS), the company's second consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP net income … ~Breakeven”; consensus “~$0–5M.”

surprises.description: The average deal size signed in Q2 rose more than 90% year over year, an unexpectedly strong sign of progress in Marqeta’s move toward larger enterprise and Fortune 500 customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The average deal size signed in Q2 rose over 90% year-over-year,” reflecting a shift toward “larger, more established enterprise and Fortune 500 customers.”

surprises.description: Marqeta largely exhausted its existing $100 million repurchase authorization in Q2 and approved a further $150 million buyback, a larger concrete capital-return commitment than the preview had specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 3.2 million shares at an average post-split price of $15.90 in Q2, largely exhausting its $100 million authorization, and the board approved an additional $150 million buyback.”

in_line: Non-Block TPV continued to grow more than twice as fast as Block TPV, consistent with the preview’s Q1 2x diversification benchmark.
Block net revenue concentration declined to 41%, down sequentially and year over year, in the direction the preview was watching for after citing 42% Cash App gross-profit-relevant mix in Q1.
Gross-profit take rate was approximately 10 basis points, consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued compression toward roughly 10 basis points.

surprises.description: Jacobs’ backlog rose to $29 billion from the preview’s cited $27 billion record, rather than merely tracking the preview’s base case of flat-to-up sequentially. The 27% year-over-year increase and continued book-to-bill above 1.0x indicate stronger order momentum than that base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog rose 27% year-over-year to a record $29 billion, with a trailing 12-month book-to-bill of 1.4x on gross revenue and 1.2x on net revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... backlog roughly flat-to-up sequentially.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted net revenue growth was more than 8%, above management’s roughly 7.5% frame in the preview. That was a modest upside to the growth pace investors were expecting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “More than 8% organic adjusted net revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mgmt's own FQ3 frame | ... ~7.5% net revenue growth.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 15.2%, modestly above the approximately 15% expected in the preview; EBITDA growth of 17% also exceeded the preview’s roughly 14% derived estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA reached $367 million, up 17%, with margin at 15.2%, expanding 109 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~15% adj. EBITDA margin”; the preview’s bridge math estimated “~$360M adj. EBITDA (+~14% YoY).”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was approximately 16%, a little below the preview’s expectation that Q4 would be above 16%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance calls for approximately 16% adjusted EBITDA margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance requires ~15% in FQ3 and >16% in FQ4 vs. 14.1% in FQ2.”

surprises.description: Jacobs reached its below-2.0x net leverage target a quarter early: leverage was 1.8x in Q3, whereas the preview described the target as an FY26 exit goal. This is ahead of the anticipated deleveraging timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage declined to 1.8x, reaching the below-2.0x target a quarter early, with a plan to delever to approximately 1.5x by end of FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage was 2.1x at FQ2 with a <2.0x FY26 exit target and 1.5x in FY27.”

surprises.description: Share repurchases reached $614 million through Q3, and Jacobs said it remained on track to return more than 100% of free cash flow for a second straight year. The preview cited $472 million of buybacks YTD and a return policy above 60% of free cash flow, so the reported pace and intended payout were stronger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total share repurchases reached $614 million through Q3, keeping the company on track to return over 100% of free cash flow to shareholders for a second straight year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buybacks were $472M YTD against a >60%-of-FCF return policy.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS was $1.84, matching the preview’s Barchart figure of $1.84 and close to the cited $1.83 consensus; the approximately 14% growth was also in line with the preview’s 13.6% year-over-year estimate.
Q3 adjusted free cash flow of $541 million plus roughly $150 million guided for Q4 implies about $691 million for H2, within the preview’s expected $600–$700 million range.
Direct AI build-out at 11% of adjusted net revenue was within the preview’s 10–11% estimate for the broader AI ecosystem, consistent with the expected strong AI-related demand.

The third FY26 guidance increase was anticipated as the likeliest outcome in the preview. The new $7.20–$7.30 adjusted EPS range has a $7.25 midpoint, close to the cited FY26 consensus estimates of $7.22–$7.23.

surprises.description: Gilead’s base-business sales excluding Veklury reached $7.6 billion, above the preview’s $7.30 billion consensus for total product sales, and grew 10% year over year versus the preview’s 4% expected revenue growth. The reported core business was therefore stronger than the headline consensus implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Base business sales (excluding Veklury) grew 10% year-over-year to $7.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $7.37B” and “Total product sales: $7.30B”; total revenue consensus was “+4%” year over year.

surprises.description: HIV sales grew 12% and Gilead raised its full-year HIV growth outlook to 9%–10%, above the roughly 8% growth guidance the preview said was expected. This is a stronger growth result and outlook than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HIV sales rose 12% year-over-year to $5.7 billion,” and Gilead raised full-year HIV growth guidance “to 9%-10% from the prior 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “HIV growth guidance was moved to ~8% from ~6%.”

surprises.description: Yeztugo’s $232 million of Q2 sales was below the roughly $278 million quarterly pace implied by the $1 billion full-year target, and below the preview’s $250 million level at which it said the guide would be at risk. Sequential growth and persistency were encouraging, but the quarter did not meet the preview’s pace for a confident guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Yeztugo generated $232 million in sales, up 40% sequentially,” with “over 70% persistency”; full-year guidance was maintained at “approximately $1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The ~$1B FY guide needs ~$278M/quarter across Q2–Q4”; “A Q2 print materially below ~$250M puts the guide at risk.”

surprises.description: Biktarvy sales were $3.8 billion, ahead of the preview’s roughly $3.6 billion estimate, with 7% growth versus about 2% expected. However, management also said HIV treatment market growth slowed as Affordable Care Act subsidy changes pushed patients out of insurance coverage, a specific headwind the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Biktarvy sales of $3.8 billion were up 7% year-over-year,” while “HIV treatment market growth slowed in Q2 due to Affordable Care Act subsidy changes pushing patients out of insurance coverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Biktarvy | ~$3.6B | … ~+2%”; the preview’s bear case mentioned possible HIV deceleration on a government-pricing headwind.

surprises.description: Trodelvy sales modestly exceeded the preview’s estimate, reaching $457 million versus $448 million expected, and grew 26% versus the preview’s 23% expected growth. The preview already knew about the first-line approval, so the surprise is the stronger sales result rather than the approval itself.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trodelvy sales grew 26% year-over-year to $457 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Trodelvy: $448M” and “+23%”; the preview said to watch “1L uptake.”

surprises.description: The acquired IPR&D charge was slightly below the expected amount, and the reported non-GAAP loss was narrower than consensus: $11.2 billion of charges and negative $6.75 EPS versus about $11.5 billion and negative $7.07 expected. The large loss itself was anticipated, so the difference is only a modestly better-than-expected print.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Acquired IPR&D expenses of $11.2 billion … drove non-GAAP diluted EPS to negative $6.75.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~$11.5 billion of acquired IPR&D charges” and consensus non-GAAP EPS of “–$7.07.”

surprises.description: The broader PrEP business doubled year over year and passed $1 billion in quarterly sales, providing stronger current evidence of demand than the preview’s PrEP TAM debate and cited bearish forecast framing suggested. The preview did not provide a quarterly PrEP sales consensus, so the size of the beat cannot be quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The PrEP business doubled year-over-year and exceeded $1 billion in quarterly sales for the first time, now operating at a $4 billion annual run rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “a debate — PrEP TAM” and noted Leerink was “cutting 2031 PrEP sales to $4B from $6B.”

surprises.description: Livdelzi’s more-than-doubling sales growth and positive Phase III IDEAL data were not discussed in the preview, which said liver-disease portfolio consensus was unavailable. The results add an unanticipated growth and potential label-expansion data point, although no pre-release estimate is available to quantify a beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Livdelzi sales more than doubled year-over-year to $167 million,” with “positive Phase III IDEAL data supporting potential label expansion as early as next year.”

in_line: Cell therapy sales declined 14% year over year to $417 million, matching the preview’s $417 million and 14% decline consensus; the newly stated mid-teens full-year decline guidance is consistent with the preview’s identification of cell therapy as a weak spot.
Yeztugo’s approximately $1 billion full-year guidance was maintained, in line with the preview’s expectation of roughly $1 billion.

surprises.description: Q3 room-night guidance of 3%–5% fell below the preview’s 5%–7% buy-side expectation, with the lower end also in the preview’s warning zone for a slipping recovery. Management also guided Q3 gross bookings, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA to growth of 4%–6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for room night growth of 3%-5% and gross bookings, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA each growing 4%-6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side wants Q3 room nights guided to +5% to +7%”; “anything with a 4-handle or below implies the recovery is slipping.”

surprises.description: The full-year gross bookings outlook was reduced to high-single-digit growth, below the preview’s high-single to low-double-digit framework. Management attributed the reduction primarily to lower flight-ticket growth, while saying the accommodation outlook was largely unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year gross bookings outlook, now expecting high single-digit growth, primarily due to lower flight ticket growth while the accommodation outlook remains largely unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 framework: gross bookings growth high-single to low-double-digit.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross bookings grew 9%, well above both the 4%–6% company guide and the preview’s 5.8% consensus growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross bookings rose 9% (8% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross bookings $49.42B … +5.8%”; company guide “+4% to +6%.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue growth of 8% exceeded the preview’s 5.8% consensus estimate and the company’s 4%–6% guide; constant-currency growth of 7% also topped the preview’s 2%–4% constant-currency guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue increased 8% (7% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … +5.8%”; company guide “+4% to +6% (cc +2% to +4%).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $2.6 billion, with 9% growth and nearly 40 basis points of margin expansion—stronger than the preview’s implied roughly $2.2 billion and 4%–6% growth, and better than the preview’s concern that reinvestment could pressure margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $2.6 billion grew 9% year-over-year with margin expanding nearly 40 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$2.2B (implied)”; “+4–6% guided”; the preview warned that “EBITDA margin misses even on an in-line revenue line” if marketing ROI deteriorated.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $2.54 beat the preview’s $2.44–$2.46 estimate range and grew 15%, above the preview’s 10%–11% consensus growth expectation. The call said a 6% share-count reduction aided the increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $2.54 rose 15%, aided by a 6% reduction in share count.”

surprises.description: Q2 room nights grew 5%, above the 2%–4% company guide and the preview’s 3.7% consensus estimate, exceeding even the high end of guidance by about one percentage point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 room nights grew 5%, exceeding the high end of guidance by about 1 percentage point.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Room nights … +3.7%”; company guide “+2% to +4%.”

surprises.description: Flight-ticket growth was only 4%, far below the preview’s expected 20.1% growth in air-ticket volume, and management identified weaker flight-ticket growth as the primary reason for lowering the full-year gross bookings outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Flight tickets grew only 4% (down from prior quarters) amid reduced airline capacity and higher prices”; the full-year gross bookings outlook was lowered “primarily due to lower flight ticket growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Air tickets 19.22M … +20.1%.”

surprises.description: Connected Trip transactions grew at a low-double-digit rate and more than twice Booking.com’s total transaction growth, short of the preview’s high-teens growth and roughly three-times outperformance expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Connected Trip transactions grew low double digits—more than twice Booking.com's total transaction growth—and represented a low double-digit percentage of total transactions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Connected Trip transactions grew high-teens, ~3x total transaction growth, at a low-double-digit share of transactions.”

surprises.description: The transformation program’s expected annual run-rate savings rose to about $650 million, above the previously stated $550 million target. The additional $100 million from procurement is expected primarily in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised expected annual run-rate savings from the transformation program to approximately $650 million from $550 million (originally $450 million), with the incremental $100 million from procurement to be realized primarily in 2027.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased $3.7 billion of stock in Q2, slightly above the preview’s $3.6 billion Q1 record as a benchmark for the next quarter; total shareholder returns reached a record $4.1 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned a record $4.1 billion to shareholders in the quarter, including $3.7 billion in buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Record $3.6B repurchased in Q1”; the checklist called a repeat of “Q1's record $3.6B” a signal to watch.

surprises.description: Management said traffic from large language models remains significantly below 1% of room nights and has not moved materially in recent quarters, indicating that this source of traffic was still very small despite the preview’s focus on AI-related disintermediation and requests for AI proof points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Traffic received from large language models on both paid and unpaid bases remains significantly below 1% of room nights and has not moved materially in recent quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the stock's de-rating is substantially an AI-disintermediation fear” and called for “AI/agentic proof points with numbers.”

surprises.description: Alternative accommodations grew 4%, slower than overall room nights, despite accounting for about 37% of Booking.com room nights. The preview did not provide a separate growth expectation for this category.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alternative accommodations grew 4%—slower than overall room nights—representing about 37% of Booking.com's room nights.”

in_line: The merchant mix continued shifting toward merchant bookings, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a continued merchant shift; the call said merchant gross bookings reached about 73% of total, up 4 percentage points.

The Middle East conflict remained a drag on international travel, consistent with the preview’s focus on a material conflict-related headwind; the call said its indirect impact was slightly higher than Q1’s roughly 2-point drag.

surprises.description: The preview said the key guidance question was whether Pacira would reaffirm or raise its $745–770 million revenue outlook. Instead, Pacira lowered the range to $735–760 million and also reduced SG&A guidance to $310–330 million from $320–340 million, citing the Zimmer transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to $735-$760 million (from $745-$770 million) and SG&A guidance to $310-$330 million (from $320-$340 million) to reflect the Zimmer transaction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance action — reaffirm vs. raise of the $745–770M range.”

surprises.description: The preview asked whether EXPAREL could sustain the roughly 7% Q1 volume-growth pace. Q2 volume growth was about 4%, and EXPAREL sales grew only 3%; management cited slower elective soft-tissue procedures, particularly in hospitals, as well as vial mix and discounting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EXPAREL net sales grew only 3% to $109.5 million as volume growth of ~4% (a step down from prior quarters) was partially offset by vial mix shift and discounting from a third GPO that went live mid-2025.” Elective soft-tissue procedures slowed “particularly in the hospital inpatient setting.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EXPAREL volume growth — can the ~7% Q1 volume pace hold amid NOPAIN Act separate reimbursement dynamics?”

surprises.description: Total revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s consensus estimate: $192.4 million versus about $191.1 million, despite the weaker EXPAREL growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues rose 6% year-over-year to $192.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | ~$191.1M.”

surprises.description: Pacira reported a new UnitedHealthcare access improvement for EXPAREL: separate reimbursement outside the surgical bundle, with covered lives rising to well over 150 million. The preview discussed reimbursement dynamics generally but did not anticipate this specific coverage change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “UnitedHealthcare added separate reimbursement outside the surgical bundle for EXPAREL, bringing total covered lives to well over 150 million (roughly 50% of the market).”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that Pacira had completed the iovera divestiture to Zimmer Biomet for $70 million upfront plus up to $70 million in revenue-based milestones, while retaining participation in the spasticity program. The preview did not mention a planned or completed sale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pacira completed the divestiture of iovera to Zimmer Biomet … for up to $140 million ($70 million upfront plus $70 million in revenue-based milestones), while retaining participation in the spasticity program.”

surprises.description: UnitedHealthcare also placed ZILRETTA on its preferred drug list without prior authorization, a specific access improvement not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: UnitedHealthcare “placed ZILRETTA on its preferred drug list without prior authorization.”

surprises.description: The call identified a year-end iovera spasticity registrational-study catalyst that the preview had not flagged among its expected pipeline milestones.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Three key pipeline catalysts are expected by year-end 2026,” including “the iovera spasticity registrational study.”

surprises.description: Pacira disclosed that LG Chem had filed for EXPAREL approval in South Korea, with revenue positioned to begin in 2027—an international commercialization development not covered by the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LG Chem filed for EXPAREL approval in South Korea, positioning revenue to begin in 2027.”

in_line: EXPAREL full-year sales guidance was reiterated at $600–620 million, as flagged in the preview’s guidance discussion.
The preview expected ZILRETTA shoulder osteoarthritis Phase 3 results by year-end 2026; the call included those results among the expected year-end catalysts.
The preview flagged PCRX-201 knee-OA Phase 2 progress; the call said top-line Part A data are expected by year-end 2026.

surprises.description: PROCEPT lowered its 2026 U.S. procedure growth outlook to 25–29%, from the preview’s expected 39–48%, implying about 7,000 fewer procedures at the midpoint. Q2 procedures were also softer than expected: just over 13,100, or 21% growth, versus the preview’s roughly 13,500 and assumption of about 30% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 U.S. procedures totaled over 13,100, growing 21% year-over-year, with softer growth attributed to concentrated weakness in legacy AquaBeam accounts; full-year U.S. procedure guidance was lowered to 54,000–56,000, a reduction of approximately 7,000 at the midpoint.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview assumed Q2 procedures of ~13.5K, or +30% year-over-year, and cited standing FY2026 U.S. procedure growth guidance of +39–48% (≈60.2–64.1K).

surprises.description: Despite the procedure-growth shortfall, PROCEPT kept full-year revenue guidance at $390–410 million rather than narrowing it as the preview’s base case anticipated. That leaves the revenue target intact even as the company’s procedure outlook was materially reduced.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company maintained total revenue guidance of $390–410 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected FY2026 guidance to be narrowed to the low end, around $385–398 million, and said the buy-side was positioned for a narrow.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in above consensus, though still within the company’s pre-release range. The $94.5 million result exceeded the $92.64 million consensus estimate by about 2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 total revenue was $94.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was $92.64 million, with company guidance of $91–95 million.

surprises.description: New-system ASP was substantially higher than the preview’s expected $450,000–$460,000 range for the rest of 2026. Q2 ASP reached approximately $495,000, a record high.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company placed 65 Hydros systems at a record-high U.S. ASP of approximately $495,000, up from $485,000 in Q1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided new-system ASP down to $450–460K for the rest of 2026; the preview flagged erosion below that level as something to watch.

surprises.description: Quarterly gross margin was 66%, above the preview’s roughly 65% expectation. The company said the result was aided by a $2.9 million tariff recovery, so the reported margin included that benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 gross margin was 66%, versus 65% in the prior year, aided by a $2.9 million tariff recovery.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected gross margin of approximately 65%.

surprises.description: PROCEPT raised its full-year operating-expense outlook and shifted its adjusted EBITDA loss range toward a larger loss, despite reaffirming positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4. The preview’s standing outlook was about $350 million of operating expense and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $30–17 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company raised full-year operating expense guidance to $355–360 million and narrowed adjusted EBITDA loss guidance to $30–35 million, while reaffirming positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Standing FY2026 guidance was Opex of ~$350M and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $(30)M–$(17)M; the preview also flagged reaffirmation of positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4.

surprises.description: Replacement-system demand was stronger than PROCEPT’s internal models: 14 replacement units were sold in Q2, and the company now expects about 40 for the full year. The preview did not identify replacement sales as a specific expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Replacement activity accelerated, with 14 units in Q2 exceeding internal models; the company now expects approximately 40 replacement sales for the full year.

in_line: Full-year gross margin guidance remained approximately 65%, in line with the preview’s standing outlook.
The company reaffirmed positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2026, as the preview expected it to do.

surprises.description: Service organic growth was 13%, well above the preview’s greater-than-7% Q1 bar. This also put the reported pace well above the sequential improvement management had previously targeted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Service revenue increased 27% with organic service growth of 13%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Service organic growth vs. the ‘>7%’ bar management set for Q1” and management had guided to “sequentially higher service organic growth in Q1 (above Q4's 7%).”

surprises.description: Distribution revenue grew, but the segment’s profitability weakened: gross margin fell 380 basis points and adjusted operating income declined 12%. That was a negative counterpoint to the preview’s focus on distribution/rentals momentum.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Distribution revenue grew 11% but distribution gross margin fell 380 basis points to 31.4% due to unusually high prior-year vendor rebates, and adjusted operating income declined 12% to $4.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Distribution/rentals momentum (rentals ran at low-double-digit organic growth).”

surprises.description: The adjusted EPS figure exceeded the preview’s $0.38 consensus, but GAAP diluted EPS was only $0.14. Because the preview did not specify whether consensus was GAAP or adjusted, the comparison is favorable on an adjusted basis but unclear on a GAAP basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP diluted EPS was $0.14 and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.51.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 EPS: $0.38” and “the page does not state whether this is a GAAP or adjusted basis.”

surprises.description: The GAAP-to-adjusted EPS gap did not narrow as the preview flagged: it was $0.37 this quarter ($0.51 adjusted versus $0.14 GAAP), compared with $0.35 in Q4 ($0.56 versus $0.21).
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP diluted EPS was $0.14 and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.51.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP vs. adjusted spread — acquisition amortization and transition costs cut Q4 GAAP EPS to $0.21 vs. $0.56 adjusted; watch whether that gap narrows.”

in_line: Management guided to high-single-digit service organic growth for FY2027, consistent with the preview’s stated full-year target.
Management guided to service gross-margin expansion for the full year, consistent with the preview’s expectation of year-over-year improvement.

surprises.description: Consolidated revenue was $510.3 million, above the preview’s roughly $500.1 million estimate; the year-over-year decline was 3%, rather than the expected 5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated net revenue was $510.3 million, down 3% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue of ~$500M implies ‑5.0% YoY”; the consensus table lists “~$500.1M.”

surprises.description: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA came in above the preview’s estimated range, and the margin was just above its estimated range as well.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $208 million, down 9.3%, and margin contracting 281 basis points to 40.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA ~$198–203M” and “Adj. EBITDA margin ~39.5–40.5%.”

surprises.description: Las Vegas operations revenue was stronger than the preview’s estimate, at $503.2 million versus an estimated $490–495 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Las Vegas operations posted net revenue of $503.2 million (down 2%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “LV Ops net revenue | my est. ~$490–495M.”

surprises.description: Las Vegas operations held a 45.2% EBITDA margin, staying above the 45% level the preview identified as an important threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $227.5 million (down 5%), with margin down 143 basis points to 45.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “LV Ops margin printing below 45% for a second straight quarter starts breaking a core part of the bull thesis.”

surprises.description: Green Valley Ranch’s renovation disruption was lower than the preview’s $9 million expectation: management put the Q2 impact at about $7 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Green Valley Ranch's hotel renovation removed over 21,000 room nights in Q2, causing about $7 million in temporary disruption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$9M Green Valley Ranch East Tower” disruption.

surprises.description: The company disclosed an approximately $8 million one-time anniversary and brand-marketing expense for Q3, an unanticipated cost, though management expects the campaign to have a net positive top-line effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will incur an approximately $8 million one-time 50th anniversary and brand marketing expense hitting Q3 corporate expense, though management expects a net positive top-line effect from the campaign.”

surprises.description: Management said there were no Q2 share repurchases, with capital directed to project spending; the preview had highlighted buyback activity as a capital-allocation question but did not specify an expected repurchase amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “No share repurchases made in Q2 as capital was directed toward project spend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation — buyback activity against ~$573M authority at a 15%-higher share price.”

surprises.description: Management described work on two greenfield projects and a Durango room-and-spa expansion, adding potential development projects beyond those specifically discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is actively working on two greenfield projects plus a Durango room-and-spa expansion, with more details expected in early 2027.”

in_line: Green Valley Ranch’s full hotel product, including the East Tower, is expected back online in September, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of mid-September.
North Fork remains fully financed, on budget at approximately $750 million all-in, and on pace for an early Q4 2026 opening, as the preview expected.
Full-year 2026 capital spending guidance was reaffirmed at $375–425 million, matching the preview’s stated range.

Management’s expectation of about a 10% sequential decline in Las Vegas operations from Q2 to Q3 is broadly consistent with the preview’s discussion of typical Q2-to-Q3 seasonality and the prior-year decline.
Durango North remains on schedule for a second-half 2027 opening, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a 2027 opening.

surprises.description: Latham raised its FY26 outlook instead of narrowing it toward the low end as the preview’s base case anticipated. The company lifted the midpoint of sales growth guidance from 9% to 11.7% and adjusted EBITDA growth from 12.7% to 15.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, lifting the midpoint of sales growth to 11.7% from 9% and adjusted EBITDA growth to 15.2% from 12.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A ‘narrow to the low half’ is the base case; an outright reaffirm of the full range is a bull signal.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $197 million, about 4.6% above the $188.4 million consensus and growing 14% year over year versus the preview’s 9.1% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales grew 14% year-over-year to $197 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $188.4M”; “Implied Y/Y | +9.1%.”

surprises.description: Growth was more organic than the preview expected: organic sales growth was 10% versus roughly 6% embedded in consensus. The preview expected Freedom Pools to add 2–3 points, while the acquisition contributed 4 points; in-ground pool sales also rose 14% organically.
surprises.fact_evidence: “10% organic growth and 4% from the Freedom Pools acquisition”; “In-ground pool sales rose 23% (14% organic).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Freedom Pools … call it 2–3 pts of the 9.1% consensus growth. So consensus embeds only ~6% organic.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 35.5%, well below the preview’s 37.5–38.0% estimate and its expectation of year-over-year expansion. Management attributed about 140 basis points of the decline to $2.8 million of ramp-up costs after demand outpaced production early in Q2, and said it expects to recover most of those costs in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined 160 basis points to 35.5% due to approximately $2.8 million (~140 bps) of incremental ramp-up costs from a demand surge that outpaced production early in Q2”; “Management expects to recover the majority of the ramp-up costs in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~37.5–38.0% (my est.)”; “Gross margin ≥ 37.1% (Q2'25) — proves lean/value-engineering gains outrun resin and freight.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $40 million, below the preview’s $43–45 million estimate, and its margin contracted to 22.6% rather than the approximately 23.5% margin in the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 12% to $40 million, but adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 50 basis points to 22.6% from 23.1%.”

surprises.description: Net income declined to $13 million and diluted EPS was $0.11, with management citing a $5 million unfavorable foreign-currency swing. The preview’s EPS figure was normalized and cautioned against a direct GAAP comparison, but it anticipated roughly 30% year-over-year EPS growth rather than a decline in net income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income fell to $13 million ($0.11 per diluted share) from $16 million ($0.13) a year ago, hurt by an unfavorable $5 million foreign currency swing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $0.17”; “Implied Y/Y | +~30%”; “MarketBeat's $0.17 is a normalized figure … Do not treat a GAAP headline as a miss without checking the bridge.”

surprises.description: Leverage was already down to 2.2x, below the preview’s anticipated Q2 range of about 2.3–2.5x, and management expects it to fall below 2x by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt was $280 million with net leverage of 2.2x, expected to fall below 2x by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Leverage back toward ~2.3–2.5x and FCF conversion.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a completed restructuring and early-retirement program producing $2.5 million of annualized savings, with a $1.5 million one-time charge expected in the second half; the preview did not flag these actions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed restructuring and early retirement programs yielding $2.5 million in annualized savings, with an associated one-time $1.5 million charge in the second half.”

in_line: The preview flagged resin and transportation inflation as risks; management reported rising Middle East-related commodity and freight costs, partly offset by surcharges and new vinyl-liner price increases.

surprises.description: Tigo was expected to report Q2 revenue of $30.82 million, within its $30–32 million guidance range; it reported only $25.4 million, also just 0.8% above Q1. The shortfall was substantial against both consensus and the company’s own guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 5.6% year-over-year to $25.4 million but came in below prior guidance, and was up only 0.8% sequentially from $25.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus sits right on the guide ($30.82M” and the company guided “$30–32M revenue”; the preview’s base case was “$30.5–31.5M (in line).”

surprises.description: The preview treated reaffirmation or a modest narrowing of the $130–135 million FY26 revenue outlook as the key debate, with its bear case at $110–120 million. Tigo instead cut the outlook to $100–110 million, and management said a return to growth may not come until Q1 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue outlook was cut sharply to $100-110 million, down from the prior $130-135 million guidance, implying roughly flat year-over-year performance.” Management “expects a return to growth potentially as early as Q1 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “FY26 revenue guidance ($130–135M) — reaffirm, narrow, or cut” as the main issue; its bear scenario was a cut “to $110–120M.” It described the back-half plan as requiring “back-to-back record quarters of ~$37–39M.”

surprises.description: The expected $1–3 million adjusted EBITDA quarter came in almost at breakeven, and Q3 guidance still allows for a loss. This was a much weaker result and near-term outlook than the preview’s expected swing to positive EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA collapsed to just $52,000 versus $1.1 million in the prior-year period, and Q3 guidance ranges from a $1 million loss to a positive $500,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The company’s Q2 guide was “$1–3M” adjusted EBITDA; the preview cited “~$2M (guide midpoint)” and expected “Swing to positive.”

surprises.description: The EG4 qualified-inverter ramp was expected to begin contributing during the first half, with initial deliveries already underway; instead, its volume ramp was pushed to Q4. The delay was a primary reason Tigo could not support its prior full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The volume ramp of the key EG4 Section 45X and ITC-qualified optimized inverter partnership was pushed from Q1/Q2 to Q4 2026 due to the partner's internal operational issues, a primary driver of the guidance cut.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “initial deliveries began ~May” and identified the “EG4 inverter shipment ramp” as a Q2 proof point; it said management’s back-half case leaned on “45X/48E-qualified product (EG4 inverter partnership).”

surprises.description: Gross margin was expected around 43–44%, with the preview flagging below 41% as a downside case. Reported margin was 39.3%; even management’s Q3 and Q4 targets were only 40%, although margin excluding GO ESS was higher at 42.1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 39.3% from 44.7% a year ago, though excluding GO ESS it was 42.1%, and management targets 40% gross margin for Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “43–44%” in its base case and said “Sub-41% would break the ‘structurally improved margin’ story.”

surprises.description: GO ESS was expected to provide a product-ramp proof point, but it contributed only a small share of Q2 revenue as the new battery ramped more slowly than planned. That was an additional headwind behind the full-year outlook cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GO ESS contributed only $2.2 million (8.6% of revenue) as the new GO Battery ramped more slowly than planned, another factor behind the guidance reduction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the “GO ESS 47.9 kWh European launch” and the “EG4/GO ESS ramp” among the Q2 proof points to watch.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted whether the U.S. market had found a floor after the residential tax-credit expiration. Instead, U.S. sales were still down year over year, indicating continued weakness in that market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. sales declined 4% following the expiration of the residential clean energy tax credit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Americas revenue “the cleanest read on whether the US resi channel has found a floor” and made stabilization to “≥$6M” part of its bull case.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted cash burn and the risk that inventory might rebuild ahead of the anticipated ramp. Instead, cash increased materially from Q1 and inventory continued to fall, a more favorable working-capital outcome than those concerns implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash rose to $16.9 million, up $5.3 million sequentially and $9.2 million from year-end 2025, while inventory fell 34.3% ($10.7 million) from year-end to $20.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “cash burn” and warned that “a rebuild ahead of the ‘back-half ramp’ would consume the EBITDA”; it also cited cash of “$11.6M” at Q1.

surprises.description: Reported GAAP net income might appear to suggest profitability, but it was produced by a large tax benefit while the business had a pretax loss. The preview warned that GAAP earnings could be noisy, but the specific tax benefit was not anticipated in its stated expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income of $2.2 million was driven by a $3.2 million income tax benefit, masking a pretax loss of $1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “GAAP EPS is noisy” and advised anchoring on adjusted EBITDA and gross margin, but did not forecast a tax benefit.

surprises.description: Management cited FCC restrictions on foreign-produced inverters as a tailwind for its U.S. manufacturing strategy, an additional policy catalyst beyond the EU restrictions discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “views FCC restrictions on foreign-produced inverters and EU restrictions on high-risk vendors as tailwinds for its U.S. manufacturing strategy.”

in_line: EMEA remained the main revenue engine, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would carry the quarter: it drove 73.1% of revenue, with Germany and Italy growing year over year.
Management continued to cite EU restrictions as a potential tailwind, broadly consistent with the preview’s discussion of EU restrictions as share-gain optionality.

surprises.description: FILSPARI U.S. sales reached $141.1 million, above the preview’s implied $132–137 million range; total revenue of $169.6 million also exceeded the $157.3 million consensus. The preview’s roughly $3 million license-revenue assumption was also below the reported $8.2 million, which included a $5 million Chugai milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FILSPARI contributing record U.S. revenue of $141.1 million”; “license/collaboration revenue was $8.2 million (including a $5 million Chugai milestone), bringing total revenue to $169.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $157.3M”; “FILSPARI US net sales… implied ~$132–137M”; the preview estimated “~$3M license.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for first-time FSGS-specific patient start forms, but the reported figure in the supplied call facts is only a combined count of more than 2,000 across IgAN and FSGS. The call facts do not give the FSGS-only count the preview said was due.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 2,000 new patient start forms across IgA nephropathy and FSGS in the quarter”; the supplied facts give no FSGS-only start-form count.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FSGS-specific patient start forms” were “the single most important disclosure”; the preview said management had deferred the FSGS PSF number to this call.

surprises.description: Reported GAAP R&D and SG&A expenses were above the preview’s modeled total of about $142 million, at $156.4 million. The reported total included $22.2 million of non-cash charges, and management cited HARMONY enrollment, pegtibatinase manufacturing, and the FSGS launch as drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total GAAP R&D and SG&A expenses were $156.4 million (including $22.2 million in non-cash charges), with increases driven by HARMONY Phase III enrollment, pegtibatinase manufacturing, and the FSGS launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base-case build used “R&D ~$58M, SG&A ~$84M.”

surprises.description: The company completed a convertible-note refinancing that substantially increased quarter-end cash, a financing transaction not anticipated in the preview. It repurchased about $221 million of 2029 notes, issued $525 million of 2032 notes, and incurred a $40 million inducement expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ended Q2 with approximately $489.2 million in cash and investments after a convertible refinancing (repurchasing ~$221 million of 2.25% 2029 notes and issuing $525 million of 0.5% 2032 notes), incurring a $40 million inducement expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Q1 cash and the expected July Everest payment, but did not anticipate a convertible refinancing or an inducement expense.

surprises.description: Management gave a planned 2H 2026 timeline for a Phase IV FSGS study in African-ancestry patients, a study and timing not raised in the preview. This adds a new clinical plan, though the supplied facts do not establish a change to an existing expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A planned Phase IV FSGS study in African-ancestry patients in 2H 2026.”

in_line: The FSGS launch was described as exceeding internal expectations and outpacing the comparable initial phase of the IgAN launch, consistent with the preview’s expectation that FSGS momentum would be ahead of IgAN.
Thiola and Thiola EC sales of $20.3 million were in line with the preview’s roughly $19–20 million expectation.
The $112.5 million Everest upfront payment was paid in July, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the outflow would occur in Q3 rather than Q2.

surprises.description: The preview treated an opening within the first half of 2027 as a positive outcome and a slip past midyear as a downside risk. Wynn Al Marjan Island is now scheduled to open in September 2027, later than that window.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The opening was pushed to September 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A firm date inside 1H27 is a clear positive; a slip past mid-2027 … is the most under-priced downside risk in the print.”

surprises.description: The preview identified a budget increase as a downside risk, but the project budget rose by about $600 million, with an additional $140 million of equity needed for Wynn’s share. Management also expects $525 million to $650 million of remaining project equity, including Enclave.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wynn Al Marjan Island's total project budget was increased by approximately $600 million, with about half attributed to regional conflict disruptions”; the delay requires “an additional $140 million of equity for Wynn's 40% share.” Remaining project equity, including Enclave, is expected to be “approximately $525 million to $650 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A slip past mid-2027 or a budget increase is the most under-priced downside risk in the print.”

surprises.description: Las Vegas generated $215.2 million of adjusted property EBITDA, below the preview’s $225–235 million base-case range and its stated $230 million support threshold. The shortfall came despite casino revenue growth and only a modest reported unfavorable hold impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wynn Las Vegas delivered $215.2 million of adjusted property EBITDA on $643.2 million of revenue at a 33.5% margin,” with “unfavorable hold costing just over $3.6 million and casino revenues up 5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “LV EBITDAR ~$225–235M”; it also said, “Any confirmation that Q2 LV EBITDAR held ≥$230M is the single biggest support for the domestic half of the thesis.”

surprises.description: Macau adjusted property EBITDA was a clear beat against the preview’s roughly $263 million base case, even with unfavorable VIP hold. Mass drop was also up 5%, rather than showing the weakness feared from the World Cup-affected market backdrop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Macau generated $297 million of adjusted property EBITDA on $1 billion of revenue at a 29.6% margin,” with “unfavorable VIP hold negatively impacting results by over $8.6 million and mass drop up 5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “Macau combined … ~$263M”; it described Q2 market GGR as roughly flat year over year and highlighted World Cup-related weakness.

surprises.description: The forecast for 2026 Macau expansionary CapEx came in below the preview’s $400–450 million expectation: management now expects $350–400 million, even with the Enclave tower and newly approved Event Center and theater in the spending plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total 2026 expansionary CapEx in Macau is now expected to land in the $350 million to $400 million range,” tied to “the Enclave hotel tower and the newly approved Wynn Palace Event Center and theater.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 project capex is … $400–450M Macau.”

surprises.description: Wynn reported unusually low hold in Las Vegas during July, an unfavorable update not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of quarter-to-date trends. Drop volumes and RevPAR nevertheless grew, and management deferred details to the next call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported unusually low hold in Las Vegas during July, though drop volumes and RevPAR grew, with specifics deferred to the next call.”

surprises.description: Wynn Macau raised its final dividend to $150 million from $124 million, an increase not flagged in the preview’s discussion of returns. The preview had called for an accelerated buyback; the reported $75 million of quarterly repurchases is consistent with that focus rather than a separate surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Wynn Macau final dividend raised to $150 million from $124 million,” alongside “$75 million in share repurchases during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Wynn Resorts dividend as “$0.25/qtr” and said, “an accelerated repurchase is the cheapest credibility signal available to management.”

surprises.description: Reported global cash and revolver availability was $4 billion, below the $4.4 billion of liquidity cited in the preview. The call gave a different regional split, with $2.3 billion in Macau and $1.7 billion in the U.S.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed liquidity of $4 billion in global cash and revolver availability ($2.3 billion in Macau, $1.7 billion in the U.S.).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$4.4B liquidity ($1.6B US / $2.8B Macau) against $10.52B debt.”

in_line: Encore Boston Harbor reported $56.1 million of adjusted property EBITDA, within the preview’s $55–58 million scenario range; revenue of $209.3 million was also close to its roughly $210 million estimate.

Macau early-Q3 volumes were slightly down year over year amid World Cup and seasonal effects, then improved in late July and early August. This broadly matched the preview’s expectation that the World Cup drag would ease and its emphasis on whether Wynn would corroborate a rebound.
The $0.25 per-share Wynn Resorts dividend was maintained, as anticipated in the preview.

surprises.description: Sales were $25.7 million, well above the preview’s $22.0 million estimate; the legacy business excluding Midwest grew about 28%, versus the preview’s 8.6% organic-growth build. Shipments rose 15.2% and average selling price rose about 23%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 37.6% year-over-year to $25.7 million,” with “pounds shipped up 15.2% and average selling price up approximately 23%”; “the legacy business (excluding Midwest) grew about 28%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net sales” of “$22.0” million and “organic” sales of “20.3” million, or “+8.6%” year over year.

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 21.6%, above the preview’s 19.5% estimate and its 19% validation bar. That recovery came despite management citing petroleum-based raw-material inflation and higher conversion costs as pressures on margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit” rose 14% to “$5.5 million,” while “gross margin declined to 21.6% from 26.1% year-over-year, pressured by petroleum-based raw material inflation and higher conversion costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin of “19.5%” and said “≥19% validates.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $1.5 million, substantially above the preview’s roughly breakeven estimate of $0.1 million, not merely the expected move into positive territory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations turned positive at $1.5 million (5.7% of sales), reversing a loss of roughly $300,000 in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA” of “~0.1” million and described Q2 as a “first credible shot at breakeven.”

surprises.description: SG&A was $5.5 million, $0.9 million below the preview’s $6.4 million estimate rather than roughly flat with the prior year as the preview model assumed. Management also cited a longer-term target of about 15% of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A fell about $900,000 to $5.5 million (21.5% of sales versus 35.5% prior year), with a longer-term target of roughly 15% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated SG&A of “6.4” million and described it as “flat” year over year.

surprises.description: The active selling pipeline reached $140 million, far above the preview’s reference point of roughly $24–25 million for Q1 and its expectation that the pipeline would hold above $24 million. The reported pipeline was also up about 33% sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The active selling project pipeline reached a record $140 million, up approximately 33% sequentially, boosted by Midwest's addition and legacy momentum.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 pipeline of “$24–25M” and set the bar at “Pipeline holds >$24M.”

surprises.description: The company converted 17 commercial opportunities, below the preview’s bar of at least 25 wins. However, the 26% conversion rate was above the cited industry benchmark, making the reported conversion picture mixed rather than uniformly weak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company converted 17 commercial opportunities across 13 customers worth approximately $5.8 million in annualized revenue at a 26% conversion rate, above the industry benchmark of 10%-15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 bar was “wins ≥25”; it also cited Q1 conversion of 22%.

surprises.description: Management said to expect moderate gross-margin contraction in Q4, whereas the preview’s model required substantial margin recovery in the second half to support its low-20s full-year margin framing. The call facts do not say whether management reaffirmed or changed a full-year margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided investors to expect moderate gross margin contraction in Q4 due to seasonal patterns and custom manufacturing program turnover, consistent with 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said H2 needed “~25%” gross margin to average “low 20s” for FY revenue, and flagged whether management would reaffirm “FY26 ‘low 20s’ gross margin language.”

surprises.description: Cash ended at $28.1 million, below the preview’s roughly $32 million estimate. The reported uses included the acquisition, $6.9 million of repurchases, and $7.7 million used by operations; total liquidity remained about $46 million with no revolver borrowings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash fell about $29.5 million from year-end to $28.1 million, driven by the Midwest acquisition, $6.9 million in share repurchases, and $7.7 million used by operations, leaving roughly $46 million total liquidity with no revolver borrowings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated ending cash of “~32” million.

surprises.description: The cash conversion cycle lengthened by 12 days to 75 days, and management set an initial improvement target rather than reporting that working-capital efficiency had already improved. The preview did not flag this metric or set an expectation for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The cash conversion cycle increased 12 days to 75 days,” with an initial target of a “5-day improvement worth roughly $1 million-$1.5 million in cash,” aiming toward 70 days.

in_line: Midwest’s contribution was close to the preview build: it generated $1.9 million in sales versus an estimated $1.7 million stub-period contribution, entered at about 26% gross margin versus the preview’s roughly 25%, and was immediately accretive to adjusted EBITDA, as expected.
