surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded the top of the $30–35 million range, helped by the revenue upside and favorable mix, despite the preview’s concerns about overhead absorption and mix headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $38.2 million came in above the high end of the $30-35 million guidance range, driven by higher revenue and favorable mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “less favorable mix, and manufacturing-overhead absorption” were Q2 headwinds and noted that “A Q2 adjusted-EBITDA guide was not explicitly broken out in available coverage.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a substantial shekel-related earnings headwind that was not flagged in the preview: it reduced Q2 adjusted EBITDA and is expected to constrain second-half margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A strengthening Israeli shekel reduced Q2 adjusted EBITDA by $2.5 million and is expected to create a $5-7 million EBITDA headwind for the full year, limiting second-half margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Margins and cash” and overhead absorption on the capacity ramp, but did not mention an Israeli shekel headwind.

surprises.description: Kratos gave a much more explicit and rapid hypersonics growth outlook than the preview’s general reference to hypersonic programs: the business is projected to roughly double in 2026 and more than triple its 2025 size by 2027, becoming the company’s largest segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The hypersonics business is projected to grow from ~$200 million in 2025 to ~$400 million in 2026 and at least $700 million in 2027, positioning it to become Kratos' largest segment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “hypersonics (Erinyes / test-vehicle work)” under program color to watch, but gave no comparable revenue or segment-growth outlook.

surprises.description: Kratos revealed a large, specific Spartan engine production commitment: supply-chain orders for 3,000 engines in 2027 and components for another 5,000 in 2028, at about $50,000 per engine. The preview mentioned a Spartan ramp but not commitments on this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kratos is placing supply-chain orders for 3,000 Spartan turbojet engines to be produced in 2027 and plans components for an additional 5,000 engines for 2028, at an average selling price of ~$50,000 each.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Spartan turbojet production ramp” as program color to watch, without specifying production quantities or selling price.

surprises.description: Management added major multiyear demand visibility not quantified in the preview, citing a roughly $7 billion five-year Mach-TB program and Air Force plans for large JASSM/LRASM and low-cost cruise-missile volumes as engine demand drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management cited the Mach-TB hypersonic program at ~$7 billion over five years and Air Force plans for over 11,000 JASSM/LRASM missiles and tens of thousands of low-cost cruise missiles as major multiyear engine demand drivers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned hypersonics and engine-related program color, but did not cite the Mach-TB program value or these missile plans as demand drivers.

surprises.description: The preview expected negative operating cash flow, but management’s stated 2026 investment range of $250–270 million was above the preview’s roughly $160 million FY26 capex figure; Q2 also used cash as receivables and long-lead inventory prepayments rose.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating cash flow was negative $11 million and free cash flow was negative $18.9 million, reflecting ~$59 million higher receivables and long-lead inventory prepayments, with total 2026 investments held at $250-270 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “~$160M FY26 capex” and “guided-negative operating cash flow.”

surprises.description: Bookings remained substantial, but the reported trailing book-to-bill was 1.3:1 versus the 1.6:1 figure cited for Q1; the $15 billion pipeline provides a positive counterpoint to that lower ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month book-to-bill was 1.3:1 with $1.99 billion in bookings, while the bid-and-proposal pipeline expanded to $15 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “record $2.0B backlog and 1.6:1 book-to-bill at Q1” and said July awards “should support another strong bookings print.”

in_line: The July award flow was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of strong awards: it had cited roughly $400 million in hypersonic/national-security funding and a roughly $100 million space-domain-awareness award, while the call reported about $400 million in hypersonic and other funding and a roughly $100 million space award.
Negative operating cash flow was anticipated in the preview, even though the reported Q2 working-capital outflows and stated investment range added detail.

surprises.description: Q3 lock guidance was weaker than the preview’s stated threshold for confidence in a recovery: the $5.25–$7.25 billion range has a midpoint below $7 billion, though its high end slightly exceeds that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided Q3 pull-through weighted lock volume of $5.25-$7.25 billion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side needs locks guided ≥$7B to believe Q2 was a recovery rather than a pipeline harvest.”

surprises.description: Management guided Q3 gain-on-sale margin to rise further to 360–390 bps, above the Q2 guide range the preview focused on. The preview did not specify an expected Q3 margin range, so the size of the beat against a specific forecast is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance was 360-390 bps, after Q2 pull-through weighted gain-on-sale margin expanded to 345 bps.

surprises.description: Home equity losses narrowed sharply within the quarter, suggesting the new segment was approaching monthly break-even faster than the preview’s general expectation that HELOC would contribute to earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: Home equity monthly losses, excluding fair value, narrowed from $15 million in April to $2 million in June.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had called HELOC “a consistent contributor to earnings” and urged investors to look for a disclosed contribution.

surprises.description: loanDepot announced a substantial servicing-rights monetization to bolster liquidity, one of the financing actions the preview identified as a potential upside catalyst. The proceeds were not yet settled, so the liquidity benefit was prospective.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company monetized approximately $10 billion of servicing rights post-quarter, expected to settle later in the year to bolster liquidity.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called an “MSR sale to fund” the maturity a major binary and said “MSR monetization” was a genuine upside catalyst.

surprises.description: Cash fell to $229 million, below the preview’s cited $250 million downside marker. The decline was smaller than the preview’s illustrative $60 million burn, but the ending cash balance was lower than that marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash fell $48 million to $229 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described cash below $250 million as a bear-case condition and warned that another roughly $60 million burn would put runway concerns in focus.

surprises.description: The company made discounted repurchases of senior notes and brought in outside advisers, showing concrete action on the maturity issue; however, the facts do not report a completed refinancing or other final resolution.
surprises.fact_evidence: loanDepot repurchased $16 million of senior notes at 90% of par during the quarter and another $27 million at 86% of par post-quarter, while flagging maturities as a high priority requiring outside advisers.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “credible 2027 notes resolution” was needed for the bull case and warned that “another deferral” would widen the liquidity discount.

surprises.description: Purchase activity strengthened substantially, with purchase volume and market share rising, whereas the preview emphasized the prior decline in purchase mix and flagged a weak pipeline as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: Purchase market share increased 33% in Q2, with purchase volume up 44%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted purchase mix had fallen to 41% from 72% year over year and warned that Q2 could be a pipeline drawdown rather than a recovery.

surprises.description: Expense growth was limited mainly to volume-related costs, and management initiated about $12 million in annualized productivity savings. That was better than the preview’s concern that rising expenses could undermine operating leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: The adjusted net loss narrowed as revenue rose while expense growth was limited primarily to volume-related costs; management also initiated approximately $12 million of annualized productivity/cost savings initiatives.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided expenses up and warned that expenses above roughly $350 million could make the operating-leverage story fail.

surprises.description: The company reported notable year-over-year gains in loan-officer count and marketing efficiency that were not quantified in the preview’s operating expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: Over the past year, loanDepot grew net loan officer count by 18%, increased return on marketing by 70%, boosted lead-to-funded conversion by 50%, and cut marketing cost per funding by 34%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged headcount and operational leverage as issues to watch, but did not anticipate these specific efficiency gains.

in_line: Q2 pull-through weighted gain-on-sale margin of 345 bps was within the preview’s expected 330–360 bps range, and the preview had anticipated a recovery driven by richer home-equity product mix.
Q2 origination volume of $8.0 billion was within the preview’s cited Q2 funded-volume guidance of $7.25–$9.25 billion.
A Q2 adjusted net loss, rather than a return to profitability, was consistent with the preview’s stated base case of a small loss despite the published +$0.03 consensus.

surprises.description: Ultragenyx reported Q2 revenue of $214 million, about 18% above the preview’s roughly $181–182 million consensus range. This was a substantial upside gap against the expected headline revenue figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $214 million, the highest quarterly revenue in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Zacks consensus” revenue was “$181.01M”; “Investing.com consensus” was “$182.1M.”

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was materially smaller than analysts expected: $0.90 per share versus preview estimates of losses of $1.22–$1.27 per share. The gap was favorable even though the company remained loss-making.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss for the quarter was $92 million, or $0.90 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS estimates ranged from “–$1.27” to “–$1.22.”

surprises.description: Crysvita reached $156 million, well above the preview’s benchmark of roughly $120 million—its Q2 2025 revenue—and above the preview’s expectation that it would rebound toward or above that level. This was a stronger-than-anticipated result on the product the preview identified as the key revenue pinch point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CRISVITA contributing $156 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs to show the rebound, ideally toward/above the $120M year-ago level.”

surprises.description: Operating cash use fell to $97 million from $197 million in Q1, a sharper improvement than the preview’s roughly $200 million quarterly-burn framing suggested. The reported ending cash range of roughly $406–436 million still leaves cash below the Q1 balance, but the lower quarterly operating burn eased the immediate runway concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net cash used in operations of $97 million, a significant decrease from Q1”; the company ended the quarter with “roughly $406-436 million in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said cash was “$534M at 3/31/26 against $197M of Q1 operating burn” and described burn as “running at ~$200M/quarter.”

surprises.description: The call gave a more favorable picture of the ASPIRE Angelman trial’s success criteria and efficacy context than the preview contained: statistical success requires only one of two endpoints to meet its specified threshold, and management cited near a 10-point Bayley improvement at one year versus a 5–6 point clinically meaningful change and an expected placebo effect of one point or less.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Split alpha (80% to Bayley-4 cognition raw score, 20% to MDRI), requiring only one endpoint to hit—Bayley p≤0.04 or MDRI p≤0.01—for statistical success”; management said “a 5-6 point Bayley cognition change is clinically meaningful” and prior data showed “near a 10-point Bayley improvement at one year,” with “expected placebo effect of one point or less.”

surprises.description: Citruzumab’s path to approval appears to require more clinical work than the preview had flagged: the MHRA may require a new randomized study, while the FDA needs additional clinical data and does not yet accept BMD as a primary approval endpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MHRA may require a new randomized study”; the FDA is “open to alternative fracture analyses but needs additional clinical data before a potential BLA, as BMD is not yet accepted as a primary approval endpoint.”

surprises.description: Management pointed to potential non-dilutive capital from monetizing DTX401 and UX111 priority review vouchers if the products are approved. That offered a financing source not identified in the preview’s discussion of burn and financing risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management targets profitability in 2027 with “non-dilutive capital from monetizing priority review vouchers for DTX401 and UX111 if approved.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “cash runway and financing risk” and expected questions on “financing ahead of the Aug 23 / Sep 19 PDUFAs.”

surprises.description: The company described launch infrastructure as more prepared than the preview’s questions about readiness and pre-launch spending conveyed: the gene therapy launches would use existing commercial infrastructure, with substantial overlap with current products and QTCs already under contract.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The upcoming gene therapy launches leverage existing commercial infrastructure with ~75% institutional overlap with Dojolvi and Mepsevii,” and “QTCs already under contract.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called out “PDUFA readiness / launch commentary” and questions about “pre-launch spend for two potential Q3 approvals.”

in_line: The company reaffirmed full-year revenue and combined R&D/SG&A operating expense guidance, matching the preview’s stated bar of a reaffirmation.
The DTX401 and UX111 PDUFA dates matched the dates already in the preview, and the ASPIRE readout remained within the preview’s expected H2 2026 window.
The 2027 profitability target and at least 15% reduction in combined R&D/SG&A versus 2025 were already described in the preview; the call reiterated that framework.

surprises.description: Tinder's engagement trend was more encouraging than the preview's expectation of MAU decline merely grinding better: DAU decline improved from 4% in Q2 to about 2.5% in July and nearly positive in August, with positive year-over-year DAU expected imminently for the first time in over three years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tinder DAU declined 4% year-over-year in Q2, its best result in 10 quarters, improving to down ~2.5% in July and nearly positive in August,” with positive year-over-year DAU expected “imminently.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as “Tinder payers –4% to –5%, MAU grinding better” and said an “explicit pull-forward of the MAU-growth timeline” would signal the bull case.

surprises.description: E&E's decline was much steeper than the preview's modeled structural erosion: direct revenue fell 17% and payers fell 21%, despite the Azar headwind already being anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “E&E direct revenue fell 17% to $179 million with payers down 21% to 2.7 million,” pressured mainly by the Azar redesign.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview characterized E&E as having “structural mid-single-digit erosion” and said guidance embedded a “$20M Azar headwind.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA and margin came in above the preview's already-increased profitability expectations: EBITDA was $331 million versus an estimated $328–330 million, and the 39% margin exceeded the roughly 38.3% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 14% to $331 million with a 39% margin, exceeding expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$328–330M” adjusted EBITDA and “~38.3%” adjusted EBITDA margin.

surprises.description: Match Group's 2026 alternative-payment savings are expected to exceed the preview's stated assumption by about $20 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alternative payment savings are now expected to contribute ~$130 million in 2026 (about $20 million above plan).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “$110M app-store savings assumption” as something to watch.

surprises.description: The Google fee structure points to very little alternative-payment benefit in 2027, a disappointing outcome not quantified in the preview's discussion of app-store savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: Google's new fee structure effective March 2026 “offers only ~$5 million of benefit in 2027, a disappointing outcome for developers.”

surprises.description: Revenue slightly missed live consensus, although it remained within the company's prior guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue was $853 million,” down 1% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited live consensus of “~$857.7M” and company guidance of “$850–860M.”

surprises.description: Hinge revenue was a little below the preview's dollar estimate and the threshold it identified, though its 22% growth rate was around the expected growth pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hinge delivered direct revenue of $204 million, up 22%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$207M” and said Hinge “Needs ≥$205M / +22% FXN.”

surprises.description: The company made a stronger capital-return commitment than the preview described, pledging to return all free cash flow to shareholders.
surprises.fact_evidence: Match repurchased 7.3 million shares for $245 million, reduced diluted shares 5% year-over-year, and “pledged to return 100% of free cash flow to shareholders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the existing buyback pace and said it was “doing real work on EPS,” but did not describe a commitment to return all free cash flow.

in_line: Tinder payers declined 5%, matching the preview's stated Q2 expectation of roughly a 5% decline.
Tinder MAU was down 7%, consistent with the preview's recent readings of about 7% down in March and 6.6% down in April, although the continued decline fell short of its more optimistic scenario.
The reported $30–$40 million full-year 2026 Tinder UX/product-change revenue headwind was broadly consistent with the preview's expectation of about $30 million of known drag.

surprises.description: Business revenue was $2.44 billion, about $55 million above the preview’s $2.385 billion base estimate, and declined only 1.8% year over year rather than the roughly 4% decline implied by that estimate. The call also characterized revenue as slightly ahead of consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total business revenue declined 1.8% year-over-year to $2.44 billion,” and results “came in slightly ahead of consensus.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview base case: “Business revenue” of “~$2,385M” versus Q2’25’s $2,490M.

surprises.description: Lumen announced $13 billion in new PCF deals, whereas the preview framed additional bookings beyond the existing roughly $13 billion backlog as upside optionality and treated no incremental deals as part of its long-term projections.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced $13 billion in new PCF deals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New PCF bookings beyond the ~$13B backlog”; long-term projections “include no incremental deals.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow excluding special items came in at positive $327 million, far better than the preview’s seasonal expectation of roughly negative $200 million. The quarter also included about $476 million of PCF cash received.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow excluding special items was $327 million”; “PCF cash received of ~$476 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview base case: “FCF (ex-items)” of “~−$200M,” described as “seasonally negative.”

surprises.description: Strategic revenue grew 14% year over year and reached 53% of business revenue, exceeding the preview’s cited 9.4% strategic growth rate and its watchpoint of a mix above 51%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strategic revenue grew 14% year-over-year and reached 53% of total business revenue, up from 45%” a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “strategic +9.4% Y/Y” and flagged whether strategic mix would be “>51%.”

surprises.description: The preview said the $32 million PCF milestone recognized in Q1 “won't reoccur in Q2,” but Q2 PCF revenue included a $36 million California milestone pulled forward from the second half. That boosted Q2 revenue while shifting some expected second-half revenue into the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 PCF revenue of approximately $91 million,” including “~$36 million of State of California milestone pulled forward from the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had flagged a “$32M PCF delivery milestone in Q1 that ‘won't reoccur in Q2.’”

surprises.description: Legacy revenue declined about 15%, a steeper contraction than the preview’s most recent reference point of a 10% decline. That indicates faster legacy erosion even as strategic revenue growth was stronger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy revenue declined about 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “legacy −10% in Q1” while flagging the business-revenue trajectory as a key issue.

surprises.description: Management said the modernization and simplification savings plan was on track for $700 million exiting 2026 and $1 billion exiting 2027, addressing the preview’s concern that planned cost reductions might not land and could leave an EBITDA shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is targeting “$700 million in modernization and simplification cost savings exiting 2026 and $1 billion exiting 2027,” both “on track.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Street worried about “a modest EBITDA shortfall unless planned cost reductions land.”

surprises.description: NaaS adoption, active ports, and active services all grew quarter over quarter, but at slightly slower rates than the Q1 figures highlighted in the preview. More than 20% of new adopters were brand new to Lumen, a positive customer-quality detail not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: New adoption was up 22% quarter over quarter, active ports 34%, and active services 29%; “over 20% of new adopters” were brand new to Lumen, and customers exceeded 3,000.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 adoption “+25% q/q,” ports “+35% q/q,” services “+32% q/q,” and approximately 2,500 customers.

surprises.description: Management said Alkira could provide upside beyond Investor Day targets, although it will quantify that upside in 2027 guidance. The preview noted Alkira’s recent closing and expected capex avoidance, but did not flag upside beyond the targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Alkira to provide upside beyond Investor Day targets,” with quantification “coming in 2027 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Alkira had closed July 7 and flagged the claimed “$100–200M aggregate capex avoidance.”

surprises.description: Strategic 100- and 400-gig waves revenue grew nearly 11% year over year in North American enterprise channels, while waves sales rose nearly 35%, providing a stronger forward-demand signal that the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Strategic 100- and 400-gig waves revenue grew “nearly 11% year-over-year” and waves sales “surged nearly 35% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Lumen disclosed plans to phase out enterprise voice and communications products, which account for only a low-single-digit share of sales, and said incremental digital services could approach 80% adjusted EBITDA margins. The portfolio shift and margin potential were not called out in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “phasing out enterprise voice and communications products,” which contribute a “low-single-digit percentage of sales,” and expects incremental digital services to approach “80% adjusted EBITDA margin.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed $204 million of special items impacting adjusted EBITDA, a sizable one-off amount the preview did not identify or estimate; the provided facts do not clarify the items’ direction or composition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Special items impacting adjusted EBITDA totaled $204 million in the quarter.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA excluding special items was $802 million, within the preview’s $790–810 million base-case range of about $800 million.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to come in below the $404.2M consensus, with the preview’s bottom-up base case at $355–370M. It reached about $405M, meeting consensus and landing well above that base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached approximately $405 million,” driven by higher deliveries, a 3.7% sequential ASP increase, and $25 million in regulatory credit sales.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat $355–370M as the true base case and expect a headline ‘miss’ versus the Visible Alpha number”; Visible Alpha consensus was “$404.2M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected gross margin to improve from Q1’s -110.4% toward roughly -75%, partly because it expected Q1’s impairment to be absent. Instead, gross margin was -105%, including a $300M inventory impairment that reduced margin by 74 percentage points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was negative 105% including a $300 million inventory impairment that hurt margin by 74 percentage points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus ~-75%”; Q2 “should mechanically improve on higher delivered volume and absence of that charge.”

surprises.description: Cash outflow was substantially worse than the preview’s roughly $981M cash-burn estimate: free cash flow was negative $1.476B. Management said much of the outflow was working capital trapped in inventory rather than permanent cash burn, which partly qualifies the miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative $1.476 billion for the quarter,” with management characterizing much of it as “working capital trapped in inventory rather than permanent cash burn.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Cantor modeled “~$981M of Q2 burn.”

surprises.description: The preview expected an updated FY2026 outlook and viewed 14,000–18,000 units as a realistic reinstated range. Instead, management warned production and deliveries would be below current consensus, with Q3 and Q4 production below Q2 and second-half delivery growth more moderate; no numerical annual guidance is provided in the reported facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “explicitly warned that both production and delivery figures will come in below current consensus estimates,” and said “Q3 and Q4 production [is] expected below Q2 levels” due to the single-shift configuration. Second-half delivery growth is expected to be “more moderate” than the prior year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management “explicitly promised an updated outlook on this call”; the preview said “Realistic reinstated range is likely 14,000–18,000.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a substantial quantified cash-flow improvement and cost-savings plan, beyond the preview’s expectation that restructuring might be described qualitatively. The $1.4B cash-flow figure includes both structural changes and spending phased into later years, while early workforce and shift actions are projected to save $158M annually.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company identified “approximately $1.4 billion of 2026 cash flow improvements” across operating costs, capital spending, and working capital. A one-fifth U.S. workforce reduction and elimination of the Arizona second shift are projected to generate “$158 million in annualized savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the buy-side wanted “a dollar-quantified cost-out target” and expected restructuring could be “framed qualitatively.”

surprises.description: Liquidity was lower than the preview’s approximately $4.7B pro forma estimate: reported liquidity was $3B at quarter-end, with another $800M term loan drawn after the quarter. However, management still expected runway well into 2027, broadly reaffirming the preview’s runway expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total liquidity stood at $3 billion as of June 30 ($800 million cash plus $2.2 billion of credit facility capacity),” and the company drew “an additional $800 million term loan after quarter-end, expecting runway well into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma liquidity ~$4.7B” and management had said it funded operations “into the second half of 2027.”

surprises.description: The preview pointed to a Midsize launch in H2 2026. The reported timeline instead places the Saudi factory’s production readiness in early 2027 and Cosmos volume production in the second half, with formal guidance withheld until year-end and supplier-localization and infrastructure risks still outstanding.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AMP-2 Saudi factory is expected to be production-ready in early 2027 with mid-size (Cosmos) volume production in the second half”; the company “withheld formal guidance until year-end results” and cited supplier-localization and infrastructure risks.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Midsize launch targeted for H2 2026”; the preview called confirmation of “H2 2026 or slip” a key milestone.

in_line: Q2 deliveries were 3,953, matching the actual delivery figure already reported before the release; the preview noted deliveries were already known.

The Uber/Nuro robotaxi program remained on a 2026 launch path, consistent with the preview’s expectation of 2026 production and service timing: regular production is expected in Q4 and launch is targeted for late 2026.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $255 million, $3 million above both the top of company guidance and the preview’s roughly $252 million consensus estimate. That was a positive beat, though it landed at the top of the preview’s $253–255 million whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $255 million, beating the high end of guidance by $3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Street Consensus ~$252M”; the preview also said buy-side was likely carrying “$253–255M revenue.”

surprises.description: Operating profitability substantially exceeded the preview’s expectations: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 16.8% versus guidance of 14.5–15.0%, and the company raised its full-year margin outlook to about 18% from 16.0–16.5%, reaching its 2027 target a year early. The preview anticipated only a modest margin raise, not this scale of improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP operating margin reached 16.8%, a 180 basis point beat versus guidance”; full-year guidance was raised “to approximately 18%,” achieving the 2027 target “a full year early.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin” Q2 guide: “14.5–15.0%”; FY2026 framework: “16.0–16.5%.” The preview’s base case anticipated “modest margin/FCF raise.”

surprises.description: Customer acquisition was stronger than the preview highlighted: Workiva added 283 customers year over year and recorded its strongest quarter for net new customer additions in seven quarters. Customers acquired in the last 12 months also accounted for about 45% of the Q2 subscription revenue increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer count reached 6,750, up 283 year-over-year,” with “the strongest quarter for net new customer additions in the past seven quarters”; recent additions accounted for “approximately 45% of the Q2 subscription revenue increase.”

surprises.description: The largest contract cohort continued to expand quickly but slowed: contracts over $500,000 grew 33%, down from 39% growth in Q1 and just below the preview’s bullish marker of at least 35%. This is a modest shortfall against the preview’s stronger-growth scenario, though the cohort still grew substantially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contracts over $500,000 up 33% to 276 versus Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the $500K+ tier was the “platform-standardization proof point,” warned that “deceleration here undercuts” the standardization narrative, and set “≥35%” as the bull-scenario marker.

in_line: FY2026 revenue guidance of $1.040–$1.044 billion and subscription growth of approximately 19% matched the preview’s expectation that revenue guidance would rise to $1.040–$1.045 billion while the subscription growth guide stayed near 19%.
The 100-basis-point increase in full-year free cash flow margin outlook to approximately 21% was consistent with the preview’s expectation of a modest FCF raise from about 20%.

NRR of 111% was around the preview’s expected level; on a constant-currency basis it was roughly flat, consistent with the preview’s focus on NRR ex-FX of at least 110%. Gross retention of 97% also matched the preview’s cited level and remained above the 96% target.
Multi-solution customers generated 76% of subscription revenue, close to the preview’s cited 75% baseline and consistent with its expectation of continued platform standardization.
The preview highlighted continued repurchases as part of the capital-return story; Q2 buybacks of $123 million were close to the $122 million repurchased in Q1.

surprises.description: Q4 total revenue was $11.3 million above the top of company guidance, a stronger beat than the preview’s consensus of about $431 million and even its bull-case range of $437–441 million implied. The reported beat was about 2.6% above the guidance ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 recurring revenue grew 12.4% to $415.6 million and total revenue grew 11%, with results beating the top end of revenue guidance by $11.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” company guide “$428.4–433.4M”; consensus “~$430.9–431.4M.”

surprises.description: Recurring revenue reached $415.6 million, about $8.4 million above the guidance ceiling, and grew 12.4% versus the preview’s expected 9–10% growth. That indicates a stronger core subscription result than the preview’s base case, which expected FY27 recurring growth to decelerate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 recurring revenue grew 12.4% to $415.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Recurring & other revenue” company guide “$402.2–407.2M (+9–10%)”; the base scenario expected FY27 recurring growth of “+8.5–9.5%.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $12.9 million above the top of guidance, with a 32.7% margin versus the guided 30.0–30.6%. Full-year adjusted EBITDA also exceeded the preview’s stated FY26 guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $145.5 million (32.7% margin), exceeding the top of guidance by $12.9 million, while full-year adjusted EBITDA reached $654.9 million (37% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 adjusted EBITDA guide: “$128.6–132.6M (30.0–30.6% margin)”; full-year FY26 guide: “$638–642M.”

surprises.description: The initial FY27 total revenue range is close to the preview’s roughly $1.89 billion consensus, but the company expects only about 8% growth in recurring and other revenue. That is below the preview’s 8.5–9.5% base-case range and its stated 9% threshold for an intact growth algorithm.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 guidance calls for total revenue of $1.880-$1.895 billion (~7% growth) and recurring/other revenue of ~8% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY27 consensus was “~$1.89B revenue (~+7.5%)”; the base scenario expected recurring growth of “+8.5–9.5%,” and the preview said “9%+ = algorithm intact.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that an accounting change will add 120–140 basis points to FY27 adjusted EBITDA margins as deferred contract cost amortization is extended from seven to eight years. The preview discussed expected margin expansion but did not flag this accounting-driven uplift, so the reported margin benefit is not solely an operating improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An accounting change extending deferred contract cost amortization from 7 to 8 years will add approximately 120-140 basis points to adjusted EBITDA margins in fiscal '27, ratably over the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “The Street models ~100bps of annual expansion” in FY27 adjusted EBITDA ex-float margin.

surprises.description: The acquired Grayscale and Aidora products are still subscale, as the preview anticipated, but management now disclosed a slight FY27 margin headwind from them. Management also said new products should become margin-accretive over time and reaffirmed its 80%+ gross-margin target at $3 billion of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The recent Grayscale and Aidora AI acquisitions are subscale and represent a slight margin headwind in fiscal '27, but management expects new products to be margin-accretive over time and reaffirmed the 80%+ gross margin target at $3 billion revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Grayscale and Aidora as “both explicitly immaterial to revenue” and said investors needed AI monetization proof points.

in_line: FY27 total revenue guidance of $1.880–$1.895 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s roughly $1.89 billion consensus.
The assumption of flat client workforce levels in FY27 matched the preview, which described flat YoY workforce levels as management’s model assumption.
Grayscale and Aidora remaining subscale and immaterial to revenue was consistent with the preview’s description of the acquisitions.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $114.6 million, far above the preview’s $50 million consensus and its $54–58 million base case, because IP licensing revenue reached $60.6 million on a TP-Link settlement rather than the expected near-zero-to-$1 million IP quarter. This single settlement was the main driver of the revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue for Q2 2026 was $114.6 million, more than doubling from $51.2 million,” driven largely by a significant Wi-Fi 6 licensing settlement; the IP platform generated “approximately $60.6 million in licensing revenue, primarily from a single TP-Link settlement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$50.0M”; the preview’s base case was “~$54–58M.” IP was expected at “$0.3–1.0M (binary),” and the preview said “$0–1M is already in the price.”

surprises.description: Adjusted earnings and EBITDA were far stronger than forecast: adjusted net income was $12.8 million, or $0.13 per diluted share, versus an expected adjusted loss of $0.09 per share. Total adjusted EBITDA was $17.3 million and operated-segment adjusted EBITDA was $22.8 million, also well above the preview’s estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company adjusted EBITDA was $17.3 million and operated segment adjusted EBITDA was $22.8 million,” while “adjusted net income was $12.8 million ($0.13 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus adjusted diluted EPS was “($0.09)”; the preview estimated total-company adjusted EBITDA at “$2–4M” and operated-segment adjusted EBITDA at “$7–9M.”

surprises.description: Deflecto’s revenue landed within the expected range, but its margin did not improve as the preview hoped: adjusted EBITDA was only $1.1 million on $27.1 million of revenue, about a 4% margin rather than moving toward 6% or more. Management also cited softer end-market demand, with operating leverage dependent on trucking inventory working through the system.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Deflecto generated $27.1 million revenue but only $1.1 million adjusted EBITDA amid softer end-market demand,” and management expected leverage as “Class A trucking inventory works through the system.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Deflecto revenue of “$27–29M” and said “A move toward 6%+ validates the operating-improvement narrative,” versus Q1’s 4.3% margin.

surprises.description: Book value declined rather than holding roughly flat, falling to $5.71 per share from $5.87 and below the preview’s $5.85-or-higher threshold. The decline was attributed partly to a full write-off of the MalinJ1/Viamet life sciences investment, an unanticipated one-off hit to book value.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Book value declined to $557 million ($5.71 per share) from $567.2 million ($5.87 per share) last quarter,” pressured by parent expenses and “the full write-off of the MalinJ1/Viamet life sciences investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “If BVPS holds ≥$5.85 the discount argument is intact” and its base case expected “BVPS ~flat.”

surprises.description: A $9.4 million gain from the public securities portfolio was an additional positive contribution the preview did not identify: an investee announced an acquisition agreement, allowing Acacia to exit at an attractive return.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The public securities portfolio contributed $9.4 million in gains as one investee announced an acquisition agreement, allowing Acacia to exit at an attractive return.”

surprises.description: IP licensing revenue was exceptionally high, but the segment’s adjusted EBITDA was tempered by a $3.7 million legacy litigation expense that was not adjusted out. Management said it does not expect the expense to recur and hopes to recover more than the amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 IP results included “$3.7 million of nonrecurring legacy litigation expense (not adjusted out of EBITDA)” that management “does not expect to recur and hopes to recover in excess of that amount.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected only “$0.3–1.0M” of IP revenue and flagged “rising legal spend” as a bear-case risk; it did not anticipate this specific legacy expense or potential recovery.

surprises.description: Printronix revenue came in slightly below the preview’s range, although the business remained a cash generator as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Printronix generated $6 million revenue, $1 million adjusted EBITDA, and $900,000 free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Printronix revenue at “$6.5–7.5M” and described it as “Steady.”

surprises.description: The call facts did not report a buyback authorization, despite the preview identifying one as a key capital-allocation catalyst and saying investors had been told to expect one in 2026. The capital-allocation commentary instead pointed to an active acquisition pipeline and a possible direct ownership stake in Mycovia Pharmaceuticals.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged “an active acquisition pipeline and possible direct ownership stake in Mycovia Pharmaceuticals”; the provided call facts report no buyback authorization.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called “an announced repurchase authorization” the “highest-leverage non-operational catalyst” and said “the buy-side has been told to expect this in 2026.”

surprises.description: Management raised a possible direct ownership stake in Mycovia Pharmaceuticals, a more specific potential investment than the preview’s general discussion of acquisition opportunities. It was a possibility rather than a completed deal or committed deployment.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged a “possible direct ownership stake in Mycovia Pharmaceuticals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed an “active pipeline” and possible acquisition deployment generally, but did not mention Mycovia or a direct ownership stake.

in_line: Benchmark revenue of $20.5 million was within the preview’s $20–22 million estimate, and its $9.8 million adjusted EBITDA was within the $8–10 million range; the expected full-quarter Cherokee contribution was reflected in the record quarter.
Deflecto revenue of $27.1 million was within the preview’s $27–29 million range, even though its adjusted EBITDA margin failed to improve.

The company’s $334.6 million in cash, securities, and loans receivable was close to the preview’s roughly $330 million figure; parent-company debt remained zero and consolidated nonrecourse debt was approximately in line with the preview.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin declined 30 basis points year over year, rather than reaching the preview’s 44%–45% guide. Using the preview’s 42.8% prior-year margin, that implies roughly 42.5%, about 150–250 basis points below the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin declined 30 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin (co. guide) 44%–45%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.72, $0.08 above the $0.64 consensus estimate, and was flat year over year rather than falling as the preview anticipated. The preview estimated an approximately 12% decline on a continuing-operations basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS from continuing operations was $0.72, flat year-over-year (aided by a $0.04 favorable currency impact).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.64”; the preview also estimated “~−12% est. ex-divestiture.”

surprises.description: Organic net sales grew 1.1%, below the preview’s expectation of 2%–3% sales growth. The available call facts do not provide reported net sales dollars for a direct comparison with consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 organic net sales returned to growth, rising 1.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 net sales guide (co.) | +2% to +3%”; the preview also said consensus implied “+2.8% vs continuing ops.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $78.9 million, below the preview’s estimated $85–$95 million range. Adjusted operating income also fell to $53 million from $63.6 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income declined to $53 million (9.3% of net sales) from $63.6 million (11.3%) last year, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $78.9 million from $81.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$85–95M (derived).”

surprises.description: The wet-shave manufacturing consolidation caused a substantial, unexpected drag on international sales: management attributed about 350–400 basis points of Q3 international sales impact to supply disruptions. Management called the issue transitory and expects international sales to return to mid-single-digit growth in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Supply chain disruptions from the wet shave manufacturing consolidation created a ~350–400 bps drag on international sales in Q3,” and management expects “international back to mid-single-digit growth in Q4.”

surprises.description: Management narrowed the fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS range to $1.80–$2.00 from $1.70–$2.10, keeping the midpoint unchanged while raising the low end and lowering the high end. The preview had expected the existing range to be reaffirmed unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year fiscal 2026 guidance at the midpoint: … adjusted EPS of $1.80–$2.00.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS range — narrowed, raised, or cut”; the base case expected the “FY range reaffirmed unchanged at $1.70–$2.10.”

surprises.description: Management went beyond the preview’s FY2026 focus by signaling low-single-digit organic sales growth and year-over-year gross-margin expansion in fiscal 2027. This was a favorable forward outlook, although formal FY2027 guidance is still pending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects fiscal 2027 gross margin to expand year-over-year and signaled a return to low-single-digit organic sales growth, though formal guidance will come at the November year-end call.”

in_line: North America organic sales rose 3%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that North America would return to low-single-digit positive growth.
Adjusted free cash flow guidance remained $80–$110 million, as the preview expected.
Year-end net debt leverage of 3.3–3.4x was within the preview’s expected 3.3–3.5x range.
The $0.15 quarterly dividend was consistent with the preview’s stated $0.60 annual dividend.

surprises.description: Net new ARR reached $85 million, far above the preview’s estimated $45–55 million and even above its bull-case threshold of $60 million. Growth was up 66% overall and 41% organically after excluding Bindplane, so the result was not just acquisition-driven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new ARR reached $85 million, up 66% overall and 41% organically after excluding the $13 million Bindplane acquisition contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 is seasonally the lightest NNARR quarter; my estimate is ~$45–55M CC is needed to stay on plan”; the bull case specified “NNARR ≥$60M.”

surprises.description: Q1 revenue and profitability both exceeded the preview’s expectations: revenue was above the consensus estimate and the high end of guidance, while operating margin and EPS beat the high ends of their respective guidance ranges. The EPS result also came in above the preview’s consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue was $555 million and subscription revenue was $530 million, both up 15% and exceeding the high end of guidance by 100 basis points”; “Non-GAAP operating margin was 29%, beating guidance by 100 basis points”; “Non-GAAP EPS of $0.48 came in $0.03 above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus was “~$549.5M” against guidance of “$547–551M”; Q1 non-GAAP operating margin guidance was “27.4–28.0%”; EPS guidance was “$0.44–0.45” and consensus “~$0.44.”

surprises.description: Dynatrace reported unusually strong new-logo momentum, including record new-logo ARR growth above 160%, 122 new logos, and average land size near $285,000 after five consecutive quarters of increases. The preview discussed GTM pipeline but did not set an expectation for new-logo results of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record new logo ARR growth of more than 160%, adding 122 new logos with an average land size of nearly $285,000, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of increasing land size.”

surprises.description: The call gave a more constructive forward view for retention than the preview’s base case of NRR holding flat at 110%: management expects NRR to inflect higher in the back half, when 70% of DPS renewals occur. Current NRR itself remained at 110%, rather than showing an immediate increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net retention rate was 110% on a 12-month basis with gross retention in the mid-90s, and management expects NRR to inflect higher in the back half as 70% of DPS renewals occur then.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “NRR flat at 110%”; the preview described the DPS renewal cohort as “the single largest swing factor in the year.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance by $0.04 to $1.97–$1.99, rather than simply reaffirming the preview’s $1.93–$1.95 range. The preview noted that a guidance raise backed by net new ARR was what the buy-side wanted, although the call facts do not specify the operational basis for the EPS increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS guidance was raised $0.04 to $1.97–$1.99.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 full-year guide … EPS $1.93–1.95”; the preview said “reaffirm is the default” and that the buy-side was looking for “a guidance raise backed by net new ARR.”

surprises.description: The AI opportunity had stronger reported adoption and monetization evidence than the preview’s prior-quarter reference points: more than 1,000 customers were monitoring AI/LLM workloads versus about 850 previously, and more than 800 were running autonomous operations versus about 500. Management also said AI users’ consumption grows 1.5 times faster and described three monetization drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 1,000 customers now monitoring AI/LLM workloads (up from ~850) and over 800 running autonomous operations (up from ~500)”; “Customers using AI capabilities show consumption growth 1.5x higher than non-AI cohort customers,” with “three distinct AI monetization drivers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “850+ customers observing AI/LLM workloads” and “500+ deploying agentic capabilities in production” as key proof points to watch.

surprises.description: The CFO announced plans to retire by fiscal year-end, creating a leadership transition that the preview had not flagged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Jim Benson announced plans to retire by the end of the fiscal year, with a successor search underway and a transition expected.”

surprises.description: The company increased share repurchases to $275 million in Q1, or 7.1 million shares. The preview discussed buyback-related interest-income drag but gave no expectation for this quarter’s repurchase amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Share repurchases increased to $275 million (7.1 million shares) in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned “below-the-line drag from buyback-reduced interest income” but gave no Q1 repurchase expectation.

in_line: NRR was 110%, matching the preview’s stated 110% level, and gross retention remained in the mid-90s.

Full-year constant-currency ARR growth guidance was maintained at 15.5%–16.5%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the FY27 guide would likely be reaffirmed. The additional $23 million FX headwind did not lead to a change in that range.
Log management remained above 100% growth, as the preview identified continued growth above 100% as an important proof point, although the call also reported consumption approaching $200 million.

surprises.description: DIBS reported Q2 GMV of $96 million, up 7% year over year, versus the preview’s $86–91 million guidance range and roughly $88–89 million buy-side expectation. That was a substantial upside to the expected roughly flat-to-down result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GMV reached $96 million, up 7% year-over-year, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GMV: ~$88–89M (buy-side)”; company guidance was “$86–91M,” with the functional whisper at “GMV ~$89–90M (flat to -1% YoY).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was approximately 6%, far above the preview’s expected roughly 0% to +1% and the company’s -2% to +2% guidance range. The result substantially exceeded the modestly positive profitability the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin came in at approximately 6%” and was “well above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus adjusted EBITDA margin was “~0% to +1%,” and company guidance was “-2% to +2%.” The preview described the whisper as “adj. EBITDA modestly positive.”

surprises.description: Net revenue was $23.3 million, above the preview’s $22.23 million consensus and even the $22.6 million top of company guidance. This was a clear upside to the preview’s expected midpoint-level result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue grew 5% to $23.3 million, also beating the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus net revenue was “$22.23M”; company guidance was “$21.6–22.6M,” and the preview said to “Anchor to $22.2M.”

surprises.description: Management raised its full-year GMV outlook to year-over-year growth, moving beyond the preview’s expected path of a return to GMV growth only by Q4. The preview treated the Q4 inflection as the central milestone, not full-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management upgraded its full-year 2026 outlook to expect year-over-year GMV growth (up from prior expectation of growth only in Q4), independent of any macro or housing market recovery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the thesis was that “GMV growth returns by Q4 2026,” and described the base case as “no change to the Q4 language.”

surprises.description: DIBS lowered its full-year revenue take-rate outlook to 24–25%, below the preview’s expectation that take rate would remain at or above 25%. Management attributed the reduction to a mix shift toward higher-value orders with lower blended commissions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year revenue take rate outlook to 24-25% (from 25-26%) due to a mix shift toward higher-value orders carrying lower blended commission rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Take rate ≥25%” as a catalyst to watch and said Q1 take rate “ran 25–26%.”

surprises.description: The company no longer expects positive free cash flow in 2026, contrary to the preview’s expectation that positive full-year FCF would be reaffirmed. Management said the change reflects an accounting reclassification tied to payment processor agreements, while maintaining its positive adjusted EBITDA outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An accounting reclassification tied to payment processor agreements means the company is no longer likely to generate positive free cash flow in 2026, though it maintains its positive full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called “positive adj. EBITDA + positive FCF” a reaffirmation to watch and said withdrawal would be “a thesis-breaker.”

surprises.description: Average order value rose 10%, exceeding the preview’s minimum watch threshold of 5% growth and its cited Q1 AOV growth of 7%. Median order value also rose 10%, indicating the increase was not limited to the average.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average order value rose 10% to approximately $2,850, while median order value also grew 10% to about $1,500.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “AOV growth ≥5%” as a catalyst and cited Q1 AOV of “~$2,750 (+7%).”

in_line: Active buyers fell 10% to about 57,700, consistent with the preview’s concern that the decline could remain around 10% (its base case was buyers still down 8% to 10%).
The positive full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was maintained, consistent with the preview’s expectation that this commitment would be reaffirmed.
The company continued its buyback, as the preview expected execution of the announced authorization; it repurchased approximately 2.4 million shares for $11.1 million in Q2.

surprises.description: CVS reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $2.58, far above the preview’s $1.86–$1.87 consensus range. That is a much larger beat than the preview’s scenarios anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EPS of $2.58, up over 40% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS” Q2 FY2026E: “$1.86 – $1.87.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue exceeded $106 billion versus the preview’s $100.18 billion consensus, a substantial beat. The preview expected revenue growth to decelerate to about 1.3% year over year, whereas reported revenue was up over 7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue of over $106 billion (up over 7%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” Q2 FY2026E: “$100.18B”; the preview said consensus implied “+1.3%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: CVS raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.90–$8.10, well above the preview’s expected raise to roughly $7.55–$7.70. The new range’s low end is above the preview’s expected high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance by $0.60 to $7.90-$8.10.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for a “Raise to ~ $7.55 – $7.70” in its base case and said the “bar is a new range with a midpoint around $7.60+.”

surprises.description: The reported 87.4% Health Care Benefits medical benefit ratio was much lower than the preview’s 89.3% consensus. About 140 basis points came from favorable prior-year development and exchange risk-adjustment updates, leaving an implied ratio around 88.8%—still better than expected, but by less than the headline gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “87.4% medical benefit ratio,” including “approximately $500 million (140 basis points) benefit from favorable prior year development and individual exchange risk adjustment updates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Medical Benefit Ratio (MBR)” Q2 FY2026E: “89.3%.”

surprises.description: CVS raised full-year cash flow from operations guidance to at least $11.5 billion, $2 billion above its existing $9.5 billion floor. The preview listed the existing guidance but did not anticipate an increase of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 cash flow from operations guidance was raised by $2 billion to at least $11.5 billion, with $10.6 billion already generated in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Standing FY2026 guidance: “Cash flow from operations | ≥$9.5B | from ≥$9.0B.”

surprises.description: CVS raised Pharmacy and Consumer Wellness full-year adjusted operating income guidance by $220 million to at least $6.4 billion, above the preview’s existing $6.18 billion floor. The preview expected PCW strength, but not this larger guide increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pharmacy and Consumer Wellness full-year adjusted operating income guidance was raised by $220 million to at least $6.4 billion,” supported by “7% same-store prescription volume growth and 3% same-store pharmacy sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Standing FY2026 guidance: “PCW adj. operating income | ≥$6.18B | +$90M.” The preview also cited “PCW strength on >29% script share and Rite Aid share gains.”

surprises.description: CVS’s 2027 Caremark commentary was concerning: it said membership would decline after a more disciplined selling season and retention was trending slightly below historical norms. The preview highlighted the selling season and retention as key debates, including Cigna’s claim of greater than 97% retention, but did not anticipate this specific negative outlook from CVS.
surprises.fact_evidence: CVS warned of “Caremark membership declines from a more disciplined selling season” and “a retention rate trending slightly below historical norms.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “Health Services / Caremark adjusted operating income and 2027 selling season” and contrasted CVS with Cigna’s “>97% 2026 retention.”

surprises.description: CVS cited continued 340B program pressure as a 2027 headwind, a risk the preview did not identify among its Caremark or other key debates.
surprises.fact_evidence: CVS warned of “continued 340B program pressure.”

surprises.description: CVS disclosed a commitment to spend over $20 billion on technology over the next decade and said AI and technology efficiencies had already generated over $1 billion in OpEx savings. The preview did not discuss this scale of technology investment or the reported savings, so the net financial implication versus expectations is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Committing over $20 billion to technology over the next decade” and “already generated over $1 billion in OpEx savings from AI and technology efficiencies.”

surprises.description: CVS disclosed that its 2026 guidance assumes no share repurchases, with only enough 2027 repurchases to offset dilution. The preview did not set an expectation for buybacks, making this new capital-allocation information rather than a clear miss against a stated forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The guidance assumes no share repurchases in 2026 and only offsetting dilution in 2027,” with leverage “approximately 3.5x” and “$2.7 billion of parent cash at quarter end.”

surprises.description: CVS provided specific low cash prices for GLP-1-related offerings, including $29 weight-management visits and cash-pay therapies as low as $149. The preview discussed GLP-1 formulary economics but did not anticipate these pricing details; their earnings effect was not specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: CVS was “pricing GLP-1 weight management visits at $29 and cash-pay GLP-1 therapies as low as $149.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “GLP-1 formulary economics with Zepbound returning as preferred” and described the expected mix as “revenue-additive, margin-dilutive”; it did not give expectations for these service prices.

in_line: The preliminary 2027 adjusted EPS outlook of at least $8.44 was broadly in line with the preview’s $8.37 consensus estimate; CVS also reaffirmed its mid-teens EPS CAGR through 2028, as the preview highlighted.

surprises.description: EVgo cut 2026 revenue guidance to $400–430 million from the preview’s expected $410–470 million reaffirmation, lowering both ends of the range. The revised low end is below the prior range’s floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For full-year 2026, EVgo guided total revenue of $400 million to $430 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: $410–470M (reaffirm expected)” and the preview’s key metric was to “reaffirm, narrow, or cut” that range.

surprises.description: EVgo lowered its 2026 adjusted EBITDA range to a loss of $25 million to $5 million, eliminating the prior range’s possibility of positive full-year EBITDA. The preview expected the $(20)–$20 million range to be reaffirmed and highlighted the positive end as a key debate, although Q4 profitability is still expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EVgo lowered its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a loss of negative $25 million to negative $5 million, with Q4 expected to be positive while Q3 remains negative.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance as “$(20)M – +$20M” and said “FY26 $410–470M reaffirmed unchanged” in its base case; it also flagged whether management would “still stand behind the positive end of the range.”

surprises.description: Throughput per stall was weaker than the preview expected from a seasonal rebound: it fell 2% year over year, despite improving 7% sequentially. EVgo attributed the softness to legacy equipment weakness and winding-down OEM charging credit programs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Daily throughput per stall declined 2% year-over-year but grew 7% sequentially, coming in softer than expected due to legacy equipment weakness and winding-down OEM charging credit programs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 “should seasonally rebound” and identified a reading below 270 kWh per stall per day as a red flag.

surprises.description: EVgo disclosed a Tesla agreement to deploy EVgo-branded 500-kilowatt V4 Superchargers with Magic Dock, serving both NACS and CCS vehicles, which management says more than doubles its addressable market. The agreement’s financial contribution is not expected until 2027, rather than providing a near-term 2026 lift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EVgo entered an agreement with Tesla to deploy EVgo-branded V4 500-kilowatt Superchargers with Magic Dock technology serving both NACS and CCS vehicles, which management says more than doubles its addressable market”; the deployment is “expected to add revenue with little to no incremental growth G&A” and “meaningful financial impact starting in 2027 rather than 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “new AV partner announcement” would be a genuine narrative unlock, but did not anticipate a Tesla deployment or specify its timing or economics.

surprises.description: EVgo reduced its vehicle-in-operation outlook after S&P’s long-range EV forecast fell sharply. The preview discussed post-credit EV demand but did not flag a lower vehicle outlook; the revised forecast still implies the vehicle park doubles.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EVgo reduced its VIO outlook, citing S&P's June 2026 forecast of nearly 13 million EVs by 2030, a figure 60% lower than the forecast from three years ago, though still representing a doubling of the vehicle park.”

surprises.description: EVgo raised its eXtend revenue guidance to $90–95 million, a favorable change against the preview’s concern about the eXtend construction backlog dropping off, though the preview gave no prior full-year eXtend guide for a direct comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For full-year 2026, EVgo … raised eXtend revenue guidance to $90-95 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “the eXtend construction backlog ‘drops off’ significantly in 2027,” but did not state a full-year 2026 eXtend revenue expectation.

surprises.description: EVgo said 2027 stall additions are expected to be 2.5 to 3 times the number of owned-and-operated stalls added in 2025, an additional growth outlook not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2027 additions are expected at 2.5x to 3x the number of owned-and-operated stalls added in 2025.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $83 million, within the preview’s $78–84 million base-case range and the company’s $75–85 million guide; the preview characterized the quarter itself as close to a non-event.

Charging network revenue was $61 million, at the top of the preview’s ~$59–61 million estimate, and its 19% growth was close to the expected 15–18% range. The 18th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth also matched the preview’s expectation that the streak would survive.

The full-year stall-build schedule remained heavily weighted to Q4, as the preview expected: about 60% of builds are now weighted to Q4, consistent with its description of the plan as significantly Q4-weighted.

EVgo reaffirmed its approximately $500 million 2030 recurring adjusted EBITDA target, consistent with the preview’s discussion of that ambition; it also gave 2030 stall-growth and mid-30% EBITDA-margin targets.

Available liquidity of approximately $835 million, including more than $630 million of undrawn DOE and commercial bank capacity, was broadly consistent with the preview’s discussion of substantial available facility capacity.

surprises.description: EQH reported operating EPS of $1.70 versus the preview’s $1.66 consensus, a small beat; EPS was $1.75 excluding notable items. The 24% year-over-year increase also left the company on track for full-year growth above 15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating EPS was $1.70 ($1.75 excluding notable items)” and the company was “on track for its full-year guidance of greater than 15% EPS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 operating EPS: $1.66.”

surprises.description: Instead of the 2–3% Q2 alternative-portfolio return management had previously guided to, the portfolio returned only slightly over 1% annualized. The resulting $49 million below-plan drag was partly offset by a $35 million tax benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: The alternatives portfolio “returned only slightly over 1% annualized due to lagged Q1 private equity impacts, resulting in a $49 million below-plan drag partly offset by a $35 million tax benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On the Q1 2026 call, management guided alternatives portfolio returns of 2–3% in Q2 2026.”

surprises.description: AB reversed the preview’s identified weak spot: it moved from $7.1 billion of Q1 outflows to $0.8 billion of positive net inflows, although a $9 billion Equitable sub-advisory mandate boosted the result. All segments posted positive net flows, and AUM/A reached a record $1.2 trillion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AllianceBernstein returned to positive net inflows of $0.8 billion, boosted by a $9 billion sub-advisory mandate from Equitable”; “all segments posting positive net flows”; and AUM/A “reached a record $1.2 trillion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called AB’s “−$7.1B net outflows from active equities” the “clearest weak spot” and flagged renewed AB outflows as a downside risk.

surprises.description: AB raised its full-year 2026 performance-fee guidance by $20 million at both ends of the range, above the preview’s cited outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 performance fee guidance to $115-$135 million from $95-$115 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a $95–$115 million performance-fee outlook.

surprises.description: EQH recorded a $453 million GAAP net loss, which the preview did not flag, despite reporting positive operating EPS. The call attributed the loss to noneconomic hedge-portfolio impacts from strong equity markets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a GAAP net loss of $453 million, driven by noneconomic hedge portfolio impacts from strong equity markets.”

surprises.description: Quarterly shareholder returns were much higher than the preview’s Q1 run rate and the stated full-year payout target: EQH returned $449 million, with a 92% quarterly payout ratio. Management nevertheless maintained its 60–70% full-year payout expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Equitable returned $449 million to shareholders including $366 million of buybacks, a 92% payout ratio for the quarter, though management still expects a full-year payout ratio of 60% to 70%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 returns of $223 million against a “60–70% payout target” and said to watch whether the Q2 repurchase pace held through the proxy blackout.

surprises.description: The call added a combined-company target not cited in the preview: a 15%+ ROE on a capital base of more than $30 billion. The preview’s cited 10%+ EPS-accretion target was reaffirmed rather than raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: The merger is “targeting at least 10% accretion to EPS and cash flow per share by end of 2028 plus a 15%+ ROE on a $30 billion+ capital base.”

surprises.description: EQH agreed to sell its unprofitable Employee Benefits business, an unanticipated portfolio change. Management described the near-term earnings effect as neutral to slightly positive and said proceeds would be redeployed into at-scale businesses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company agreed to sell its unprofitable Employee Benefits business (800,000 customers, ~$500 million premiums) to The Hartford at a neutral-to-slightly-positive near-term earnings impact, redeploying proceeds into at-scale businesses.”

in_line: Merger shareholder approval was already reported before the call at 97.24% of EQH votes cast; the call’s report of over 97% support was consistent with that, as was the expected year-end 2026 close.
The merger’s at-least-10% EPS-accretion target by year-end 2028 was consistent with the preview’s expectation of 10%+ run-rate EPS accretion.
Retirement’s positive inflows and spread strength were consistent with the preview’s focus on Retirement as a source of strength; management also said core spreads should remain near current levels.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $339 million, above the preview’s $332.5 million consensus and the $335 million top of guidance. The preview’s own $336 million base estimate was also exceeded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue reached $339 million, up 10% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, exceeding consensus and the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus $332.5M”; Q4 guidance was “$330–335M”; the preview’s base estimate was “$336M.”

surprises.description: Q4 gross margin reached 62.7%, above both the preview’s roughly 62.0% consensus and the 62.2% high end of guidance, rather than landing around the expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin rose to 62.7%, above guidance, driven by a 40 basis point product margin improvement from pricing actions and supply chain cost management.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 gross-margin consensus was “~62.0%” and guidance was “61.8–62.2%.”

surprises.description: FY27 revenue guidance of $1.38–$1.40 billion is above the preview’s roughly $1.36 billion Street estimate and reaches the top of the preview’s base-case range, but its midpoint is below the $1.40 billion-plus level the preview said was needed to validate the growth story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company issued FY27 guidance of $1.38-$1.4 billion in revenue (roughly 8-9% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put FY27 revenue at “~$1.36B (+~6.5%)” for the Street and said “$1.40B+ (10%+) needed to hold the multiple”; its base scenario was “$1.36–1.39B.”

surprises.description: FY27 EPS guidance of $1.28–$1.33 is above both the preview’s implied Street figure of about $1.21 and its $1.25-plus bull threshold, a stronger outlook than the preview’s base range of $1.20–$1.24.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company issued FY27 guidance of … EPS of $1.28-$1.33, representing more than 20% EPS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 EPS at “~$1.21 implied” and a bull bogey of “$1.25+”; its base scenario was “$1.20–1.24 EPS.”

surprises.description: SaaS ARR was $244 million and grew 18%, materially slower than the preview’s expected $246–$248 million and 26–28% growth. Management’s stated path back toward mid-20% growth is only by the end of FY27, later and less ambitious than the preview’s expectation for FY27 growth in the upper half of the 20–30% band.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SaaS ARR grew 18% year-over-year to $244 million, decelerating from 24% growth a year ago due to tough comps, with management guiding a reacceleration toward mid-20% by end of FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q4 ARR of “~$246–248M” and “+26–28%”; it said to watch for FY27 ARR growth in “the upper half of the 20–30% band.”

surprises.description: Extreme Platform ONE generated more than $50 million of bookings, surpassing its roughly $40 million target, and accounted for nearly half of Q4 subscription bookings. That is stronger than the preview’s watch-case of bookings doubling again and provides the requested bookings disclosure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Extreme Platform ONE reached nearly 50% of Q4 subscription bookings (30% for the full year) and exceeded its ~$40 million bookings target with over $50 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said bookings were “tracking to double again in Q4” and identified an “absolute bookings or ARR figure” as a meaningful disclosure upgrade.

surprises.description: FY26 non-GAAP EPS was $1.06, above the preview’s $1.02–$1.04 full-year guidance range, while revenue landed at the top of its expected range. The EPS result therefore outperformed the preview’s expectation even though full-year revenue was broadly in line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 revenue grew 13% to $1.28 billion with non-GAAP EPS of $1.06, up 26% from $0.84.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue guidance of “$1,275–1,280M” and non-GAAP EPS guidance of “$1.02–1.04.”
