surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern that another weak cash-flow quarter and continued buybacks could raise balance-sheet questions, the company reported $65 million of Q4 cash flow and ended with $47 million of net cash. The reported cash flow is not specified as free cash flow, so it cannot be directly equated with the preview’s FCF comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated $65 million of cash flow and $59 million of EBITDA in Q4, ended with $47 million net cash, repurchased $87 million of shares in FY26 (up from $38 million), and secured a new $500 million revolving credit facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q3 FCF of “$7.8M vs. $24.2M a year ago” and said “a second weak quarter with $50M/qtr of buybacks running … invites balance-sheet questions.”

in_line: FY26 revenue was $1.28 billion, consistent with the preview’s $1,275–$1,280 million full-year guidance range; full-year operating margin of 14.8% was also within the preview’s 14.7–14.9% range.
The preview expected the component supply chain to be secured through FY27–28; management said supply was secured into FY28 and beyond.
FY27 revenue guidance landed at the top of the preview’s stated $1.36–$1.39 billion base-case range, even though it did not reach the $1.40 billion-plus bull threshold.

surprises.description: Geron reported Q2 net revenue of $57.5 million, above the preview’s $55.3–$56.3 million consensus range and its roughly $56–$57 million whisper. The 11% sequential increase also exceeded the preview’s implied 6.6% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue grew 17% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter to $57.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (RYTELO net product) | Consensus | $55.3M (range $55.3–$56.3M)” and “Implied seq. growth | +6.6% vs. Q1's $51.8M”; the preview’s whisper was “~$56–57M.”

surprises.description: Management now expects full-year RYTELO revenue to land in the mid- to high end of the $220–$240 million range. The preview expected the full range to be reaffirmed but viewed the top half as unlikely, so this is a more confident outlook than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects to land at the mid- to high end of its full-year 2026 RYTELO net revenue guidance range of $220 million to $240 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case was “guide reaffirmed at $220–240M” and assessed the high end as “Stretch” and “unreachable absent a step-change in 1L/2L penetration.”

surprises.description: First- and second-line patient starts reached 34%, one percentage point above the 33% level the preview cited. It is a modest improvement, though still below the preview’s greater-than-35% bull-case marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First- and second-line patient starts reached 34% on a rolling 12-month basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “1L/2L patient starts at 33%” and said the bull case required “specific 1L/2L mix above 35%.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross-to-net deductions were 20.7%, slightly below the preview’s base-case expectation that they would drift to 22–23%. The company’s low-to-mid-20s outlook for the rest of the year was in line with the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross-to-net deductions rose to 20.7% in Q2 2026 from 15.3% a year earlier, with guidance for the low-to-mid 20s for the remainder of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “G2N drifts to 22–23%”; it also expected guidance of “low-to-mid 20s” for the rest of 2026.

surprises.description: Geron disclosed that it is evaluating a modification to the IMPACT MF interim-analysis event threshold, a methodological review the preview did not anticipate. The projected timelines remain unchanged, so there was no timing acceleration or delay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Geron is evaluating a modification to the event threshold for the interim analysis of the Phase III IMPACT MF trial, though projected timelines and the final OS analysis in second-half 2028 remain unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the interim as “event-driven, triggered at ~35% of planned deaths” and expected it in “H2 2026”; it said any timing tightening would be notable.

surprises.description: Management estimated an ex-U.S. lower-risk MDS opportunity in the thousands of patients, comparable to the U.S. opportunity. The preview expected a European commercialization update before year-end but did not flag this estimate of the market opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to disclose its European commercialization strategy for lower-risk MDS before year-end, estimating an ex-U.S. patient opportunity in the thousands comparable to the U.S.”

in_line: RYTELO demand grew 5% quarter-over-quarter, in line with the preview’s 5–7% base-case expectation.
Full-year operating expense guidance remained $230–$240 million, as expected.
The low-to-mid-20s gross-to-net guidance for the remainder of the year matched the preview’s expectation.
IMPACT MF interim and final-analysis timelines remained unchanged, consistent with the preview’s expectation of an H2 2026 interim and a final analysis in H2 2028.
The European commercialization strategy update is still planned before year-end, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: The preview expected full-year adjusted EPS guidance to be reaffirmed or raised, with consensus at $13.80–$13.84 and company guidance at $13.80–$14.00. Instead, GPN lowered its range to $13.60–$13.80.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered its full-year outlook,” guiding to adjusted EPS of “$13.60–$13.80.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance: raise, narrow, or reaffirm”; the preview said company guidance was “$13.80–$14.00” and consensus was “$13.80–$13.84.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for Q2 normalized adjusted operating margin expansion of roughly 120–140 basis points in its base case, and said the quarter needed to move toward 150 basis points or more. GPN reported only 70 basis points of expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margins expanded 70 basis points on a normalized basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “margin +120–140 bps”; the preview said Q2 needed “a visible step-up toward +150–170 bps.”

surprises.description: The preview expected normalized constant-currency revenue growth of about 5% or better to sustain the growth narrative. GPN reported 4% normalized growth, below that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted net revenue was $3.16 billion, up 4% on a normalized basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the full-year target was “~5%” and Q2 “needs ≥5% cc”; its base case also assumed “~5% norm. cc.”

surprises.description: The preview expected adjusted net revenue to be closer to $3.00–$3.05 billion after warning that the $3.17 billion consensus figure was likely GAAP revenue. Actual adjusted net revenue was $3.16 billion, above that inferred range, even though normalized growth was below the preview’s growth bogey.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted net revenue was $3.16 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted net revenue will likely print closer to $3.00–$3.05B.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a Middle East conflict-related travel shock. GPN said reduced travel volumes tied to the conflict cut Q2 revenue growth by about 100 basis points and assumed the impact would continue through the rest of 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue growth absorbed “an approximately 100 basis point headwind from reduced travel volumes tied to the Middle East conflict”; the full-year outlook assumes the impact “persists through the rest of 2026.”

surprises.description: Although the preview treated $3.46 as consensus and expected a base-case EPS result of $3.46–$3.52, it also judged the effective whisper to be $3.50–$3.55. The reported $3.46 met consensus but fell short of that higher previewed whisper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 12% to $3.46.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The effective whisper is nearer $3.50–$3.55.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS of $3.46 matched the preview’s stated Q2 consensus of $3.46.

GPN kept its commitment to return more than $2 billion to shareholders in 2026 and continued to expect $7.5 billion of cumulative returns by the end of 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated capital-return commitments.

surprises.description: Freshpet reported Q2 net sales of $305.6 million, well above the preview’s $292.7 million consensus estimate. The 15.5% growth rate was also much stronger than the preview’s expected 10.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 15.5% year-over-year to $305.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $292.7M”; “+10.6%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 48.6%, above the preview’s expected range of 47.0%–47.5%. This was a stronger margin result than the preview’s roughly 10–60 basis-point year-over-year expansion implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 170 basis points to 48.6%, the highest level since Q1 2020.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin | ~47.0–47.5%”; “Guide: +50–100bps FY at midpoint.”

surprises.description: Management raised both full-year guidance ranges, although the preview’s base case was a reaffirmation. Sales growth guidance moved from 8%–11% to 10%–12%, and adjusted EBITDA guidance rose by $5 million at both ends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting net sales growth of 10%-12% (up from 8%-11%) and adjusted EBITDA of $210M-$220M (up from $205M-$215M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case is reaffirm at 8–11% / $205–215M”; “a raise is the upside surprise.”

surprises.description: Growth was even more volume-led and less burdened by negative price/mix than the preview’s concern about widening negative mix suggested. Volume rose 15.7% while price/mix was only 0.2% unfavorable, rather than the preview’s cited -3% or worse downside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “15.7% volume growth with a slight 0.2% unfavorable price/mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Volume-led growth with modest negative mix is healthy. A widening negative price/mix (-3% or worse) is the tell”; the bull scenario specified “price/mix ≥ flat.”

surprises.description: Freshpet raised its 2027 adjusted gross-margin floor to at least 49%, above the preview’s expected target of greater than 48%. It reiterated, rather than changed, the 20%–22% adjusted EBITDA margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2027 adjusted gross margin floor from at least 48% to at least 49%, while reiterating its 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin target of 20%-22%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 2027 algorithm. Targets are adj. gross margin >48% and adj. EBITDA margin 20–22%.”

surprises.description: Logistics costs were a newly disclosed headwind: they rose to 6.9% of sales, and the full-year outlook now includes an additional $8 million of elevated costs. The preview did not flag this cost pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Logistics costs rose to 6.9% of net sales (from 5.7% a year ago) due to higher fuel and trucking capacity pressures, with guidance now assuming an additional $8 million in elevated logistics costs for 2026.”

surprises.description: The bag-technology update put a sizable whole-business margin benefit on the record: more than 100 basis points when fully optimized. The preview expected benefits to be weighted toward 2027 but did not quantify this potential contribution; the call also indicated only about 25 basis points in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New bag manufacturing technology is expected to deliver over 100 basis points of gross margin improvement on the entire business when fully optimized, with only ~25 bps benefit expected in 2026 and full-rate contribution reached during 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New bag-line technology (launched Jan 2026, converted April 2026) reaches ~35% of bag capacity by year-end with benefits ‘skewed to 2027.’”

surprises.description: Digital orders grew 41% and increased to 16.7% of the business from 16.1% in Q1, a channel-growth update the preview did not identify as an expected result or key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital orders grew 41% and accounted for 16.7% of total business (up from 16.1% in Q1), with approximately 78% of e-commerce sales fulfilled through Freshpet’s fridge network.”

surprises.description: Management reported a 7% buying-rate increase and 13% combined penetration-plus-buy-rate growth over the trailing 52 weeks, with buying rate now contributing more of that growth. This is a favorable update on the household-growth debate the preview highlighted, though the preview did not provide a specific Q2 benchmark for these measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MVP households now account for 71% of sales and spend 5x more per year than the average household, with buying rate growth of 7% now driving a larger share of the 13% combined penetration-plus-buy-rate growth over the trailing 52 weeks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Household penetration and buy rate” were listed as a key metric to watch; the preview cited Q1 buy rate growth of “+6%” and said “Decelerating penetration adds were the specific cause” of a prior guide-down.

surprises.description: Freshpet reported completing $86.5 million of its $150 million buyback authorization and repurchasing 1.6 million shares. The preview identified the capital-return and capacity decision as a debate but did not anticipate this amount of completed repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company executed $86.5 million of its $150 million buyback authorization, repurchasing 1.6 million shares.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said it would decide mid-year whether to accelerate line installs”; the preview said acceleration “pushes out the buyback” while no acceleration “pulls the FCF/return-of-capital story forward.”

surprises.description: Freshpet said its U.S. dog-food share was 4.3%, up from the 4.2% figure cited in the preview, and added that it is the second most popular brand among Gen Z and Millennial dog households in a category it believes can reach $10 billion. The modest share increase and additional demographic and category claims add to the competitive narrative the preview was watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Freshpet holds just 4.3% market share in U.S. dog food and treats, positioning it as the fastest-growing dog food brand and the second most popular among Gen Z and Millennial dog households in a category management believes can reach $10 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Freshpet cited 4.2% share of US dog food” and “fastest-growing brand.”

in_line: Freshpet reiterated its 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin target of 20%–22%, matching the preview’s stated target.
MVP households remained at 71% of sales, matching the preview’s cited 71% share.
The bag-technology contribution was described as weighted toward 2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation that benefits would be “skewed to 2027.”
Freshpet again described itself as the fastest-growing dog-food brand, consistent with the competitive position cited in the preview.

surprises.description: NYT added 280,000 digital subscribers, below the preview’s 320,000 Street expectation, though within its estimated 260,000–290,000 whisper range. The result missed the more aggressive published bar but was in line with the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company added 280,000 net new digital subscribers in Q2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Street is at ~12.84M EOP, implying ~320K net adds. I’d treat the buy-side whisper as ~260–290K; the base scenario expects 265–300K.

surprises.description: Digital advertising grew faster than the preview’s high-teens expectation and exceeded guidance. Total advertising also came in above the level implied by the preview’s digital and print advertising estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: Digital advertising revenues grew 20.7% to $114 million, beating guidance, while total advertising revenues rose 11.3% to $149 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Digital advertising: ~$110–112M; ‘high teens’ (guide). Print advertising: $34.5M. The preview said anything below ~15% would reframe the ad story.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating costs grew 10%, above the company’s 8%–9% guidance cited in the preview. The call attributed the overrun mainly to variable compensation tied to financial outperformance, rather than structural cost changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted operating costs grew 10%, exceeding the 8%-9% guidance, primarily due to incremental variable compensation tied to financial outperformance rather than structural changes.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted operating costs: ~$596–602M; +8–9% (guide).

surprises.description: Q3 digital subscription revenue growth is guided to 12%–15%, below Q2’s 16.4% growth and a deceleration from the recent pace. Management attributed part of the slowdown to the comparison with last year’s Q3 paywalling of the Mini game.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance calls for digital subscription revenue growth of 12%-15%, below recent trends, partly due to the cohort mix impact from paywalling the Mini game in last year's Q3.

surprises.description: The call disclosed that 2026 free cash flow benefits from about $60 million of tax-related items that mostly will not recur after fiscal 2026, and that some first-half working-capital gains are expected to reverse. This qualifies the durability of cash generation underlying the preview’s capital-return discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: 2026 free cash flow includes an approximately $60 million tax-related benefit, the majority of which is not expected to recur beyond fiscal 2026, and some first-half working capital gains are expected to reverse.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Commitment is ‘at least 50% of FCF over the mid-term’ against $542M LTM FCF.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating profit and EPS both modestly exceeded the preview’s earnings bridge: AOP was about $155 million versus an estimate of roughly $151 million, and EPS was $0.69 versus $0.67 consensus. The beat was positive but not a large departure from the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted operating profit grew 16% to approximately $155 million, and adjusted diluted EPS rose 19% to $0.69.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s guidance bridge estimated adjusted operating profit of ~$151M and adjusted EPS of ~$0.66–0.68; consensus adjusted diluted EPS was $0.67.

in_line: Digital subscription revenue was $408 million, within the preview’s roughly $400–410 million expectation; total subscription revenue of about $538 million was also within its $529–539 million range.
Digital-only ARPU growth of 3.1% was broadly in line with the preview’s 2.5%–3% base-case expectation and its focus on tenured price increases.

The company said it remained on track toward 15 million subscribers, consistent with the preview’s focus on that target; the preview’s base case expected the target to be reaffirmed without additional color.
The return of about $160 million to shareholders in the first half was consistent with the preview’s expectation of returning at least 50% of free cash flow over the mid-term.
Management’s acknowledgment that big tech platforms are driving less traffic to publishers was consistent with the preview’s flagged debate about search-referral erosion.

surprises.description: Kaltura reported $46.9 million of Q2 revenue, above both the $46.0 million high end of its guidance and the $45.60 million consensus. Subscription revenue of $45.6 million also exceeded the high end of its guidance, $44.1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $46.9 million” and “subscription revenue of $45.6 million,” with both “exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 total revenue guidance of “$45.2–46.0M” and consensus of “$45.60M”; subscription guidance was “$43.3–44.1M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in well above the expected $2–3 million range, rather than declining as the preview’s guidance implied. The $5.9 million result and 12% margin were also substantially above the preview’s implied 4.4–6.5% margin range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached a record second-quarter high of $5.9 million,” above the “$2-3 million guidance range,” with margin “expanding 300 basis points to 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$2.0–3.0M,” implying “−27% to −51%” year-over-year, and an adjusted EBITDA margin of “4.4–6.5%.”

surprises.description: Kaltura raised its full-year outlook instead of simply reaffirming it, with the clearest comparable change in EBITDA: the new $15.8–17.2 million range is above the preview’s expected $13.8–15.2 million range. The preview did not provide a directly comparable full-year subscription-revenue range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised,” including adjusted EBITDA of “$15.8-17.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$13.8–15.2M” and described the base case as “FY reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: PathFactory contributed $4.9 million of subscription revenue, far above the preview’s inferred quarterly contribution of roughly $1.4–1.8 million. However, management also expects continuing attrition and revenue headwinds from its standalone product, so the larger contribution does not remove the ongoing concern about that business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PathFactory contributed $4.9 million in subscription revenue this quarter, higher than expected,” but management anticipates “continued attrition and revenue headwinds from its core standalone product over the next few quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview inferred “~$1.4–1.8M of quarterly PathFactory revenue” and said the standalone revenue had not been disclosed.

surprises.description: The disclosed AI pipeline was much larger than the preview’s reference to a few dozen opportunities, with more than 500 opportunities now identified. The stated $17 million is non-weighted potential annual contract value, so it is pipeline rather than booked revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AI-related sales pipeline for H2 2026 and 2027 now exceeds 500 opportunities representing approximately $17 million in non-weighted potential annual contract value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the prior disclosure as “a few dozen opportunities.”

surprises.description: Kaltura signed a record number of AI-including deals, including nine for Agentic Avatars, but those deals totaled only about $1 million in contract value. The volume is encouraging, while the small combined value falls short of evidence of a reference-scale AI win.
surprises.fact_evidence: Kaltura “signed a record 14 new deals including AI offerings—double its prior record—with nine including the new Agentic Avatars product, but combined total contract value was only about $1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 had disclosed “three AI-related deals, ‘small’” and that a bull outcome required the new AI portfolio to have “converted at least one reference-scale deal.”

surprises.description: Management indicated that H2 new subscription bookings could exceed 2.5 times H1 bookings, providing a stronger stated bookings ramp than the preview quantified. The forecast is conditional, and the preview’s central concern was whether the back-half acceleration would be validated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects H2 new subscription bookings to potentially exceed 2.5 times the amount booked in H1,” driven by both enterprise/education and media/telecom.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the key issue was whether “the H2 guide validate[s] a back-half AI ramp” and flagged the implied H2 revenue acceleration.

in_line: Net dollar retention was 96%, within the preview’s expected base-case range of 95–96% and below its 97%+ bull threshold.
Meaningful AI revenue contribution remains deferred to 2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation that more meaningful contribution would be in 2027.
Media & Telecom revenue continued to decline, and management still expects declines in 2026 before a sequential recovery in 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated timeline.

surprises.description: Lineage raised full-year same-store NOI guidance from negative 4% to negative 1% to negative 3% to flat, an improvement beyond the preview’s modeled range. The increase suggests a stronger outlook for this measure than the preview’s base case of reaffirmed guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lineage raised its full-year same-store NOI guidance to negative 3% to flat (from negative 4% to negative 1%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled FY26 SSNOI guidance of “(4)% to (1)%” and said the base case was that “guidance is reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The GIS full-year NOI outlook fell from 0% to positive 2% to negative 4% to negative 2%, a substantial downgrade the preview did not flag. Management attributed it to a $7 million legal settlement and lagging carrier rate pass-throughs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The GIS segment's full-year NOI outlook was lowered to negative 4% to negative 2% (from 0% to positive 2%), driven by a $7 million legal settlement and lagging carrier rate pass-throughs.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that the Big Bear facility fire is expected to reduce adjusted EBITDA by about $15 million across Q3 and Q4, with guidance excluding any insurance recovery. The preview did not anticipate this disruption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Big Bear facility fire (~500,000 sq ft, ~85,000 pallet positions, roughly 1% of global capacity) is expected to create a ~$15 million adjusted EBITDA drag across Q3 and Q4, though guidance excludes any business interruption insurance recovery.”

surprises.description: AFFO per share guidance was raised to $2.80–$3.05 from $2.75–$3.00. That is better than the preview’s expected reaffirmation or midpoint-or-better framing, although management did not narrow the range as the preview’s buy-side expectation contemplated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increased AFFO per share guidance to $2.80-$3.05 (from $2.75-$3.00).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors expected “either a narrowing to the upper half or an explicit midpoint-or-better framing,” and warned that “a flat reaffirmation” would disappoint.

surprises.description: Q2 AFFO per share of $0.76 modestly exceeded the preview’s modeled $0.73–$0.75 range. Adjusted EBITDA of about $320 million was within the modeled $318–$325 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was approximately $320 million and total AFFO was ~$198 million ($0.76 per share), both ahead of internal expectations and consensus estimates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “AFFO / share $0.73–$0.75” and “Adj. EBITDA $318–325M.”

surprises.description: Physical occupancy rose 90 basis points year over year, marking the first year-over-year increase since Lineage went public and reversing the declines seen in 2025. The preview anticipated a normal seasonal decline in Q2 occupancy and did not point to a year-over-year gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store physical occupancy rose 90 basis points year-over-year, marking the first year-over-year occupancy gain since the company went public and an inflection after 2025 declines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 carries a normal seasonal decline”; the preview also noted physical occupancy had “fell 290bps sequentially to 76.4% in Q1.”

surprises.description: Management said Q3 will be the toughest year-over-year comparison, with same-store NOI growth likely below Q2 levels, but projected close to flat year-over-year growth in Q4. The preview discussed the expected fading FX tailwind but did not set out this quarter-by-quarter path.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 2026 to be the toughest year-over-year comparison with same-store NOI growth likely below Q2 levels, while Q4 is projected to reach close to flat year-over-year same-store NOI growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FX tailwind was expected to diminish in the second half, but gave no Q3 or Q4 same-store NOI outlook.

surprises.description: The preview looked for a concrete portfolio-review deliverable; instead, Lineage described plans to divest more than $1 billion of assets and said a comprehensive review update is expected by year-end, without reporting a completed transaction. The asset-sale plan is a concrete step, but the timing of a fuller update leaves the anticipated transaction detail outstanding.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported leverage is approximately 6.0x versus a targeted 5.0x-5.5x range, and management plans to divest over $1 billion of assets, with a comprehensive strategic review update expected by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for a “portfolio review deliverable” such as an “asset sale, JV, or portfolio transaction” and said silence for a second consecutive quarter could read as inability to transact.

surprises.description: Lineage reported a development and ramping pipeline of 20 facilities, with $1.1 billion invested, more than $134 million of expected incremental stabilized NOI, and 71% pre-leasing—operating detail not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has 20 facilities under construction or ramping with $1.1 billion invested, expected to deliver over $134 million of incremental stabilized NOI, and pre-leasing stands at 71%.”

in_line: Same-store NOI declined 2.9% year over year, within the preview’s modeled negative 2% to negative 3% range. The 90-basis-point FX tailwind was also close to the preview’s expectation of about 100 basis points, though the reported decline was slightly weaker than the preview’s roughly negative 2.5% validation threshold.

Trade-related international container volumes fell 14%, an improvement from the 17% decline in Q1, consistent with the preview’s expectation that investors would look for a second-derivative improvement in volumes.
Reported leverage of approximately 6.0x was in line with the preview’s stated 6.0x reported leverage.

surprises.description: Q2 comparable sales growth was 4.2%, well above the preview’s 1.8% consensus growth estimate. Sales of $1.8 billion also exceeded company expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 4.2% on a comparable basis to $1.8 billion” and “exceeding company expectations.”

surprises.description: Primo raised its full-year comparable sales growth range to 2%–4%, rather than simply holding the prior 1%–3% range the preview said was likely safe. This was the second consecutive quarterly increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 comparable net sales growth guidance for a second consecutive quarter to 2%-4%, up from the prior 1%-3% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sales guide (+1–3%) is likely safe.”

surprises.description: Direct delivery sales turned slightly positive at 0.4%, a quarter earlier than the preview’s expected breakeven. However, the improvement came from price/mix rather than volume, and the customer base remained smaller, tempering the recovery signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct delivery net sales returned to growth at 0.4%, a 340 basis point sequential improvement and one quarter ahead of expectations, though driven by price/mix rather than volume as the customer base remained smaller.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided Q2 to breakeven, H2 to modest growth.”

surprises.description: Despite strong comparable sales growth, companywide volume contributed negative 0.1%; the 4.3% price/mix contribution accounted for essentially all the growth. That leaves the reported growth less volume-led than the preview’s recovery discussion around direct-delivery customers implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total comparable growth was almost entirely price/mix-driven, with a 4.3% price/mix contribution offset by a negative 0.1% volume contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Direct Delivery reaching breakeven and net customer adds turning positive” was listed as a catalyst, and the preview described the recovery narrative as depending on direct delivery.

surprises.description: Management reported tighter freight conditions and higher spot transportation rates as a margin pressure, rather than the freight moderation or mitigation the preview identified as a needed support for the EBITDA bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “faces margin pressure from a tighter freight market and higher spot transportation rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the EBITDA bridge needed “freight/commodity mitigation” and described “freight moderating” in its bull scenario.

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $385 million was at the top of the preview’s estimated $370–385 million Street zone; the 21.4% comparable margin was within the preview’s roughly 21.0%–21.8% range.
The company reaffirmed its $1.465–$1.515 billion adjusted EBITDA guidance, matching the preview’s base case that the range would be held unchanged.
Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance remained $790–$810 million, as the preview identified reaffirmation of that range as the expected outcome.
Retail growth was broad-based and premium brands remained a strong growth engine, consistent with the preview’s expectation of solid retail and its focus on premium water.
The quarterly dividend remained $0.12, consistent with the preview’s stated $0.48 annual dividend.

surprises.description: The preview expected Insulet to reaffirm FY26 guidance, or possibly narrow it to the low end. Instead, management cut the full-year U.S. Omnipod growth outlook to 17–19%, citing weaker-than-expected Type 2 retention and utilization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year U.S. Omnipod growth outlook to 17-19%,” with worse-than-anticipated Type 2 retention and utilization accounting for roughly two-thirds of the reduction.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Currently 21–23% cc total company / 22–24% Omnipod … Reaffirm = neutral-to-positive. Narrowing to the low end = the recall cost them volume.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted Type 2 as a key growth story and expected it to remain around 40% of new starts, but did not anticipate the retention and utilization problem. Management reported that Type 2 patients were over 40% of U.S. starts, yet their retention and utilization were weaker than Type 1, especially in the first 90 days.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Type 2 patients represented over 40% of U.S. new customer starts,” but the company saw “lower retention and modestly lower utilization versus Type 1,” concentrated in “the critical first 90 days of onboarding.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch … whether Type 2 stayed ~40% of new starts (~5% penetrated — the primary long-duration growth story),” and whether management disclosed “attrition/churn.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.36, below the preview’s $1.42 consensus midpoint and even its $1.38 low estimate, as well as its $1.45–$1.52 base-case range. This was a miss despite EPS growing about 42% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew approximately 42% year-over-year to $1.36.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.42 mid (range $1.38–$1.47)” and base case “Adj. EPS $1.45–1.52.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a preliminary FY27 U.S. Omnipod growth range of 9–14%, with a 12% midpoint and no benefit assumed from remediation actions. The preview anticipated competitive entrants as a risk but did not provide an expectation for this growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2027 U.S. Omnipod growth [was] framed in a wide 9-14% range (12% midpoint) that assumes no benefit from remediation actions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged a “2027 competitive patch-pump wave” and listed upcoming competitors, but gave no FY27 U.S. Omnipod growth expectation.

surprises.description: The company said total-company constant-currency revenue growth would exit 2026 in the mid-teens, signaling a sharper late-year deceleration than the preview’s FY26 growth outlook alone conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “preliminarily expects total company constant currency revenue growth to exit 2026 in the mid-teens.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 guidance was “21–23% cc total company” and expected a reaffirmation or possible nudge, but did not forecast the exit growth rate.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin rose sharply rather than showing the margin pressure emphasized in the preview: it expanded 320 basis points to 72.9%, helped by productivity, pricing, and volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 320 basis points year-over-year to 72.9%, driven by manufacturing productivity gains, positive pricing, and higher volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 adjusted gross margin was “71.0%, down 90bp Y/Y,” and highlighted recall costs and raw-material and freight costs as headwinds to watch.

surprises.description: Insulet raised its FY26 adjusted EPS growth outlook to at least 30%, above its prior company target of more than 25% cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “now expects adjusted EPS growth of at least 30% for 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the current FY26 target as “>25% adj. EPS growth.”

surprises.description: International Omnipod guidance was raised to 30–32% constant-currency growth for the year, with management pointing to strong first-half momentum. The preview expected international strength, but did not anticipate this full-year guidance increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “raised international Omnipod full-year growth guidance to 30-32% constant currency,” citing strong first-half momentum, including Omnipod 5 becoming Australia’s “#1 pump for new users” and a Spain launch.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected international strength in its base case, citing “Spain + Libre 3 Plus,” and listed the Spain launch as a catalyst; it did not state a full-year international growth outlook.

surprises.description: Revenue was essentially in line with sell-side consensus but slightly exceeded the company’s Q2 constant-currency guidance range: constant-currency growth was 22.7% versus the guided 20–22%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total company revenue reached $802 million, growing 23.5% reported and 22.7% constant currency, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed total-company Q2 guidance of “+20–22%” constant currency and consensus revenue of “~$803M.”

in_line: Reported revenue of $802 million was essentially in line with the preview’s approximately $803 million consensus estimate.

Type 2 patients were over 40% of U.S. new customer starts, consistent with the preview’s expectation that they would remain around 40%, although their retention and utilization were unexpectedly weaker.
The company reiterated its approximately 100 basis points of FY26 operating-margin expansion target, consistent with the preview’s stated target.
Pricing remained stable to slightly up, with no pricing pressure cited as the cause of the U.S. outlook cut; the preview had flagged promotional or pricing responses as a possible bearish signal.

surprises.description: Recursion cut its FY2026 cash operating expense guidance to $375 million, below the preview’s standing guide of less than $390 million. It said this represents nearly a 40% reduction from comparable 2024 pro forma expenses while maintaining all outcome targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “lowered its 2026 full-year cash operating expense guidance to $375 million,” representing “a nearly 40% reduction from comparable 2024 pro forma expenses while maintaining all outcome targets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash operating expenses < $390M for FY2026”; the bull scenario allowed for the guide to be “lowered.”

surprises.description: The quarter-end cash balance was about $557 million, below the preview’s estimated range of $575–595 million. The reported operating runway through early 2028 was in line with the preview, but the cash balance itself came in light.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ended the quarter with approximately $557 million in cash and equivalents,” providing “an operating runway through early 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash & equivalents: ~$575–595M (est.)”; the standing guidance was “Operating runway into early 2028.”

surprises.description: Recursion reported more than $260 million in upfront and milestone payments from Roche-Genentech, versus the preview’s cited $213 million. It also disclosed potential for over $300 million in additional milestones for each future small molecule program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Roche-Genentech collaboration has yielded more than $260 million in upfront and milestone payments, with potential for over $300 million in additional milestones for each future small molecule program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$213M from Roche/Genentech” and noted a “$30M milestone in 2025.”

surprises.description: REC-7735 advanced beyond the preview’s expected 2H26 go/no-go decision: it received FDA IND clearance, and Recursion said its Phase I trial will start later this year. The preview had not anticipated IND clearance or a trial start on that timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “REC-7735 received FDA IND clearance”; “The Phase I ZINNIA trial will initiate later this year with first data expected in the first half of 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “REC-7735 and REC-102 go/no-go calls were guided for 2H26.”

surprises.description: Recursion disclosed that its engine advances candidates using about 330 compounds over roughly 1.5 years, compared with industry benchmarks of about 2,500 compounds over 4 years. The preview discussed the platform narrative but did not anticipate these specific speed and capital-efficiency comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recursion's engine advances candidates using roughly 330 compounds over about 1.5 years, compared with industry benchmarks of roughly 2,500 compounds over 4 years, representing major speed and capital efficiency gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “how the Recursion OS platform is monetized versus advanced internally,” without giving efficiency benchmarks.

surprises.description: Recursion announced two senior hires—a Chief AI Officer from Microsoft Research and a new head of drug design—which the preview had not anticipated. The preview expected attention on the new CEO’s narrative and possible portfolio or infrastructure decisions, but did not flag these appointments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company strengthened leadership by hiring Dr. Hoifung Poon (from Microsoft Research) as Chief AI Officer and Dr. Donovan Chin to head drug design.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “portfolio prioritization, headcount/infrastructure decisions, or any pivot in how the Recursion OS platform is monetized versus advanced internally.”

in_line: REC-4881’s reported 43% median polyp-burden reduction after 3 months and persistence of effects 3 months off treatment were broadly in line with the preview’s cited 43% reduction at 12 weeks and durability after treatment.

The expected FDA engagement update for REC-4881 remained on the preview’s 2H26 timetable: the call said an update was expected before year-end, but provided no specific endpoint, registrational path, or trial-start timing.
Recursion said it had generated over $500 million in realized partnership cash inflows, consistent with the preview’s statement that cumulative partner inflows exceeded $500 million.
The early discovery program with Genentech was consistent with the preview’s flagged possibility of a Roche-Genentech early-stage program nomination seeded from delivered maps.
The operating runway through early 2028 matched the preview’s standing runway guidance.

surprises.description: The preview treated Q3 guidance and July trends as the quarter’s main new information, but Shake Shack said it will stop issuing quarterly guidance and move to annual-only guidance. That removes the expected near-term quarterly outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Shake Shack is discontinuing quarterly guidance in favor of annual-only guidance going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The entire event risk sits in the Q3 guide” and “Q3-to-date / July comps” were identified as key items to watch.

surprises.description: The preview focused on whether restaurant margins could stabilize, but management said the prior 2025–2027 margin-expansion target is under review and identified that target—not unit growth—as the key uncertainty. This is a more explicit challenge to the longer-term margin outlook than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The prior three-year (2025-2027) targets of low-teens unit growth and 50+ basis points of annual restaurant margin expansion are under review, with the restaurant margin goal being the key uncertainty rather than unit growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “a specific 2027 recovery bridge” and described the margin trajectory as a key debate, but did not indicate that the targets were under review.

surprises.description: Restaurant-level margin reached 23.0%, above the preview’s 22.5% estimate and at the top of the company’s 22.0%–23.0% range. The beat came despite record-high beef costs, though the preview had already identified beef inflation as the main pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level profit margin declined 90 basis points year-over-year to 23.0% of Shack sales,” with record-high beef costs “up mid-teens,” partially offset by “60 basis points of labor efficiency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated restaurant-level margin at “~22.5%” against guidance of “22.0%–23.0%.”

surprises.description: Same-Shack sales were 3.5%, above the preview’s 2.5%–3.0% range, and traffic was positive rather than the negative-traffic outcome the preview warned about. However, the estimated World Cup benefit reduces underlying comps to roughly the mid-2% range, close to expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-Shack sales grew 3.5% (2.0% traffic, 1.5% price mix),” but excluding an estimated “~90 basis point World Cup benefit,” comps were “closer to mid-2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected same-Shack sales of “~+2.5–3.0%” and flagged the possibility that the comp could come “with negative traffic.”

surprises.description: Management put full-year adjusted EBITDA and net income at the low end of the existing ranges. The preview viewed reaffirmation as a mild upside surprise because it feared another cut, but the low-end positioning and cost explanation are more cautious than a strong reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided full-year adjusted EBITDA and net income to the low end of the “$225-$235 million range” due to “persistent beef inflation and higher fuel and distribution costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market was watching whether Shake Shack would “reiterate $225–235M or cut again,” and that “a reiteration is the mild upside surprise.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted H2 pricing as a question, but management quantified near-term pricing roll-offs: 2% in August and another 1.4% in December. With beef still elevated into July, further price increases remain possible, suggesting continued cost pressure and potential reliance on pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 2% of pricing rolls off in August and an additional 1.4% rolls off in December, while beef costs remained elevated into July, leaving open the possibility of further price increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Beef cost guidance + H2 menu pricing” as a key issue and said to “watch for a stated H2 pricing action.”

surprises.description: The app channel grew much faster than the preview’s discussion of the value platform suggested, with management describing it as a highly incremental, high-frequency channel. The preview did not provide an app-growth or app-mix expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable app channel sales grew nearly 30% year-over-year and the app now represents just over 10% of channel mix,” described as “the highest-frequency and most incremental channel.”

surprises.description: Other operating expenses rose as a share of sales, partly because of higher delivery commissions. The preview did not forecast this pressure separately from restaurant-level margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Other operating expenses rose 80 basis points partly due to higher delivery commissions.”

surprises.description: Shake Shack reported that new units are generating over 30% cash-on-cash returns, a unit-economics detail not addressed in the preview. The preview did expect roughly 16 openings and continued 60–65 unit guidance, so the surprise is the return disclosure rather than the opening pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company opened “16 new company-operated Shacks (a Q2 record),” reached 33 year-to-date, reaffirmed 60–65 openings for 2026, and said new units generate “over 30% cash-on-cash returns.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~16” Q2 company-operated openings and cited full-year guidance of “60–65.”

surprises.description: Revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s consensus estimate, though it remained inside the company’s pre-announced range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue rose 17.2% year-over-year to $417.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$416M” and cited company guidance of “$415–420M.”

in_line: The 16 company-operated openings and reaffirmed 60–65 full-year openings matched the preview’s expectations; the newly disclosed cash-on-cash returns are captured separately.
The underlying same-Shack comp, after removing the estimated World Cup benefit, was roughly in the preview’s expected 2.5%–3.0% range.
The annual full-year EBITDA range was not cut, consistent with the preview’s base expectation of a reiteration, although management placed results at its low end.

surprises.description: Gross bookings reached more than $58 billion, above both the $57.2 billion Street estimate and the $57.75 billion high end of company guidance. The reported 22% growth rate was at the top of the preview’s expected 20–22% range, but the dollar result exceeded the bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross bookings grew 22% year-over-year to more than $58 billion, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross Bookings: $57.2B (Street)” and company guidance of “$56.25–57.75B”; the preview described implied growth of “~+20–22%.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS growth was 35%, above the preview’s expected 29–32% growth. Using the preview’s $0.63 prior-year EPS, that growth implies roughly $0.85 per share, above the $0.83 consensus estimate and the $0.82 high end of guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS grew 35% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “+29–32%” growth and listed consensus EPS of “$0.83” with guidance of “$0.78–$0.82.”

surprises.description: Uber disclosed a nearly 500-basis-point year-over-year decline in Mobility revenue take rate, with about 400 basis points attributed to an optical UK business-model change. The preview had flagged persistence of accounting-related take-rate pressure as a key question but gave no expectation for a decline of this size; the 7.6% Mobility operating-income margin was described as strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mobility revenue take rate declined nearly 500 basis points year-over-year, with about 400 basis points attributable to an optical UK business model change, while mobility operating income margin remained strong at 7.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked “how much of that [business-model] headwind persists in Q2” and highlighted “Take rate and the revenue/bookings divergence.”

surprises.description: Uber gave concrete AV rollout milestones—live in 7 cities, targeting 15 by year-end, and planning more markets in 2027—plus a commitment to deliver 120,000 vehicles over the next few years. However, AV trips are still less than 0.5% of roughly 300 million weekly trips, so the disclosed rollout has not yet translated into meaningful platform volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Uber is live with AV partners in 7 cities and on track to reach 15 cities by year-end”; AV trips “represent less than 0.5% of Uber's total volume of roughly 300 million trips per week”; the company has a “commitment to deliver 120,000 vehicles over the next few years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the buy-side wanted “deployment numbers, not commentary,” specifically “live vehicle counts, city-level utilization, and unit economics per AV trip.”

surprises.description: Uber said its Delivery Hero agreement could expand reach to nearly 100 markets and roughly double the number of markets offering both mobility and delivery. That is a broader footprint opportunity than the preview’s description of Delivery Hero as operating in 50 markets.
surprises.fact_evidence: The agreement is “expected to expand reach to nearly 100 markets and roughly double the number of markets offering both mobility and delivery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Delivery Hero as “50 markets” and focused on accretion, dilution, synergies, and the antitrust path.

surprises.description: Uber spent about $4 billion toward Delivery Hero stock purchases in Q2. The preview described the $14.8 billion transaction as all-stock and emphasized its dilution and accretion implications, but did not anticipate this additional stock-purchase deployment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Uber deployed about $4 billion toward Delivery Hero stock purchases in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the deal “$14.8B all-stock” and asked for “share count impact, synergy targets, and how they intend to run capital returns through the pendency.”

surprises.description: Share repurchases were not simply continuing at the prior pace: Uber said it bought back $3.5 billion year-to-date but plans to rebuild repurchases within months toward its 50%-of-free-cash-flow target. That is a more qualified near-term buyback picture than the preview’s request for reaffirmation of buyback capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Uber ... has bought back $3.5 billion of stock year-to-date, with plans to rebuild share repurchases within months toward its 50%-of-free-cash-flow target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “whether buybacks continue” as a key question and said the bull case required “reaffirmed buyback capacity despite the all-stock DH deal.”

surprises.description: US Mobility trips and bookings accelerated, with management attributing growth partly to suburban markets where fewer than 10% of eligible consumers have used Uber, versus more than 50% in dense markets. The preview was watching for intact US demand but did not identify this large suburban usage gap as a specific growth runway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “US mobility trips and gross bookings accelerated in Q2” and in suburban markets “under 10% of eligible consumers have used Uber versus over 50% in dense markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case called for “US demand intact”; it did not give an expectation for suburban adoption or usage.

surprises.description: Uber disclosed that only 20% of consumers use both rides and Eats, while cross-platform users are growing 1.5 times faster than single-product users. The preview discussed membership and advertising as platform-margin drivers but did not flag this cross-product adoption gap or growth differential.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only 20% of consumers use both rides and eats, and cross-platform users are growing 1.5x faster than single-product users.”

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month free cash flow surpassed $10 billion for the first time in Uber’s history. The preview offered a quarterly FCF estimate of roughly $2.4–2.7 billion but did not anticipate or set an expectation for this record annual run-rate milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow surpassed $10 billion for the first time in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed quarterly free cash flow of “~$2.4–2.7B” as its own estimate, with “no clean consensus.”

in_line: Non-GAAP EPS growth was strong, but it exceeded rather than merely matched the preview’s expected 29–32% growth range.
AV investment of about $10 billion was broadly consistent with the preview’s stated commitment of more than $10 billion.

surprises.description: VCP traction fell short of the preview’s bar: VYX had 25 signed customers versus the expected 28–32, and $286 million of remaining contract value versus the expected more than $350 million. RCV was also below the $293 million reported in Q1, despite growing 65% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VCP contracts reached 25 signed customers representing $286 million of remaining contract value, up 65% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for ~28–32 cumulative contracts and RCV >$350M.”

surprises.description: Retail outperformed the preview’s already-positive momentum expectations: revenue grew 4% excluding the hardware impact, while adjusted EBITDA rose 20% and margin reached 26.6%. The preview’s bull case required Retail margin of at least 18%, well below the reported level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail revenue grew 4% excluding the hardware impact and retail adjusted EBITDA rose 20% to $97 million, with margin up 880 bps to 26.6% (350 bps excluding hardware).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Retail momentum and payments attach”; the bull case required “Retail EBITDA margin holds ≥18%.”

surprises.description: Restaurants’ EBITDA decline worsened rather than moderating: adjusted EBITDA fell 15%, compared with an 8% decline in Q1. Revenue remained down 6% excluding hardware, with delayed refreshes, SMB weakness, and the Brazil divestiture cited as pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restaurant revenue declined 6% excluding hardware (a $10 million drop) driven by delayed hardware refreshes, SMB weakness, and the Brazil divestiture, with adjusted EBITDA down 15% to $58 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for on-time launch confirmation and whether Restaurants EBITDA decline moderates.”

surprises.description: Recurring revenue was a larger share of sales than the preview’s post-transition expectation: it reached 83% of total revenue, above the preview’s expectation of more than 75%. Recurring revenue also grew 3%, including 6% growth in software.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue reached 83% of total revenue in Q2”; recurring revenue was “up 3% (software +6%, services +1%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Recurring revenue … should be >75% of revenue post-ODM.”

surprises.description: The quarter included an unanticipated cost and demand headwind: memory-chip inflation is expected to cost $20–$30 million, and passing it through in prices is contributing to customer caution and delayed hardware and project purchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Memory chip cost inflation represents a $20-$30 million headwind being passed through via price, contributing to customer caution and delayed hardware and project purchases.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS beat the preview’s consensus estimate, coming in at $0.17 versus $0.15. The call said EPS was flat year over year because of a higher tax rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was flat at $0.17 due to a higher tax rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS: $0.15.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was within the preview’s expected dollar range, but the margin result was stronger than the preview’s expectation of modest Q2 margins: margin expanded 460 basis points, or 80 basis points excluding the hardware transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 5% to $98 million with margin expanding 460 basis points to 18.7% (80 bps excluding the hardware transition).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management explicitly guided Q2/Q3 margins to be ‘modest’”; Q2 adjusted EBITDA was estimated at “~$95–100M.”

surprises.description: VYX disclosed share repurchases that the preview did not anticipate: it bought back approximately $11 million of shares during the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated $56 million adjusted free cash flow (before restructuring), ended the quarter at 2x net leverage, invested $41 million in CapEx, and repurchased approximately $11 million of shares.”

in_line: Revenue of $523 million was close to the preview’s $516.9 million consensus and within its $505–525 million base-case range; the preview cautioned that the reported revenue comparison was distorted by the hardware accounting transition.
Adjusted EBITDA of $98 million was within the preview’s estimated $95–100 million range.
Management maintained FY2026 revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS guidance, as the preview’s base case expected; the call indicated sequential improvement in the second half.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $277.8M, above the preview’s $268–271M company guide and ~$269.7M consensus. That is a clear beat of both the guide and the consensus bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue grew 26.6% to $277.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guide … $268–271M”; “Consensus ~$269.7M.”

surprises.description: Q2 bookings reached $295.9M, above the preview’s $280–285M guide and $282.5M midpoint, exceeding even the preview’s cited ~$285M buy-side whisper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 bookings grew 33% year-over-year to $295.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total Bookings … $280–285M”; “Total Bookings vs. $282.5M midpoint”; “Buy-side whisper is effectively the guide high end, ~$285M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 36.4%, well above the preview’s roughly 32% estimate and the 32% key-metric threshold, and it exceeded the 35% margin target set at IPO. The reported ~900 bps of year-over-year expansion was also much greater than the preview’s ~400–500 bps base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin hit 36.4%, exceeding the 35% target set at IPO five years ago, with roughly 900 basis points of margin expansion year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA / margin … ~$85–88M / ~32%”; “Base … margin ~32%, +400–500bps Y/Y”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ≥ 32%.”

surprises.description: The preview expected over 80% eGate coverage by the end of Q2, but the company reported coverage of only over 70%. The rollout’s reported progress therefore fell short of the specific target investors were told to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “eGates now cover over 70% of the network.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management targeted >80% of the network by end of Q2”; “eGate coverage hits ~80%.”

surprises.description: Active CLEAR+ members reached 8.3M, below the preview’s ~8.4M estimate and its 8.35–8.42M base-case range. The increase from Q1’s 8.2M was about 100,000, short of the preview’s 150,000-net-add threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active CLEAR+ members grew 15.2% to 8.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Active CLEAR+ members … ~8.4M”; “Active CLEAR+ 8.35–8.42M”; “Active CLEAR+ ≥ 8.4M with net adds ≥150k.”

surprises.description: The company raised standard membership pricing by $10 effective July 1 and said early retention remained healthy with no observed impact. The preview treated a pricing-action update as a potential bull catalyst and otherwise anticipated a measured approach to increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised standard membership pricing by $10 (from $209 to $219) effective July 1st, with early retention rates remaining healthy and no observed impact on retention.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A … pricing-action update” was listed as a bull catalyst; the base case anticipated a “measured approach to price increases.”

surprises.description: CLEAR1 net new customer signings and pipeline each increased over 50% sequentially, providing concrete evidence of continued momentum beyond the preview’s Q1 reference point. The preview emphasized CLEAR1 as a key debate but said hard dollar or ARR disclosure would be the stronger catalyst; the call’s figures were sequential rather than dollar or ARR disclosures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CLEAR1 net new customer signings increased over 50% sequentially from Q1 to Q2, and the pipeline also grew over 50% quarter-over-quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CLEAR1 growth rate and disclosure quality” was a key metric; “Any hard dollar disclosure, ARR figure, or named multiyear logos is a bull catalyst.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased about $22M of shares in Q3 to date, a substantial shift from the preview’s cited $1.2M Q1 buyback. The preview specifically flagged a return to repurchases as a potentially meaningful capital-allocation signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased ~$22 million of shares in Q3 to date at an average price of $52.73.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buyback was only $1.2M in Q1”; “a shift back toward repurchase … would read as management calling the stock cheap.”

surprises.description: A $315M accrued Amex partnership liability will be paid in Q3, resulting in negative Q3 free cash flow. The preview discussed the full-year FCF outlook but did not flag this large payment or a negative quarterly cash-flow period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $315 million accrued partnership liability with the Amex credit card partner will be paid out in Q3, resulting in negative Q3 free cash flow (already reflected in guidance).”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $284M–$287M puts the midpoint at $285.5M, modestly above the preview’s $280M–$285M base-case range and above its $283M checklist threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $284M-$287M.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … Q3 guide $280–285M”; “Q3'26 revenue guide ≥ $283M.”

in_line: FY2026 free cash flow guidance rose from at least $465M to at least $480M, meeting the preview’s expectation of a raise above $465M and landing at the top of its $470M–$480M base-case range.

surprises.description: Revenue was about $248 million, based on the reported 11% year-over-year decline, below the preview’s $255.5 million consensus and implying a steeper decline than the expected 8.2%. Management attributed the weakness partly to a 34% drop in network revenue and a shift away from larger jobs after a mid-March oil and gas price spike.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 11% year-over-year,” driven by “a 34% drop in network revenue” and “a demand shift away from larger jobs following a mid-March oil and gas price spike.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $255.50M” with implied year-over-year change of “‑8.2%.”

surprises.description: Angi recorded a $235 million non-cash goodwill and trade name impairment on its U.S. reporting unit, an unanticipated charge tied to a sustained decline in market capitalization. It does not affect cash, liquidity, or covenants, but is a substantial reported one-off charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$235 million non-cash goodwill and trade name impairment charge entirely on its U.S. reporting unit,” triggered by “a sustained decline in market capitalization,” with “no impact on cash, liquidity, or covenants.”

surprises.description: U.S. service requests fell 6% and leads fell 13% year over year, reversing the growth in proprietary requests and leads reported for Q1. Revenue per lead did rise 1%, as Angi moved away from heavily discounted legacy ad products.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. service requests fell 6% and leads fell 13% year-over-year,” while “revenue per lead rose 1%” due to shifting away from discounted legacy ad products.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 “Proprietary Service Requests +17%, Proprietary Leads +13%” and said pro count and churn were the “core bear thesis,” with stabilization important.

surprises.description: Management said July EBITDA margin was already several hundred basis points above Q2, an encouraging improvement in the near-term profitability trajectory that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July EBITDA margin was already several hundred basis points above Q2.”

surprises.description: Angi shifted about $6 million of inefficient TV advertising spend to higher-ROI channels in Q2 and expects to remove a comparable amount in Q3. The preview had not anticipated this specific marketing reallocation and planned further reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reallocated about $6 million of inefficient TV spend in Q2 to higher-ROI channels” and “expects to remove a comparable amount in Q3.”

surprises.description: The large Pro segment is growing more than 20% year over year despite fewer than 10 sellers deployed year to date, with 30 planned by year-end. This is a positive growth and sales-expansion proof point not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of pro churn and revenue weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The large Pro segment is growing more than 20% year-over-year with fewer than 10 sellers deployed year-to-date,” with plans “to reach 30 sellers by year-end.”

surprises.description: Management described a sizable opportunity from increasing Angi’s penetration among large Pros: roughly $2.5 billion in revenue at small-to-midsized penetration levels and a longer-term $5 billion opportunity before Pro software and services. The preview did not flag these market-size estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: Matching small-to-midsized penetration in large Pro could bring revenue to “roughly $2.5 billion,” with “a longer-term $5 billion revenue opportunity before entering Pro software and services.”

surprises.description: Pro sales effectiveness and per-Pro capacity showed stronger figures than the preview had discussed: win rates were up about 20% year over year, and average capacity per Pro grew about 13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro win rates have risen roughly 20% year-over-year,” from “about 1 in 9 leads won two years ago to roughly 1 in 6 currently,” and “average capacity per Pro grew about 13% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Overall Pro capacity improved sharply from being down 13% in Q1 to roughly flat year over year in July. Management identified this as a key gate for returning to growth in 2027, a more specific improvement signal than the preview provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro capacity trends improved from down 13% in Q1 to down 2% in June and roughly flat in July year-over-year,” and are “a key gating factor for returning to growth in 2027.”

surprises.description: Angi said ChatGPT ads were already generating roughly $3 million in revenue run rate at a profit, an AI monetization result not anticipated by the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Generating roughly $3 million revenue run rate on ChatGPT ads at a profit.”

surprises.description: The first Pro AI agent, AI Front Desk, was live with dozens of Pros and about 80% retention, going beyond the preview’s expectation that the first agent would be testing within several weeks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its first Pro AI agent (AI Front Desk) is live with dozens of Pros and about 80% retention.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: On the Q1 call management targeted first agent testing “within several weeks.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed approximately $50 million in annual adjusted EBITDA minus CapEx as a target, whereas the preview characterized that figure as a directional floor rather than a commitment. The reaffirmation provides somewhat firmer support for the stated level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed its target of approximately $50 million in annual adjusted EBITDA minus CapEx.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said approximately “$50M/yr of Adjusted EBITDA less capex” was framed as a “directional floor, not a commitment.”

in_line: Management did not reinstate financial guidance, consistent with the preview’s expectation that guidance would remain absent unless the company reinstated a framework.
Management continued to place accelerated growth in 2027, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of material revenue acceleration in 2027.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case was about $69 million of adjusted EBITDA, with a guidance-implied range of roughly $65–75 million. ADV reported $76 million, a smaller year-over-year decline than the preview’s roughly 20% midpoint expectation, though below its stated $78 million threshold for a clear beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 12% to $76 million” (down 9% excluding divestitures).
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Base” adjusted EBITDA was “$69M (−20%)”; the preview also identified “~$65–75M guidance-implied band” and said “Above $78M = genuine beat.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the first half to account for only the low 40% range of full-year adjusted EBITDA, implying a more heavily backloaded year. Management instead said the second half would be about 53% of the total, implying roughly 47% in the first half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-half adjusted EBITDA will represent approximately 53% of the full-year total, with Q4 expected to exceed Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited management’s prior expectation that “the first half [would] represent in the low 40% range of full year adjusted EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Net revenue was above the preview’s $742 million base estimate and grew faster than its expected 0.8% year-over-year increase. The preview’s $887 million consensus was on a different, GAAP revenue basis, so it is not directly comparable to the reported net-revenue figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenues rose 3% year-over-year to $757 million (up 4% excluding divestitures).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was “Revenue (Net) … $742M (+0.8%).”

surprises.description: Experiential revenue growth was within the preview’s expected range, but adjusted EBITDA grew much faster than revenue. That contrasts with the preview’s base-case concern that growth in the segment would be margin-dilutive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Experiential Services was the standout segment, with revenues up 19% to $296 million and adjusted EBITDA up 32% to $34 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected Experiential growth of “15–20% but margin-dilutive”; it said to watch whether “EBITDA growth keeps pace with revenue.”

surprises.description: Retailer Services grew revenue but suffered a steep adjusted EBITDA decline, rather than showing the steadier performance suggested by its recent results and role as a higher-margin segment. Management attributed the decline partly to temporary higher execution costs on a new project.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retailer Services revenue grew 3% to $237 million but adjusted EBITDA fell approximately 25% to $20 million” due partly to “higher execution costs on a new project management deemed temporary.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Retailer as “the steady one” that carried “higher margins,” and cited Q1 Retailer revenue growth of 4.2% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 14.4%.

surprises.description: Net leverage was materially higher than the preview’s estimate, despite its expectation that another quarter of debt paydown would support deleveraging. Management said cash would primarily go toward debt reduction, but reported leverage of about 4.5x trailing EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $102 million in cash and net debt of approximately 4.5x trailing EBITDA,” with free cash flow directed primarily toward debt reduction.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net leverage … ~4.0–4.2x” and said “Another quarter of paydown de-risks the equity stub materially.”

surprises.description: The release quantified divestitures as a meaningful drag on both Q2 and full-year results, a headwind not addressed in the preview’s estimates. The Q2 impact also explains part of the difference between reported and excluding-divestiture performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Divestitures created a Q2 headwind of roughly $5 million to revenues and $3 million to adjusted EBITDA, with full-year 2026 headwinds expected at approximately $20 million to revenues and over $10 million to adjusted EBITDA.”

in_line: Branded Services’ revenue decline was broadly in line with the preview’s base case on an excluding-divestitures basis: reported revenue fell 13%, or 11% excluding divestitures, versus the preview’s expected decline of 9–11%.
ADV reiterated its full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, as well as adjusted unlevered free cash flow guidance of $250–275 million, as the preview expected.
Q2 adjusted unlevered free cash flow was weak but positive at $19 million, consistent with the preview’s warning that elevated DSO could make Q2 cash flow weak or negative.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $34 million, about 17% above the preview’s roughly $29.1 million consensus and above even its $32–34 million bull-case range’s lower end. This was a substantial beat against the expected quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $34 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2'26 Consensus | $29.08M (Zacks); $29.30M (alt. compiler)”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 27%, exceeding the preview’s roughly 24% estimate and its 25% bull-case threshold. The reported margin therefore came in well above the expected recovery from Q1’s 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 27% in Q2, up from 20% in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~24% (not formally polled)”; the bull case expected “≥25%.”

surprises.description: Amprius raised its full-year revenue floor to $140 million, up from $130 million. That exceeded the preview’s bull-case threshold of $135 million rather than merely reaffirming the existing guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second consecutive quarter to at least $140 million revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 guide: revenue ≥$130M”; the bull case anticipated a raise “to ≥$135M.”

surprises.description: Full-year gross-margin guidance rose to at least 28%, above the preview’s cited 25% FY target. The increase goes beyond the anticipated Q2 margin recovery and signals a higher full-year margin floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Raised] full-year 2026 guidance … to … at least 28% gross margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management reaffirmed a 25% FY target.”
