surprises.description: The company’s full-year net-loss ceiling moved from less than $8 million in the preview to $10 million or less. That is a looser loss target, despite the preview’s focus on how H1 losses already appeared to exceed the old full-year limit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amprius reiterated … a net loss of $10 million or less.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 guide: … net loss <$8.0M (≤$0.06/sh).”

surprises.description: Q2 GAAP net loss was $5.1 million, or $0.04 per share, versus the preview’s roughly $4.3 million expected loss and $0.03 per-share consensus. The company cited a one-time noncash $1.9 million warrant fair-value adjustment; adjusted net loss was $3.2 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss narrowed to $5.1 million (negative $0.04 per share) in Q2, including a onetime noncash $1.9 million warrant fair-value adjustment; adjusted net loss was $3.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) | ($0.03)”; the preview estimated “Q2 net loss is ~$4.3M.”

surprises.description: Cash ended Q2 at $74.5 million, up $12.2 million in the quarter, well above the preview’s $62.4 million starting balance and its flat-to-up expectation. The reported increase was supported by warrant and option exercises, rather than being presented as an operating-cash or AR-collection improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $74.5 million cash and no debt, up $12.2 million in the quarter, funded by $12.3 million from warrant exercises and $4.5 million from option exercises with no ATM program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$62.4M at Q1-end”; “Cash flat-to-up on AR collection is the tell.”

surprises.description: Amprius disclosed a three-year Stark Future contract expected to generate at least $100 million through 2029, with shipments beginning early next year. The preview discussed possible partner announcements but did not anticipate a contract of this scale or identify this customer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amprius signed a 3-year contract with Barcelona-based Stark Future expected to generate at least $100 million in revenue through 2029, with shipments starting early next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New order / partner announcements” were a catalyst to watch; the preview said additional US partner announcements were “expected.”

surprises.description: The company reported a new $24 million order from a European drone manufacturer for SA124 SiCore cylindrical cells, to be delivered over roughly 2.5 quarters. The preview watched for order conversion but did not specify or forecast this order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company won a new $24 million order from a European drone manufacturer for SA124 SiCore cylindrical cells, expected to be delivered over roughly 2.5 quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The question is conversion: how much flows to Amprius cells and when.”

surprises.description: Amprius said its cells are used by half of the 19 drone manufacturers invited to a Department of War demonstration, with a possible 60,000-drone order to follow for top performers. The preview discussed defense-customer awards and cell demand generally, but did not flag this specific demonstration or potential procurement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amprius cells are used by half of the 19 drone manufacturers invited to the Department of War's Fort Carson demonstration, after which the DoW plans to order 60,000 drones from top performers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted defense customers had received “~$500M in new orders” and asked “how much flows to Amprius cells and when.”

surprises.description: The preview expected announcements about additional US manufacturing partners, but the reported update identified Nanotech as the US partner and described a target of full US NDAA compliance in 2027 rather than announcing another partner. That leaves the anticipated near-term partner announcement unreported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 2 GWh of annual capacity across four China partners, three South Korea partners, and U.S. partner Nanotech, targeting full U.S. NDAA compliance in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said pouch-cell announcements with additional US partners were ‘expected.’”

surprises.description: The preview framed the key mix debate as US defense versus China LEV, while the reported results said EMEA generated 68% of revenue. This makes EMEA the dominant stated regional contributor, a geographic mix detail the preview had not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SiCore accounting for 98% of revenue and EMEA driving 68% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mix: US defense vs. China LEV.”

in_line: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance above $4 million was reiterated, in line with the preview’s ≥$4.0 million guide.
SiCore represented 98% of revenue, close to the preview’s statement that it was 97% of Q1 product revenue.
The company continued to report no debt, consistent with the preview’s no-debt description.

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EPS growth was stronger than the preview’s 9.3% consensus growth expectation: Cencora reported 12% growth, implying roughly $4.48 per share versus the $4.37 consensus estimate. The preview’s higher $4.43 whisper proxy was also below that implied result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EPS grew 12%, supported by $1 billion of opportunistic share repurchases executed at an average price of $268 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS $4.37” versus “$4.00” a year earlier; “Most Accurate” (whisper proxy) was “$4.43.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income grew 17% to $1.2 billion, well ahead of the preview’s low Q3 bar: its summed segment estimates implied only about 3.9% growth. The preview expected much of the year’s acceleration to be back-loaded into Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income grew 17% to $1.2 billion, with double-digit growth across both reportable segments and the 'other' category.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Summed segment OI of ~$1,099M is only +3.9% YoY” and “The Street is loading essentially the entire back-half acceleration into Q4.”

surprises.description: U.S. Healthcare Solutions operating income substantially exceeded the preview’s $940.9 million consensus and its expected 4.3% growth, reaching $966 million with 16% growth. The preview said $960 million or more would de-risk the Q4 ramp, and Cencora also reported double-digit organic growth excluding One Oncology and the lost customer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Healthcare Solutions operating income grew 16% to $966 million, delivering double-digit organic growth even when excluding One Oncology and the lost oncology customer, a sharp acceleration from 7% last quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “USHS segment op income $940.9M” and “+4.3%”; the preview added, “Anything ≥$960M de-risks the Q4 hockey stick materially.”

surprises.description: International Healthcare Solutions operating income grew far faster than the preview’s 1.4% expectation, rising 21% as reported and 23% in constant currency. The reported strength was partly helped by favorable timing of manufacturer price adjustments, making the beat less purely operational.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International Healthcare Solutions operating income rose 21% as-reported (23% constant currency) to $166 million, aided by favorable manufacturer price adjustment timing in a developing market country.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IHS segment op income $158.5M” and “+1.4%.”

surprises.description: Cencora raised both ends of its FY26 adjusted EPS range by $0.05, rather than merely narrowing to the upper end of the existing range as the preview’s base case anticipated. The increase was positive but smaller than the preview’s bull-case operational raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cencora raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.75-$17.95, up from the prior $17.70-$17.90 range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as “FY26 narrowed to upper half ($17.80–$17.90)” and the bull case as “FY26 raised to ≥$17.90–$18.05 on operations.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a quantified FY27 earnings headwind if the MWI/Covetrus merger closes midyear: roughly $150 million of operating income, or about $0.35 per share. The preview flagged the deal and regulatory uncertainty but did not anticipate a quantified impact on FY27.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A mid-fiscal-year MWI/Covetrus merger close would create a ~$150 million operating income headwind, netting to roughly a $0.35 EPS headwind, as a modeling consideration for fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged an “MWI Animal Health / Covetrus” regulatory update and said any “divestitures, timeline slippage, or deal risk” was live Q&A; it also cited FY27 EPS consensus of “$19.81.”

surprises.description: Management lowered International revenue growth expectations to approximately 8% (7% in constant currency) because of a stronger dollar. The preview discussed International operating income and reported a segment revenue consensus, but did not anticipate this reduction in the revenue outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered International revenue growth expectations to approximately 8% (7% constant currency) due to a stronger dollar.”

surprises.description: U.S. revenue was guided to the lower half of the existing 4%-6% growth range, a softer outlook than the preview’s broad company-level range alone suggested. The preview did not give a specific U.S. forward-growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided U.S. revenue to the lower half of the 4%-6% growth range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue growth 4–6%.”

surprises.description: Gross profit margin expanded 61 basis points, with management attributing the increase largely to One Oncology. The preview was watching for the acquisition’s accretion ramp after noting a smaller-than-expected contribution in Q2, but it did not forecast this margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin expanding 61 basis points to 4.16%, largely driven by the One Oncology acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said One Oncology contributed “smaller than expected” operating income in Q2 and called Q3 “the first clean quarter,” with a quantified contribution a key item to watch.

in_line: Consolidated revenue was broadly in line with the preview’s headline consensus: $84.8 billion reported versus $84.89 billion expected, with reported growth of 5% versus the preview’s 5.2% estimate.

surprises.description: CDW reported Q2 net sales of $6.6 billion, up 10%, well above the preview’s $6.21–6.26 billion consensus range and expected 3.8%–4.7% growth. The sales beat was much larger than anticipated, although gross profit came in around the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales of $6.6 billion (up 10%)” and gross profit of “$1.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Consensus | $6.21–6.26B | +3.8% to +4.7%”; gross profit estimate “~$1.29–1.31B.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin fell to 20.1%, down 70 basis points year over year, substantially below the preview’s estimated 20.6%–20.9% and its expectation of flat to down 20 basis points. CDW attributed the decline to large enterprise hardware infrastructure deals and a lower relative services contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin declined 70 basis points year-over-year to 20.1%,” driven by “mix shift toward large enterprise hardware infrastructure deals and lower relative services contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | *~20.6–20.9%* | flat to -20bps”; the preview also said “Below ~20.5% is a problem.”

surprises.description: CDW raised its full-year outlook beyond the preview’s expected framing: it now expects high-end high-single-digit non-GAAP EPS growth rather than the high end of mid-single digits, and mid-single-digit gross profit growth rather than low-to-mid single digits. The 200–300 basis-point outperformance expectation for the U.S. IT market was reiterated, not raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “raised full-year guidance,” expecting “mid-single-digit gross profit growth, high-end high-single-digit non-GAAP EPS growth, and US IT market growth in the mid-single digits with 200-300 bps of CDW outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected gross profit growth of “low-to-mid single digits,” non-GAAP EPS growth at the “high end of mid-single digits,” and “200–300bps” outperformance.

surprises.description: Despite the sales and EPS strength, CDW expects full-year gross margin to be modestly below 2025, with second-half margin below the comparable 2025 period. That is weaker than the preview’s expectation that full-year margin would be approximately in line with 2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 gross margin is expected to be modestly below 2025,” with “second-half gross margins projected below second-half 2025 levels due to product and end-market mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guide is ‘approximately in line with 2025.’”

surprises.description: Adjusted free cash flow conversion was sharply lower in the first half than the preview’s recent-quarter comparison suggested: it was 42% of non-GAAP net income versus 85% in Q1, and management said it was well below its 80%–90% target. A roughly $400 million inventory increase drove the shortfall, which management expects to normalize by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half adjusted free cash flow was $278 million (42% of non-GAAP net income), well below the 80-90% target,” driven by “a roughly $400 million inventory increase” that management expects “to normalize by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 adjusted FCF $251M at 85% conversion”; the preview also flagged adjusted FCF and buyback as a key item to watch.

surprises.description: Government sales rose about 14%, stronger than the preview’s concern that federal weakness could continue to weigh on the segment. The preview highlighted federal declines and described state and local growth as masking them; the reported overall government growth was considerably stronger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Government net sales rose approximately 14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 Government was “+4.6% with state/local double-digit masking federal decline” and flagged federal/government commentary as a key debate.

surprises.description: International growth accelerated to approximately 23%, ahead of the preview’s expectation that the U.K. and Canada would sustain the +17.9% pace seen in Q1; Canada also had a record quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International grew approximately 23% (a record quarter in Canada).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull-case requirements included “UK/Canada sustaining the +17.9% pace seen in Q1.”

surprises.description: CDW’s non-GAAP EPS grew 11.9% and operating income grew 7%, both faster than gross profit growth of 6.3%. That is a more favorable operating-leverage picture than the preview’s cited Q1 negative jaws and its call for evidence of SG&A leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS growth of 11.9% and operating income growth of 7% both exceeded gross profit growth of 6.3%,” signaling “an inflection toward improved operating leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q1 SG&A +7.0% vs. GP +6.0% — negative jaws” and said investors wanted “an SG&A leverage datapoint.”

surprises.description: CFO Al Miralles announced that he plans to retire in 2027, a management succession development not anticipated in the preview. The call said the transition would be orderly and that a successor search is underway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Al Miralles announced plans to retire in 2027 after completion of an orderly transition, with a search for his successor currently underway.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS of $2.91 exceeded both the $2.80 consensus and management’s prior $2.79–$2.83 guidance range, though the beat was much smaller than the sales surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $2.91 (up 11.9%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | Consensus | $2.80”; management’s Q2 guide was “high single-digit YoY growth → $2.79–2.83.”

in_line: Gross profit was $1.3 billion, approximately within the preview’s estimated $1.29–1.31 billion range, despite the much larger-than-expected sales beat.
Non-GAAP operating income of $556 million was within the preview’s derived $545–560 million estimate.
CDW reiterated 200–300 basis points of outperformance versus the U.S. IT market, as the preview expected.
Services revenue grew only 1%, broadly consistent with the preview’s cautious baseline of services remaining around flat.

surprises.description: BioCryst raised 2026 total-revenue guidance to $690–$715 million, above both its previous $635–$660 million range and the preview’s $669.4 million Street estimate. The increase was substantially larger than the preview’s scenario for a possible guide raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to $690-$715 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue (Street): $669.4M”; “A raise is the cleanest bull catalyst”; bull scenario: “guide raised to ≥$640–655M.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP operating profit was far above the preview’s estimate, at $113.2 million versus roughly $58–$62 million. This is a large quarterly beat, though the call facts also report a sizable license payment that boosted revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted a non-GAAP operating profit of $113.2 million for the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating profit: ~$58–62M (my est.).”

surprises.description: Q2 total revenue was boosted by a $55.7 million navenibart European license upfront payment, making revenue materially higher than the preview’s $166–$169 million anchor expectation. The preview mentioned a possible unmodeled Neopharmed payment as an explanation for an aggregator outlier, but did not use it as its base expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 45% year-over-year on a comparable basis, boosted by $55.7 million recognized from the navenibart European license upfront payment with Neopharmed Gentili.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anchor on $166–169M total”; the preview also described the $183.3M aggregator figure as possibly “including a Neopharmed milestone nobody else is modeling.”

surprises.description: ORLADEYO revenue of $158.2 million came in slightly below the $161 million consensus estimate, although it was within the preview’s $158–$164 million base-case range and comparable growth was close to the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ORLADEYO revenue reached $158.2 million in Q2 2026, growing 10% year-over-year on a comparable basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ORLADEYO net revenue: $161M”; base scenario: “$158–164M.”

surprises.description: Pediatric pellets had already generated 47 prescriptions through July 31, exceeding the total number the company had expected for all of 2026. The preview treated pediatric revenue conservatively and focused on confirming availability, not on prescriptions running ahead of the full-year expectation so early.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ORLADEYO pediatric pellets received 47 prescriptions through July 31, already exceeding the total expected for all of 2026, with several prescriptions coming from physicians new to prescribing ORLADEYO.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pediatric ORLADEYO pellets … available early August 2026”; “peds was conservatively modeled.”

surprises.description: BioCryst reported positive cash flow even excluding the license upfront payment, alongside cash of just over $350 million. That is a stronger cash-generation update than the preview’s balance-sheet snapshot alone implied, though no specific cash-flow forecast was provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “ended with just over $350 million in cash, generating positive cash flow even excluding the license upfront payment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “cash $259M ($331M pro forma with the $70M Neopharmed upfront)” and highlighted the balance sheet as “the underappreciated item.”

surprises.description: Management said excess cash flow could support business development, debt reduction, and/or buybacks. This broadened the capital-allocation possibilities discussed, but management did not announce a specific transaction or commitment.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “signaled flexibility to pursue business development, debt reduction, and/or buybacks with excess cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said capital-structure commentary was a key watch item and that “any commentary on refinancing or buying back the royalty obligation is a genuine re-rating lever”; its base case assumed “no BD.”

in_line: ORLADEYO’s roughly 10% comparable year-over-year growth was close to the preview’s roughly 11% ex-Europe estimate, despite revenue being slightly below the $161 million consensus.
ORLADEYO full-year guidance remained at $625–$645 million, consistent with the preview’s base case of a reaffirmation and its note that the pediatric delay was not expected to affect 2026 guidance.
The $420–$440 million non-GAAP operating-cost range and the internal-discovery/Birmingham restructuring were already described in the preview as announced on June 29.
The preview expected ALPHA-ORBIT to be fully enrolled and top-line data in Q3 2027; the call confirmed completed enrollment and the same top-line timing.
BCX17725’s Netherton syndrome proof-of-concept work and year-end clinical-data timing matched the preview’s expected year-end checkpoint.

Management’s view that newer injectable competitors are mainly taking share from TAKHZYRO rather than ORLADEYO repeated the competitive framing already reported after Q1 and highlighted in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview warned that warrant and derivative marks might produce a large non-cash gain and a misleading EPS beat. Instead, Eos reported a $276 million net loss, driven primarily by non-cash fair-value adjustments to warrants and derivatives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss of $276 million” and “the net loss [was] driven primarily by non-cash fair value adjustments to warrants and derivatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With the stock down sharply through Q2, warrant liabilities likely marked down again — a large non-cash gain.”

surprises.description: The call cited adjusted gross margin of negative 52% and product adjusted gross margin of negative 40%, substantially less negative than the preview’s expected gross margin of negative 69% to negative 73%. The measures are not explicitly stated to be on the same basis, so this is a favorable difference in the reported figures, not a clean like-for-like comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was negative 52% and product adjusted gross margin improved to negative 40%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: -69% to -73%” and “The percentage improved 5–9pts QoQ.”

surprises.description: The preview expected adjusted gross margin to turn positive before year-end 2026, while the call described a roughly 10% gross-margin target by Q2 2027. The call did give a quantified improvement bridge of more than 72 points over 12 months, making the plan more specific even as the stated target date is later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 72 points of adjusted gross margin improvement over the next 12 months,” targeting “roughly 10% gross margins by Q2 2027,” with specified contributions from materials, conversion costs, field services, and yield.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. GM-positive timing” was listed as “before year-end”; the preview also said the key question was whether management would provide a credible cost-down bridge.

surprises.description: Eos disclosed that one Frontier Power-related project generated about 80% of Q2 revenue and that about half of backlog now comes from that affiliated entity. The preview discussed Frontier funding and project pipeline but did not flag this degree of revenue and backlog concentration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One Frontier Power-related project accounted for roughly 80% of Q2 revenue,” and “roughly 50% of backlog now derives from that single affiliated entity.”

surprises.description: The company said it would consolidate Line 1 into Thorn Hill, expecting an additional 10–15% reduction in conversion costs with about a nine-month payback. The preview focused on unit-cost reductions but did not anticipate this specific consolidation, which also temporarily sacrifices revenue at the top of guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidating Line 1 into the Thorn Hill facility is expected to deliver an additional 10-15% reduction in conversion costs with an estimated payback period of approximately 9 months,” while “temporarily sacrific[ing] near-term revenue at the top of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors needed to see “falling unit cost” and a “credible unit-cost bridge,” but did not mention consolidating Line 1 into Thorn Hill.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $68.8 million was essentially the pre-announced $68–69 million and consensus estimate of $68.77 million.
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $71.4 million was within the preview’s expected range of negative $67 million to negative $72 million.
FY26 revenue guidance of $300–350 million was broadly in line with the preview’s expected narrowing around $300–340 million, though the reported upper end was higher.
Quarter-end cash of $364 million matched the preview’s pre-announced cash figure of approximately $364 million.
Backlog of $807 million matched the preview’s pre-announced backlog figure.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.51, well above the preview’s $1.33 consensus and also above its estimated $1.38–$1.42 buy-side bar. That was a substantially stronger per-share result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income from continuing operations was $68 million, or $1.51 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.33”; “assume a buy-side bar of roughly $1.38–$1.42.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $481 million, versus the preview’s roughly $454–$458 million expectation for a flat-like-for-like quarter. The reported result was a clear beat and instead showed 7% organic growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue grew 7% organically to $481 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $453.9M (alt. feed $457.7M)” and “like-for-like… roughly flat revenue.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.9%, materially below the preview’s roughly 27.5% Q3 bogey and expected second-half step-up. Gross margin fell to 47% from 48.7%, as material and SG&A costs offset revenue gains; management pointed to continued price/cost catch-up in Q4. EBITDA dollars of $125 million, however, were close to the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose only 2% to $125 million as increased material and SG&A costs offset revenue gains, and EBITDA margin was 25.9%”; “Gross margin declined to 47% from 48.7%”; management expects “continued price/cost catch-up in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin vs. the ~27% second-half bogey”; the base case expected “$125–129M / ~27.5%” and described Q3 as the first full quarter of the price increase and a margin step-up.

surprises.description: Volume grew 1% instead of declining by the 5–6% the preview expected. That reversal was a favorable demand surprise, while the 6% price/mix contribution was close to the preview’s roughly 5% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue growth was driven by “6% favorable price/mix and 1% volume growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 ran volume -6%”; the base case expected “Volume -5/-6%, price/mix +5%.”

surprises.description: Griffon repaid the remaining $285 million Term Loan B balance and reported pro forma leverage of about 2.0x, slightly below the preview’s estimated 2.1–2.2x after the Australasia transaction. It also set a new 1.5–2.5x leverage target range, which the preview had not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repaid the remaining $285 million Term Loan B balance, lowered net leverage to a pro forma ~2.0x, and set a new leverage target range of 1.5x to 2.5x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “pro forma” leverage of “~2.1–2.2x” and described the buyback-versus-deleveraging split as a swing factor.

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 interest expense guidance fell to $80 million, $13 million below the prior $93 million outlook cited in the preview. The reduction reflects both debt paydown and interest income from the transaction PIK notes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 interest expense guidance was cut by $13 million to $80 million due to debt paydown and interest income from transaction PIK notes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance… interest expense $93M.”

in_line: Management maintained FY2026 guidance of $1.8 billion revenue and $458 million adjusted EBITDA, as the preview’s base case expected.
Adjusted EBITDA of $125 million was close to the preview’s $127 million estimate and within its $125–129 million base-case range, even though the margin was below expectations.
Price/mix contributed 6%, close to the preview’s expectation of about 5% and its forecast of continued price/mix benefit.

The Australasia JV closed on the expected terms: $181 million cash, a $49 million note, and a 49% equity interest; the preview already expected the closing and completion of the transformation into a pure-play building-products company.
A $0.22 quarterly dividend matched the preview’s stated dividend, and the expectation of Q4 as the seasonal high point was consistent with its seasonal-peak outlook.

surprises.description: LAW reported $43.1 million of Q2 revenue, $0.43 million above the $42.67 million consensus and $0.6 million above the prior guidance midpoint. The beat was positive but modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue was $43.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2'26 Consensus: $42.67M”; company guidance was “$41.5–43.5M (mid $42.5M).”

surprises.description: Software revenue, the preview’s key metric, came in slightly above the guidance midpoint and consensus estimate, rather than merely landing within the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Software revenue of $36.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Software revenue | ~$36.6M (guide mid)”; guidance was “$36.1–37.1M.”

surprises.description: Services revenue was higher than the preview’s implied estimate, contributing to the overall revenue beat; the preview had cautioned that services were lumpy and could make a total-revenue beat lower quality.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Services revenue of $6.3 million (up 18%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Services revenue | ~$5.9M implied”; the preview also said, “Services ($7.2M in Q1, +25%) is lumpy, large-matter-driven.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year revenue guidance, including a higher software-revenue floor, instead of maintaining the prior range. The increase was small at the midpoint, but it addressed the preview’s call for a genuine guidance raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 total revenue guidance was raised to $172 million-$179 million and software revenue to $147.5 million-$152.5 million, reflecting increased second-half confidence.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior guidance was “$169.25–178.75M” total and “$146–152.5M” software; the preview said a “genuine raise — especially to the software line — is the cleanest bullish signal available.”

surprises.description: The new DISCO platform commercial model reached its December year-end run-rate target by June, six months early, with both volume and pricing adoption ahead of expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new DISCO platform commercial model hit its December 2026 year-end run-rate target by June, with adoption exceeding expectations on both volume and pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case required that “the DISCO platform bundle converts to real ARR”; it did not anticipate the year-end run-rate target being reached by June.

surprises.description: Revenue attributable to generative and agentic AI more than tripled, giving the market a concrete monetization signal rather than only an adoption anecdote. The preview specifically identified AI-attributable revenue disclosure as a key watch item.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue attributable to generative AI and agentic AI capabilities more than tripled year-over-year, with Auto Review setting a new revenue record driven by record volume and larger average review size.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market wanted “attach rates, pricing, or disclosed AI-attributable revenue — not another adoption anecdote.”

surprises.description: The >$100,000 customer cohort’s TTM revenue growth accelerated from the previously reported 13% to 15%, and the cohort count rose from 347 to 354. This was stronger than the preview’s concern that customer-count growth could decelerate below 9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers generating more than $100,000 in trailing-12-month revenue grew to 354, representing $128 million or 77% of total revenue, up 15% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “347 customers >$100K TTM revenue, +9% YoY” and “$124M / 77% of TTM revenue, +13% YoY,” and flagged deceleration below +9% as a concern.

surprises.description: The Unified Litigation Solution launched, but management said investors should not include any solution revenue in 2026 models because it remains an unpriced pilot. The launch is progress, but it offers no near-term modeled revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched its new Unified Litigation Solution combining evidence and full U.S. case law, but management explicitly told investors not to build any solution revenue into models for 2026 as it remains in an unpriced pilot phase.”

surprises.description: Management flagged that lower ingest fees under the new platform model could become a future revenue headwind, although no meaningful drag has appeared yet. The preview did not identify this specific risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged a potential future revenue headwind from lower ingest fees under the new DISCO platform model, though no meaningful drag has materialized to date.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow was substantially less negative than a year earlier, a positive development against the preview’s focus on cash burn and the risk that it could erode faster than modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow improving to negative $1.1 million from negative $4.2 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted cash burn, noting “operating cash flow was −$11.7M in Q1” and that “any sign it is eroding faster than modeled matters.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $3.4 million, close to the preview’s roughly negative $3.5 million consensus and the midpoint of company guidance; the negative 8% margin was also in line with the preview’s expectation of about negative 8%.
Management reiterated that it expects adjusted EBITDA to turn positive in Q4, as the preview identified this as the central commitment to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.6%, well below the preview’s estimated 21.5%–22.0%; gross margin was 41%, rather than expanding from Q1’s 41.2% toward the preview’s roughly 41.5% base case. Management cited higher tariff costs and the absence of a prior-year tariff-capitalization benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell 72 basis points to 41% and adjusted EBITDA margin declined 223 basis points to 19.6%,” largely due to “higher tariff costs” and a prior-year “$3-3.5 million” non-cash tariff capitalization benefit that did not repeat.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin (est.) ~21.5–22.0%”; the base scenario expected “GM ~41.5%,” and the preview said gross margin “should expand.”

surprises.description: American Performance remained in decline at -2.1%, rather than returning to positive growth as the preview’s clean test of the Q1 destock explanation anticipated. The decline improved substantially from Q1’s -9.7%, but the division did not turn positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “American Performance sales declined 2.1% but improved sequentially from a 9.7% Q1 decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A return to positive validates the entire ‘sell-through was fine’ thesis”; the preview described Q2 as “the clean test.”

surprises.description: Sales were close to published consensus, but growth of 3.2% fell short of the preview’s roughly 6% management-derived whisper. Core sales growth was stronger at 4.9%, but still below that bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales grew 3.2% to $172 million, with core business net sales (excluding portfolio rebalancing) up 4.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited consensus net sales of “$172.6M” and a management-derived “~+6%” whisper, saying “the +6% is the whisper.”

surprises.description: The quarter produced a $2.4 million GAAP net loss, in contrast to the preview’s expectation of year-over-year EPS growth. The call attributed the loss to the divestiture of Brothers Trucks and Scott Drake.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a GAAP net loss of $2.4 million versus net income of $10.9 million a year earlier, driven by the divestiture of non-core restoration brands (Brothers Trucks and Scott Drake).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed diluted EPS consensus of “$0.11” versus “$0.09” a year earlier, or “+22%.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow reached $40.9 million, above the preview’s estimated $28–35 million range despite the difficult year-ago comparison. The result was partly aided by a one-time tariff refund, so it was not all recurring cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated $40.9 million in quarterly free cash flow, up $5.2 million year-over-year, aided by the one-time IEEPA tariff refund.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated free cash flow of “~$28–35M” and said it was expected to be down from the prior-year “$35.7M (record).”

surprises.description: Adjusted net income more than doubled, but the improvement included an unanticipated one-time tariff refund of about $10–11 million. That makes the strong adjusted earnings result less indicative of the underlying quarter than the headline growth suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income more than doubled year-over-year to $24 million from $10.6 million, though this was aided by a one-time ~$10-11 million IEEPA tariff refund.”

surprises.description: The previously unquantified national retail partnership was given a concrete figure: approximately $12 million of new retailer placements are due to launch in Q3. The call did not specify how much of that represents ongoing revenue or its margin profile.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured approximately $12 million of new national retailer placements launching in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the partnership was described as “meaningful incremental annual business” but was “unquantified,” and asked for “Q3 pipe-fill dollars, ongoing run-rate, and margin profile.”

surprises.description: Management said cost-reduction initiatives should deliver at or above the top of the previously stated $5–7 million range by year-end, indicating a better outcome than simply reaching the announced range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects cost reduction initiatives to deliver at or above the top end of its $5-7 million range by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “$5–7M more [was] expected in 2026.”

in_line: Net sales of $172 million were essentially in line with the $172.6 million published consensus, even though growth missed the higher management-derived whisper.
Full-year guidance was reaffirmed rather than cut again after the restoration-brand divestitures; the preview treated a clean restatement or maintaining the range as the base case.
Leverage fell to 3.74x, within the preview’s 3.65x–3.75x base-case range, and management reaffirmed its below-3.5x year-end target.

The company both repurchased stock and reduced debt: it bought approximately $2 million of stock during the quarter and made a $15 million voluntary debt repayment after quarter-end, consistent with the preview’s focus on whether management could do both.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $2.70, above both the preview’s approximately $2.42 whisper estimate and its $2.63 consensus estimate. The beat was meaningful, especially against the preview’s warning that consensus was lagging the lower whisper figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 13% year-over-year to $2.70.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Most Accurate Estimate (~$2.42) sits well below the $2.63 consensus”; “Score the print against ~$2.42, not $2.63.”

surprises.description: The company cut its full-year outlook more than the preview’s expected move toward 290,000–300,000 RV wholesale units: the new range starts at 280,000. Adjusted revenue guidance fell to $3.9–$4.1 billion from $4.2–$4.3 billion, and adjusted EPS guidance fell to $8.25–$8.75 from $8.75–$9.25.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year RV industry wholesale shipment forecast to 280,000-300,000 units from a prior 315,000-330,000, and now guides adjusted revenue of $3.9-$4.1 billion with adjusted EPS of $8.25-$8.75.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY units cut toward 290–300k; EPS trimmed to low end or withdrawn”; “A guidance revision is the base case, not the risk case.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted net sales declined 4%, rather than delivering the preview’s expected 1.4% growth. The reported $1.1 billion was also below the preview’s $1.12–$1.13 billion estimate range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated adjusted net sales declined 4% to $1.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales … Q2’26 Consensus $1.12–1.13B”; “YoY +1.4%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin reached 9.3%, above the preview’s approximately 8.9% consensus-implied margin and its 8.3% whisper-implied margin. This was a stronger margin outcome despite the revenue shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating profit grew 8% to $99 million with margin expanding 110 basis points to 9.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating margin ~8.9% (implied)”; “$2.42 whisper ⇒ ~$93M operating profit ⇒ ~8.3% margin.”

surprises.description: RV content per unit rose 11%, slightly below the preview’s +13% towable content-per-unit figure. The increase still held up despite a shift toward lower-content single-axle trailers, but it was a little less than the preview’s offset assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RV content per unit rose 11% year-over-year to $5,831 … despite an unfavorable mix shift toward lower-content single-axle trailers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Towable CPU was $5,826 (+13% YoY)”; “Any deceleration here breaks the offset story.”

surprises.description: Aftermarket sales grew 11%, ahead of the preview’s estimate of roughly 7% growth. The preview highlighted aftermarket as an important offset, but the reported growth was stronger than its segment build assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aftermarket sales grew 11%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Aftermarket … ~$286M … +7%.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that the top five innovations have a $270 million annualized revenue run rate and that another $140 million of business was awarded for the 2027 model year change. The preview did not quantify this product-driven revenue pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The top 5 innovations are generating an estimated $270 million annualized revenue run rate, with an additional $140 million of new business awarded for the 2027 model year change.”

surprises.description: The company said nearly $90 million of IHEPA tariff refunds would be passed through to customers with minimal P&L impact, rather than appearing as a meaningful earnings benefit. The preview did not discuss these refunds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will return nearly $90 million in IHEPA tariff refunds to customers as a pass-through with minimal P&L impact, having handled the recovery internally rather than paying third-party contingency fees.”

surprises.description: Management added a longer-term aftermarket demand signal: roughly 1.5 million units with $15 billion of installed LCI content are entering repair cycles. The preview emphasized aftermarket growth but did not identify this installed-base repair-cycle opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 1.5 million units backed by $15 billion of installed LCI content are entering repair cycles as a future aftermarket tailwind.”

in_line: The preview expected a reduction in the full-year RV unit outlook and a trim to full-year adjusted EPS; the company did cut both, although the unit range extended below the preview’s anticipated 290,000–300,000 framework.
The company maintained its 7.5%–8.0% full-year adjusted operating margin guidance, consistent with the existing range cited in the preview.
Adjusted operating profit of $99 million was close to the preview’s approximately $100 million consensus-implied estimate.

surprises.description: Nextdoor reported 22.9 million WAU, above the preview’s 22.3–22.6 million base-case range and above its >22.8 million bull threshold. The second straight quarter of sequential growth was expected as a possibility, but the reported level was stronger than the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Platform WAU hit an all-time high of 22.9 million, up 5% year-over-year and rising sequentially for the second consecutive quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “22.3–22.6M”; its bull case expected “>22.8M (+5% YoY).”

surprises.description: Self-serve revenue grew 32%, accelerating from 28% and exceeding the preview’s base-case 26–28% range and its bull-case threshold of at least 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The self-serve channel grew 32% year-over-year (accelerating from 28% last quarter).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a base case of “~70% of revenue at ~26–28%” and a bull case requiring self-serve growth of “≥30%.”

surprises.description: Despite the faster self-serve growth, its revenue share was about 67%, below the preview’s roughly 70% base- and bull-case markers and down from the 68% share cited for Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: Self-serve “now represents roughly 67% of total revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 at “68% of revenue” and described a base case of “~70%” and a bull case of “≥70% mix.”

surprises.description: Nextdoor raised full-year guidance to low-teens revenue growth and approximately 10% adjusted EBITDA margin, stronger than the preview’s roughly 10% revenue-growth and high-single-digit margin baseline. The revenue outlook is around the preview’s bull case, while the margin is at the low end of its low-double-digit bull-case description.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to low-teens revenue growth and an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described existing guidance as “~10% revenue growth” and a “high single digit” EBITDA margin; its bull case called for “~12% growth and low-double-digit EBITDA margin.”

in_line: Revenue of $75 million exceeded the company’s $73 million guide high end, but was within the preview’s $74–75 million whisper range.
Adjusted EBITDA of $10 million was well above the company’s $4–6 million guide, but matched the top of the preview’s $8–10 million whisper range.

surprises.description: ZBH reported Q2 sales of $2.177 billion and 4% organic constant-currency growth, above the preview’s $2.13–$2.14 billion revenue consensus and its 2.5%–3.5% base-case organic-growth range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales reached $2.177 billion, up 4.8% reported and 4% organic constant currency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $2.13B (Zacks) / $2.14B (Street)” and the Base scenario expected “organic cc 2.5–3.5%.”

surprises.description: The company raised its FY2026 organic constant-currency growth range to 2.25%–3.25% from 1%–3%. The preview wanted the floor raised to at least 2%, so the new floor cleared that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 organic constant currency revenue guidance to 2.25%-3.25% from 1%-3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side wants the low end lifted to ≥2%” and the catalyst checklist says “the buy-side wants the floor raised.”

surprises.description: Technology, Data, Bone Cement and Surgical grew 21.5%, far above the segment’s 5.7% consensus estimate; U.S. technology sales rose over 50%, driven by ROSA rather than one-time bone-cement events.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Technology, Data, Bone Cement and Surgical segment grew 21.5%, with U.S. technology sales up over 50%, driven by ROSA robotics rather than one-time bone cement events.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Segment consensus growth (Zacks): … Technology, Data, Bone Cement & Surgical +5.7%.”

surprises.description: Hips grew well ahead of the preview’s segment estimate: U.S. Hips grew 5.9% and overall Hips grew 5.1% constant currency, versus 1.7% consensus. The reported U.S. adoption of Z1, HAMMR and OrthoGrid provided concrete growth drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Hips grew 5.9% (5.1% constant currency overall), driven by the Z1 stem now exceeding 40% of U.S. hip stems, HAMMR used in over 25% of U.S. primary hip cases, and record OrthoGrid adoption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Segment consensus growth (Zacks): Knees +1.9% · Hips +1.7%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin fell to 71.1% and adjusted operating margin to 25.7%, rather than holding gross margin stable as management had previously indicated. The reported declines were 120 and 210 basis points, respectively.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin fell 120 basis points to 71.1% and adjusted operating margin fell 210 basis points to 25.7%, reflecting higher manufacturing costs and channel investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “guided gross margin stable through year-end” and flagged the “Adj. operating margin (27.3% Q1) and gross margin (73%)” as metrics to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $2.07, beating the $2.01 consensus and avoiding the decline the preview expected, although EPS was flat year over year. The preview’s base-case range of $2.03–$2.08 had otherwise anticipated a result around this level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $2.07, flat versus prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $2.01 | −2.9%” and the Base scenario expected “$2.03–$2.08.”

surprises.description: The iodine core hip launch in Japan was described as outpacing supply, selling at a 40% price premium and converting both existing and competing accounts—an upbeat product-launch update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The iodine core hip launch in Japan (a ~$0.5 billion market) is outpacing supply, commanding a 40% price premium and converting both existing and competitive accounts.”

surprises.description: Paragon 28 is expected to contribute 110 basis points to FY reported sales growth, 10 basis points more than the company’s initial expectation; integration was also described as largely complete.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paragon 28 is growing mid-teens with commercial integration largely complete, contributing 110 basis points to full-year reported sales growth versus an initial expectation of 100 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call described the “initial expectation of 100 basis points.”

in_line: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $8.47–$8.59 from $8.40–$8.55, consistent with the preview’s expectation that a raise was largely expected and with its Street estimate of $8.47–$8.48.
The FY2026 buyback plan was up to $1 billion, in line with the preview’s stated $1.0 billion FY26 plan; $500 million had been repurchased in the first half.

surprises.description: Orthofix disclosed that a European distributor arrangement is expected to add about $15 million of 2026 sales, mostly in Q4, but create an approximately $22 million sales headwind in 2027. The preview did not flag this near-term sales lift and subsequent-year drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A strategic arrangement with a European distributor funding MDR certification is expected to contribute ~$15 million of incremental net sales in 2026 (mostly in Q4), but creates an approximately $22 million net sales headwind in 2027.”

surprises.description: The expected H2 acceleration did not materialize in the outlook: excluding the EU arrangement, management expects core organic growth of only roughly 2–3%, with Q3 sales roughly consistent with Q2. The preview said management had indicated about 6% growth in H2 was needed, making the outlook notably weaker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the ~$15 million EU MDR benefit, core organic revenue growth in the second half is expected to slow to roughly 2-3%, driven by ongoing weakness among smaller U.S. spine distributors, and Q3 net sales are expected to be roughly consistent with Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said Q2 needed ~6% cc growth to hit the ~5% H1 target, accelerating to ~6% in H2.”

surprises.description: Q2 pro forma constant-currency sales growth was 5%, below the roughly 6% Q2 pace the preview said was needed to meet the H1 growth target. The reported growth rate was positive, but fell short of that stated hurdle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orthofix delivered 5% pro forma constant currency net sales growth year-over-year in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said Q2 needed ~6% cc growth to hit the ~5% H1 target.”

surprises.description: U.S. Spine Fixation grew only 3% as smaller distributors declined steeply, despite the preview's expectation that the earlier distributor transition was largely behind the company and its call for Q2 growth to support acceleration. The top 30 distributors continued to perform well, so weakness was concentrated among smaller accounts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Spine Fixation grew only 3% due to steep declines among smaller distributors, while the top 30 distributors representing ~80% of Spine Fixation sales continued performing well.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 called the first wave ‘largely behind us,’ with top-30 distributors +27% y/y. Management said Q2 needed ~6% cc growth… Tier-2 conversions were slated for 2026 — any repeat of the biologics disruption is a fresh negative.”

surprises.description: Global Limb Reconstruction grew 11% on a constant-currency basis, ahead of the preview's roughly 7% reported-growth estimate, but the growth came mainly from international demand while U.S. growth was below expectations. That mix differed from the preview's expectation of a U.S. recovery toward double-digit growth in H2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global Limb Reconstruction net sales grew 11% on a constant currency basis to $37.7 million, led by international demand for TrueLok Elevate and FITBONE, while U.S. growth came in below expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global Limb Reconstruction ~$35.5M (+7% rep.).” The preview also listed “U.S. Limb Reconstruction back to double-digit growth in H2.”

surprises.description: Biologics sales were approximately flat for a second consecutive quarter, a stabilization that the preview had not forecast and that contrasts with its concern about a possible repeat of distributor-related disruption. Management nevertheless stopped short of calling it a sustained return to growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Biologics net sales were approximately flat year-over-year, marking a second consecutive quarter of improvement from double-digit declines in 2025, though management stopped short of declaring a sustained return to growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tier-2 conversions were slated for 2026 — any repeat of the biologics disruption is a fresh negative.”

surprises.description: Therapeutic Solutions grew 3% to $64.2 million, slightly below the preview's estimate of about $65 million and 4% growth. The segment still grew despite temporary reimbursement pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Therapeutic Solutions generated $64.2 million in net sales, up 3% year-over-year despite temporary reimbursement pressure during part of the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Therapeutic Solutions/BGT ~$65M (+4%).”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted gross margin was 71.7%, with management citing unfavorable geographic mix, international credit losses, and continued launch investment as pressures. The preview did not identify these specific margin headwinds, even though its EBITDA estimate was broadly in line with the reported result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted gross margin was 71.7%, pressured by unfavorable geographic mix, international credit losses, and continued launch investments.”

in_line: FY2026 net sales guidance of $845–855 million matched the preview's base case of partial restoration ($845–855 million), though it was below the preview's full-restoration case of $850–860 million.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $95–98 million restored the level the preview identified as the pre-May expectation.

CMS restored Medicare reimbursement retroactive to May 18, consistent with the reversal the preview expected; the preview also anticipated that the reimbursement change could be worth about $12 million to guidance.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $20.1 million was within the preview's estimated range of roughly $19–21 million.

surprises.description: Inventory rose to $8.6 million from $7.1 million at Q1-end, rather than drawing down; management said it was building buffer stock ahead of the facility move. That is a larger build than the preview’s Q1-end figure and its stated focus on inventory drawdown and burn suggested investors would watch for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventories grew to $8.6 million from $5.6 million at the start of the year, reflecting buffer stock building ahead of the planned facility relocation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The question is inventory drawdown and burn.” The preview also reported Q1-end inventory of “$7.1M.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $8.3 million, just below the preview’s lowest cited estimate of $8.36 million, though it remained within the preview’s $8.0–$8.8 million base-case range. Management expected shipments to continue at a similar pace from the current backlog, providing some forward reassurance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $8.3 million” and management expected “shipments to continue at a similar pace given current backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited revenue estimates of “$8.36M” and “$8.89M,” and a base case of “$8.0–8.8M.”

surprises.description: The company is close to finalizing a lease for a facility twice the size of its current site, but the relocation timeline has slipped from management’s earlier estimates. The preview had flagged that no site had yet been selected, so lease progress is favorable, while the delay remains a concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Close to finalizing a lease for a new facility twice the size of its current location,” though “the timeline has slipped from initial overly aggressive estimates.” Design and permitting are expected to take “3-4 months,” followed by “7-8 months” for construction and installation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the site was “not yet selected” and had been “taking longer than expected”; it flagged watching for “a signed site” and the relocation timeline.

surprises.description: Congressional funding has been approved for CPS HybridTech Armor ballistic shields on Navy destroyers, with contracts expected later this year. This creates a path for that product to return to revenue that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Congressional funding has been approved for CPS HybridTech Armor ballistic shields on Navy destroyers, with contracts expected to be issued later this year, marking a return to revenue for that product.”

surprises.description: Cash and marketable securities were $19.2 million, below the preview’s expectation of liquidity at roughly $20 million or more after the offering. The difference is modest, but the reported balance came in below that post-offering expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined cash and marketable securities” were “$19.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma for ~$9.0M net proceeds, liquidity should be ~$20M+.”

surprises.description: SG&A increased to $1.5 million from $1.2 million, largely because of one-time, noncash stock-option expenses. The preview raised the possibility of first-quarter cleanups but did not anticipate this specific expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A rose to $1.5 million from $1.2 million a year ago, driven largely by one-time noncash stock option expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the first reported quarter for the new CFO could bring “possible reserve/estimate cleanups.”

surprises.description: The Navy exercised a six-month option in June for ACV lightweighting work, extending that program. The preview did not mention this option exercise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Navy exercised a 6-month ACV lightweighting option in June.”

surprises.description: A backlog of SBIR/STTR proposals dating back to August 2024 is still awaiting government funding decisions, indicating that this potential work remains unresolved. The preview did not flag these pending decisions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A backlog of SBIR/STTR proposals dating back to August 2024 still awaits government funding decisions.”

surprises.description: Army-funded tungsten warhead development is scheduled to run through fall 2027, providing a longer-dated program runway not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Army-funded tungsten warhead development runs through fall 2027.”

in_line: Net income was roughly breakeven at $40,000, or $0.00 per share, matching the preview’s $0.00–$0.02 EPS range and its roughly breakeven base case.

Gross margin recovered to 14.8% from Q1’s 8.6%, within the preview’s 11–15% base-case range and above its 13–14% concern threshold; it remained below Q2 2025’s 16.5%, with higher material and plating costs cited.

surprises.description: Corebridge reported operating EPS of $1.12, above the $1.08 consensus, despite a weak contribution from Variable Investment Income. Run-rate operating EPS was $1.35 after adjusting for below-target VII, indicating stronger underlying earnings than the headline comparison suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted pretax operating income was $664 million with EPS of $1.12, while run rate operating EPS reached $1.35, up 16% year-over-year after adjusting for below-target Variable Investment Income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating EPS: Q2 2026 consensus $1.08.”

surprises.description: Variable Investment Income remained weak and management expects it to stay below target for the rest of the year, rather than rebound. That leaves Corebridge diverging from peers that were guiding to second-half improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Variable Investment Income underperformed due to weak private equity marks and is expected to remain below target for the remainder of the year, diverging from peers guiding to second-half improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Variable investment income was weak in Q1 ($22M vs. $88M a year ago) — watch for a rebound, as it swings operating EPS quarter to quarter.”

surprises.description: The merger’s combined-company targets are more specific and accelerated than the preview’s stated synergy and accretion goals: management now targets $5 billion of earnings, $4 billion of cash generation, and over 15% ROE by 2027. The preview described more than $500 million of synergies and over 10% EPS accretion by the end of 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The combined Corebridge-Equitable company targets $5 billion of earnings, $4 billion of cash generation, and over 15% ROE by 2027, supported by $500 million in cost synergies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The companies target more than $500 million of run-rate expense synergies and >10% EPS accretion by end-2028.”

surprises.description: Buybacks are set to slow sharply after Q2: management expects only approximately $350 million of repurchases in the second half, despite more than $1.4 billion of holdco liquidity above 12-month needs. That implies about $1.9 billion of buybacks for 2026, a slower pace than the preview’s question about whether the large buyback pace would continue ahead of the merger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to only approximately $350 million in share repurchases for the second half despite holding over $1.4 billion in holdco liquidity exceeding 12-month needs, implying roughly $1.9 billion of total 2026 buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Merger execution: any update on regulatory approvals (‘on track’ as of the Q1 call), integration planning, synergy phasing, and whether the buyback pace continues ahead of the close.”

surprises.description: Institutional Markets reversed the weak flow trend highlighted in the preview, with APTOI up 36% year over year and reserves expanding 17%. The quarter also included $1.8 billion of GIC issuances, and management described the low GIC share of the general account as room to grow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Institutional Markets APTOI grew 36% year-over-year on 17% reserve expansion, with $1.8 billion of GIC issuances in the quarter”; GICs are “just 5% of the general account versus 10-15% for peers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Institutional Markets premiums/deposits fell 45%. Watch flows and spread income in the retirement businesses.”

surprises.description: Life Insurance’s run-rate APTOI came in above the top of guidance on favorable mortality, outperforming the weak segment trend suggested by the prior quarter. Reported APTOI still fell year over year, but the run-rate result was better than management’s stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Life Insurance delivered run rate APTOI of $122 million above the top end of guidance on favorable mortality, though reported APTOI declined 11% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 adjusted pre-tax operating income fell YoY in Individual Retirement (−9%), Group Retirement (−28%), and Life (−11%).”

surprises.description: Regulatory progress was more concrete than the preview’s description of approvals as the main remaining merger condition: federal antitrust and FINRA approvals are complete, all state and international filings have been submitted, and the deal remains on track for a year-end close.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The merger regulatory process is advancing with federal antitrust and FINRA approvals complete and all state/international filings submitted, keeping the transaction on track to close by year-end 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With both shareholder bases having approved the Equitable merger on July 30 … regulatory approvals [are] the principal remaining condition.”

in_line: Individual Retirement remained pressured, as the preview had flagged flows as an issue: sales fell year over year and sequentially to $3.8 billion, although June was the strongest sales month of the year.
Life Insurance’s reported APTOI still declined 11% year over year, consistent with the weak segment trend highlighted in the preview; the run-rate result, however, exceeded guidance.

surprises.description: FRP cut full-year NOI guidance to about $36.2 million from its original $37.1 million plan. Delayed industrial lease-up and D.C. multifamily headwinds drove the reduction, partly offset by stronger mining performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year NOI guidance to approximately $36.2 million from an original plan of $37.1 million,” driven by “$800,000 in delayed industrial lease-up and $1 million of D.C. multifamily headwinds,” partly offset by “$850,000 of stronger mining performance.”

surprises.description: Industrial tenant interest had not converted into signed leases as the preview hoped to see: only about 20,700 square feet were signed, despite 97,500 square feet in active negotiations. Management said stronger tenant activity had not yet translated into signed leases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only about 20,700 square feet have been signed with 97,500 square feet in active negotiation,” and “stronger tenant activity has not yet translated into signed leases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for signed leases converting to occupancy” after management reported “53,000 sq ft signed or under LOI.”

surprises.description: A Maryland same-store industrial portfolio suffered a sharp occupancy decline, from 92% in Q1 2025 to 70.6%, due to lost government tenants and a tenant bankruptcy. That specific deterioration adds to the industrial leasing weakness flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Maryland same-store industrial portfolio (Hollander and Cranberry) fell to 70.6% occupancy from 92% in Q1 2025 due to lost government tenants and a tenant bankruptcy.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described industrial occupancy as weak and said to “watch for signed leases converting to occupancy.”

surprises.description: D.C. multifamily weakness included substantial rent nonpayment, lengthy eviction timelines, and new tenants paying lower rents than departing tenants. The preview flagged underperforming D.C. assets and a goal of stabilizing occupancy, but did not anticipate these specific collection and trade-out headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 8% of tenants are not paying rent,” evictions take “12 to 18 months due to district policies,” and “new-tenant trade-out rates are running 10% below prior tenants.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted D.C. assets were underperforming and management’s “2026 priority is stabilizing DC occupancy.”

surprises.description: Management signaled that most future discretionary growth capital will go to industrial real estate, a strategic allocation shift not identified in the preview. Multifamily and mining remain part of the business, but are not the stated focus for most new discretionary growth capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Most future discretionary growth capital will target industrial real estate,” signaling a pivot toward that segment “while maintaining multifamily and mining.”

surprises.description: Despite shareholders pressing for repurchases and citing a roughly $40 NAV against a share price near $21.50, management reiterated that it prioritizes development over dividends or meaningful buybacks. The preview did not flag this capital-allocation debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiple shareholders, including the fourth-largest holder, pressed hard for buybacks citing a NAV near $40 versus a ~$21.50 share price,” but management “reiterated it prioritizes new development capital over dividends or meaningful buybacks.”

in_line: Q2 pro rata NOI was approximately $9.4 million, within the preview’s stated recent-quarter range of about $8.9–$9.7 million.

Mining remained a source of strength, consistent with the preview’s description of mining royalties as the segment carrying results; its stronger performance also partly offset the guidance reduction.
Liquidity was approximately $130 million at quarter-end, consistent with the preview’s report of about $130 million at Q1.

surprises.description: The preview treated 15% AMS/DRS organic growth as the floor for the 14th consecutive quarter. BCO reported 14%, falling short of that threshold and breaking the expected streak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AMS/DRS grew 14% organically” and delivered its “14th consecutive quarter of mid-teens or better organic growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 “would be the 14th” quarter at ≥15% and called a print below 15% the largest de-rating risk.

surprises.description: Revenue growth was slightly below the preview’s implied consensus pace: total revenue grew 7%, versus consensus-implied year-over-year growth of 7.7%. The FX tailwind was also 3%, below the roughly 6% tailwind cited for Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 organic revenue growth was 4% with total revenue up 7% (including a 3% FX tailwind).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put revenue consensus at “$1.40B” and implied year-over-year growth at “+7.7%”; it also said to watch whether the FX tailwind persisted at Q1’s “~6%.”

surprises.description: Several large AMS/DRS installations moved out of Q2 into the second half because of customer timing, leaving organic growth at about 2% in North America, Latin America, and Europe. The preview did not flag these project delays, so some expected Q2 activity was deferred rather than realized in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Several large AMS/DRS installations slipped from Q2 into the second half due to customer-driven timing,” contributing to growth decelerating to “about 2% in North America, Latin America and Europe.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected a 14th quarter of at least 15% AMS/DRS organic growth and discussed regional operating profit, but did not anticipate Q2 installation delays.

surprises.description: EBITDA and margins came in above the preview’s expectations: adjusted EBITDA was $257 million versus about $255 million expected, and the 18.5% margin exceeded the roughly 18.2% expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EBITDA margins reached a record 18.5%, up 70 basis points year-over-year,” and adjusted EBITDA was “up 11% to $257 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Adj. EBITDA ~$255M” and “Adj. EBITDA margin ~18.2%.”

surprises.description: EPS of $2.13 beat the $2.05 consensus, but fell just short of the preview’s stated $2.15 realistic ‘beat’ threshold. The result was therefore better than consensus but a little below the preview’s higher bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EPS grew 18% to $2.13.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus EPS of “$2.05” and said “$2.15–2.25 is the realistic ‘beat,’ not $2.06.”

surprises.description: BCO raised full-year profit guidance, whereas the preview’s base case expected the FY26 framework to remain unchanged. The 30–50 basis-point margin-expansion framework was reaffirmed rather than narrowed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year profit guidance, with Q2 EBITDA above the midpoint of prior guidance,” while reaffirming mid-single-digit organic growth and 30–50 bps of EBITDA margin expansion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the FY framework to be “reaffirmed”; it identified a raised margin-expansion band toward 50 bps as a bull-case outcome.

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month free cash flow was $468 million, below the preview’s cited $502 million run rate and its roughly 50% conversion figure. Conversion was still 46%, above the 40–45% full-year target range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow reached $468 million with 46% EBITDA conversion, above the full-year target range of 40–45%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said TTM FCF had crossed “$500M” at “$502M, ~50% conversion.”

surprises.description: The Atleos closing timeline moved forward to early Q1 2027 from the preview’s expectation of end-Q1 2027, with substantial regulatory progress also reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The NCR Atleos acquisition closing timeline was moved forward to early Q1 2027,” with U.S. antitrust early termination granted and “80%+ of money transmitter jurisdictions cleared.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the deal as not closing until “end-Q1 2027” and identified international regulatory approval as the remaining gate.

surprises.description: BCO reported a notable set of new customer wins that the preview had not identified: a 5,000-location U.S. retail DRS agreement, a European bank consortium outsourcing deal, and an Indonesia Mandiri Bank AMS deal covering more than a third of its ATM estate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The new wins included “a 5,000-location U.S. retail DRS enterprise agreement (nearly doubling wallet share),” a European bank consortium deal, and Mandiri Bank servicing “over 1/3 of its 13,000+ ATM estate.”

surprises.description: The call reported North America EBITDA margins at 19.8% on a trailing 12-month basis, approaching an intermediate 20% target—a margin milestone the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America EBITDA margins hit 19.8% on a trailing 12-month basis, approaching the 20% intermediate target.”

in_line: BCO reaffirmed the mid-single-digit organic growth and 30–50 bps EBITDA margin-expansion framework, consistent with the preview’s expected FY26 framework.

AMS/DRS remained a major growth contributor and more than doubled to over $1.5 billion in revenue, consistent with the preview’s emphasis on the segment’s ongoing growth and increasing share of company revenue.

surprises.description: Limbach’s adjusted EBITDA was $13.9 million, well below the preview’s estimated $19–20 million, while adjusted diluted EPS of $0.64 and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.39 were also below the preview’s respective consensus estimates of $0.93–$0.98 and about $0.73.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 22.3% to $13.9 million” and “adjusted diluted EPS declined to $0.64”; net income was $4.7 million, or “$0.39 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.93–0.98”; “GAAP diluted EPS ~$0.73”; “Adjusted EBITDA ~$19–20M (derived).”

surprises.description: Gross margin came in at 21.5%, below the preview’s roughly 25% consensus estimate and its 24% base estimate. The preview highlighted margin recovery as the key test, but GCR margin fell to 14.5% and ODR margin to 24%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total gross margin compressed sharply to 21.5%”; GCR segment margin was “14.5%” and ODR margin was “24%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~25% (derived)” and “I model…24.0%”; the preview said “Anything below ~24% makes the FY guide arithmetically unreachable.”

surprises.description: The full-year outlook was reset in opposite directions: revenue guidance rose to $760–790 million, above the preview’s expected trimmed range, but adjusted EBITDA guidance fell to $78–84 million, below both the prior guide and the preview’s likely range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reset 2026 guidance, “raising revenue to $760-790 million but lowering adjusted EBITDA to $78-84 million” because of “near-term margin and execution headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated a trimmed guide of “~$700–730M / $82–88M”; it also identified guidance as the “highest-variance item.”
