surprises.fact_evidence: “CJ margin compressing to 39% from 45% partly due to PSG labor costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gives a “CJ 40%” FY margin guide and flags watching “CJ segment EBITDA margin vs. 40% guide.”

surprises.description: Dice’s margin remained at 26%, four percentage points above the 22% FY guide, despite the preview’s expectation that management might spend margin back toward that guide. This leaves profitability higher than the guide implied, though the call facts do not specify the level of sales and marketing spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dice margin improving to 26% from 23%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists the FY guide as “Dice 22%” and says Dice’s 28% Q1 margin could be spent “back into sales/marketing.”

surprises.description: The reported technology-posting data included an unexpectedly sharp shift toward AI requirements: about 75% of new postings required at least one AI-related skill, nearly double the roughly 38% share a year earlier. The preview discussed rising tech postings but not this AI-skills measure, and the facts do not establish its effect on DHX.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 75% of new postings now require at least one AI-related skill, nearly double the ~38% from a year ago.”

in_line: The FY2026 revenue range remained $124–128 million, with ClearanceJobs and Dice each expected to contribute $62–64 million, as the preview expected the existing guidance to be maintained.
Dice bookings fell 14% year over year: still declining, but within the preview’s base-case range of a 12%–15% decline and better than the prior quarter’s 20% decline.
Adjusted EBITDA of $8.3 million at a 27% margin was within the preview’s $8.0–$8.2 million estimate and 26%–27% margin range.
Dice recruitment-package customers were down 15%, matching the decline the preview expected.

surprises.description: MercadoLibre reported more than $10 billion of revenue, up 50% year over year, versus published consensus of about $9.74–$9.77 billion and implied growth of roughly 44%. That beat consensus, although it was around the preview’s estimated $10 billion buy-side expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue surpassed $10 billion for the first time, growing 50% year-on-year in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenues & financial income: $9.74 – $9.77B” and “Implied Y/Y: +43.5 – 43.9%”; the preview also said “buy-side revenue expectations sit above consensus (~$10.0B).”

surprises.description: Brazil items growth remained at 56% year over year, rather than slowing below the preview’s roughly 45% warning threshold despite the mid-quarter import-duty change and competitive pressure. Items per buyer grew 19% and conversion rose 1.1 percentage points, reinforcing the stronger-than-feared engagement result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In Brazil, items per buyer grew 19% year-on-year and conversion rose 1.1 percentage points”; “items overall growing 56% versus 26% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “If Brazil items growth decelerates materially below ~45%, the ‘we’re buying share that compounds’ argument weakens,” and flagged the import-duty change and Temu/Shopee competition as risks.

surprises.description: Overall NIMAL recovered to 21% from 18% in Q1, substantially above the preview’s expectation that it would stabilize around 17–18%. The call attributed the improvement to recovering Brazil consumer spreads and normalization of provisions after the Q1 spike.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NIMAL improved from 18% in Q1 2026 to 21% in Q2 2026, driven by recovering Brazil consumer spreads as provisions normalized after a Q1 spike.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether “NIMAL stabilizes near 17–18%.”

surprises.description: 15–90 day NPLs fell to 7.0% total and 4.6% for credit cards, better than the preview’s 8.0% total NPL reference and its concern that a rise would signal underwriting deterioration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “15-90 day NPLs held at 7.0% total and 4.6% for credit cards, near historical lows.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “15–90 day NPL held at 8.0%” and said to watch whether it rose above 8.5%.

surprises.description: Adjusted free cash flow was positive at $214 million, avoiding the consecutive negative quarters the preview warned could raise funding concerns after Q1’s negative $56 million. This was achieved despite $441 million of capex and $2.1 billion invested in growing the credit book.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow was $214 million despite capital expenditure of $441 million and $2.1 billion invested into growing the credit book.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said adjusted FCF was “–$56M in Q1'26” and warned that “Two consecutive negative quarters would raise the question of whether the credit build eventually requires external capital.”

surprises.description: Brazil credit-card issuance accelerated to 2.6 million cards from 1.6 million a year earlier, while card NIMAL was -2.5%. That indicates a larger and still loss-making card-growth push even as total portfolio NIMAL improved; the preview had flagged immature card cohorts as a drag but did not anticipate this issuance pace or card-level figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Credit card issuance in Brazil accelerated to 2.6 million cards this quarter versus 1.6 million a year ago, with card NIMAL at -2.5% (versus near breakeven a year ago) and each cohort reaching NIMAL breakeven in 12-18 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said NIMAL had fallen partly because of “credit-card mix (immature cohorts)” and asked whether overall NIMAL would stabilize near 17–18%.

surprises.description: The advertising business grew 73% year over year, with use of an AI ad-orchestrator tool up 66%. The preview did not set an advertising growth expectation, so this was an unanticipated positive operating datapoint rather than a beat against a stated forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The advertising business grew 73% year-on-year, aided by AI tools including an ad orchestrator whose usage grew 66%.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted unusually strong economics from customers using both Marketplace and Mercado Pago: these ecosystemic users grew 37% and generate materially more commerce, payments volume, and assets under management. The preview discussed engagement metrics but did not anticipate these cross-product economics or their scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ecosystemic users (using both Marketplace and Mercado Pago) generate 70% more GMV, 90% more TPV and double the assets under management, growing 37% year-on-year, and are multiples more profitable.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed roughly $80 million more year-over-year AI investment, but also cited operating leverage in development and customer service: product development fell from 8.4% to 7.2% of revenue and the service-rep count declined from 10,000 to 7,000 despite threefold business growth. This adds quantified AI spending while showing efficiencies that the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI investment rose roughly $80 million year-on-year, while product development scaled from 8.4% to 7.2% of revenues and customer service reps fell from 10,000 to 7,000 despite 3x business growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “AI” among the investment-cycle areas and said the key question was whether management had “stopped adding new investment buckets,” but gave no AI-spend or productivity figures.

in_line: Income from operations was $683 million with a 6.7% margin, within the preview’s derived $650–700 million operating-income range and 6.7–7.1% margin range. The 550-basis-point year-over-year margin decline also matched the preview’s expected 510–550-basis-point contraction.

surprises.description: OraSure withdrew the InteliQuick CT/NG FDA submission and no longer expects clearance or a U.S. launch in 2026, rather than reaching the anticipated midyear clearance and H2 launch ramp. Management plans to resubmit after addressing FDA feedback.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Withdrew its FDA submission” and “no longer expects FDA clearance or U.S. launch in 2026,” planning to resubmit after incorporating FDA feedback.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided to “midyear clearance” with revenue ramping in H2; the preview said the key question was whether CT/NG was “under active review” or whether the launch would slide into 2027.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $30.6 million, above the preview’s preferred $29.0–$29.3 million consensus anchor and above the company’s $30 million guidance ceiling. The result was stronger than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $30.6 million,” exceeding the company’s guidance range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to treat “$29.0–29.3M as the number the tape will trade against” and listed company guidance of $27–30M.

surprises.description: Diagnostics revenue reached $19.4 million, well above the preview’s $17.3 million base-case estimate, and grew 14.7% sequentially. That segment was a major source of the revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diagnostics revenue reached $19.4 million, growing 14.7% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case modeled “Diagnostics ~$17.3M.”

surprises.description: Gross margins were higher than the preview’s roughly 42–43% Q2 expectation: GAAP margin reached 43.5% and non-GAAP margin 44.2%. Management attributed the improvement to lower scrap and operational efficiencies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin expanded 120 basis points sequentially to 43.5%,” while “non-GAAP gross margin rose to 44.2% from 43.4%,” driven by “lower scrap and operational efficiencies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected gross margin of “~42–43%” and cited Q1 margins of 42.3% GAAP and 43.4% non-GAAP.

surprises.description: Sample Management Solutions revenue was $9.9 million, above the preview’s $9.4 million base-case estimate, and rose 9% sequentially despite the preview’s concern about subdued academic and government demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sample Management Solutions revenue was $9.9 million, up 9% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case modeled “SMS ~$9.4M” and described academic and government demand as “subdued.”

surprises.description: The cash picture was better than the preview’s downside warning: cash ended at $161 million, above the roughly $155 million level it identified as a sign of accelerating burn, and operating cash flow was negative $9.9 million. Management also reaffirmed its breakeven operating cash flow target entering 2027, as the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$161 million in cash and cash equivalents”; operating cash flow was “negative $9.9 million,” and management reaffirmed breakeven operating cash flow entering 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said cash “below ~$155M” would indicate accelerating burn and put the breakeven target under pressure; it also noted Q1 operating cash flow of –$14M.

surprises.description: The CT/NG delay was not expected to add to cash usage because reduced milestone payments on the contingent consideration would more than offset the added resubmission costs. The preview discussed the regulatory risk and cash-burn concern but not this offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: The delay “is not expected to increase cash usage,” as reduced milestone payments on the approximately $20 million contingent consideration will “more than offset incremental resubmission costs.”

surprises.description: OraSure sharply reduced Q2 repurchases, buying back only $2 million of shares, and said it had paused repurchases to preserve balance-sheet flexibility for launches. The preview flagged repurchase pace as a signal but did not specify an expected reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: OraSure “paused share repurchases in Q2,” buying back “647,000 shares for $2 million,” to prioritize balance-sheet flexibility for product launches.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1’s $5 million buyback and said “buyback pace signals management’s own read.”

surprises.description: Sickle SCAN revenue was growing twice as fast in 2026 as in 2025, an encouraging product trend not anticipated in the preview’s description of the base business as flat-to-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sickle SCAN revenue is growing twice as fast in 2026 as in 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the “base business” as “flat-to-down.”

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $29.5–$32.5 million was broadly in line with the preview’s low-$30-million expectation.
Management reaffirmed the target of breakeven operating cash flow entering 2027, as the preview anticipated.
Colli-Pee Dx clearance and OraQuick Ebola 2.0 EUA were already known before the release; the preview described both clearances as completed.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $3.13 billion, beating the $3.00 billion consensus by $130 million and growing 13% year over year, versus the preview’s expected 8.6% growth. Strong LMR demand and accelerated quick-turn conversion drove the upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 13% year-over-year to a record level, beating consensus by $130 million, driven by strong LMR demand and accelerated quick-turn conversion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Consensus … $3.00B … Implied Y/Y +8.6%.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS reached $4.41, well above the $3.86 consensus and the preview’s $3.90+ buy-side whisper. The $0.25 IEPA tariff-refund benefit contributed, but EPS was still about $4.16 excluding it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $4.41, up 24% from $3.57 a year ago, including a $0.25 benefit from IEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS … Consensus … $3.86”; “the buy-side whisper is effectively $3.90+.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 32.9%, far above the preview’s roughly flat year-over-year base case and its 29.5% bull-case threshold. Even excluding the $60 million IEPA refund benefit, margin expanded 140 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 32.9%, or 140 basis points excluding the $60 million IEPA refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … margin roughly flat y/y”; “Bull … non-GAAP op margin ≥29.5%.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY26 revenue guidance to approximately $12.975 billion and EPS guidance to $17.62–$17.72. This exceeded the preview’s expected revenue raise to at least $12.85 billion and its bar of at least $17.00 at the low end of EPS guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $175 million to approximately $12.975 billion and lifted non-GAAP EPS guidance to $17.62-$17.72 from $16.87-$16.99.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bar … is a raise to ≥$17.00 at the low end plus revenue ≥$12.85B.”

surprises.description: Memory costs are now expected to reach $150 million this year, above the preview’s expectation of more than $100 million. Most of the impact is expected in the second half, adding more cost pressure than the preview’s already elevated estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Memory costs are now expected to reach $150 million this year, up from $50 million last year and up $100 million from prior guidance, with most of the impact hitting the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Memory/DRAM spend more than doubles to >$100M in 2026.”

surprises.description: Instead of the roughly $60 million tariff headwind the preview expected, tariffs are now expected to be net neutral for the full year because IEPA refunds offset the planned headwinds. The refund also contributed $0.25 to Q2 EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tariffs are now expected to be net neutral for the full year as $60 million in IEPA refunds offset previously planned tariff headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tariffs are a ~$60M headwind weighted to H1.”

surprises.description: Silvus is now expected to generate roughly $850 million in FY26 revenue, $100 million above the $750 million target already in the preview. The preview anticipated a possible further raise, but the reported target was higher than that stated baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Silvus generated about $230 million in Q2 (up from $210 million in Q1) and is now expected to deliver roughly $850 million in full-year revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Silvus revenue target raised to $750M for 2026”; “Watch for another Silvus raise.”

surprises.description: The call introduced a year-end 2026 APX Next subscriber target of 300,000, with nearly $100 million in ARR at roughly $300 per subscriber. The preview did not flag an APX subscriber or ARR outlook, so there was no stated benchmark to compare with this new target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APX Next software subscribers are expected to reach 300,000 by year-end 2026 (up from ~200,000 in 2025), representing nearly $100 million in ARR at roughly $300 per subscriber.”

in_line: Backlog remained at a record level and was up 11% year over year, consistent with the preview’s emphasis on a record backlog of about $15.7 billion and 11% growth. It was down $71 million sequentially, which the call attributed to UK Home Office revenue recognition.

The counter-drone acquisition was anticipated in the preview at roughly $1.5 billion and approximately $185 million of expected revenue; the call reported an agreement on those terms and a second-half closing.

surprises.description: Envista raised its 2026 outlook to 3.5%-4.5% core growth, 11%-14% adjusted EBITDA growth, and $1.50-$1.55 adjusted EPS. That was a stronger move than the preview’s base case of reaffirming the prior EPS range, and the new EPS range is also above the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 3.5%-4.5% core growth, 11%-14% adjusted EBITDA growth, and adjusted EPS of $1.50-$1.55.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise is the bull trigger; a reaffirm is the base case”; the preview’s bull case was “Raise to $1.42–$1.48.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.41, well above the preview’s $0.34 consensus estimate. The 21% gap was materially larger than the preview’s expected year-over-year growth of 31% implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS up 58% to $0.41.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus: “$0.34.”

surprises.description: Core sales grew 5%, above the preview’s implied 1%-3% range and the 4% threshold it highlighted. This was a stronger underlying-growth read than the preview’s base case of 3.5%-4.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 core sales grew 5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed core sales growth of “~1–3% (implied)” and highlighted “Core growth ≥ 4%” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 14.7%, above the preview’s roughly 13.5% implied estimate and its 13.8%-14.2% base case. The 230-basis-point expansion also exceeded the preview’s expected margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 230 basis points to 14.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA margin ~13.5% (implied)” and gave a base case of “~13.8–14.2%.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow recovered to $105 million, above the preview’s $90 million-plus bull-case marker and the $76.4 million generated in Q2 2025. The result was stronger than the preview’s concern that Q2 needed a very large catch-up after Q1’s negative cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was $105 million (158% conversion), up $29 million year-over-year”; full-year conversion is expected “near 100%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Envista “needs a very large H1 catch-up” and cited “FCF > $90M” in its bull case.

surprises.description: The cash-flow recovery included a $13 million IEEPA tariff recovery that the preview had not anticipated. That makes part of the strong Q2 cash result a one-off benefit rather than recurring operating cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 free cash flow was “aided by a $13 million IEEPA tariff recovery.”

surprises.description: China commentary was more constructive than the preview’s concern that double-digit declines and destocking would persist: management projected a return to moderate growth and said implant price compression would be only 10%-15%. The offset is substantial expected ortho price compression of roughly 45%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China VBP is now expected in the second half, with roughly 45% price compression on ortho (VBP 1) but only 10%-15% on implants (VBP 2), and China is projected to return to moderate growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said China implants had seen “strong double-digit declines,” warned that “channel destocking likely persisted through Q2,” and flagged the risk of “extended VBP 2.0 destocking through Q2.”

surprises.description: Envista repurchased about 2.4 million shares in Q2, up from the 1.6 million shares cited for Q1, while the preview had raised the possibility that weak cash flow could constrain buybacks. The stronger cash result and continued repurchases indicate a faster pace than that risk scenario implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Envista repurchased approximately 2.4 million shares in Q2 at an average price of $24.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 repurchases of “1.6M shares for ~$43M” and said a soft FCF print “constrains the buyback narrative.”

surprises.description: The implant F Series launch was running ahead of plan, with about 25% of sales coming from competitive conversions—an additional favorable product-launch update not specifically anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The implant F Series launch is running ahead of plan with about 25% of sales from competitive conversion.”

surprises.description: The full-year non-GAAP tax-rate outlook was lowered by about two percentage points, providing an additional EPS tailwind that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year non-GAAP tax rate guidance to approximately 26%, about 2 points below initial guidance, aiding EPS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call states the new rate is “about 2 points below initial guidance.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $731 million was above the preview’s published consensus range of $716-$720 million, but essentially matched its estimated buy-side whisper range of $728-$735 million. Thus it beat the published bar without surprising relative to the preview’s higher expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue of $731 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview treated “$716–720M as published consensus” and “$728–735M as the realistic buy-side whisper.”

in_line: Equipment & Consumables grew 8.5% with high-single-digit growth in consumables and diagnostics, consistent with the preview’s expectation that E&C could hold high-single-digit core growth.

The Q4 calendar headwind and roughly 3.5% normalized second-half core growth were broadly in line with the preview’s warning about four fewer selling days in Q4 and its 2%-4% full-year core-growth framing.
The VBP timing moving into the second half was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that VBP 2.0 would be delayed into Q3 and affect the second half.
Brackets & Wires’ high-single-digit decline against a strong tariff-driven prior-year comparison was consistent with the preview’s warning about possible payback from last year’s pre-buying.
Full-year cash conversion near 100% remained the stated target, matching the preview’s cited conversion goal.

surprises.description: SiTime guided to Q3 combined revenue of $285–$295 million, well above the preview’s $250–$265 million base case and above its $280 million bull-case threshold. The midpoint is $290 million, versus the preview’s roughly $255 million street-math benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for combined revenue of $285-$295 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Combined base case: $250–265M”; the bull case was “$280M+.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook for core SiTime, excluding TPD, was $200–$210 million, or about 30% sequential growth. That is stronger than the preview’s estimate of $172–$188 million for the organic business, suggesting the combined-guide upside is not just from the acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core SiTime (ex-TPD) expected to grow ~30% sequentially to $200-$210 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic SiTime at $150M in Q2 growing high-teens sequentially … → $172–188M.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $2.34, above both the preview’s $1.93 consensus and its $2.10–$2.20 buy-side whisper range. The result also exceeded the preview’s $2.30 bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income reached $65.7 million, or $2.34 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus” EPS was “$1.93”; “The buy-side whisper” was “$2.10–2.20”; the bull case was “$2.30+.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $157.4 million beat the preview’s $145.09 million consensus and slightly exceeded its $152–$156 million buy-side whisper range. It came just below the preview’s $158 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $157.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus was “$145.09M”; the whisper was “$152–156M”; the bull case was “$158M+.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 67.1%, 2.1 percentage points above the preview’s roughly 65% expectation. The preview had framed margin progress as important to the deal thesis, although its specific 66–68% range was for the Q3 guide, not Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 67.1%, up 8.9 points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin consensus was “~65%”; company guidance was “~65.0% ±1.0 pt.”

surprises.description: TPD is expected to contribute about $85 million in Q3, above the preview’s estimated $68–$80 million for the initial quarter. Management also said it is tracking well above the original $300 million annualized run-rate target, rather than merely reiterating that target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TPD … is expected to contribute ~$85 million in Q3 alone, tracking well above its original $300 million annualized run-rate target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated TPD at “$68–80M” in the first stub quarter and said reiterating “≥$300M” was the floor.

surprises.description: Despite the zero-coupon notes, management warned that Q3 interest income will fall to about $4 million after the proceeds were deployed. The preview expected no cash interest drag from the converts and did not anticipate this reduction in interest income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management funded the acquisition with a $1.35 billion zero-coupon convertible notes offering due 2031, but warned Q3 interest income will drop to ~$4 million after proceeds were deployed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Because the converts carry a 0% coupon, there is no cash interest drag.”

surprises.description: Management offered a specific, upbeat 2027 optical-growth outlook: 1.6T optical-module revenue is expected to grow 100%, with 800G also growing. The preview discussed datacenter and optical demand as key drivers but did not anticipate this growth outlook or quantify it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In 2027, the company expects its 1.6T optical module revenue to grow 100% (with 800G also growing).”

surprises.description: Management said it sees no signs of a 2027 slowdown and reaffirmed a multiyear growth rate of about 30% or slightly higher, while citing a potential $2.5 billion expansion of CED’s addressable market by 2030 from timing integration into chiplets and modules. The preview did not identify these specific longer-term growth and market-expansion claims.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed a multiyear growth rate of ~30% or slightly higher, sees no signs of slowdown in 2027, and projects timing integration into chiplets and modules could expand its CED SAM by $2.5 billion by 2030.”

in_line: CED maintained triple-digit year-over-year growth: the segment grew 181%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that datacenter/comms growth would remain triple-digit. The preview also wanted double-digit sequential growth, but the reported facts do not provide a sequential CED growth rate.
TPD’s roughly 70% gross margin was consistent with the preview’s expectation that the acquired business ran at about 70% gross margin.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was just $0.1 million, below the preview’s roughly $0.5–2 million base case and the $1.0 million Zacks estimate. The preview also described revenue as a proxy for TVA-related pre-FEED progress, so the reported figure did not show that activity in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NuScale reported Q2 2026 revenue of just $0.1 million,” down from $8.1 million a year earlier, because Fluor’s RoPower FEED Phase 2 work ended in late 2025 and there was no comparable current activity.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “consensus expects roughly the same in Q2” after Q1 revenue of $0.6M; the consensus table lists Q2 revenue of “$1.0M,” and the base scenario expects “~$0.5–2M.”

surprises.description: Cash, cash equivalents and investments reached about $1.9 billion—far above the preview’s expected Q2 level of roughly $830–850 million. The preview had expected a sequential decline absent a binding PPA, while the call reported a $900 million increase since March 31.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NuScale closed Q2 2026 with approximately $1.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents and investments, an increase of $900 million since March 31, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Absent a PPA, Q2 cash should land near $830–850M.”

surprises.description: The potential TVA deployment discussed on the call extended up to 8 GW, above the preview’s description of the existing TVA–ENTRA1 agreement as covering up to 6 GW. This points to a potentially larger program, although the PPA was still under discussion rather than signed.
surprises.fact_evidence: ENTRA1 was in “active discussions with the Tennessee Valley Authority toward a definitive PPA for a potential 6-to-8 gigawatt deployment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Sept 2025 TVA–ENTRA1 agreement covers up to 6 GW (72 modules).”

surprises.description: NuScale described a broader and more advanced supplier base than the preview’s reference to 37 key suppliers aligned to 2026 milestones: it said it had more than 60 specialized suppliers, agreements with over half, and components already in production. That suggests more supply-chain readiness than the preview had highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: NuScale had “assembled a network of more than 60 specialized suppliers” and signed master supplier agreements with “more than half”; many components, including Doosan heavy forgings, had been in production over the past two years.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s secondary watch list referred to “37 key suppliers aligned to 2026 milestones” and asked about long-lead component production status.

surprises.description: The call quantified a potential regulatory shortcut for a new U.S. project: about 60% of the prior CFPP license application could carry over, potentially saving time and regulatory cost. The preview did not identify this carryover as a potential benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 60% of the prior CFPP project’s Combined Construction and Operating License Application (COLA) can be carried over to a new U.S. project, potentially saving significant time and regulatory cost.”

surprises.description: Management gave a construction timeline of a little under 40 months from first safety-related concrete to mechanical completion, excluding NRC licensing. The preview did not provide a comparable construction-duration expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Construction from first safety-related concrete pour to mechanical completion is expected to take a little less than 40 months, excluding upfront NRC licensing time.”

surprises.description: Management quantified NuScale’s OEM/module portion at roughly 30% or more of total project cost, with the balance assigned to EPC and other contractors. The preview did not specify how much of a project’s cost NuScale’s own scope would represent.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NuScale’s OEM/module scope [is expected] to represent roughly 30%+ of total project cost, with the remainder going to EPC and other contractors.”

surprises.description: The call emphasized NuScale’s existing NRC design certification and use of conventional low-enriched uranium, avoiding the commercial-scale HALEU supply risk facing some competitors. These readiness advantages were not identified in the preview’s stated watch items.
surprises.fact_evidence: NuScale “remains the only SMR company to have received NRC design certification” and “uses conventional low-enriched uranium, avoiding the commercial-scale HALEU supply risk faced by several competing designs.”

in_line: The TVA PPA had not been reported as signed; instead, ENTRA1 was in active discussions toward a definitive agreement. The preview expected the likely outcome to be continued progress rather than delivery of a signed PPA on the call.

The cash-and-investment composition included a treasury reclassification rather than new fundraising: the call said roughly $800 million of investments reflected a move into longer-term high-grade instruments. The preview had raised cash balance and funding as key issues but did not forecast this specific reclassification.

RoPower remained gated by project steps rather than reaching final notice to proceed: the preview had already described the project as gated on pre-EPC financing and flagged financing close and FID language as items to watch.

surprises.description: Enact raised its 2026 capital-return target to $550–600 million from $500 million, above the preview’s expectation that the roughly $500 million target would be reaffirmed. The increase was attributed to strong first-half performance and excess capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enact raised its 2026 capital return guidance to $550-600 million, up from prior guidance of $500 million, citing strong first-half business performance and excess capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital return **~$500M** for 2026”; the base case expected capital-return guides to be “reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Full-year operating-expense guidance fell to $205–210 million from $215–220 million, better than the preview’s expectation that the existing range would be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 operating expenses (excluding reorganization costs) are now forecast at $205-210 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating expenses **$215–220M**, excluding reorganization costs”; the preview said to watch for qualification of the guide and described reaffirmation in its base case.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.26 topped the preview’s $1.19–$1.21 consensus band, though it was within the preview’s $1.24–$1.28 functional buy-side bar and at the top of its base-case range. The result was a modest consensus beat rather than an obvious beat over the higher bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted operating income was $177 million, with diluted EPS of $1.26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working band for this note: EPS $1.19–$1.21”; the preview also said “the functional buy-side bar is closer to **$1.24–$1.28**” and gave a base-case range of “$1.20–$1.26.”

surprises.description: Enact expected its base premium rate to remain relatively flat versus 2025, a steadier outlook than the preview’s emphasis on gradual premium-rate declines across the market and the risk of pricing pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Base premium rate expected to remain relatively flat versus 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Gross premium rates have continued to drift lower gradually” at peer MGIC and flagged “any gross premium rate commentary” as a key issue to watch.

surprises.description: Management said second-half delinquencies could rise partly because newer, lower-HPA purchase vintages have higher LTVs and DTIs. The preview anticipated seasonal increases and portfolio aging, but this added a specific risk factor beyond the expected seasonal framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects delinquency rates to rise in the second half of 2026 due to seasonality and newer, lower-HPA purchase vintages carrying higher LTVs and DTIs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had warned DQ “may tick up from the 2.6%” on portfolio aging and that a seasonal increase would likely be accepted if Enact said the same thing as MGIC.

in_line: NIW was $15 billion, at the top of the preview’s expected $13.5–15 billion base-case range and consistent with its view that $14–15 billion was achievable.
Persistency held at 80%, matching the preview’s 79–80% expectation.

The 14% loss ratio was within the preview’s 13–16% base-case range. The $37 million reserve release was below the preview’s cited $40 million-plus release concern, rather than indicating a larger-than-anticipated release-driven result.
Q2 shareholder returns totaled $127 million, broadly matching the preview’s approximately $125 million quarterly pace; buybacks were $93 million versus the preview’s expected roughly $95–110 million.
IIF reached $274 billion, consistent with the preview’s expectation of modest in-force growth.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $61.9M versus the preview’s $52.5M consensus (and its inferred $53–55M functional bar), a substantially larger beat than expected. It was also a record quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $61.9 million,” up 45% year-over-year and 40% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $52.5M”; the preview also said the “functional bar is likely $53–55M.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 revenue guide’s low end rose from $225M to $230M, while the $260M top end stayed unchanged. The preview’s base case expected an unchanged guide, so this was a modest upward revision rather than the larger raise or narrowing described in its bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $230 million to $260 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the company guide as “$225–260M” and said the base case was “Guide reaffirmed unchanged at $225–260M.”

surprises.description: Management clarified that the FY2026 guide excludes any LivePerson contribution. That resolves the preview’s central open question in the more demanding direction: the organic business must deliver the guided revenue without a LivePerson stub.
surprises.fact_evidence: The raised FY2026 guidance is “excluding any contribution from the pending LivePerson acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether the $225–260M guide includes a LivePerson stub — the single most underappreciated question”; the preview said an organic-only guide would require SoundHound to “roughly sequentially double its core business in two quarters.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $9.6M, far better than even the preview’s optimistic marker of a loss narrowing toward $20M, and well below its $24–27M base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss was $9.6 million, a 33% year-over-year improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called narrowing “toward ~$20M” the bull marker and put base-case burn at “~$24–27M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin reached 58%, well above the preview’s roughly 50% bar and its bull-case threshold of getting back above 50%. GAAP gross margin also rose to 45%, rather than showing the compression the preview was concerned about.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin was 58% (flat YoY but up 8 points sequentially)” and “GAAP gross margin rose to 45% (up 6 points YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Holding the 50% line non-GAAP is the bar,” flagged “a third consecutive compression quarter,” and set the bull case at non-GAAP gross margin “back above 50%.”

surprises.description: Management set a future gross-margin target above 70%, a higher stated destination than the preview’s discussion of scaling toward software margins and its near-term focus on holding the 50% line. The call did not provide a timeline for reaching that target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “targeting over 70% gross margin in the future.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the thesis as “scale into software margins” and focused on “Holding the 50% line non-GAAP”; it did not state a target above 70%.

surprises.description: Loss per share was better than consensus on both bases: adjusted loss was $0.02 versus the expected $0.03, and GAAP loss was $0.10 versus the expected $0.13. This ran counter to the preview’s warning that the GAAP result could show a meaningful step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $42.8 million ($0.10 per share) while non-GAAP net loss was $9 million ($0.02 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “EPS — adjusted | −$0.03” and “EPS — GAAP | −$0.13”; the preview said “a −$0.13 GAAP Q2 implies a meaningful GAAP-only step-down.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a sizable customer commitment signed in under 90 days from demo to contract, delivered as a channel deal serving customers across 20 countries. The preview asked for evidence of contracted large deals but did not anticipate this specific win.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed an 8-figure customer commitment in under 90 days from initial demo to contract,” a “channel deal serving customers across 20 countries.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said evidence of “named enterprise wins” or “confirmation that H2 large deals are contracted rather than pipelined” would support the bull case; it did not identify this commitment.

surprises.description: Management gave a positive closing expectation for LivePerson, saying the deal is expected to close before year-end. The preview highlighted the August 20 shareholder vote as a real execution risk and said hedging on the vote would be concerning.
surprises.fact_evidence: LivePerson “secured all key regulatory clearances and is expected to close before year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the August 20 vote “a real execution risk” and listed “any hedging on the Aug 20 meeting” as a catalyst to watch; it already noted that all regulatory gates appeared cleared.

surprises.description: The call added specific LivePerson deal benefits not laid out in the preview: the acquisition would add 25 Fortune 100 brands and eliminate LivePerson’s debt. These are additional strategic and financial details, rather than a change to the previewed $350–400M 2027 framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: The acquisition is “adding 25 of the Fortune 100 brands and eliminating LivePerson's debt.”

surprises.description: OASYS was described as driving record win rates across demos, RFPs, and pilots, while restaurant renewal rates reached 100% for key accounts. The preview identified restaurants as a newer growth leg but did not anticipate these results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OASYS, launched in May 2026, is driving record win rates across demos, RFPs, and pilots, with restaurant renewal rates hitting 100% for key accounts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “Restaurants/QSR and healthcare” as “the newer legs” and did not specify expected OASYS win rates or renewal rates.

surprises.description: SMB smart-answering revenue more than doubled year-over-year, a specific operating result the preview did not forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SMB ‘smart answering’ revenue more than doubling year-over-year.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the $350–400M minimum 2027 revenue range, conditional on the LivePerson acquisition closing; this matched the preview’s stated FY2027 company framework of $350–400M including LivePerson.

surprises.description: VEL’s held-for-investment NPL rate fell to 9.6%, below the preview’s expected 10.0%–10.4% range, and charge-offs were only $700,000, below the five-quarter trailing average. Resolutions continued to clear above par, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation for favorable resolution economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-performing loans fell to 9.6% of held-for-investment loans,” down from 10.3% a year ago; the company resolved $90.5 million of NPLs with net gains of 102.7% and total recoveries of 107.7%, while charge-offs were only $700,000, below the 5-quarter trailing average.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NPLs flat ~10.0–10.4%” in the base scenario; the preview also said to watch for NPLs below 9.8% in the bull case and expected resolutions to keep clearing above 100%.

surprises.description: Portfolio NIM reached 3.66%, above the 3.5% standing target and above the preview’s base-case range of 3.50%–3.56%. It also exceeded the preview’s 3.60% bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Portfolio NIM was 3.66%, above the 3.5% target and up 10 basis points from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NIM stabilizing ~3.5% for FY26”; the base case was “3.50–3.56%” and the bull case was “≥3.60%.”

surprises.description: Loan production was $672.6 million, below the preview’s $700–$780 million base case and below its $680 million threshold for a weak quarter. Production did rise sequentially from Q1, but the dollar total fell year over year despite the preview’s expectation of a seasonal step-up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total loan production was $672.6 million,” down from $725 million a year ago; it increased 5.2% from Q1’s $639 million, while unit production rose 3.3%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario projected “$700–780M”; the preview said “anything below ~$680M” would put the second-half growth narrative in question and described Q2 as “the seasonal step-up quarter.”

surprises.description: The portfolio reached $7.0 billion, but its 2.2% sequential growth was below the preview’s roughly 5% q/q expectation and its projected $7.15–$7.2 billion level. The 19% year-over-year increase was also below the preview’s roughly 25% growth context.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The total loan portfolio grew to $7.0 billion in UPB, a 19% year-over-year increase and 2.2% sequential increase from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “~+5% q/q would put the book at ~$7.15–7.2B” and projected “~$7.15B” in its base scenario.

surprises.description: Management reported that July was the best month ever for submissions, an encouraging new indicator for second-half production that the preview had not identified in its expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said “July was the best month ever for submissions.”

in_line: Diluted book value per share rose to $18.43, up roughly 18% year over year, consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued high-teens book-value compounding.

New HFI originations maintained a roughly 10% weighted-average coupon and conservative LTVs, in line with the preview’s focus on holding coupons around 10% or higher and avoiding LTVs above roughly 65%.

Management reaffirmed that origination volumes should increase in the second half and exceed last year’s levels, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the second-half growth language would be maintained; no formal numerical guidance was provided.
NPL resolutions continued to clear above par, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: CMRC cut its FY2026 revenue outlook by $18 million at the midpoint and its non-GAAP operating-income outlook by $12.5 million, with both new ranges below the prior ranges’ low ends. The preview’s base case expected the full range to be reaffirmed; even its bear case described a cut to the lower half, not guidance below the previous low end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $18 million at the midpoint (to $336.5-344.5 million) and non-GAAP operating income by $12.5 million (to $28-34 million), driven roughly evenly by a deliberate partner ecosystem decision and more cautious new account booking assumptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (~50%)” expected “FY range reaffirmed unchanged”; the bear case described “FY guide cut to lower half ($347.5–355M).”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP operating income was $8.1 million, well above the $4–5 million guide and the preview’s $5–6 million base case. That was a much stronger profit result than expected despite revenue landing within guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $84.5 million (within guidance), with non-GAAP operating income of $8.1 million beating the high end of the $4-5 million guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income” guide: “$4M – $5M”; base scenario: “$5M–$6M.”

surprises.description: The company reported that BigCommerce Payments GMV is running more than 30% ahead of its internal plans, with adoption reaching additional merchant groups. The preview worried the first full quarter might yield only underwhelming qualitative commentary, although it did not provide an external forecast for Payments volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BigCommerce Payments GMV is running more than 30% ahead of internal plans since its U.S. launch, with adoption expanding to select performance plan merchants and larger accounts, plus a UK launch planned later this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “qualitative hand-waving = it's early and underwhelming,” while noting that “quantified attach = confidence.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin fell 170 basis points sequentially, a steeper decline than the preview’s roughly 100-basis-point base-case assumption. Management attributed the pressure primarily to higher hosting costs from AI crawler and agent traffic that it chose to keep open.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin declined sequentially from 77.4% in Q1 to 75.7% in Q2, driven primarily by higher hosting costs from increased AI crawler and agent traffic that management deliberately chose to keep open.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “GM down ~100bps”; the preview said a “Q2 gross margin compresses another 200bps+” would be a downside case.

surprises.description: Management identified longer sales cycles specifically in B2C replatforming, as merchants deliberate over AI and agentic discovery strategies. The preview discussed AI-related monetization as a potential opportunity but did not anticipate this decision-making delay; management said B2B, Feedonomics, and product intelligence had not materially weakened.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Softness is concentrated specifically in B2C replatforming, where longer sales cycles reflect merchants deliberating over AI/agentic discovery strategies, while B2B, Feedonomics, and product intelligence showed no material weakening.”

surprises.description: NRR improved to 95.8%, modestly above the preview’s estimated 95.5% and its base-case range, though it did not reach the 96% milestone the preview highlighted as evidence of stronger cross-sell.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue retention improved sequentially for the third consecutive quarter to 95.8%, up from 95.4% in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated NRR at “~95.5%” and gave a base case of “95.3–95.7%”; it called “a print through 96%” the first real evidence the cross-sell motion works.

in_line: Q2 revenue was $84.5 million, within the $84.5–$85.5 million company guide and close to the preview’s roughly $85 million consensus estimate.
ARR ended at $360.5 million, essentially matching the preview’s approximately $361 million estimate.
GMV grew 14%, consistent with the preview’s characterization of the persistent gap between platform-volume growth and revenue growth; the preview also highlighted B2B momentum.

surprises.description: Albemarle reported Q2 sales of $1.7 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $858 million, above preview estimates of $1.59 billion and about $734 million. The quarter beat expectations on both measures, with the larger gap in EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 31% year-over-year to $1.7 billion,” and “adjusted EBITDA more than doubled (up 155%) to $858 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2'26 Cons. | $1.59B”; “Adj. EBITDA (segment sum) | ~ $734M.”

surprises.description: The company cut its full-year energy storage volume outlook to 225,000–235,000 tons LCE, or flat to down 4% year-over-year, rather than maintaining the preview’s expectation of flat volume. The June Greenbushes CGP3 fire was the stated cause, partly offset by stronger Wodgina production.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 energy storage volumes were cut to 225,000-235,000 tons LCE (flat to down 4% year-over-year) due to the June 9 CGP3 fire at Greenbushes, partially offset by stronger Wodgina production.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guidance is flat volume”; the preview also called a volume raise “the cleanest bull signal.”

surprises.description: Albemarle raised its full-year specialties outlook, lifting sales to $1.4–$1.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $275–$325 million. This was an upside revision from the prior guidance range, with bromine price gains from Middle East supply disruptions driving the increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Albemarle raised its full-year specialties outlook to net sales of $1.4-1.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $275-325 million, driven by bromine price gains from Middle East supply disruptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY raised at Q1 to $1.3–1.5B sales / $225–275M EBITDA”; the preview also said a further raise was part of its bull scenario.

surprises.description: Management guided to sequential declines in Q3 sales, EBITDA, and margins in both segments, despite the preview’s expectation that energy storage volumes would be seasonally stronger in Q2 and Q3. The outlook cites lower energy storage volumes, potentially lower pricing, and higher-cost spodumene inventory flowing through.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided that Q3 sales, EBITDA and margins will decline sequentially in both segments,” citing “lower energy storage volumes, potentially lower pricing, and higher-cost spodumene inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 was 53kt with CFO Neal Sheorey guiding Q2/Q3 seasonally stronger and Q4 weaker on 2025 year-end destocking.”

surprises.description: Q2 energy storage realized pricing was about $20/kg LCE, below the preview’s roughly $21/kg estimate. The reported price was also about 15% below market pricing because of spodumene dilution and a three-month pricing lag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 realized price of ~$20/kg LCE was about 15% below market pricing due to spodumene dilution and a 3-month pricing lag.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~57kt LCE at ~$21/kg realized” and said Q2 realized price “should step up materially from Q1's ~$17/kg.”

surprises.description: Current lithium market conditions were tighter than the preview’s demand-and-supply discussion suggested: demand was running above forecast and inventories were near record lows, despite the preview highlighting falling spot prices and supply restarts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global lithium demand grew 45% year-over-year through May, running above forecast, while inventories fell to near-record lows—carbonate under 3 weeks and hydroxide under a month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the demand backdrop as “tracking 37%” and noted spot was “−15% in a month” after several supply restarts.

surprises.description: Albemarle raised its stationary-storage demand forecast for 2026 by 11% and lifted the low end of its 2030 total lithium demand outlook by 100,000 tons. The preview discussed demand growth generally but did not anticipate these upward forecast revisions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 stationary storage forecast 11% to 900-1,100 GWh and lifted the low end of its 2030 total lithium demand outlook by 100,000 tons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “15–40% demand-growth backdrop (tracking 37%)” but gave no expected upward revision to the stationary-storage or 2030 demand forecasts.

surprises.description: Management projected high-single-digit energy storage volume growth in 2027 and reaffirmed a 240,000–260,000-ton LCE target as CGP3 ramps to full run rate by Q1 2027. This provided a constructive growth outlook rather than the possible downside framing for 2027 raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects high-single-digit energy storage volume growth in 2027 as CGP3 ramps to full run rate by Q1 2027, targeting 240,000-260,000 tons LCE consistent with its 15% CAGR trajectory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether management would “re-introduce downside framing for 2027.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.92, well above the preview’s roughly $1.70 consensus estimate and even above its bull-case range of $1.85–$1.95’s lower bound by a small margin. The beat was about 12% versus the consensus midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EPS was $1.92, up from $1.68 in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat ~$200M / $1.70 as the number to beat”; the bull scenario put adjusted EPS at “$1.85–1.95.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance was cut to $825–855 million, rather than being reaffirmed or raised from the prior $865–895 million range; it is also below the preview’s $869.9 million consensus. The preview had flagged guidance as the most important line and described narrowing toward the low end as a risk, but the reported range was cut below it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[A] downward revision to full-year total revenue guidance of $825-855 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: $869.9M (cons.) vs guide $865–895M”; the preview said a raise was the bull trigger and “narrow to the low end” would be a warning.

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance fell to $445–470 million, below the prior $475–500 million range the preview expected management to reaffirm or improve. The new range implies essentially flat EBITDA despite projected revenue growth, rather than the EBITDA-accretive outcome the preview associated with the acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $445-470 million implies essentially flat performance versus 2025, despite 8% projected revenue growth at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance as “$475–500M” and said the base case was to “Reaffirm $865–895M / $475–500M.” It also said management called the acquisition “immediately EBITDA-accretive.”

surprises.description: The Nuscenta franchise fell to $35.2 million, substantially below the preview’s $45 million estimate, with a 24% year-over-year decline rather than the expected 3% decline. The reported explanation was lower net pricing on authorized generics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nuscenta franchise revenue fell 24% year-over-year to $35.2 million due to lower net pricing on authorized generics.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The segment estimate was “Nucynta … Q2’26E … $45M (–3%).”

surprises.description: Jornay PM revenue reached $46.1 million, above the preview’s $44 million estimate, with 41% year-over-year growth versus the estimate’s 35%. Prescription growth was 13.1%, while prescribers reached a new high above 30,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Journet PM generated $46.1 million in net revenue, up 41% year-over-year, with prescriptions growing 13.1% and prescribers reaching an all-time high of over 30,000 HCPs (up 17.6%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The segment estimate was “Jornay PM … Q2’26E … $44M (+35%).”

surprises.description: Belbuca revenue was $57.7 million, beating the preview’s $52 million estimate and growing 10% year over year rather than being flat. The company also reported new formulary access covering an additional 9 million lives, a development the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Belbuca revenue grew 10% year-over-year to $57.7 million and recently secured formulary access for an additional 9 million lives effective in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The segment estimate was “Belbuca … Q2’26E … $52M (flat).”

surprises.description: Astaris contributed $12.9 million in its initial partial-quarter sales, versus the preview’s $10 million stub estimate. The company also raised its Astaris revenue guidance to $65–75 million, above the preview’s cited $60–70 million expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Astaris … contributed $12.9 million in initial revenue from about a month and a half of sales”; “The company raised its full-year Astaris revenue guidance to $65-75 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “AZSTARYS (stub) … $10M” and said management targeted “$60–70M for the remainder of 2026.”

surprises.description: The company reported a $15.1 million GAAP net loss, largely because of $24.1 million in acquisition-related expenses. The preview focused on adjusted EPS and did not give an expectation for GAAP earnings or these expenses, so the gap versus expectations is not quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted a GAAP net loss of $15.1 million (loss of $0.46 per share) versus net income of $12 million a year earlier, largely due to $24.1 million in Astaris acquisition-related expenses.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $113.8 million, above the preview’s buy-side estimate range of roughly $105–112 million, though the top end was exceeded by only a small amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 8% to $113.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated adjusted EBITDA at “~$105–112M (buy-side).”

in_line: Total net product revenue was $199.9 million, essentially matching the preview’s roughly $200 million consensus estimate; the preview also expected 6%–7% year-over-year growth, versus the reported 6%.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA was approximately 2.1 times, broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of about 2 times leverage after the acquisition.

surprises.description: The preview cited FY27 Street EPS of $13.48, implying roughly 7% growth, while management set low-single-digit revenue growth and only modest EPS leverage as the starting assumption. That points to a weaker FY27 earnings-growth outlook than investors were expecting.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management characterized FY27 as low single-digit revenue growth with only modest EPS leverage as a starting assumption, versus Street expectations of around 7% EPS growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY27 Street EPS: $13.48.

surprises.description: The preview’s H2 bridge implied roughly $5.20 billion of Q4 revenue and described the Q4 ramp as demanding. Management instead expects Q4 revenue growth to slow to about 2.5% from Q3’s 4.4%, although it attributed the deceleration almost entirely to the tougher Alaris comparison rather than underlying weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 revenue growth is expected to decelerate to roughly 2.5% from 4.4% in Q3, driven almost entirely by the tougher Alaris capital comparison rather than underlying weakness.
surprises.expectation_evidence: H2 FY26 implied revenue: ~$10.1B; Q4 implied residual: ~$5.20B. The preview called the Q4 ramp a “demanding bar.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue and adjusted EPS both exceeded the preview’s consensus: revenue was about $110 million above the $4.89 billion estimate, and EPS was 9 cents above $3.14. The beats were meaningful but modest relative to the estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 FY26 revenue was $5 billion, up 4.4% FX-neutral. Adjusted EPS was $3.23 and ahead of expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q3 FY26 consensus: revenue $4.89B; adjusted diluted EPS $3.14.

surprises.description: BD lifted the FY26 EPS guidance midpoint to $12.67 from $12.62, and moved revenue guidance to the high end of its low-single-digit FX-neutral range. The preview’s base case anticipated an upward narrowing of the EPS range, so the midpoint increase was favorable, though the range was not narrowed.
surprises.fact_evidence: BD raised the midpoint of full-year guidance to a range of $12.62 to $12.72. It also raised full-year revenue guidance to the high end of its low single-digit FX-neutral range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: FY26 range “narrowed upward”; the preview also flagged narrowing to $12.60–$12.72 as a sign the ramp was on track.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted BioPharma Systems as the only negative segment in Q2 and flagged vaccine demand as a drag. The reported facts instead emphasized broad portfolio growth: four platforms grew double digits and more than 90% of the portfolio grew at a high-single-digit rate, though they did not provide a specific BioPharma Systems result.
surprises.fact_evidence: Four growth platforms delivered double-digit growth (biologic drug delivery, advanced patient monitoring, PureWick, advanced tissue regeneration), with over 90% of the portfolio growing high single digits.
surprises.expectation_evidence: BioPharma Systems revenue and organic growth were flagged as a key watch: Q2 was “−1.8% FXN” and “vaccine demand is the drag.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview noting $2.1 billion of debt retirement, BD ended the quarter with net leverage still above its long-term target, limiting balance-sheet flexibility. The preview did not specify an expected leverage level, so the remaining constraint is new information rather than a direct miss against a stated target for this quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net leverage ended at approximately 2.9x, still above the long-term target of 2.5x, constraining balance sheet flexibility.

in_line: Adjusted operating margin was 24.9%, broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of approximately 25% including tariffs.
The Alaris headwind matched the preview: about 100 basis points in FY26, rising to about 200 basis points in FY27.
Advanced patient monitoring was among the double-digit growth platforms, consistent with the preview’s expectation that APM double-digit growth would continue.

surprises.description: Net revenue was $331 million, down 13%, a smaller decline than the preview’s estimated 15.6%–20.3% drop and above its $320.7 million consensus estimate. The preview expected the refranchising and partnership exit to weigh on the headline, but the reported decline was less severe.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue fell 13% to $331 million due to the planned re-franchising of the Western US and Japan, though organic revenue was essentially flat excluding those deals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue: $320.7M” and “~$303M (−20.3% YoY)”; the preview also characterized consensus as “−16% to −20% YoY.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $28.8 million, below the preview’s roughly $30–32 million estimate, and the 8.7% margin was below its 9.8% base case. EBITDA still grew 43% and accelerated from Q1’s 38% growth, but the reported dollars and margin fell short of the preview’s expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 43% year-over-year to $28.8 million,” and “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 340 basis points to 8.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … my est. ~$30–32M” and “My working base case: … adjusted EBITDA $31M (9.8% margin).”

surprises.description: U.S. average weekly sales per door reached about $697, up 33% year over year. That was a much stronger increase than the preview’s expected continuation of the +16.7% trajectory, although it remained just below the preview’s bull-case threshold of more than $700.
surprises.fact_evidence: “US average weekly sales per door rose 33% year-over-year to approximately $697.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1: $685, +16.7% YoY” and the base case called for sales per door “up low-double-digits”; the bull case specified “Sales/door >$700.”

surprises.description: First-half capex was down 70% year over year and free cash flow improved by more than $100 million versus the prior-year first half. That is a stronger cash-generation update than the preview’s more general expectation that positive free cash flow would be sustained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half capex dropped 70% year-over-year to $16.1 million, and free cash flow improved by more than $100 million versus the first half of last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Sustaining positive FCF is the proof point” and noted the $50–60 million capex guide was “roughly a 50% cut versus 2025.”

surprises.description: Management newly highlighted that the prior-year Q3 comparison included a $9.3 million cyber-insurance gain. That creates a specific comparison headwind for assessing the expected second-half acceleration that the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company maintained guidance “while noting Q3 2025 included a $9.3 million cyber insurance gain that inflated the prior-year comparison.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the “H2 acceleration promise” and said “H2 comps go clean once McDonald's fully laps,” without mentioning the Q3 cyber-insurance gain.

surprises.description: The call reported digital sales growth and loyalty engagement that the preview did not discuss: digital sales grew 8% and represented about 22% of U.S. retail sales, while the loyalty base approached 18 million members. These are favorable channel and engagement datapoints, but the preview provided no benchmark for how much growth to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital channel sales grew 8% year-over-year and now represent about 22% of total US retail sales,” with “a loyalty program of nearly 18 million members who visit ~30% more frequently.”

in_line: Full-year guidance was maintained at $1.25–$1.35 billion net revenue, 2%–4% constant-currency system-wide sales growth, $140–$150 million adjusted EBITDA, and $50–$60 million capex; the preview described reaffirmation of the $140–$150 million EBITDA guide as table stakes.
System-wide sales grew 2.6% in constant currency excluding the ended McDonald’s USA partnership, within the preview’s 2%–4% full-year growth range.
Net leverage was 5.4x, within the preview’s expected roughly 5.3–5.5x range and below its stated 5.5x year-end target.

surprises.description: EPAM cut its FY2026 revenue growth outlook to 3.2%–4.2% reported and 2%–3% organic constant currency, below the previous 4.0%–6.5% reported and 2.5%–5.0% organic range. This was a second cut, with the organic-growth floor now below the preview’s stated 2.5% floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 3.2%-4.2% reported (2%-3% organic constant currency), citing North American weakness they described as largely idiosyncratic to EPAM rather than macro-driven.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance: revenue growth +4.0% to +6.5% (organic cc +2.5% to +5.0%); the preview called the organic cc floor of +2.5% the most important framing.

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue outlook was well below the preview’s implied $1.44–$1.46 billion range, and management expected revenue to be flattish from Q3 to Q4 rather than accelerating in the second half. The $1.410–$1.425 billion range implies only 1.7% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $1.410-$1.425 billion implies only 1.7% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, with revenue expected to be flattish from Q3 to Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus math implies Q3 around $1.44–$1.46B. The preview said the FY26 range mathematically requires H2 acceleration.

surprises.description: Large AI-led client deals that were expected to support second-half acceleration were still unsigned, and meaningful revenue contribution was pushed out to the first half of 2027. That is a later timeline than the preview’s H2 2026 assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: A pipeline of large AI-led deals (Agentic managed services, application maintenance) with existing clients remains unsigned, with meaningful revenue contribution now pushed to first half of 2027 rather than second half 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the ~10 large multi-year vendor-consolidation deals in the pipeline underpinned an assumed H2 acceleration, while noting conversion timing was uncertain.

surprises.description: Cash generation did not rebound as the preview hoped: Q2 operating cash flow was slightly negative after Q1’s negative quarter, and management reduced its full-year free-cash-flow conversion outlook to around 70%, below the typical 80%–90% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 operating cash flow turned negative at -$2 million (versus +$53 million a year ago) with DSO rising to 82 days, prompting a cut in full-year free cash flow conversion guidance to around 70% versus the typical 80%-90%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for a clean Q2 OCF rebound after Q1’s –$36.4M and said a second negative quarter would be a serious problem; it also highlighted the FY cash-conversion story.

surprises.description: EPAM’s Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $3.38 exceeded the $3.14 consensus and the prior guidance range’s $3.18 high end. The gap was substantially larger than the preview’s expected modest beat or $3.20–$3.25 whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP diluted EPS grew 22% year-over-year to $3.38.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance was $3.10–$3.18, with Street consensus at $3.14; the preview estimated a buy-side whisper of $3.20–$3.25.

surprises.description: Pure AI-native revenue exceeded the preview’s $145–$155 million expected range and the $140 million caution threshold. It was also the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth, and management remained on track for the $600 million 2026 target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Pure AI native revenues exceeded $160 million (over 11% of business), marking the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth and keeping the company on track for its $600 million 2026 target.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Straight-line-to-target requires roughly $145–$155M in Q2; below $140M would challenge the growth narrative.

surprises.description: The Americas, EPAM’s largest region, slowed from 2.5% growth in Q1 to just 0.5% in Q2 instead of showing the inflection the preview said mattered most. Management attributed the broader North American weakness to company-specific factors.
surprises.fact_evidence: Americas, representing 57% of revenue, grew only 0.5% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Americas growth of +2.5% in Q1 and said an inflection there mattered more than the EMEA number.

surprises.description: Software & Hi-Tech swung from 10.9% growth in Q1 to a 1.3% decline in Q2. The preview’s latest reported baseline for this vertical was still strong growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Software and Hi-Tech declined 1.3% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 vertical growth: Software & Hi-Tech +10.9%.

surprises.description: Business Information & Media’s decline deepened from 0.7% in Q1 to 2.1% in Q2, indicating further deterioration in a vertical that was already slightly down.
surprises.fact_evidence: Business Information & Media fell 2.1%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 vertical growth: Business Information & Media –0.7%.

surprises.description: Despite the weaker revenue outlook, management raised profitability guidance to the high end of the 15%–16% adjusted operating-margin range. The preview expected the range to be maintained and highlighted the need for roughly 100 basis points of sequential Q2 expansion; Q2 gross margin also improved year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 32% from 30.1% a year earlier, and management raised profitability guidance to the high end of the 15%-16% adjusted operating margin range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP operating margin guidance was 15%–16%; Q1 was 14.3% and the preview said the Q2 guide needs about 100bps of sequential expansion. The preview said trimming the FY margin band would be a negative signal.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in at the top of the company’s outlook range and slightly above the $1.407 billion consensus, although the beat was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue was $1.415 billion, up 4.5% year-over-year reported and 3.4% organic constant currency, coming in at the high end of the outlook range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was $1.407B; company guidance was $1.400B–$1.415B.

in_line: Financial Services grew 11.5% year-over-year, matching the 11.5% Q1 pace reported in the preview.

surprises.description: HAE raised FY27 guidance from 4%-7% reported and 3%-6% organic revenue growth to 5%-8% reported and 4%-7% organic growth. The new ranges are one percentage point higher at both ends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year FY27 guidance to 5%-8% reported revenue growth and 4%-7% organic growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue growth: 4–7% reported; 3–6% organic.”

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $339 million, above the preview’s $327.9 million consensus and $332 million estimate. Revenue grew 6%, versus consensus-implied growth of 2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% (both reported and organic) to $339 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $327.9M”; the preview’s own estimate was “$332M (+3.3%).”

surprises.description: Plasma organic growth reached 8%, well above the preview’s roughly 3%-5% estimates and above its stated +6% threshold for the most bullish Plasma datapoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plasma revenue grew 8% organic.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Plasma at “$136M (+4.7%)” and said “Plasma above +6% organic is the single most bullish datapoint available.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.14 exceeded the preview’s $1.07-$1.09 consensus range, despite the preview’s bearish estimate-revision trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 4% to $1.14.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $1.07 – $1.09.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 60.4%, about 100 basis points above the preview’s roughly 59.4% consensus. Management said margin expanded when excluding the prior-year software-license benefit, clarifying that the reported year-over-year decline did not reflect underlying contraction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 gross margin was 60.4%, down 40 basis points year-over-year, but expanded excluding a ~200 basis point prior-year benefit from upfront software license revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin: ~59.4% (street).”
