surprises.description: Persona PLUS was converting faster and delivering greater yield improvement than the preview quantified: rollout was ahead of schedule, at 30-40 centers per week, with yields more than 5% above earlier Persona offerings and potential to convert the U.S. market this year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Persona PLUS is delivering yield improvements exceeding 5% over prior Persona offerings, rolling out ahead of schedule at 30-40 centers per week with potential to convert the entire U.S. market this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Persona PLUS conversions” as a Plasma swing factor but did not forecast this rollout pace or yield improvement.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin of 23.4% was below the preview’s 24%-25% estimate, even though management reaffirmed its full-year margin-expansion target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin was 23.4%, down 70 basis points year-over-year, with the company reaffirming 50-100 basis points of operating margin expansion for FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin: ~24–25% (my est.).”

surprises.description: Although Interventional Technologies returned to growth, sensor-guided technologies still faced ensoETM and OEM weakness. The preview had said the OEM and esophageal-cooling headwinds were now lapped, so their continued drag was a negative qualification to the inflection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interventional Technologies returned to growth at 3% organic ... though sensor-guided technologies were dragged down by ensoETM softness and OEM weakness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the decline was attributed to “OEM sourcing changes and esophageal cooling headwinds now lapped.”

surprises.description: Management said M&A was off the table for now, emphasizing organic growth and deleveraging. The preview noted deleveraging was co-prioritized with buybacks but did not flag an explicit pause in M&A.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid down $100 million of revolver debt ... with M&A stated as off the table for now in favor of organic growth and deleveraging.”

in_line: Interventional Technologies returned to 3% organic growth, consistent with the preview’s expectation that another quarter of growth could validate the inflection thesis.
The $153 million CSL-customer-loss and liquid-solutions-divestiture overhang was fully lapped, consistent with the preview’s description of FY27 as the first clean year post-CSL.
Management reaffirmed 50-100 basis points of FY27 operating-margin expansion and EPS growth broadly in line with reported revenue, consistent with the preview’s guidance baseline.
The $100 million revolver paydown and continued deleveraging priority were consistent with the preview’s note that deleveraging was co-prioritized with repurchases.

surprises.description: The Roivant webcast reported a $950 million upfront payment from the Moderna settlement, with roughly $770 million going to Genevant and the remainder to Arbutus. Roivant also said cash was just under $4 billion before receipt of the $772 million; the preview did not anticipate this Roivant-level inflow, and that cash figure is not comparable to its Immunovant cash estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “received a $950 million upfront payment from the Moderna settlement,” with “roughly $770 million going to Genevant”; “cash stood just under $4 billion before receipt of the $772 million.”

surprises.description: A favorable appellate ruling in the '498 case could produce a further $1.3 billion, and Roivant said it filed three new international lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech in July. The preview did not flag these litigation developments or potential proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A favorable appellate ruling in the ongoing '498 Federal Circuit case could yield an additional $1.3 billion,” and “three new international lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech were filed in July.”

surprises.description: Roivant repurchased about $200 million of stock during the quarter, with a slightly higher amount including March. The preview mentioned watching Roivant’s capital-allocation commentary but did not anticipate a buyback; the reported average price in the high $20s was also well above the roughly $10 average in the earlier $1.5 billion round.
surprises.fact_evidence: “repurchased about $200 million of stock in the quarter (slightly more including March), buying back at an average price in the high $20s versus around $10 per share in the earlier $1.5 billion round.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “Roivant call framing” and “any hint at a strategic transaction, partnership, or further monetization of the Immunovant stake”; it did not mention a Roivant buyback.

surprises.description: Roivant expected a dermatomyositis launch by the end of September after priority review, but characterized the ramp as “slow and steady,” noting limited prior off-label JAK use and a concentrated referral-center base. The preview did not discuss this Roivant product or its launch outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “expects to launch brepiprazole (brepocitinib) in dermatomyositis by the end of September 2026,” while management guided to a “‘slow and steady’ dermatomyositis launch”; “only low-to-mid single-digit percentages of patients have prior off-label JAK experience” and about “200 myositis referral centers treat roughly half of U.S. patients.”

surprises.description: Roivant reported a greater-than-20-point Phase II cutaneous sarcoidosis benefit versus roughly no change on placebo—well beyond its 5-point clinical-meaningfulness goal—and said it had started the Phase III study ahead of schedule. The preview did not flag this program or signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “greater than 20-point benefit on the CSAMI scale versus roughly nothing on placebo,” “well above the 5-point clinical meaningfulness goal,” and the Phase III study was initiated “ahead of schedule.”

surprises.description: Roivant said PH-ILD top-line data are expected in the second half of 2026, while cautioning that the study is not powered for six-minute walk distance and that management is hoping for a clear PVR signal. This program and endpoint caveat were not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Top-line PH-ILD data … is expected in the second half of 2026,” with the company “hoping for a clear PVR signal but not powered for six-minute walk distance.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $653 million, far above the preview’s operative expectation of about $496 million and also above published consensus of about $597.7 million. The result therefore beat even the higher consensus figure, while sharply exceeding management’s previously implied flat-sequential revenue shape.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $653 million, up 31% versus Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat ~$500M as the operative revenue bar”; published consensus revenue was “~$597.7M.” The preview also said management guided Q2 revenue “in line with Q1” at “~$496M.”

surprises.description: Management raised the FY2026 revenue range to $2.6–$2.7 billion rather than trimming it toward the low end as the preview’s base case anticipated. The new midpoint is $150 million above the prior midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $2.6-$2.7 billion (from $2.4-$2.6 billion).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said the “FY revenue guide [is] trimmed toward $2.4–2.5B low end”; it listed the existing range as “$2.4–2.6B.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $28 million, above management’s implied roughly $22 million expectation and above the low end of the preview’s $25–$30 million derived consensus range. Some of the beat came from recognizing development work earlier than expected, which also reduces the near-term EBITDA step-up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $653 million… with adjusted EBITDA of $28 million… both above management's expectations”; the outperformance “stemmed from recognizing prior-year development originally expected in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put management-implied Q2 adjusted EBITDA at “~$22M” and derived consensus at “~$25–30M.”

surprises.description: The expected Q2-to-Q3 EBITDA increase is now only about $4–$7 million because some development was recognized in Q2. That is a smaller step-up than the preview’s stated expectation for $10–$15 million of sequential improvement in Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA outperformance stemmed from recognizing prior-year development originally expected in Q3, so the Q2-to-Q3 increase was cut to ~$4-$7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said sequential EBITDA improvement of “$10–15M” was “coming in Q3 and Q4.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 adjusted EBITDA range was narrowed and its midpoint raised to $127.5 million, rather than simply being held at $110–$140 million as the preview’s base case expected. The midpoint increase is modest compared with the revenue-guidance revision.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Narrowed adjusted EBITDA guidance to $120-$135 million (from $110-$140 million), raising the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the “EBITDA guide $110–140M held”; its catalyst checklist said the guide might be “held vs. cut.”

surprises.description: Management made a new 2027 commitment for at least $150 million of adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint, with revenue growth above 25%, based on contracts already under agreement. The preview focused on whether near-term launches would support FY2026 guidance and did not set out this 2027 outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company committed to a 2027 adjusted EBITDA midpoint at or above $150 million and expects revenue growth of more than 25% in 2027, based on contracts already under agreement.”

surprises.description: Q2 MER rose to 95%, about 200 basis points worse than Q1 and above the preview’s roughly 93% expectation. This is a weaker near-term medical-cost result even though the full-year MER expectation remained around 93%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 medical expense ratio was 95%, up ~200 basis points from Q1's 93%, driven by the May 1 Highmark Performance Suite launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed management-implied Q2 MER at “~93%” and said the FY guide was “~93%.”

surprises.description: The call quantified a Medicaid expansion membership decline that the preview had not anticipated: an industry-wide drop of about 20%, translating into a 4–5% membership headwind for Evolent and likely flat-to-down Tech & Services revenue in 2027. This adds a specific future headwind to the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects a ~20% decline in Medicaid expansion members industry-wide, translating to a roughly 4-5% Medicaid membership headwind for Evolent, with Tech & Services revenue likely flat to down in 2027.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed an oncology Performance Suite partnership expected to generate about $300 million in annualized revenue, with a launch expected by December 2026. The preview discussed other expected launches but did not identify this partnership or its revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new oncology Performance Suite partnership with an existing imaging client covering ~1.5 million lives across 11 states is expected to launch by December 2026 and generate ~$300 million in annualized revenue.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted a need for a quantified ACA exchange disenrollment figure, but the reported facts provide a quantified Medicaid expansion headwind instead and no ACA exchange disenrollment number. The specific uncertainty the preview called out therefore remains unaddressed in the information provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call facts quantify “a ~20% decline in Medicaid expansion members industry-wide” and a “4-5% Medicaid membership headwind for Evolent”; no ACA exchange disenrollment figure is reported in the provided facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “ACA exchange disenrollment — quantified” as a key metric and said “A hard number, even a bad one, removes uncertainty.”

surprises.description: The company reported net debt of $808.3 million, below the preview’s rough estimate of about $843 million of net debt based on $985 million of debt and $142 million of cash. However, unrestricted cash was $115.7 million and the ABL revolver was paid down only to its $62.5 million minimum, so the liquidity picture is not uniformly better.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Evolent ended Q2 with $115.7 million in unrestricted cash and $808.3 million in net debt, paid down the ABL revolver by $10 million to its $62.5 million minimum.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “$985M total debt against $142M cash.”

in_line: Full-year MER remained expected to be around 93%, as the preview had indicated, despite the higher-than-expected 95% Q2 reading.

The Auth Intelligence AI gains were broadly within the preview’s anticipated range: the preview described auto-approval improvements of “high teens up to 30%” and progress toward roughly 80% of authorization volume, while the call reported lifts of up to 20 percentage points and coverage of more than one-third of previously manual-review volume.

surprises.description: KLIC’s Q4 revenue guide was $375 million, well above the preview’s implied bar of about $328 million and even above its bull-case threshold of $355 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue to $375 million, a 13.5% sequential increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 FY2026 guide bar: ~$328M revenue (+6% q/q)” and the bull case called for “≥$355M.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $1.42 substantially exceeded the preview’s implied $1.13 bar and its bull-case threshold of $1.30.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026… non-GAAP EPS [is guided] to $1.42,” up from Q3’s $1.20.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 FY2026 guide bar:… ~$1.13 non-GAAP EPS” and the bull case called for “≥$1.30.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was approximately $330 million, above the $310 million consensus and just above the top of the company’s $310 million ± $20 million guidance range. The preview treated the quarter as largely de-risked, but this was still a modest beat against its live consensus bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue “increased 36.2% sequentially” and “exceed[ed] guidance”; Q2 revenue was $242.6 million, implying Q3 revenue of about $330 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q3 revenue consensus was “$310M”; company guidance was “$310M ± $20M.”

surprises.description: Q3 EPS beat the preview’s estimates: non-GAAP EPS was $1.20 versus $1.00 expected, and GAAP EPS was $1.07 versus about $0.87 expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 EPS was “$1.07 GAAP and $1.20 non-GAAP.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q3 consensus was “$1.00” non-GAAP diluted EPS and “~$0.87” GAAP diluted EPS.

surprises.description: Advanced Solutions revenue exceeded its prior-quarter record by 20%, whereas the preview highlighted a recent sequential decline in APS and flagged another decline as a possible negative signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advanced Solutions segment revenue exceeded last quarter's record by 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 base… APS down sequentially on lower refurbished-system sales”; “a second consecutive decline there would be a quiet negative signal.”

surprises.description: KLIC gave a concrete, substantial FY2027 TCB revenue outlook: $150 million to $200 million, implying 50–100% growth over its FY2026 target. The preview asked for FY2027 TCB framing but did not anticipate a quantified range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management projects thermal compression bonding (TCB) revenue of $150 million to $200 million in FY2027, implying 50-100% growth over the FY2026 target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any FY2027 TCB framing.”

surprises.description: Demand and visibility appeared stronger than the preview’s durability concerns implied: utilization was above 95% in China and around 90% in memory and general semiconductor, with purchase orders extending unusually far into fiscal Q2 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Utilization rates reached over 95% in China and around 90% across memory and general semiconductor end markets, with inbound POs extending unusually far into fiscal Q2 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called memory and China the “most cyclical, least visible piece of the beat” and flagged whether China was “pulling in or digesting.”

surprises.description: General semiconductor revenue rose 52.6% sequentially, a particularly sharp acceleration relative to the preview’s Q2 baseline of 19.4% sequential growth and its general expectation of strength through the business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “General semiconductor revenue surged 52.6% sequentially to $227.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q2 General Semiconductor revenue of “$148.9M (+19.4% q/q)” and quoted management expecting “strength throughout the business.”

surprises.description: KLIC disclosed that it had quadrupled traditional wire-bonding capacity over two quarters and said it had previously supported quarterly revenue run rates of $400 million. The preview discussed Advanced Solutions capacity, but did not anticipate this scale of traditional wire-bonding capacity expansion or the historical run-rate detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company increased its traditional wire bonding capacity 4x over the past two quarters and indicated it has previously supported $400 million quarterly run rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on spending to build capacity for “~$400M of annual Advanced Solutions revenue by 1H FY2027.”

surprises.description: Management described data center demand as an important source of NAND wire-bonding demand, saying data centers represent about 40% of the NAND market and rely on wire bonding at least as much as smartphones and PCs. The preview discussed NAND and AI-related memory demand but did not forecast this specific market framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center now represents approximately 40% of the NAND market and relies on wire bonding at least as much as smartphones and PCs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed “NAND capacity” and “new vertical-wire solutions targeting LPDDR for on-prem AI,” but gave no expectation for data center’s share of NAND or its relative wire-bonding reliance.

surprises.description: KLIC set a first-half FY2027 delivery window for a hybrid-bonding tool to a customer, a concrete milestone beyond the preview’s discussion of hybrid-bonding R&D and qualification activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to deliver a hybrid bonding tool to a customer in the first half of fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted increased R&D in “hybrid bonding” and called for a “concrete HBM datapoint,” but did not specify a hybrid-bonding tool delivery date.

in_line: Q4 gross margin guidance was 48%, in line with the preview’s expectation of roughly 48% for the base case.
Management maintained its FY2026 target of more than $100 million in TCB revenue, consistent with the preview’s stated target.

surprises.description: KDP reported Q2 EPS of $0.57, above the preview’s $0.55 consensus, and 16.3% growth exceeded management’s high-single-digit growth framing. That was a clear earnings beat, though not as large as the preview’s bull-case threshold of $0.58.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS grew 16.3% to $0.57, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS $0.55”; management “guided to high-single-digit EPS growth in Q2.”

surprises.description: Legacy KDP sales grew 7.3%, above the company’s 4–6% full-year range, and management now expects full-year growth at the high end of that range. This points to stronger legacy-business growth than the preview’s guidance baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding JDE Peet's, legacy KDP net sales grew 7.3%”; management “now expects growth at the high end of the 4-6% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Legacy KDP 4–6% cc sales.”

surprises.description: Consolidated net sales growth of 74.6% was ahead of the preview’s 72.3% consensus growth estimate, despite the preview warning that the first fully consolidated JDE Peet’s quarter made the headline difficult to model.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total net sales up 74.6%, largely driven by the JDE Peet's acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales … +72.3%” versus the prior-year quarter.

surprises.description: U.S. Refreshment Beverages grew 10%, ahead of the preview’s 7% consensus, with 6.5 points from volume/mix. It remained below Q1’s 11.9% growth, but volume/mix was stronger than the preview’s minimum 5-point threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Refreshment Beverages … delivered 10% net sales growth (6.5 points volume/mix, 3.5 points pricing).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus implied “+7.0%”; the preview said investors wanted volume/mix to “stay ≥5 pts.”

surprises.description: U.S. Coffee operating income fell 24.7% amid green coffee inflation and tariffs, while pod shipments also declined sharply. That contrasts with the preview’s expectation that coffee margin pressure would meaningfully ease in Q2 after peaking in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Coffee operating income fell 24.7% due to green coffee inflation and tariffs, with pod shipments down 11.6% as reported (8.3% excluding the Peet's reporting shift).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had said Q1 was “peak year-over-year margin pressure for coffee,” with “meaningful” easing in Q2; the preview called Q2 the first test of that promise.

surprises.description: Management said JDE Peet’s Q2 profit contribution likely marks the high watermark for quarterly earnings contribution in 2026 because of timing benefits and the Peet’s K-Cup reporting shift. The preview highlighted uncertainty around modeling the new structure but did not flag this near-term peak risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management warned this Q2 profit likely represents the high watermark for quarterly earnings contribution in 2026 due to timing benefits and the Peet's K-Cup reporting shift.”

surprises.description: The energy portfolio has already reached more than 9% market share and about $1.5 billion in net sales, with a double-digit share goal achieved at 15 major customers. The preview did not identify this business as a catalyst or discuss its scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The energy portfolio crossed 9% market share … now a ~$1.5 billion net sales business … tracking toward a double-digit share goal already achieved in 15 major customers.”

surprises.description: KDP disclosed an incremental 2% non-cash EPS headwind from purchase-price-allocation depreciation, offset by a one-time cash benefit from tariff refunds, leaving the net EPS impact neutral. Neither offsetting item was in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An incremental 2% non-cash depreciation EPS headwind from the JDE Peet's purchase price allocation, offset by a one-time cash benefit from tariff refunds, netting to neutral EPS impact.”

surprises.description: Pro forma leverage improved to 4.4x, slightly better than expected and below the preview’s cited mid-year level of about 4.5x. This is a modestly better starting point for the planned deleveraging.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma management leverage improved to 4.4x at quarter end (slightly better than expected).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage ~4.5x at mid-year.”

surprises.description: Brewer shipments returned to growth at 2.1%, a positive counterpoint to the decline in coffee pods that the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brewer shipments returned to growth at +2.1%.”

in_line: Full-year net sales guidance of $25.9–26.4 billion and low-double-digit constant-currency EPS growth were reaffirmed, matching the preview’s base-case expectation of no guidance change.
The approximately $2.5 billion full-year free-cash-flow target matched the preview’s expectation.
Management reaffirmed the $400 million JDE Peet’s cost-synergy program, as expected.
The early-2027 Global Coffee Co. separation timeline remains the target and the CEO search is underway; the preview expected the timeline to remain on track, while noting the CEO vacancy.

surprises.description: Kemper reported a $464.8 million GAAP net loss, or $7.90 per share, after a $460 million non-cash goodwill impairment in specialty auto. The preview discussed the stock’s decline and possible new-CEO reserve actions, but did not anticipate a goodwill write-down of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss of $464.8 million, or $7.90 per share, driven primarily by a $460 million non-cash goodwill impairment in its specialty auto segment.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating EPS was $0.45, above the preview’s $0.32–$0.33 consensus range by about 36%–41%. The preview’s base case was $0.28–$0.38, so the result also exceeded its central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted consolidated net operating income was $26.3 million, or $0.45 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating EPS: $0.32 – $0.33”; the base scenario projected “$0.28 – $0.38.”

surprises.description: Kemper recorded a $16.6 million after-tax allowance for credit losses on surplus notes issued to Kemper Reciprocal Exchange, an unanticipated charge that weighs on reported results. The company also said roughly $15 million of notes remain to be evaluated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded a $16.6 million after-tax ($21 million pre-tax) allowance for credit losses on surplus notes issued to Kemper Reciprocal Exchange, with roughly $15 million of surplus notes remaining to be evaluated going forward.”

surprises.description: California personal-auto policies fell 10% sequentially and California’s share of the personal-auto portfolio declined 2.5 percentage points. The preview expected Kemper to shrink California, but the pace of this decline makes the portfolio contraction sharper than its general expectation of controlled shrinkage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “California's share of the personal auto portfolio declined 2.5 percentage points during the quarter, driven by a 10% sequential decline in policies in force.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the book as “deliberately shrinking in California” and asked whether “the California shrink [is] controlled or uncontrolled.”

surprises.description: Commercial auto had $17.7 million of adverse prior-year reserve development, continuing a pattern the call described as roughly five consecutive quarters. The preview’s base case assumed a clean quarter with no new charges, although it had flagged adverse development as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported results were hurt by $17.7 million of prior year reserve development, marking roughly the fifth consecutive quarter of adverse development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case assumed “a clean quarter, no new charges”; the preview also noted Q1 had “only $3.2M” of development and identified adverse prior-year development as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: Management said commercial auto would take meaningfully more rate and tighten underwriting, accepting slower near-term growth because of reserve exposure concentrated in bodily injury and litigious California. That is a more cautious growth stance than the preview’s expectation of continued double-digit PIF growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial auto holds about $1 billion in reserves, 90% tied to bodily injury coverage and 45% concentrated in litigious California, prompting management to take meaningfully more rate and tighten underwriting at the expense of near-term growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected commercial auto to hold “~92%” combined ratio “with continued double-digit PIF growth,” and cited Q1 PIF growth of about 10% year over year.

surprises.description: Holding-company liquidity was reported at $766 million, far above the preview’s cited Q1 level of $80 million. This materially eases the capital and dividend-coverage concern emphasized in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $766 million of holding company liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$80M of holding company liquidity” at Q1 and highlighted capital adequacy and dividend coverage as a key concern.

surprises.description: Kemper identified more than $80 million of cumulative annualized restructuring savings, up $20 million from the prior quarter. That is ahead of the preview’s expectation of more than $60 million in run-rate savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Identified more than $80 million of cumulative annualized run-rate restructuring savings (up $20 million from last quarter).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “>$60M” in restructuring run-rate savings, with “$50M actioned.”

in_line: Commercial auto’s underlying combined ratio of 93.7% and year-over-year PIF growth of 9.2% were broadly close to the preview’s expectation of a roughly 92% ratio and continued double-digit growth.

The preview’s base case put specialty P&C underlying combined ratio around 105%–106%; the reported personal-auto normalized underlying ratio was 105.2%, broadly near that range, though it is not the same segment measure.

surprises.description: Intellia reported a major Phase III HAELO efficacy result, with lonvo-z significantly improving the primary and all key secondary endpoints and reducing mean monthly attacks by 87% versus placebo. The preview did not anticipate a new Phase III readout in this release.
surprises.fact_evidence: HAELO “achieved statistical significance on the primary and all key secondary endpoints,” with an “87% reduction in mean monthly attacks versus placebo”; 62% of patients were entirely attack-free and therapy-free.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a previously unflagged nex-z liver-safety risk associated with HLA-C*05:01: carriers had significantly higher rates of Grade 3+ transaminase elevations. The reported rarity and transience of Grade 4 elevations and new monitoring measures partly temper, but do not remove, this concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: An analysis of over 600 samples found C*05:01 carriers (12% of samples) had “significantly higher rates of Grade 3+ transaminase elevations,” with all five highest elevations in carriers. Grade 4 elevations occurred in less than 1% of MAGNITUDE patients, were transient and mostly resolved without intervention; management implemented HLA typing and monitoring measures.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's bogey was “zero new hepatic SAEs under the new mitigation protocol” and it warned that “any new Grade 3/4 transaminase event resets the platform-risk debate.”

surprises.description: Intellia gave additional strong nex-z target-engagement data that the preview had not identified as an expected update: a 90% mean TTR reduction, reached within a month and maintained across patients since 2021 dosing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Nex-z “demonstrated a 90% mean TTR reduction,” with serum TTR below 20 micrograms per milliliter, achieved within one month and maintained consistently across all patients since 2021 dosing.

surprises.description: Lonvo-z's reported treatment-arm safety was especially favorable: all treatment-emergent adverse events were Grade 1 or 2, with no serious adverse events reported by the cutoff. The preview did not set out a lonvo-z safety expectation for this release.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All treatment-emergent adverse events” were Grade 1 or Grade 2, with “no serious adverse events in the treatment arm as of the data cutoff.”

surprises.description: Management specifically addressed the negative CARDIO-TTRansform result for eplontersen and argued it was drug-specific rather than evidence against Intellia's combination-therapy thesis. The preview did not flag this external result or this management response as a debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said the negative CARDIO-TTRansform result for eplontersen was “drug-specific” and did not undermine its combination-therapy thesis; MAGNITUDE had enrolled over 650 patients and its blinded event rate was within the company's internally projected range.

in_line: Lonvo-z regulatory and launch timing: the call expected FDA acceptance of the BLA by year-end and a potential U.S. launch in H1 2027, consistent with the preview's H2 2026 BLA-completion and H1 2027 launch framework.
Cash and runway: Q2 cash of $628.4 million and runway into at least 2028, excluding product revenue, were broadly in line with the preview's $600–625 million cash estimate and explicit runway bogey.

Nex-z trial restart and MAGNITUDE-2 enrollment: enrollment and dosing resumed in Q2, with MAGNITUDE-2 enrollment still on track to finish later this year, consistent with the preview's expectation that enrollment would be on track for H2 2026.
Q2 net loss: the reported $106.6 million loss was close to the preview's derived estimate of about $108 million.

surprises.description: Planet Fitness reported revenue of $365 million, above the $355.8 million consensus, while adjusted EBITDA of $153 million and adjusted EPS of $0.88 also exceeded the preview’s estimates of about $150 million and $0.85. The beats were positive, although adjusted EBITDA grew more slowly than revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 7% to $365 million, and adjusted EBITDA increased 3.5% to $153 million”; “Adjusted net income per diluted share was $0.88.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $355.8M”; “Adj. EPS (diluted) $0.85”; “Adj. EBITDA ~$150M (my est.).”

surprises.description: System-wide same-club sales grew 1.7%, above the preview’s modeled 0–1% range, but the comp was driven entirely by rate growth rather than member growth. That made the reported comp stronger than expected on the headline number, without evidence that new joins had recovered.
surprises.fact_evidence: “System-wide same club sales grew 1.7% in Q2 2026, driven entirely by rate growth (over 100% of the comp) rather than member growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “System-wide SCS ~0–1% (my est.)”; “A print of 0% is in-line, not a miss.” The preview also noted that “~90% of Q1's comp came from rate.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year EPS growth outlook to approximately 6% from approximately 4%, exceeding the preview’s stated outlook. The increase was attributed to share repurchases rather than an improvement in the underlying operating outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year EPS growth outlook to approximately 6% (from 4%) driven by share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adj. EPS growth … ~4%” in revised FY2026 guidance.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 41.8% from 43.3% a year earlier even as revenue rose 7%. The preview flagged prior margin compression and low-margin equipment as risks, but gave no Q2 margin estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 3.5% to $153 million, though adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 41.8% from 43.3% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Equipment is the lowest-margin line”; “This also explains Q1's margin compression (41.5% vs. 42.3%).”

surprises.description: Planet Fitness said it will test a $10 Classic Card promotion nationally, below the existing $15 price. The company stressed that this is a test and not a permanent price rollback, but the promotion was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will test a $10 Classic Card promotion nationally later this quarter but explicitly stated it is not intended to roll back the $15 price permanently.”

surprises.description: The company completed the sale of its Australia franchise stake and indicated it may also exit its Spain territory and selected corporate clubs to recycle capital. The preview did not flag these divestitures or potential exits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed the sale of its Australia franchise stake to Franchise Equity Partners and signaled potential future exits of its Spain territory and select corporate clubs to recycle capital.”

in_line: Ending membership was 21.5 million, within the preview’s modeled Q2 range of approximately 21.4–21.5 million; the preview also described Q2 as seasonally the weakest add quarter.
Average monthly attrition of 3.5% was in line with the preview’s expectation of attrition in the top half of the historical 3%–4% range.
Black Card penetration of approximately 68% was broadly in line with the preview’s 67% estimate, despite the year-over-year basis-point increase being somewhat lower than the preview cited.
The nationwide Black Card price increase remained paused, consistent with the preview’s description of the national increase as paused.

surprises.description: Total revenue was $31.7 million, above the preview’s $27.12–$27.47 million consensus, even though IBTROZI product revenue was $23.2 million. The $8.5 million of collaboration/license revenue was substantially above the preview’s estimate of $2–$3 million in China/Japan royalties.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue of $31.7 million (including $8.5 million in collaboration/license revenue) exceeded the median estimate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $27.12M (Zacks) / $27.47M (Street composite)” and “$23–25M of product revenue … with $2–3M of China/Japan royalties.”

surprises.description: About 160 patients started IBTROZI, well below the preview’s roughly 200–220 base-case expectation. Management also said the finite pool of TKI-pretreated patients was depleted faster than expected, contributing to declining total starts and a shift toward first-line revenue stacking.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 160 new patients started IBTROZI in Q2”; “Total new patient starts are declining as the finite TKI-pretreated prevalence pool … has been largely depleted faster than expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New patient starts” were expected to be “~205–220” in the base case; the preview said “below 200 makes 2H26 consensus of ~$120M look stretched.”

surprises.description: First-line adoption was much stronger than the preview’s already-rising-mix expectation: about 85% of new starts were first-line, and first-line starts grew about 30% quarter over quarter. The preview’s bull scenario assumed a mix of about 60%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About 85% [of new patients] in the first-line setting—up from roughly 30% at launch”; “first-line new patient starts grew approximately 30% over the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “1L share needs to keep climbing past 50%”; the bull scenario assumed “1L mix ~60%.”

surprises.description: The call described IBTROZI as the most-prescribed ROS1 TKI across all lines and said it is selected for more than half of new first-line patients—market-position claims the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IBTROZI is now the most prescribed ROS1 TKI across all lines of therapy per IQVIA claims”; it is “chosen for new first-line patients over 50% of the time.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted strong TKI-naive clinical results for IBTROZI—90% ORR and 50-month median DOR and PFS—which the preview did not identify as an expected Q2 update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IBTROZI demonstrated a 90% ORR and 50-month median DOR and PFS in TKI-naive patients in TRUST-I.”

surprises.description: The newly approved competitor Jideytro was presented as having CNS warnings and notable adverse-event concerns, while priced roughly 8% higher as a later-line therapy. The preview did not discuss this competitor, so the competitive development is new, though the approval itself adds competition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly approved competitor zidesamtinib … carries CNS warnings plus notable adverse events (38% edema, 25% peripheral neuropathy, pancreatic toxicity signals) … and is priced roughly 8% higher as a later-line therapy.”

surprises.description: Updated safusidenib Phase II results were favorable: ORR rose to 52% from 44%, with a 79% 36-month PFS rate, and the call compared these results favorably with vorasidenib. The preview discussed the upcoming studies but did not set expectations for these clinical results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Safusidenib's updated Phase II J201 data … showed ORR increasing to 52% (from 44%) at 39-month median follow-up with a 79% 36-month PFS rate,” versus vorasidenib’s “21% ORR and 52% 36-month PFS rate.”

surprises.description: Q2 cash ended at $661 million, below the preview’s modeled range of $690–$730 million after the convertible financing. Management nevertheless said it believes capital is sufficient to reach profitability and fund the safusidenib launch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $661 million in cash and equivalents” and “believes it has sufficient capital to reach profitability and fund the safusidenib launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “We model cash landing near $690–730M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected full repayment of the senior secured loan from the convertible proceeds, but the call said proceeds were used only partly to prepay the Sagard term loan. The prepayment still materially lowered cash interest expense, but the paydown was less than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “used [the proceeds] partly to prepay a 10%-minimum Sagard term loan, materially lowering cash interest expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “full repayment of the senior secured loan.”

surprises.description: The convertible offering was about five times oversubscribed, indicating stronger demand than the preview had specified; the preview discussed the offering size and proceeds but not demand for the notes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nuvation completed a ~5x oversubscribed 0.75% convertible senior notes offering due 2032.”

in_line: IBTROZI net U.S. product revenue of $23.2 million was in line with the median estimate of the 10 covering analysts and within the preview’s $23–$25 million base-case range.
The two safusidenib studies discussed on the call were already announced before the release; the preview noted the G307 Phase III and G209 Phase II trials.
The company remained eligible for an approximately $30 million Eisai milestone upon anticipated European approval in the first half of 2027, consistent with the preview’s timing.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $3.1 million, about 23% below the preview’s roughly $4.02 million consensus; instead of the expected 30% year-over-year growth, revenue was essentially flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $3.1 million, essentially flat versus Q2 2025.”

surprises.description: The first-half bookings total implies Q2 bookings were only about $2.1 million after Q1’s $33.4 million, far below the preview’s unofficial $10–15 million bar. The first-half headline was largely carried by the $20 million FAU sale, rather than sustained bookings momentum.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First half 2026 bookings surged 1,120% to $35.5 million”; the preview reported Q1 bookings of “$33.4M.” The difference implies approximately $2.1 million of Q2 bookings.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 bookings vs. an unofficial ~$10–15M bar”; the preview also said “<$5M breaks the ‘inflection’ narrative.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss was $37.1 million, wider than the preview’s $30–35 million base-case range, with management attributing the increase to personnel and go-to-market investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss widened 85% year-over-year to $37.1 million,” driven by “increased personnel and go-to-market investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “adj. EBITDA loss ~$30–35M.”

surprises.description: Production applications contributed substantially more to QCaaS than a year earlier: they generated over 37% of first-half QCaaS revenue and the company had six applications in production. The preview discussed monetization prospects but did not anticipate this level of production usage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Production applications generated over 37% ($1.3 million) of first-half QCaaS revenue versus just 9.8% (~$300,000) a year earlier,” and “the company now has six customer applications in production.”

surprises.description: The dual-rail research reported approximately 99.9% two-qubit gate fidelity at 500-nanosecond gate times and a targeted Lambda of 10, a concrete performance result beyond the preview’s mention of a new gate and simulations indicating up to a 10-fold reduction in logical error rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Nature-published dual-rail research demonstrated approximately 99.9% two-qubit gate fidelity at 500-nanosecond gate times,” supporting “a targeted Lambda of 10 versus roughly 2 for other superconducting approaches.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Aug. 4 announcement as a “new two-qubit entangling gate” with “simulations indicating logical error rates could fall up to 10-fold.”

in_line: RPO was $40.7 million, down from $42.4 million in Q1 but still between the preview’s roughly $40 million downside threshold and $45 million upside threshold.
Cash and marketable securities were $546.2 million, within the preview’s base-case range of approximately $545–570 million.

Management expected Q3 revenue to rise modestly, Q4 revenue to rise significantly and make up the majority of the year, with two annealing systems expected to ship in Q4. This is consistent with the preview’s expectation of H2-weighted revenue and at least two 2026 system deliveries, though it makes the concentration in Q4 explicit.
The roadmap’s 17-qubit 2026 target, 181-qubit 2028 target and 100-logical-qubit 2032 target were consistent with milestones the preview had already described.

surprises.description: Oscar reported Q2 revenue of $4.9 billion, above the preview’s primary $4.71 billion consensus estimate, though close to the higher alternative estimates it cited. The beat was supported by 46% membership growth and rate increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 70% year-over-year to $4.9 billion, driven by 46% membership growth to 2.96 million effectuated members and rate increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $4.71B (+65% y/y)”

surprises.description: Q2 MLR was 79.2%, substantially below the roughly 83% level implied by the preview’s consensus math and below its bull-case threshold of 81%. Favorable prior-period development contributed, alongside disciplined pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 medical loss ratio improved nearly 12 points year-over-year to 79.2%, aided by favorable prior period development and disciplined pricing versus a prior-year market reset.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied MLR in consensus: ... a ~83% Q2 MLR”; the preview also said “Below 81% and the ‘MLR reset is structural’ thesis is validated.”

surprises.description: First-half earnings were stronger than the preview’s implied path: it said H1 operating profit was likely near $850 million, while Oscar reported $1.1 billion in earnings from operations and about $1 billion in net income. First-half diluted EPS of $3.16 also exceeded the roughly $2.44 implied by the preview’s Q1 actual EPS of $2.07 plus Q2 consensus EPS of $0.37.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record first-half profitability of approximately $1 billion in net income, or $3.16 per diluted share, with $1.1 billion in earnings from operations”; Q2 “earnings from operations improved $619 million year-over-year to $389 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H1 EFO likely near $850M”; the preview also cited Q1 EPS of “$2.07” and Q2 consensus EPS of “$0.37.”

surprises.description: Q2 SG&A ratio reached 14.2%, well below the roughly 15.8% ratio used in the preview’s consensus math. The company also reached its long-term SG&A target about a year ahead of plan and improved its full-year ratio guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A expense ratio hit a record-low 14.2% in Q2, a 450 basis point year-over-year improvement, reaching the company's long-term target roughly a year ahead of plan”; FY SG&A guidance “improved 20 basis points to 15.6%-16.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 consensus math used “a ~15.8% SG&A ratio,” and its FY26 guidance table showed “15.8% – 16.3%.”

surprises.description: Oscar raised FY26 earnings-from-operations guidance by $250 million to $500 million–$700 million. The preview expected a raise, but its base case was about $500 million–$650 million, so the actual upper end was above that anticipated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year 2026 earnings from operations guidance was raised $250 million to a range of $500 million-$700 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “guidance raised modestly to ~$500–650M EFO”; its bull trigger was “FY26 EFO guide raised to $700M+.”

surprises.description: Full-year MLR guidance improved by 90 basis points at the midpoint, to 81.5%–82.5%. The preview laid out the previous 82.4%–83.4% range but did not anticipate this specific improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year MLR guidance improved 90 basis points at the midpoint to 81.5%-82.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s FY26 guidance table listed MLR of “82.4% – 83.4%.”

surprises.description: A large favorable prior-period adjustment boosted reported results, including an approximately $160 million favorable 2025 CMS risk-adjustment true-up. This contrasts with the preview’s mention of adverse prior-year risk-adjustment development in Q1 and its concern that adverse development could repeat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total favorable prior period development was $164 million in Q2 (including a ~$160 million favorable 2025 CMS risk adjustment true-up) and $232 million year-to-date, boosting reported MLR.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 carried “$85M adverse prior-year risk-adjustment development” and described its bear scenario as “adverse prior-period/risk-adjustment development repeats.”

surprises.description: Management now expects back-half membership churn of roughly 2%–4% per month, double prior expectations. It attributed the increase to delayed CMS eligibility disenrollments and said it was a timing issue without revenue impact, tempering the downside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects back-half membership churn of roughly 2%-4% per month (double prior expectations) due to delayed CMS eligibility disenrollments, but characterized it as timing with no revenue impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Q2 opening membership drop as “non-payers with normal utilization” and said the membership test was confirming “~2.9–3.0M ending members.”

in_line: Effectuated membership was 2.96 million, within the preview’s expected roughly 2.9–3.0 million range.

The favorable 2026 Wakely morbidity signal was consistent with the preview, which said management had not incorporated the favorable market-morbidity signal into reserves and that it could provide upside.

surprises.description: Papa John's cut FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $180–$190 million from $200–$210 million, including an additional $18 million of franchisee and transformation investment. This is a substantial reset below the preview's flagged $200–$210 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management revised 2026 guidance downward, now expecting adjusted EBITDA of $180-$190 million including an incremental $18 million of franchisee/transformation investment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance ($200–210M); the preview also said a cut to a $180–195M range was not discounted.

surprises.description: North America comps fell 8.3%, worse than the preview's roughly 6%–7% expectation and its -6.7% broker anchor. The decline was driven almost entirely by fewer transactions and lower customer acquisition, despite a flat system ticket.
surprises.fact_evidence: North America comparable sales declined 8.3% in Q2, driven almost entirely by transaction/order volume declines and lower customer acquisition, while overall system ticket was flat year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: NA comparable sales: ~-6% to -7% (BofA -6.7%); the preview also said -8% or worse breaks the stabilization narrative.

surprises.description: The Board said the company would pursue its transformation rather than a sale after an 18-month strategic review. The preview treated the status of the reported $47-per-share proposal as unresolved and suggested talks might have lapsed or stalled.
surprises.fact_evidence: After an 18-month strategic review that explored a potential sale, the Board concluded that executing the transformation plan—not a sale—is the actionable value-creation path, though it remains open to actionable alternatives.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Irth Capital $47/share take-private proposal was reported March–June 2026. “I could not confirm its current status”; the preview said the market was pricing near-zero deal probability, implying talks may have lapsed or stalled.

surprises.description: Papa John's announced it would suspend its quarterly dividend beginning in August, contrary to the preview's expectation that the dividend would be reaffirmed. The preview flagged dividend coverage as less comfortable but still described it as adequate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Papa John's Board intends to suspend its quarterly dividend beginning in August to increase flexibility for transformation investments, despite approximately $500 million of total liquidity and a 3.3x covenant leverage ratio.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaffirmation is the expected outcome; anything less is a de-rating event.” The preview also said dividend coverage was “adequate but no longer comfortable.”

surprises.description: FY26 North America comp guidance was reset to down 6%–8%, rather than the prior down 2%–4% range. That abandons the substantial second-half recovery the preview identified as necessary to meet the original outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management now expects North America comps down 6%-8% in 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance reiterated May 7, 2026: “NA comps -2% to -4%.” The preview said hitting the midpoint required roughly flat-to-positive NA comps in H2.

surprises.description: International comps grew 1.5%, below the preview's expected 2.5%–3.5%. Growth continued for a seventh straight quarter, but the Middle East was roughly flat rather than the preview's cited Q1 growth there.
surprises.fact_evidence: International remained positive with 1.5% comparable sales growth (seventh consecutive positive quarter); the Middle East was roughly flat due to regional conflict.
surprises.expectation_evidence: International comps: ~+2.5% to +3.5% (BofA 2.5%); the preview also cited Q1 Middle East comps of +9%.

surprises.description: The company gave a somewhat weaker global system-sales outlook, forecasting a 2%–4% decline instead of the prior flat-to-down-low-single-digit outlook. The ranges overlap, so the change is less severe than the cuts to North America comps and EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management now expects global system-wide sales to decline 2%-4%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance reiterated May 7, 2026: “global system-wide sales flat to down LSD.”

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow was only $9 million, down from $37 million a year earlier. The preview already flagged negative Q1 free cash flow, but characterized dividend coverage as adequate; the weak first-half total and subsequent dividend suspension show greater cash-generation pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: Free cash flow through the first half fell to $9 million from $37 million a year earlier, reflecting lower net income and transformation-related investments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said dividend coverage was “adequate but no longer comfortable” and cited Q1 FCF of -$6.2M versus +$19.1M a year earlier.

surprises.description: Papa John's described a broader leadership reset than the preview's already-known interim CFO transition: it included a new Global Chief Marketing Officer, the CMO's departure, a new SVP International, and a newly created development chief role. This adds turnover and execution uncertainty during the transformation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company announced a broad leadership shakeup, including a new Global Chief Marketing Officer, the departure of CMO Jenna Bromberg, a new SVP International, a newly created Global Chief Development Officer, and an interim CFO with an active search underway.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the interim CFO transition and highlighted the “interim-CFO posture” as a key issue, but did not anticipate the broader leadership changes.

surprises.description: The company accelerated its North America closure plan, now expecting 200–250 closures in 2026, and set an asset-light target of mid-single-digit company ownership, including refranchising 28 Orlando restaurants. The preview discussed a roughly 300-closure plan through 2027 but did not flag this ownership shift or Orlando refranchising.
surprises.fact_evidence: Portfolio optimization is accelerating with 200-250 North America closures now expected in 2026 (versus 300 planned across 2026-2027), and management is pursuing an asset-light model targeting mid-single-digit company ownership, including refranchising 28 Orlando restaurants.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “closure pace vs. the ~300 U.S. closures-by-2027 plan.”

in_line: Q2 consolidated revenue of $482 million was essentially in line with the preview's approximately $481 million consensus estimate.

surprises.description: Scholar Rock finished Q2 with $492 million in cash and marketable securities, above the preview’s $420–480 million estimate. The company said the balance included $63 million in net ATM proceeds, so the cash level was higher than expected partly because of additional share issuance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with “$492 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, including $63 million in net ATM proceeds during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash + marketable sec.: $420 – 480M.”

surprises.description: The second fill/finish site provides more than just the expected backup supply: Scholar Rock said it now has more commercially ready vials from that site than from Catalent Indiana. This strengthens the practical supply alternative while Catalent’s classification remains unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company has “more commercially-ready apitegromab vials from its second fill/finish facility than from Catalent Indiana,” with vials from both sites awaiting approval at the labeling and packaging site.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview looked for “commercial drug product physically in hand” from facility #2 and confirmation that “finished commercial supply exists.”

surprises.description: Management said removing either fill/finish facility from the application would not affect the ongoing FDA review timeline, and described the second facility as a fully independent approval path. The preview discussed the second site as insurance but did not anticipate this explicit assurance about review timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said “removing either facility from the application would not impact the ongoing review timeline,” and that the second facility offers “a fully independent approval path.”

surprises.description: Europe remains dependent on Catalent Indiana: it is still the sole site in the MAA, and the EMA is waiting for the FDA’s inspection classification while the company only discusses potentially adding the second site. That is less resolved than the preview’s conditional expectation that facility #2 would be swapped into the MAA if Catalent was not reclassified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “European approval currently depends on FDA clearance of Catalent Indiana (the sole site in the MAA),” while discussions continue “to potentially add the second facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “If Catalent is not reclassified, SRRK swaps in facility #2 for the MAA.”

in_line: The Catalent Indiana classification was still pending, consistent with the preview’s base case that the 90-day window could lapse without FDA action.
The September 30, 2026 PDUFA date remained in place, as the preview expected.
Q2 operating expenses of $108.9 million were within the preview’s $108–118 million estimate.
The second-site commercial supply was confirmed, consistent with the preview’s expectation that facility #2 product would be available.
The Phase II FORGE trial had started, as the preview asked investors to confirm, and SRK-439 Phase I data were still expected later in 2026.
The company described the expected post-approval $150 million debt draw and planned priority review voucher monetization, both financing sources anticipated in the preview.

surprises.description: SGI guided to FY2026 adjusted EPS of $2.85–$3.15, below the preview’s expected $3.00–$3.40 range, and to about $7.6 billion of sales rather than $7.8–$7.9 billion. Management also lowered its industry outlook to a mid-single-digit decline from a low-single-digit decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance is $2.85 to $3.15 on approximately $7.6 billion of sales at midpoint, with the industry now expected down mid-single digits versus a prior expectation of down low single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance: reaffirm, narrow, or trim ($3.00–$3.40 adj. EPS; ~$7.8–7.9B sales).” The base case was “$3.00–$3.40 reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales were about $1.8 billion, below the preview’s $1.89 billion consensus, while adjusted EPS matched the $0.58 estimate. This was a meaningful revenue shortfall even though the quarter’s earnings per share came in as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales were $1.8 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $297 million and record adjusted EPS of $0.58.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 net sales consensus of “$1.89B” and adjusted EPS consensus of “$0.58.”

surprises.description: Mattress Firm sales were about $922 million, well below the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $966 million, despite slight same-store sales growth. The segment revenue expectation therefore was not met even though same-store sales were positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mattress Firm net sales were approximately $922 million with only slight same-store sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Mattress Firm sales (derived) ~ $966M” and said the estimate “implicitly requires positive same-store sales.”

surprises.description: Tempur Sealy North America’s operating margin reached 26.7%, far above the preview’s 23.3% estimate, with gross margin expanding 680 basis points. The $30 million of quarterly net synergy benefit helps explain the stronger-than-expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tempur Sealy North America adjusted gross margin expanded 680 basis points to 61.8% and operating margin improved 400 basis points to 26.7%, driven by $30 million of net synergy benefit in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated TSNA operating income of “$143.1M (23.3% mgn).”

surprises.description: Management said the July 4 holiday period was notably weak, then reported that Mattress Firm same-store sales rebounded to roughly flat after the holiday ended around July 15. That sharp within-period weakness and rebound was not specifically anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The July 4 holiday period was notably weak, but Mattress Firm same-store sales rebounded to roughly flat after the holiday ended around July 15.”

surprises.description: The Leggett & Platt combination is now expected to close before the end of Q3, earlier than the preview’s target of year-end 2026. The company also said the deal is expected to be immediately adjusted-EPS accretive before synergies, a quantified earnings implication the preview identified as new information.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Leggett & Platt combination is expected to close before the end of Q3, ahead of original expectations, with a shareholder vote August 20, and is projected to deliver immediate adjusted EPS accretion before synergies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said closing was “targeted by YE26” and that “any quantified synergy number or accretion detail is new information.”

surprises.description: SGI returned more than $160 million to shareholders alongside $182 million of free cash flow. That is substantially above the preview’s stated capital-return baseline of at least 50% of free cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company delivered record operating cash flow of $236 million and free cash flow of $182 million … and returned over $160 million to shareholders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “≥50% of FCF returned.”

surprises.description: The company refinanced and upsized its credit facility, extended maturities to 2031, and said the changes would lower future interest expense; the preview did not flag this financing action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The credit facility was refinanced and upsized with maturities extended to 2031 to lower future interest expense.”

surprises.description: Kingsdown products are set to expand from a 200-store pilot to nearly 800 Mattress Firm stores over six months, a rollout not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kingsdown products will expand from a 200-store pilot to nearly 800 Mattress Firm stores over the next six months.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.58, matching consensus and the top of management’s previously guided $0.56–$0.58 range.
Mattress Firm reported slight same-store sales growth, broadly meeting the preview’s implied expectation of positive same-store sales.
The roughly $10 million Q2 commodity-inflation headwind and management’s expectation that second-half pricing would offset it were in line with the preview’s expectations.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.76, far above the preview’s $1.28 consensus estimate. The gap was substantially larger than a routine beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.76, and the reported results beat expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS (cont. ops) $1.28 ($1.27 alt.)”

surprises.description: Teleflex cut full-year pro forma constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 3.5%–4.5% from 4.5%–5.5%, rather than maintaining the guide as the preview’s base case expected. The company attributed the cut entirely to slower-than-expected BIOTRONIK integration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year 2026 pro forma constant currency revenue growth guidance to 3.5%-4.5% from 4.5%-5.5%, entirely due to a slower-than-expected Vascular Intervention (BIOTRONIK) integration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … FY guide maintained”; the preview also described the FY guidance as “reaffirmed at Q1.”

surprises.description: The Interventional segment fell 1%, worse than the preview’s concern that another roughly 3% print would indicate underperformance. Integration disruption also pushed completion from the originally planned mid-2026 to the second half of 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interventional segment revenue fell 1% to $211.9 million” due to integration disruptions primarily affecting BIOTRONIK VI; “full integration [is] now extended through the second half of 2026 versus the originally planned mid-2026 completion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Interventional segment (+3.0% in Q1) — the VI integration tell”; “another ~3% print says the $825M Biotronik VI deal is underperforming.”

surprises.description: Despite cutting revenue guidance, Teleflex raised adjusted EPS guidance to $6.90–$7.20 from $6.25–$6.55, rather than maintaining the range. The increase was attributed to repurchases, lower interest expense, and a lower tax rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.90-$7.20 from $6.25-$6.55,” driven by share repurchases, lower interest expense, and a lower tax rate.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … FY guide maintained”; the preview said “a plain reaffirmation is now a bullish outcome.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 61.7%, below the preview’s hoped-for sequential recovery toward 62.5% or higher, although it was within the preview’s 61%–62% estimate. Operating margin was 19.6%; tariffs, lower-margin VI mix, and R&D spending—including 7.9% of sales in H1 versus a historical roughly 6%—were cited as pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin fell 280 bps to 61.7% and operating margin fell 520 bps to 19.6%,” pressured by tariffs, lower-margin VI business, and increased R&D spending.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sequential recovery toward 62.5%+ validates the H2 ramp”; the preview’s derived gross-margin estimate was “~61–62%.”

surprises.description: Management cautioned that Vascular and Surgical growth would moderate in the second half because of tougher comparisons and distributor inventory normalization. The preview listed their recent growth but did not flag this second-half moderation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Vascular grew 8% and Surgical 9.2%, “though management cautioned second-half growth will moderate due to tougher comps and distributor inventory normalization.”

surprises.description: Management offered a firmer 2027 performance framework than the preview had specified: it expects a meaningful step-up and targets a steady-state operating margin of about 23%. It also did not dispute analyst 2027 EPS estimates of roughly $11.25–$11.50.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a meaningful step-up in financial performance in 2027, targeting a steady-state operating margin of approximately 23%, and did not dispute analyst EPS estimates of roughly $11.25-$11.50 for 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any long-range framework” from the new CEO, but did not provide a 2027 margin target or EPS expectation.

surprises.description: Teleflex cited Freesolve, a resorbable scaffold, as a future growth driver and disclosed a BIOMAG-II randomized-data readout expected in late 2027. The preview did not mention this product or readout.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Freesolve resorbable scaffold (BIOMAG-II randomized data readout expected late 2027) [is a] key future growth driver.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted constant-currency growth of 4.7% was close to the preview’s derived estimate of about 5.0%; reported revenue of $570.3 million also exceeded the $559.6 million consensus estimate.

EZPLAZ’s FDA approval, immaterial 2026 revenue, and potential as a future contributor were anticipated in the preview; the call’s description of it as a 2027 contributor was consistent with that framing.
The OEM proceeds were used for debt repayment and repurchases, broadly in line with the preview’s focus on deploying the roughly $1.25 billion of proceeds toward the buyback and debt reduction.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $16.7 million, far above the $9.20 million consensus and also well above the preview’s inferred $10.5 million “real bar.”
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $16.7 million,” up 107% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$9.20M”; the preview also described “a ~$10.5M whisper” inferred from the Q1 growth trend.

surprises.description: Management’s internal Q4 revenue target of $25 million implies a much stronger second half than the preview’s roughly flat H2 expectation, although the targets are explicitly not formal guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management gave an “internal (non-guidance) revenue target” of “$25 million in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said consensus implied “~$18.3M for H2” and “a flat H2 at ~$9.1M/quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a specific near-term order wave from the Drone Dominance Gauntlet Program; management said more than 60,000 drones are expected to be ordered in the second half, mostly in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “More than 60,000 drones are expected to be ordered under the Drone Dominance Gauntlet Program Phase 2 in the second half of 2026, mostly in Q4.”

surprises.description: The Q3 internal target calls for a sequential revenue decline, contrary to the preview’s expectation—based on management’s prior framing—that revenue would continue growing sequentially through 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management targeted “$12-14 million in Q3,” with “a sequential decline due to infrastructure buildout.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had described “consistent growth… full speed growth,” with “no anticipated 2026 slowdown,” and that the company was “guiding to sequential growth every quarter.”

surprises.description: Management cited an aspirational 2027 revenue target of $250 million, far above the preview’s $52.25 million FY2027 consensus, but also said current capacity supports only about $20 million per quarter—making the target ambitious rather than an assured run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “$250 million as the aspirational 2027 revenue target”; “current 70,000 sq ft capacity supports only about $20 million per quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY2027E revenue $52.25M” and called for a capacity datapoint, including motor output targeted at 100,000 per month later in 2026.

surprises.description: Q2 was affected by supply-chain disruption from outgrowing an electronics vendor, turning a risk the preview raised as a possible downside scenario into an actual operating problem.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “outgrowing an electronics vendor causing supply chain disruptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear scenario said “Supply-chain/lead-time slippage pushes shipments to Q3,” and the preview flagged supply-chain and lead-time slippage as a risk.

surprises.description: Management also disclosed an intermittent quality problem on a motor SKU that required production-process remedies; the preview did not identify this specific issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “an intermittent quality issue on a motor SKU requiring production process remedies.”

surprises.description: The company raised $60 million through ATM block transactions despite the preview’s view that its large cash balance meant there was no financing risk; this adds liquidity but also entails share issuance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised $60 million at $30 per share via ATM block transactions,” and ended the quarter with “$229 million cash, no debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “$222.9M cash and $312.7M working capital at 3/31 means no financing risk.”

in_line: Q2 EPS was a loss of $0.16 per share, matching the preview’s consensus estimate of -$0.16.
Gross margin was 34.7%, within the preview’s estimated 33–35% range and above its 33% watch threshold.
Operating expenses were $13.6 million, consistent with the preview’s warning that opex could run at $12 million or more.

surprises.description: Revenue was $435 million, well above the preview’s $386 million consensus and its own roughly $395 million base case. That is a much larger beat than the preview’s expected 2–3% upside to consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue reached a record $435 million (up 24% year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue of $386M”; “My base case revenue is ~$395M, ~2.5% above the Street.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $2.21 substantially exceeded the preview’s $1.79–$1.81 consensus range and even its $1.98 bull case. The preview had cautioned that a reported $2.24 projection was spurious, making the actual result a clear beat against the usable consensus anchor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS hit a record $2.21.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (diluted, w/ tax benefit) | $1.79–$1.81”; the bull scenario estimated “~$1.98.”

surprises.description: Long-term net flows swung to a $4.2 billion inflow, far stronger than the preview’s base case of roughly $0.2 billion of outflows to breakeven. Management also said flows accelerated further into Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record net long-term inflows of $4.2 billion represented a nearly $5 billion positive swing from the same quarter last year,” and “flows accelerated further into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “LT net outflows narrow to roughly -$0.2B to breakeven” in the base case; the preview said a first positive net-flow quarter would be “a genuine narrative unlock.”

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA margin reached 55.8%, well above the preview’s 53%+ bogey and its 54.5% bull-case assumption. This was a stronger margin result than the preview’s already-optimistic seasonality-driven outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 55.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 should get comp relief; 53%+ is the bogey”; the bull scenario assumed “54.5% EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Victory raised long-term adjusted EBITDA margin guidance from 49% to 50%, citing structural efficiency gains after Pioneer. The preview watched for a synergy increase but did not cite this higher long-term margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised long-term adjusted EBITDA margin guidance from 49% to 50%, reflecting structural efficiency gains post-Pioneer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided cash comp to low-to-mid 20% of revenue”; the preview flagged “any raise to the synergy number,” but did not state an expected long-term margin-guide change.

surprises.description: The realized average fee rate was 47.9 basis points, above the preview’s expected 46–47 basis-point normalized range and its concern that mix could pull the rate down to 46 basis points. Management nevertheless guided to a normalized 46–47 basis-point range going forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue reached a record $435 million … at an average fee rate of 47.9 basis points, though management guided to a normalized 46-47 bps range going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided the investment management realized fee rate to 46–47 bps long-term”; the preview said mix shift could “drag it to 46 bps.”

surprises.description: Pioneer’s integration was completed in five quarters and the full $110 million of net run-rate synergies was realized. The preview said $104 million was already realized and integration was substantially complete, so the full realization and completion are a positive, but more limited, upside to an expectation that most of the work was done.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Pioneer integration was completed in five quarters, with the full $110 million in net run rate expense synergies fully realized.”
