GRLNF was also slightly above the preview’s $615–$620 million expectation at $624 million, with 11% organic growth meeting the preview’s key threshold rather than falling into the feared high-single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross revenue grew 34% year-over-year to $1.29 billion, beating the $1.17 billion guidance, while gross revenue less network fees grew 51% to $624 million (11% organic).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed gross revenue guidance and Street at “~$1.17B,” GRLNF Street at “~$615–620M,” and said “Organic GRLNF ≥11%” would mean the thesis remained intact.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA modestly exceeded expectations: $284 million at a 46% margin versus the preview’s roughly $278 million and 45.2% margin. The beat was positive but much smaller than the revenue and FCF beats.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 39% year-over-year to $284 million at a 46% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$278M (45.2% margin)” for Q2.

surprises.description: Shift4 One was live in 12 countries and management said it was on track to surpass the 15-country year-end goal. That is ahead of the preview’s checkpoint of at least 10 countries and points to faster rollout than the stated goal alone implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Shift4 One (payments, DCC and tax-free shopping) is now live in 12 countries, on track to surpass the 15-country goal by year-end 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview tracked “7 → 15 countries by year-end” and its checklist said “Shift4 One country count ≥10” would be ahead of plan.

surprises.description: The Q2 Middle East travel impact came in modestly below the embedded $20 million drag, a small positive relative to the preview’s question about whether that estimate would prove conservative or light. The better Q2 outcome was tempered by management’s larger estimated Q3 headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Q2 impact came in modestly better than the forecasted $20 million drag.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 guidance embeds a ~$20M Middle East travel-disruption headwind” and the preview asked whether “the $20M Q2 embed prove conservative or light?”

in_line: Pro forma net leverage was 3.7x, matching the preview’s stated level, and management continued to expect deleveraging to the low 3s by year-end.
Q2 organic GRLNF growth was 11%, meeting the preview’s ≥11% threshold for the key organic-growth test.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $220 million, well above the roughly $203 million consensus and above the company’s $198–208 million guidance range. The 10% growth and 34% margin also substantially exceeded the preview’s expected 2% EBITDA growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 10% to $220 million” and “adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 200 basis points to 34%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” consensus “~$203M (mid)” with implied Y/Y growth of “+2.0%”; company guidance was “$198–208M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 59%, beating the preview’s roughly 57% expectation and expanding from an already strong 58% a year earlier. This was better than expected despite the preview flagging claims costs and summer weather as likely sources of margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 100 basis points to 59%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin” consensus was “~57%”; the preview called Q2 “the air-conditioning failure quarter” and described claims costs and weather as margin risks.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS growth of nearly 20% substantially exceeded the preview’s consensus expectation of 8% growth. The preview cautioned that buybacks could make EPS outperform EBITDA, but the reported growth still came in well above the stated bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS growth of nearly 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus adjusted diluted EPS was “$1.76” versus $1.63 a year earlier, implying “+8.0%”; the preview noted the EPS/EBITDA divergence was buyback-driven.

surprises.description: The company now expects about $330 million of 2026 repurchases and says it will complete its authorization nearly a year ahead of schedule. The preview cited $60 million repurchased in Q1 and an authorization completion target of early 2027, but did not anticipate this faster pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now expects to repurchase approximately $330 million of stock in 2026, completing its authorization nearly a year ahead of schedule,” with “$181 million” already repurchased through July 31.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “buyback pace vs. $60M in Q1” and said the authorization was “targeted for completion by early 2027.”

surprises.description: Retention came in at 79.6%, above both the Q2 prior-year rate of 78.3% and the preview’s 79% bull-case threshold. That was a stronger result than the preview’s concern that another year-over-year decline could indicate churn.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retention rate remained near all-time highs at 79.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2'25 retention was “78.3%,” identified a second consecutive year-over-year decline as a risk, and listed “retention ≥79%” in its bull-case conditions.

surprises.description: Q2 received about $9 million of favorable weather and cost-development effects, helping results, although management expects most of the weather benefit to reverse in Q3. The preview highlighted weather and claims costs as a potential downside risk rather than anticipating these favorable Q2 contributions.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 benefited from “approximately $5 million of favorable weather and about $4 million of favorable cost development,” while management expects “the weather benefit to largely reverse in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q2 as weather- and claims-cost-levered, called contractor costs and summer heat key risks, and identified gross margin as the most likely source of a bad surprise.

surprises.description: The real estate channel grew member count 7% and improved attach rate by 30 basis points despite flat existing-home sales. This showed stronger channel performance than the preview’s modest Q1 real estate growth and focus on attach rates as the controllable driver suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The real estate channel grew member count 7% and improved attach rate 30 basis points” despite flat existing-home sales expected around 4 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 first-year real estate revenue was “$28M (+3%)” and that existing-home-sale volumes remained “the exogenous constraint”; it said to watch attach rate as the controllable metric.

in_line: Revenue of $645 million was close to the $642.1 million consensus and matched the preview’s $645 million base-case scenario.
Total member count grew 1%, meeting the preview’s expectation that Q2 total members turn positive year over year and aligning with the roughly 1% full-year member-growth guidance.

The full-year guidance increase was broadly anticipated conditional on the EBITDA result: the preview said EBITDA of at least $215 million should lead to a $20–30 million guide increase; EBITDA was $220 million and the company raised adjusted EBITDA guidance by $20 million.

surprises.description: Genie reported diluted EPS of $0.43, well above the preview’s $0.25 published consensus and its estimated $0.12–$0.18 buy-side bar. The earnings result was much stronger than either expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net income attributable to Genie common stockholders surged to $11.4 million ($0.43 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.25”; the preview also estimated “the real buy-side bar” at “$0.12–$0.18.”

surprises.description: Consolidated gross margin reached 33.5%, substantially above the preview’s roughly 24% real bar and even its 27–29% bull scenario. The preview treated margin normalization as the quarter’s central test, and the reported recovery was much stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross profit rose 43.4% to $33.7 million with gross margin expanding to 33.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin vs. ~24% (the real bar)”; the bull scenario anticipated “27–29%.”

surprises.description: The customer book contracted sequentially instead of delivering the preview’s expected second consecutive quarter of sequential growth: RCEs fell from 354,000 to 345,000 and meters from 364,000 to 363,000. Gross new additions also slipped to 65,000 from 70,000 a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The customer base shrank to 345,000 RCEs and 363,000 meters” from 413,000 RCEs and 419,000 meters a year earlier; “gross new customer additions” were 65,000 versus 70,000.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bull case requires a second consecutive quarter of sequential growth with churn stable or lower.”

surprises.description: Electricity and gas volumes sold fell sharply, contrary to the preview’s expectation that summer usage would support volume. Higher revenue per unit partly offset the lower volumes, but electricity kilowatt hours fell 17% and gas therms fell 23%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Electricity kilowatt hours sold fell 17% while revenue per kWh rose 12%, and natural gas therms sold dropped 23% while revenue per therm surged 50%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “higher usage/pass-through” to offset the smaller meter book; the bull scenario anticipated that “hot summer drives volume.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in below both the $104.57 million consensus and the preview’s $103–110 million base-case range, at $100.4 million. The shortfall was limited relative to consensus, but the decline was steeper than the preview’s implied 0.7% year-over-year drop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenue declined 4.6% year-over-year to $100.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $104.57M”; the preview’s base scenario was “$103–110M” and showed implied year-over-year revenue of “–0.7%.”

surprises.description: Genie restarted share repurchases, buying about 47,000 Class B shares for $659,000 after no open-market buyback in Q1. The preview had highlighted a resumption as a potential signal that the company would put its cash to work.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned capital by repurchasing ~47,000 Class B shares for $659,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Resumption of repurchases would be the clearest management signal that the balance sheet is being put to work.”

in_line: GREW posted positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.3 million, close to the preview’s base-case expectation of breakeven and consistent with management’s stated plan for Genie Solar to be profitable for the remainder of the year.
SG&A rose with the deliberate shift toward higher-cost customer-acquisition channels; the preview had already flagged that acquisition spending would stay elevated.
Cash, restricted cash, and marketable securities totaled $204.3 million, broadly in line with the preview’s estimate of about $200 million in cash and securities.

surprises.description: Gogo reported Q2 revenue of $222.8 million, below the preview’s roughly $229.4 million consensus and down 1% year over year rather than the expected 1.5% increase. The shortfall was about 3% versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $222.8 million, down 1% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$229.4M”; “Implied Y/Y | +1.5%.”

surprises.description: Management cut FY26 revenue guidance to $870–$895 million from $905–$945 million, despite the preview treating guidance reaffirmation as the base case. The company attributed the cut primarily to Galileo and 5G equipment shipments slipping into the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gogo lowered its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $870–$895 million, driven primarily by the timing of Galileo and 5G equipment shipments slipping into the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management reaffirmed FY26 guidance at Q1 ($905–945M revenue…)”; the base scenario expected guidance to be “reaffirmed but unchanged.”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance fell to $175–$185 million from $198–$218 million. Litigation expense accounted for roughly half the reduction, with product mix accounting for the rest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $175–$185 million, with litigation expense accounting for roughly half the reduction and product mix the remainder.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said guidance had been reaffirmed at Q1 and listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$198–218M.”

surprises.description: FY26 free cash flow guidance was reduced to $65–$85 million from $90–$110 million, against the preview’s emphasis on reaffirmation of that range as the key test. This also leaves the company below the preview’s implied full-year cash-flow path.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow guidance was revised to $65–$85 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “FY26 FCF guidance ($90–110M) — reaffirm vs. cut” as its highest-priority catalyst and said a reaffirmed guide would be enough for the stock to work.

surprises.description: Q2 Galileo shipments were 108, below the preview’s 120–130-unit bar for showing sequential acceleration. That gap weighs against the expected H2 OEM ramp, even though the total number of aircraft online increased.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cumulative Galileo terminal shipments reached 518 units after 108 units shipped in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q2 shipment number below ~120–130 units puts the entire H2 acceleration narrative in question.”

surprises.description: Gogo lowered its FY26 Galileo aircraft-online target to the mid-500s from about 600, a setback to the expected rollout outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced its full-year Galileo aircraft-online target to the mid-500s from a prior expectation of about 600 units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the buy-side as watching the H2 OEM/Galileo ramp and said OEM installs “come online really in Q3, Q4”; it also referenced the prior expectation of about 600 aircraft online.

surprises.description: Military and government service revenue accelerated far beyond the preview’s description of recent momentum: it rose 40% year over year and 20% sequentially, driven by increased usage under existing agreements tied to the Middle East conflict.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Military and government service revenue surged 40% year-over-year and 20% sequentially, driven by heightened usage tied to the Middle East conflict under pre-existing blanket purchase agreements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted service revenue was “+7% Q/Q in Q1” and called military/government momentum a credible offset, but did not anticipate growth of this scale.

surprises.description: 5G shipments rose to 138 units from 52 in Q1, while C1 systems online reached a record 690, up 24% sequentially. That points to stronger near-term 5G activity than the preview’s expectation that units online would ramp in late Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gogo 5G unit shipments rose 165% sequentially to 138 units, and C1 systems online hit a record 690, up 24% from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “52 5G units sold in Q1 (record)” and that “units online ramping ‘late Q3 and Q4.’”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was positive $21.6 million but came in below the preview’s implied $25–$35 million quarterly range. It improved sharply from Q1, but missed the preview’s modeled quarter-level expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow improved to positive $21.6 million from negative $19.2 million in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 free cash flow as “~$25–35M” implied by its model.

in_line: Net leverage rose to 3.8x, consistent with the preview’s warning that leverage was expected to rise in Q2–Q3; the preview said a print above roughly 3.9–4.0x would be the concerning threshold.
The $40 million Satcom Direct earn-out and $21.1 million debt paydown were already identified in the preview as Q2 cash outflows.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $99.3 million, well above both the $86–88 million quarterly guide and the roughly $87.3–87.7 million consensus estimate. The beat was substantially larger than the preview’s bull-case range of $90–93 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached a record $99.3 million” and beat the quarter’s guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus was “$87.33M” / “$87.67M”; company guide was “$86–88M.” The preview’s bull scenario was “$90–93M.”

surprises.description: Amtagvi revenue reached about $91 million, far above its $79–81 million quarterly guide. This was a major segment beat, not just a result of other revenue lines lifting the total.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amtagvi revenue hit a record ~$91 million,” well above the “$79-81 million guidance range for the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Amtagvi (US)” was guided at “$79–81M”; the preview’s bull case assumed Amtagvi of “≥$84M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin surged to 56%, exceeding the prior 50% peak and the preview’s bull-case threshold of 50% or more. That was a much stronger recovery than the preview’s base expectation of 45–48%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached an all-time high of 56%, up from 41% in Q1 and above the prior peak of 50%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “GM 45–48%”; its bull case expected “GM back to ≥50%.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects to raise the $350–370 million FY2026 revenue range in a separate Q3 announcement, rather than simply reaffirming the range as the preview’s base case expected. The preview also treated a cut as a meaningful risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “reviewing and expects to raise full-year 2026 total revenue guidance (currently $350-370 million) via a separate announcement during Q3,” citing “very strong Q3 performance to date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case was FY26 “reaffirmed unchanged,” while the bull case was guidance “narrowed to high end ($360–370M) or raised.”

surprises.description: Iovance reported that R&D expense fell for a fourth consecutive quarter and SG&A stayed flat despite 39% sequential revenue growth, indicating better expense leverage than the preview specifically forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses declined for the fourth consecutive quarter to ~$59 million (from $62 million), while SG&A held flat at ~$39 million despite 39% revenue growth.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that more than 50 commercial Amtagvi patients are now being treated per month, providing a concrete throughput measure of commercial adoption that the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Iovance is now treating more than 50 commercial Amtagvi patients per month.”

surprises.description: Management reported that more than 75% of Amtagvi patients are covered by private payers and that plans covering over 250 million lives have added coverage. The preview did not set an expectation for payer access at this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “More than 75% of Amtagvi patients are covered by private payers, plans covering over 250 million lives have added coverage.”

surprises.description: The FDA granted Fast Track designation for lifileucel in two soft tissue sarcomas, adding a regulatory milestone beyond the preview’s discussion of sarcoma enrollment and the existing response-rate result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA granted Fast Track designation for lifileucel in two soft tissue sarcomas.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed sarcoma with “enrollment begins Q3 2026” and “50% cORR in first six evaluable,” but did not anticipate this designation.

surprises.description: The network’s community centers now make up one-third of ATCs, a specific indication that the community-center expansion highlighted in the preview is progressing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Community centers [are] now one-third of the network.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “the shift toward community (vs academic) centers” as the mechanism for geographic reach, but gave no expected share.

surprises.description: Manufacturing turnaround time improved to 31 days or less, slightly better than the preview’s already-fast benchmark of 32 days or less.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The manufacturing turnaround time is 31 days or less.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited turnaround time of “32 days or less at Q1.”

in_line: ATC count exceeded 95 and remained on track for at least 110 by year-end, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of ATCs in the high-90s/~100 and its stated ≥110 year-end target.
The cash runway into the second half of 2028 was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that cash would fund operations “well into 2028.”
The LUN-202 enrollment and data timing remained within the preview’s anticipated 2026 milestones: enrollment was nearing completion and a Q4 data update was expected.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue, EBITDA and adjusted EPS all materially exceeded the preview’s bar: revenue was $4.2B versus a $3.75–3.90B estimate, EBITDA was $1.2B versus about $985M, and EPS was $1.79 versus a $1.40–1.50 whisper range. The EBITDA and EPS gaps were especially large.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fourth quarter total revenue jumped 28% to $4.2 billion and EBITDA climbed 27% to $1.2 billion”; “Q4 adjusted EPS increased 41% to $1.79 versus $1.27 in the prior year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Treat $3.75–3.90B as the real bar on revenue and $1.40–1.50 as the real bar on EPS,” and estimated “~$985M” of Q4 adjusted EBITDA.

surprises.description: Full-year results also came in ahead of the preview: revenue topped $17B versus an estimate of about $16.8B, EBITDA reached a record $3.9B versus about $3.70B, and adjusted EPS was $5.42 versus roughly $5.02. The EPS and EBITDA gaps were moderate; the revenue gap was smaller.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 revenue grew 5% to over $17 billion and EBITDA rose 8% to a record $3.9 billion”; “Full-year adjusted EPS rose 13% to $5.42.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated FY26 revenue at “~$16.8B,” adjusted EBITDA at “~$3.70B,” and adjusted EPS at “~$5.02.”

surprises.description: Q4 advertising growth was much stronger than the preview’s build implied: advertising revenue surged 78%, compared with the preview’s estimate of about 43% growth, with the World Cup identified as the driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fourth quarter total revenue jumped 28% to $4.2 billion … driven by a 78% surge in advertising revenue tied to the FIFA Men's World Cup.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q4 revenue build estimated advertising at “~$1,545M” and “+43%,” including “~$415M World Cup” advertising in the quarter.

surprises.description: Tubi’s revenue growth substantially outpaced the preview’s expectation, reaching 35% rather than roughly 20%–23%; viewing time also rose 17%. Tubi remained EBITDA-positive in every quarter, consistent with the preview’s expectation of breakeven or better.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tubi delivered its best quarter ever with 35% revenue growth and 17% higher total viewing time,” and was “EBITDA positive in each quarter of fiscal 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Tubi revenue growth of “+23%” (and cited “Tubi +20%+” in its Q4 build), with “breakeven-or-better for three straight quarters.”

surprises.description: Digital investment losses were lower than the preview’s already-below-prior-year expectation, at less than $200M for FY26 versus the preview’s reference to about $290M in FY25. Management also expects further bottom-line improvement in FY27.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital investment losses moderated from just under $300 million in fiscal 2025 to less than $200 million in fiscal 2026, with further bottom-line improvement expected in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 digital investment was tracking “comfortably inside” FY25’s “$290M” and flagged FY27 investment framing as a key watch item.

surprises.description: FOX One retention and incremental subscriber quality sounded better than the already-positive retention expectation: management said churn was well below expectations and subscribers were proving incremental, with minimal cannibalization of traditional MVPD customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FOX One subscribers are proving truly incremental with minimal cannibalization of traditional MVPD customers and churn running well below expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that management had said churn was “much lower than we had expected” and expected qualitative retention confidence, while identifying post-World Cup churn as a key debate.

surprises.description: The upfront showed broad ad-demand strength not specified in the preview: volume grew by double digits across sports, news and Tubi, strength appeared in 8 of 10 tracked categories, and momentum continued into fiscal Q1 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The upfront delivered double-digit volume growth across sports, news and Tubi, with strength in 8 of the 10 tracked ad categories, and momentum continuing into fiscal Q1 2027.”

surprises.description: The political outlook was more specific and potentially stronger for FOX than the preview’s general expectation of a record industry midterm cycle: management said FOX’s political revenue could exceed $260M from the last midterm and approach the $400M-plus level from the 2024 presidential cycle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects a record midterm political cycle, potentially exceeding the $260 million from the last midterm and approaching the $400 million-plus seen in the 2024 presidential cycle.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “record $11B” midterm cycle, referring to estimated total industry spend, but did not give a FOX political revenue outlook.

surprises.description: FOX said it would not amend its current NFL contract and would defer rights repricing discussions until closer to the 2030 opt-out seasons. This pushes any repricing discussion farther out than the preview’s focus on a possible sports-rights cost step-up as a FY27 margin risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FOX will not amend its existing NFL contract, which runs through the 2029 season, deferring any rights repricing negotiations until closer to the 2030 opt-out seasons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed a “sports-rights step-up quantified as a FY27 margin headwind” as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: FOX raised its semiannual dividend to $0.29, an incremental capital return action beyond the preview’s focus on repurchases and the remaining buyback authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “raised its semiannual dividend to $0.29.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on “$3.5B remaining on the authorization” and cumulative repurchases, without forecasting a dividend increase.

in_line: The company expects a record midterm political cycle, consistent with the preview’s expectation of record $11B total industry midterm spending; the more specific FOX revenue potential is a separate upside detail noted above.
The pending Roku acquisition is still expected to close in the first half of calendar 2027, matching the preview’s stated close timing expectation.

Cumulative buybacks were broadly in line with the preview’s expectation: the preview cited more than $8.5B repurchased and about 36% of shares, versus the reported $8.6B of buybacks and about 36% of shares.

surprises.description: LifeStance reported Q2 revenue of $435 million, about 5% above the $414.3 million consensus and above the $405–425 million guidance range. The preview expected a beat to be likely, but the reported revenue was stronger than its base-case range of $416–421 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 26% year-over-year to $435 million, exceeding expectations on both higher visit volumes and revenue per visit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” revenue: “$414.3M”; base scenario revenue: “$416–421M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $66 million, well above the roughly $55 million consensus and the $50–60 million guidance range; the 15.2% margin also exceeded the preview’s 13.3% guide-implied margin and 13.5% watch threshold. This was a substantially stronger conversion of revenue into earnings than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled, rising 94% to $66 million with a margin of 15.2%, an improvement of over 500 basis points versus Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$55M (guide-anchored)”; “Guide mid ($55M/$415M) = 13.3%”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ≥13.5%.”

surprises.description: The full-year revenue midpoint rose by $45 million, from $1.66 billion to $1.705 billion, and the adjusted EBITDA midpoint rose by $15 million, from $210 million to $225 million. The revenue raise exceeded the preview’s $20 million-plus bar, and the new EBITDA midpoint moved above the old $220 million high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance across all metrics, lifting revenue by $45 million to $1.685-$1.725 billion” and “adjusted EBITDA by $15 million to $215-$235 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bar is a $20M+ revenue and $10M+ EBITDA raise at the midpoint”; “the buy-side wants the new midpoint at or above the old high end” of $220 million for EBITDA.

surprises.description: Revenue per visit rose 6%, stronger than the preview’s roughly $163 base-case level and its 4% increase in the bull scenario. Management also narrowed its full-year rate outlook to mid-single-digit increases, citing payer-contracting visibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue per visit increased 6% to $167, prompting management to narrow the full-year rate guidance from low-to-mid to mid-single-digit increases driven by payer contracting visibility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “TRPV ~$163”; “Bull” scenario: “TRPV +4%.”

surprises.description: Net clinician adds were 193, below the preview’s roughly 250-shareholder whisper and its 230–280 base-case range. The preview specifically warned that fewer than 200 adds would fall short of expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The clinician base grew 11% to 8,542, with 193 net adds in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net clinician adds vs. ~250 whisper”; base case: “Adds ~230–280”; “Below +200 adds undercuts the 2027 revenue build.”

surprises.description: The company had deployed $97 million of its previous repurchase authorization, including $49 million in Q2, and approved another $100 million authorization. The preview said use of the existing authorization was untested and did not anticipate a new authorization after that program was nearly used.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a new $100 million share repurchase authorization after deploying $97 million of the prior program, including $49 million in the second quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF and buyback — $100M authorization (Feb 2026); 6M shares repurchased alongside the May secondary. Actual open-market usage is untested.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA is expected to decline sequentially to $49–59 million as LifeStance makes second-half investments in technology, clinical excellence, and clinician compensation and benefits. The preview anticipated second-half costs and a cautious outlook, but did not identify these additional investment areas as the reason for the near-term decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance implies sequentially lower adjusted EBITDA of $49-$59 million due to second-half strategic investments in technology, clinical excellence, and enhanced clinician compensation/benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY EBITDA guide implies 2H dollars below 1H”; the preview attributed the implied pressure to “the multi-year EHR migration cost and de novo drag.”

surprises.description: Management said specialty services should outgrow the core business in future years, a longer-term growth outlook not stated in the preview. The preview’s roughly 40% growth expectation for 2026 was otherwise consistent with the call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty services generated roughly $50 million of revenue last year and are expected to grow about 40% in 2026, with growth outpacing the core business in future years.”

in_line: Visits per average clinician rose 7% year-over-year for the third consecutive quarter, matching the preview’s expectation that productivity had run at about +7% for three straight quarters.
The clinician base grew 11% to 8,542, close to the preview’s expected base of roughly 8,550–8,600, even though quarterly net adds were below expectations.
Specialty services’ roughly 40% expected growth in 2026 was consistent with the preview’s sell-side estimate of about +40%.

The EHR transition and potential short-term productivity disruption were already flagged as a key debate in the preview; the call said the transition is planned for 2027, with 2026 as a planning year and a phased rollout.

surprises.description: Lexicon reported only $0.7 million of Q2 revenue, far below the $3.99 million consensus and the preview’s roughly $4.0 million estimate. The preview expected $2.8 million of licensing, royalties, and other revenue, but the reported total consisted of $0.7 million of INPEFA sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues fell to $0.7 million (INPEFA net sales)” versus $28.9 million in Q2 2025, which included “$27.5 million in Novo Nordisk licensing revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue” consensus was “$3.99M”; the preview’s Q2 estimate was “Total revenue” of “4.0,” including “Licensing / royalties / other” of “2.8.”

surprises.description: INPEFA sales were $0.7 million, below the preview’s $1.2 million estimate and below the $1.0 million level it identified as a potential concern. This was a separate product-sales shortfall within the much larger total-revenue miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues fell to $0.7 million (INPEFA net sales).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “INPEFA net product revenue” at “1.2” and said “a print materially below $1.0M would only matter” as a read-through on sotagliflozin’s commercial infrastructure.

surprises.description: The Zynquista resubmission is now expected by the end of October 2026 rather than the previously guided mid-2026 timeline. Management’s estimate of a standard six-month review puts a decision in Q2 2027, later than the preview’s expectation of a possible 2026 approval.
surprises.fact_evidence: Lexicon “anticipates resubmitting its Zynquista NDA for type 1 diabetes by the end of October 2026, a slight delay from a previously guided mid-2026 timeline”; a “standard 6-month FDA review” would place a decision in “Q2 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said guidance had been “resubmission mid-2026, potential approval in 2026” and noted that approval in 2026 required resubmission by roughly end-June.

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was worse than expected: net loss was $31.8 million, or $0.07 per share, versus the preview’s $19.2 million net-loss estimate and consensus EPS of -$0.05. The preview’s own EPS estimate was -$0.04.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss was $31.8 million ($0.07 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss” of “(19.2)” and “EPS” of “−$0.04”; it listed consensus EPS as “−$0.05.”

surprises.description: The quarter included an unexpected $4.3 million loss from extinguishing debt when Lexicon repaid its Oxford Finance term loans. The preview did not anticipate this one-off charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net loss “included a $4.3 million loss ($0.01 per share) on early extinguishment of debt tied to repaying the Oxford Finance term loans.”

surprises.description: Cash and short-term investments ended June at $190.6 million, about $9.6 million above the preview’s roughly $181 million estimate. The reported balance was aided by a new $100 million Hercules Capital debt facility, rather than just the cash assumptions laid out in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Lexicon held “$190.6 million in cash and short-term investments as of June 30, 2026,” aided by “a new $100 million Hercules Capital debt facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash + investments (6/30)” at “~$181M” and referred to “$45M of undrawn Hercules tranches.”

surprises.description: STENO1’s reported safety profile was reassuring against the preview’s concern that the FDA-required dataset might prove insufficient: DKA rates were described as similar to standard care and well below those in the earlier inTandem trials. The expected exposure levels are still prospective, however, and are not due until the end of August.
surprises.fact_evidence: STENO1 is expected to achieve the FDA-required sotagliflozin exposure levels “by the end of August 2026,” with “DKA rates similar to standard of care and well below those in the earlier inTandem trials.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified the FDA-required patient-exposure and safety data as central and listed a STENO1 dataset “flagged as insufficient” as a bear-case trigger.

in_line: SONATA-HCM enrollment was significantly above target, consistent with the preview’s statement that enrollment had “substantially exceeded” the 500-patient target; the Q1 2027 topline timing was also reaffirmed.

A possible third $10 million Novo Nordisk milestone later in the year was consistent with the preview’s expectation that another $10 million payment was in reach and that the sell-side’s full-year revenue estimate implied H2 licensing revenue.

surprises.description: The preview modeled about $6 million of operating profit and $5 million of net income, but NACCO reported a $2.3 million operating loss and a $1 million net loss (13 cents per share). The $12 million solar-development impairments were not in the preview and drove the reversal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NACCO recorded $12 million in solar development impairment charges tied to two REGEN Resources projects, driving a consolidated operating loss of $2.3 million and a net loss of $1 million (13 cents per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The modeled estimates were “Operating profit … ~$6.0M,” “Net income … ~$5.0M,” and “Diluted EPS … ~$0.70.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $15.9 million, well above the preview’s $11.5 million estimate, even excluding the solar charges. That is a substantially stronger underlying quarterly result than modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA, which excludes the solar charges, rose 72% year-over-year to $15.9 million from $9.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Adjusted EBITDA … ~$11.5M” and “+24%” year over year.

surprises.description: Management said full-year operating profit and net income would fall below 2025 levels because of the solar charges, rather than maintaining the preview’s expectation of meaningful consolidated year-over-year improvement. Adjusted EBITDA is still projected to improve, but management expects growth to moderate in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects full-year 2026 operating profit and net income to fall below 2025 levels due to the solar charges, while adjusted EBITDA is projected to improve year-over-year but with moderating growth in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged whether the FY “meaningful year-over-year improvement” language would remain intact and described the base case as “FY language unchanged.”

surprises.description: The company warned that further solar curtailment or impairment charges could occur in the second half while it seeks asset sales and contract amendments. The preview did not flag this potential for additional charges.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management warned of “possible additional curtailment or impairment charges in the second half of 2026” while pursuing actions to monetize the solar investments and limit exposure.

surprises.description: Utility Coal Mining operating profit reached $6.3 million, above the preview’s roughly $5.5 million estimate, but the reported strength was partly tied to an unusual outage-related accounting effect: reclamation costs were charged to the balance sheet rather than the income statement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Utility coal mining operating profit surged to $6.3 million from $1.2 million” as the company shifted resources to reclamation during a “significant unplanned power plant outage,” “charging costs to the balance sheet rather than the income statement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Utility Coal Mining operating profit at “~$5.5M” and said “Need ≥$5M” to validate the guidance.

surprises.description: NACCO disclosed delayed payments from the Mississippi Lignite Mining Company customer and said it was actively pursuing remedies, with caution about collection timing and inventory valuation. The preview did not identify this customer-payment issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “actively pursuing remedies for delayed payments” from the customer under a contract running “from 1995 to 2032,” and its outlook reflects “caution around collection timing and inventory valuation.”

surprises.description: Minerals and Royalties operating profit was $6.7 million, far above the preview’s $4.2 million estimate and contrary to its modeled quarterly decline. Higher oil prices drove a 46% jump in royalty revenues.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Minerals and royalties operating profit increased to $6.7 million from $5.2 million, aided by a 46% jump in royalty revenues from higher oil prices.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Minerals & Royalties operating profit at “~$4.2M” and said the segment was “Guided to decline on gas production declines.”

surprises.description: NACCO reported $72.3 million of revenue, modestly above the preview’s roughly $70 million estimate; revenue grew 6% rather than the modeled 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenues increased 6% to $72.3 million from $68.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Q2 revenue at “~$70M” and “+3%” year over year.

surprises.description: The company’s remaining-year investment plan was reduced to up to $35 million from the preview’s stated guidance of up to $57 million of additional capex. NACCO also said it would invest only when opportunities meet its capital criteria.
surprises.fact_evidence: NACCO “plans to invest up to $35 million in the remainder of the year only if opportunities meet its capital criteria.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had guided to “up to $57M of additional capex over the balance of 2026.”

in_line: Contract Mining operating profit was $3.8 million, close to the preview’s roughly $4.0 million estimate and above its $3.5 million watch threshold.
Debt of $120.1 million was below the preview’s approximately $140 million watch level.
Management’s expectation that Minerals and Royalties profit would decline in the second half is broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of a decline for the year.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $54.0 million, $4.65 million above the preview’s $49.35 million consensus estimate. The beat was stronger than the preview’s base case of $47–50 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues rose 19.7% to $54.0 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026E | $49.35M”; the base case projected “Revenue | $47–50M.”

surprises.description: Montauk Ag Renewables did not generate power for sale in Q2, despite the preview expecting the first partial quarter of North Carolina revenue, with generation having started in May. Power sales began only in July, and switchgear modifications were still expected to finish in mid-August.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company began generating power for sale from its Turkey, North Carolina facility in July 2026,” with switchgear programming expected to be completed “by mid-August.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the first quarter with any NC revenue — only two months of it”; the preview also said electricity revenue “started May 2026.”

surprises.description: The renewable-electricity outlook was materially lower than the guidance cited in the preview: production is now 185,000–195,000 MWh rather than 195,000–207,000 MWh, and revenue is $23–26 million rather than $33–37 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Montauk reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance” of “185,000-195,000 MWh renewable electricity production ($23-26 million revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “195–207k MWh” and “REG revenue $33–37M.”

surprises.description: RNG commodity revenue fell sharply as lower-price fixed-contract volumes expired, an underlying headwind the preview did not identify. This contrasts with the overall revenue beat and indicates weakness in this revenue stream.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RNG commodity revenue fell approximately 63.7% as fixed lower-price contract volumes declined about 80% due to contract expirations.”

surprises.description: Net income turned positive at $0.2 million, versus the preview’s expected GAAP loss implied by its $(0.02) EPS estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income turned positive at $0.2 million compared to a $5.5 million net loss in Q2 2025.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $12.3 million, above the preview’s estimated $9–11 million range. It exceeded even the top of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA surged 144.5% to $12.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$9–11M (no formal consensus).”

surprises.description: GreenWave-related environmental-attribute revenues were a substantial, unanticipated contributor to the quarter: about $8.4 million came from GreenWave RIN distributions and pathway dispensing, with additional JV investment income reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue was driven primarily by “~$8.4 million in environmental attribute revenues from GreenWave RIN distributions and pathway dispensing”; GreenWave contributed “approximately $3.8 million in JV investment income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on RIN sell-through and current-period generation, describing Q2 RIN revenue as needing to be “carried by current-period generation at spot”; it did not anticipate this GreenWave contribution.

surprises.description: The company reported long-term agreements covering more than 350,000 hog spaces toward its 400,000–450,000-space first-phase target, a concrete development milestone not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Secured long-term agreements covering over 350,000 of the targeted 400,000-450,000 hog spaces for its first development phase.”

in_line: RNG production and revenue guidance was reaffirmed at 5.8–6.0 million MMBtu and $175–190 million, consistent with the preview’s stated guidance.
Q2 realized RIN pricing of $2.45 was close to the preview’s expectation of roughly $2.40–$2.42.
The committed average price for most Q3 RNG-production RINs, $2.66, was roughly in line with July’s $2.64 D3 index price.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $57 million, above the preview’s $50.0–$52.1 million consensus range, although still within its $45–$60 million base-case range. This was a modest headline beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue fell to $57 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue **$50.0M** (Zacks-derived) to **$52.1M** (ChartMill)”; the preview also described the base case as “Revenue | **$45–60M**.”

surprises.description: Novavax reported $19 million in product sales, up 76%, driven by Matrix-M demand from Takeda and Serum Institute. The preview expected near-zero Q2 Nuvaxovid sales but did not forecast this Matrix-M contribution to product sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product sales rose 76% year-over-year to $19 million, driven by Matrix-M demand from Takeda and Serum Institute.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Nuvaxovid product sales near zero (Q2 is the seasonal trough).”

surprises.description: The company raised its FY2026 adjusted revenue range by $5 million at both ends, rather than reiterating the existing range as the preview expected. The increase was small, and the revised guidance excludes Sanofi supply sales, royalties, and milestones.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted revenue guidance to $235-$275 million ($255 million midpoint), a $5 million midpoint increase, while noting this excludes Sanofi supply sales, royalties, and milestones.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted revenue guide: reiterated $230–270M, raised, or narrowed to the low end?”

surprises.description: Novavax lowered its FY2026 combined GAAP R&D and SG&A expense guidance by $10 million at the midpoint, an improvement on the preview’s expectation that the expense guide would be reaffirmed. The preview’s stated expense range was on a non-GAAP basis, so the comparison is not like-for-like.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered full-year 2026 combined GAAP R&D and SG&A expense guidance to $390 million midpoint (a $10 million improvement).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance to be defended” included “Non-GAAP R&D + SG&A | $310–340M”; the base scenario expected “expense guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The company said the expected $75 million Sanofi tech-transfer milestone would extend its cash runway into 2029, beyond the preview’s stated runway expectation of into 2028. The extension depends on the milestone being received.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The expected $75 million Sanofi tech transfer milestone would extend the company's cash runway from 2028 into 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash + AR | Funds ops into 2028”; the preview also flagged runway language of “into 2028 without new inflows.”

in_line: The $75 million Sanofi tech-transfer milestone was not reported as recognized in Q2 and is expected upon completion around mid-2027, consistent with the preview’s view that it was most likely outside FY2026 guidance.

The Matrix-M partner footprint remained consistent with the preview: four of the top 10 pharma companies have licensing or material-transfer agreements, and partners cover more than 30 areas of experimentation.
Sanofi’s intent to be an early mover in the COVID-flu combination market and its advanced discussions on Phase III timing matched the preview’s focus on regulatory alignment and Phase III timing.

The 2028 cost-reduction and profitability goals were consistent with the preview’s expected targets: approximately $150–$200 million in combined non-GAAP R&D and SG&A and non-GAAP profitability as early as 2028.

surprises.description: The preview estimated June 30 cash of about $90–94 million; the company reported $100.4 million in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash. That is above the forecast range, although the reported figure includes restricted cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaling $100.4 million as of June 30, 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview’s EPS estimate was a $0.06 loss per share, but Ocugen reported a $0.07 loss per share. The preview warned that financing-related accounting could weigh on GAAP results, but the reported loss was still worse than its estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a net loss of $0.07 per share versus $0.05 the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) … My Estimate $(0.06)”

surprises.description: R&D expense was below the preview’s expected $11.5–13.0 million range, coming in at $10.7 million despite the preview’s expectation that spending would step up as late-stage trials advanced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D of $10.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&D expense … My Estimate $11.5 – $13.0M”; the preview also said “R&D should step up.”

surprises.description: G&A expense came in below the preview’s $7.5–8.5 million estimate, at $7.2 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “G&A of $7.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “G&A expense … My Estimate $7.5 – $8.5M”

surprises.description: The reported Phase 2 Armada result for OCU410 was a statistically significant 31% reduction in geographic atrophy lesion growth in the specified lesion range, with roughly twice the benefit of approved complement inhibitors from one injection. The preview did not set an expectation for this efficacy result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OCU410 delivered a statistically significant 31% reduction in GA lesion growth (in lesions 2.5-17.5 mm2), roughly twice the benefit of approved complement inhibitors from a single injection, plus 27% ellipsoid zone preservation.”

surprises.description: Management set a target of three BLA submissions by 2028, including a mid-2027 BLA submission for OCU410ST. The preview focused on the OCU400 rolling BLA and did not anticipate this broader submission target or OCU410ST filing timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is targeting three BLA submissions by 2028”; “OCU410ST … followed by BLA submission mid-2027.”

surprises.description: Ocugen reported that more than 325 patients across its pipeline had been treated without a drug-related serious adverse event, a safety update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Across the pipeline (Phase 1-3), more than 325 patients have been treated with no drug-related serious adverse events reported to date.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted additional potential funding sources beyond the Root licensing opportunity discussed in the preview: a possible $100–200 million priority review voucher sale and about $15 million from Janus Henderson warrants if exercised. These are potential, not completed, sources of capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a potential priority review voucher sale valued at $100-200 million, 10 million Janus Henderson warrants at $1.50 (expiring August 2027) that could raise ~$15 million.”

in_line: The company said the $130 million financing extended its cash runway into 2028, consistent with the preview’s expectation that runway into 2028 would be reaffirmed.
OCU400 had completed enrollment and was expected to report Phase 3 Limelight top-line data in Q1 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated enrollment status and timing.

OCU410ST had completed enrollment/dosing, with its interim decision expected in Q3 2026 and top-line data in Q2 2027, consistent with the preview’s expected GARDian3 interim timing and Q2 2027 topline.
OCU410 Phase 3 initiation was targeted for September 2026, within the preview’s expected Q3 2026 start window.
The Root Pharmaceutical MENA licensing term sheet remained part of the funding picture, as the preview had already identified the term sheet and its execution window.

surprises.description: PLTK reported Q2 revenue of $731.1 million, above the preview’s $713.1 million consensus, and revenue grew 5.0% year over year versus the preview’s expected 2.5%. The sequential decline was also milder than the preview’s 4.2% consensus-based decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $731.1 million, down 1.8% sequentially but up 5.0% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $713.1M” consensus; “YoY +2.5%”; “QoQ −4.2%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $206.1 million, well above the preview’s modeled roughly $180 million and above the $200 million level the preview said would validate the guide. The 28.2% margin also exceeded the preview’s roughly 25% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $206.1 million”; “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 28.2% in Q2 from 16.8% in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: No published consensus sourced — I model ~$180M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~25% (modeled)”; “≥$200M validates the guide.”

surprises.description: Although PLTK kept its full-year guidance ranges unchanged, management now expects to finish toward the lower end of both revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance. That is weaker than the preview’s base case of an unchanged reaffirmation without this lower-end qualification.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is maintaining its full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance ranges but now expects to finish toward the lower end of both.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (~50%): … FY guide reaffirmed unchanged”; the preview also said “Base case is an in-line-to-slightly-better quarter … and a reaffirmed guide.”

surprises.description: D2C revenue came in below the preview’s modeled $290–300 million range and declined sequentially rather than being roughly flat. Its 39.3% share of revenue was close to the preview’s 40% threshold, but the revenue level and sequential trend were weaker than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “D2C revenue reached $286.9 million, or 39.3% of total revenue, up 63.1% year-over-year despite a 1.7% sequential decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “DTC revenue ~$290–300M (modeled)”; the base scenario expected “DTC flat sequentially.”

surprises.description: Disney Solitaire rose 15.5% sequentially even as marketing spend was reduced meaningfully. The preview identified sequential growth as the bull-case outcome but highlighted the risk of decay after the earlier front-loaded acquisition spend; the reported growth was a stronger result than that concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Disney Solitaire generated $142.4 million, up 15.5% sequentially and 288.6% year-over-year, growing even as marketing spend was reduced meaningfully.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “This is the first clean read on the decay curve without the marketing crutch. Sequential growth = bull case intact; a >15% sequential drop = the whole SuperPlay valuation narrative wobbles.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that Super Play titles, including Disney Solitaire, are expected to decline sequentially in the second half, with Super Play marketing investment being cut roughly 70% versus the first half and the largest step-down in Q3. The preview focused on the immediate post-spend Disney trajectory and did not anticipate this explicit second-half revenue decline and steep investment reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Super Play titles, including Disney Solitaire, will see revenue decline sequentially in the second half due to deliberately front-loaded user acquisition spend tied to the earnout structure”; “Overall Super Play marketing investment is being cut by roughly 70% in the second half versus the first half, with the largest step-down concentrated in Q3.”

surprises.description: Bingo Blitz weakened more than the preview’s already-negative outlook: revenue fell 9.5% year over year versus the preview’s cited 5.4% decline, and it also fell sequentially. Management attributed the weakness to players acquired in the last 12 months after shifting away from incentive-driven acquisition channels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bingo Blitz revenue fell to $145.1 million, down 5.6% sequentially and 9.5% year-over-year, with declines concentrated in players acquired in the last 12 months after a shift away from incentive-driven acquisition channels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bingo Blitz $153.7M (−5.4% YoY).”

surprises.description: Audience metrics deteriorated more than the preview anticipated: DAU fell 9.1% year over year versus the preview’s expected 4.4% decline. Daily paying users also declined, though the preview did not give a specific expectation for that metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average daily active users down 9.1% year-over-year to 8 million and daily paying users down 2.9% to 367,000.”

surprises.description: ARPDAU rose substantially faster than the preview expected, increasing 16.1% year over year versus the preview’s cited 8.0% increase. This more than offset the expected level of monetization growth even as the audience contracted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ARPDAU rose 16.1% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Shrinking-audience-squeezed-harder … 8.6M DAU (−4.4% YoY) monetized harder at $0.94 ARPDAU (+8.0%).”

surprises.description: Management newly cited softening consumer sentiment and inflation pressure on discretionary spending, including a steeper-than-typical demand step-down from May to June. The preview discussed softer DTC traffic as a risk but did not flag this broader demand deterioration or the unusually sharp monthly step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged softening consumer sentiment and inflation pressure on discretionary spending, observing a steeper-than-typical demand step-down from May to June.”

in_line: The full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance ranges themselves were maintained, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a reaffirmation; the lower-end outlook within those ranges was a separate negative surprise.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $265.7 million, well above the $249.7 million consensus estimate. The roughly $16 million beat was stronger than the preview’s expectation that the quarter’s headline print would be close to flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue rose 6.5% to $265.7 million” and beat internal sales expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 FY27 Consensus” revenue: “$249.7M”; the preview said the quarter’s print was “close to irrelevant” and consensus implied “~flat” year-over-year revenue.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.98, above the preview’s $0.88–$0.89 consensus range. That also reversed the expected year-over-year decline, despite higher acquisition-financing interest expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased approximately 3% year-over-year to $0.98,” partly offset by higher interest expense from acquisition financing.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 FY27 Consensus” adjusted diluted EPS: “$0.88 (some feeds $0.89)” and implied “–7.5%” year-over-year.

surprises.description: Organic revenue growth was 3.2% excluding FX and Breathe Right, stronger than the preview’s base-case expectation of a decline and above its flat-to-modestly-negative hurdle. However, about 2 points came from retailer order timing, which management expects to reverse into a modest organic decline in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic growth of 3.2% excluding FX and the Breathe Right acquisition”; retailer order timing “added about 2 points of growth in Q1 and is expected to reverse in Q2,” prompting guidance for “a modest organic revenue decline” in Q2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Organic –2% to –4%”; it said Q1 needed to be “at least flat-to-modestly-negative” to support the full-year outlook.

surprises.description: Q1 adjusted gross margin was 55%, above the preview’s approximate 52%–54% range and with less year-over-year compression than its expected 250–350 basis points. Management still reported a 120-basis-point decline, citing transportation costs and mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 55% in Q1 (down 120 basis points year-over-year on higher transportation costs and mix).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q1 gross margin at “~52–54%” and expected “–250 to –350 bps” year-over-year.

surprises.description: Quarterly adjusted free cash flow reached a record $83.7 million, contrary to the preview’s expectation that it would likely be down because of interest and deal costs. Management attributed much of the result to favorable working-capital timing, so the record may not represent a recurring run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarterly record adjusted free cash flow of $83.7 million, largely driven by favorable working capital timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said free cash flow was “Likely down on interest + deal costs.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $4.55–$4.65 was below the preview’s pro forma bridge of roughly $4.60–$4.75, especially at the top end. The guidance was raised, but its range leaves less earnings upside than the preview modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2027… adjusted EPS [guidance was raised] to $4.55-$4.65.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s pro forma FY27 bridge estimated “~$4.60–4.75”; its base scenario expected “$4.60–4.72.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance rose to at least $270 million, above the May guidance of at least $250 million. This was a favorable increase against the prior outlook, even though the preview had warned that near-term cash flow could be pressured.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised to at least $270 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave May FY27 guidance as “FCF ≥$250M.”

in_line: Full-year revenue guidance of $1.29–$1.315 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s pro forma estimate of about $1.29–$1.31 billion; the preview expected a mechanical acquisition-driven reset.
The acquisitions’ roughly $190 million of revenue contribution this year was close to the preview’s estimated combined contribution of about $185–$200 million.

Clear Eyes remained supply-constrained, with improvement expected in the second half and recovery taking multiple years, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q1 would remain constrained and the capacity ramp would be an H2 story.

Net debt of about $2 billion and projected year-end leverage just below 4x were broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of roughly $1.9–$2.0 billion of post-deal net debt and leverage around 4x.
Breathe Right’s expected annualized accretion of about $0.25 was within the preview’s $0.20–$0.30 estimate.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 revenue of about $505.5–506.3 million. Adding continuing-operations revenue of $442 million and TheFork's $61 million of discontinued-operations revenue gives $503 million, a small miss against that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 continuing operations revenue was $442 million”; “TheFork (now discontinued operations) contributed $61 million revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $505.5–506.3M.”

surprises.description: The preview put adjusted EBITDA at about $80–82 million. The reported $76 million from continuing operations plus $11 million from TheFork totals $87 million, above that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 continuing operations revenue was $442 million with adjusted EBITDA of $76 million, while TheFork (now discontinued operations) contributed $61 million revenue and $11 million adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$80–82M (implied).”

surprises.description: The preview expected Hotels & Other revenue to decline 21–24%, implying roughly $156–162 million. It came in at $163 million, slightly better than the top of that range, while its 28% adjusted EBITDA margin remained strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Hotels & Other segment revenue declined 21% to $163 million, though it remained highly profitable at 28% adjusted EBITDA margin, down only about 100 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hotels & Other — still the profit engine — is guided to shrink 21–24%.”

surprises.description: For Q3, Experiences bookings are guided to grow 5–7%, but revenue is guided from down 2% to up 1%. That leaves a bookings-to-revenue gap wider than the roughly 3-point spread the preview treated as the expected case, even allowing for about 1 point of currency headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 Experiences guidance projects 5% to 7% bookings growth but revenue of -2% to +1% (including ~1 point of currency headwind).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance implies bookings growing ~3pts faster than revenue, blamed on higher cancellations. If that gap holds at ~3pts, it's a macro story. If it widens, it's a structural take-rate story.”

surprises.description: The preview framed FY26 as approximately flat in revenue and expected investors to look for that framing to be reaffirmed. The new Q3 outlook instead calls for continuing-operations revenue to fall 7–10% and describes the second-half outlook as more prudent, a more cautious trajectory than the preview's flat-year framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for continuing operations revenue declines of 7% to 10% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 17% to 20%, reflecting a more prudent second-half outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: ‘approximately flat revenue, approximately flat adj. EBITDA margin.’”

surprises.description: Experiences adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 11%, down 290 basis points, as channel mix shifted toward free channels. The preview highlighted the question of whether cost reductions could offset mix decay; the segment's margin contraction shows that mix pressure was substantial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Experiences segment adjusted EBITDA fell to $31 million (11% of revenue), down 290 basis points, due to a free/paid channel mix shift across Viator and Tripadvisor points of sale.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether cost-out is offsetting mix decay or merely masking it.”

surprises.description: The preview described $700 million as inbound cash from TheFork; the company now expects approximately $680 million in net proceeds. The deal remains expected to close before year-end, but expected net cash is below the headline transaction value.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tripadvisor agreed to sell TheFork to American Express for $700 million, expecting approximately $680 million in net proceeds”; closing is “anticipated before year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TheFork ($700M cash to American Express)” and “$700M of inbound cash.”

in_line: Experiences bookings grew 5%, at the bottom of the preview's 5–8% guide; Viator's 10% point-of-sale growth was partly offset by the Tripadvisor point-of-sale SEO drag the preview warned about.

TheFork was classified as discontinued operations, one of the print-mechanics outcomes the preview explicitly flagged. Including its revenue, the quarter's total was near consensus rather than the much lower continuing-operations headline alone.
Hotels & Other's 21% revenue decline was within the preview's expected 21–24% decline range.

No shares were repurchased during the portfolio review, while proceeds were left for debt reduction and/or repurchases. The preview's base case anticipated capital-allocation decisions being deferred until closing, although it had also noted investor hopes for a sized commitment.

surprises.description: VAC’s Q2 contract sales were far above the preview’s roughly $470 million estimate and +4% to +8% company guide: sales rose 22% to $545 million. The result also exceeded the preview’s bull-case marker of $481 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 contract sales rose 22% year-over-year to $545 million,” exceeding the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Consolidated contract sales ~$470M” and cited company guidance of “+4% to +8% ($463–481M).” Its bull case was “$481M+ (+8%+).”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised substantially, rather than merely reaffirmed or narrowed toward the upper half as the preview hoped. The new $805–830 million range is $50 million above the prior range and implies a stronger H2 than the preview’s already demanding ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by $50 million to $805-830 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$755–780M” and said the buy side wanted it “narrowed to the upper half or raised”; its base case was “reaffirmed,” while its bull case was “narrowed to the upper half or raised.”

surprises.description: The Q2 VPG result greatly exceeded the preview’s expectation of a mid-to-high-single-digit increase and its view that VPG might decelerate from April while remaining positive. VPG instead rose 23% and exceeded the high end of guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Contract sales were driven by “industry-leading VPGs of $4,477 (up 23%), exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed VPG as “Up mid-to-high single digits” and said its base case was that “VPG decelerates from April’s +12.7% but stays positive.”

surprises.description: Management described unusually strong monthly momentum: May and June were the company’s two highest sales months on record, and July growth stayed near 29%. That was much stronger than the preview’s concern that momentum might roll over after April, particularly given HGV’s late-quarter weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “May and June were the two highest sales months in company history,” and “July trends continued at roughly 29% growth, consistent with May/June.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the guide leaned on momentum with only April in hand, asked whether “June held,” and highlighted HGV’s report that sales execution “fell short in the back half of the quarter.” Its base case expected VPG to “decelerate from April’s +12.7%.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA beat both the preview’s guide-midpoint estimate and the top of the company’s prior range. The $215 million result was $20 million above the midpoint of guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 6% to $215 million, coming in $20 million above the midpoint of Q2 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated adjusted EBITDA at “~$194M (guide midpoint)” and cited company guidance of “$187–202M.”

surprises.description: Full-year contract sales growth guidance was lifted to 18%–20%, with management indicating 25%–29% growth in the second half. The preview focused on the existing Q2 guide and H2 EBITDA ramp, but did not anticipate this substantially higher full-year sales outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “lifted contract sales growth guidance to 18-20%, implying 25-29% growth in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 contract sales guidance of “+4% to +8%” and discussed the H2 EBITDA ramp, but gave no comparable full-year contract-sales growth outlook.

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted free cash flow range rose to $410–460 million, a $35 million increase at the midpoint. The preview’s existing reference point was $375–425 million, although it did expect H1 cash flow above roughly $200 million to keep the story intact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date adjusted free cash flow reached $201 million versus just $22 million in the prior-year period,” and full-year guidance was raised to “$410-460 million (a $35 million midpoint increase).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited the “$375–425M FY guide” and said “H1 FCF tracking above ~$200M keeps the story intact”; its bull case anticipated a guide raised “above $425M.”

surprises.description: Owner sales and owner VPG were exceptionally strong, with owner contract sales growing faster than the already-surprising companywide result. The preview did not set an owner-sales or owner-VPG expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owner contract sales surged 41% year-over-year, fueled by a 33% lift in owner VPG.”

surprises.description: VAC provided a much larger quantified scale-up for its Inner Circle events than the preview had available: the platform is expected to grow from about 50 events in 2026 to 1,000 in 2027, with VPGs well above average. The preview had asked for quantified proof points from the initiative but did not anticipate this scale or performance detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Inner Circle event platform is scaling aggressively from about 50 events in 2026 to a targeted 1,000 events in 2027,” with events “generating VPGs well above average.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked for “quantified early reads” on the modernization initiatives, including Inner Circle, and said investors needed “package sales, tour flow generated, conversion,” not adjectives.

surprises.description: Management signaled openness to opportunistic share repurchases once leverage falls into the upper 3s. The preview highlighted capital returns and buyback pace as a watch point, but did not have this specific conditional buyback signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net corporate debt was $3.1 billion and leverage fell to “~4x from 4.2x”; management signaled “openness to opportunistic share repurchases as leverage drops into the upper 3s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Buyback pace … leverage trajectory” as a key item to watch, but did not describe a specific repurchase trigger or management commitment.

in_line: Year-to-date adjusted free cash flow of $201 million was broadly in line with the preview’s marker that H1 tracking above roughly $200 million would keep the cash-flow story intact; the raised full-year guide was the upside surprise.

surprises.description: Adjusted core EPS was $1.19, well above the preview’s central estimate of about $0.90 (and above the cited alternative estimate of $1.11). That is a positive reversal from the preview’s expected 22% year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted core EPS increased 3% to $1.19.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS — adjusted core: ~$0.90 (some feeds $1.11)” and “Implied Δ: –22% YoY.”

surprises.description: Reported diluted EPS was only $0.09, far below the preview’s derived estimate of $0.50–$0.65. The call attributed the gap to $23 million of charges and operating costs tied to legacy fraudulent problem loans.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported diluted EPS was only $0.09 due to $23 million of charges and operating costs tied to legacy fraudulent problem loans.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS — GAAP diluted: not cleanly published; my est. $0.50–0.65.”

surprises.description: Transaction volume reached $14.4 billion, below the preview’s $15.5–$16.5 billion estimate and representing just 3% year-over-year growth rather than the preview’s implied 11–18%. Financing volume grew, but that did not prevent the overall shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 transaction volume rose 3% year-over-year to $14.4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Transaction volume … my est. $15.5–16.5B” and “Implied Δ: +11–18% YoY.”

surprises.description: Management said the core business would land toward the lower end of original guidance if current market conditions persist, rather than offering the confident, on-track outlook the preview expected in its base case. The outcome could be higher if conditions improve, so this was a conditional caution rather than a stated guidance cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The core business would land toward the lower end of original guidance if current market conditions persist, or middle-to-upper range if conditions improve.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as the guide being “on track” and the bull case as “FY guide reaffirmed with confidence.”
