surprises.description: The legacy Fannie Mae review is expected to produce another $12–$16 million of credit-related charges in Q3, despite management saying no further loan repurchases are anticipated from either GSE. The additional charges are a negative departure from the preview’s no-new-charges bull-case catalyst, while the expected end of repurchases is a favorable part of the update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An additional $12 million to $16 million in credit-related charges in Q3 2026 to finalize Fannie Mae's review, with no further loan repurchases anticipated from either GSE.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “repurchase exposure ≤$165M with zero new charges” as a catalyst and said any new disclosure could reset the trust discount.

surprises.description: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac lending volume fell 10% in the quarter even though the preview emphasized expanded GSE lending capacity as a source of volume runway. The year-to-date share gain to nearly 15% is a counterpoint, but the quarterly volume decline was weaker than that constructive capacity backdrop suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac lending volumes fell 10% in the quarter against a strong prior-year comparison, though year-to-date GSE market share climbed 350 basis points to nearly 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the 2026 caps provided a “volume runway” and highlighted that “the volume runway exists if WD can take it.”

in_line: The quarterly dividend was maintained at $0.68 per share, as the preview’s catalyst checklist contemplated.

The at-risk book’s two-times DSCR and 61% weighted average underwritten LTV were consistent with the preview’s description of the underlying book as healthy, with DSCR above 2x and average LTV of 61%.

surprises.description: Viatris beat the Q2 revenue consensus by about 3%, while adjusted EPS of $0.69 was about 11% above consensus; adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion also topped the preview’s $1.00–$1.05 billion estimate. The profitability beat was especially strong relative to those expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues of $3.8 billion … adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion, and adjusted EPS of $0.69, all exceeding expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … $3.68B”; “Adjusted EPS … $0.62”; “Adjusted EBITDA ~$1.00–1.05B (my est., not published consensus).”

surprises.description: Greater China growth came in much stronger than the preview’s expected slowdown: sales grew 16% year over year versus the preview’s 7.3% estimate, with e-commerce up 36%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Greater China net sales grew 16% year-over-year with e-commerce sales up 36%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The segment table put Greater China at “$631.7M” and “+7.3%” year over year, and said “Street models a big slowdown.”

surprises.description: The preview expected management to reiterate no policy change this year, but the call flagged a hospital-channel procurement policy change that is expected to moderate Greater China growth in the second half. This adds a newly identified headwind to the strong current-quarter performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects growth to moderate in the second half due to a hospital-channel procurement policy change.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to listen for “reiteration of Le Goff’s ‘no policy change this year’ (VBP) call.”

surprises.description: The Nashik facility fire and May FDA inspection are expected to cost $100–$150 million of second-half revenue, a supply disruption not identified in the preview. The impact is limited to low-margin generics, with no single affected product above $20 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Supply disruptions from the Nashik facility fire and May 2026 FDA inspection are expected to reduce second-half revenues by $100 million to $150 million, primarily affecting low-margin generics with no single impacted product exceeding $20 million.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 57.5%, improving by nearly a percentage point, against the preview’s 56.0% Q1 reference point. The preview flagged margin quality as a key watch item but did not forecast this improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin improved nearly 1 percentage point to 57.5%, driven by strong Greater China performance and favorable North American generics product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adjusted gross margin vs. 56.0% (Q1)” as a metric to watch.

surprises.description: Management gave a new, favorable outlook for fast-acting meloxicam: FDA approval is expected by year-end and peak sales could reach $500 million. The preview discussed new-product revenue and Gwyn Lo, but did not flag this product’s approval timing or sales potential.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fast-acting meloxicam is expected to gain FDA approval by year-end and is projected to reach up to $500 million in peak sales,” with opioid-sparing labeling negotiations beginning in October–November.

surprises.description: Management said selatogrel could still be commercially acceptable with a 10%–15% benefit, even though the Phase III study is powered to detect a 20% risk reduction. This is new framing that may lower the efficacy bar for commercial viability, while also highlighting that the study could deliver a smaller benefit than its design targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The selatogrel Phase III SOS study is powered for a 20% risk reduction but management believes a 10-15% benefit would be commercially acceptable,” with a readout expected in the first half of 2027.

surprises.description: Both cenerimod Phase III SLE studies enrolled more than 70% interferon-1 high patients, exceeding the target, an encouraging trial-enrollment update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Both Phase III cenerimod SLE studies enrolled over 70% interferon-1 high patients (exceeding target), with top-line results expected in early 2027.”

surprises.description: Viatris disclosed that it divested its Tirva eye-care rights, a portfolio change not discussed in the preview; the facts provided do not indicate the financial terms or rationale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company divested its Tirva eye-care rights.”

surprises.description: The FDA approved Viatris’s Winland contraceptive patch, a product approval not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] received FDA approval for the Winland contraceptive patch.”

in_line: A full-year guidance increase was expected: the preview said consensus already embedded a raise and described a top-half raise as its base case. Viatris raised the midpoint of full-year guidance across its key metrics.

surprises.description: CARS’ adjusted EBITDA margin reached 29.4%, above both the 28.0–29.0% company range and the preview’s roughly 28.5% consensus expectation. Adjusted EBITDA was $53 million, also above the preview’s roughly $51.5 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded nearly 100 basis points to 29.4%, outperforming the high end of guidance for the second consecutive quarter, with adjusted EBITDA of $53 million up 4% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ~28.5% (implied)” and “Company Guide (set May 7) 28.0–29.0%”; “Adj. EBITDA ~$51.5M (implied).”

surprises.description: The Q3 margin range of 28.5–29.5% is below the roughly 30–31% H2 pace the preview said was needed to achieve the reaffirmed full-year 29–30% margin guidance. The full-year guide was held, but the near-term range leaves the back-half ramp unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of flat to 2% revenue growth and 29% to 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, with Q3 revenue guided flat to up 2% and Q3 margin of 28.5% to 29.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “To hit the FY 29–30% guide, H2 margins need to run ~30–31%” and “The back-half ramp is the single biggest credibility question on this print.”

surprises.description: OEM and national revenue fell 18%, substantially steeper than the preview’s base expectation of an 8–12% decline and worse than the prior-quarter decline. That is a sharper Q2 drop than the preview’s expected trough scenario suggested, even though total revenue remained in guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “3% dealer revenue growth offsetting an 18% decline in OEM and national revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified OEM & National revenue as “−12% Y/Y” in Q1, said management called Q2 “the trough,” and gave a base case of “OEM/National −8–12%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.51 exceeded the preview’s $0.49 consensus estimate. The beat was positive but relatively small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS increased to $0.51 from $0.41.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $0.49.”

surprises.description: Marketplace revenue grew more than 7%, and marketplace subscribers reached their highest level since 2023. That is stronger evidence of marketplace growth than the preview’s concern that another sequential dealer-count decline could undermine the subscription-growth thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marketplace revenue grew over 7% year-over-year, the fastest growth rate in the company's public history outside of 2021's pandemic recovery, with marketplace subscribers hitting their highest level since 2023.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a second sequential decline turns ‘intentional pruning’ into ‘churn,’ and the bull case on marketplace subscription growth breaks,” with dealer count expected around 19,390 sequentially in its base case.

surprises.description: ARPD reached $2,500, a record for marketplace-only ARPD, slightly above the preview’s base-case estimate of about $2,480 and providing evidence that package bundling is raising monetization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 ARPD was $2,500, up 3% year-over-year and 1% sequentially, setting a new record for marketplace-only ARPD driven by Premium Plus.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “ARPD ~$2,480”; it also said “ARPD > $2,500 would be the first hard evidence the bundle is monetizing.”

surprises.description: Website units declined, and management described a product-innovation turnaround that will take 2–3 quarters, with renewed website growth not expected until 2027. The preview focused on declining traffic but did not flag this product-led recovery timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Website (DI) units declined year-over-year, with management signaling a 2-3 quarter product-innovation turnaround plan and expecting renewed website growth in 2027.”

surprises.description: Despite lower traffic and unique visitors, lead conversion rose by double digits and performance-marketing cost per lead improved. That is a more favorable efficiency result than the preview’s emphasis on persistent traffic declines as a structural concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Website traffic and unique visitors declined year-over-year due to an intentional shift away from low-converting traffic, while Q2 lead conversion rose double digits and performance marketing cost per lead improved.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted traffic declines as “the structural bear thesis” and called for watching “Persistent double-digit UV decline.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $179.9 million, within the company’s $178.7–182.3 million guide and close to the preview’s $180.6 million consensus estimate.
Full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance were reaffirmed, as the preview identified reaffirmation as the base case.
Premium Plus penetration was at or near double digits mid-year and tracking toward the 15% year-end target, consistent with the preview’s cited 7% Q1 level and 15% target.
The $90 million full-year repurchase target remained in place, and the company said it was pacing toward it.

surprises.description: Allstate reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $8.99, far above the preview’s tradeable expectation of roughly $5.75–$5.85. The gap was about 54%–56%, substantially larger than the preview’s base-case EPS of about $6.40.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted net income was $2.3 billion or $8.99 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat $5.75–5.85 as the tradeable bar”; the preview’s base scenario estimated “Adj. EPS ~ $6.40.”

surprises.description: Property-Liability profitability was substantially better than the preview’s base case: the reported combined ratio was 86.6% versus a modeled base of about 92.0%. The underlying loss ratio improved 1.1 points, while a 1-point higher expense ratio partly offset that improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Property-Liability combined ratio improved 4.5 points to 86.6%,” with “1.1 points of underlying loss ratio improvement,” partly offset by “a 1-point higher expense ratio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario forecast a “Reported P-L CR ~92.0” and an underlying CR of “~81.0”; the preview said “At or below ~80 is a clean beat; 82+ confirms the margin-rollover thesis.”

surprises.description: Favorable reserve development was greater than the preview’s base-case allowance: prior-year reserve releases contributed 2 points to the quarterly combined-ratio improvement, versus a modeled base of about 0.5 point favorable development. Auto releases reached $1.5 billion year-to-date, with about half of the bodily-injury changes tied to accident years 2023 and 2024.
surprises.fact_evidence: The combined-ratio improvement included “2 points of prior-year reserve releases”; “Auto claim reserve releases totaled $1.5 billion year-to-date,” with about half of bodily-injury changes relating to 2023 and 2024.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario assumed “~0.5 pt favorable PYD”; the preview said a repeat near Q1’s $840M of favorable auto releases would be “low-quality EPS” and that the well was drying up.

surprises.description: Total revenue exceeded the preview’s main consensus estimate, growing 11.8% rather than the anticipated 5.7% year-over-year. It also came in above the preview’s modeled base of about $17.7 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues grew 11.8% year-over-year to $18.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus was “$17.73B (+5.7% YoY)” and the base scenario estimated revenue of “~$17.7B.”

surprises.description: Net investment income was above the preview’s estimated range, reaching $1.0 billion versus an estimate of $0.90–$0.95 billion. The reported 33.8% increase was also a pronounced tailwind to earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net investment income surged 33.8% to $1 billion,” reflecting duration lengthening and the prior increase in public-equity holdings.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “NII ~$0.90–0.95B” and described NII as a “quiet tailwind.”

surprises.description: Despite the strong results, management warned that auto margins are running well below the mid-90s target combined ratio and could normalize. Flat pricing and elevated bodily-injury severity remain concerns, making the commentary more cautionary than the preview’s base-case expectation of no change in tone.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said auto margins are “running well below the mid-90s target combined ratio” (year-to-date underlying 88.5%), noted “flat pricing and the potential for normalization,” and flagged elevated bodily-injury severity.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “reiteration of the Q1 ‘Rubik’s Cube’ framing … with no change in tone”; the preview described Q1 as expressing confidence in beating industry-average combined ratios.

surprises.description: Shareholder returns included $1 billion of buybacks in the quarter, and $9.5 billion of deployable holding-company capital was available. The preview highlighted buyback pace as a key watch item and identified acceleration as a potential offset to decelerating EPS, but did not specify an expected quarterly amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned $1.3 billion to shareholders in the quarter including $1 billion of buybacks,” with “$2.6 billion remaining under the $4 billion authorization” and “$9.5 billion of deployable holding-company capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Buyback pace” was a catalyst to watch and called acceleration “the most credible offset to decelerating EPS.”

in_line: Catastrophe losses had already been disclosed before the release at $1.72 billion pre-tax; the call’s statement that lower catastrophe losses improved the combined ratio by 2.4 points does not indicate a new departure from that disclosed setup.
Net rate changes across 36 locations had zero impact, consistent with the preview’s expectation of roughly neutral pricing.

Auto policies in force grew 2.8%, a modest acceleration from Q1’s 2.6% and broadly consistent with the preview’s focus on growth approaching 3%; it did not clearly exceed the preview’s bull-case threshold.

surprises.description: BGSF reported Q2 revenue of $22.3 million, well below the preview’s $24.0–$24.5 million base-case range and the $24.5 million consensus figure. Revenue fell 5.1% year over year instead of growing as the preview’s estimates implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue was $22.3 million, down 5.1% year-over-year, driven by lower billed hours as property owners curbed discretionary temporary staffing spending.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ≥$24.5M and the FY guide reaffirmed”; the base case expected “$24.0–24.5M (+2–4%).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA remained loss-making at $298,000, rather than reaching the positive $300,000–$600,000 range expected in the preview’s base case. This was the key operating-leverage test the preview identified for the seasonal up-quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $298,000 in Q2, narrowing from the $1.2 million loss a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Adj. EBITDA” of “+$0.3–0.6M” and said Q2 “should put Q2 around breakeven-to-modestly-positive.”

surprises.description: Management’s full-year revenue outlook was for results to remain relatively consistent with 2025, softer than the preview’s expectation of low- to mid-single-digit growth. That outlook represents a meaningful reduction from the growth trajectory the preview said would be needed to support its guidance assumptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects full-year 2026 revenue to remain relatively consistent with 2025 levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance on the table: FY26 revenue growth of low- to mid-single-digits vs. 2025 (≈$96–98M).”

surprises.description: The PropTech contribution was pushed out relative to the preview’s expectation: the preview put its 1%–2% revenue contribution in FY26, while management now expects that contribution in 2027 after a six-month ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The PropTech offering, following a six-month ramp, is expected to contribute approximately 1% to 2% of revenue in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “PropTech/Yardi consulting at 1–2% of FY26 revenue.”

surprises.description: GAAP continuing-operations EPS was a loss of $0.08, worse than the preview’s near-zero expectation, although adjusted EPS was a loss of just $0.02 and therefore closer to that expectation. The reported GAAP result was an improvement from the prior year, but the comparison here is to the near-zero outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $0.08 per diluted share” and “adjusted EPS loss of $0.02.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 EPS consensus of “~$0.00” and said its base case had “GAAP EPS” of “$(0.02) to +$0.01.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 35.5%, below the preview’s 35.8%–36.0% base-case range, though management’s full-year outlook remained in the expected 36%-range. The quarterly shortfall was modest rather than a major break from the preview’s stated downside threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 35.5% versus 35.8% a year ago, with management guiding to a full-year gross margin in the 36% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “35.8–36.0%”; it said sub-35.5% would signal price/mix pressure.

surprises.description: Management said staffing requests were up year over year but were translating into fewer billed hours. That points to weaker conversion of requests into billable work than the preview’s generally flat-to-slightly-up demand framing, even as it helps explain the revenue miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management noted “year-over-year staffing request volumes are up but translating into fewer billed hours.”

in_line: The full-year gross-margin outlook remained in the 36% range, as the preview expected.
The full benefit of cost-reduction initiatives was expected to begin in Q3; management likewise said those initiatives’ full benefit begins in Q3.
Ongoing G&A of roughly $12 million, including about $2 million in public-company costs, matched the preview’s stated run-rate expectation.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.47, above the preview’s published consensus of about $0.41. It landed within the preview’s $0.44–$0.48 base-case range and its $0.45–$0.50 buy-side whisper, so the beat was against consensus rather than against the preview’s higher scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 47% to $0.47.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS **$0.4057**”; the preview also gave a “Base” scenario of “**$0.44–0.48**” and said “The buy-side whisper is likely **$0.45–0.50**.”

surprises.description: Core pawn same-store gross profit grew 13%, below the preview’s thesis-intact bogey of more than 18% and its roughly 20% whisper. That is a shortfall on a metric the preview flagged as the key test of whether growth extended beyond scrap, despite 24% core pawn revenue growth and 28% core pawn gross profit growth overall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core pawn revenues grew 24% and core pawn gross profit rose 28%, with same-store core pawn gross profit up 13%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SS core pawn GP >+18% = thesis intact”; the preview also cited “~+20% whisper.”

surprises.description: PLO reached a record $382 million, but came in just below the preview’s expected $385–$395 million base range and its roughly $390 million catalyst level. The record and 31% growth were strong, but the total was slightly short of the expected seasonal build.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total PLO reached a record $382 million, up 31%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$385–395M base”; the catalyst checklist also cited “PLO vs. ~$390M.”

surprises.description: Scrap gross margin was 26%, a little above the preview’s 20–25% base expectation. However, management expects further normalization toward 15–20% if gold does not rise, below the preview’s roughly 22% historical-margin assumption; the current result was somewhat better than expected, while the forward outlook was weaker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scrap gross margin fell to 26% from 38% in the prior quarter,” and management expects “continued normalization toward historical levels of 15%-20% if gold prices don't rise further.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected scrap to “normalize to ~22–25% GM”; its scrap-margin bogey called “20–25% = in line.”

surprises.description: U.S. same-store store expenses rose only 6%, better than the preview’s threshold of less than 11% for expense discipline. The preview had highlighted store-expense growth and integration costs as an area to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Pawn segment EBITDA improved 23% to $64.5 million with EBITDA margin up 200 basis points to 26%, as store expenses rose only 6% on a same-store basis versus faster revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s store-expense bogey was “SS store expense <+11% = discipline holding” and noted a “sequential increase through the year” from management.

surprises.description: Latin America delivered strong segment growth despite the preview’s warning that Mexico’s minimum-wage increase was a persistent regional cost drag: PLO grew 33% in constant currency, segment EBITDA rose 40%, and merchandise margin expanded 490 basis points. The preview did not set a specific LatAm forecast, so the strength is a positive contrast to the cost concern rather than a quantified beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Latin America PLO grew 33% in constant currency to $93.7 million, with segment EBITDA up 40% to $25.4 million and merchandise margin expanding 490 basis points to 36%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “Mexico minimum wage +13%” as “a persistent LatAm drag.”

in_line: U.S. average loan size rose 16% to $240, matching the preview’s stated figure; U.S. jewelry mix was 69%, also matching its expectation.
Latin America jewelry mix was 49%, close to the preview’s expected 48%.
The acquisition of 33 Guatemala stores was broadly in line with the preview’s estimate of about 32 acquired stores.

The $4 million share repurchase did not indicate an accelerated pace versus the preview’s note that only $4 million had been repurchased in H1; the preview had raised acceleration as a possibility, not an expectation.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.65 and adjusted net earnings were $85 million, below the preview’s $0.78 and roughly $103 million expectations. Earnings also fell from both Q1 and Q2 2025 rather than remaining roughly flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net earnings were $85 million or $0.65 per share in Q2 2026,” down $25 million from Q1 and $18 million from Q2 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS” consensus: “$0.78”; “Adj. net earnings: ~$103M (derived)” and implied YoY “~flat.”

surprises.description: Alternative returns weakened further instead of recovering toward the preview’s base-case range: the annualized return was 5.9%, and management expects only roughly 7%–8% in Q3. Management described a blended return around 10% based on the portfolio’s characteristics, below the preview’s 12%–14% long-term target range, though the facts do not say the formal target was reset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alternative investment income fell to $49 million ($0.38 per share) as the annualized alts return dropped to 5.9% from 8.3% in Q1, well below the 12% long-term expected return.” Management expects “roughly 7%-8%” in Q3 and cited a “blended ~10% return.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed alts “recover to 9–10.5%”; it said a return to “~11–12% is worth roughly +$0.15–0.25/share vs. Q1” and identified 12%–14% as the long-term target.

surprises.description: Gross sales and AUM came in below the preview’s trajectory: gross sales were $2.7 billion versus a $3.5–4.0 billion base case, and AUM before reinsurance was $74.7 billion rather than the expected $76–77 billion. The core retail component was comparatively resilient, but did not offset the lower total sales figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross sales were $2.7 billion ($2 billion core, $700 million opportunistic)” and AUM before reinsurance was “$74.7 billion” at June 30.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “gross sales $3.5–4.0B” and “AUM b/r $76–77B.”

surprises.description: Fixed-income yield improved more than the preview’s flat-to-stable setup suggested, rising 14 basis points from Q1 to 4.91%. The preview had described Q1 yield as 4.77% and flagged spread compression as the key forward-looking concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fixed income yield rose to 4.91%, up 14 basis points from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 fixed-income yield “held at 4.77% with core spreads defended” and identified spread compression on new business as the key forward-looking tell.

surprises.description: Peak Altitude discussion advanced beyond a process simply remaining ongoing: management is exploring strategic alternatives and is targeting a sale of about 51% to a partner. That gives a more concrete partial-stake structure, though no completed transaction, valuation, or timing was reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: Peak Altitude is “being explored for strategic alternatives, targeting sale of ~51% to a partner to unlock value the market currently ascribes little to.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the Peak process to be “ongoing”; it said a concrete step such as a “partial stake sale” would be a catalyst.

surprises.description: Book value per share excluding AOCI was slightly below the preview’s stated level, at $45.93 versus $46.51. The shortfall was small, despite management also noting the longer-term increase since the 2020 acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Book value per share excluding AOCI rose to $45.93.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited BVPS ex-AOCI of “$46.51.”

surprises.description: The first-half buyback was larger than the preview’s stated Q1 pace, but management framed repurchases as opportunistic rather than a primary capital use. The company had repurchased $120 million in the first half and said only $12–15 million remained under authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased 4.5 million shares for $120 million at an average price of $26.44 in the first half,” with “only $12-15 million remaining under authorization,” and buybacks described as “opportunistic rather than a primary use of capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted a “$100M buyback authorized March 2026” and “~$29M used in Q1.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a small potential capital impact from new NAIC CLO charges: an estimated roughly 10-point RBC reduction before management action, while maintaining the ratio above the 400% target. This capital-charge update was not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New NAIC CLO capital charges are estimated to reduce RBC by only about 10 points before management action,” with the company “maintaining its RBC ratio above the 400% target.”

in_line: Core retail indexed annuity and life sales were $1.8 billion, broadly in line with the preview’s Q1 core-sales reference of $1.9–2.0 billion; management described the quarter as one of the strongest on record despite industry FIA contraction.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $102.9 million, far below the $108.9–109.1 million consensus and also below the preview’s $106.5 million base case. Revenue grew only 0.8%, rather than the 6.6–6.8% consensus growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose only 0.8% to $102.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $108.9–109.1M”; the preview’s base case was “~$106.5M (+4.3%).”

surprises.description: Comparable funeral volume fell 3.5% in Q2, materially weaker than the preview’s roughly flat base case and its warning that anything worse than flat would undermine the recovery story. The decline continued through all six months, rather than showing the expected Q2 recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable funeral volume declined 3.5% in Q2 and 4.7% in the first six months,” with mortality rates “negative every month from January through June.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Volume roughly flat” in the base case; “Anything worse than flat comparable volume breaks the recovery story.”

surprises.description: Management cut full-year revenue guidance by about $5 million to $435–445 million, instead of reaffirming the preview’s $440–450 million range. It attributed the cut mainly to delayed acquisition timing and weaker first-half volume, directly challenging the expected H2 revenue ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance by about $5 million to $435-445 million, attributing the cut mainly to delayed acquisition timing and weaker first-half volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Reaffirm $440–450M unchanged”; the preview called for the market to assess whether management “defends the $440–450M FY range.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.78 missed the $0.82 consensus and the preview’s $0.81 base case. The miss was notable even though EPS increased from $0.74 a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 5.4% to $0.78 from $0.74.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $0.82”; the preview’s base case was “$0.81 adj. EPS.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue and volume shortfalls, Q2 EBITDA margin reached 32.3%, above the preview’s 31.0–31.5% estimate. Management also raised its full-year margin outlook to 31–31.5% and lowered the overhead range to 13.5–14%, indicating stronger profitability than the preview’s cited margin and overhead targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted consolidated EBITDA grew 3.1% to $33.3 million with margin expanding 70 basis points to 32.3%”; full-year margin was “raised to 31-31.5%,” while overhead guidance was lowered to “13.5-14% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was estimated at “~31.0–31.5%”; the preview cited an FY overhead target of “13.5–14.5%” and noted margin guidance sources of “30.5–31.5%.”

surprises.description: Funeral volume turned to strong low-single-digit growth in July after six straight months of decline, and management said this supported a much stronger second half. That is a more encouraging near-term volume signal than the preview’s roughly flat base-case assumption, although the full-year revenue outlook was cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Funeral volume returned to positive strong low-single-digit growth in July after six months of decline, supporting the company's expectation for a much stronger second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “Volume roughly flat”; its bull case assumed comparable volume “turns positive.”

surprises.description: Insurance-funded pre-need funeral contracts sold rose 21.1%, alongside 14% growth in financial revenue—an additional source of growth not identified in the preview’s discussion of funeral volume and cemetery pre-need production.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Insurance-funded pre-need funeral contracts sold rose 21.1% and financial revenue increased 14% to $9.3 million year-over-year.”

in_line: Bank leverage was 4.0 times, matching the preview’s cited 4.0x level and remaining within its 3.5–4.0x year-end target range.

surprises.description: Kinetik was expected to deliver roughly $230–240 million of Q2 adjusted EBITDA, with the preview’s buy-side bar around $245 million. It reported $281 million, well above both benchmarks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 was a record quarter with adjusted EBITDA of $281 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA vs. the $230–240M quarterly guide”; “effective buy-side bar as ~$245M EBITDA.”

surprises.description: The preview showed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $950 million–$1.05 billion as affirmed. Kinetik instead raised the range by $70 million at the midpoint, to $1.04–$1.1 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by $70 million (7%) at the midpoint to a new range of $1.04 billion to $1.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 Adj. EBITDA: $950–1,050M (guide, affirmed).”

surprises.description: The preview said the 2H outlook assumed Waha-related shut-ins would persist through December, while noting potential upside if curtailed volumes returned early. Kinetik said curtailments should fall from an estimated 250 MMcf/d to about 25 MMcf/d in 2H, with none assumed in Q4, and expects to exit 2026 near 2.2 Bcf/d of processed volumes—about 10% above its normalized current run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Processed natural gas volumes were flat year-over-year at 1.74 Bcf/d despite an estimated 250 MMcf/d of Waha price-related curtailments, which are expected to fall to about 25 MMcf/d for the second half of 2026 with none assumed in Q4”; “expects to exit 2026 approaching 2.2 Bcf/d… implying roughly 10% growth from the normalized ~1.96 Bcf/d current run rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management modeled ~220 MMcf/d of average full-year Waha price-related shut-ins… and… guided the 2H ramp assuming curtailments persist through December.”

surprises.description: The preview put FY26 capital spending at $450–510 million. Kinetik raised its 2026 capex outlook to about $560 million, citing Kings Landing II, optimization work, compression equipment, and pulled-forward customer development spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2026 capital expenditure guidance was raised to approximately $560 million,” driven by “Kings Landing II, optimization projects, compression equipment purchases, and pulled-forward customer development spending.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 capex (incl. maint.): $450–510M.”

surprises.description: Kings Landing II was expected to enter service in 2H 2028. Kinetik now expects completion by mid-2028, bringing the project forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Accelerated its completion to mid-2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Kings Landing II — 300 MMcf/d, ~$260M, in-service 2H 2028.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated that coverage could compress toward 1.25–1.3x at a $235 million EBITDA quarter. Instead, Q2 dividend coverage improved to about 1.5x, alongside $195 million of distributable cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Distributable cash flow of $195 million”; “Q2 dividend was $0.81 per share with coverage improving to approximately 1.5x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At a $235M EBITDA quarter, coverage compresses toward ~1.25–1.3x.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted 3.9x leverage and elevated capex as a balance-sheet concern, and said a deleveraging path would matter. Kinetik reported leverage of 3.8x and expects it to decline further by year-end despite the higher capital program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarter-end leverage was 3.8x with liquidity exceeding $1 billion, and management expects leverage to decline further by year-end even with the elevated capital program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Leverage at 3.9x against a rising capex program is the bear's balance-sheet hook; any deleveraging path commentary matters.”

surprises.description: The preview’s cadence arithmetic used about $265 million per quarter for the second half. Kinetik’s Q3 midpoint is consistent with that assumption, but its Q4 guide of $270–280 million is higher, indicating a stronger-than-modeled Q4 run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 EBITDA is guided to $260-270 million and Q4 to $270-280 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Simple arithmetic on management's own cadence ($251 actual + $235 Q2 + $265 × 2) = ~$1,016M.”

in_line: Pipeline Transportation’s decline was attributed primarily to the EPIC Crude divestiture, consistent with the preview’s warning that the segment comparison would be distorted by that divestiture.
The Q2 dividend remained $0.81 per share, matching the preview’s stated quarterly dividend of $0.81.
The system-wide processing capacity outlook above 2.7 Bcf/d was already anticipated in the preview; the reported surprise was the faster Kings Landing II completion timing.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.37, about twice the preview’s $0.185–$0.19 consensus estimate. Although EPS declined from a year earlier, it substantially exceeded the expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS fell to $0.37 from $0.54 a year earlier,” reflecting lower profitability and a more normalized effective tax rate.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS: $0.185–0.19.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $1.04 billion, above the preview’s $1.009 billion consensus and a much smaller year-over-year decline than the company’s guided range implied. The decline improved 500 basis points from Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $1.04 billion, down 5.8% year-over-year but well ahead of guidance of down 7% to 9%, with the year-over-year decline improving 500 basis points versus Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $1,009.3M”; company guidance was “−7% to −9%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 3%, above the preview’s expected 2.5%–2.7% range and the company’s 2.5% floor. The year-over-year decline was also narrower than the preview’s estimated 80 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin returned to 3% ($31.1 million), exceeding guidance of at least 2.5% and improving 150 basis points sequentially, though still down 40 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin: ~2.6% (derived)” and “a print of 2.5–2.7% is table stakes; ≥2.9% is a genuine beat.”

surprises.description: ETM underlying revenue grew 3.1% year over year, sharply outperforming the preview’s estimate of an approximately 11% decline. Talent Solutions also grew about 6%, with both RPO and MSP specialties posting double-digit growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ETM underlying revenue grew 3.1% year-over-year while Talent Solutions grew about 6% with both RPO and MSP specialties posting double-digit growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s segment build estimated ETM revenue at “~$463M” and “−11%,” citing large commercial-account losses.

surprises.description: SET’s year-over-year revenue decline was 3%, much better than the preview’s estimated 9% decline, and revenue grew sequentially for the first time in two years. That is a stronger segment inflection than the preview’s model anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SET revenue grew sequentially for the first time in two years, marking a claimed inflection point, though underlying revenue still declined 3% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated SET revenue at “~$289M” and “−9%,” and noted Q1 was “−11.6%.”

surprises.description: Management raised its full-year expectations and provided a stronger, more specific Q4 frame: mid- to upper-single-digit revenue growth and about 4% adjusted EBITDA margin. The 53rd week adds roughly four points to Q4 revenue while weighing on margin, so the headline growth includes a calendar boost and the margin outlook has that qualification.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year expectations, now projecting a low-to-mid single-digit revenue decline and 10 to 20 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin improvement”; Q4 guidance calls for “mid- to upper-single-digit revenue growth and roughly 200 basis points of margin expansion to about 4%,” with a 53rd week that “adds ~4 points to revenue while negatively impacting adjusted EBITDA margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market was watching for a “second-half 2026 inflection to organic revenue growth and EBITDA margin expansion” and whether “modest year-over-year revenue growth and measurable adjusted EBITDA margin expansion in the second half” would hold.

surprises.description: Education revenue declined 4.4%, worse than the preview’s estimate of a 2% decline. That was a weaker segment result than expected despite signs of customer retention and future therapy demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Education revenue declined 4.4% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Education revenue at “~$260M” and “−2%.”

surprises.description: SET’s outcome-based solutions reached 40% of segment revenue, up from roughly one-third a year earlier. The preview did not flag this shift toward milestone- and SLA-based work.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SET outcome-based solutions rose to 40% of SET's total revenue, up from roughly one-third a year ago, reflecting an intentional shift toward higher-margin milestone and SLA-based work.”

surprises.description: Education reported a 100% renewal rate in the K-12 staffing sales cycle and positioned therapy services for record provider starts in September. These retention and pipeline details were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The K-12 staffing sales cycle delivered a 100% renewal rate, with therapy services (currently ~8% of the segment mix) positioned for record September provider starts.”

in_line: Federal and large-customer headwinds fully anniversarying in Q4 was consistent with the preview’s expectation that discrete headwinds would roll off during the second half.
Free cash flow turning positive and debt declining were directionally consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q2 cash flow should seasonally reverse Q1’s negative free cash flow.
The quarterly dividend remained at $0.075, matching the preview’s note that the dividend had been maintained.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $65.5 million, well above the preview’s $62.5–$63.5 million company guide and its $63.3–$63.5 million buy-side whisper. The reported 6.4% growth also exceeded the preview’s implied growth of at most 2.4%; management said underlying organic growth was mid-single digits excluding FX and the Martino acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 6.4% year-over-year to $65.5 million, with a $700,000 positive FX impact”; excluding FX and the Martino acquisition, “underlying organic growth was mid-single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $62.86M” consensus and “$62.5M–$63.5M” company guidance; the preview’s buy-side whisper was “$63.3–63.5M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the double-digit adjusted EBITDA growth streak to end because Q2 needed $9.13 million to grow 10% year over year, above the top of the company’s guide. Instead, EBITDA grew 12.9% to $9.4 million, extending the streak to seven quarters, while the 14.3% margin exceeded the preview’s 13.5% level to watch and the guide’s 14.2% upper-end margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 12.9% to $9.4 million—the seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA growth—while adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 80 basis points to 14.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the streak “almost certainly ends this quarter,” that “To print +10% YoY adj. EBITDA, ISG needs $9.13M — above the top end of its own guidance,” and flagged “Adj. EBITDA ≥$8.5M and margin ≥13.5%.”

surprises.description: AI-related revenue reached $26 million, surpassing the preview’s bull-case threshold of more than $22 million. Its 64% growth also cleared the preview’s warning level of below 50%, although it was slower than the roughly 75% growth cited for Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-related revenue surged 64% to $26 million in Q2” and represented “37% of firm-wide revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case called for “AI revenue >$22M” and said “a sub-50% growth rate would be read badly.”

surprises.description: Americas revenue grew 6.7%, stronger than the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly flat to 1% growth and a clear return to growth after the prior-quarter decline. This exceeded management’s stated commitment to deliver solid year-over-year growth in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Americas revenue grew 6.7% to $42.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Americas ~flat to +1%,” and highlighted management’s guidance to “solid year-over-year growth in Q2.”

surprises.description: The preview pointed to Q2 as a historically strong operating-cash-flow quarter, citing $12.0 million in Q2 2025. Actual Q2 operating cash flow was $5.2 million, substantially below that historical comparison, even though it improved from cash usage in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Generated $5.2 million in operating cash flow (versus a $700,000 usage in Q1).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 and Q3 are historically strong cash quarters ($12.0M and $11.1M from operations in 2025).”

surprises.description: Recurring revenue grew only 7%, below the preview’s roughly 8% growth threshold for maintaining the thesis, and its 45%–47% share did not reach the 50% milestone the preview identified as a key watchpoint. It did set a record at $30 million, and management still targets a mix above 50% within the next couple of years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue hit a record $30 million (up 7%), now roughly 45%-47% of total revenue, with management targeting over 50% within the next couple of years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said recurring revenue was “~47% of revenue in Q1'26, +9% YoY,” identified “Crossing 50%” as a key watchpoint, and said “deceleration below ~8% undercuts the thesis.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS improved to $0.10, above the preview’s expected range of $0.08–$0.09. The preview cautioned that EPS estimates were dispersed and their GAAP-versus-adjusted basis was uncertain, so the gap was positive but relatively limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS improved to $0.10 from $0.08 a year earlier.”

surprises.description: The Board authorized a new $30 million repurchase program, the company’s largest, and management expects buybacks to accelerate in the second half. The preview noted the existing Q1 buyback and aggressive-buyback language, but did not anticipate a new authorization of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a new $30 million share repurchase authorization—the largest in company history—with management guiding investors to expect accelerated buybacks in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$2.1M repurchased in Q1'26” and that the CFO framed it as “aggressively buying back shares.”

surprises.description: Gross debt-to-EBITDA ended at 1.7x, better than the 1.8x level the preview cited as the Q1 baseline. This is a modestly stronger leverage position than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered gross debt-to-EBITDA to 1.7x from 1.9x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited gross debt/EBITDA of “1.8x” at Q1.

surprises.description: Management said M&A valuations had become more “frothy” than a year earlier, an added caution about acquisition pricing that the preview did not flag. The comments indicate a less favorable valuation environment, but do not establish that the company will stop pursuing acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management noted “M&A valuations are becoming more ‘frothy’ than a year ago.”

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $63.5–$64.5 million was in line with the preview’s expected range of roughly $63.5–$64.5 million; Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $8.5–$9.5 million was also broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of about $8.9–$9.1 million per quarter for H2.

Asia Pacific revenue rose about 24% sequentially, from $4.1 million in Q1 to $5.1 million in Q2, close to the preview’s expectation of roughly 20% sequential growth, though it remained down 6.7% year over year.
Management’s comment that client decision-making remained measured was consistent with the preview’s warning to watch for deferred decisions and elongated sales cycles.

surprises.description: Murphy raised its 2026 CapEx midpoint to $1.55 billion from $1.25 billion, well above the preview’s $1.2–1.3 billion full-year range. Nearly all of the increase is for organic growth, including Bubale and Eagle Ford spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Murphy raised its 2026 capital expenditure midpoint from $1.25 billion to $1.55 billion, with nearly all of the ~$300 million increase supporting organic growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 capex (co. guide) | $1.2–1.3B” and the base case expected “FY guide reaffirmed but not raised.”

surprises.description: The Hai Su Vang-4X well was dry and Murphy revised the resource estimate downward, contrary to the preview’s expectation that appraisal could deliver a resource upgrade. The field remains a material opportunity, but management said results may trend toward the lower end of the unchanged 30,000–50,000 boe/d Vietnam peak-production outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Hai Su Vang-4X well in Vietnam was a dry hole, prompting a downward resource revision, though the field still represents a material 200-300 million barrel oil equivalent opportunity”; “Vietnam's peak production outlook remains unchanged at 30,000-50,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, though management signaled results may trend toward the lower end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hai Su Vang appraisal: recoverable resource already expanded to >430 MMBOE”; “A resource upgrade here is the main non-macro upside catalyst.”

surprises.description: Management indicated that 2027 CapEx will likely exceed the prior $1.2–1.3 billion range and could rise further depending on Bubale appraisal results. The preview discussed 2026 spending but did not flag a higher 2027 spending outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2027 CapEx will likely exceed the prior $1.2-1.3 billion range and could go higher depending on Bubale appraisal results.”

surprises.description: Management warned that free cash flow could be negative in some periods before Hai Su Vang first oil, a more explicit downside to cash generation than the preview’s general warning to listen for cautious FCF framing at a roughly $70 strip.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow could turn negative in some periods before Hai Su Vang first oil.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear case cited “cautious FCF framing at $70 strip,” but did not anticipate periods of negative free cash flow.

surprises.description: Bubale encountered oil in both the Turonian and Cenomanian reservoirs after the first two of three exploration wells were noncommercial, providing an unexpected positive exploration result amid the preview’s concern about Côte d'Ivoire dry-hole risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Bubale discovery in Côte d'Ivoire encountered oil in both the Turonian and Cenomanian reservoirs after the first two of three exploration wells were noncommercial.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any new dry-hole write-offs” and described the Côte d'Ivoire exploration program as a key focus; it did not anticipate a Bubale discovery.

surprises.description: Second-quarter production reached 169,000 boe/d, above the preview’s base-case expectation of about 165,000 boe/d and at the top of the company’s 161,000–169,000 boe/d guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second quarter production averaged 169,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, above the midpoint of guidance, led by Tupper Montney and Eagle Ford outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “In-line volumes ~165 MBOEPD.”

surprises.description: Lac Da Vang’s expected ramp appears slower than the preview’s timeline: net production is now expected at 5,000–9,000 bpd by the end of 2027 and 10,000–15,000 bpd in 2028–2029, rather than reaching its 10,000–15,000 bpd peak in late 2027/2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lac Da Vang net production expected to reach 5,000-9,000 bpd by end of 2027 and ramp to 10,000-15,000 bpd by 2028-2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Lac Da Vang was “ramping to a net 10–15 MBOEPD peak in late 2027/2028.”

in_line: Chinook #8 and Lac Da Vang remain on track for fourth-quarter first oil, consistent with the preview’s Q4 2026 first-oil expectation for both projects.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $3.86, far above the preview’s roughly $2.95 consensus and $3.05 estimate; the reported 44% year-over-year growth was also well ahead of the preview’s expected 20.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted diluted EPS rose 44% year-over-year to $3.86.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $2.95 (range $2.90–2.98)” and “My estimate … EPS $3.05”; consensus growth was “+20.4%.”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $2.4 billion, materially above the preview’s $2.21–$2.22 billion consensus and $2.24 billion estimate. Growth of 15% in USD also exceeded the preview’s expected 3.8%–5.6% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue reached $2.4 billion, up 15% in USD (14% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales $2.21–2.22B”; “My estimate … Rev $2.24B”; expected growth was “+3.8% to +5.6%.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY2026 guidance to $12.20–$12.70 in adjusted EPS and 8%–10% gross profit growth. That is a stronger outlook than the preview’s anticipated raise to roughly $11.50–$12.00 EPS and its description of the existing gross profit outlook as low-single-digit growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting gross profit growth of 8% to 10% and adjusted diluted EPS of $12.20 to $12.70.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market bar was “~$11.50,” described a possible raise “to $11.75–12.00,” and stated the existing guide was for “GP growth low-single-digit.”

surprises.description: Total gross profit grew 18%, well above the preview’s roughly 6% consensus growth estimate and $470–$477 million estimate. The preview had also highlighted the gap between Q1’s 14% gross profit growth and the low-single-digit full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total gross profit grew 18%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross profit ~$470M (est.)” versus $442.3 million a year earlier, with “+6%” expected growth; the preview also noted FY guidance of “low single digits.”

surprises.description: Cloud gross profit grew 39%, above the preview’s 25% watch threshold and continuing to accelerate despite the preview’s warning that Q2 was the last easy comparison before partner-program headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cloud gross profit grew 39% to $171 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “Cloud GP growth ≥25%” and called Q2 “the last easy comp before partner-program headwinds.”

surprises.description: Core services gross profit rose 21%, above the preview’s high-single-digit guide expectation. The reported growth was aided by acquisition contributions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core services gross profit rose 21% to $95 million, both aided by acquisition contributions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Insight Core services GP … guide is high-single-digit.”

surprises.description: Hardware gross profit rose 10% rather than staying flat as the preview’s guide discussion anticipated, even though hardware gross margin fell 110 basis points on pricing and client mix. This was a better result in gross profit dollars, with the margin pressure still evident.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hardware gross margin declined 110 basis points due to pricing and client mix, even though hardware gross profit rose 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management cited “flat hardware GP on component costs” and identified “Hardware gross profit dollars, not revenue” as a key watch item.

surprises.description: Total gross margin was 21.7%, up 60 basis points, rather than the roughly 21.3% estimate and expected compression the preview described. The preview specifically warned that a result below 21% would confirm hardware mix pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America grew 16% and EMEA grew 13%, lifting total gross margin 60 bps to 21.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Gross margin ~21.3%” and said Q1’s 21.7% versus a 21.5% FY guide implied compression; it flagged “Sub-21%” as a concern.

surprises.description: APAC gross profit surged 67% on cybersecurity acquisition contributions, a regional result the preview did not specifically anticipate or forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC gross profit surged 67% from cybersecurity acquisition contributions.”

in_line: Management’s caution that Q4 would be the year’s lowest EPS-growth quarter fits the preview’s warning that the second half would face tougher comparisons and EPS declines, with cloud partner-program changes and memory uncertainty among the risks.

Pausing M&A and prioritizing the remaining share repurchase authorization was consistent with the preview’s expectation that M&A would remain paused in 2026 and that buybacks would use more than 90% of projected free cash flow.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 29% and its margin expanded 90 basis points; this broadly matched the preview’s expectation of a solid beat supported by SG&A leverage.

surprises.description: Q2 sales reached $128.9 million, well above the preview’s $118–120 million whisper range and $116.1 million consensus. The gap was about 7–11% versus those expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 19% year-over-year to $128.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat the whisper as revenue ~$118–120M”; consensus net sales was “$116.1M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $17.9 million with a 13.9% margin, beating the preview’s roughly $14.5–15.0 million base estimate and its 12.5% base-case margin. EBITDA was near the preview’s bull-case range, while margin was above the 13% level flagged as important.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA increased 36% to $17.9 million with margins expanding 170 basis points to 13.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est.): ~$14.5–15.0M”; base case “~12.5%”; the preview also flagged “Adj. EBITDA margin ≥13%.”

surprises.description: The refinancing produced a quantified annual pick-interest reduction of about $13 million, with the pick rate falling from 14.5% to 10%. The preview viewed a refinancing as possible but did not forecast these terms or savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: The refinancing “cut[] the pick rate from 14.5% to 10% and reduc[es] annual pick interest by approximately $13 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A refinancing announcement on or near this call is live”; the preview said a concrete refi would remove a balance-sheet overhang.

surprises.description: The preferred reduction required another 5.5 million shares, taking shares outstanding to 82.6 million versus the preview’s 77.1 million post-PIPE count and leaving only 7.4 million of the 90 million authorized shares unused. That is additional dilution and much less share-issuance capacity than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The refinancing swapped 5.5 million shares for the preferred reduction, bringing shares outstanding to 82.6 million out of 90 million authorized, exhausting available common stock.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Shares o/s: 77.1M (post-PIPE)” and described the PIPE’s “24.5M shares” as “+46% dilution.”

surprises.description: The data-center/electric-grid business was already $80 million on a trailing-12-month basis and management raised the near-term target to $120 million, above the preview’s cited $70-million-plus current level and $100 million goal. The machine-installation and November sales milestones also put more detail around the ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: The business is “currently $80 million on a trailing-12-month basis with a near-term target of $120 million”; “50 machines” are being installed and monthly sales are expected to exceed $1 million starting in November.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said combined Electric Grid + Data Center was “>$70M LTM” with “a stated goal of $100M,” and that final machine installs were expected in November.

surprises.description: The reported outlook facts provide a $120 million near-term target but no specific 2027 data-center or liquid-cooling sales figure. That falls short of the preview’s stated expectation for a hard 2027 number, which it identified as a key item investors were looking for.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call facts give a “near-term target of $120 million” and a prospecting pipeline “approaching $100 million,” but no 2027 sales figure.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A hard dollar number for 2027 is what the buy side is paying for”; the preview called the “absence of a number” the “biggest single disappointment risk.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a multi-year defense weapons agreement worth $12–15 million from one customer, alongside medical, data-center, and defense wins that are expected to ramp entirely in the second half. The preview discussed the NVIDIA award but did not identify this defense contract or its value.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recently announced wins in medical, data center, and defense will not impact first-half results and ramp up entirely in the second half, including a multi-year defense weapons agreement worth $12-15 million from one customer.”

surprises.description: The long-term adjusted EBITDA margin target rose to 14–16%, above the 13% multi-year target cited in the preview. Management also described a 25% minimum gross-margin and IRR hurdle for new capital investments.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “raised its long-term adjusted EBITDA margin target to 14-16% with a 25% floor on both gross margin and IRR for new capital investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “The multi-year target is 13%.”

surprises.description: Automotive was about 40% of sales, with management targeting one-third as growth markets expand rather than because automotive is shrinking. That offers a more concrete diversification path than the preview’s discussion of auto softness and the company’s broader transformation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Automotive has declined to about 40% of company sales, with a target of one-third as growth markets expand rather than automotive shrinking.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the transformation toward “electric grid / AI data center / defense / medical” components and flagged “China auto soft, global auto ~-2% for the year.”

in_line: The full-year sales and adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised, as the preview expected a guidance update and treated a raise as the base case; the new ranges are $460–480 million in sales and $55–65 million in adjusted EBITDA.
The new-business-wins target rose to $80–100 million from the prior $80–90 million range, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the wins guide could be raised.
Power Solutions sales exceeded the preview’s bull-case watch level of $60 million, reaching $62.3 million.
The refinancing was completed, consistent with the preview’s view that an announcement was possible; its specific interest savings and the extra share issuance are captured above.

surprises.description: The preview put diluted EPS at about $1.14, but StoneX reported $1.00. Net operating revenues of $719.7 million also came in above the preview’s $650–700 million range, so the revenue beat did not translate into the expected earnings; net income was down 27% from Q2 versus an implied sequential decline of about 17%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net operating revenues rose 47% year-over-year to $719.7 million,” while “net income” was $127.9 million and “diluted EPS climbed” to $1.00; net income “fell 27% versus the record immediately preceding second quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net operating revenues (est.): ~$650–700M”; “Diluted EPS: ~$1.14”; Q2 diluted EPS was $1.380, implying a roughly 17% sequential decline to consensus.

surprises.description: The preview’s implied quarterly ROE was about 21%, but reported ROE was 18.4%. It remained above StoneX’s 15% target, though tangible ROE of 25% was also below the preview’s bull-case reference to Q2’s 37%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Return on equity was 18.4% for the quarter (25% return on tangible equity), well above the company's 15% target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Implied ROE (ann.) ~21%” and said the bull case would signal tangible-book ROE “near Q2's 37%.”

surprises.description: FX/CFD and Self-Directed Retail were a pronounced weak spot, with no specific deterioration forecast in the preview. FX/CFD revenues fell 19% year over year and Self-Directed Retail segment income fell 36%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FX/CFD was the sole weak area with revenues down 19% year-over-year and Self-Directed Retail segment income falling 36%,” as ADV dropped 27%.

surprises.description: The Benchmark Company delivered its best quarter to date, an additional Institutional-segment contribution the preview did not identify as an expected source of results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Benchmark Company delivered its best quarter to date, contributing $29.5 million in net operating revenues to the Institutional segment.”

surprises.description: Payments reached record ADV and grew net operating revenues, though revenue growth lagged volume growth as the mix shift reduced rate capture. The preview discussed mix and rate-capture risks generally, but did not flag this payments result specifically.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payments hit record ADV of $96 million (up 20%) with net operating revenues up 12%, though rate per million declined 7% due to the shift toward high-volume, low-value bank flows on the X-Pay platform.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “Mix shift toward lower-capture listed business can offset volume strength.”

surprises.description: R.J. O’Brien’s quarterly revenue included a $9.8 million unrealized negative mark-to-market, a specific earnings drag the preview did not forecast for Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The R.J. O'Brien acquisition contributed $78.8 million in net operating revenues for the quarter (net of a $9.8 million unrealized negative mark-to-market).”

in_line: The preview expected orderly sequential moderation after Q2’s record quarter. Physical contract operating revenues did decline 39% sequentially, despite rising 106% year over year.

R.J. O’Brien integration remained on track for substantial completion later in FY26, consistent with the preview’s expectation of completion by fiscal year-end. Its synergy path—roughly $37–38 million annualized exiting Q3, mid-$40 million by fiscal year-end, and $50 million by the end of Q1 FY27—was broadly consistent with the preview’s ~$45 million FY26 target and $50 million total target.
The preview estimated annual net-income sensitivity of $47.6 million per 100 basis points; management’s updated estimate was $46.9 million, close to that expectation.

surprises.description: Q1 constant-currency revenue growth was 13%, well above the company's mid- to high-single-digit outlook and the preview's 7.6%–8.4% consensus growth range. This was a substantial top-line beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue grew 13% in constant currency, beating the company's mid- to high single-digit guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue” consensus growth of “+7.6% to +8.4%”; company guidance was “+mid-to-high-single-digit constant currency.”

surprises.description: Asia grew 25%, led by China sales growth above 40%, far stronger than the preview's high-single-digit Asia and mid-teens China expectations. RL also raised its Asia growth outlook, although China growth is still expected to moderate later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Asia led regional growth at 25%” and “China sales surging over 40%”; Asia guidance increased to “high single to low double digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “high-single-digit Asia growth for FY27” and “China mid-teens”; it said Asia growth above 20% would fund a raise.

surprises.description: Pricing and gross-margin performance exceeded the preview's bar: AUR rose 15% rather than the expected high-single-digit rate, and adjusted gross margin expanded 130 basis points, comfortably above the preview's roughly 50-basis-point concern threshold despite higher costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 73.6%,” with “15% AUR growth” more than offsetting incremental tariff, labor, and non-cotton material costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 AUR was guided “high-single-digit”; the preview said “Anything under ~+50bps expansion, with a promotional explanation” would challenge the premiumization thesis.

surprises.description: Global DTC comps rose 12%, ahead of the preview's HSD DTC-comps base case. That indicates stronger comparable-store and online demand than the working scenario assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global DTC comps up 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base scenario assumed “HSD DTC comps.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin expanded 150 basis points, above both the company's 80–120-basis-point Q1 outlook and the preview's 100–140-basis-point base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded 150 basis points to 18.5% while operating income grew 23%, both ahead of plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 operating-margin guidance was “+80–120bps cc”; the preview's base case expected “op margin +100–140bps.”

surprises.description: North America wholesale grew 22%, but the headline was partly driven by temporary shipment timing and resumed shipments to a luxury account. The planned acceleration of off-price and low-tier door reductions also qualifies the strength, rather than showing an unambiguously broad-based channel rebound.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America wholesale grew 22%, but roughly 15 points came from shipment timing shifts and resumed shipments to a luxury account,” and management plans “accelerated off-price and low-tier door reductions in the back half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described North America as guided to “low-single-digit FY27 growth,” noted “continued lower-tier door exits,” and flagged wholesale softness as a risk.

surprises.description: RL raised its full-year gross-margin outlook to roughly 50–70 basis points of expansion. That is stronger than the prior outlook for only modest expansion despite the preview's emphasis on H2 tariff exposure and the need to understand the margin bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin outlook was raised to roughly 50-70 bps of expansion, up from prior guidance of modest expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted that post-July tariff rates had changed and called for a “quantified dollar impact and mitigation”; it also identified the “H2 tariff bridge” as a key issue.

surprises.description: The call facts provided do not quantify the impact of the new post-July tariff regime or give a specific mitigation bridge. The reported margin expansion shows that Q1 costs were absorbed, but it does not resolve the H2 tariff question the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call facts say gross-margin growth was driven by AUR that “more than offset incremental tariff, labor, and non-cotton material costs,” but provide no quantified post-July tariff impact or mitigation plan.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “a quantified dollar impact and mitigation” under the post-July-24 tariff regime.

in_line: The FY27 constant-currency revenue-growth guide was raised to 5%–6%, reaching the preview's expected roughly 6% level.
FY27 operating-margin expansion guidance of 60–80 basis points matched the preview's expected 60–80-basis-point range.
The expectation that China growth would moderate to around mid-teens for the full year remained in place, despite the much stronger-than-expected Q1 result.

surprises.description: Revenue was $153.8 million, about 6% above the $145.09 million consensus, and organic constant-currency growth was 9% versus the preview’s 3% bogey. The favorable FX contribution was only about $1.3 million, so the beat was not primarily FX-driven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% year-over-year to $153.8 million, with 9% organic constant-currency growth and approximately $1.3 million of favorable FX tailwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $145.09M”; organic constant-currency growth bogey: “≥3% organic.”

surprises.description: Profitability recovered more strongly than the preview’s margin assumptions: operating margin reached 10.2% versus an estimated 8.3%, and adjusted EBITDA margin was 15.4% versus an estimated 14.1%. This substantially exceeded the preview’s expectation that margin recovery might still be partial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 170 basis points year-over-year to a record 34.9%”; “adjusted EBITDA rose 18% to $23.7 million (15.4% of revenue)”; “Operating income rose to $15.6 million from $11.7 million, lifting operating margin to 10.2% from 8.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (est.) ~$20.5M / ~14.1% margin”; “Op. margin (est.) ~8.3%”; the base case expected margin to “recover[] to ~13.5–14% adj. EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Orders and backlog came in far above the preview’s demand thresholds: orders reached a record $201.3 million and book-to-bill was 1.31x, while backlog rose to $298 million. The preview’s bogeys were orders of at least $150 million, book-to-bill of at least 1.05x, and backlog of at least $255 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orders surged 49% year-over-year and 27% sequentially to a record $201.3 million, producing a 1.31x book-to-bill ratio and $298 million backlog convertible within three to nine months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Orders ≥$150M”; “≥1.05x”; backlog “≥$255M.”

surprises.description: Data-center and infrastructure sales grew 60%, well beyond the preview’s expectation of continued double-digit growth. The quarter’s $16.3 million of sales also represented 10.6% of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center and infrastructure sales reached $16.3 million (10.6% of revenue) in Q2, up 60% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: For industrial detail and data-center power quality, the preview’s bogey was “Continued double-digit growth.”

surprises.description: Aerospace and defense returned to growth at 16%, much stronger than the preview’s expectation that a return to growth would be a meaningful positive surprise. The growth occurred despite the MTEM Booker program cancellation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aerospace/defense grew 16% (despite the MTEM Booker program cancellation).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A&D returning to growth on the drone-propulsion and replenishment orders management cited would be a meaningful positive surprise”; Q1 A&D was “−3%.”

surprises.description: Vehicle revenue declined 7%, reversing the preview’s reported Q1 vehicle growth of 7%. The call attributed the decline to weaker power sports demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The vehicle market declined 7% on weaker power sports demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s end-market trend from Q1 listed “Vehicle +7% (commercial auto).”

surprises.description: Management put a concrete figure and multi-year duration on STAND savings: $5–7 million in 2026, with a similar annual savings opportunity for two to three years. The preview said investors wanted a dollar figure for second-half savings and noted that management had not provided formal quantitative guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “STAND cost savings are guided at $5–7 million for 2026 with a two-to-three-year runway of similar annual savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the buy-side wants a dollar figure for 2H savings, not adjectives” and “Management does not give formal guidance.”

surprises.description: Leverage was better than the preview’s stated ceiling: it reached 1.63x, below the 1.75x threshold, as total debt fell by $7.1 million from year-end. The company also reported $42 million of cash and $162 million of unused revolver capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt fell $7.1 million since year-end 2025 to $173.3 million, improving leverage to 1.63x, with $42 million cash and $162 million of unused revolver capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s leverage bogey was “Net leverage ≤1.75x.”
