in_line: Full-year restructuring costs of $2–3 million matched the preview’s expectation of $2–3 million for FY2026.

surprises.description: Investors were watching for power growth capital to stay within the existing $280–340 million guidance; BKV instead raised it to $400–475 million, a $128 million increase at the midpoint, largely for long-lead equipment orders for Jack County.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BKV increased its 2026 strategic power capital guidance to $400-$475 million, a $128 million increase at the midpoint, driven largely by long lead time equipment orders for the Jack County project.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Power growth capital is guided to $280–340M for FY26”; the preview also flagged “another increase to power growth capital” as a bear catalyst.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case anticipated a mildly soft earnings print, but BKV reported record adjusted EBITDAX of $142 million and record adjusted net income of $51 million, more than twice the first-quarter result despite lower natural gas prices.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BKV posted record adjusted EBITDAX of $142 million and record adjusted net income of $51 million, more than twice its first quarter result despite lower natural gas prices.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case is a mildly soft adjusted EPS print that the market looks through.”

surprises.description: The preview expected full-year production guidance of 915–955 MMcfe/d; BKV raised the midpoint to 950 MMcfe/d, implying 3%–4% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 Upstream production guidance to a midpoint of 950 MMcfe/d, a 1.6% increase implying 3% to 4% year-over-year production growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Upstream production and cost control vs. 915–955 MMcfe/d”; FY2026 production guidance was “915–955 MMcfe/d.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag an appraisal result of this strength: the Upper Barnett Yarbrough 8H produced about twice the type curve over its first 30 days, lowering breakeven for nearly half the inventory and unlocking a 114-well inventory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Upper Barnett Yarbrough 8H appraisal well produced approximately 2x above type curve over its first 30 days, lowering breakeven for nearly half the inventory to $3.25/MMBtu and unlocking a 114-well inventory.”

surprises.description: The preview expected advanced completions to lift performance by about 20%; BKV reported performance 25% above type curve after 180 days, alongside all-in DC&F of $525 per lateral foot versus the preview’s $533-per-foot base.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BKV achieved the lowest cost per lateral foot of any major U.S. shale gas basin at $525 all-in DC&F, with advanced completions delivering well performance 25% above type curve after 180 days.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~20%-uplift advanced completions” and “a $533/ft base.”

surprises.description: The PPA timeline was unchanged, but discussions had advanced beyond the preview’s base-case framing: management said commercial discussions had narrowed to a select set of advanced counterparties, without reporting a signed agreement or naming one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed expectations to sign a Temple power purchase agreement within 2026 to early 2027, with commercial discussions narrowed to a select set of advanced counterparties.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated the PPA “still ‘on track for 2026–early 2027’”; it described the expected base framing as “repeat of the ‘deliberate, disciplined’ PPA framing.”

in_line: Temple power adjusted EBITDA was $36 million, within the preview’s expected Q2 range of $30–45 million.
The Temple PPA timeline remained within the preview’s expected 2026-to-early-2027 window.

The three operating carbon capture projects and the 1.5-million-ton-per-year 2028 target were consistent with the preview’s expectation that the Eagle Ford project would begin injection by the end of Q2 and that BKV was pursuing the 2028 target.

The combined Temple and Jack County developments’ potential 1.4 gigawatts of added dispatchable generation was consistent with the preview’s cited visibility of up to 1.4 gigawatts of incremental capacity.
The reported hedge coverage and price—66% of remaining 2026 gas production at $3.88/MMBtu—were close to the preview’s 67% at $3.86/MMBtu.

surprises.description: The preview’s pre-quarter YTD adjusted EPS of $3.35, combined with its Q3 consensus estimate of a $0.08 loss, implied roughly $3.27 YTD after Q3. UGI reported $3.17, about $0.10 below that implied level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date adjusted diluted EPS declined to $3.17 from $3.55,” largely due to the absence of prior-year investment tax credits and higher interest expense.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “YTD FY26 adjusted EPS is $3.35” and Q3 adjusted diluted EPS consensus was “$(0.08).”

surprises.description: Total reportable segment EBIT was $58 million, just below the preview’s $60–$75 million base-case range. AmeriGas was the main drag: its EBIT declined by $25 million, while weather-adjusted retail gallons fell 6% excluding the Hawaii divestiture, rather than being flat as the preview’s bull case assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 total reportable segment EBIT fell to $58 million from $72 million,” primarily from a “$25 million decline at AmeriGas”; retail gallons “declined only 6% on a weather-adjusted basis excluding the Hawaii divestiture.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case projected segment EBIT of “$60–75M”; its bull-case operating assumptions included “weather-adjusted gallons flat.”

surprises.description: UGI Utilities’ rate case moved to a recommended settlement before the preview’s expected October PUC decision. The settlement provides a two-step $65 million increase and a stay-out through January 2029, resolving the case earlier than the preview’s timeline suggested, though the increase is below the $99.4 million request.
surprises.fact_evidence: The settlement was “recommended for approval without modification” and provides “a two-step $65 million rate increase” with a “stay-out through January 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the PUC decision was due “Oct 29, 2026” and that “Settlement vs. litigated outcome sets the FY27 base”; it cited a “$99.4M” request.

surprises.description: Midstream growth is expected to arrive later than the preview’s call for stabilization would suggest: management now expects growth to be more mid- to back-end loaded, with well-pad expansions starting in fiscal 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: UGI reaffirmed its long-term EPS CAGR, “though midstream growth is now expected to be more mid- to back-end loaded due to Appalachian production timing and well-pad expansions starting in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Midstream & Marketing “needs to show stabilization” and described the bull case as signaling that prior delays were “timing, not demand.”

surprises.description: AmeriGas reduced net debt by about $270 million in one quarter and lowered leverage from the 4.7x level cited in the preview to 4.3x, making faster progress toward its sub-4x year-end target than the preview’s starting point alone indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: AmeriGas “reduced net debt by approximately $270 million versus the prior quarter and lowered leverage to 4.3x, its lowest point in 10 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported AmeriGas leverage of “4.7x at Q2” and a “sub-4.0x FY-end target.”

surprises.description: Management expects AmeriGas to resume meaningful cash distributions to UGI in fiscal 2027, a new source of parent-level cash not identified in the preview’s capital-allocation discussion. The resumption remains conditional on leverage and free-cash-flow targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects AmeriGas to “resume meaningful cash distributions to the parent in fiscal 2027 for the first time in years,” contingent on leverage below 4x by year-end and more than $100 million of free cash flow this year.

surprises.description: UGI completed its cast iron replacement commitment ahead of schedule, an operational milestone the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: UGI “completed its cast iron replacement commitment ahead of schedule.”

in_line: UGI reaffirmed fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.75–$2.90, as the preview expected.
UGI reaffirmed its 5%–7% consolidated EPS CAGR through 2029, matching the preview’s stated long-term outlook.
AmeriGas net customer attrition improved to approximately 2%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that attrition would improve.

surprises.description: Q3 EPS implied by the reported year-to-date figure was about $1.41 ($7.33 year to date less the preview’s $5.92 H1 actual), above the preview’s $1.34–$1.36 consensus range. That is a modest beat, rather than the in-line result described in the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: Atmos reported year-to-date fiscal 2026 net income of $1.2 billion, or $7.33 per diluted share.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS” consensus was “$1.34 (Zacks) / $1.36 (Barchart)”; H1 FY2026 actual was $5.92.

surprises.description: Despite the implied Q3 EPS beat, Atmos reaffirmed the $8.40–$8.50 FY2026 range instead of raising guidance. The preview said investors wanted Q3 upside plus a raise, although its base case also allowed a reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 EPS guidance of $8.40 to $8.50.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The market wants Q3 upside plus a guidance raise to the upper half or above”; the preview also described an in-line result with reaffirmed guidance as “slightly disappointing.”

surprises.description: APT spreads narrowed significantly after June as takeaway capacity came online sooner than expected, and management now expects the second-half APT uplift at the low end of its prior range. This is less favorable than the preview’s potential for full capture of the April–May spread benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: APT’s captured through-system spreads averaged $4.66 in the first nine months versus $1.77 a year earlier, “but have narrowed significantly since June as new takeaway capacity came online sooner than expected”; management expects the second-half uptick at the “lower end” of $0.08–$0.12 and said $0.08 was captured in Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said April/May spreads were “far wider than most models assumed,” identified them as the likeliest source of a beat, and described the June normalization as something to watch; its bull case assumed APT “fully captures” the spread blowout.

surprises.description: Regulatory operating-income increases implemented since the start of the fiscal year exceeded the preview’s approximate on-schedule target, reaching $396 million versus an expected cumulative level around $370 million or more.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company implemented $396 million of annualized operating income increases since the fiscal year's start” and has seven filings pending for nearly $334 million more.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited $135.3 million implemented through Q2, expected roughly $240 million during Q3, and said “anything approaching ~$370M+ confirms plan.”

surprises.description: Atmos raised the low end of its FY2026 O&M guidance by $10 million, signaling somewhat higher spending than the preview’s stated range. It also said annual O&M increases of 4% are expected going forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 O&M guidance (excluding net bad debt) was raised to $875 million to $885 million as spending trends slightly higher, with 4% annual O&M increases expected going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited an FY2026 O&M guide of “$865–$885M” and warned that a gross O&M overrun was a likely source of a miss.

surprises.description: The call disclosed 12 new industrial customers expected to use about 950,000 Mcf per year, adding specific new-load detail that the preview said had been absent from the prior call and could emerge as a first-time disclosure.
surprises.fact_evidence: Atmos added “12 new industrial customers expected to use ~950,000 Mcf per year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that large-load demand was “absent from the Q2 call” and said any first-time disclosure of large industrial or power-generation load would be noteworthy.

surprises.description: Available liquidity and forward-sale proceeds were both higher than the preview’s figures, while equity capitalization was slightly lower. The funding data are a modest improvement overall, though the capitalization comparison is not favorable.
surprises.fact_evidence: Atmos ended the quarter with 60% equity capitalization, $4.6 billion in available liquidity, and roughly $937 million in forward sale proceeds.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited 60.9% equity capitalization, $4.1 billion of liquidity, and approximately $890 million of net forward-sale proceeds.

in_line: Customer additions were in line with the preview: nearly 51,000 over the trailing 12 months, with roughly 39,000 in Texas.
Full-year FY2026 capital expenditures remained on track at approximately $4.2 billion, consistent with the preview; the reported safety-and-reliability share was also within its stated expectation.
The company’s 6%–8% ongoing EPS-growth target is broadly consistent with the preview’s FY2027 consensus of $9.00, or about 6.5% growth from the FY2026 guidance range.
No short-term debt was consistent with the preview’s balance-sheet expectation.

surprises.description: Curtiss-Wright reported Q2 sales of $924 million, slightly below the preview’s assumed $935–945 million buy-side whisper, although essentially in line with the $926.2 million consensus estimate. The shortfall is modest relative to the whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales of $924 million grew 5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Assume a buy-side whisper of roughly $3.70–3.75 EPS on ~$935–945M revenue.”

surprises.description: Operating performance was stronger than the preview’s roughly 18.5% Q2 margin estimate and high-single-digit-plus operating-income growth roadmap: operating margin reached 19.4%, up 110 basis points, and operating income grew 12%. EPS growth of 15% also exceeded the preview’s implied 12.1% growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 110 basis points to 19.4%”; “Operating income up 12% and diluted EPS up 15%, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin ~18.5% (est.)”; management’s Q2 roadmap: “Q2 operating income growth: ‘high single digits plus.’” Consensus adjusted EPS was “$3.61 – $3.62” versus “$3.23” a year earlier, implying “+12.1%.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was substantially above the preview’s estimated $120–135 million range: it reached $160 million, with 116% cash conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow reached $160 million, a 37% year-over-year improvement, representing a strong 116% cash conversion rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow | ~$120–135M (est.).”

surprises.description: The full-year outlook was raised across sales, EPS and operating margin, rather than merely reaffirmed: sales growth is now 8%–9% versus 7%–8%, diluted EPS is $15.10–$15.40 versus $14.90–$15.30, and margin is 19.1%–19.3% versus 19.0%–19.2%. The EPS midpoint is $15.25, though the new low end remains below the preview’s stated bull-case threshold of $15.30.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to 8%-9% sales growth, 14%-16% diluted EPS growth to $15.10-$15.40, and record operating margin of 19.1%-19.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guide was sales growth “+7–8%,” diluted EPS “$14.90–15.30,” and operating margin “19.0–19.2%.” The preview said a bull-case raise would be “to ~$15.20–15.55.”

surprises.description: Full-year free-cash-flow guidance was raised to $585–605 million from $580–600 million, with management still expecting a record despite capital expenditures increasing nearly 30% year over year for growth investments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was raised to a record $585-$605 million despite a nearly 30% year-over-year increase in capital expenditures for growth investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow | $580–600M.”

surprises.description: Defense and Electronics orders were far stronger than the preview’s flat Q2 sales-and-margin framing suggested: orders surged nearly 50% year over year in Q2 and were up over 30% year to date, a record segment performance. The call reported orders, not the segment’s realized sales or margin, so this is a demand signal rather than a direct sales or margin comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense and Electronics orders surged nearly 50% year-over-year in Q2 and are up over 30% year-to-date, marking a record segment performance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Defense Electronics: sales and margins expected to be roughly flat vs. prior-year Q2.”

surprises.description: The AP1000 reactor coolant pump order was not announced, and management only continued to expect it this year. The preview had identified another quarter of “still expected” without an award or firm timing as a credibility concern for the nuclear catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management continues to expect an AP1000 reactor coolant pump order this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The AP1000 reactor coolant pump order is still expected in calendar 2026”; the preview also called “another quarter of ‘still expected’” a “slow-bleed credibility risk.”

surprises.description: Curtiss-Wright reported approximately $95 million in Maritime Industrial Base funding, up from $70 million at the end of March, adding $25 million of funding progress for the Pennsylvania facility expansion beyond the preview’s general mention of maritime industrial base support.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Curtiss-Wright has now been awarded approximately $95 million in Maritime Industrial Base funding, up from $70 million at the end of March, supporting an $80 million multiyear Pennsylvania facility expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the “$80M Cheswick, PA expansion” as “backed by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and maritime industrial base funding,” but did not state an expected award amount.

in_line: Q2 sales growth of 5% was close to the $926.2 million consensus revenue estimate and matched management’s expected mid-single-digit growth.
Q2 orders grew 8% with book-to-bill above 1.1x, within the preview’s base-case book-to-bill range of roughly 1.0–1.2x and above its stated sub-1.0x concern threshold.
The preview expected the AP1000 reactor coolant pump order in calendar 2026 and said it was outside guidance; management continues to expect an order this year, but did not report an award.
The preview anticipated second-half-weighted margin expansion; management’s flat Q3 sequential margin outlook and record Q4 margin above 20% are consistent with that back-half-weighted pattern.

surprises.description: Lee had modeled roughly breakeven earnings, with EPS around +$0.03, but reported $5.2 million of net income—the first profitable quarter since 2024. That is a better result than the central expectation, though the preview cautioned that the published EPS estimate was unreliable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net income was $5.2 million, marking Lee's first profitable quarter since 2024.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS … (pt. +$0.03)” and “EPS … (pt. +$0.03)” in the model; the preview also said the published $(0.16) consensus estimate was “a carry-forward, not a model.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a possible raise to double-digit full-year EBITDA growth, while Lee raised its outlook to 22%–28% growth. That is a stronger increase than the preview’s broad expectation of a move into double digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to growth of 22% to 28%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A guidance raise to double-digit growth is the single most likely positive surprise”; the preview also described the existing company guide as “Mid-single-digit % growth.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $18 million, above the preview’s $17 million central estimate, and grew 23% year over year versus the model’s 13% growth. The preview expected organic EBITDA of $17 million or more to be a good result; growth remained 19% even excluding insurance proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA grew 23% year-over-year to $18 million”; “Excluding $560,000 in cyber-event business interruption insurance proceeds, Q3 adjusted EBITDA still grew 19% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The model put adjusted EBITDA at “$15–19M (pt. $17M)” and “+13%”; the preview said “Organic $17M+ is a genuinely good print.”

surprises.description: Digital-only subscribers ended at 584,000, below the 591,000 level the preview highlighted and down sequentially rather than flat or growing around 590,000. The count still fell within the preview’s broader 580,000–600,000 model range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with 584,000 digital-only subscribers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged subscribers “vs. 591k,” said “Sequential growth validates” the clean-baseline claim, and modeled “580–600k” with a base case “flat at ~590k.”

surprises.description: Quarterly digital-only subscription revenue was $22 million, slightly below the preview’s $22.5–$23.5 million model range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “584,000 digital-only subscribers generating $22 million in quarterly subscription revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Digital-only sub revenue” at “$22.5–23.5M.”

surprises.description: Lee stated a new goal for digital gross margin to cover all SG&A within three years. The preview discussed digital growth and sustainability but did not identify this specific coverage milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “expects digital gross margin to fully cover SG&A within three years.”

in_line: Digital revenue reached 57% of company revenue, consistent with the preview’s 57%–58% estimate.
Cash costs declined 15%, at the low end of the preview’s expected 12%–15% decline.
Cash ended at $59 million, within the preview’s expected $59–$62 million range.
The interest-rate reduction and approximately $18 million in annual savings were in line with the preview’s expectation of about $18 million per year from the 5% coupon.
The Hoffman Media Group management agreement was already described in the preview as effective June 1 and expected to contribute modestly in the quarter.

surprises.description: IBP reported Q2 revenue of $778 million, about 5% above the $740–743 million consensus range and above the preview’s $755–768 million bull case. Revenue rose 2% year over year instead of declining about 2% as consensus implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 net revenue rose 2% to $778 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue | $740.4M – $743.3M” and the bull scenario projected “$755–768M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted earnings materially exceeded consensus: adjusted EPS was $2.91 versus $2.54–$2.57 expected, while adjusted EBITDA was $131 million versus the preview’s estimated $115–120 million. EPS was within the preview’s bull-case range, but well above the central consensus expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $131 million (16.9% margin) with adjusted net income of $78 million, or $2.91 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $2.54 – $2.57”; “Adj. EBITDA | ~$115–120M (est.).”

surprises.description: New residential same-branch sales fell 6%, a milder decline than the preview’s implied expectation of roughly 8%–10%. Total same-branch sales were down less than 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-branch sales declined less than 1% as new residential same-branch sales fell 6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue of ~$742M implicitly needs residential same-branch in roughly the −8% to −10% zone.”

surprises.description: Multifamily demand showed a positive inflection in June and July, with a growing contract backlog, despite the preview’s broadly unfavorable housing backdrop. IBP also said the South represents about 60% of its multifamily revenue, versus 43% of national completions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multifamily sales inflected positively in June and July, with a growing contract backlog,” and “the South Census region accounts for ~60% of IBP's multifamily revenue versus only 43% of national completions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the macro backdrop as “all unfavorable” and said sharper 2026 starts declines were “a 2H26/1H27 revenue problem.”

surprises.description: The announced spray-foam material increase is being passed through and is expected to be margin-neutral longer term, but pass-through timing may weigh on Q3 margins. That near-term lag is a negative wrinkle versus the preview’s expectation that manufacturers would largely capture the increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A ~25% spray foam material cost increase is being passed through, expected to be at least margin neutral longer term but potentially a margin drag in Q3 due to pass-through timing lag.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said manufacturers were “expected to largely capture” the announced 25% spray-foam price increases and flagged whether IBP was “passing through or eating it.”

surprises.description: IBP repurchased about $76 million of stock in Q2, substantially above the $25.4 million buyback cited for Q1 in the preview. The preview had identified a more aggressive buyback as a potential capital-allocation signal, but had not projected this level of repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased ~365,000 shares for $76 million in Q2 (with ~$398 million remaining authorization).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$25.4M / 91K shares in Q1” and said “aggressive buyback ... would read as a management valuation signal.”

surprises.description: Management said it would be willing to raise leverage to 3x for the right commercial or adjacent platform deal, beyond the preview’s stated 2x leverage target. This increases capacity for a larger acquisition but also implies greater willingness to take on debt.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt to trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA leverage was 1.34x ... well below the 2x target, with willingness to go to 3x for the right platform deal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “1.2x net leverage vs. a 2.0x target” and said “capacity is not the constraint — willingness is.”

in_line: Adjusted gross margin was 33.3%, meeting the preview’s key threshold of 33% or better and its 33.0%–33.5% bull-case range.
Commercial same-branch sales rose 10%, matching the preview’s base-case assumption of about +10%.
Other segment same-branch sales grew 28%, within the preview’s expected +25%–30% range.
The Q3 dividend was $0.39 per share, with a year-over-year increase of more than 5%, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about 24% higher year over year versus the preview's 17.5% consensus growth, and adjusted EPS was $1.33 versus $1.23 consensus. EBITDA, margin and EPS also exceeded the high end of company guidance; the 32.1% EBITDA margin was above the preview's roughly 31.9% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 24% year-over-year”; “EBITDA margin expanded 340 basis points to 32.1%”; “Adjusted EPS came in at $1.33”; revenue, EBITDA, margin and EPS “all exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview consensus was revenue of $2.41bn and EPS of $1.23, with expected revenue growth of 17.5% and EBITDA margin of about 31.9%. Its bull case put revenue at $2.46–2.50bn and EPS at $1.31–1.36.

surprises.description: The full-year outlook rose further than the preview's already elevated whisper range: revenue guidance is now $10.05bn and EPS $5.27, versus preview whispers of about $9.75–9.80bn and $5.05–5.10. The preview flagged a raise as essential, but these figures are above its anticipated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was raised across the board to revenue of $10.05 billion, EBITDA of $3.23 billion, and EPS of $5.27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whisper is ~$5.05–5.10 adj. EPS on ~$9.75–9.80bn revenue.”

surprises.description: The full-year free-cash-flow outlook rose to $1.9bn, above the preview's stated threshold of moving above $1.8bn. The preview called an FCF guide above $1.8bn a strong secondary positive signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow guidance of $1.9 billion (±$50 million) at 90% conversion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF guide moving above $1.8bn is a strong secondary tell.”

surprises.description: Spares grew strongly, but the reported first-half mix was about 22%, below the preview's ≥24% watch level. That makes the mix outcome less strong than the preview's bull-case trigger despite the 37% growth in spares revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total spares revenue … rose 37% to approximately $560 million, now representing about 22% of total revenue in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch for ≥24%” spares as a share of revenue and specified “Spares >24% of revenue” in its bull case.

in_line: IGT growth remained close to the prior quarter's exceptional pace: Q2 revenue rose 38%, versus 39% growth in Q1, consistent with the preview's focus on data-center power demand.
CAM's sequential dilution of Fastening Systems margins and the expectation that the acquisition's EPS contribution turns positive in 2027 were consistent with the preview's CAM discussion.

The 2026 capex expectation above $500 million and a further significant step-up in 2027 were broadly consistent with the preview's roughly $500 million 2026 capex outlook and expectation of higher 2027 investment.

surprises.description: Revenue was $857 million against the preview’s roughly $897 million consensus, a shortfall of about 4.5%. The preview already identified this as a miss, so it was not new information by the call, but it remained below the stated expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue was $857 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $857M” versus “~$897M cons. (4 analysts)” and “Miss, ~−4.5%.”

surprises.description: The call described Q3 free cash flow as negative, whereas the preview listed Q3 free cash flow of $32 million. Management said the quarter beat internal forecasts because of working-capital reductions, but that does not match the positive Q3 figure in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative in the quarter as expected but beat internal forecasts, helped by proactive working capital reductions in inventories and receivables.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow | $32M (CFO $76M − capex $44M).”

surprises.description: Management lowered the fully synergized pro forma adjusted EBITDA target to $405 million from an original estimate of about $445 million, citing a changed macro backdrop. The preview focused on the FY26 guidance trim and synergy tracking, but did not flag a reduction of this longer-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's pro forma adjusted EBITDA target of $405 million (fully synergized) is down from an original ~$445 million estimate, reflecting a changed macro backdrop.”

surprises.description: Management said roughly $20 million of additional Project CORE and merger-synergy benefit should carry into fiscal 2027. That provides a specific continuation of self-help beyond FY26, addressing the preview’s open question about whether FY26 would exhaust the programs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 marked the first quarter realizing full run-rate benefits from both Project CORE and merger synergies, with roughly $20 million of additional synergy/CORE benefit expected to carry into fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Confirm both are tracking and, critically, whether FY27 carries incremental capture or whether FY26 exhausts the program.”

surprises.description: Full-year CapEx was tracking to about $60 million, versus the original roughly $80 million guide. The lower spend was not flagged in the preview and was described as the main offset to lower EBITDA in the cash-flow bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx is now tracking to about $60 million (roughly $15 million per quarter) versus an original ~$80 million guide, serving as the main offset to lower EBITDA in the cash flow bridge.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Original ~$80 million guide.”

surprises.description: Management expected to exit the transition services agreement and migrate off legacy Amcor ERP systems before the end of calendar 2026, with integration costs ramping down and a net cash benefit. The preview did not identify this as a cash-flow or integration milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will exit its transition services agreement and migrate off legacy Amcor ERP systems before the end of calendar 2026, which is expected to be a net cash benefit as integration costs ramp down.”

surprises.description: Americas price was a negative $13 million despite 1% volume growth, reflecting Project CORE portfolio and mix walk-away actions. The preview anticipated the volume growth but did not mention this price drag; the deliberate walk-away actions make the implications mixed rather than purely adverse.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Americas volume up 1% led by infrastructure, though Americas price was a negative $13 million due to Project CORE portfolio and mix walk-away actions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic volume: +1%” and “Americas volume up 1%.”

surprises.description: For Rest of World, management attributed weakness to European demand softness and inflation flowing through faster than pricing, but also said a couple million dollars of price recovery should flow into Q4. That expected near-term recovery was a more constructive detail than the preview’s focus on persistent European deterioration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rest of World adjusted EBITDA declined slightly as European demand softness and inflation moving through faster than pricing caused a lag, with a couple million dollars of price recovery expected to flow into Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RoW EBITDA −7%” and “European softness has now persisted across three quarters.”

in_line: FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was moved to the low end of the prior range, as the preview anticipated; management cited persistent inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty.
FY26 free cash flow guidance of $90 million to $110 million was reaffirmed, as expected.
Americas adjusted EBITDA grew 16% to $71 million, matching the preview’s stated segment result.
Organic volume grew 1%, matching the preview’s expectation of thin positive volume growth.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $99 million, up 9% year over year, consistent with the preview’s description of a record Q3 and 9% improvement.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating EPS was $6.41, above the preview’s $5.96–$6.03 consensus range and its own estimate of about $6.05. The beat was partly supported by about $0.15 per share from a tax-equity investment that reduced income tax expense by $4.6 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating EPS rose 17% year-over-year to $6.41, boosted by roughly $0.15 per share from a tax equity investment that reduced income tax expense by $4.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating EPS | Consensus | $5.96” and “Adj. operating EPS (alt.) | Consensus | $6.03”; the preview’s own estimate was “~$6.05.”

surprises.description: Primerica lowered its full-year term-life policy outlook from flat to down about 2% to a mid-single-digit decline. Q2 issued policies were down 12%, worse than the preview’s expected mid-single-digit decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Issued policies dropped 12%, with management guiding full-year issued policies to decline mid-single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guide was “FY2026 term life policies issued: flat to down ~2%”; the preview expected policies “down mid-single digits (~84–86k)” in its base case and identified a guide cut as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: Management lowered the full-year sales-force outlook to flat to down 2%, instead of the prior expectation of flat to up 1%. It said recruiting improvements were coming more slowly than hoped and licensing was lagging recruiting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered its full-year sales force size outlook to flat to down 2% versus 2025, as recruiting improvements arrived slower than hoped and licensing lags behind recruiting.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q1 guidance cited in the preview was “FY2026 life-licensed reps: flat to up ~1% vs. 12/31/25.”

surprises.description: Full-year ISP sales guidance increased to 10%–15% growth, above the preview’s expectation of upper-single-digit growth. Q2 securities sales were up 23%, with especially strong managed-account sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total securities sales grew 23% year-over-year, led by managed account sales up 43%, mutual fund sales up 20%, and variable annuity sales up 17%, with full-year ISP sales guided to increase 10% to 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guidance cited in the preview was “FY2026 ISP sales: upper-single-digit growth.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end AUM reached $140 billion, below the preview’s estimate of about $145 billion. Net inflows were $397 million, up from the $362 million Q1 figure noted in the preview but below its bull-case marker of more than $500 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assets under management reached a record $140 billion, up 16% year-over-year, with approximately $397 million of net inflows during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “ending client assets should land near ~$145B”; its bull case looked for “net inflows >$500M.”

surprises.description: Shareholder returns exceeded the preview’s implied quarterly buyback pace: the company repurchased $135 million of shares, versus roughly $113 million per quarter implied by the remaining authorization, and also paid $37 million in dividends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned $173 million to shareholders in Q2 ($135 million buybacks, $37 million dividends), bringing year-to-date total returns to $352 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the remaining authorization implied “~$113M/quarter for the balance” of 2026.

in_line: The Term Life benefits and claims ratio of 57.9% was essentially in line with the preview’s expectation of about 58%; the smaller $4.9 million remeasurement gain was also consistent with the preview’s expectation that the prior quarter’s larger favorable gain would not repeat.
Investments/ISP revenue growth of 21% was close to the preview’s modeled ISP growth of about 22%.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $240 million, about 14% above the $210.8 million consensus, rather than the preview’s expected $205–215 million base-case range. Management said production rates were steady and met retail and order intake levels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $240 million, up 12.1% year-over-year and 32.7% sequentially, driven by steady production rates meeting retail and order intake levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus” revenue of “$210.8M”; the base-case scenario expected “$205–215M.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS reached $0.63, well above the preview’s $0.365–$0.39 consensus range. This was a much stronger quarter than the preview’s expectation of only modest earnings power, even with acquisition-related costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS surged to $0.63 in Q2 from $0.05 in Q1, despite $0.11 of OMARS acquisition-related expenses weighing on the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS” consensus of “$0.365 (MarketBeat) / $0.39 (Zacks via Nasdaq).”

surprises.description: The full-year EPS outlook was less reassuring than the preview’s expected anchor of earnings generally in line with FY25: management instead expects EPS roughly flat versus 2023 and cited cumulative OMARS expenses as a drag. The facts do not provide a comparable EPS figure for 2023, so the size of the shortfall versus the preview’s $1.98 FY25 anchor cannot be quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year EPS is expected to be roughly flat versus 2023, held back by cumulative OMARS one-time expenses of about $0.24-$0.29 across the year (with $0.04-$0.05 remaining).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had reaffirmed EPS “generally in line with FY25” ($1.98 diluted); the preview called this the key EPS guidance anchor.

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin came in above the preview’s roughly 14.0–14.3% expectation, at 15%. The full-year outlook for margins to normalize to the mid-13% range, however, was consistent with the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit was $35.9 million, or 15% of sales, though management expects full-year gross margins to normalize to the mid-13% range as chassis mix increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 gross margin was expected at “~14.0–14.3%”; the preview also said the FY guide called for gross margin to fall to “mid-13%.”

surprises.description: Military commitments rose to more than $200 million, up from the preview’s cited level of more than $150 million, and the revenue timeline was pulled forward: production is beginning in 2025 and most revenue is expected in 2026–27 rather than 2028–29.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Military commitments have surpassed $200 million, up from $150 million last quarter, with production beginning in 2025 and most revenue recognized in 2026 and 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “>$150M in commitments, production starting 2027, revenue mostly 2028–29.”

surprises.description: The facility schedule was substantially earlier than the preview expected: the preview anticipated a late-summer 2026 groundbreaking and an H2 FY26 cash-flow drag, while management described construction beginning in Q4 2024 and production readiness by late 2025. Funding is expected largely from organic cash flow, as the preview had flagged capex as a material cash-flow concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new 200,000+ square foot manufacturing facility is targeted to be production-ready by late 2025, with construction beginning Q4 2024 and funding expected largely from organic cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “$100M / 200,000+ sq ft expansion was targeted to break ground late summer 2026” and described “a material FCF drag beginning in H2.”

surprises.description: OMARS costs were more front-loaded than the preview’s expectation that about $0.13 per share would remain spread across Q2–Q4: Q2 alone included $0.11 per share of acquisition-related expenses, with only $0.04–$0.05 remaining for the rest of the year. The remaining burden is therefore lower than expected, although more of it hit Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 included “$0.11 of OMARS acquisition-related expenses”; full-year one-time expenses are estimated at “about $0.24-$0.29” with “$0.04-$0.05 remaining.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1’s roughly $0.13 of non-cash charges was “roughly half the FY26 total” and estimated “~$0.13 remains spread across Q2–Q4.”

surprises.description: The company reduced debt by another $20 million since Q1 while increasing cash, a stronger balance-sheet improvement than the preview’s simple watchpoint about whether cash and debt would remain stable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced debt by an additional $20 million since Q1 while growing its cash balance to $55.6 million, up $2.6 million sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged whether the “$53.0M cash / $21.0M LT debt balance sheet stays as clean.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the $850–900 million full-year revenue guidance range, as the preview expected the range to hold; it also targeted roughly $250 million per quarter in the back half, consistent with the preview’s anticipated H2 ramp.
Management expects full-year gross margins to normalize to the mid-13% range as chassis mix increases, matching the preview’s stated margin outlook.

Domestic retail demand and dealer inventories remain flat at historical averages, consistent with the preview’s focus on soft retail and historically average inventory levels; the preview treated an order inflection as a possible upside case, not an assured expectation.
The preview anticipated continued buybacks and dividends; the company returned approximately $4.9 million through repurchases and dividends in Q2, with $11.5 million remaining under authorization.

surprises.description: Nine reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million, below the $10–15 million guidance range and well below the preview’s $12.5 million base estimate. Management attributed the shortfall to coiled tubing margin compression.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million fell below original guidance, driven by coiled tubing margin compression.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” guidance of “$10.0–15.0M” and a “$12.5M” base estimate; the preview also said “EBITDA below $10M cannot be” excused.

surprises.description: Coiled tubing costs rose about 12% quarter-over-quarter, and price increases did not fully offset the inflation. That left margins compressed, contrary to the preview’s upside case that price increases would stick.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Coiled tubing costs including consumables, labor, and repairs rose about 12% quarter-over-quarter, and price increases failed to fully offset the inflation, causing margin compression.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case required that “first price increases stick,” and its pricing checklist asked whether “anything actually” stuck.

surprises.description: Two large-diameter coiled tubing units—about 17% of that fleet—were taken out of service for maintenance, with one not expected back until near year-end. The preview identified coiled tubing rate erosion as a risk but did not anticipate this equipment outage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two large-diameter coiled tubing units (about 17% of the large-diameter fleet) went out of service on maintenance issues,” and the second is “not expected to return until near year-end.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook was weaker than the preview’s base case: revenue guidance of $133–143 million is centered below Q2 revenue, and adjusted EBITDA is expected to be flat to modestly down rather than flat to modestly up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $133 million to $143 million, with adjusted EBITDA expected to be flat to modestly down versus Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Q3 guide flat to modestly up.”

surprises.description: Completion tools substantially outperformed the preview’s estimate: revenue reached $37.1 million, up 44% quarter-over-quarter, versus an estimated $29.0 million and 12% growth. The reported drivers were a 45% increase in stages, strong international sales, and domestic share gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completion tools revenue surged 44% quarter-over-quarter to $37.1 million on a 45% increase in stages, boosted by strong international sales and domestic market share gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated completion tools revenue of “~$29.0M” and “+12%.”

surprises.description: Wireline missed the expected weather-driven rebound: revenue was $23 million, down 4% quarter-over-quarter, versus the preview’s $27.5 million estimate and 15% expected growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wireline revenue declined 4% to $23 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated wireline at “~$27.5M” and “+15%,” calling it the “largest weather snapback.”

surprises.description: Coiled tubing revenue fell 2% to $26.4 million instead of the expected 2% increase. Days worked rose 16%, but the day rate fell 15%, indicating a sharper rate decline than the preview’s modest-growth estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Coiled tubing days worked rise 16% but day rate fall 15% (revenue down 2% to $26.4 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated coiled tubing revenue of “~$27.5M” and “+2%,” while noting Q1 day rates were down 18%.

surprises.description: Cementing grew more slowly than forecast: revenue rose 3% to $55.3 million, rather than reaching the preview’s $56.5 million estimate and 6% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cementing revenue grew 3% to $55.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated cementing revenue of “~$56.5M” and “+6%.”

surprises.description: The company now expects full-year CapEx toward the middle-to-lower end of its $20–30 million range and said this supports cash flow neutrality in the second half. That is more reassuring than the preview’s concern that back-half-weighted spending could pressure H2 cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx guidance of $20 million to $30 million was reaffirmed but now expected in the middle-to-lower end, supporting cash flow neutrality in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “back-half weighted spend could pressure H2 FCF.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $141.8 million was within the original $136–146 million guidance range and close to the preview’s approximately $140.8 million street proxy and $141 million base estimate.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.29, above the preview’s $0.26–$0.27 consensus estimates and $0.28 base estimate, though it reached the preview’s stated buy-side whisper range. The result was a modest beat against the base estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS up 12% to $0.29.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.26” and “$0.27” consensus; “My estimates (base) … Adj. EPS $0.28”; “buy-side whisper is realistically … $0.28–0.29 adj. EPS.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $59.4 million came in below the preview’s estimated $60–$62 million range and $62 million base estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA up 6% to $59.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$60–62M”; “My estimates (base) … Adj. EBITDA $62M.”

surprises.description: Management maintained full-year guidance, but said revenue should land at the high end while gross profit and adjusted EBITDA should land at the low end because of margin pressure. That was weaker than the preview’s expectation of at least a midpoint nudge or, in its base case, reaffirmation with language that results were tracking to the upper half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company maintained full-year guidance but expects revenue at the higher end ($1.01-$1.04 billion range) while gross profit ($405-425M) and adjusted EBITDA ($230-245M) will land at the lower end due to margin pressure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The market is positioned for at least a midpoint nudge”; the base scenario expected “FY26 guide reaffirmed with ‘tracking to upper half’ language.”

surprises.description: Payables revenue growth was 21.6%, below the preview’s view that growth above roughly 25% would be a clean beat. It was not the mid-teens slowdown the preview identified as a concern, but it fell short of the expected stronger growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payables revenue grew 21.6% to $30.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything above ~25% is a clean beat; a step down to mid-teens reframes Q1 as a pull-forward.”

surprises.description: Payables’ faster growth came with a sharp deterioration in profitability: adjusted gross profit fell and margin contracted 760 basis points as lower-margin buyer-funded revenue became dominant and was booked gross. The preview expected Payables growth to be a strong contributor and said management had flagged no one-time items, but did not anticipate this margin effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross profit fell 10.4% and margins dropped 760 basis points to 21.4% as buyer-funded revenue (up 26.3%) now dominates and is booked on a gross basis at lower margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “+35.6% to $32.4M in Q1 with adj. EBITDA +55%, driven by enterprise customers using it as a working-capital substitute for revolvers. Management flagged no one-time items.”

surprises.description: Treasury Solutions revenue grew 14.9%, in line with the preview’s mid-teens expectation, but its margin fell about 590 basis points. The preview described Treasury as the profit engine with roughly 89.8% Q1 adjusted gross margin and anticipated that the rate headwind was mainly a comparison issue, not this degree of mix-driven compression.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Treasury Solutions revenue grew 14.9% to $60.5 million, but gross margins compressed roughly 590 basis points to 88.5% due to mix shift from Passport (up 125%) and Priority Tech Ventures (up nearly 400%), which run at only 30-40% margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “It grew 17.5% in Q1 despite 75bp of Y/Y Fed cuts compressing float income”; “the rate headwind is now purely a comp issue that rolls off in Q4”; “If balances hold ~$1.9B and growth stays mid-teens.”

surprises.description: Merchant Solutions grew faster than its recent pace and its adjusted gross profit and margin improved, countering the preview’s concern that organic growth might stall. Revenue growth was 7.7% overall and 4.5% organically, versus Q1 growth of 6.7% and 3.9% organic.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merchant Solutions revenue rose 7.7% to $175.8 million (4.5% organic), with adjusted gross profit up 12.4% to $39.8 million and margins improving over 100 basis points to 22.7%, aided by acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 revenue +6.7% (only +3.9% organic)”; the preview flagged “Merchant Solutions card volume (the deceleration risk)” and said volume below about 2% would confirm the organic engine was stalling.

surprises.description: Recently enacted Mastercard and Visa interchange increases added cost of goods sold, creating an additional margin headwind alongside the lower-margin gross-basis Payables mix. The preview did not flag these price increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recently enacted Mastercard and Visa interchange price increases raised cost of goods sold, creating a margin ‘double whammy’ alongside the gross-revenue accounting on growing buyer-funded payables.”

surprises.description: Net leverage improved to 3.8x from 4.0x in Q1, reaching the preview’s highlighted threshold for a potential deleveraging catalyst. The preview also flagged buyback activity as a possible catalyst, but the provided call facts do not report any buyback.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved to 3.8x at quarter-end from 4.0x in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A print at ≤3.8x plus visible buyback under the $40M authorization is the de-rating catalyst.”

surprises.description: Management declined to comment on the ongoing special committee evaluation of a take-private proposal, leaving the matter unresolved. The preview did not mention the proposal or identify it as an overhang.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management declined to comment on the ongoing special committee evaluation of a take-private proposal, which analysts noted is a key overhang preventing share movement despite solid fundamentals.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $262.3 million was within the preview’s stated $258–$263 million consensus range and near its $262–$265 million buy-side whisper range.
Treasury Solutions revenue growth of 14.9% was consistent with the preview’s expectation of mid-teens growth.

surprises.description: REPX raised full-year oil production guidance by 2% to a midpoint of 23,000 barrels per day, above the preview’s 22,000–23,000 range. The roughly 30% year-over-year growth was already expected, but the higher midpoint was not.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year oil production guidance was raised 2% to 23,000 barrels per day at the midpoint.”

surprises.description: The Targa pipeline, which the preview expected to begin commercial operations in Q3, is now expected in early Q4. The delay also means drilling and completion activity is shifting from Texas to New Mexico, with DUCs carrying into next year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Targa high-pressure gathering pipeline is expected in service early Q4 2026,” and a “1.2 drilled-to-turned-in-line ratio” is “carrying DUCs into next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Targa high-pressure trunk line timing (New Mexico) — guided to Q3 commercial operations with 20+ drilled-but-uncompleted wells waiting on it.”

surprises.description: Full-year CapEx guidance rose to $236 million, above the preview’s $200–220 million range and 12% above the prior guidance. About two-thirds of the new total is for infrastructure, making this a substantial increase over the expected spending level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year CapEx guidance was raised 12% (or $26 million) to $236 million, with roughly one-third tied to upstream activity and two-thirds to infrastructure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “capex $200–220M ($210M mid).” The preview also said “a second FY capex raise … would be poorly received.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $6 million, below the preview’s base-case estimate of $10–20 million. Operating cash flow rose, but cash CapEx jumped sharply to $73 million and absorbed most of it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow rose 35% quarter-over-quarter to $64 million, but cash CapEx jumped 153% to $73 million, cutting Q2 free cash flow to just $6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FCF ~$10–20M”; it also said Q2 FCF “could compress toward breakeven.”

surprises.description: Instead of reducing debt as the preview said management prioritized, REPX drew on its credit facility and principal debt increased by $26 million to $273 million. Leverage stayed around 1.0x, but the debt balance moved in the opposite direction from the expected paydown.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Principal debt increased 11% (or $26 million) to $273 million as the company drew on its credit facility, keeping leverage around 1.0x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the majority of excess FCF post-dividend goes to debt reduction from $247M” and flagged the “debt trajectory from $247M / 1.0x.”

surprises.description: April and May midstream constraints forced temporary well shut-ins that reduced Q2 oil production by about 2,000 barrels per day. The preview focused on the Q2 production range and the future Targa line, but did not anticipate this specific production interruption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Midstream constraints during April and May forced temporary well shut-ins that reduced Q2 oil production by approximately 2,000 barrels per day.”

surprises.description: Silverback production is now about twice the buy-side case projection even though no new wells have been drilled, and per-well workover costs have fallen about 59%. This substantially exceeds the projection cited on the call and indicates better production and workover economics than that case assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Silverback acquisition's production is now approximately double the buy-side case projection with no new wells drilled, and per-well workover costs fell about 59%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call described the comparison as “double the buy-side case projection.”

surprises.description: A relatively small, intentional workover spend produced a notable increment of oil from low-decline wells: about $2.3 million added roughly 700 barrels per day. The preview did not flag this production contribution or its cost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly $2.3 million of intentional workover spend added about 700 barrels of oil per day of incremental production from low-decline wells.”

in_line: Q2 oil production grew 5% sequentially, consistent with the preview’s expectation of sequential growth and within its stated 20,700–21,300 barrels-per-day Q2 guidance range.
Full-year oil production guidance still implies approximately 30% year-over-year growth, consistent with the growth outlook the preview said investors expected.

surprises.description: Tennant’s adjusted diluted EPS was $0.83, well below the preview’s $1.33–$1.34 consensus, and adjusted EBITDA was $35.3 million versus the preview’s estimated $47–49 million. The shortfall was much larger than the preview’s expected modest year-over-year declines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $35.3 million (10.9% of sales) … and adjusted diluted EPS dropped to $0.83,” with roughly half the shortfall from gross margin and half from higher operating expenses.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS Consensus: $1.33–$1.34”; “Adjusted EBITDA: ~$47–49M (derived).”

surprises.description: Instead of reaffirming the existing full-year guidance as the preview’s base case anticipated, Tennant raised its sales range but cut profitability guidance: adjusted EPS fell to $3.80–$4.45 from $4.70–$5.30, and adjusted EBITDA to $155–$170 million from $175–$190 million. The sales increase alongside the profit cuts signals stronger demand but materially weaker expected profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year net sales guidance to $1.27–1.31 billion but cut adjusted EBITDA guidance to $155–170 million and adjusted EPS to $3.80–4.45 (down from prior $4.70–5.30).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year guidance treatment. Reaffirm, narrow, raise, or cut”; the base case expected “FY guide reaffirmed unchanged,” and the preview called a guidance raise “unlikely.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 39.5%, below the preview’s 40% expectation, and the recovery outlook is slower than the preview’s anticipated low-40s second half: management expects Q3 to remain flat near 39.5% before reaching roughly 41% in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 39.5%, down 260 basis points year-over-year but up 140 basis points sequentially,” with Q3 expected “to stay flat near 39.5% before improving to roughly 41% in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs ≥40%”; the preview also expected “low 40s” for the second half and said to look for “visible sequential gain through the quarter.”

surprises.description: Net sales were $324 million, missing the preview’s $329.55 million consensus and its $328–$332 million base-case range. North American parts shortages constrained shipments despite stronger orders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales grew only 1.7% to $324 million as North American parts shortages constrained shipments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales Q2 FY26 Consensus: $329.55M”; the base case expected “~$328–332M.”

surprises.description: Orders and backlog built more strongly than the preview’s expected backlog-conversion story: orders rose 6.6% year over year and backlog reached $127 million, rather than drawing down the $109 million Q1 backlog. This indicates demand was stronger than shipments showed, but also that fulfillment constraints persisted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orders reached $339 million, up 6.6% year-over-year,” and “Backlog climbed to $127 million, up $18 million from Q1 and $50 million since year-end,” while parts shortages constrained shipments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 “must show that backlog converting to shipped revenue” and called for the “$109M backlog” to be “drawn down.”

surprises.description: The North American ERP recovery timeline slipped further: normal operations are now expected in the first half of 2027 rather than the original second half of 2026. That postpones the operational recovery the preview framed as central to Q2’s backlog conversion and margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ERP optimization timeline slipped one to two quarters, with a return to normal North American operations now expected in the first half of 2027 versus the original second half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Q2 the “ERP recovery quarter” and said “Q2 must show that backlog converting to shipped revenue.”

surprises.description: Robotics growth remained strong but was far below the preview’s expectation that growth would stay near Q1’s 85% rate: Q2 robotics revenue grew 37% year over year. The full-year outlook and 2028 target still point to substantial growth, but the near-term pace was slower than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Robotics revenue grew 37% year-over-year to $31 million in Q2,” with full-year guidance of $130–145 million and a target of $250 million by 2028.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “sustaining anything near +85% growth supports the premium multiple” and flagged sustaining “anything near +85%” as the trajectory to watch.

surprises.description: Regional performance was weaker than the preview’s recent trends suggested: EMEA shifted from +1.0% organic growth in Q1 to a 2.8% decline, with negative pricing, while APAC fell 10.6% versus Q1’s 2.0% decline. North America was essentially flat rather than clearly inflecting positive, although Latin America grew 21%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMEA organic sales declined 2.8% with negative net pricing from increased discounting,” “APAC fell 10.6%,” and “North America was essentially flat (-0.2%) and Latin America grew 21%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 organic growth of “EMEA +1.0%, APAC -2.0%” and said the Americas was the region that “must inflect.”

surprises.description: The expected cash-flow inflection was not evident in the first-half result: operating cash flow remained a $26.2 million use, compared with $22.1 million generated in the prior-year first half. The preview specifically looked for Q2 cash flow to swing decisively positive from Q1’s outflow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half operating cash flow was a use of $26.2 million versus $22.1 million generated a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 OCF needs to swing decisively positive” from Q1’s “- $31.2M”; the catalyst checklist called for an “Operating cash flow inflection.”

in_line: EMEA deployment remained deferred beyond 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the EMEA ERP rollout would stay deferred past 2026.
Net leverage was 2x trailing-12-month adjusted EBITDA, at the upper end of the 1x–2x target range, broadly consistent with the preview’s estimate of 1.78x near the top of that range.

The CFO retirement and successor search were already disclosed in the preview; the call’s expectation of naming a successor by Q1 2027 is consistent with the previously stated Q2 2027 retirement timing.

surprises.description: The preview put Q1 revenue consensus at $592.9 million, but the reported tobacco and ingredients revenues add up to about $524 million, roughly 12% below that estimate. Tobacco revenue fell 13% and ingredients revenue fell 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Tobacco revenue was down 13% to $437 million; ingredients revenue was down 3% to $87 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $592.9M” for Q1 FY2027 consensus.

surprises.description: The preview expected adjusted EPS of $0.25, but the company reported a $5 million net loss and just $2.3 million of consolidated operating income. This was a much weaker profitability result than the preview’s base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated operating income fell to $2.3 million from $33.8 million year-over-year, and the company posted a net loss of $5 million versus net income of $8.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (adjusted) | $0.25” for Q1 FY2027 consensus.

surprises.description: Tobacco operating income was far below the preview’s expected $28–36 million base-case range, collapsing to $3.5 million. The preview anticipated a difficult comparison and customer delays, but not a result this far below its modeled range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tobacco segment operating income collapsed to $3.5 million in Q1 FY2027 from $35.7 million a year earlier,” with customers delaying purchases amid oversupply.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “tobacco op income $28–36M.”

surprises.description: Ingredients slipped into an operating loss rather than delivering the roughly breakeven result in the preview’s base case. The loss was relatively small, but it continued the segment’s weak performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Ingredients reported a “$700,000 operating loss” versus $1.7 million of operating income a year earlier, with revenue down 3%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Ingredients ~breakeven”; the preview also identified the $1.7 million prior-year operating income as the Q1 comparison.

surprises.description: Foreign currency movements created a specific additional headwind to tobacco operating income that the preview did not identify in its operating outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Foreign currency movements caused a $4.4 million negative operating income variance in the tobacco segment versus the prior-year quarter.”

in_line: Management said full-year customer demand remains consistent with its initial sales plan, with shipments weighted toward the second half; the preview had flagged delayed customer commitments and the seasonal timing of shipments.

Management expects uncommitted inventories to move toward the 20% target as the season progresses and tobacco margins to normalize over coming quarters, broadly matching the preview’s expected FY2027 recovery framing.
Management does not expect to repeat last year’s large dark air-cured inventory write-downs, consistent with the preview’s base case of no meaningful incremental charge.

Net debt was lower year over year, consistent with the preview’s note that debt had been declining, though the call did not provide the uncommitted-inventory percentage the preview identified as the key checkpoint.

surprises.description: APA maintained its Egypt BOE outlook despite revising gross oil and gas guidance, avoiding the further adjusted-production cut the preview identified as a key risk. It also said about half of Egypt gas production now benefits from revised pricing, with minimal free-cash-flow impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In Egypt, APA revised guidance to gross oil production of about 118,000 bpd and gross gas of 535 million cubic feet per day, maintaining the original BOE outlook with minimal free cash flow impact, and now has about half of gas production benefiting from revised pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a second cut” in Egypt adjusted guidance; the base case expected Egypt to “drift[] to ~67–69 MBoe/d,” while the bear case anticipated a cut “again to ~64–66 MBoe/d.”

surprises.description: APA raised its full-year free-cash-flow outlook to about $2.3 billion at current strip pricing, modestly above the roughly $2.2 billion level the preview said investors wanted reaffirmed. The company attributed roughly $950 million pretax to its gas trading portfolio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “At current strip pricing, APA expects approximately $2.3 billion of total free cash flow in 2026, including roughly $950 million pretax from its gas trading portfolio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any FCF guide below the standing ~$2.2B is the bear trigger”; the catalyst checklist said investors wanted “reaffirmation” of FY26 FCF at that level.

surprises.description: APA increased its year-end annualized cost-savings target to about $500 million, exceeding the preview’s expected $450 million target. The company also reported total reductions including interest savings of roughly $675 million versus 2024.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its year-end annualized run-rate cost savings target to approximately $500 million, up from the prior $450 million goal, with total cost reductions including interest savings reaching roughly $675 million versus 2024.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview stated the target was “$450M cumulative run-rate by YE26.”

surprises.description: APA raised full-year Permian oil production guidance by 3,000 barrels per day while planning to operate with only four rigs for the rest of the year and keeping its capital budget unchanged. The preview’s base case expected guidance to be reaffirmed, while higher Permian volumes were described as an upside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year Permian oil production guidance to 123,000 barrels per day (up from 120,000) while cutting the rig count to 4 for the rest of the year and holding the $1.3 billion capital budget unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “FY guidance reaffirmed, not raised”; its bull case required “an explicit H2 volume restoration in the Permian.”

surprises.description: APA repaid more debt in the first half than the preview cited and now expects to reach its $3 billion net-debt target in 2027, ahead of the original three-to-four-year timeline. That is faster progress than the preview’s central discussion of the debt target and paydown cadence suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repaid $752 million of bond debt in the first half of 2026 (including $673 million in Q2) and now expects to reach its $3 billion net debt target in 2027, ahead of the original 3-4 year timeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “YTD debt repayment $634M” and described the $3 billion net-debt target as an outstanding goal to monitor.

surprises.description: APA disclosed plans for higher exploration spending in 2027, including two Alaska wells and a Uruguay well, rather than providing only the general exploration-related swing narrative flagged in the preview. ENI will partly fund the Uruguay well, which offsets some of that spending exposure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Exploration spend rises in 2027 (~$100-120 million for two Alaska wells) with a Uruguay well planned for late 2027 partly funded by new partner ENI.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS was $1.89 per diluted share, essentially in line with the preview’s approximately $1.88 Street mean.
Full-year lease operating expense guidance was reduced to $1.5 billion, consistent with the preview’s expectation that LOE would hold at about $1.5 billion.
APA reaffirmed its commitment to return at least 60% of 2026 free cash flow to shareholders, consistent with the preview’s focus on the existing 60% return framework.
GranMorgu remained on budget and on schedule for first oil in mid-2028, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: MMI reported Q2 revenue of $203 million, about 4.5% above the preview’s $194.3 million consensus. The beat was stronger than the preview’s base case of $192–198 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 18% year-over-year to $203 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $194.3M”; base scenario: “$192–198M.”

surprises.description: MMI earned $0.10 per share, beating the preview’s $0.03 consensus by $0.07 and delivering positive GAAP earnings in a quarter when the preview described crossing zero as the key test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income swung to $4 million ($0.10 per share) from a net loss of $11 million ($0.28 per share) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) +$0.03”; “Consensus wants MMI's first positive Q2 EPS of the cycle.”

surprises.description: Private client brokerage reached $106 million, exceeding the preview’s roughly $95 million whisper despite the preview’s concern about weakness in MMI’s core single-asset market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Private client brokerage grew 14% to $106 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Private-client brokerage revenue vs. ~$95M whisper”; the preview also described multifamily individual asset sales as “–7% Y/Y” and said the market had “decelerated in Q2.”

surprises.description: Middle-market brokerage returned to growth, rising 13% to $22 million, rather than remaining weak after its Q1 decline. The preview had identified a return to growth as a bull-case condition, not its expected baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Middle market grew 13% to $22 million,” with “broad-based recovery across price segments for the first time since the market disruption began.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a bull case required “middle market ($10–20M) returns to growth after Q1's –5.9%”; its bear case said “middle market stays negative.”

surprises.description: Transactions above $20 million grew 43% to $33 million, a sharp acceleration after an extended period of institutional softness; the preview had not forecast this scale of growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The larger transaction segment (deals above $20 million) grew 43% to $33 million, the strongest growth since Q4 2024 after an extended period of institutional softness.”

surprises.description: Brokerage growth came in at 18%, above the preview’s implied 12–15% growth range. The stronger brokerage result helped drive the overall revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brokerage up 18%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Brokerage commissions: ~$158–162M (est.)” versus $141.4 million a year earlier, implying “+12–15%.”

surprises.description: Financing revenue rose only 15%, below the preview’s estimated $31–34 million and implied 18–29% growth range. Loan count rose 17%, but dollar volume grew just 5%, showing weaker dollar-volume growth than the headline loan-count increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Financing revenue rose 15% to $30 million on a 17% increase in transaction count to 480 loans, though dollar volume grew only 5% to $4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Financing fees ~$31–34M (est.)” and implied “+18–29%”; the preview also said “sustaining even +25% signals” the buildout was compounding.

surprises.description: SG&A stayed virtually flat in dollars instead of rising modestly as the preview expected, falling to 35% of revenue and producing stronger operating leverage than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A held virtually flat in dollars but fell to 35% of revenue from 42% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 guardrails called for “SG&A up modestly in absolute dollars.”

surprises.description: Management said cost of services is expected to increase sequentially in Q3 as commissions to senior producers rise. The preview focused on the Q2 cost range and did not flag this additional Q3 cost pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost of services rose 50 basis points to 62.4% of revenue, reflecting higher commissions paid to more senior producers, and is expected to increase sequentially in Q3.”

in_line: Cost of services was 62.4% of revenue, within the preview’s 62.0–63.5% Q2 guide range.
Adjusted EBITDA was $12 million, at the low end of the preview’s estimated $12–15 million range.
Management described only modest year-over-year pipeline growth entering Q3 amid rate volatility, consistent with the preview’s cautious base-case H2 tone.
The $0.25 semiannual dividend was consistent with the preview’s stated $0.25 semiannual dividend.
