surprises.description: The preview estimated Q2 GAAP EPS of $0.10–$0.15, while the call reported net income of $12.6 million, or $0.08 per share. That is below the preview’s GAAP estimate, though the preview cautioned that derivative marks could make GAAP EPS noisy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $12.6 million ($0.08 per share)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS +$0.10 to +$0.15 (derivative reversal)”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $31 million, well above the preview’s estimate of roughly $15–20 million. The result was also a 50% sequential increase, rather than the modest cash generation the preview modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow rose 50% sequentially to $31 million in Q2”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow: ~$15–20M”

surprises.description: The balance sheet improved beyond the preview’s roughly $220 million net-debt trajectory: cash exceeded $150 million, net debt fell to $200 million, and leverage was 1.2x. Management also said the ratio could fall below 1x by year-end, better than the preview’s expectation of leverage at or below 1.5x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash on hand grew to over $150 million while net debt fell to $200 million, lowering the trailing 12-month net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio to 1.2x, with management targeting potentially under 1x by year-end 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$55M+ keeps net debt/EBITDA at/below 1.5x” and “validates the ~$220M net debt trajectory.”

surprises.description: Q2 production reached 34,700 boe/d, modestly above the preview’s roughly 34,300 boe/d guide-midpoint expectation, and was up year over year despite no new drilling or acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 production reached 34,700 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 3% year-over-year despite no new drilling or acquisitions”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Production ~34.3 MBoe/d (guide midpoint)”

surprises.description: The Q3 production outlook was for more than 35,000 boe/d, but the preview said the buy side wanted roughly 36,000 boe/d back after the turnaround. The stated floor is therefore below the preview’s desired recovery level, although it does exceed 35,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance exceeding 35,000 boe/d.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy side wants ~36 MBoe/d back in Q3”

surprises.description: Q2 LOE was $72 million, within the $71–79 million guidance range and below the preview’s $75 million midpoint threshold. However, management expects Q3 LOE to rise to $73–81 million because workover and facility maintenance were deferred, adding a cost increase beyond the preview’s Q2-focused turnaround discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 LOE came in at $72 million, below guidance, but is expected to rise to $73-81 million in Q3 due to deferred workover and facility maintenance work.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “LOE ≤ $75M (guide midpoint)” and “What matters is whether the turnaround stayed on schedule and on budget.”

surprises.description: Management said successful surety litigation could produce claims in the hundreds of millions of dollars, with antitrust damages trebled, and estimated resolution in roughly two years. The preview did not flag this potential legal recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management believes successful surety litigation could yield claims reaching hundreds of millions of dollars, with antitrust damages statutorily trebled, and expects resolution within roughly two years.”

surprises.description: Management asserted that the company’s enterprise value is below its PDP PV-10, a valuation comparison the preview did not discuss. This is a favorable management framing, not a reported change in valuation or a quantified result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated the company's enterprise value is below its PDP PV-10”

surprises.description: Management said actual produced reserves over the past 10–15 years exceeded 1P reserve estimates by more than double. The preview did not raise this historical reserve-performance claim.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Actual produced reserves over the past 10-15 years have exceeded 1P reserve estimates by more than double.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the possibility that management had added hedges during the April–May price spike; management instead said it had no plans to add 2027 hedges at this time. Whether that is favorable depends on future prices, but the anticipated hedge possibility was not confirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management … [held] no plans to add 2027 hedges at this time.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If management layered in H2'26/2027 hedges during the April–May $100+ window, that is a material, under-appreciated value capture”

surprises.description: Management expressed a current preference for returning capital through dividends rather than buybacks. The preview noted that maintaining the dividend was a low bar, but did not set an expectation about buybacks or this specific preference.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management indicated a preference for returning capital via dividends over buybacks currently”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was over $54 million, close to the preview’s roughly $55 million base estimate.
Q2 LOE of $72 million was within the $71–79 million guide and below the preview’s $75 million midpoint threshold.

Full-year capital guidance of $20–25 million (excluding acquisitions) was essentially in line with the preview’s $19.5–24.5 million range; spending trending toward the higher end was a modest shift within that range.
Management continued to prioritize accretive producing-property acquisitions, consistent with the preview’s emphasis on acquisition capacity and the company’s stated acquisition framework.

surprises.description: ATN was expected to generate about $48.5 million of adjusted EBITDA, with $49 million identified as the level that would validate the operating trajectory. It reported $49.7 million, with a 27% margin versus the preview’s 26.6% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew nearly 9% year-over-year to $49.7 million, with total adjusted EBITDA margin expanding roughly 170 basis points to 27%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” estimate: “$48.5M” and “Adj. EBITDA margin” estimate: “26.6%”; the preview also said “≥$49M makes a guide narrowing to $188–193M hard to avoid.”

surprises.description: Revenue was expected at $183.2 million consensus, or $182.5 million in the preview’s estimate. ATN reported $184.5 million, modestly above both benchmarks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 2% year-over-year to $184.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus $183.2M” and “My Estimate $182.5M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected post-sale net leverage of roughly 1.0–1.5x. ATN reported 0.91x, below the low end of that expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved dramatically to 0.91x from 2.36x at year-end 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Post-close it should print roughly 1.0–1.5x.”

surprises.description: The preview said a buyback authorization was the largest potential upside surprise and that silence was the most likely disappointment. The Board expanded the repurchase authorization to $30 million, although the report does not say that the full amount was repurchased.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board expanded the share repurchase authorization to $30 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation of the ~$200M residual — only $68M is spoken for. With a $357M market cap, a buyback authorization is the largest single upside surprise available”; “Silence here is the most likely disappointment.”

surprises.description: The preview described about $140 million of provisional BEAD awards and said the program would have no significant impact on 2026. ATN now cited approximately $150 million of funding available within its footprint later this year and into 2027, though the facts do not quantify resulting revenue or earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $150 million of BEAD government broadband funding is available within ATN's Alaska and Southwest footprint later this year and into 2027 to subsidize rural fiber expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “BEAD is going to be more like the coming years. It's not going to have any significant impact on 2026”; the preview also cited “$140M provisional awards.”

surprises.description: ATN disclosed an agreement to sell spectrum licenses for up to $41 million, a potential source of proceeds not identified in the preview. The transaction is expected to close in 2027, so the proceeds are not immediate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed an agreement to sell certain spectrum licenses for up to $41 million (closing expected in 2027).”

in_line: ATN reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance and net capital expenditures of $105 million to $115 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of reiterated FY26 guidance and its stated capex range.

The tower sale produced the expected large one-time GAAP gain and sharply positive reported net income; the preview explicitly warned that headline GAAP EPS would be sharply positive because of the gain and was not a meaningful measure of operating performance.
The reported recurring adjusted EBITDA impact from the tower sale—about $1 million per period—was consistent with the preview’s estimate of roughly $1 million per month of drag.

surprises.description: Black Hills reported adjusted Q2 EPS of $0.54, well above the preview’s $0.40–$0.41 consensus range. The result was driven in part by $0.21 per share from new rates and rider recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted Q2 2026 EPS was $0.54” ... “driven by $0.21 per share of new rates and rider recovery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS” consensus: “$0.40 – $0.41.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects to deliver in the upper half of its 4%–6% long-term growth target. The preview expected guidance to be reaffirmed, but did not anticipate this more optimistic growth-target language.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects to deliver in the upper half of its 4% to 6% long-term growth target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaffirmed $4.25–$4.45, no change” was the preview’s base case.

surprises.description: The 1.8-gigawatt data center project has not reached a definitive agreement, but management is now optimistic about finalizing one in Q3. That is an improvement on the preview’s concern that the June target had passed and its reference to December 31 as the extended milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In advanced negotiations on a 1.8 gigawatt data center project” and “remains optimistic about finalizing definitive agreements in Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “June 30, 2026” target “appears to have passed unmet” and noted “Dec 31 as the extended milestone.”

surprises.description: Despite Crusoe exiting the project, management said negotiations were unaffected because it had been negotiating directly with the hyperscale end user throughout. This addresses the preview’s concern that the customer might waver after Crusoe’s departure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Crusoe's exit from the 1.8 gigawatt project has had no impact on negotiations,” and management had been “negotiating directly with the hyperscale end user throughout.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “customer wavers post-Crusoe” as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: The generation reservation agreement now provides for up to $377 million of refundable customer advances for long-lead equipment, versus the preview’s reference to $201 million of refundable contributions. The larger stated amount strengthens the project’s funding support, though the advances remain refundable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A generation reservation agreement was extended through August 31 and provides for up to $377 million of refundable customer advances funding long-lead generation equipment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “$201M of refundable customer contributions.”

surprises.description: Wyoming Electric’s July peak reached 439 MW, up 16% from the prior-year peak. The preview noted a Q1 peak of 393 MW, up 4%, and identified load growth as a key metric, so the reported peak indicates stronger growth than that earlier data point suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wyoming electric peaked at 439 megawatts in July, a 16% increase over last year's peak.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported “Q1 peak load hit 393 MW (+4%)” and said to watch “weather-normalized load and large-load MW.”

in_line: Black Hills reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.25–$4.45, as the preview’s base case expected.
The 600 MW of data center load included in the financial plan and the pipeline exceeding 3 GW are broadly consistent with the preview’s 600 MW-by-2030 plan and >3 GW pipeline discussion.
The merger still has one remaining approval, with the Montana decision expected in 2026; the preview also described Montana as the only remaining approval and expected the merger to close in 2H26.
Lang II remains on schedule for Q4 2026, as the preview specifically expected it to be on track for that in-service date.
The company issued $50 million of equity via ATM year-to-date, within the preview’s stated $50–$70 million 2026 equity need.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating results per share were $0.75, well below the preview’s $0.85 consensus estimate and down from $0.81 a year ago. The per-share result missed even though revenue grew.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating results per share fell to $0.75 from $0.81.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $0.85.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was essentially flat, below the preview’s roughly $28.0–28.5 million estimate, which implied 4–6% growth. This weak profitability result stands out against the 8.5% revenue increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was essentially flat year-over-year at $27.0 million versus $26.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est.): ~$28.0–28.5M”; the preview also described the base case as “$27.8–28.6M.”

surprises.description: Higher self-insured healthcare costs created an unanticipated $3.2 million year-over-year headwind, with most of it concentrated in Q2. The preview expected operating costs to normalize rather than flagging this sizable cost pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher-than-average self-insured healthcare costs created an approximately $3.2 million year-over-year headwind, roughly 80% of which hit in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided this ‘back to a more normal rate’ on volume leverage.”

surprises.description: USPH hired about 50 clinicians ahead of the NYU Langone transition, bringing costs forward before the related reimbursement begins. The preview anticipated alliance ramp-up but did not identify this near-term staffing burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company front-loaded approximately 50 clinician hires (estimated at over $100,000 each) ahead of the NYU Langone hospital transition, pressuring Q2 margins before reimbursement kicks in.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The NYU Metro and Gulf Coast hospital alliances … ramp sequentially, reaching full quarterly run-rate only in Q4.”

surprises.description: Hospital-affiliation activity was more visible in Q2 than the preview’s base case of de minimis alliance contribution: 31 clinics were integrated and affiliations contributed $5.6 million of PT revenue. The remaining 39 clinics are still expected to integrate in Q3, with a projected Q4 EBITDA impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hospital affiliations contributed $5.6 million to Q2 PT revenue, with 31 clinics integrated in Q2 and the remaining 39 expected to integrate in Q3, projecting a $1.5–2 million EBITDA impact in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “alliances de minimis in Q2”; it also called for clinic-conversion and Q2-contribution details.

surprises.description: Clinic-level volume was stronger than the preview’s hard-comp framing suggested: average daily visits reached a new high of 33.5, above the prior-year record of 32.7, while total visits grew 6.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average daily visits per clinic hit an all-time high of 33.5, up from 32.7 a year ago, while total visits grew 6.6% to 1,662,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Q2'25 set a record at 32.7” and characterized it as “a genuinely hard comp in the seasonal peak.”

surprises.description: Revenue exceeded the preview’s $211.4 million consensus estimate, reaching $214 million. The beat was modest relative to the expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 8.5% to $214 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue: $211.4M.”

surprises.description: USPH maintained its full-year EBITDA range despite Q2 EBITDA of $27 million, below the preview’s estimate and its warning that a result at or below $27 million would make the guidance difficult to achieve. The preview’s base case did expect reaffirmation, so the surprise is against that stated downside warning rather than its central scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $102 million to $106 million despite margin pressures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything at/below $27M leaves >$54.8M needed in H2 … effectively unachievable, which forces a guide cut.” The preview also listed reaffirmation as its base case.

surprises.description: The company repurchased $19.2 million of shares while credit-facility borrowings rose by $59 million from year-end. The preview discussed acquisition funding and the upsized facility, but did not anticipate this combination of buybacks and increased borrowing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased 306,000 shares for $19.2 million, and increased credit facility borrowings to $221 million from $162 million at year-end.”

in_line: Physical therapy revenue per visit was $107.59, just above the preview’s $107.50 confirmation threshold.
The 12-clinic acquisition had been expected to close July 1 and land in Q3; the call reported it completed for $16.4 million.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.45, above both the $0.35 consensus and the $0.39 high end of Q3 guidance; GAAP EPS of $0.32 also exceeded its $0.30 guidance ceiling. This was a substantially stronger earnings result than the preview’s expected $0.37–$0.39 base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EPS was $0.45”; “Q3 GAAP diluted EPS rose 39% year-over-year to $0.32.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP Adj. Diluted EPS” consensus “$0.35” and guidance “$0.30 – $0.39”; GAAP diluted EPS guidance “$0.21 – $0.30.” The preview’s base scenario expected “$0.37–0.39.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $22 million, beating the preview’s $19–$20 million base expectation and exceeding the $20 million top of Q3 guidance. The $22 million result was stronger than the preview’s expected operating leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 30% to $22 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “$19–20M” adjusted EBITDA; Q3 guidance was “$17.0M – $20.0M.”

surprises.description: Retail GMV grew 19%, well above the preview’s expectation of roughly 10% growth, while direct profit rose 30%, around the preview’s 29% expectation. The stronger GMV result was accompanied by a managed direct-to-consumer consignment business that nearly doubled year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The retail (RSCG) segment set records with GMV up 19% to $121.6 million and direct profit up 30%, aided by a managed direct-to-consumer consignment business that nearly doubled year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said RSCG “delivered 10% GMV growth and 29% direct profit growth in Q2” and highlighted RetailRush scaling, with “more than doubling GMV sequentially.”

surprises.description: CAG GMV fell 1% rather than showing the backlog conversion the preview identified as a potential Q3 catalyst. The decline was attributed to project timing, so the anticipated conversion had not yet shown up in GMV.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The capital assets group (CAG) saw GMV decline 1% due to project timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “several hundred million dollars of GMV” in mandates and said “any quantified backlog-to-revenue timeline is a positive catalyst”; it also called Q3 a test of backlog conversion after Q2 GMV growth of only 3%.

surprises.description: Despite CAG’s GMV decline, its direct profit grew 13% as its take rate expanded 270 basis points on stronger pricing and mix. That profit resilience was a positive offset to the weaker-than-hoped project conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct profit grew 13% as its take rate expanded 270 basis points from stronger pricing and mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged CAG backlog conversion and described a “mid-to-high 40%” segment direct-profit margin target, but did not forecast a 270-basis-point take-rate expansion alongside declining GMV.

surprises.description: GovDeals GMV grew 9%, just below the preview’s stated 10% growth checkpoint. The record GMV and strong bidder activity are encouraging, but the segment narrowly missed the preview’s reacceleration threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The GovDeals segment achieved record GMV of $274 million (up 9%), with buyer registrations up 23%, new bidders up 42%, and conversion rates up 35% despite lower marketing spend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist called for “GovDeals GMV growth ≥ 10%.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS guidance has a $0.455 midpoint, above the preview’s $0.43 consensus, and adjusted EBITDA is guided to $22–$25 million. The company also expects its highest annual adjusted EBITDA in 13 years, making the outlook stronger than the preview’s neutral, consensus-bracketing case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal Q4 guidance projects… adjusted EBITDA of $22–25 million, and non-GAAP adjusted EPS of $0.41–0.50, positioning the company for its highest annual adjusted EBITDA in 13 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Q4 guidance “bracketing $0.43” neutral and described “~$0.43” as its base case; it said a midpoint below $0.40 would be a negative outcome.

surprises.description: Management expects Q4 retail GMV and revenue to be lower sequentially, a headwind not identified in the preview’s discussion of a scaling retail channel and peak-season GMV. This qualifies the otherwise strong Q4 company-wide guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 earnings are expected to be pressured by… sequentially lower GMV and revenue in the retail segment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted RSCG’s growth and scaling direct-to-consumer channel, and described the Q4 setup as requiring “both peak seasonal GMV and continued opex leverage.”

surprises.description: The reported revenue-to-GMV ratio was about 28.6% ($129.6 million divided by $453 million), slightly below the preview’s 29% checkpoint. Revenue itself landed within the preview’s $126–$132 million base range, so this is a narrow mix/take-rate shortfall rather than a headline revenue miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated GMV grew 10% year-over-year to a record $453 million, with GAAP revenue up 8% to $129.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist called for “Revenue/GMV ≥ 29%” and said actual take rates had run “29–31%”; its base scenario expected revenue of “$126–132M.”

surprises.description: Cash and short-term investments ended at $231.1 million, above the $204 million cash balance cited in the preview. The company still reported zero debt and $50 million of remaining repurchase authorization, rather than a disclosed new deployment of capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $231.1 million in cash and short-term investments, zero debt, and $50 million remaining in share repurchase authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$204M cash” and “$50M remaining buyback authorization.”

in_line: Consolidated GMV of $453 million was within the preview’s $450–$460 million base-case range.
GAAP revenue of $129.6 million was within the preview’s $126–$132 million base-case range, even though the resulting revenue-to-GMV ratio was slightly below its 29% checkpoint.
RSCG direct profit growth of 30% was close to the preview’s 29% reference point.
The preview explicitly identified a potentially higher tax rate as one possible source of below-the-line pressure; the call reported a Q4 effective tax rate approaching the low-to-mid 30s.
The preview did not expect an aggressive buyback announcement; the call reported $50 million of remaining authorization and did not describe a new repurchase action.

surprises.description: CF reported second-quarter EPS of $4.73, below the preview’s published consensus range of $5.63–$5.71 and further below its $6.00–$6.25 working whisper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-quarter net earnings of $727 million or $4.73 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $5.63 – $5.71”; the preview also says, “Assume a working whisper of $6.00–6.25.”

surprises.description: Yazoo City’s restart has slipped from late 2026 to the first half of 2027 because electrical equipment procurement took longer than expected, extending the outage beyond the timing previously contemplated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Yazoo City complex is now expected to resume operations in the first half of 2027 (delayed from late 2026 due to extended electrical equipment procurement).”

surprises.description: CF raised its mid-cycle outlook: baseline EBITDA is now approximately $2.9 billion and free cash flow $1.7 billion, with strategic initiatives expected to lift mid-cycle EBITDA to about $3.3 billion by 2030. That is more constructive than the preview’s emphasis on falling FY27 earnings and weaker forward fertilizer prices.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its baseline mid-cycle EBITDA expectation to approximately $2.9 billion and free cash flow to $1.7 billion, with strategic initiatives expected to lift mid-cycle EBITDA to approximately $3.3 billion by 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus FY27 EPS is modeled to fall 28% to $11.36 from $15.86 in FY26.”

surprises.description: CF’s mid-cycle NOLA urea price assumption rose by $30 per short ton, from $355 to $385, with most of the increase attributed to higher global capital costs rather than solely to geopolitical changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The mid-cycle NOLA urea price assumption increased from $355 to $385 per short ton, of which about $10 reflects structural geopolitical cost changes and the remainder reflects higher global capital costs.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a substantial second-quarter fixed-cost increase, including higher purchased-ammonia costs and Yazoo-related fixed-cost absorption, neither of which was highlighted as a cost pressure in the preview’s main cost discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-quarter fixed costs rose about $75 million, with roughly $60 million split between higher purchased ammonia costs and Yazoo City-related fixed cost absorption.”

surprises.description: CF disclosed that low-carbon ammonia was already about 10% of first-half ammonia sales volumes and earned a premium above $20 per ton, an additional source of premium-priced sales not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Low carbon ammonia comprised approximately 10% of first-half ammonia sales volumes and earned an average premium of more than $20 per ton.”

surprises.description: Yazoo City is being reconfigured to make ammonium nitrate solution, ammonia, and DEF rather than ammonium nitrate. The preview discussed the outage and restart but did not anticipate this change in product mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “It will be reconfigured to produce ammonium nitrate solution, ammonia and DEF rather than ammonium nitrate.”

surprises.description: CF said approximately 50% of Blue Point construction CapEx is fixed, providing some protection against cost inflation; the preview flagged capex inflation as a risk but did not report this cost protection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Blue Point construction is expected to begin in August with approximately 50% of CapEx fixed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for cost-inflation creep and any incremental low-carbon offtake signings.”

in_line: The quarterly dividend increase to $0.60 per share, up 20%, matched the preview, which already listed a $0.60 quarterly dividend raised by 20%.

High asset utilization was consistent with the preview’s focus on strong operating rates: CF said it ran available ammonia capacity at nearly 98% in the first half, while the preview noted Q1 utilization of 99% of available capacity.

surprises.description: LandBridge’s Q2 revenue was well above the preview’s $60.0 million consensus, and adjusted EBITDA also exceeded the preview’s roughly $52–53 million estimate. Revenue reached $66.8 million and adjusted EBITDA was $59.8 million, with an 89% margin versus the approximately 88% expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $66.8 million”; “Adjusted EBITDA was $59.8 million (89% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus” revenue “$60.00M”; adjusted EBITDA “~$52–53M”; margin “~88%.”

surprises.description: The company reaffirmed its full-year adjusted EBITDA range instead of raising it or narrowing it toward the upper end, as the preview said investors wanted. The preview explicitly characterized a reaffirmation of the full range as soft at this point in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $210–$230 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy side wants $220M+ at the low end”; “a raise to $220–235M or a narrow to the upper half is a genuine positive surprise”; “a reaffirm of the full wide range at this point in the year reads as soft.”

surprises.description: The digital-infrastructure update showed a wider pipeline than the preview had described, with seven counterparties representing more than 10 GW across the footprint. But it stopped short of the hard milestone the preview was watching for: the reported counterparties were still at LOI, option, or late-stage negotiation, and management only expects multiple arrangements to become firm leases by the end of next year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Currently under LOI, option, or in late-stage negotiations with seven power and digital infrastructure counterparties representing more than 10 gigawatts”; management “expects multiple digital infrastructure LOIs and options to convert into firm leases with revenues starting by the end of next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview watched for “option exercise or conversion to a definitive long-term lease, named power partners or hyperscaler counterparties” and said specific commitments, not adjectives, would matter.

surprises.description: The corporate-conversion process advanced beyond the preview’s expectation that the committee was still evaluating the idea: the board unanimously approved conversion to a Texas corporation. The approval could support index eligibility, although the call facts do not establish that inclusion itself has been secured.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The board unanimously approved converting LandBridge from a Delaware LLC to a Texas corporation to enable potential index eligibility (S&P, Russell, CRISP) and broaden its investor base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the board had formed a special committee “to evaluate converting” and identified a recommendation or timeline as a catalyst, noting “no assurance of recommendation, completion, or inclusion.”

surprises.description: Net leverage improved to the top of the company’s stated target range, rather than remaining at the preview’s reported 2.7x, and liquidity was higher than the preview’s $259.7 million figure. This was a better balance-sheet update than the preview’s starting point implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved to 2.5x from 2.7x last quarter, with total liquidity of $269.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “2.7x net leverage vs. a stated 2.0–2.5x target” and “$259.7M liquidity.”

surprises.description: After quarter-end, LandBridge increased its revolving-credit capacity and lowered its borrowing cost, developments the preview had not anticipated. The added capacity and 25-basis-point cost reduction are favorable financing terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “After quarter-end, the company expanded its revolving credit facility from $275 million to $375 million (with capacity to reach $475 million) and cut borrowing costs by 25 basis points.”

surprises.description: The prevailing royalty rate for new produced-water facilities rose from 14 cents to 15 cents per barrel, and management expects further increases as pore space becomes scarcer. The preview did not flag a rate increase or this pricing outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The prevailing produced water royalty rate for new facilities is now $0.15 per barrel (up from 14 cents), with management expecting rates to keep rising as pore space scarcity intensifies along the state line.”

in_line: Oil and gas royalties remained a small part of the business: they were about 5% of Q2 revenue, close to the preview’s 6% Q1 share and its framing of commodity royalties as a limited swing factor.

surprises.description: Revenue was $71.3 million, well above the preview’s roughly $65.6–66.0 million expectation. Organic growth was 17%, also far stronger than the preview’s estimate of 6%, while FlackTek contributed about the expected amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue rose 29% year-over-year to a record $71.3 million, with 17% organic growth after excluding FlakTek's $6.6 million contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $65.60M” consensus; the base case estimated “$66.0M” revenue and “+6% YoY organic,” with “~$7M” from FlackTek.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.49, beating the preview’s approximately $0.40 estimate by $0.09. The preview highlighted uncertainty about whether consensus EPS was GAAP or adjusted; the reported GAAP EPS of $0.33 was above its own approximately $0.30 estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 9% to $0.49”; GAAP net income was $3.9 million, or “$0.33/share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adjusted EPS ~ $0.40” and “GAAP EPS ~ $0.30,” while noting that “it is not clear whether the $0.40 is GAAP or adjusted.”

surprises.description: Space revenue rose 86% and orders reached $14.4 million at a 2.3x book-to-bill, turning the preview’s conversion-year watchpoint into a strong early ramp. Management also characterized the resulting revenue level as a new sustainable run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Space revenue surged 86% year-over-year with orders of $14.4 million and a 2.3x book-to-bill,” which management called “a new sustainable revenue run rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 space revenue was “flat” despite orders surging “+76%,” and that “FY27 was framed as the conversion year”; it warned that flat Q1 revenue would make the year riskier.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 25%, above the preview’s 24.0% Q1 estimate and at the threshold it said was needed to support the full-year bridge. The year-over-year decline was expected, but the reported margin was stronger than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 25% from 26.5% a year ago due to higher lower-margin defense mix,” while improving “230 basis points sequentially from Q4 fiscal 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “Gross margin 24.0%” and said Q1 needed to “print ≥24% to make the full-year bridge credible.”

surprises.description: Backlog reached $557 million, exceeding the preview’s $530 million watch level and the top of its $525–540 million base-case range. It set a sixth consecutive record rather than merely holding above the prior record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog reached a sixth consecutive record of $557 million, up 15% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Watch: does backlog hold above $530M?” and gave a base-case range of “$525–540M,” with a bull-case record above “$540M.”

surprises.description: Operating cash outflow was $12.7 million, materially larger than the prior-year Q1 outflow cited in the preview as the seasonal benchmark. The preview anticipated soft cash flow from bonus timing, but the reported use was substantially deeper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating activities used $12.7 million of cash in the quarter due to billing/collection timing and bonus payments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a soft Q1 OCF is seasonally normal” and cited Q1 FY26 operating cash flow of “negative $2.3M on bonus timing.”

in_line: Fiscal 2027 guidance was reaffirmed at $285–295 million of revenue and $35–40 million of adjusted EBITDA, as the preview expected stability rather than an increase or cut.
Adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.3%, close to the preview’s 12.1% estimate.
The $50 million strategic investment, debt repayment, and resulting net-cash position were consistent with the preview’s expectation of a net-cash balance after the proceeds.
Fiscal 2027 capex guidance of $18–22 million matched the preview.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.39, above the preview’s $1.26 headline consensus and $1.32 whisper. The beat was positive but smaller against the higher whisper than against consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net earnings were $370 million or $1.39 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat $1.26 as the headline bar and ~$1.32 as the whisper.”

surprises.description: Title earnings conversion was stronger than the preview’s base case: the 17.8% margin exceeded its 16.0–16.5% expectation, and adjusted pretax title earnings of $448 million were above its projected $390–405 million range. The margin also cleared the preview’s 17.0%+ bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted pretax title earnings of $448 million in Q2 2026” and “an industry-leading adjusted pretax title margin of 17.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case: 16.0–16.5%” and “Bull … Title margin 17.0%+”; the base case projected “title earnings ~$390–405M.”

surprises.description: Instead of only reiterating or firming the annual margin outlook, management guided to modest compression in the second half relative to Q2. That tempers the strong Q2 margin result, though the call facts do not say the 15–20% full-year range was withdrawn.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to modest compression in adjusted pretax title margin in the second half of 2026 relative to Q2,” citing front-loaded recruiting and acquisition expenses ahead of revenue ramp.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had reaffirmed the “15–20% annual range” and identified a bull signal as “a reiterated (or firmed) 15–20% margin range.”

surprises.description: F&G contributed only $65 million to Q2 adjusted net earnings, well below the preview’s $85–95 million base case. Its share of FNF’s first-half adjusted net earnings was also 23%, below the preview’s roughly 32% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “F&G's adjusted net earnings contribution to the segment declined to $65 million from $89 million in Q2 2025”; F&G contributed “23% of the first-half total,” down from 32% a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “F&G ~$85–95M” and described F&G as “now ~32% of consolidated adjusted earnings.”

surprises.description: Commercial title activity appears to have run ahead of the preview’s expected Q2 range. The reported first-half total of $778 million, less the preview’s stated Q1 result of $338 million, implies about $440 million for Q2, above the $380–400 million Q2 expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct commercial revenue reached $778 million in the first six months, up 24% over $626 million in the first half of 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for FNF commercial revenue of $380–400M vs. $333M last year”; the preview also reported Q1 direct commercial revenue of $338M.

surprises.description: F&G’s AUM grew more slowly than the preview anticipated: $74.7 billion and 8% year-over-year growth, versus an expectation of about $75 billion and 11% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “F&G's assets under management before reinsurance grew 8% year-over-year to $74.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AUM ~$75B before flow reinsurance (+11%).”

surprises.description: F&G announced a formal process to explore strategic alternatives for Peak Altitude, an event the preview did not identify as a likely catalyst. Management’s preference for a 51% partner and use of proceeds to grow the core business rather than pursue M&A makes the potential outcome and shareholder benefit uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “F&G has launched a formal process to explore strategic alternatives for its Peak Altitude distribution unit” after nearly $700 million invested and with $80 million of 2025 EBITDA; management favors a “51% partner structure” and says proceeds would likely go toward growing the core business over M&A.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Capital return and F&G stake strategy” as a catalyst and said “Any further F&G distribution or accelerated buyback” was the most plausible narrative-shift catalyst.

in_line: The refi order fade was broadly as previewed: the preview said the Q1 refi tailwind would not repeat at the same intensity, and reported refinance orders fell 22% from Q1 as mortgage rates rose.
Purchase-order trends were broadly consistent with the preview’s view that volume risk was largely retired: daily purchase orders were up 7% sequentially and 4% year-over-year in July.

surprises.description: Matador exceeded the high end of its Q2 production guidance, then raised its full-year oil-growth outlook to 4%–7% while reducing capital expenditures by 1%. The preview’s base case expected FY volumes to be held, with a further guidance increase only in its bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Matador exceeded the high end of its production guidance and raised full-year year-over-year oil growth guidance to a range of 4% to 7% while simultaneously reducing capital expenditures by 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “FY26 volumes held”; “Bull” scenario: “FY26 guide raised again.”

surprises.description: Despite generating $303 million of Q2 free cash flow, Matador now expects about $900 million for the full year, below the preview’s expected reaffirmation of roughly $1.0 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Matador generated near-record adjusted free cash flow of $303 million in Q2 2026 and expects to generate approximately $900 million in free cash flow for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 Adjusted FCF — guided $1.1–1.2B in May, cut to ~$1.0B on July 23. Does it hold at current strip?” The base case expected “~$1.0B AFCF reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Matador has already used $200 million of Q2 cash flow to reduce acquisition-related RBL borrowing from $1.25 billion to below $1 billion, and expects the debt to be largely repaid by year-end. That is a faster paydown path than the preview’s 12–18-month leverage target after the acquisition closes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company used $200 million of the quarter's cash flow to pay down acquisition-related bank debt, reducing the RBL borrowing from $1.25 billion to under $1 billion, and expects it largely repaid by year-end.” Management also “targets monthly debt repayment of roughly $100 million at current prices” and considers “$70/barrel oil” sufficient to remain profitable.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management targets ~1.0x leverage within 12–18 months of close — any slippage in that framing is the bear trigger.”

surprises.description: The quarter included a significant marketing gain that management said was non-recurring, an earnings-quality caveat not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of the quarter’s price and gas-realization drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The quarter included a significant marketing gain that management characterized as non-recurring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on realized gas pricing as “the single largest swing factor” and described the base case as “realized gas ~$0.30/Mcf”; it did not flag a one-time marketing gain.

surprises.description: Matador disclosed projected returns above 80% on newly acquired assets, compared with above 50% on existing assets, citing high-quality rock, 15%–20% higher oil EURs, and 12.5% federal royalties. The preview discussed acquisition acreage but did not anticipate this return differential.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Newly acquired assets are projected to deliver rates of return above 80%, compared to over 50% on existing assets, driven by high-quality rock, 15%-20% higher oil EURs, and low 1/8 (12.5%) federal royalty rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Paloma acquisition’s acreage, production, reserves, and locations, but gave no projected return comparison.

surprises.description: Matador expects well costs on the new federal acreage to fall to about $600 per foot through batch development and longer laterals, an operational cost outlook not included in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Well costs on the new federal acreage are expected to fall to approximately $600 per foot, aided by batch development across 9 or more benches and longer laterals.”

surprises.description: The BLM lease sale extended inventory life to more than 15 years, with drilling potentially starting by late 2026 or early 2027 across nine zones. The preview discussed Woodford optionality and the Rae’s Creek well but did not anticipate this inventory-life extension or drilling timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The BLM federal lease sale extended inventory life to over 15 years, with management drilling potentially beginning as early as end of 2026 or early 2027 across acreage featuring 9 different zones.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Woodford / Ridge Runner optionality” and asked investors to watch for a follow-up well program or 2027 capital allocation, but did not give this inventory-life or timing outlook.

surprises.description: Drilling efficiency on three-mile laterals improved from roughly 20 days to about 10 days, a substantial operational improvement not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Drilling efficiency on 3-mile laterals improved from roughly 20 days to about 10 days.”

surprises.description: Matador reported a 5% increase in oil and natural gas reserves during the quarter, from 667 million to 703 million BOE; the preview did not discuss a quarterly reserve change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oil and natural gas reserves grew 5% during the quarter, rising from 667 million to 703 million barrels of oil equivalent.”

in_line: Management’s expectation of improved natural-gas realizations from the early Hugh Brinson pipeline startup and Energy Transfer arrangements was consistent with the preview’s focus on the early pipeline startup and potential gas uplift.
The Rae’s Creek exploratory well tested above 2,200 barrels, in line with the preview, which already reported that the well had tested above 2,200 BOE/d.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $172 million, above the preview's $162.8 million consensus by about 5.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total sales rose 17% year-over-year to a record $172 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2'26 Consensus | $162.80M”

surprises.description: Loar raised its 2026 sales, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS guidance, with the new sales range above the preview's bull-case range and the EPS range above the prior guide and Street estimate. The higher outlook is a stronger raise than the preview's base-case scenario anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its calendar 2026 guidance to net sales of $665M-$675M, adjusted EBITDA of $265M-$270M (~40% margin), and adjusted EPS of $1.32-$1.36, up from $1.26-$1.30 prior.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull” scenario: “FY guide to ~$658–668M / EPS $1.32–1.36”; “Base” scenario: “FY guide nudged to ~$650–660M.” The preview listed Street sales at “$653.67M” and adjusted EPS at “$1.30.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects to “meet or beat” the high end of the newly raised annual guidance. That suggests a more confident, potentially conservative outlook than the preview's focus on whether Loar would raise enough to clear a Street already near the prior guide's top end.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management framed guidance as a figure they expect to “meet or beat” at the high end, with first-half sales and adjusted EBITDA growth of approximately 38% and 47%, respectively.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A merely in-line quarter with a reaffirmed guide is a de-facto disappointment”; “The buy-side is underwriting another raise.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged Harper's initial margin dilution as a risk, but management reported that all three recent acquisitions—Beadlight, LMB, and Harper—are performing ahead of expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All three recent acquisitions (Beadlight, LMB, Harper) are performing ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Harper Engineering … was called ‘significantly dilutive’ to margins initially”; the preview also said to watch whether “Harper integration is pulling margin toward the ~40% FY target.”

surprises.description: The company said about $200 million of its organic pipeline had converted into secured initial orders, an update beyond the preview's expectation of simply seeing the pipeline grow. The orders are purchase-order based rather than long-term agreements, which qualifies the strength of the conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The organic new business pipeline totals approximately $750 million of revenue potential over five years (up ~$50M from May), with ~$200 million now converted to secured initial orders”; the orders are “on a purchase-order basis (not long-term agreements).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Another sequential increase is the cheapest credibility signal management can deliver.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date free cash flow was about 1.9 times reported net income while capital expenditure remained around 3% of sales. The preview discussed leverage and possible M&A but did not set an expectation for cash conversion or capex.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex) reached approximately 1.9x reported net income, with capex held at ~3% of sales (~$20M).”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 40.5%, at the preview's expected 40.0–40.5% base-case range and matching the Q1 record; the preview identified 41%+ as the bull-case threshold.
Defense returned to growth at 8%, consistent with the preview's call for a positive Q2 inflection after Q1's decline.
The five-year organic pipeline increased to about $750 million from $700 million in May, consistent with the preview's expectation of another sequential increase.

surprises.description: Cheniere raised 2026 EBITDA guidance to $7.9–$8.4 billion and DCF guidance to $5.3–$5.8 billion, above the preview’s expected ranges; the new low end is higher than the previous high end for both metrics. The preview expected incremental upside to come mostly from optimization, but management attributed most of the quantified increase to higher production and locking in open volumes, with $100–$150 million from optimization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second consecutive quarter to $7.9-$8.4 billion consolidated adjusted EBITDA and $5.3-$5.8 billion DCF, with the new low end exceeding the previous high end for both metrics.” The increase included “roughly $300 million from a 0.5 million-tonne production increase, $200 million from locking in open volumes and higher Henry Hub, and $100-$150 million from optimization activities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave FY26 guidance of “$7.25–7.75B” EBITDA and “$4.75–5.25B” DCF; its bull scenario expected “$7.6–8.0B” EBITDA and “$5.0–5.4B” DCF. It also said “the incremental lever is mostly optimization/trading, not spot exposure.”

surprises.description: Cheniere signed a $4.7 billion turnkey EPC contract for Sabine Pass Phase 1 and has financing underway, a concrete project-development step not anticipated in the preview. The expected early-2027 FID timing itself remained consistent with the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed a ~$4.7 billion lump-sum turnkey EPC contract with Bechtel for Sabine Pass Phase 1,” adding “over 6 million tonnes per annum (~10% platform growth),” with “FID expected early 2027 and financing already underway.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “LNTP guided for late 2026, FID early 2027” for the next growth leg; it did not anticipate a signed EPC contract or financing already underway.

surprises.description: The mid-scale Corpus Christi Trains 8 and 9 were further along than expected: they were over 48% complete versus 37% at Q1 in the preview, while still ahead of schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mid-scale Trains 8 and 9 are over 48% complete and ahead of schedule.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the trains were “37% complete at Q1” and “tracking ahead of schedule.”

surprises.description: Management said the $8-plus-billion EBITDA level can be sustained even when marketing margins normalize to $2.50–$3, rather than depending on today’s unusually high margins. The preview did not anticipate this specific normalized-margin run-rate claim.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects the “$8+ billion EBITDA level to be sustainable run-rate even at normalized $2.50-$3 marketing margins (versus current $10-$13), rather than a one-off tied to elevated LNG prices.”

surprises.description: Cheniere designated most IPM volumes for normal-purchase/normal-sale accounting, which management said would remove mark-to-market derivative swings from those volumes and reduce the number of negative-net-income quarters in the historical comparison. The preview warned that derivatives distorted GAAP results but did not anticipate this accounting change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company designated normal-purchase/normal-sale accounting for ~75% of IPM volumes starting mid-June,” which “will eliminate mark-to-market derivative swings and would have cut negative net income quarters since 2021 from six to two.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described GAAP EPS as “dominated by non-cash mark-to-market on IPM gas supply derivatives” and said “Do not trade the EPS line”; it did not mention a change in accounting treatment.

surprises.description: The Strait of Hormuz disruption and resulting shift in LNG flows were not anticipated in the preview: Qatar and UAE exports fell, U.S. exports to Asia reached a record, and Europe faced a large storage deficit. Those conditions are supportive of demand for Cheniere’s exports, though the disruption itself makes the market backdrop mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: The disruption “cut Qatar/UAE exports by ~18 million tonnes in the quarter, drove U.S. exports to Asia to a record ~11 million tonnes, and left Europe with an ~11 Bcm storage deficit that management expects will struggle to reach even 70% fullness before winter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed softened TTF and JKM prices and an Asia premium, but did not anticipate a Hormuz-related supply disruption or its reported export and storage effects.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $1.8 billion and DCF of $1.2 billion were within the preview’s estimates of about $1.70 billion and $1.10–$1.20 billion, respectively.
Q2 exports of 672 TBtu across 184 cargoes were within the preview’s estimates of 660–690 TBtu and 180–190 cargoes.
Full-year production guidance of 53–54 million tonnes matched the preview’s expected 53–54 million tonnes.

Train 6 was substantially completed in June and Train 7 was commissioning, consistent with the preview’s expectation of Train 6 first LNG in Q2 and Train 7 beginning production around early August; the preview also identified Train 7 completion in Aug/Sep as a possible upside case.
The early-2027 FID timing was consistent with the preview’s expected early-2027 FID framing.

Q2 repurchases of about $550 million were broadly consistent with a steady pace after the preview cited about $535 million in Q1; the preview’s accelerated-buyback bull case was above $600 million per quarter.

surprises.description: Chord generated $414 million of adjusted free cash flow in Q2, which the call said exceeded expectations. The preview anticipated a strong quarter but did not give a consensus FCF estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Generated adjusted free cash flow of $414 million in Q2 2026, exceeding expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call states that Q2 adjusted free cash flow exceeded expectations.

surprises.description: Chord returned $220 million, or 54% of adjusted FCF, in Q2—a firmer payout than the preview's concern that management might taper repurchases and prioritize the balance sheet. The preview expected at least a 50% return under the stated framework, so the result was above that floor, though the call did not break out the repurchase amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Returned 54% ($220 million) to shareholders via base dividends and share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a sub-$75M buyback quarter would confirm that deleveraging now outranks returns,” and described the framework as “≥50% of adj. FCF returned at leverage <1.0x.”

surprises.description: The reported oil-volume result was at the high end of company guidance, but fell short of the preview's 166–168 MBopd functional whisper; Chord also held full-year guidance at 161,000 bpd rather than delivering the second raise the preview identified as a catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oil production came in at the high end of guidance” and full-year oil volume guidance “was maintained at 161,000 barrels per day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put the functional whisper at “~166–168 MBopd” and said to watch for “a second FY oil guidance raise.”

surprises.description: Chord raised full-year LOE guidance to $10.30/BOE, near the top of the preview's stated $9.55–$10.35/BOE range, reflecting higher workover, non-operated, and production-enhancement costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year LOE expense guidance was raised to $10.30 per BOE,” reflecting “higher workover costs, and increased non-operated LOE.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 LOE guidance as “$9.55–10.35/Boe.”

surprises.description: Although Bakken crude traded at a premium to WTI in Q2, Chord expects that premium to fade and now guides differentials to just below WTI. That is less favorable than the preview's expectation that the differential would tighten toward flat or a premium.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bakken crude traded at premiums to WTI during Q2 2026,” but the company “now guides differentials to just below WTI as the premium is expected to fade over the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the differential historically “tightens ... toward flat or a premium” and identified “≤ −$1.00/bbl” as a potential beat driver.

surprises.description: The hedge update showed 38% of second-half 2026 oil volumes hedged, the same coverage level the preview cited before the release, rather than reporting a higher 2H percentage after the preview flagged possible additions. Coverage for 2027 did rise from the preview's 14% figure to about 18%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hedged approximately 38% of its second-half 2026 oil volumes and about 18% of 2027 volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “~38% of oil ... hedged for balance of 2026” and “~14% oil for 2027,” and asked whether management had layered on hedges in April/May.

surprises.description: Chord reported successful execution of the basin's first trimulfrac and said it could make up 20%–50% of next year's development program, offering a potential completion-cost reduction that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Successfully executed the basin's first trimulfrac, which could represent 20% to 50% of next year's development program to reduce completion costs.”

in_line: The 75%-or-more target for shareholder returns in Q3 and Q4 is consistent with the preview's stated framework of 75%+ returns below 0.5x leverage.
Four-mile well performance and cycle times remained in line with expectations as the program scaled, matching the preview's focus on the four-mile program.
Dropping a frac crew and reducing capital spending in the second half was anticipated: the preview said management had flagged a midyear spot frac crew drop.

surprises.description: The preview expected fuel-supply economics of about +2 cpg overall, with core contribution around 2.5 cpg and a possible inventory drag. Murphy instead said the controllables portion alone earned over 7 cpg, a substantially stronger result for that component than the preview’s core estimate suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The controllables portion of the fuel supply business earned over $0.07 per gallon this quarter,” reflecting “the advantage of Murphy's supply assets during the current supply-constrained environment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Fuel supply segment cpg (and inventory revaluation split)”: “+2 cpg (core ~2.5, mark ~-0.5 to -3).”

surprises.description: The preview looked for elevated fuel margins and cited further margin expansion as a possible Q3 tailwind, but management’s back-half all-in fuel-margin guide was about 35 cpg and described as intentionally conservative. That is cautious guidance relative to the high-30s margins reported for early August, though management sees upside if prices fall for an extended period.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided to “an all-in fuel margin of approximately $0.35 per gallon for the back half of the year,” characterized as “intentionally conservative with upside if prices fall for an extended period.” The first five days of August had margins “in the high 30s cents per gallon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said July/August QTD margins in the “high-30s/40s cpg” would support the bull case and noted that lower expected Q3 gasoline prices “historically supports further margin expansion.”

surprises.description: Merchandise contribution is now expected toward the low end of guidance, below the preview’s roughly $230 million estimate. Management cited consumer budget pressure and the lingering effect of Q1 storm closures, rather than the preview’s modeled merchandise growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merchandise contribution is expected to land toward the low end of the guidance range due to consumer budget pressures and Q1 weather impacts that closed up to half the network during winter storms.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated merchandise contribution of “~$230M” and described the base case as “merch ~$230M.”

surprises.description: New-store deliveries are expected near 45 units, the bottom of the 45–55-unit range, rather than tracking more broadly toward the preview’s on-track view. Management said the upper end depended on tuck-in acquisitions that are not in the current pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New store (NTI) deliveries will come in closer to 45 units at the lower end of guidance,” because “the high end assumed tuck-in acquisitions that are not currently in the pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “45–55 NTIs + up to 30 raze-and-rebuilds guided for FY26” and described the unit-growth outlook as “On track.”

surprises.description: Capital spending is trending to the high end of the guided range, with spending pulled forward and additional life-cycle and land-bank investment. The preview gave the $475–525 million range and expected the plan to be on track, but did not anticipate these specific spending drivers or the high-end trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CapEx is trending to the high end of the range” due to “pulling forward 2027 store construction, proactive life-cycle investments, and land bank investment”; new stores take about three years to reach full profitability ramp.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “capex $475–525M” and characterized the unit-growth outlook as “On track.”

surprises.description: Management described fuel-supply tightness from the geopolitical conflict as persisting well into next year, rather than quickly normalizing. The preview discussed the ceasefire and resumption-of-traffic news behind the price decline but did not anticipate this prolonged-tightness outlook; the implications are mixed because tight conditions also benefit Murphy’s supply assets.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management believes “fuel supply tightness from the geopolitical conflict will not normalize until well into next year” and “does not expect a quick resolution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Brent decline as driven by “ceasefire/resumption-of-traffic news” and framed the quarter around the resulting price waterfall.

in_line: Q2 same-store fuel volume growth of 0.5% was within the preview’s flat-to-+1.5% estimate.
Early-August volume growth of 1.5% and margins in the high 30s were consistent with the preview’s anticipated positive July/August margin color.

The Q3 nicotine promotional-comp headwind was already flagged in the preview; management’s expectation that nicotine remains a second-half tailwind is consistent with the preview’s discussion of nicotine strength.

Loyalty sign-ups above $600,000 per month were broadly consistent with the preview’s reference to roughly $600,000 of sign-ups in March and its focus on whether loyalty gains would translate into fuel-volume growth.

surprises.description: Revenue was just over $51 million, well below the preview’s $58.7–$59.0 million consensus range—roughly a 13% shortfall, despite 48% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue rose 48% year-over-year to just over $51 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026 Consensus | $58.7 – $59.0M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $34 million, below the preview’s roughly $40 million estimate. The 49% year-over-year increase still fell about 15% short of that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 49% to $34 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$40M (my est., no published consensus).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.57, below the preview’s $0.68–$0.78 estimate range. Separately, GAAP EPS of $0.72 was slightly below the stated $0.75 consensus, though the preview cautioned that the consensus accounting basis was unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income reached $21 million ($0.57 per share)” and “Net income was approximately $27 million ($0.72 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimates: … Adj. EPS $0.68–0.78”; the preview also lists “EPS | $0.75” and says it is unclear whether that figure is GAAP or adjusted.

surprises.description: Realized gas price fell to $1.36 per Mcf, far below the preview’s $2.30–$2.55 estimate. The preview anticipated soft gas pricing, but the reported price was substantially weaker than that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Realized natural gas prices fell sharply to $1.36 per Mcf from $3.13 in the prior quarter due to widening regional differentials.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gas … Q2E Realized $2.30–2.55/Mcf”; the preview attributed its estimate to “HH ~$2.94 less Mid-Con discount.”

surprises.description: Production of 19.7 Mboe per day came in just above the preview’s estimated 18.5–19.5 Mboe per day range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 production grew 11% year-over-year to 19.7 Mboe per day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Production | ~18.5–19.5 MBoe/d (my est.).”

surprises.description: SandRidge paid another $0.20 special dividend alongside its regular dividend, following the prior quarter’s special, rather than the preview’s base-case expectation of maintaining only the $0.13 regular dividend. It also declared the regular $0.13 dividend for August.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SandRidge paid $10.6 million in dividends during the quarter, including a 13-cent regular dividend and a 20-cent special dividend, and declared another 13-cent dividend for August 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “base dividend $0.13 maintained, no special,” and said “A second consecutive special says the cash engine is intact.”

surprises.description: A step-out well below the Cherokee Shale delivered a strong result and pointed to possible stacked-pay development, an opportunity the preview did not identify as an upcoming catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A step-out well testing a sub-member below the Cherokee Shale delivered a 90-day average rate of approximately 11,000 Mcfe per day and over 1 Bcf cumulative production after 100 days, opening potential stacked-pay development.”

surprises.description: The 2026 plan now calls for completing nine operated Cherokee wells, one more than the eight completions the preview expected, while retaining the expected 10-well drilling program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2026 capital program is budgeted at $76 million to $97 million to drill 10 operated Cherokee wells (completing nine).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 2026 program is one rig, 10 operated Cherokee wells drilled, 8 completed, 2 rolling into 2027.”

surprises.description: Management said the $76–$97 million 2026 capital program is fully funded by operating cash flow, a reassuring funding statement against the preview’s warning that Q1 free cash flow was negative and the company was not self-funding quarter after quarter at low prices.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2026 capital program is budgeted at $76 million to $97 million … fully funded by operating cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q1 free cash flow was −$1.1M — this is not a self-funding quarter-in, quarter-out story at low prices.”

in_line: Realized oil price was $95.35 per barrel, at the top end of the preview’s $88–$95 estimate.
The roughly 30% of 2026 guided production hedged was consistent with the preview’s estimate of just under 30%; the reported 43% oil and 37% gas hedge coverage also matched the preview.
The $0.13 regular dividend was maintained, as the preview’s base case expected.
The Cherokee acquisition’s 7,000 net acres and 21 well interests matched the preview’s description of the deal.

surprises.description: DXP reported Q2 sales of $576.5 million, 6.2% above the $543 million consensus in the preview. The result was also in line with the preview’s estimate that holding April’s sales pace through the quarter would produce about $576 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total sales grew 15.6% year-over-year to $576.5 million, with organic sales up 11.1% and acquisitions contributing $49.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $543.0M”; the preview also said, “holding April's pace all quarter implies ~ $576M revenue (+15.5%).”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $1.76, about 11% above the preview’s $1.59 consensus and above its base-case range of $1.60–$1.70. The result was close to, but just below, the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS rose to $1.76 from $1.43 in Q2 2025, with net income increasing to $28.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS $1.59”; the base scenario expected “$1.60–1.70.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $70.4 million versus the preview’s estimated $62 million, and the 12.2% margin exceeded its roughly 11.4% consensus estimate. That is a stronger profitability result than the preview’s base case of an 11.4%–11.7% margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $70.4 million with margins expanding to a record 12.2%, up from 11.5% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$62M (est.)”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~11.4%.” The base scenario expected “EBITDA margin 11.4–11.7%.”

surprises.description: IPS sales grew 52.6%, with organic growth of 13.3%, rather than the project-timing downside highlighted in the preview. Acquisitions supplied $47 million of IPS sales, so the surge was partly acquired, but organic growth was still strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Innovative Pumping Solutions segment surged 52.6% year-over-year to $142.7 million, though $47 million came from acquisitions with organic IPS growth of 13.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “IPS project timing slips right” in its bear scenario and said a “backlog decline here reframes the whole 2H setup even on a Q2 beat.”

surprises.description: Water and wastewater had a larger role in IPS than the preview quantified: it was approaching 70% of segment sales and was identified as supporting the record EBITDA margin. The preview expected the 15th consecutive quarter of DXP Water sequential growth, but did not anticipate this pronounced mix contribution to margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water and wastewater is now approaching 70% of IPS segment sales, driving the higher-margin mix that supported the record EBITDA margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a 15th consecutive quarter of sequential water growth would “sustain[] the secular story that supports the multiple.”

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow reached $56 million, a substantial improvement from the preview’s discussion of Q1 cash generation and its concern that M&A had consumed most YTD capital deployment. The preview provided no first-half FCF estimate, so the size of the result was not explicitly forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half 2026 free cash flow reached $56 million, a sharp reversal from negative $8.6 million in the prior year period, with trailing four-quarter free cash flow of $118.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 FCF of “$26.3M” and said “FCF conversion … and working capital … matter because M&A consumed 95% of YTD capital deployment.”

surprises.description: DXP completed four acquisitions in the first half, more than the preview’s stated expectation of one to two acquisitions before the end of Q2. The higher pace supports growth but also means more acquisition spending and integration activity than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DXP completed four acquisitions in the first half for $135.6 million total consideration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “1 to 2 acquisitions before the second quarter ends.”

surprises.description: DXP also completed the Mico Limited deal to establish a Canadian DXP Water presence, a geographic beachhead not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of the expected Mequipco transaction. The deal was funded with cash and stock.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plus the Mico Limited deal (funded with cash and stock) to establish a DXP Water beachhead in Canada.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified Mequipco as “signed August 1” and described it as “a Q3 event”; it did not mention Mico Limited or a Canadian beachhead.

surprises.description: DXP’s credit profile was stronger than the preview’s leverage concern suggested: secured leverage was 2.31x versus the 2.6x Q1 figure, and S&P upgraded the issuer rating from B to B+. The preview had flagged leverage and balance-sheet capacity as items to watch but did not anticipate the rating upgrade.
surprises.fact_evidence: “S&P Global upgraded DXP's issuer credit rating to B+ from B,” and the company reported “$374.5 million in total liquidity with a secured leverage ratio of 2.31x and $842.5 million in total debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch secured leverage vs. the 2.6x base and the ≤3.5x net target” and raised the question of whether stock consideration signaled “the balance sheet is tightening.”

in_line: DXP Water posted its 15th consecutive quarter of sequential growth, as the preview specifically said a 15th quarter would sustain the water-growth story.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating loss was $4.6 million, worse than the preview’s expected $2.0–$3.0 million company-guidance range and roughly $2.5 million consensus loss. Management attributed $1.7 million of pressure to unexpected French employer payroll taxes tied to RSU vesting as the stock price rose.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating loss was $4.6 million” and was “pressured by $1.7 million in unexpected French employer payroll taxes tied to RSU vesting amid a rising stock price.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. loss” company guide “$(2.0)–$(3.0)M”; consensus “~$(2.5)M.”

surprises.description: Management described the first non-GAAP operating profit as possible “as early as Q4,” which is less firm on timing than the preview’s expectation of profitability “by Q4 2026.” The profitability path remains in view, but the phrasing leaves more room for it to occur later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to report its first non-GAAP operating profit as early as Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has guided to non-GAAP profitability by Q4 2026”; the preview also said “Any language softening the Q4 breakeven commitment is a de-rating event.”

surprises.description: Royalties remained strong over the trailing year, but they dipped slightly sequentially because of a customer’s supply-chain issues. The preview highlighted continued royalty growth and expansion in large royalty reporters, but did not anticipate a sequential dip.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month royalties hit a record $8.6 million, growing 65% year-over-year, though royalties showed a slight sequential dip due to a customer's supply chain issues.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TTM $7.9M, +67% Y/Y”; the preview said to “watch both the quarterly royalty dollar figure and whether the >$1M reporter count expands again.”

surprises.description: RPO reached a new high of $135 million, up from the $118.3 million Q1 baseline cited in the preview; just over half is expected to convert to revenue within 12 months. The preview gave no Q2 RPO expectation, so the record level was not specifically anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligation (RPO) reached an all-time high of $135 million, with just over half expected to be recognized as revenue in the next 12 months.”

surprises.description: The company ended the quarter with $123 million in cash after completing an ATM that raised about $72 million net, a substantial change from the preview’s cited $41.9 million of cash and investments. The added liquidity is positive, though it came from issuing shares.
