U.S. sales returned to growth at 3%, in line with the preview’s focus on a flat-to-positive U.S. trajectory.
Core Collectibles grew 9%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the segment would continue growing, although the preview highlighted stronger prior-quarter momentum.
The $19 million sale of the IEEPA tariff claims was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that Funko might monetize its roughly $20 million of claims.
Europe remained a strong growth region, consistent with the preview’s expectation that European strength would continue.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in below the preview’s roughly $4.1 million consensus estimate, at $3.9 million. That was about 45% year-over-year growth, below the preview’s expected 52%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $3.9 million, up approximately 45% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Q2 cash burn of $7.9 million was above the preview’s implied quarterly pace of roughly $6.5–7 million, though it remained just below the preview’s roughly $8 million risk threshold and full-year burn guidance was maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net cash burn excluding financing improved to $7.9 million in Q2” and “full-year cash burn guidance maintained at $26-28 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Plan burn implies ~$6.5–7M/quarter” and “Burn above ~$8M ... reopens the dilution question.”

surprises.description: The company raised $10.6 million net through its ATM, leaving $43.5 million in cash and extending runway into 2028. The preview instead modeled a clean Q2 exit around $34–35 million, so the higher cash balance came with unanticipated equity issuance and dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$43.5 million in cash as of June 30, 2026, boosted by $10.6 million in net ATM proceeds raised at an average price of $1.52 per share, extending runway into 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “a clean Q2 exits around $34–35M” and “Burn above ~$8M or any softening of the runway language reopens the dilution question.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 50.7%, slightly below the preview’s 51–52% estimate and its 51% watch level, although it remained above 50% for a fourth consecutive quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 50.7% in Q2, expanding roughly 150 basis points year-over-year and marking the fourth consecutive quarter above 50%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~51–52% (my est.)” and “Gross margin ≥51% ... confirms the pricing thesis.”

surprises.description: The company reported an initial placement within one of the largest national IDNs and expansion beyond first sites at other health systems, providing evidence of conversion from the multi-unit hospital and IDN pipeline the preview identified as a key H2 bridge. The placement was not quantified or named, so it fell short of the preview’s highest-value disclosure scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured an initial placement within one of the largest national IDNs in early July and expanded beyond first sites at other health systems during Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management explicitly flagged ‘several multi-unit hospital and IDN opportunities’ as the H2 bridge” and “Named or quantified multi-unit wins are the highest-value disclosure on this call.”

in_line: The company sold 12 systems, in line with the preview’s estimate of roughly 11–12 units.
The $20–22 million full-year revenue guidance was reiterated, as expected; the resulting $12–14 million second-half requirement matched the preview’s guide math.
EPS was -$0.09, matching the preview’s -$0.09 estimate.
The Contrast PMR study was approximately 75% enrolled with an FDA submission targeted by year-end 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a year-end contrast-indication catalyst.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $351.2 million, about 3% above the preview’s $340.45 million consensus, rather than merely matching the expected modest decline. Management also now expects a low-single-digit second-half decline, milder than the preview’s implied 4–7% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $351.2 million (up 2%)”; “The company expects second-half reported revenue to decline low single digits due to IRA pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $340.45M”; “The FY guide implies $723–743M in 2H, or −4% to −7% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Guardian raised its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA range to $129–131 million, above the preview’s expected modest increase to roughly $125–129 million and above the flagged $126 million threshold. This was a larger guidance step-up than the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guardian raised full-year 2026 guidance to … adjusted EBITDA of $129-$131 million (from $123-$127 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … FY guide nudged to $125–129M or reiterated at high end”; “FY26 adj. EBITDA guide raised to ≥$126M.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross profit reached $80 million, above the preview’s expected $74–77 million, while gross margin was 22.8% versus an anticipated level around 22%. The results showed stronger gross-profit dollars and margin than the preview’s already-healthy baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit rising 18% to $80 million and gross margin expanding to 22.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for ~$74–77M of GP at ~22% margin.”

surprises.description: The expected 2027 IRA tranche impact was revised down: it is now estimated at about 40% of the 2026 tranche’s revenue impact, versus the prior 50% estimate. Management also said the margin impact is mitigated, a more reassuring outlook than the preview’s concern about whether IRA offsets would prove durable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2027 IRA drug tranche is expected to represent roughly 40% of the 2026 tranche's revenue impact (down from a prior 50% estimate), and management believes the margin impact is mitigated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Question is whether mitigation is structural or one-time”; “The market has been paying for the durability of the IRA offset.”

surprises.description: Cash rose to nearly $90 million from about $65 million at Q1, with no debt, and management identified potential Omnicare asset opportunities that are not included in guidance. The preview noted the $65 million cash balance and a robust acquisition pipeline, but did not flag this larger cash position or the Omnicare opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guardian ended the quarter with nearly $90 million in cash (up from ~$65 million) and no debt, keeping dry powder for potential Omnicare asset opportunities not reflected in guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash $65M at Q1 with IRA-driven working capital timing noise management called temporary”; “Pipeline ‘very robust.’”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that about 13.5 million Class B shares will convert to Class A in late September, with an estimated 35–37 million Class A shares held by insiders and trading restrictions lasting until after Q3 earnings in November. The preview discussed an earlier follow-on but did not identify this upcoming conversion and timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A final tranche of ~13.5 million Class B shares converts to Class A in late September, leaving an estimated 35-37 million Class A shares held by insiders, subject to trading restrictions until after Q3 earnings in November.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $29.7 million was within the preview’s estimated $28–30 million range.

Residents served exceeded 210,000 and grew at a high-single-digit rate, broadly consistent with the preview’s estimate of roughly 211–213 thousand and 8–9% growth; script growth was also high single digits.
The $8.5 million payer settlement boosted reported net income but was excluded from adjusted EBITDA, as the preview had explicitly anticipated.

surprises.description: The preview expected Canada CFR credit sales to appear in Q3, but did not quantify the scale or describe the pathway’s retroactive reach. Gevo reported that the newly approved pathway opens a market of more than 1 billion gallons per year and that roughly $17 million of banked credits had already been sold for Q3 recognition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Newly approved Canada Clean Fuel Regulation pathway opens a more than 1 billion gallon per year compliance market and applies retroactively, with roughly $17 million of banked CFR credits already sold for Q3 recognition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Canada CFR credit sales show up in Q3 financials.”

surprises.description: Gevo gave a specific carbon-business run-rate outlook of more than $30 million in annual revenue, excluding banked CFR credit sales; the preview did not provide an expectation for this run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects the carbon business to deliver over $30 million per year in run-rate revenue, excluding banked CFR credit sales.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $47 million, matching the preview’s roughly $47 million consensus estimate.
FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to more than $60 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that a figure with a “6” handle would be a clear win.
The Lake Preston project discontinuation and a significant non-cash impairment were anticipated; the preview specifically warned that a write-down could make GAAP EPS dramatically negative.
The more-than-$70-million 45Z monetization target and H2 cash collection were expected; the reported $20 million collected after quarter-end is consistent with that timing.
The North Star project’s roughly $600 million capital estimate, year-end decision target, and offtake agreements as the key gating item were consistent with the preview.
The North Dakota debottlenecking was expected to involve Q2 tie-in downtime; the reported capacity increase remains on track for year-end.

surprises.description: ICF's non-GAAP EPS was $1.86, about 10% above the preview's $1.69 consensus and above its base-case range of $1.66–$1.74. The call attributed part of the result to a lower tax rate, lower interest expense, and a reduced share count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS rose 12% year-over-year to $1.86,” aided by a 17.8% tax rate that “contributed a $0.11 non-GAAP EPS benefit,” lower interest expense, and reduced share count.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | $1.69” consensus; the base scenario expected “$1.66–$1.74.”

surprises.description: Quarterly bookings were substantially weaker than the preview's desired level: in-quarter book-to-bill was 0.85, versus the preview's bullish threshold of at least 1.2. Backlog also fell to $3.3 billion from $3.4 billion, while trailing book-to-bill of 1.09 remained below the preview's desired level above 1.2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The in-quarter book-to-bill was only 0.85 and backlog slipped to $3.3 billion, driven primarily by slower federal procurement awards”; trailing 12-month book-to-bill was 1.09.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bulls need TTM >1.2 and quarterly ≥1.2; sub-1.0 confirms procurement stress.”

surprises.description: Federal revenue fell 9.5% year over year, rather than showing the sequential improvement the preview said was needed to keep the recovery path credible. The call linked the weak bookings and backlog to slower federal procurement awards.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 9.5% year-over-year decline in federal revenue” was offset by non-federal growth; slower federal procurement awards were the primary driver of the weaker in-quarter book-to-bill and backlog decline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said federal revenue “needs another clean sequential gain (~$190M+) to keep that credible,” referring to management's path to year-over-year growth by Q4.

surprises.description: Commercial energy was weaker than the preview's near-term requirement: it grew only about 3% in the first half, leaving the company needing mid-teens growth in the second half to reach its roughly 10% full-year target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial energy grew only about 3% in the first half, requiring mid-teens growth in the second half to hit the roughly 10% full-year target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 needs high-single-digit reported growth to make the FY target arithmetically reachable.”

surprises.description: International government revenue grew 35% year over year as EU and U.K. contracts ramped, stronger than the preview's 17.5% Q1 growth reference and its description of faster-than-planned ramping as a bull-case outcome. Management also projected double-digit international growth in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International government revenue surged 35% year-over-year,” driven by ramping EU and U.K. contracts, with management guiding to “double-digit international growth in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 international growth of “+17.5% Y/Y” and described EU/U.K. contracts ramping “ahead of plan” as part of the bull scenario.

surprises.description: Revenue came in slightly below the $478.3 million consensus, despite landing within the preview's base-case range. The miss was modest, at about 0.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 total revenue was “$474.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $478.3M” Q2 FY26 consensus; the preview's base scenario was “$472–483M (in line).”

in_line: Full-year 2026 revenue, GAAP EPS, and non-GAAP EPS guidance was reaffirmed unchanged, as the preview expected in its base scenario.
Adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.2%, matching the preview's roughly 11.2% expectation, and the company remained on track for its targeted 10–20 basis points of full-year expansion.
The company continued share repurchases, consistent with the preview's expectation of continued buybacks; the $0.14 quarterly dividend also matched the amount cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Revenue was $1.1 million, well below the preview’s $1.7–2.0 million estimate and $1.84 million consensus. The preview cautioned that collaboration revenue is lumpy, but the reported figure was still below its bear-case threshold of $1.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues fell to $1.1 million from $2.8 million a year earlier,” driven by lower Roche collaboration revenue and the prior-year VAC termination.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue” consensus “$1.84M”; estimate “$1.7–2.0M.” The bear scenario cited “<$1.5M.”

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter above the preview’s $46–49 million estimate, and the runway extended into Q3 2028 rather than the expected Q2 2028. The extra quarter of runway is a better outcome than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lineage ended Q2 2026 … with $50.8 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities,” expected to fund operations “into the third quarter of 2028, one quarter longer than the prior runway.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Cash estimate: “$46–49M”; existing runway “into Q2 2028.” The preview called for cash “≥ $46M and ‘into Q2 2028’ reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Lineage disclosed raising $4.6 million through its ATM shortly before quarter-end. The preview identified ATM usage as a downside risk, but did not expect or report a specific raise in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised approximately $4.6 million via its ATM on June 26 … at a weighted average price of $1.28 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “an ATM/financing disclosure with the stock near 52-week lows” was a primary downside risk and listed “ATM usage disclosed” in its bear scenario.

surprises.description: GAAP results swung to positive net income and EPS, versus the preview’s expected loss. The call attributed the result mainly to a noncash warrant remeasurement gain and the absence of the prior-year VAC impairment, consistent with the preview’s warning that falling share prices can mechanically improve EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income of $1.5 million ($0.01 basic EPS) versus a net loss of $30.5 million ($0.13 loss per share) a year earlier,” primarily from a noncash warrant liability remeasurement gain and absence of the prior-year “$14.8 million VAC impairment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: GAAP EPS consensus was “($0.03)” and the preview estimate was “($0.01)–($0.03).” It also noted that “the stock falling produces an EPS ‘beat.’”

surprises.description: Combined R&D and G&A reached $10.0 million, the top of the preview’s estimated range and above its stated $9.5 million watchpoint. Each expense line was individually within its forecast range, so the shortfall was spending at the high end rather than a major forecast break.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses rose to $4.8 million from $3.1 million” and “G&A rose to $5.2 million from $4.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated total opex at “$9.4–10.0M” but listed “Total opex ≤ $9.5M” as a catalyst checklist item. R&D was estimated at “$4.4–4.8M” and G&A at “$4.9–5.2M.”

surprises.description: Management said it may shift OPC1 toward chronic spinal-cord-injury patients, emphasizing that they are roughly ten times more prevalent than subacute patients and offer more reliable trial baselines. The preview discussed chronic participants and the FDA comparability package, but did not flag a possible change in program focus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “may shift the OPC1 spinal cord injury program toward chronic patients,” who are “roughly 10x more prevalent than subacute patients and provide more reliable trial baselines”; all current DOSED candidates are chronic patients.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on the “FDA comparability package later in 2026,” the second chronic SCI participant, and whether DOSED enrollment would be expanded; it did not describe a possible chronic-patient focus shift.

surprises.description: The DOSED study reported two chronic patients stable and free of adverse events, including one at one year. The preview anticipated a chronic-patient follow-up update, but the reported safety status was not specified in its expectations; the study is not designed to establish efficacy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two chronic patients (one at one year, one at 90 days) remained adverse-event-free and stable with no unexpected procedural, product or device-related events,” though “the study is not designed to measure efficacy.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the first chronic participant was “approaching 12-month follow-up” and listed a “12-month chronic data tease” as something to watch.

surprises.description: Management added a before-year-end update expectation for the ILT1 diabetes islet-cell program and cited an AlloSCOPE 5D production-cost target in the hundreds of dollars per dose. The preview did not identify either detail, though the cost figure is a target rather than a reported achieved cost.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects updates on the ILT1 diabetes islet-cell program before year-end,” with the program and COR1 leveraging AlloSCOPE 5D, “targeting production costs in the hundreds of dollars per dose.”

in_line: R&D of $4.8 million and G&A of $5.2 million were each within the preview’s respective estimated ranges, though both were at the high end.
COR1’s expected initial in-vivo animal data by year-end was broadly consistent with the preview, which said the program had advanced into in-vivo testing and initial data were expected in 2026.

surprises.description: Nephros reported Q2 revenue of $6 million, well above the preview’s $5.0–5.15 million estimate, and revenue rose sequentially despite the preview describing Q2 as seasonally soft. The 36% year-over-year growth also substantially exceeded the preview’s implied 13–17%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $6 million, up 36% year-over-year and approximately 15% sequentially from the prior record quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~ $5.0–5.15M (derived)” and “A sequential decline from Q1’26’s $5.21M is normal”; the base case was “$4.95–5.15M +12–17% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Reported gross margin was 67%, far above the preview’s 58.5–60% base case, but the apparent recovery was largely a timing effect: about $500,000 of the $600,000 tariff refund related to prior periods and inflated Q2 margin by roughly 9 percentage points. The call said underlying margin remained pressured, so the headline result overstated the improvement investors might have inferred.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported gross margin rose to 67% from 63% a year earlier, but roughly $500,000 of the $600,000 tariff refund actually related to prior periods, inflating this quarter’s margin by about 9 percentage points”; “underlying margin remains pressured by the ongoing 10% tariff, a stronger euro, higher shipping costs, and lower-margin service revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “GM 58.5–60%,” and it said “If GM doesn’t print ≥58.5%, the recovery thesis is broken.” It also said the bull case required management to “quantify tariff refund recovery.”

surprises.description: Profitability was much stronger than the preview’s near-break-even expectation: net income reached approximately $1.2 million, while adjusted EBITDA rose to roughly $1.3 million. This is a substantial improvement against a preview that expected diluted EPS of just $0.01 and emphasized that revenue growth had not been converting into profit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income surged over 400% to approximately $1.2 million from $237,000 a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA rose 260% to roughly $1.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) $0.01”; the preview also said “Growth has stopped converting to profit” and described the base case as “EPS $0.01.”

surprises.description: The cash balance increased to about $4.7 million from $4.0 million at the end of Q1, contrary to the preview’s concern that cash could draw down toward $3.0–3.5 million. However, first-half operating cash flow was negative, so the stronger ending cash balance did not reflect positive operating cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash grew to approximately $4.7 million as of June 30, 2026 (up from $4 million at March 31), and the company remains debt-free, though first-half operating cash flow turned negative at negative $990,000 due to rising receivables and inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Cash. $5.4M (YE25) → $4.0M (Q1’26) — a $1.4M draw in one quarter” and warned that “another sequential draw toward ~$3.0M puts a financing conversation on the table by year-end”; its checklist said “Cash balance vs. $3.5M.”

surprises.description: Programmatic product growth accelerated beyond the preview’s expected range: it grew about 27% year over year, versus the preview’s base-case expectation of 20–24%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Programmatic product revenue grew approximately 27% year-over-year, representing the recurring core foundation of the business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “programmatic +20–24%” and said deceleration “below ~20%” would undercut the recurring-base story.

surprises.description: Service-only revenue nearly tripled, an unanticipated source of growth as customers relied more on Nephros for installation, replacement, and ongoing support. The call also noted that lower-margin service revenue contributed to underlying margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Service-only revenue nearly tripled year-over-year as customers increasingly rely on Nephros for installation, replacement, and ongoing support”; the call cited “lower-margin service revenue” as a pressure on underlying margin.

surprises.description: Revenue growth came overwhelmingly from expanding within existing customers, while the total customer count was only slightly above the prior quarter. That left the preview’s site-growth and Greater New York traction questions without evidence of a meaningful new-site contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Growth was driven overwhelmingly by expansion within existing customers rather than new sites, with total customer count at 1,724, only slightly above the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Active sites & revenue/site” as a key metric, calling site count “the leading indicator,” and flagged “NYC region traction” as a catalyst to watch after hiring a dedicated Greater New York sales leader.

in_line: New PFAS, microplastics, and nanoplastics products had not gained meaningful traction and were expected to become revenue drivers only two to three quarters out; this is consistent with the preview’s warning not to underwrite these as 2026 revenue drivers.
The education platform remained unmonetized; the preview did not present it as a near-term revenue driver.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $45.5 million, about $5 million above the top of guidance and well above the preview's $35–36 million estimate. The roughly $2 million tariff refund contributed, but EBITDA excluding it still beat the guidance high end by about $3.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $45.5 million (including ~$2 million of IEEPA tariff refunds) beat the high end of guidance by roughly $5 million”; margin was “12.7% (12.2% ex-refund).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$35–36M (implied)” and company guidance of “$32M – $40M.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year sales guidance to $1.42–$1.47 billion, above the preview's prior $1.328–$1.416 billion range, and raised the EBITDA floor while narrowing the range to $176–$196 million. That was better than the preview's concern that the guide could be trimmed into the lower half, although the new EBITDA ceiling is lower than before.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year net sales guidance to $1.42–$1.47 billion and narrowed adjusted EBITDA guidance to $176–$196 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY2026 (reaffirmed at Q1): net sales $1.328–1.416B; adj. EBITDA $174–203M”; the preview said to watch whether the EBITDA range was “narrowed to the lower half ($174–188M).”

surprises.description: Despite the higher sales outlook, the implied full-year margin fell to about 12.4%–13.3% from the February framework of 13.1%–14.3%. That undercuts the preview's already steep expected H2 margin ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Implied full-year margin was cut to approximately 12.4%–13.3% from the 13.1%–14.3% framework given in February, reflecting mix and inflation pressures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “To hit even the low end of the FY EBITDA guide, Fox needs H2 margins ~520bps above H1”; “At the high end it needs ~950bps.”

surprises.description: The cost headwind proved more severe and broader than the preview's warning about steel and aluminum inflation: incremental steel, aluminum, freight, and fuel costs are nearly $20 million above plan, with about $15 million expected in the second half and no cost relief assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Incremental external input cost inflation (steel, aluminum, freight, fuel) is running nearly $20 million above plan, with about $15 million expected in the second half,” and the company is “not underwriting any commodity or freight cost relief.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “explicitly flagged steel and aluminum cost inflation building into Q2.”

surprises.description: The savings program was much more concretely advanced than the preview's concern that cumulative savings might still be below $12–15 million: the company had captured over $25 million in the first half and remained on track for about $50 million for the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The profit optimization program captured over $25 million of gross savings in the first half and remains on track for approximately $50 million in gross savings for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 had delivered only “mid-single-digit millions” and said “if Q2 delivered <$12–15M cumulative, the H2 ramp is arithmetically stretched.”

surprises.description: Powersports grew 22.5% in Q2, faster than the preview's expectation that the segment would hold mid-teens growth, and was described as a stabilizing force as OEMs worked through inventory imbalances.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Powersports grew 22.5% in Q2 and 28% in the first half year-over-year as OEMs worked through channel inventory imbalances, becoming a stabilizing force.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's bull case assumed “PVG holds mid-teens growth” and called PVG “the one clean growth engine.”

surprises.description: SSG's year-over-year sales decline was accompanied by a 12.5% sequential rebound and essentially flat segment margin; management also expected bike sales to be flat year over year. That was more resilient than the preview's emphasis on ongoing bike destocking and Marucci weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SSG net sales fell 9.4% year-over-year to $124.3 million but rose 12.5% sequentially, with segment margin held essentially flat despite the revenue decline; bike is expected to be flat versus prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “bike channel destocking plus flagged weakness at Marucci” and said “any inflection to flat/positive is the bull's best evidence.”

surprises.description: The Ford F-150 aluminum disruption is expected to last into early-to-mid September, extending the supply issue into Q3 rather than being contained to the first half as the preview's base case hoped.
surprises.fact_evidence: AAG was “hampered by the Ford F-150 aluminum supply disruption now expected to resolve in early-to-mid September.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base-case call description said the F-150 issue would be “characterized as contained to H1”; it also flagged that BofA believed it could “bleed into Q3.”

surprises.description: AAG's profitability improved despite lower sales and the supply disruption, with adjusted EBITDA margin up about 70 basis points year over year and 500 basis points sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: AAG net sales “fell 4% to $109.6 million” but “adjusted EBITDA margin improved ~70 bps year-over-year and ~500 bps sequentially.”

surprises.description: The company reported additional tariff-recovery upside not included in its guidance: it may recover up to $8 million of prior tariff costs. This was separate from the roughly $2 million refund already included in Q2 EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company may recover up to $8 million of additional prior tariff costs not included in guidance.”

surprises.description: Balance-sheet indicators improved rather than deteriorating: debt fell by $20.5 million sequentially and inventory days declined from about 150 to 136, while leverage stayed around 3.7x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt declined $20.5 million sequentially to $667.7 million,” and “days inventory improved to ~136 from ~150 days”; net leverage was “3.7x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that if Q2 FCF remained negative and inventory had not come down, “leverage drifts toward 4.2–4.5x.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was modestly above the $353.1 million consensus estimate and landed at the top of the guided range, rather than the preview's central $353–358 million base-case band.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $358.1 million … landing at the high end of the guided range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 consensus net sales of “$353.1M” and a base case of “$353–358M.”

in_line: SSG's 9.4% year-over-year sales decline was broadly consistent with the preview's expectation of a down mid-single-digit to high-single-digit quarter.
Net leverage of 3.7x was essentially in line with the preview's estimate of about 3.77x.

surprises.description: Instead of reaffirming the FY2026 outlook as the preview expected, management said the prior Q4 EPS guidance of $0.79–$0.89 needs to be re-evaluated. The shift toward holding more SBA 7(a) loans is expected to reduce near-term gain-on-sale income and pressure net interest income, with updated guidance not expected for 45–60 days.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is shifting strategy to hold more SBA 7(a) loans on the balance sheet, which will reduce near-term gain-on-sale income and pressure the top-line net interest income, prompting a re-evaluation of prior Q4 guidance of $0.79-$0.89. Company guidance will be reissued within an estimated 45-60 day window.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance language — ‘reaffirm $2.15–$2.55’ is the base case.”

surprises.description: The planned securitization is sized at $300–$400 million, below the preview’s expected $400–$500 million Q4 collateral pool at most of the range. The call facts do not confirm that the planned deal has the same timing or scope as the preview’s expected Q4 ALP securitization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans a securitization out of the bank sized between $300 million and $400 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q4 ALP securitization ($400–500M collateral pool, per management) is the largest single swing factor.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a $15 million loan to a summer camp operator that is in bankruptcy—an unexpected borrower-specific credit issue. Management nevertheless expects to recover the loan fully, tempering the downside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Disclosed a $15 million loan to a summer camp operator (Sunmad Holdings) in bankruptcy that management expects to fully recover.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Credit quality — the swing factor nobody models well.”

surprises.description: Assets grew 50% year over year while expenses rose only 3.6%, indicating substantially faster growth in assets than in expenses. The preview did not quantify or flag this degree of operating leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assets grew 50% year-over-year while expenses rose only 3.6%, demonstrating operating leverage.”

in_line: Diluted EPS was $0.47, close to the $0.46 consensus and within the preview’s $0.46–$0.49 base-case range.

Bank net interest income rose to $25 million from $16.2 million a year earlier, and cost of deposits declined from Q1 to Q2; these developments are consistent with the preview’s expectation that the deposit-funding shift would support margin improvement.
Consumer deposits continued to account for substantial growth, consistent with the preview’s warning that another consumer-heavy deposit mix was possible.

surprises.description: LOCO raised full-year system-wide comp guidance to 3.5%-4.5% from 2%-4%, a larger improvement than the preview’s discussion of the existing range and possible downside risk. The higher range is a positive update to the sales outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year system-wide comp sales guidance to 3.5%-4.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “System-wide comps | +2% to +4% (raised from +2–3%).”

surprises.description: Commodity inflation was 4.1%, above the preview’s 1.5%-2.5% full-year food-and-paper inflation outlook, with produce driving much of the increase. Restaurant-level margin still improved, but the input-cost pressure was worse than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level margin improved to 19.5% from 19.1% a year earlier, staying within the 18-20% long-term target despite 4.1% commodity inflation driven largely by produce.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Food & paper inflation | +1.5% – 2.5%.”

surprises.description: Early Q3 comps were running at 5.8%, even though management expects the full quarter to land at 3.5%-4.5% after an outsized July benefit from World Cup advertising and tougher comparisons. That early pace is stronger than the preview’s concern about comp deceleration, but management cautioned against extrapolating it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3-to-date (through July 29) system-wide comparable sales accelerated to 5.8%, but management guided full Q3 comps to 3.5%-4.5%, citing outsized July benefit from World Cup advertising and tougher upcoming comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “That implies either genuine deceleration in May/June or standard conservatism.”

surprises.description: GAAP net income reached $12.8 million, or $0.43 per share, largely because of a $6.3 million legal settlement; adjusted EPS was $0.30, a much more modest result. The preview focused on adjusted EPS and did not anticipate this one-off boost to the GAAP headline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income jumped to $12.8 million ($0.43/share) from $7.1 million ($0.24/share), largely boosted by a $6.3 million legal settlement, while adjusted EPS was more modest at $0.30 versus $0.28.”

surprises.description: Labor expense fell 90 basis points to 29.9% of restaurant sales, with wage inflation below 1% in the quarter—better than the preview’s 1.5%-2.5% wage-inflation outlook. Lower health insurance and workers’ compensation costs also helped.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Labor expense improved 90 basis points to 29.9% of restaurant sales, aided by wage inflation under 1% in the quarter and lower health insurance and workers' comp costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Wage inflation | +1.5% – 2.5%.”

surprises.description: The company lowered 2026 capital spending guidance to $33-$37 million from $37-$40 million because of remodel timing. This reduces expected spending, though the stated reason is timing rather than a reduction in planned investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut 2026 capital spending guidance to $33-$37 million due to remodel timing.”

surprises.description: LOCO paid down $21 million on its revolver, leaving $30 million in debt, and extended its $150 million credit facility to 2031. The longer facility and paydown improve the debt picture, while the new spread is roughly 50 basis points higher; the preview had no specific expectation for these financing changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paid down $21 million on its revolver leaving $30 million in debt, and extended its $150 million credit facility to 2031 at a spread roughly 50 basis points higher.”

in_line: Q2 system-wide comps were 3.9%, within the preview’s cited 3%-4% company guide; transactions declined 0.9%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that traffic would be roughly flat to negative.
Adjusted EPS of $0.30 was in the preview’s $0.30-$0.31 base-case range and close to the $0.29 consensus estimate; the preview also said a headline EPS beat was close to the base case.
Restaurant-level margin of 19.5% was at the top of the preview’s 19.0%-19.5% company-guidance range.
The adjusted EBITDA guidance increase to $68-$70 million was consistent with the preview’s expectation of a raise or a narrowing toward the top half of the prior $67.5-$69.5 million range.
Full-year restaurant-margin guidance remained at 18.25%-18.75%, as in the preview.
The company reaffirmed plans for 18-20 new restaurants, matching the preview’s expectation; the preview also highlighted expansion outside California, consistent with the reported development plans.
Digital sales continued to rise, as the preview had flagged as a secondary item to watch.

surprises.description: The large auto-insurance carrier relationship stabilized rather than continuing to worsen in Q2, which is better than the preview’s expectation that the shortfall would hit Q2 harder. It still remained below levels seen earlier in the year, so the issue was not resolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's largest auto insurance carrier relationship has stabilized but remains below levels seen earlier in the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said monetization from one large auto carrier ‘started running below expectations’ in Q1 and would hit Q2 harder.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance implies 17% year-over-year growth, a stronger growth outlook than the preview’s basic expectation that guidance should at least imply growth. The guide is boosted by student-loan regulatory tailwinds and the February college-finance acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $244–$260 million implies 17% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, boosted by student loan regulatory tailwinds and the February college finance acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q3'26 guide that doesn't imply growth off that base signals the search erosion is outrunning banking/loans growth.”

surprises.description: SMB revenue declined 11%, a milder drop than the preview’s estimate of about 15% decline. Business-loan originations partly offset continued organic-search declines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SMB revenue fell 11% year-over-year to $22 million, dragged down by organic search declines in non-loan products but partially offset by growth in business loan originations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance midpoint implies … SMB ~$21M (−15%).”

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow doubled to a record $141 million, but the result was helped by tax refunds and the absence of federal corporate tax payments. Management also said federal corporate taxes are not expected in 2026, with normalized taxes anticipated in Q2 or Q3 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow grew 100% year-over-year to a record $141 million, aided by $9 million in tax refunds and no federal corporate tax payments”; the company “does not expect to be a federal corporate taxpayer in 2026” and anticipates normalized taxes in “Q2 or Q3 of 2027.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a much larger customer-acquisition investment for longer-payback customers: roughly five times the 2025 level for paybacks beyond the current year, creating a $15–$20 million 2026 operating-income headwind. The preview anticipated multi-quarter investment but did not quantify this headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is increasing customer acquisition spend with payback periods beyond the current year roughly fivefold versus 2025, representing a $15–$20 million NGOI headwind for full-year 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base = repetition of ‘multi-quarter initiative’ with no new numbers”; the preview also said an explicit spend-peak quarter was a key marker to watch.

surprises.description: Full-year NGOI guidance was narrowed to $90–$105 million rather than reaffirmed unchanged at $85–$110 million. The midpoint is unchanged, but the higher floor and lower ceiling give a tighter range; profitability is also expected to be more concentrated in Q3 than in prior years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year NGOI guidance was narrowed to $90–$105 million while maintaining the prior midpoint, with profitability expected to be more concentrated in Q3 than in prior years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side expects reaffirmation”; the preview’s base case was “FY $85–110M reaffirmed unchanged.”

surprises.description: Consumer revenue was slightly above the preview’s segment estimate: $175 million and 8% growth versus an estimate of about $173 million and 7% growth. Personal loans and deposit accounts drove growth, while credit cards continued to decline from organic-search headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $175 million, driven by personal loans (up $12 million) and deposit accounts, though partially offset by continued declines in consumer credit cards from organic search headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance midpoint implies Consumer ~$173M (+7%).”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $197 million was close to the preview’s $195.3 million consensus and $194 million guidance midpoint, and within the $186–$202 million guidance range.
Q2 non-GAAP operating income of $12 million was within the $6–$14 million guidance range and at the upper end of the preview’s $9–$12 million base case.
Credit-card declines from organic-search headwinds and SMB pressure from organic search were both anticipated in the preview.

The company continued repurchasing stock: $23 million in Q2, with $67 million remaining under authorization. The preview flagged buyback pace and share-count reduction as watch items but did not set a Q2 repurchase target.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $753 million, well above the preview’s $695–715 million credible whisper range, and growth was about 38% reported or 40% excluding true-ups versus the preview’s expected 28–31% growth. This was a substantially larger beat than the preview’s already-high revenue hurdle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was approximately $753 million, up ~38% year-over-year (~40% ex true-ups)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I put the credible buy-side whisper at $695–715M”; the base scenario expected “$700–715M (+28–31% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: Signatera clinical MRD volume reached 283,000 units, above the preview’s 268,000–275,000 watch range and its 278,000+ bull threshold. The 34,000-unit sequential increase also far exceeded the preview’s cited roughly 20,000-unit trailing average.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clinical MRD (Signatera) units of 283,000 growing ~56% year-over-year and rising 34,000 units sequentially, its largest sequential increase to date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for 268–275k”; “above 278k re-rates the story”; management had guided to “quarterly growth along the lines of the trailing 12-month average” (~“+20k”).

surprises.description: Signatera ASP reached roughly $1,275 in Q2, rather than merely being on track to reach that level by year-end. The preview’s stated target was therefore reached earlier than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signatera ASP rose ~$25 sequentially to roughly $1,275.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$1,250 in Q1”; “target $1,275 by year-end”; “Signatera 268k+ units and ASP on track to $1,275.”

surprises.description: The preview expected gross margin recovery to 66% or better, but reported gross margin was about 65%. That was below the preview’s 66%+ watch level and the 65.5–66.5% base-case range, although it remained within company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin held strong at ~65%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for 66%+”; the base scenario expected “65.5–66.5%.”

surprises.description: The call’s Q3 Signatera outlook was for sequential growth above the prior roughly 25,000-unit record, more than the preview’s approximately 20,000-unit trailing-average reference. Management did caution that Q3 would not match Q2’s exceptional 34,000-unit increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 Signatera growth will not repeat the record 34,000 units—partly inflated by weather-suppressed Q1—but expects to exceed the prior sequential record of roughly 25,000 units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided to “quarterly growth along the lines of the trailing 12-month average” (~“+20k”).

surprises.description: Revenue true-ups declined from roughly $60 million in Q1 to about $52 million, while DSOs fell by around four days to an average of 57 days. This was better than the preview’s concern about another outsized true-up alongside rising DSOs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “True-ups declining to ~$52 million in absolute and percentage terms”; “reduced DSOs by ~4 days to an average of 57 days.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “a repeat outsized true-up alongside rising DSOs” as the quality-of-earnings risk.

surprises.description: Natera disclosed that the seven additional Signatera tumor-type submissions could add an estimated $150–$200 to ASP, with approvals expected to roll in over 12–18 months and the impact weighted toward 2027. The preview flagged the seven pending histologies but did not provide this quantified ASP contribution or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 7 additional Signatera tumor-type indications submitted to MolDX could add an estimated $150–$200 to ASP, with rolling approvals expected over the next 12–18 months and impact weighted toward 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for … any update on the seven additional histologies in MolDX/CMS review.”

surprises.description: Signatera received FDA companion-diagnostic approval for muscle-invasive bladder cancer, a regulatory milestone the preview did not identify among the expected updates. The preview did flag other milestones, including the NCCN recommendation and EU IVDR certification.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signatera achieved multiple regulatory milestones, becoming the first MRD test with FDA companion-diagnostic approval (muscle-invasive bladder cancer).”

surprises.description: Women’s health delivered high-single-digit year-over-year growth despite the preview’s emphasis on Q2 as the seasonally slowest quarter. Management attributed performance to market-share gains and the enhanced Panorama test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Women's health delivered high single-digit year-over-year growth despite seasonal softness, aided by market share gains and the enhanced Panorama test.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q2 as “management's explicitly stated seasonally slowest women's health quarter.”

surprises.description: The enhanced Panorama test reduced the no-call rate from about 2% to 0.5%, an improvement the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The enhanced Panorama test … cut the no-call rate from ~2% to 0.5%.”

in_line: The full-year revenue guidance midpoint rose by $100 million to $2.88 billion, within the preview’s expected $2.86–2.94 billion range and above its stated $2.86 billion bar.

The loss per share narrowed, as the preview specifically expected a sequential narrowing from Q1’s $0.60 loss; the preview also expected a reaffirmed positive-cash-flow commitment, and the call reported positive cash inflow.
The long-term Signatera ASP target of around $2,000 was consistent with the preview’s stated long-term ambition.
The Japanese PMDA approval, EU IVDR certification, and NCCN Category 1 bladder recommendation were anticipated or already flagged in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 total revenue of $56.5 million beat the $54.06 million consensus, and net product revenue of $53.6 million exceeded the preview’s implied $51–52 million range and the company’s $50–52 million guide. Bottle sales also rose 26% sequentially to 2,929, above the preview’s 2,800-bottle bullish threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $56.5 million, with net product revenue of $53.6 million”; “ex-factory bottle sales rose 26% quarter-over-quarter and 12% year-over-year to 2,929 bottles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Consensus | $54.06M”; “NERLYNX net product revenue | ~$51–52M (implied) | Guidance $50–52M”; “>$52M = destocking confirmed transitory”; “Bull needs bottle volumes back above ~2,800.”

surprises.description: Earnings substantially exceeded expectations: Puma reported $8.2 million of GAAP net income and $0.16 per diluted share, versus consensus EPS of $0.04 and company guidance for $2–4 million of net income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Puma reported Q2 2026 GAAP net income of $8.2 million ($0.16 per diluted share)”; non-GAAP net income was “$10.1 million.”

surprises.description: Puma raised its full-year product revenue and net income guidance, rather than reaffirming it as the preview’s base case anticipated. The increases were modest, however, and fell well short of the preview’s bullish scenario of product revenue above $229 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 net product revenue guidance to $205-209 million (from $202-206 million) and net income guidance to $17-20 million (from $16-19 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance action | Stock has priced a third consecutive raise”; “reaffirm = neutral-negative given the run”; the bull scenario called for “FY guide raised to ~$228–234M / NI $20–23M.”

surprises.description: The full-year royalty outlook was cut even though the preview treated the existing $20–23 million range as the guide and highlighted the importance of the large H2 royalty contribution. Management also flagged possible lower China royalty rates once generics reach a market-share threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China royalty rates could be reduced as early as late 2026 or 2027 once generic NERLYNX reaches a market-share threshold, and full-year royalty guidance was trimmed to $19-22 million from $20-23 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H2 royalty phasing | FY guide $20–23M less Q1 $2.8M less Q2 $2–3M ⇒ $14–18M must land in H2”; “Any hedging on shipment timing breaks the FY net income bridge.”

surprises.description: Bottle sales were strong, but new patient starts declined 6% sequentially, a weaker underlying-starts signal than the preview’s expectation that the Q1 new-start cohort would convert into volume growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ex-factory bottle sales rose 26% quarter-over-quarter and 12% year-over-year to 2,929 bottles, though new patient starts declined 6% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1’26… new patient starts +25% q/q, +11% y/y”; the bull scenario expected “the +25% q/q new-start cohort converts.”

surprises.description: Instead of simply confirming broader enrollment expansion and the expected dose-escalation progress, management reported that ALISCA-Breast1 enrollment would continue only in the 40mg and 50mg groups, focused on patients with Aurora kinase pathway biomarkers. The amended enrollment is expected in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ALISCA-Breast1 trial was amended to continue enrollment only in the 40mg and 50mg dose groups, targeting patients with Aurora kinase pathway biomarkers, with amended enrollment expected in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “confirmation of ALISCA-Breast1/Lung1 expansion enrollment (H2’26), 70mg escalation tolerability, Phase 3 design + Q4’26 Breast1 data date.”

surprises.description: Management said it can fund Phase III trials in both ER-positive breast cancer and small cell lung cancer, potentially staggering them, while remaining committed to positive net income. This directly addresses the preview’s concern that Phase III plans could require an equity raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated it can fund Phase III trials for alisertib in both ER-positive breast cancer and small cell lung cancer, potentially staggered, while remaining committed to positive net income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Phase 3 funding without dilution” as a key metric and said “any hint of a Phase 3 requiring an equity raise is a negative.”

surprises.description: Management offered a notably affirmative demand outlook, expecting 2026 to be the first time NERLYNX has delivered positive U.S. demand growth in two consecutive years. The preview focused on whether the Q1 inventory drawdown was temporary, but did not state this specific outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects 2026 to mark the first-ever back-to-back years of positive year-over-year U.S. NERLYNX demand growth in the drug's launch history.”

in_line: Management’s 2026 R&D expense outlook of 34–37% year-over-year growth matched the preview’s stated expectation that R&D would rise 34–37% to fund alisertib.

surprises.description: PLSE expected to have about $68–72 million in cash at quarter-end, and the preview said no financing in the base case. Instead, cash was over $101.6 million after $57.5 million of net ATM proceeds since May, including about $13 million from insiders; the larger cash cushion is positive, but the equity raise also means dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over $101.6 million in cash as of quarter-end (up $33.3 million sequentially), raising $57.5 million in net ATM proceeds since May, including approximately $13 million from insiders and $44.5 million from outside investors.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash & equiv. 6/30/26: $68–72M”; the base scenario anticipated “no financing announced,” while the preview called a raise a key downside risk.

surprises.description: The reported losses were larger than the preview’s own estimates and slightly worse than the top end of its implied consensus range. GAAP net loss was $24.7 million versus an estimated roughly $20.2 million and implied consensus of about $21–24 million; non-GAAP net loss was $19.4 million versus an estimated roughly $17.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss widened to $24.7 million” and “non-GAAP net loss rose to $19.4 million,” driven by increased clinical trial and compensation spending.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “GAAP net loss ~($20.2M)” and “Non-GAAP net loss ~(17.5).” It also gave “~($21–24M) implied” GAAP consensus.

surprises.description: The pivotal study’s planned enrollment rose from 145 to 164 patients, and the eligibility rule was broadened to include patients failing any one of four AAD classes. PLSE still expects to finish enrollment by early October, but the larger target and changed eligibility criteria were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amended its pivotal study protocol to increase the total enrollment target from 145 to 164 patients (adding 19) while loosening AAD failure criteria so patients failing any one of four AAD classes qualify, yet still expects enrollment completion by early October.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the expected enrollment completion timing but did not anticipate a higher enrollment target or changed AAD criteria.

surprises.description: Several early high-volume sites have already reached a 15% per-site enrollment cap, creating a constraint the preview did not flag. The company says it is managing the cap and has expanded the active study base to 12 sites, while keeping its early-October completion target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A per-site enrollment cap of 15% is being managed as several early high-volume sites have already reached their cap, with the active study site base expanded to 12 (of up to 30 allowed) and continuing to grow.”

surprises.description: The call gave a concrete European regulatory schedule for the cardiac catheter: CE Mark submission in the second half of 2026 and potential approval around mid-2027. The preview focused on the lack of a public U.S. PMA schedule and did not anticipate this European timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plans to submit for CE Mark for its cardiac catheter in the second half of 2026, targeting potential EU approval around mid-2027, roughly six months post-submission.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “not put a public date on submission or expected approval” and highlighted first PMA timing guidance as a key potential update; it did not give a CE Mark expectation.

surprises.description: The surgical clamp program delivered an unanticipated feasibility and timing update: its EU study had over 70 patients, 94% pulmonary vein isolation success at three months, and average ablation time of 4.41 seconds per patient, while the company remained on schedule for a 2026 CE Mark filing. The preview did not discuss this program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The surgical clamp EU feasibility study treated over 70 patients across six sites with 94% pulmonary vein isolation success at three months and average ablation time of 4.41 seconds per patient, remaining on schedule for CE Mark filing before end of 2026.”

surprises.description: Investigational sites reported five to seven catheter ablation cases per day, compared with the two to three cases per day cited for competing catheters. The preview flagged competitive positioning as an issue but did not anticipate this specific throughput evidence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiple investigational sites performed five to seven catheter ablation cases per day with ablation times of seven to eight minutes or faster, versus the typical two to three cases per day for competing ablation catheters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for competitive framing versus approved PFA platforms, but gave no expected case-throughput figures.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $434,000 was below the preview’s $530,000 consensus estimate, though it was close to the preview’s own $450,000 estimate and within its stated $0.4–0.6 million expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $434,000,” a sequential increase from $400,000 in Q1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: ~$0.53M” consensus; the preview’s own estimate was “$0.45M” and its stated range was “$0.4–0.6M.”

in_line: NanoPulse AF pivotal-study enrollment completion remains on the preview’s early-Q4-2026 schedule: the call now expects early October, while the preview’s bogey was to reaffirm “early Q4 2026.”
The European feasibility results broadly matched the preview’s cited 90% 12-month freedom-from-AF result: the call reported 90% Kaplan-Meier freedom from recurrent AF/flutter/tachycardia at one year.

surprises.description: The preview expected a roughly stable royalty run-rate, but Q2 royalties declined significantly as Gauzy’s SPD emulsion and film production slowed and essentially stopped during its court-supervised restructuring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 royalties declined significantly because SPD emulsion and film production at principal licensee Gauzy slowed and essentially stopped during its court-supervised financial restructuring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Strip out upfronts and the underlying royalty run-rate looks like $130–200K/quarter and is not visibly growing”; the base case anticipated “modest Celestiq/Ferrari/aircraft royalties.”

surprises.description: The company recorded a reserve and going-concern accounting treatment on receivables from Gauzy and Vision Systems, citing uncertainty about when it would collect them. The preview flagged going-concern language as a risk scenario, but this treatment was not part of its base-case expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Research Frontiers took a reserve and going-concern accounting treatment on receivables from Gauzy and Vision Systems, citing uncertainty over collection timing rather than ultimate collectability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for: ... going-concern language in the 10-Q”; the preview’s bear scenario said “going-concern language appears in the 10-Q.”

surprises.description: Cash ended just above $1 million, higher than the preview’s expected $0.80–$0.90 million. That is a better quarter-end balance than forecast, although management said the company may still need to raise capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Research Frontiers ended the quarter with just over $1 million in cash and may need to raise capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q2 estimate was “Cash & equivalents ... ~$0.80M – $0.90M.”

surprises.description: Two major aircraft programs were won during the quarter, an award update beyond the preview’s focus on current aircraft shipments and possible scaling. Management said aircraft windows carry roughly 15 times the royalty value per window of automotive applications.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two new major aircraft programs were won during the period,” and aircraft applications carry “roughly 15x the royalty value per window compared to automotive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said aircraft windows had been produced in Q1 and Q2 and to “watch for aircraft shipments scale”; it did not anticipate two new program wins.

surprises.description: Management described a more concrete path to restoring film supply than the preview anticipated: it viewed Gauzy’s successful emergence from bankruptcy and return to full production as the most likely plan, possibly as soon as next month. A $7 million financing and court-approved restructuring had also begun funding rehiring and restarting German production, while management said automotive programs remained intact and volumes could ramp by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management outlined four plans, with “Plan A”—Gauzy emerging from bankruptcy and resuming full production—“viewed as the most likely outcome, possibly as soon as next month.” A “recent $7 million financing” and court approval had “started funds flowing to rehire workers and restart German production”; automotive programs remained intact and volumes could “ramp back up by the end of the year.”

surprises.description: A French court ordered the sale of Gauzy’s entire Vision Systems division for about EUR 9 million despite a signed EUR 125 million offer for only part of the division. The scheduled appeal could still bring Gauzy substantial capital, so the ruling creates a setback but leaves a possible recovery path.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A French court directed the sale of Gauzy’s entire Vision Systems division to Clayens for about EUR 9 million despite a signed EUR 125 million offer for just part of it,” with a “final appeal scheduled for mid-September that could bring substantial capital to Gauzy.”

surprises.description: Management said Research Frontiers could need capital if it pursues Plan D, an acquisition of Gauzy’s SPD manufacturing assets. The preview discussed possible financing generally but did not flag this potential acquisition as a reason for raising funds.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “may need to raise capital, particularly if it pursues ‘Plan D’ of acquiring Gauzy’s SPD manufacturing assets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “a new placement/ATM” and noted that a raise could be needed, but did not mention acquiring Gauzy assets.

in_line: Management continued to rule out a reverse stock split, consistent with the preview’s description of its stance; the preview also already identified the Nasdaq bid-price notice and the roughly November 30 compliance deadline.
The Klim motorcycle-visor and sports-goggle licensee opportunity was already disclosed in the preview, which specifically flagged the partnership and the uncertainty around its monetization.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.80, matching the published consensus but falling short of the preview’s stated $0.83–$0.85 “real bar.” The preview said below $0.82 would read as deceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS jumped 19.4% to $0.80.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$0.85 is the real bar”; “Adj. EPS vs. $0.80 / whisper ~$0.83–$0.85”; “Below $0.82 reads as deceleration.”

surprises.description: Total enrollment grew only 0.7%, below the preview’s base-case expectation of 1.5–2%. Trident was the only institution that did not grow, so the anticipated broad-based enrollment improvement was not evident.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total student enrollments grew only 0.7% year-over-year, with all institutions growing except Trident University within AIU System.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “total enrollments +1.5–2%”; the preview also said management had committed to AIUS enrollments “increasing in Q2 and accelerating in Q3.”

surprises.description: Management warned that CTU’s reported enrollments may trend lower in the second half, with normalization not expected until 2027. The preview recognized tough comparisons and record graduations but expected CTU growth to hold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CTU's second-half reported enrollments may trend lower due to lapping record quarters and a record number of 2026 graduates, with normalization expected in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch whether growth holds with higher spend” and described CTU as “lapping tougher comps while graduating record cohorts.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $213.4 million was slightly above the $212.5 million consensus, but below the preview’s own $215–217 million base-case range and its expectation that revenue would come in above consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue increased just 1.8% to $213.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I model revenue above consensus”; the base case forecast “$215–217M.”

surprises.description: The full-year tax-rate outlook was higher than the preview expected: the new 23–24% range is 0.5 percentage points above the prior 22.5–23.5% range at both ends. Q2 did receive a one-time benefit from resolving a state tax matter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Q2 effective tax rate was 20.3%, benefiting 5.8% from resolution of a state income tax matter, with full-year rate expected at 23%-24%.”

surprises.description: Incremental legal fees tied to CTU litigation weighed on operating income, an expense headwind the preview did not identify. Management said CTU operating income would have grown year over year without those costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rising legal fees at CTU tied to previously disclosed litigation weighed on operating income,” and “CTU operating income would have grown year-over-year excluding these incremental costs.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its full-year adjusted operating income and adjusted EPS ranges while leaving the high ends unchanged. That was an incremental positive versus the preview’s prior ranges, though it did not reach the preview’s bull-case threshold of adjusted EPS guidance at or above $3.15.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted operating income guidance was set at $258-263 million” and “adjusted EPS guidance of $3.10-$3.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior guidance of “adj. operating income $254–$263M” and “adj. EPS $3.05–$3.16”; its bull case called for FY adjusted EPS “raised to ≥$3.15.”

surprises.description: USAHS’s adjusted operating income nearly doubled in Q2, substantially stronger than the preview’s expectation of double-digit annual growth. Its revenue growth was close to the double-digit trajectory the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The University of St. Augustine posted the strongest growth, with enrollment up 6% to ~4,200 students, revenue up 10.2% to $40.5 million, and adjusted operating income nearly doubling to $10.7 million from $5.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “double-digit adj. operating income growth for the year” and expected USAHS to “hold[] double-digit trajectory.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS of $0.80 matched the published consensus of $0.80, even though it was below the preview’s higher $0.83–$0.85 real-bar expectation.
USAHS revenue grew 10.2%, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of a double-digit growth trajectory.
A dividend increase had been flagged as possible for this release or the Q3 print; the company raised the quarterly dividend from $0.15 to $0.17.

surprises.description: Operating adjusted EBITDA was $66 million, well above the preview’s modeled range of $35–45 million. The company called it its best core operating quarter in nearly three years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income available to common shareholders was $18.5 million with operating adjusted EBITDA of $66 million,” described as “the best core operating quarter in nearly 3 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating Adj. EBITDA” Q2 estimate: “$35–45M”; the preview also said “>$40M = the deleveraging story has an engine.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in far below the preview’s roughly $295 million model, with trading gains of just $12.9 million versus modeled investment gains of about $75 million. The call attributed the year-over-year decline in trading gains primarily to a lower fair value on the Babcock & Wilcox investment, rather than the roughly flat BW mark the preview assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenues rose $14 million year-over-year to $239 million, but trading gains fell $14.8 million to $12.9 million primarily due to lower fair value on the Babcock & Wilcox investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The model estimated “Total revenues” at “~$295M” and “Investment gains” at “~$75M,” based on “SpaceX carry, flat BW.”

surprises.description: Net income available to common shareholders was $18.5 million, below the preview’s $50–70 million model. This was a substantially weaker bottom-line result than anticipated despite the strong operating adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income available to common shareholders was $18.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net income to common” Q2 estimate: “~$50–70M.”

surprises.description: Management said it could cover both remaining-2026 note maturities with investment securities and cash, addressing the preview’s central concern about whether the September maturity was funded. The stated maturities total just over $300 million, versus $723 million in investment securities plus more than $150 million in cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two senior note maturities in the remainder of 2026 totaling just over $300 million ($142 million due September 30 and $164 million due December 31), which management says it can cover with $723 million in investment securities plus over $150 million in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called whether the September maturity was “fully covered” the “single most important sentence on the call,” and noted “$337M against $175.8M of cash at Q1-end.”

surprises.description: The preview expected about $70.4 million net from the SpaceX carried-interest position, but the call quantified a $26.4 million first-half increase in carried-interest value from a fund owning SpaceX. The call facts do not establish a like-for-like Q2 amount, but they do not confirm the expected full-sized recognition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half gains [were] driven by a $26.4 million increase in carried interest value from a fund owning SpaceX.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had guided to “~$84.2M gross / $70.4M net” from SpaceX carried interest and framed Q2 recognition as a key issue.

surprises.description: The debt picture was mixed against the preview’s estimates: total debt was slightly above the modeled range, while net debt was below its modeled range. Thus gross debt reduction fell a little short of the model, but net leverage was better than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt was reduced by $497 million from December 2024 to $1.277 billion at June 30, 2026, with net debt declining $87 million in the quarter to $285 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Total debt” at “~$1.15–1.25B” and “Net debt” at “$300–380M.”

surprises.description: The call cited several signs of Capital Markets activity building: $21 billion of aggregate deal value, five senior producers added, dormant institutional accounts reactivated, and ATM fees more than doubling sequentially. The preview expected Capital Markets momentum to improve, but these concrete activity indicators were not quantified in its outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The firm participated in transactions representing $21 billion in aggregate deal value in Q2, added 5 senior producers, reactivated dormant institutional accounts, and saw ATM fees more than double sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 as BRS’s “best capital-raising quarter in five years (~$10B raised)” and said Riley expected deal share to “go up meaningfully.”

in_line: Preferred dividends remained suspended, consistent with the preview’s stated base case that suspension would continue; the call added that management was directing capital toward higher-return opportunities.

surprises.description: ResMed reported Q4 revenue of $1.5 billion, above the preview’s $1.46 billion consensus and its $1.48–$1.50 billion bull scenario. The gap was modest, but the result landed above the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue grew 9% (8% constant currency) to $1.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $1.46B” consensus; the bull scenario was “$1.48–1.50B.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $2.95 beat the $2.90 consensus, but only reached the bottom of the preview’s $2.95–$3.00 buy-side whisper range. That makes the surprise positive versus consensus but not versus the more demanding expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS up 16% to $2.95.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS $2.90” consensus; “Buy-side whisper is realistically $2.95–$3.00.”

surprises.description: Q4 gross margin was 62.3%, below the preview’s 62.8%–63.0% base-case range and down about 50 basis points sequentially. ResMed attributed the sequential decline to electronic-component and freight inflation and a 20-basis-point FX headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP gross margin expanded 90 basis points year-over-year to 62.3%, though it declined ~50 basis points sequentially due to inflation in electronic components/freight and a 20bp FX headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario called for “GM 62.8–63.0%”; the preview identified Q3 gross margin as 62.8%.

surprises.description: ResMed issued its first-ever forward revenue and EPS guidance, whereas the preview said the company did not guide revenue or EPS. The FY2027 core revenue range of 5%–7% constant-currency growth is below the preview’s long-term high-single-digit growth framework; core EPS growth is stronger at 12%–14% excluding deal-related dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For the first time in company history, ResMed issued forward guidance: FY2027 core constant currency revenue growth of 5%-7% and non-GAAP EPS of $12 to $12.25 (7%-10% reported growth).” It added: “Excluding ~$0.30 dilution from the MatrixCare divestiture and ~$0.20 dilution from the Noctrix acquisition, FY2027 core EPS growth is guided to 12%-14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company does not guide revenue or EPS”; the long-term algorithm was “high-single-digit revenue growth through 2030 with earnings growing faster than revenue.”

surprises.description: The Astral field safety notice creates an unanticipated FY2027 sales suspension and a measurable financial drag: about $75 million of revenue and $0.15 of EPS, with a $42 million provision booked in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Astral field safety notice creates a ~$75 million (130bp) FY2027 revenue headwind and ~$0.15 EPS drag, as ResMed suspends all new Astral sales for the year; a $42 million provision was booked in Q4.”

surprises.description: ResMed disclosed a MatrixCare divestiture that will remove about $220 million in revenue and $58 million in non-GAAP operating profit, and will dilute FY2027 EPS by about $0.30. The preview discussed portfolio-review questions but did not anticipate a sale; TSAs are expected to largely offset stranded costs in year one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MatrixCare divestiture, expected to close around September 1, removes ~$220 million in revenue and $58 million in non-GAAP operating profit, with TSAs expected to largely offset stranded costs in year one.” The FY2027 guide excludes “~$0.30 dilution from the MatrixCare divestiture.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that mid-single-digit Residential Care Software growth could “revive[] portfolio-review questions,” but did not forecast a divestiture.

surprises.description: ResMed announced a much larger FY2027 shareholder-return program than the preview specified: over $1.85 billion in total, including $1.5 billion of buybacks and a 10% dividend increase. The preview noted a planned Q4 buyback and the existing dividend, but not a comparable FY2027 commitment.
