surprises.fact_evidence: “ResMed plans to return over $1.85 billion to shareholders in FY2027 (up over 75% YoY), including $1.5 billion in buybacks (with a $450 million accelerated repurchase funded by MatrixCare proceeds) and a 10% dividend increase to $0.66/share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$175M buyback planned for Q4” and a “$0.60 dividend,” and flagged capital allocation as a topic for the incoming CFO.

surprises.description: Life-support device revenue fell sharply in both reported regions—45% in the Americas and 38% in Rest of World. The preview focused on expected growth in total devices and did not flag declines of this scale in life-support products.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 Americas life support device revenue fell 45% and Rest-of-World fell 38%.”

in_line: Masks grew 10%–12%, broadly in line with the preview’s 10.5% consensus for Masks & other.

The GLP-1/PAP analysis broadly matched the preview’s expected evidence: the preview described a cohort showing patients were about 11% more likely to start PAP and roughly 6% more likely to resupply at three years; the call reported 11% more likely to start and about 6% more likely to resupply at three years.

surprises.description: SIGA’s Q2 revenue was about $41 million, well above the preview’s modeled ~$23 million. The main driver was $24 million of IV TPOXX delivered in Q2 versus roughly $5 million modeled for the quarter; that delivery also completed the final product order under the 19C contract earlier than the preview’s end-of-Q3 deadline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 product-related revenues were $38 million,” including “$24 million of IV TPOXX” and $13 million of oral TPOXX; R&D revenue was approximately $3 million. The Q2 IV delivery “fulfilled the final product order under SIGA's 19C contract.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Q2 total revenue at “~$23M” (range $18–30M) and IV TPOXX at “~$5M”; it said $26M of IV deliveries was due by the end of Q3.

surprises.description: Quarterly profitability materially exceeded the modeled level: net income was about $12 million and diluted EPS was $0.17, compared with modeled net income of ~$5 million and EPS of ~$0.07. Pre-tax operating income was also about $14 million versus the preview’s ~$6 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income was approximately $12 million, or $0.17 fully diluted EPS”; pre-tax operating income was “approximately $14 million for the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Operating income ~$6M,” “Net income ~$5M,” and diluted “EPS ~$0.07.”

surprises.description: Cash ended June above the preview’s expected range: SIGA reported approximately $118 million, versus the preview’s estimate of $95–105 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: SIGA ended June 30, 2026 with “approximately $118 million in cash and no debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash (6/30/26) ~$95–105M.”

surprises.description: Management described a concrete goal of pursuing a new international customer contract with an order and hopes to deliver against it by March next year. The preview identified international orders as a possible upside, but did not point to this specific target or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “targeting a new international customer contract with an order, and hopes to deliver against that order by March of next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any first order” or “any new international procurement” as items to watch, and listed a new international order as a bull-case possibility.

in_line: The preview expected about $13 million of oral TPOXX in Q2; SIGA reported $13 million sold to two international customers.
The preview modeled approximately $3 million of Q2 R&D revenue; SIGA reported approximately $3 million.

No new U.S. procurement contract was in place, and management did not report an award or a firm award timeline. The preview had highlighted the missing follow-on contract and expected the commentary to remain a key uncertainty.

The preview expected pediatric Phase 1 results in H2 2026 and a PEP FDA submission within 12 months of May 2026; management’s targets of results by year-end 2026 and submission in H1 2027 are broadly consistent with those windows.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $17 million, above the preview’s $11–13 million guided range and roughly $5 million above its ~$12 million consensus estimate. This was a substantially stronger result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $17 million,” well above the guided range of “$11-13 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$12M” consensus; company guide “$11–13M.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $39–46 million from $35–45 million, rather than merely maintaining the prior range as the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raising adjusted EBITDA guidance to $39-46 million from $35-45 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “FY reaffirmed at $280–295M and EBITDA $35–45M.” The preview also called maintaining $35–45M the key test.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $72.1 million, below the $73.54 million consensus and at the bottom of the company’s $72–77 million range. The miss was modest, but weaker than the preview’s base-case $73–75 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue came in at approximately $72.1 million,” at the “lower end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus: “$73.54M”; base case: “$73–75M.”

surprises.description: Despite the stronger Q2 and higher full-year EBITDA outlook, management said second-half adjusted EBITDA would be under $17 million versus about $25 million in the first half, citing lower gross margins, increased R&D and commercial spending, and normalizing expenses. That signals a sharper near-term slowdown than the preview’s cost-discipline framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-half adjusted EBITDA is expected to decline to under $17 million versus $25 million in the first half,” due to gross margins of about 68%, $4 million more R&D/commercial spend, and normalizing operating expenses.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “Cost cuts … continue offsetting volume decline,” and its central question was whether the “$35–45M FY EBITDA guide survives.”

surprises.description: The FY26 revenue range was reduced again: its top end fell from $295 million to $290 million, while the low end stayed at $280 million. The preview’s base case expected the prior range to be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year revenue guidance to $280-290 million (cutting the top end).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 baseline FY26 revenue guidance: “$280–295M.” Base case: “FY reaffirmed at $280–295M.”

surprises.description: The company reported only 770 systems placed, below the preview’s base-case expectation of 800–900 and continuing the equipment weakness the preview highlighted. This was a weaker placement result than expected, though not as low as the preview’s bear-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only 770 systems placed versus 957 in the prior year,” reflecting continued capital equipment weakness.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “placements 800–900”; bull case: “placements >900.”

surprises.description: The company moved beyond the reverse-split risk discussed in the preview and said it would seek shareholder approval at a September 22 special meeting. This makes the potential listing-related action more concrete than the preview’s discussion of a possible future split.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received a NASDAQ notice for trading below the $1 minimum bid price and will seek shareholder approval for a reverse stock split at a September 22 special meeting.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a reverse split might be required and warned that “any mention of a reverse split” would pull forward dilution fears; it described the deadline and possible second 180-day period.

surprises.description: Consumables revenue declined 3.5%, a milder decline than the preview’s base-case estimate of 4–6%. The reported decline was still the second consecutive one, and the call did not provide the ex-China figure the preview identified as the key test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumables revenue declined 3.5% to $53.9 million on lower utilization,” marking the “second consecutive quarterly decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “consumables −4–6%”; the preview ranked “Consumables revenue ex-China” as the highest-importance metric.

surprises.description: Management outlined a US device-rental program and a product pipeline spanning a Q4 booster, a non-HydroFacial device planned for 2027, and a next-generation HydroFacial platform targeted for 2028. These were additional growth initiatives not anticipated in the preview, though most are not near-term revenue catalysts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New growth initiatives include a US device rental program launched in August, a next-generation HydroFacial platform targeting a 2028 launch, a new clinically validated booster in Q4, and a new non-HydroFacial device planned for 2027.”

in_line: Management’s stated plan to repay the approximately $103 million October 2026 convertible maturity with cash on hand matched the preview’s expectation of an explicit cash-repayment plan.
The installed base grew 3.8% to 36,516 systems, broadly in line with the preview’s Q1 baseline of 36,400 systems and 4% growth.

surprises.description: The preview treated Q2 revenue of about $122.5 million as essentially set at the pre-announced high end; the reported $123.8 million was about $1.3 million above that level and grew 10.8% year over year, faster than the preview's 9.3%–9.6% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $123.8 million, up 10.8% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “High end → ~$122.5M”; revenue growth expected at “+9.3% to +9.6%.”

surprises.description: Q2 profitability substantially exceeded the preview's expected high-end operating income: the reported 12.9% non-GAAP operating margin implies roughly $16 million of operating income on the reported revenue, versus the preview's estimate of about $10.3 million. The preview had characterized the quarter as de-risked, but this was a notable additional margin beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin reached 12.9%, up 370 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income” consensus “~$10.3M”; pre-announced “High end → ~$10.3M.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year profitability outlook well beyond the prior ranges: non-GAAP operating income guidance is now $68.3–$70.3 million versus $54.9–$60.4 million, and EPS is $1.11–$1.15 versus $0.88–$0.97. The preview identified the full-year outlook as the central uncertainty but expected, at most, a maintained or narrowed outlook in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance, with non-GAAP operating income of $68.3–$70.3 million … and non-GAAP EPS of $1.11–$1.15.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY2026 guidance: non-GAAP operating income “$54.9–$60.4M,” non-GAAP EPS “$0.88–$0.97”; base case: “Maintained, narrowed to high half.”

surprises.description: Management raised the Q4 exit-margin target to about 17%, above the preview's stated target of about 15% and the preview's bull-case threshold of 17%–18%+. This indicates more of the cost savings is expected to flow through to margins than the prior target implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided to exit Q4 2026 with a non-GAAP operating margin near 17%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management targeted exiting Q4'26 at “~15% non-GAAP operating margin”; the preview said buy-side wanted “≥17%.”

surprises.description: The announced workforce reduction was already known, but management now says it will reduce the non-GAAP cost structure by at least $50 million annually, above the preview's estimated $30–$40 million of gross annualized savings. Full realization is not expected until 2027, which tempers the benefit near term.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A roughly 20% headcount reduction expected to cut its non-GAAP cost structure by at least $50 million on an annualized run-rate basis, though full realization won't occur until 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$30–40M gross annualized savings.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance is a little softer than the preview's implied H2 run rate: the $123.3–$124.1 million range has a midpoint of $123.7 million, below the preview's implied roughly $124–$126 million per quarter. Management also expects CRPO to moderate and the sub-$30,000 customer cohort to turn slightly negative before stabilizing in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue guidance of $123.3–$124.1 million implies deceleration, with management expecting CRPO to moderate and the sub-30K cohort to turn slightly negative before stabilizing in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The FY guide implied H2 revenue of “$248.5–$251.5M, or ~$124–$126M per quarter”; the preview said “≥$124M = intact.”

surprises.description: Management identified the lapping of the Newswhip acquisition starting in Q3 as an additional headwind. The preview discussed possible SMB weakness and decelerating growth, but did not flag this specific acquisition comparison as a source of pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged continuing headwinds including lapping the Newswhip acquisition starting Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: The company said it plans to begin executing its $50 million buyback this quarter. The preview highlighted buyback pace as a key signal and warned that zero usage would be a negative tell, so a stated near-term start is a positive update, although no execution amount was given.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Planning to begin executing its $50 million buyback this quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “~10% of market cap” and that “zero usage is a tell”; it described aggressive execution as a bull-case signal.

surprises.description: The call disclosed stronger contract-duration and booking indicators that the preview had not quantified: multi-year contracts are now nearly half of the mix, compared with about one-third two years ago, and Q2 ACV rose 14.8% year over year. These provide new evidence of contract strength beyond the preview's focus on larger customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multi-year contracts now represent nearly half of the contract mix, up from about one-third two years ago, and Q2 ACV increased 14.8% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $8.3 million, up about 60% year over year, with trailing-12-month free cash flow around $54 million. The preview did not provide a free-cash-flow expectation, so this is new favorable information rather than a quantified beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP free cash flow was $8.3 million, up approximately 60% year-over-year, bringing trailing-12-month free cash flow to roughly $54 million.”

in_line: The roughly 20% workforce reduction itself was already announced before the release; the surprise is the stated savings estimate, not the cut.
The $18–$20 million restructuring charge, substantially all in Q3, matched the preview's expectation.

The $30,000-and-above customer cohort exceeding 60% of subscription revenue was in line with the preview's expectation that it had crossed 60%; the reported 20% growth is broadly consistent with the preview's cited 21% trailing-twelve-month growth.
The sub-$30,000 cohort remained weak, with stabilization framed for 2027; this was broadly consistent with the preview's expectation of continued SMB deceleration and stabilization into next year.
Management reaffirmed the target of reaching 30% under the Rule of 40 framework by Q4 2027, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $11.4 million, above the preview’s $10.0–10.5 million consensus range and its $9.3 million estimate. It also grew 1.7% year over year, rather than declining 6%–11% as consensus implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $11.4 million, up only 1.7% year-over-year from $11.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$10.0–10.5M” and “YoY implied | −6% to −11%”; the preview’s own estimate was “$9.3M.”

surprises.description: Management reiterated the $54–57 million full-year revenue range instead of cutting it or narrowing it toward the low end, as the preview’s base case anticipated. That leaves the previously stated growth target intact despite the preview’s concerns about the H2 ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $54 million to $57 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A cut or a ‘narrow to the low end’ is my base case”; the base scenario anticipated the guide being “trimmed to ~$48–52M or narrowed to low end.”

surprises.description: CMS granted a new G-code extending TriNav reimbursement to the office-based lab setting, adding a site of care and potentially widening access. The preview did not identify this reimbursement expansion as an expected catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In July, CMS granted a new G-code extending TriNav reimbursement into the office-based lab (OBL) setting, expanding site-of-care access.”

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter at $46.3 million, below the preview’s expected $48–50 million. The gap was $1.7–3.7 million versus that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with approximately $46.3 million in cash, which management believes fully funds its strategic growth plan.”

surprises.description: Sales and marketing expense reached $11.4 million—equal to quarterly revenue—and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to about $7.1 million. The preview flagged sales-force ramp costs and productivity as issues, but did not anticipate this reported spending level or the wider EBITDA loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to approximately $7.1 million from $5.3 million in Q2 2025, driven by sales force expansion costs”; “Sales and marketing expenses surged to $11.4 million from $7.2 million a year earlier, equaling the entire quarter's revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted a “6–9 month ramp on new hires” and flagged “Sales-force productivity” as a key metric to watch, without giving an expense or EBITDA forecast.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 86.8%, slightly above the preview’s expected 85–86% range. The reported improvement was attributed to lower TriNav unit costs and manufacturing improvements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 86.8% from 83.9% year-over-year due to lower TriNav unit costs and manufacturing improvements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~85–86%.”

in_line: TriNav Advance remained uncleared and past the MDUFA goal date, consistent with the preview’s expectation that clearance would still be pending; the call continued to anticipate clearance near-term.
Management’s expectation of sequential growth improvement in Q3 and a stronger Q4 broadly matched the preview’s view that meaningful progress was deferred to Q3–Q4.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $56.4 million, below the preview’s $60.5 million consensus and its $58–62 million base case; the preview expected year-over-year growth, but revenue was essentially flat. This is weaker than expected even though it landed just above the preview’s bear-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $56.4 million, essentially flat year-over-year versus $56.8 million, as retail partners kept channel inventory below historical norms through much of the quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $60.5M”; “YoY +6.6%”; base scenario: “$58–62M (in line).”

surprises.description: Gross margin was reported at 38.8%, far above the preview’s 29–32% estimate, but $4.3 million of tariff refunds lifted the headline figure. Excluding those refunds, margin was approximately 31.2%—within the preview’s expected range rather than a comparable jump in underlying performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin rose 660 basis points to 38.8% from 32.2%, but excluding $4.3 million of tariff refunds the underlying margin was approximately 31.2%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~29–32% (est.)”; the preview said the bull case required “a snapback toward 32%+.”

surprises.description: Retail partners continued to keep channel inventory below historical norms, rather than showing the rebound the preview said would test management’s explanation for Q1 weakness. That leaves the expected channel restock unconfirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Retail partners kept channel inventory below historical norms through much of the quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 would test management’s expectation that channel inventories would “rebound,” and identified “channel restock lands” as a bull-case driver.

surprises.description: Operating expenses rose sharply to 44% of revenue, and the net loss widened despite improved gross margins. That runs counter to the operating-expense leverage the preview said was needed to support the full-year EBITDA target, although adjusted EBITDA did turn positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: Operating expenses jumped to $24.9 million (44% of revenue) from $18.6 million (33% of revenue), reflecting increased marketing spend; net loss widened to $7.3 million from $2.9 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said meeting the EBITDA guide “demands simultaneous volume, gross margin, and opex leverage”; its Q2 adjusted EBITDA estimate was “~$0M.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased roughly $25 million of stock in one quarter, a substantial use of the authorization despite the balance-sheet concerns the preview highlighted. The preview explicitly identified an aggressive repurchase as a possible signal of confidence, so the scale of the buyback is favorable versus a pause.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company repurchased roughly $25 million of stock (nearly 2 million shares at an average $12.53) in Q2, leaving about $31 million remaining under its buyback authorization.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch buyback pace against “$56M remaining authorization” and that “aggressive repurchase signals confidence; a pause signals liquidity discipline.”

surprises.description: New tariff actions raised the effective rate on China and Vietnam imports, an unflagged cost risk, though management expects to largely offset the impact without materially affecting profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: New tariff actions raised the effective rate on China and Vietnam imports to approximately 12.5% from 10%, but management expects to largely mitigate the impact without materially affecting profitability.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive $1.3 million, above the preview’s roughly breakeven estimate, even as revenue missed and marketing costs rose.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA improved to positive $1.3 million from negative $3.0 million in the prior year period, reflecting stronger gross margins.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$0M (est.).”

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $335–$355 million in revenue and $44–$48 million in adjusted EBITDA, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the guide could be reaffirmed.
Underlying gross margin excluding tariff refunds was approximately 31.2%, within the preview’s estimated 29–32% range.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $73.2 million, about 6% below the preview’s $78.13 million consensus, and the year-over-year decline was 25% rather than the expected 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue fell 25% year-over-year to $73.2 million,” with continued demand weakness in both end markets.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $78.13M”; implied year-over-year decline: “-20.0%.”

surprises.description: A one-time $5.1 million tariff recovery lifted adjusted EPS to $0.34, far above the $0.03 consensus, but EPS was only about $0.04 excluding the recovery. The recovery is excluded from full-year guidance, so the headline beat did not represent a comparable improvement in underlying earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A non-recurring $5.1 million tariff recovery boosted adjusted EPS to $0.34 per diluted share”; excluding it, adjusted non-GAAP profit was “~$0.04 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. non-GAAP diluted EPS | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $0.03.”

surprises.description: Gross margin excluding the tariff recovery was about 27%, below the preview’s key 28% threshold and down from 29.9% a year earlier. Higher component costs and unfavorable currency were additional pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted non-GAAP gross margin was “35.4% as reported but only ~27% excluding the tariff recovery, down from 29.9% a year ago,” pressured by “~240 bps of higher component costs and ~150 bps of unfavorable currency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin — Q1 26.1% ... Need ≥28% to keep the FY math alive”; the base scenario expected “27–28%.”

surprises.description: The company reported $32.4 million of cash and $11.6 million of net cash, with no borrowings on its U.S. credit line. That is stronger than the preview’s $29.8 million of cash and roughly $3.4 million of net debt, and it had warned that further borrowing would be a red flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $32.4 million in cash, $11.6 million in net cash, no borrowings on its U.S. credit line, and available borrowing capacity of $48.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash / total debt / net debt | $29.8M / $33.3M / ~$3.4M”; the preview flagged “Any further LOC draw ... as a genuine red flag.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses fell $6.2 million year over year, a larger reduction than the $5.3 million reduction cited for Q1. The savings were substantial, though R&D fell further as well, to $4.3 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted non-GAAP operating expenses fell $6.2 million, or 24%, year-over-year,” with R&D declining “to $4.3 million from $7 million” and SG&A “to $16.8 million from $21.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “$5.3M Y/Y reduction in Q1” and asked, “Is there more, and at what point does R&D cutting compromise the Connected Home pipeline?”

surprises.description: A new smart-thermostat platform for a major HVAC OEM had begun mass production, with additional Q4 volume requested. The preview identified conversion of thermostat programs into shipments as a key debate, so production progress was more concrete than the concern that deployments might keep slipping.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new smart thermostat platform for a major HVAC OEM began mass production with additional Q4 volume requested.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “Connected Home ≥ $28M and a named thermostat program conversion,” and said to watch whether programs were “actually converting to shipments.”

surprises.description: UEI named CFO Wade Jenke as CEO as interim CEO Rick Carnifax stepped down effective that day. The preview identified a permanent CEO appointment as a high-variance possibility, but did not anticipate this specific immediate transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interim CEO Rick Carnifax stepped down effective August 6th, with CFO Wade Jenke appointed as the new CEO.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Carnifax as interim CEO for 13 months and said “A permanent appointment” was a possible high-variance narrative item.

surprises.description: UEI filed a new IP lawsuit against Amazon on the day of the call, introducing a legal development the preview did not flag. The shareholder impact is unclear from the provided information.
surprises.fact_evidence: “UEI filed a new IP lawsuit against Amazon the day of the call.”

surprises.description: The Roku litigation has a court date scheduled for 2027, a legal timeline not mentioned in the preview. The significance of that timing is unclear from the provided information.
surprises.fact_evidence: UEI “continues litigation against Roku, which has a court date scheduled for 2027.”

in_line: Excluding the one-time tariff recovery, adjusted EPS was about $0.04, close to the preview’s $0.03 consensus and within its $0.00–$0.06 base-case range.
Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.45–$0.65, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Dispensed Y-CANTH applicator units were much stronger than the preview's estimate: 19,626 units versus about 17,600 expected, and growth was over 28% sequentially versus the preview's estimate of roughly 15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dispensed applicator units rose over 28% to 19,626 units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dispensed applicator units ~17,600 (+15% q/q, +31% y/y).”

surprises.description: Despite the stronger unit count, implied U.S. Y-CANTH revenue per dispensed unit was about $260 ($5.1 million divided by 19,626 units), below the preview's roughly $285 estimate. That suggests the higher volume translated into less revenue per unit than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “US Y-CANTH net product revenue of $5.1 million” and “dispensed applicator units rose over 28% to 19,626 units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue / dispensed unit | ~$285.”

surprises.description: The reported GAAP loss was substantially worse than the preview's GAAP estimate: $0.62 per share versus about $0.42 expected. The preview cautioned that consensus EPS could use a different basis, but its own GAAP model was close to the reported comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $13.2 million ($0.62 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS | ($0.42)” and “EPS | ($0.41)” with a caveat to confirm the basis.

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was below the preview's estimate, at $11.2 million versus roughly $12.5 million expected. However, management said the new facility could extend runway into 2028, well beyond the preview's expectation of runway only into Q1 2027; that extension depends on full access to a costly facility, with $15 million contingent on milestones.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$11.2 million in cash on the balance sheet as of June 30, 2026” and “cash runway to extend into 2028, ... assuming full access to the credit facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash, 6/30/26 | ~$12.5M” and management had guided runway “into Q1 2027.”

surprises.description: Rather than the preview's base case of no financing detail, Verrica secured up to $27.5 million of non-dilutive credit from its chairman. The funding comes with a high coupon and a 16% IRR catch-up payment, and $15 million is conditional on meeting milestones, so the liquidity support is meaningful but costly and not fully assured.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A non-dilutive credit facility of up to $27.5 million from chairman Paul Manning,” with “$12.5 million available immediately and $15 million contingent” on milestones; it carries “SOFR plus 8%” and “a 16% IRR catch-up payment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base case anticipated “no financing detail”; it described a runway extension or a named partner as a bull-case outcome.

surprises.description: The Madomi Israel agreement's reported economics were not specified in the preview: Verica receives 60% of net selling price and may receive up to $8.2 million in regulatory and commercial milestones. The signing itself was anticipated in the preview, so the surprise is the disclosed economics rather than the existence of an agreement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new Israel distribution agreement with Madomi Pharma provides Verica 60% of net selling price plus up to $8.2 million in regulatory and commercial milestone payments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's model included “License & collaboration (Torii Japan supply, Medomie signing) | $0.8M.”

in_line: Total revenue of $5.9 million was close to the preview's $5.7–$5.9 million base range and modestly above the $5.73 million consensus estimate.
U.S. Y-CANTH net product revenue of $5.1 million was close to the preview's $5.0 million estimate, despite the much stronger-than-expected unit growth.

The preview already expected Torii to fund the first $40 million (about 90%) of the common-warts Phase 3 program; the call confirmed that funding arrangement and said Verica's cost share would be payable from future Japanese payments.
The VP315 abscopal-effect finding in untreated lesions was already noted in the preview; the call provided additional lesion-level detail rather than introducing the effect as a new finding.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $67.5 million, below the preview’s functional expectation of roughly $68.5–68.9 million, even though it was within the company’s stated quarterly guidance. The 15.5% year-over-year growth rate was within the preview’s implied growth range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 total revenue was $67.5 million, up 15.5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The functional bar is the high end of guidance plus Weave's habitual beat” and “the number that ‘meets’ buy-side expectations is ~$68.5–68.9M.”

surprises.description: Weave lowered its full-year revenue outlook rather than raising it or nudging it higher: the new $273–275 million range is below the prior $275–278 million range and the preview’s expected $276.94 million consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $273-275 million due to a go-to-market transition that caused bookings to fall slightly below expectations during May-July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY range is $275–278M and consensus sits at $276.9M”; the preview described a lift to “~$278–280M” as the bull trigger and expected a raise in its base case.

surprises.description: Operating performance was better than the preview’s cautious margin setup: Q2 operating income exceeded the top of its guidance, and management raised full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance despite lowering revenue guidance. Sales and marketing costs and incremental operating-income conversion also improved sharply.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating income reached $3.2 million (4.7% margin) … above the top end of guidance”; “Sales and marketing expenses fell to 38% of revenue,” improving 240 basis points sequentially; and revenue-growth-to-incremental-operating-income conversion rose to 34%. Management raised full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance to $12–14 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 non-GAAP operating income guidance of “$2.1M – $3.1M” and said the implied 2H ramp required “$5.4–8.4M,” warning to watch whether management “defends the back-half ramp or quietly leans on the low end.”

surprises.description: The deeper Athena One integration was an unanticipated expansion opportunity: Weave advanced from level one to level four, opening access to a large specialty-medical provider base and potential for higher average selling prices.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The deeper Athena One integration advanced Weave from a level-one to a level-four integration, unlocking access to over 160,000 specialty medical providers and higher ASP potential.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for evidence that AI adoption was translating into dollars, but the reported AI evidence was interaction volume rather than AI revenue, attach revenue, or per-location ARPU. The usage figures show continued adoption, but do not resolve the monetization question the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Custom AI interactions totaled 70 million (up 165% YoY) and Call Intelligence interactions rose 143%,” with no AI revenue or ARPU figure in the reported facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for ARPU-per-location or AI attach revenue disclosure” and “Adoption without ARPU lift is the bear's exhibit A.”

surprises.description: Dental added its most locations in eight quarters, a specific strength not called out in the preview’s location-add expectations. The preview did expect record adds overall and highlighted specialty medical, so this is a narrower positive surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Weave added a record number of new locations on both gross and net basis, with dental adding the most locations in eight quarters and specialty medical showing the largest increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “record gross and net location additions, with strength in specialty medical and DSO/multi-location enterprise.”

in_line: Q2 revenue growth of 15.5% year over year was within the preview’s implied 14.9%–16.6% range, despite revenue missing the preview’s higher functional dollar bar.
Payments revenue grew at roughly twice the total revenue rate, consistent with the preview’s expectation that payments growth above 2x total growth would need to repeat.
Gross and net location additions were record-setting, as the preview expected.
Free cash flow was clearly positive at $8.7 million, meeting the preview’s expectation for solidly positive Q2 free cash flow.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 74%, well above the preview’s 64–66% consensus estimate. Even excluding the settlement revenue, margin was 67%, and management cited lower manufacturing costs and $2.6 million of tariff refunds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 74% from 72% (or from 67% excluding settlement revenue), aided by lower manufacturing costs including $2.6 million of tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~64–66% (implied)” and “Gross margin vs. ~65% consensus.”

surprises.description: TXG raised its full-year revenue outlook to $610–630 million rather than maintaining the previewed $600–625 million range. The new range implies 2–5% growth excluding 2025 settlement revenue, above the preview’s 0–4% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $610–630 million, representing 2–5% growth over 2025 excluding nonrecurring settlement revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: $600–625M maintained (0–4% growth ex-2025 settlements).”

surprises.description: Atera orders had already greatly exceeded the full-year target of about 40 instruments by the end of Q2, stronger demand evidence than the preview’s roughly 40-unit shipment plan alone suggested. However, the shipment outlook stayed unchanged because manufacturing capacity is constrained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atera booked orders already greatly exceeded the full-year target of ~40 instruments by the end of Q2, though the ~40 unit shipment outlook remains unchanged due to manufacturing capacity constraints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said ~40 units ship Q3–Q4 2026, weighted to Q4”; the preview said investors wanted a “hard pre-order number” and noted production capacity could be the constraint.

surprises.description: Revenue excluding the $1.6 million patent settlement was $149.4 million, above the preview’s $146.7 million consensus and roughly flat core-revenue expectation. The reported $151 million also included the settlement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $151 million, or $149.4 million excluding a $1.6 million patent settlement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $146.7M” and “Revenue ex-settlement … $146.7M”; the preview described this as “roughly flat core revenue.”

surprises.description: Single Cell consumables revenue grew only 3% despite double-digit reaction-volume growth, a wider volume-versus-revenue gap than the preview’s Q1 reference of 6% revenue growth highlighted as a key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Single Cell consumables grew only 3% despite double-digit reaction volume growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1: $88.9M, +6% revenue with double-digit reaction-volume growth (i.e., price/mix erosion). The volume-vs-revenue gap matters … Watch whether the spread widens.”

surprises.description: Spatial consumables grew 16%, slower than the preview’s bullish case that Xenium would sustain the Q1 pace of about 31%. The preview flagged this as a key measure of whether the spatial installed base continued consuming through the instrument pause.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Spatial consumables revenue grew 16%, driven primarily by Xenium.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Xenium consumables sustain the Q1 +31% pace”; the preview also said to watch whether Xenium was “still consuming even while instrument buying pauses.”

surprises.description: Management forecast a modest sequential revenue decline in Q3, whereas the preview’s bridge assumed Q3 would be approximately level with Q2. The expected significant Q4 step-up, largely from Atera shipments, remained part of the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a modest sequential revenue step-down in Q3 as the Spatial transition peaks, followed by a significant Q4 step-up driven mostly by Atera shipments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If Q3 ≈ Q2 as guided (~$147M)” and “the credibility of the Q4 hockey stick.”

surprises.description: APAC revenue declined 19%, partly because China had about $4 million of prior-year pull-forward buying ahead of tariffs. The preview did not flag this regional weakness, while Americas and EMEA grew.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC revenue declined 19%, partly reflecting ~$4 million of prior-year pull-forward buying in China ahead of tariffs, while Americas grew 6% and EMEA grew 15%.”

surprises.description: Cash and marketable securities ended the quarter at $552 million, above the preview’s $525–540 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $552 million in cash and marketable securities (up $105 million year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash & securities ~$525–540M.”

surprises.description: Management estimated Atera’s maximum annual utilization at $1.5 million to $2–3 million per instrument, roughly twice Xenium’s, but said actual pull-through remains unquantified because no units have shipped. This added a potentially attractive use-case estimate without confirming realized demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atera's maximum utilization is estimated at $1.5 million to $2–3 million per instrument annually, roughly 2x that of Xenium, though actual pull-through remains unquantified since no units have shipped.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors wanted “a dollar or unit backlog figure” and “a 2027 capacity trajectory,” but did not discuss utilization potential.

surprises.description: TXG acquired Proteintech Genomics to strengthen proteomics and multiomics capabilities, a transaction the preview did not anticipate; no financial terms or expected impact were provided in the call facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company … acquired Proteintech Genomics to strengthen proteomics and multiomics capabilities.”

in_line: The expected pause in instrument purchases ahead of Atera was evident: total instrument revenue fell 47% year over year, with Chromium instruments down 46% and Spatial instruments down 48%. The preview modeled Spatial instruments at $3–4 million, but the facts do not provide the actual dollar amount for a direct comparison.

The roughly 40-unit Atera shipment outlook remained unchanged, consistent with the preview’s Q3–Q4 shipment expectation; the call also retained the anticipated significant Q4 step-up, driven mostly by Atera shipments.

surprises.description: HCI reported diluted EPS of $5.60, versus the preview’s $5.04 consensus and $5.25 estimate. That reversed the preview’s expectation of a year-over-year decline: EPS was up from $5.18 a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS reached $5.60 in Q2 (up from $5.18 a year earlier).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS” consensus: “$5.04”; my estimate: “$5.25”; consensus implied YoY “‑2.7%.”

surprises.description: CORE had been flagged as at risk of a third consecutive decline, but it pivoted from commercial to residential HO3 policies and ramped to roughly $6 million of new business per month. That is a clear reversal from the trajectory investors were told to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The CORE reciprocal exchange pivoted from commercial to residential (HO3) business, ramping to roughly $6 million of new business per month over recent months since first writing HO3 policies in March.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CORE declined sharply for a second consecutive quarter. A third consecutive decline turns a one-off into a trend.”

surprises.description: HCI signed GEICO to distribute a new product, with sales already underway and a potential path to organic policy growth by year-end. The preview discussed policy growth and other distribution opportunities but did not flag a GEICO deal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed GEICO in July to distribute its new product with sales already underway,” with potential organic policy growth by year-end “without Citizens takeouts, acquisitions, or new markets.”

surprises.description: HCI said pro forma book value would exceed $150 per share when unrealized Exzeo and real-estate gains are included, well above the preview’s estimate of roughly $120–125 using the current Exzeo mark. The difference is partly attributable to the call’s inclusion of real estate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma book value would exceed $150 if unrealized gains on Exzeo and real estate were included.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On today’s XZO mark that pro forma number is closer to ~$120–125.”

surprises.description: Gross premiums earned grew 6%, below the preview’s roughly 8–9% growth expectation and estimate of about $330 million. Policy growth was offset by flat average premium per policy, so premium growth fell short of the preview’s stated test for volume to offset price softness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross premiums earned grew 6% driven by policy growth with flat average premium per policy.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross premiums earned at “~$330” million and said to watch whether “GPE growth holds ≥8%.”

surprises.description: HCI completed the entire $80 million buyback authorization, whereas the preview expected about $42.5 million to remain available through February 2027. The company has no new authorization active, so the expected ongoing buyback capacity is no longer in place.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HCI fully completed its $80 million buyback authorization, repurchasing 504,000 shares (about 4% of outstanding shares), with no new authorization currently active.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$42.5M remains through Feb 2027” and management framed the pace as “roughly 2% of shares per quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview did not identify new-client Exzeo services revenue as a contributor to HCI’s growth. The call said those services helped total revenue grow, providing an additional source of revenue beyond the premium growth the preview emphasized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 11% aided by Exzeo services revenue from new clients.”

surprises.description: Reported book value per share was $86.60, below the preview’s estimate of about $89. The shortfall was modest, even though the call also presented a much higher pro forma figure including unrealized gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Book value per share reached $86.60.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “BVPS” at “~$89.”

in_line: Total revenue grew 11%, within the preview’s 8.5–11.5% year-over-year growth range.

The Q2 loss ratio was 22%, matching the preview’s estimate of about 22%; the combined ratio was 61%, close to the preview’s roughly 60% estimate and within the stated 60–65% target absent catastrophes.

The reinsurance program’s lower cost was anticipated: the preview cited a 10% cost decrease and expected the margin benefit to show up primarily from Q3 onward. The call’s more-than-10% reduction and savings are consistent with that expectation.

surprises.description: Xponential cut its 2026 revenue outlook to $250–260 million and adjusted EBITDA outlook to $91–97 million, below the previously reaffirmed ranges of $260–270 million and $100–110 million. The EBITDA midpoint is about $11 million below the prior midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting revenue of $250-260 million and adjusted EBITDA of $91-97 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed May 7, 2026): Revenue $260–270M · Adj. EBITDA $100–110M.”

surprises.description: Same-store sales were weaker than the preview’s key target: overall comps declined 6.8%, while Club Pilates declined 5%. The overall result fell below the preview’s -3% to -5% target for making a recovery path credible.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 same-store sales declined 6.8% overall and 5% for Club Pilates, coming in below expectations and modestly weaker than Q1 trends due to top-of-funnel pressure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs to show ‑3% to ‑5% to make that path credible”; the preview also said “A print at ‑6% or worse says the fix isn't working.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was slightly below the preview’s implied $22–24 million range, and the 33% margin was well below the preview’s expectation that cost cuts could hold margin near 36%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA dropped 22% to $21.9 million and margin compressed from 37% to 33%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA not cleanly published (~$22–24M implied)”; the base case also expected “cost cuts hold margin near 36%.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in above consensus despite the year-over-year decline: $66.0 million exceeded the preview’s $64.4–64.5 million estimate range by about $1.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 revenue fell 13% year-over-year to $66.0 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus Revenue $64.4–64.5M.”

surprises.description: Merchandise revenue fell $5.1 million, with most of the decline tied to the commission-only outsourced model and continuing execution problems. The preview did not flag this transition risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merchandise revenue declined $5.1 million year-over-year, with $3.9 million tied to the new commission-only outsourced model and ongoing transition execution challenges hurting results.”

surprises.description: Xponential announced a partnership with its largest franchisee for 117 Club Pilates studios across 10 states over six years, an unanticipated addition to the pipeline amid the preview’s concern that license sales were too low to support studio growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new partnership with largest franchisee Spartan Fitness Holdings is expected to open 117 Club Pilates studios across 10 states over the next six years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1: ... only 28 licenses sold”; “28 licenses/quarter does not support 150–170 net new studios.”

in_line: The strategic review remained ongoing with no further commentary, matching the preview’s base-case expectation of “no update” on the review.
Cash of $25.0 million remained above the preview’s roughly $20 million threshold, and long-term debt of $522.4 million was close to the preview’s $523.7 million figure.
The approximately 150-studio 2026 opening outlook was at the bottom of the preview’s 150–170 guidance range.

surprises.description: Alta reported Q2 revenue of $475.5 million, below the preview’s $488.7–$493.9 million consensus range by about 3%–4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $475.5 million.”

surprises.description: Material Handling revenue was lower even though the preview expected Q1 booking strength to begin converting into revenue growth. The report also showed a strong backlog, making the weaker revenue conversion notable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Material handling delivered $19 million of adjusted EBITDA, up about 13% year-over-year despite lower revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is when those bookings should start converting”; the preview also flagged “Material Handling revenue turning positive y/y.”

surprises.description: Alta trimmed the top of its full-year adjusted EBITDA range by $5 million rather than leaving the range unchanged as the preview’s base case anticipated. Management attributed the change to delivery timing uncertainty, not weaker demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alta narrowed its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $167.5–$177.5 million, cutting the upper end by $5 million due to delivery timing uncertainty rather than weaker demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the guide as “$167.5M – $182.5M” and described the base case as “reaffirming full-year guidance.”

surprises.description: Material Handling backlog reached its highest level since 2023, and industry bookings in Alta’s areas were up 12.3% in the first half. The preview noted booking strength, but did not anticipate this backlog milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Material handling backlog rose to approximately $143 million, its highest level since 2023, with industry bookings in Alta's areas up 12.3% in the first half year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 bookings up “~20%” and lift-truck bookings up “12.7% y/y,” but gave no expectation for a backlog at this level.

surprises.description: Gross margins improved despite the revenue shortfall: total gross margin expanded year over year, and new and used equipment margins rose both year over year and sequentially. The preview did not forecast this margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total gross margins expanded roughly 70 basis points year-over-year to 26.1%”; “Companywide new and used equipment gross margins improved to 15.3% in Q2, rising both year-over-year and sequentially amid reduced OEM discounting and healthier used equipment values.”

surprises.description: Average assets fell in both Material Handling and Construction, lifting returns on assets. The preview discussed deliberate rental-fleet reductions, but did not anticipate these segment-level capital-efficiency improvements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Material handling average assets fell ~$52 million (11%) and construction average assets fell ~$77 million (8%), lifting returns on assets in both segments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Alta was “deliberately” cutting the rental fleet, but did not state an expectation for these segment average-asset reductions or returns on assets.

surprises.description: Alta reported roughly $225 million of liquidity and no meaningful debt maturities until 2029, details the preview did not identify as expected. Net leverage of about 4.7x nevertheless remained above the preview’s stated year-end target of below 4.5x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total liquidity stood at approximately $225 million with net leverage steady at roughly 4.7x and no meaningful debt maturities until 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Alta had a “sub-4.5x target for YE2026” and flagged leverage progress, but did not discuss liquidity or debt maturities.

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $48.6 million was within the preview’s modeled $48–52 million range.
Free cash flow guidance of $100–$110 million was reaffirmed, as expected.

Construction showed a seasonal recovery: adjusted EBITDA improved by $16.7 million sequentially to $30.6 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the construction season would catch up.
Ecoverse showed the tariff-margin recovery the preview was watching for: management reported that tariff-related margin pressure subsided and EBITDA rose to $2.8 million from $1.1 million.

surprises.description: Progyny lowered its FY2026 revenue range to $1.36–$1.385 billion from $1.365–$1.405 billion, including a lower high end, rather than raising above the prior high end as the preview anticipated. The new ex-transition-client growth range is also lower at 9.7%–11.7%, versus 10.1%–13.3% previously.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance projects revenue of $1.36–$1.385 billion (5.5%–7.5% growth, or 9.7%–11.7% excluding the transition client).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the bar was “a beat plus a raise above the current FY26 high end” and identified “a raise to ≥$1.42B” as validating the July run; the current range was $1.365–$1.405B.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue growth modestly exceeded the preview’s expectations: reported growth was 5.3% versus the 4.7% consensus growth rate, and growth excluding the former transition client was 11% versus the preview’s 10.4% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 5.3% on a reported basis but 11% when excluding” the former client.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave consensus growth of “+4.7%” and estimated “~+10.4%” revenue growth ex-TOC.

surprises.description: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed and its midpoint edged down, rather than being raised toward the preview’s expected $240–$246 million range. The new $233–$240 million range is only slightly above the prior range’s low end and below its $244 million high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance projects… adjusted EBITDA of $233–$240 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed current guidance of “$232–244M” and its base scenario expected EBITDA to move to “~$240–246M.”

surprises.description: Gross-margin expansion was a little less than the preview’s roughly 200-basis-point durability expectation: Q2 expansion was 180 basis points. Margin still expanded strongly, but it did not quite match the anticipated pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 180 basis points year-over-year in Q2, matching Q1's expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said holding “~200bp of expansion” was what funded the EBITDA raise and expected the efficiency and stock-compensation benefits to recur through 2026.

surprises.description: Management said it had removed most 2027 client-retention risk earlier than usual, stronger timing and risk-reduction commentary than the preview’s expectation that favorable renewals and low remaining exposure would continue converting during the selling season.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “believes it has removed the vast majority of client retention risk for 2027 earlier than usual, largely derisking client turnover.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described favorable renewals already secured for two of the largest clients and remaining renewal exposure “at its lowest level at this point relative to prior years,” while calling for selling-season conversion.

surprises.description: The FY2026 adjusted EPS range moved up slightly from the prior range and its midpoint is just above the preview’s $2.06 consensus, providing a modest positive offset to the lower revenue and EBITDA outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance projects… adjusted EPS of $2.04–$2.10.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior guidance of “$1.98–2.09” and consensus of “$2.06.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance implies 6.9%–10.1% revenue growth and management cited somewhat more pronounced summer seasonality. That is softer than the preview’s roughly 12% midpoint expectation for H2 growth, although management characterized the adjustment as small and not a change in trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $335–$345 million (6.9%–10.1% growth) reflecting a slightly more pronounced summer seasonality”; management called it “roughly a 1% adjustment at the midpoint and not a change in trend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview derived H2'26 growth of “+8.8% to +15.2% (mid +12.0%)” and flagged low-end H2 guidance as implying deceleration on clean comps.

surprises.description: Progyny Select is not expected to contribute meaningfully in 2027, with the next 12–18 months focused on signing channel partners rather than generating volume. This delays a potential source of incremental growth that the preview viewed as possible upside from upsell activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Progyny Select, the new fully-insured offering, is not expected to be a meaningful contributor in 2027,” and the next 12–18 months will focus on “signing channel partners rather than driving volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had excluded material upsell contribution from guidance and that “quantifying it is pure upside.”

in_line: The company reiterated its target of adding at least 1 million new lives, and early new-client commitments are pacing ahead of the same point last year, consistent with the preview’s expectation for early commitments to pace ahead.
Trailing-12-month adjusted EBITDA margin remained at 17.2%, consistent with the reported Q1 level and the preview’s expectation that margins hold up through platform investment.

The share repurchase activity was consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued aggressive buybacks: the company reported 10.8 million shares repurchased since November and $142.5 million remaining under the current authorization.

surprises.description: Airbnb reported $27.2 billion of Q2 gross booking value, well above the preview’s $26.42 billion consensus estimate. Growth was 16%, also ahead of the preview’s implied 12.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross booking value rose 16% to $27.2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross Booking Value… Consensus $26.42B… Implied Y/Y +12.7%.”

surprises.description: Nights and Seats Booked grew 10% and accelerated from Q1, rather than decelerating slightly as the preview expected; growth also exceeded the 8.2% consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nights and Seats Booked grew 10%, accelerating from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus sits above the ~8% that guidance (‘decelerate slightly’ from +9%, less ~100bp Middle East) implies”; consensus was “145.4M” and “+8.2%.”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue outlook of $4.69–$4.77 billion exceeds the preview’s $4.55–$4.65 billion estimate, with even the bottom of the range above the preview’s high end. The preview also expected the Q3 FX tailwind to fade, while the outlook includes about three points of FX benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $4.69–$4.77 billion (15–17% growth, including ~3 points of FX tailwind).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 revenue ~ $4.55–4.65B (+~12%)”; the preview also cited “a fading FX tailwind” and expected Q3 to have “materially less” FX benefit than Q2.

surprises.description: Airbnb raised its full-year revenue outlook to at least mid-teens growth from low-to-mid-teens growth, improving on the preview’s expected reaffirmation of the prior framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance, now expecting revenue growth of at least mid-teens (up from low-to-mid teens).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 framework was “low-to-mid-teens” revenue growth and described its base case as “FY reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA margin floor rose to at least 35.5%, above the preview’s expectation that Airbnb would reaffirm a 35% floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 35.5% (up from 35%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA margin ≥35% — reaffirm or hedge”; the base case expected “FY reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to decline slightly year over year because of investment timing, a softer near-term margin outlook than the preview’s base case of an intact margin story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expected to be down slightly year-over-year due to investment timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case described the “margin story” as “intact,” while warning that reinvestment could eat into margin in its bear case.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $1.3 billion, above the preview’s derived estimate of about $1.25 billion, even though the reported 35% margin matched the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $1.3 billion at a 35% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$1.25B / ~35%.”

surprises.description: First-time bookers grew 11%, the highest rate in four years, with acceleration across several core markets. The preview discussed new World Cup guests but did not anticipate this broader strength in first-time booking growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-time bookers grew 11%, the highest growth rate in four years, with acceleration in core markets including the U.S., France, U.K. and Australia.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “1 in 6 tournament guests are new to Airbnb” but gave no expectation for overall first-time booker growth.

surprises.description: Hotel nights are growing about three times faster than home nights, and roughly 35% of first-time hotel guests later book a home. The preview flagged hotels as a small-scale area to watch but did not anticipate these growth and conversion figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hotel nights are growing approximately 3x faster than the homes business despite still being a single-digit percentage of nights booked, and roughly 35% of first-time hotel guests return to book a home.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “hotel nights <1% of total” and advised investors to “watch for first hard numbers” on hotels.

surprises.description: Airbnb said its single service fee, which pressures pricing downward to improve competitiveness, already covers about half of active listings and is expected to reach most remaining hosts by year-end. The preview did not flag this broad rollout or its pricing implications.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The single service fee, which pressures pricing downward for competitiveness, now covers about half of active listings and is expected to roll out to the majority of remaining hosts by year-end.”

surprises.description: AI reduced customer-support cost per booking by about 16% year over year, with nearly 45% of AI-assistant issues resolved without a human agent. The preview did not anticipate these quantified efficiency gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI adoption cut customer support cost per booking by about 16% year-over-year, with nearly 45% of AI-assistant issues resolved without a human agent.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $1.3 billion and trailing-twelve-month free cash flow reached $4.8 billion, above the preview’s $4.5 billion TTM figure. The reported TTM margin was 37%, versus the preview’s 36%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Airbnb generated $1.3 billion of free cash flow in Q2 (TTM $4.8 billion, 37% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$4.5B TTM FCF (36% margin).”

surprises.description: Q2 net income included a $77 million tax benefit, an unanticipated one-off that boosted the reported $816 million result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income was $816 million, boosted by a $77 million tax benefit.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was 35%, matching the preview’s estimate of approximately 35%.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.91 substantially exceeded the preview’s adjusted estimate range of $0.62–$0.66. GAAP EPS was also $0.67, above the preview’s cited $0.37 GAAP bogey, and rose year over year rather than declining.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose to $0.91 from $0.85 year-over-year”; “GAAP net income slipped to $30.3 million from $31 million but improved to $0.67 per share from $0.64.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat ~$0.62–0.66 as the adjusted Street bogey and ~$0.37 as the GAAP bogey”; the preview also cites a $0.51 EPS estimate.

surprises.description: AMPH reported Q2 revenue of $183.9 million, above the preview’s estimates of $179.92 million and $182.06 million, though within its stated base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 5% year-over-year to $183.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue estimates of “$179.92M” and “$182.06M,” and a base case of “$177–183M.”

surprises.description: BAQSIMI sales still declined despite substantial prescription growth: higher rebates and 340B discounts more than offset the increase in prescriptions. That leaves the expected price-and-rebate recovery unresolved, despite the preview’s focus on the May price increase and 340B work.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BAQSIMI net sales fell 3% to $45.5 million despite ~17% prescription growth,” as lower prices from higher rebates and 340B discounts cut sales by “~$8.1 million” versus a “$6.9 million unit volume gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said BAQSIMI’s 2026 guidance was “flat to low-single-digit growth” and called for watching whether “the May 1 price increase and the third-party 340B duplicate-discount work show up.”

surprises.description: The new ipratropium product generated $8.4 million in its first quarter, below the preview’s threshold for a genuine upside surprise of roughly $10–12 million or more. It was nevertheless approaching its targeted market-share range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly launched ipratropium bromide (generic Atrovent) contributed $8.4 million in sales in its first quarter and is approaching its 50%-80% targeted market share goal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a disclosed number above ~$10–12M is a genuine upside surprise” and described vagueness about its contribution as potentially underwhelming.

surprises.description: The call disclosed an FDA warning letter at IMS, a business representing about one-third of corporate sales, and several quarters of added remediation expense. The preview did not flag this development; continued manufacturing and shipping without a required shutdown limits the immediate disruption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IMS, which represents about one-third of corporate sales, received an FDA warning letter tied to a December 2025 inspection but continues manufacturing and shipping without a required shutdown”; remediation is expected to add “$2 million to $3 million per quarter for several quarters,” with capex redirected from the Amphastar facility.

surprises.description: BAQSIMI’s third contract year crossed the $175 million sales threshold, triggering a $100 million payment to Eli Lilly in Q3 2026—an obligation the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BAQSIMI generated $178.3 million in net sales in its third contract year, exceeding the $175 million threshold and triggering a $100 million milestone payment to Eli Lilly due in Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: AMPH repurchased about $45 million of shares, accelerating from the $29.5 million bought back in Q1 and exceeding the preview’s expectation of continued aggressive repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company accelerated buybacks, repurchasing roughly $45 million of shares in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Buyback pace” as a key metric, cited “$29.5M in Q1,” and called for “continued aggressive repurchase.”

in_line: AMPH reaffirmed full-year 2026 corporate sales guidance of mid-single-digit to high-single-digit growth, as the preview expected.

The call reported sequential profitability improvement driven by margin expansion, consistent with the preview’s expectation of at least a partial margin recovery; no gross-margin percentage was provided to compare with its 44–47% estimate.
Glucagon continued to decline, and management did not expect a return to growth; this is consistent with the preview’s expectation that legacy-product erosion would continue.

surprises.description: AMN reported Q2 revenue of $673 million, well above the preview’s $626 million consensus and the company’s $620–635 million guidance. The $25 million of labor-disruption revenue, versus $10 million assumed in guidance, contributed to the beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue was $673 million,” “6% above the high end of guidance”; “Labor disruption revenue came in at $25 million versus the $10 million assumed in guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus **$626M**”; company guide “$620–635M”; Q2 guidance “embeds only ~$10M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.77, far above the preview’s $0.22 consensus. This was a much larger earnings beat than the revenue beat alone would suggest, though non-recurring items also lifted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS jumped to $0.77 from $0.30 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS … Q2'26 Consensus **$0.22**.”

surprises.description: Reported adjusted EBITDA margin reached 10.9%, far above the preview’s 6.7–7.2% guidance range, but about $27 million of non-recurring true-ups and reserve reversals added 370 basis points. Excluding that boost, the margin was roughly 7.2%, near the expected range, so the headline EBITDA strength is not expected to repeat in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $73 million (10.9% of revenue)”; “roughly $27 million in non-recurring items … added 370 basis points to EBITDA margin and are not expected to repeat in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … 6.7–7.2% margin.”

surprises.description: Nurse and Allied revenue grew 11% to $422 million, rather than being flat to down 2% as implied by the preview’s segment guide. Travel nurse and allied volumes both grew, with AMN describing their growth rates as the strongest in four years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Nurse and Allied segment grew revenue 11% to $422 million (12% above consensus), with travel nurse volume up 6% and allied volume up 7%, the highest growth rates in four years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Nurse & Allied was guided “Flat to −2%,” with implied revenue of “$374–382M.” The preview said the market wanted “volume growth ≥5% YoY.”

surprises.description: Travel nurse orders strengthened substantially after turning positive in May: by early August they were up about 40% year over year and 20% above August 2024. That supports projected double-digit Q3 volume growth and is stronger forward momentum than the preview’s focus on whether growth could return consistently.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Travel nurse orders turned positive in May and by early August were up about 40% year-over-year and 20% higher than August 2024, supporting projected double-digit Q3 volume growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 travel nurse volume was “on the cusp of getting back to positive year-over-year growth on a consistent basis” and identified Q2 volume growth as a key debate.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $640–655 million is above the preview’s base-case range of $620–650 million, despite only $7–8 million of strike revenue being included. The higher-than-expected guide therefore does not rely on the larger strike contribution anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for consolidated revenue of $640-655 million”; “only $7-8 million of strike revenue is embedded in the Q3 outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “Q3 guided $620–650M with BWH strike revenue offsetting core softness” and its bull case looked for “~$650M+ with $30M+ disruption revenue.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook includes only $7–8 million of strike revenue, below the preview’s estimate that the known BWH event alone could contribute $20–35 million. The preview’s figure was an analyst estimate, not company guidance, but the reported embedded amount is notably lower.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only $7-8 million of strike revenue is embedded in the Q3 outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated BWH alone could be “$20–35M of Q3 revenue” and described a base case with BWH strike revenue offsetting core softness.

surprises.description: Physician and Leadership revenue declined 6%, within the preview’s expected range, but search activity was much stronger: physician search bookings rose 40% and leadership search volume rose 60%. The preview did not anticipate this strength in search.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Physician and Leadership Solutions revenue fell 6% to $165 million, though search revenue grew 27% year-over-year with physician search bookings up 40% and leadership search volume up 60%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview guided to Physician & Leadership revenue of “−6% to −8%” and discussed locums as a structural headwind, with no expectation stated for search growth.

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter at $362 million, substantially above the preview’s $175 million expectation, partly because of $117 million in strike-related client deposits. The balance-sheet figure is therefore higher than expected, but the deposits help explain the difference.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $362 million in cash (well above the $175 million expected due to $117 million in strike-related client deposits).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 working capital should unwind sharply” and expected a “big negative FCF quarter”; it also referenced about $175 million in client deposits retained from Q1.

surprises.description: Technology and Workforce revenue was in line with its expected decline, but management said language-services pricing pressure is expected to continue through 2026. That extends the pricing headwind beyond the preview’s discussion of Q1 pricing and a possible segment inflection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Technology and Workforce Solutions revenue declined 15% to $87 million with language services pricing down 8% year-over-year while volume was flat, and management expects continued pricing headwinds through 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Technology & Workforce to decline “−14% to −16%” and said language services in Q1 showed “200bps sequential margin improvement on a new offshore/customer-device service model.”

surprises.description: The Kaiser contract is now in a competitive RFP process ahead of its year-end 2026 expiration. The preview flagged Kaiser concentration and renewal commentary as a tail risk, but did not indicate that a competitive process was underway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Kaiser contract expires at the end of 2026 and is now in a competitive RFP process.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Client concentration — Kaiser is roughly 22% of revenue; any contract/renewal commentary is a tail risk in both directions.”

surprises.description: AMN lowered its expectations for international nurse growth in 2027 toward single digits because of embassy appointment backlogs and travel bans. The preview did not flag this outlook reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International nurse growth expectations for 2027 were lowered toward single digits due to embassy appointment backlogs and travel bans.”

in_line: Physician and Leadership Solutions’ total revenue fell 6%, within the preview’s expected decline of 6% to 8%.
Technology and Workforce Solutions revenue declined 15%, within the preview’s expected decline of 14% to 16%.
