surprises.description: The reported mNAV of about 0.72x was below the preview’s estimate of roughly 0.78x, indicating a larger discount to treasury value than the preview had modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SUI Group's stock traded at an mNAV of approximately 0.72x as of August 3, 2026, signaling a discount to the underlying treasury value.”

surprises.description: The legacy specialty-finance book was down to about $2.2 million at fair value, with $900,000 of first-half repayments and no significant new originations expected near-term. That is a more concrete run-off picture than the preview’s focus on credit risk, delinquencies, and recent provisions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The legacy specialty finance portfolio has shrunk to approximately $2.2 million of non-bank loans at fair value, with about $900,000 in repayments received in the first half and no significant new originations expected near-term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Chairman Polinsky flagged ‘increased credit risk and uncertainty regarding borrower delinquencies.’ Q1 carried a $1.15M provision plus $1.37M receivable impairment.”

in_line: Underlying Q2 operating expenses of $3.4 million were broadly in line with the preview’s estimated $3.0–$3.5 million of cash G&A.

Treasury holdings were approximately 109 million SUI, close to the preview’s approximately 108.8 million; staking output of roughly 5,300 SUI per day was also close to the preview’s 5,200-per-day assumption.
The Bluefin arrangement’s 6 million SUI commitment and 11% revenue share matched the preview’s stated assumptions for the expansion.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $973 million, about 1.3% below the $985.7 million consensus estimate. The shortfall was modest, while adjusted EBITDA of $69 million was close to the roughly $68 million consensus and within the expected guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $973 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus: “$985.7M.”

surprises.description: Astrana raised the low end of its full-year adjusted EBITDA range by only $5 million, to $255 million, rather than the preview’s reasonable-ask range starting around $260 million. It did raise the floor, but less than the preview said the market wanted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $255M-$280M.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The market wants the low end taken up” and “a narrow-up to ~$260–280M is the reasonable ask.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.80 exceeded the preview’s derived expectation of about $0.75, though the preview cautioned that adjusted and GAAP EPS estimates could be confused.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS hit a record $0.80.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS — adjusted diluted”: “~$0.75” consensus (derived).

surprises.description: Medical costs were slightly better than the 5.2% full-year assumption overall, but commercial outpatient specialties were trending slightly above expectations. This is more mixed than a uniformly favorable trend reading.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date medical cost trend is running slightly better than the 5.2% full-year assumption, with Medicare favorable and Medicaid in line, but commercial trending slightly above expectations in outpatient specialties.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 was “slightly better than 5.2%” and that “holds ~5% against a peer group running 7%” would support the bull case; it flagged elevated utilization or trend at the high end of the assumption as a bear signal.

surprises.description: A CMS billing-anomaly adjustment for ACO REACH 2025 caused a one-time $15 million revenue reduction that the preview had not anticipated. A corresponding expense reduction largely offset it, leaving EBITDA impact immaterial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A one-time $15 million revenue reduction tied to CMS billing anomaly adjustments for ACO REACH 2025 was largely offset by a corresponding expense reduction, resulting in an immaterial EBITDA impact.”

surprises.description: G&A improved about 210 basis points year over year, with management expecting it to reach roughly 6% of revenue by year-end. The preview discussed Prospect synergies but did not flag this degree of G&A improvement or the exit-rate target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “G&A improved approximately 210 basis points year-over-year, with the company expecting to exit 2026 at roughly 6% of revenue.”

surprises.description: Management said it is putting mid-to-high single-digit millions—about three-quarters of its outperformance—back into payer contracts, provider partnerships, and expansion markets. The preview speculated that a buyback might be possible, but did not anticipate this specific reinvestment plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is reinvesting mid-to-high single-digit millions (about three-quarters of its outperformance) into new payer contracts, provider partnerships, and expansion markets in Texas and Hawaii.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management would “evaluate dynamically” on risk-adjusted returns and that an authorization was a possibility: “Any repurchase announcement lands as a confidence signal.”

surprises.description: Astrana disclosed plans to convert tens of thousands of California Medi-Cal members from professional to full-risk arrangements over the next 12 months, a specific and substantial conversion initiative not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Converting tens of thousands of California Medi-Cal members from professional to full-risk arrangements over the next 12 months.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed medium-term mid-to-high teens organic EBITDA growth, including for 2027, despite Medicaid work-requirement changes beginning January 1, 2027. The preview discussed Medicaid and the 2027 setup but did not anticipate this explicit growth reaffirmation alongside the policy change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed medium-term mid-to-high teens organic EBITDA growth, including for 2027, despite Medicaid work-requirement changes starting January 1, 2027.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $69 million, near the high end of the $65–70 million quarterly guidance range and close to the preview’s roughly $68 million consensus estimate.
Full-year revenue guidance remained $3.8–$4.1 billion, as the preview’s base case anticipated a reaffirmation absent a larger guidance raise.
Free cash flow guidance remained $105–$132.5 million, the range already shown in the preview; the preview noted a raise as a possible upside signal but did not make it the base expectation.
Full-risk mix was close to the preview’s estimates: 81% of capitation revenue and 42% of membership, versus roughly 80% and 40% expected.
Prospect synergies tracking to the high end of the $12–$15 million target matched the preview’s stated expectation.
Net leverage was 2.26x, close to the preview’s 2.1–2.2x estimate, and the company had already been described as ahead of its original sub-2.5x deleveraging timeline.

surprises.description: Bookings were $16.2 million, well below the preview’s $19.0 million guidance midpoint and even below the $17.1 million low end. The resulting bookings growth of 25% year over year was also far below the preview’s implied 47% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bookings grew 25% year-over-year to $16.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross bookings” guidance was “$19.0M ±10% ($17.1–20.9M),” with “Implied YoY” growth of “+47%.”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue midpoint of $17 million is below the preview’s roughly $19 million expectation, and even the top of the guidance range is below $19 million. However, management still projected a record Q4 and full-year revenue above $70 million, preserving the full-year growth framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $17 million (+/-10%)” and “Q4 is expected to be a record quarter (above $18.7M), driving full-year 2026 revenue above $70 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a Q3 guide “≥ $19M” was needed and that roughly “$19–19.5M in each of Q3 and Q4” was implied by the full-year framework.

surprises.description: The company continued to burn operating cash rather than reaching the Q2 breakeven target. The $5.5 million burn was substantially lower than Q1’s $11 million, but the stated target was not met.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash burn halved to $5.5 million from $11 million in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “targeted OCF breakeven in Q2.”

surprises.description: IP results were stronger than the preview’s already-positive outlook: revenue and bookings reached records, and the pipeline grew more than fourfold rather than merely roughly doubling. Management also expects IP revenue to reach about $20 million in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IP revenue surged 238% year-over-year, achieving record bookings and revenue, with the IP pipeline up more than 4x over the past year”; management expects IP revenue “to roughly double to about $20 million in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the IP pipeline had “roughly doubled YoY” and highlighted a need for SIP bookings to “recover above $4M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin was 86.8%, below the preview’s approximately 88% expectation, and management said it had slipped sequentially because of mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin rose over 12 percentage points year-over-year to 86.8%, though it slipped 111 basis points sequentially due to mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 guidance assumption was “~88%” non-GAAP gross margin.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating expenses came in below the preview’s $15.5 million midpoint, landing near the low end of the expected range. This is a modest cost-performance upside, although still within the guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating expenses [were cut] 7.8% sequentially to $14.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed non-GAAP opex guidance of “$15.5M ±5% ($14.7–16.3M).”

surprises.description: Micron provided a $10 million convertible note that closed in Q3 and deepened its FTCO co-development partnership; the preview had not anticipated this financing or partnership development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Micron invested $10 million in a Silvaco convertible note that closed in Q3, deepening their FTCO co-development partnership.”

surprises.description: Silvaco announced a strategic partnership with Dassault Systèmes Simulia for interoperable workflows targeting AI-enabled manufacturing, a development not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed strategic partnerships with NVIDIA (GPU-accelerated physics simulation) and Dassault Systèmes Simulia (interoperable workflows) targeting AI-enabled manufacturing.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $17.8 million, essentially in line with the $17.9 million consensus and $18.0 million company-guidance midpoint; the 48% year-over-year increase was also close to the preview’s implied 49% growth.

The company achieved its first non-GAAP operating profit since late 2024, as expected. The $635,000 result was above the preview’s roughly $300,000 midpoint estimate but within its stated base-case range of $300,000–$700,000.
Full-year 2026 revenue above $70 million and a record Q4 were broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of double-digit full-year growth and a strong second half.

surprises.description: Japan’s Q2 benefit ratio was 64%, well above the preview’s 61.7% estimate and above the 60%–63% full-year guidance range. Management now expects the full-year ratio to land at the high end of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Japan's total benefit ratio came in at 64%” and, with year-to-date at 63.4%, management “now expects to be at the high end of its 60%-63% full-year guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Japan benefit/premium ratio” Q2 estimate: “61.7%”; company FY guide: “60–63%.”

surprises.description: Aflac lowered its 2026 U.S. net earned premium growth outlook from the low end of its 3%–6% guidance range to just below that range. The preview’s Q2 estimate was for 2.2% growth, but it did not anticipate this deterioration in the full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “now expects 2026 net earned premium growth to fall just below its 3%-6% guidance range, previously guided to the low end.”

surprises.description: U.S. group-product sales were slightly below the low end of expectations, despite strong growth in dental and vision. This was a modest shortfall in a business the preview had highlighted as a source of U.S. growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Dental and vision sales were “up 47%” and combined group and voluntary benefits sales were “up 7.1%,” though results were “slightly below the low end of expectations with the year weighted toward Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “the U.S. group business grew 12.4% in Q1” and described group growth as a key U.S. growth area.

surprises.description: Aflac disclosed a $4.8 billion portfolio repositioning expected to add more than $50 million to annualized net investment income, an earnings opportunity not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The investment team repositioned “$4.8 billion (about 5%) of the portfolio via switch trades,” expected to “boost net investment income by over $50 million annualized with limited capital impact.”

surprises.description: The company raised its internal reinsurance ceding limit substantially, opening more potential capacity than the preview discussed. The preview focused on the near-term earnings drag from a Japan reinsurance transaction, not this expanded capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: Aflac raised its internal reinsurance ceding limit “from 10% of U.S. GAAP assets to 30% of FSA reserves,” with Japan holding “JPY 10.8 trillion in FSA policy reserves” representing total addressable ceding capacity.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to a “negative earnings impact from the Japan reinsurance transaction ‘for the next couple of quarters.’”

surprises.description: Combined RBC was slightly above 600%, materially higher than the preview’s roughly 560% estimate; the call also disclosed $3.3 billion in unencumbered liquidity. ESR, by contrast, was close to the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported “an estimated regulatory ESR of 226% (240% including USP) and combined RBC slightly above 600%, with $3.3 billion in unencumbered liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “ESR 227% regulatory / 243% with undertaking-specific parameters; RBC ~560%.”

surprises.description: Tsumitasu was driving concurrent third-sector sales well above the initial 25% cross-sell target, a positive sales-quality result not highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Tsumitasu comprised “about 20% of sales while driving concurrent third-sector sales well above the initial 25% cross-sell target.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS was $1.75 versus the preview’s $1.77 consensus, a small miss; the $1.80 figure excluding foreign currency effects is not the reported adjusted EPS.
U.S. Q2 net earned premium growth was 2.3%, essentially matching the preview’s 2.2% estimate.
The $983 million of Q2 buybacks was within the preview’s expected range of roughly $800 million–$1.0 billion.
Japan sales declined 5.6% in Q2 after the launch-driven increase in Q1, consistent with the preview’s warning that the 25.5% Q1 increase could decay as comparisons hardened.

surprises.description: Atkore’s adjusted EPS of $1.92 exceeded even the preview’s freshest $1.78 consensus estimate by about 8%, and was above its $1.85 bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS reached $1.92; the call said key metrics improved sequentially and year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called $1.78 the “more defensible anchor”; its bull case specified “Adj. EPS >$1.85.”

surprises.description: Net sales of $795 million topped the preview’s highest cited consensus of $781.1 million, with 9% organic volume growth providing a substantial lift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net sales rose 8.1% year-over-year to $795 million,” including $65.7 million from higher volume; “Organic volume grew 9% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited revenue consensus of $781.1 million and described its base case as “$762–781M”; its bull case was “>$790M.”

surprises.description: Margins and price-cost performance were weaker than the preview’s base-case expectation of a flat spread: input costs outpaced pricing, and Electrical margin slipped despite higher sales and EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: Electrical margin “slipped to 15.4% from 15.6% as input costs outpaced pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed a “flat spread,” while its bull case expected “price/cost inflecting positive.”

surprises.description: The final punitive litigation-class settlement added a $50 million expense, leaving GAAP net income at just $0.7 million versus $43 million a year earlier; the preview did not identify this additional settlement as an expected charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income collapsed to $0.7 million ($0.02 per diluted share) from $43 million ($1.25) a year earlier, primarily due to a $50 million litigation settlement expense”; the company “settled the last of three punitive litigation classes for $50 million.”

in_line: The Prysmian all-cash acquisition at $95 per share was already disclosed in the preview, so its confirmation on the call was not new.
The lack of analyst Q&A and limited forward guidance were consistent with the preview’s expectation that the bondholder call would provide “no guidance and minimal strategy Q&A.”
Safety & Infrastructure remained the segment the preview had flagged as the operational weak link; its EBITDA fell and its margin declined despite slightly higher sales.

surprises.description: TMCI reported Q2 revenue of $45.4 million, above the preview’s $43.9–$44.0 million consensus range and a 4% year-over-year decline rather than the expected 7.2% decline. The revenue shortfall was therefore narrower than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $45.4 million, a 4% decline year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $43.9M–$44.0M” and implied YoY “−7.2%.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss was much smaller than the preview’s roughly $7 million estimate: TMCI reported a $3.5 million loss, narrowing slightly from $3.6 million a year earlier despite lower revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed slightly to $3.5 million (from $3.6 million a year earlier) despite lower revenue, demonstrating improved operating leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$(7)M (my estimate).”

surprises.description: TMCI raised the low end of its full-year revenue outlook from $202 million to $204 million while keeping the $212 million high end. The preview expected the full $202–$212 million range to be reaffirmed as the neutral outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $204-212 million (from $202-212 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirm of the full $202–212M range is the neutral outcome.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance improved by $1 million at both ends, to a loss of $3–$5 million from a loss of $4–$6 million. This was better than the preview’s stated existing guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance was improved to a loss of $3-5 million for 2026 (from a loss of $4-6 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA loss $(4)–$(6)M.”

surprises.description: Case volume growth accelerated to high single digits, above the preview’s expected mid-single-digit growth. This is a stronger volume trend than the preview’s base-case assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Case volume growth accelerated to high single digits in Q2, up from mid single digits in prior quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as “volume +MSD” and said “Mid-single-digit volume growth” was the path to the Q4 inflection.

surprises.description: Adoption of the new bunion systems among LAPAplasty surgeons rose to about 40%, up from the 35% last disclosed in the preview. That is a further increase in the portfolio cross-sell measure the preview singled out as a key indicator.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 40% of the LAPAplasty surgeon user base has now used at least one of the three new bunion systems, up from 35% in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Last disclosed: … 35% of existing Lapiplasty users had adopted ≥1 new bunion system”; the preview called this “the cleanest single proxy” for the portfolio strategy.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 78.5%, below the preview’s roughly 79% expectation, and declined 120 basis points year over year. TMCI attributed the pressure to a shift toward lower-priced products.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 78.5% in Q2 2026 from 79.7% a year earlier, reflecting the shift toward lower-priced products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~79% (not formally consensused)” and “~flat/-50bps.”

surprises.description: Management expressed confidence in achieving positive adjusted EBITDA in 2027, whereas the preview said management had previously declined to guide 2027 and that confident early 2027 framing would be a genuine surprise. It still declined to provide formal 2027 guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expressed confidence in achieving positive adjusted EBITDA in 2027, though declined to provide formal 2027 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Early, confident 2027 growth framing on this call would be a genuine surprise”; management had previously “declined to guide 2027, saying it needed to see Q4 momentum first.”

in_line: Management retained the $212 million high end of FY2026 revenue guidance, consistent with the preview’s key checkpoint that the high end remain intact.
Management continued to expect full-year cash usage to fall by approximately 50%, matching the preview’s stated expectation.
Management expected a sequential revenue step-up in Q3 and positive growth in Q4, consistent with the preview’s anticipated Q3/Q4 inflection.
Management declined to provide formal 2027 guidance, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was about $272 million, roughly 7% above the preview’s $254.5 million consensus estimate, despite still declining year over year. The result was a clear upside beat against the expected Q3 level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 total revenue was approximately $272 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $254.5M”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS came in at $0.56, more than double the preview’s $0.26 consensus estimate. That was a substantially stronger quarter than the preview’s in-line-to-soft base case suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS dropped to $0.56 from $1.12 in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $0.26”; the preview described its “base case” as “Q3 in line-to-soft.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin was 25.5%, well above the preview’s estimate of about 19–21%. The margin decline was much less severe than that estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin fell to 25.5% from 36.9% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin (my est.) | ~19–21%”; the preview also watched for margin “vs. ~20%.”

surprises.description: Embecta held its full-year revenue range at $1.015–$1.035 billion, rather than narrowing or trimming it as the preview’s base case anticipated. That was a more resilient outlook than expected given the weak U.S. business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $1.015–$1.035 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case … FY revenue guide trimmed to the low end or narrowed toward ~$1.01B”; the preview also said “a trim is largely expected.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted operating margin outlook was raised to 23.5–24%, from 22.25–23.25%. This is a meaningful improvement on the prior range, rather than the preview’s main focus on the risk of weak margins and a cost program being needed to support results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised adjusted operating margin guidance to 23.5%–24%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guide (mid)” showed the existing 22.25–23.25% range; the preview emphasized “Adj. operating margin vs. ~20%, plus a sized cost program.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose to $1.80–$1.90 from $1.55–$1.75, an increase in both ends of the range. The preview expected the EPS outlook to be held or potentially pressured alongside the revenue outlook, not raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised … adjusted EPS guidance to $1.80–$1.90 from $1.55–$1.75.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS guide held on cost actions” in the preview’s base case; the existing guide was $1.55–$1.75.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue guidance of roughly $270 million is below the preview’s implied Q4 level of about $287.5 million, despite the full-year revenue range being reaffirmed. This leaves a weaker Q4 revenue bridge than the preview’s expectations implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance implies revenue of roughly $270 million, slightly below Street expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 | ~$287.5M vs. $264.0M LY = +8.9%”; the preview said the guide implied an “organic revenue” move to “roughly +1% Y/Y in Q4.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was about 3.7x, above the preview’s roughly 3.0x reference point, though still below the 4.75x covenant limit. The preview had highlighted leverage headroom as a key risk, so the reported level was less comfortable than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company borrowed approximately $180 million to fund the Owen Mumford acquisition but repaid roughly $53 million of debt in the quarter, ending with net leverage of about 3.7x versus a 4.75x covenant limit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “net leverage ~3.0x vs. 4.75x covenant max at Q2”; the preview’s base case anticipated “leverage ~3.0–3.2x.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased about 2.7 million shares for roughly $9 million and lowered its weighted average diluted share-count guidance to 58.6 million from 59.4 million. The preview raised buyback execution as an open question, so actual repurchases and a lower share-count outlook were positive evidence of execution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned approximately $9 million to shareholders through repurchasing about 2.7 million shares, reducing the weighted average diluted share count guidance to 58.6 million from 59.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether they are actually buying, and at what pace versus debt paydown, is a real signal”; the preview also called buyback execution a “capital allocation credibility test.”

in_line: U.S. revenue was approximately $121 million, within the preview’s estimated $120–128 million range.
Full-year free cash flow guidance of about $100 million matched the preview’s $95–105 million range.

surprises.description: Revenue was $283.4 million, well above the preview’s $250–255 million base case; on the company’s property-management-adjusted comparison, revenue was up 8.6% year over year rather than the expected roughly 3% decline. This was a substantial upside gap to the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose to $283.4 million” and increased “8.6%” excluding the divested property management business.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case forecast “Revenue ex-property mgmt” of “$250–255M” and approximately “-3%” year over year.

surprises.description: The June cash balance exceeded the preview’s expected $92–97 million, reaching $105 million. Cash then rose to $121 million by July 31, partly due to an unanticipated $13 million net receipt from a lawsuit settlement.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended June 30 with “$105 million in cash and no long-term debt,” rising to “$121 million by July 31, 2026,” boosted by “a $13 million net receipt” from the settlement.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview forecast “Cash (unrestricted)” of “$92–97M” and flagged “≥$100M” as bullish.

surprises.description: The quarterly adjusted EBITDA loss was smaller than the preview’s roughly $2 million expected loss, at just under $1 million. That is a moderate improvement against the forecast, rather than merely an improvement against the prior-year quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $986,000” from a $3.6 million loss in Q2 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case forecast adjusted EBITDA of “~-$2M.”

surprises.description: The net loss was smaller than the preview’s expected GAAP loss of about $0.09 per share, coming in at $0.03 per share. The preview had already warned that the prior-year $17 million noncash charge would make the year-over-year comparison look much better, so the surprise is the additional improvement versus its forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss narrowed sharply to $2.7 million ($0.03 per share)” from $22.7 million, which included “a $17 million noncash interest charge tied to retired convertible debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview forecast GAAP EPS of “~-$0.09” and cautioned that Q2 2025’s “-$0.27 included a $17.0M derivative fair-value loss” and that GAAP EPS “should improve sharply YoY.”

surprises.description: Management reported strong cash-receipt growth from existing home sales—15% in May, 16% in June, and 8% in July—contrasting with the preview’s base case of slightly declining gross transaction value and transactions. Receipts are not the same measure as GTV, but the reported trend was more encouraging than the preview’s modeled activity outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash receipts from existing home sales rose 15% in May and 16% in June year-over-year,” with “8% growth in July 2026 versus July 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case projected GTV of “~$10.1B” (about “-1%”) and transactions of “~5,300” (about “-4%”).

surprises.description: The AI transformation is not expected to deliver meaningful non-commission operating-expense savings until 2027. The preview highlighted the need for cost reductions to outrun growth investments, so the stated timing offers no near-term savings contribution and makes the payoff later than investors might have hoped.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company launched an AI transformation using Google Cloud Agentic AI, with “meaningful non-commission operating expense savings only beginning in 2027,” funded largely by replacing existing technology spending.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors needed to see “the cuts outrunning the investments” and identified the technology transformation as part of the spending to monitor.

in_line: Average price per transaction was approximately $1.9 million for the first half of 2026, matching the preview’s Q2 base-case expectation of about $1.90 million.

surprises.description: Groupon’s Q2 billings and revenue each declined 1% year over year, rather than growing as expected; the shortfall was concentrated in North America local. The preview expected billings growth of 1.3% and revenue of $127.42 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 billings and revenue each declined 1% year-over-year, missing top-line expectations due to weakness concentrated in North America local.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue” consensus was “$127.42M” and “Gross billings” consensus was “$422.09M,” each with expected year-over-year growth; the preview also said NA Local billings needed to accelerate meaningfully above +2%.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA finished at the high end of guidance, above the preview’s roughly $14 million consensus estimate. This was a modestly better result than the expected midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA finished at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” consensus was “~$14M,” against company guidance of “$13–15M.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $15 million, exceeding the preview’s stated minimum guidance of $10 million. The preview flagged free cash flow as a key watch point after a negative Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was positive at $15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 free cash flow guidance as “≥$10M.”

surprises.description: The business accelerated to mid-single-digit growth in July, providing evidence of improving second-half momentum where the preview said the H2 inflection still needed to be demonstrated. The reported pace is a positive signal, though the preview’s full-year math required roughly 7% H2 revenue growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The business accelerated to mid-single-digit growth in July, signaling improving momentum for the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said H2 revenue needed to accelerate to “~+7%” and that the bear case required management to “fail to produce evidence the H2 inflection is underway.”

surprises.description: Organic-channel revenue returned to growth in Q2 and reached double-digit growth in July, driven by AI-generated local content and SEO improvements. The preview discussed AI-driven merchant acquisition as a key question but did not anticipate this reported channel growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue from organic channels returned to growth in Q2 and accelerated to double-digit growth in July, driven by AI-generated local content and SEO improvements.”

surprises.description: Managed channels delivered strong double-digit revenue growth in Q2 while sending fewer, more effective push and email messages. This was an unanticipated positive operating result in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Managed channels (push/email) delivered strong double-digit revenue growth in Q2 using the scaled customer data platform, sending fewer but more effective messages.”

surprises.description: Project Foundry has more than doubled engineering output per developer in six months, an unexpected productivity milestone not anticipated by the preview’s discussion of whether AI initiatives were adding merchant supply or mainly reducing costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Under Project Foundry, engineering output per developer has more than doubled in the past six months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether Project Foundry was “adding supply, or only removing cost?”

in_line: Groupon maintained its FY2026 outlook; the preview identified reaffirmation of the $513–523 million revenue and 3–5% billings ranges as the base case.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.05, below the preview’s $1.08–$1.09 consensus range; year-over-year growth was only 1% rather than the +4–7% implied by consensus. Six-month EPS growth was 8%, but the quarter’s result also left first-half EPS at $3.52, below the preview’s $3.55–$3.59 estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was $1.05, up only 1% year-over-year”; “six-month adjusted EPS growth was stronger at 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (adj.) | $1.08 – $1.09”; “+4–7%”; and “the first half (~$3.55–$3.59 cumulative).”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin was about $150 million, up 5%, below the preview’s modeled $156–$160 million and 9–12% growth. Regulated margin growth was 6%, also short of the preview’s expectation that it would remain in the low double digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted gross margin rose 5% to ~$150 million, with regulated segment margin up 6% to ~$125 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My base assumes total AGM ~$156–160M (+9–12%)”; “Watch whether Regulated AGM growth stays low-double-digit.”

surprises.description: The company raised 2026 capital guidance by $100 million, to $550–$600 million, above its prior $450–$500 million range. The increase is tied to initial Florida Energy Pathway spending and higher regulated distribution and infrastructure investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 capital guidance was raised by $100 million to a range of $550 million to $600 million, driven by initial FEP spending and increased regulated distribution and infrastructure investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 capex of $450–$500M”; the preview asked whether the plan would be raised.

surprises.description: The 2024–2028 capital plan now exceeds $2.2 billion, a substantial increase from the preview’s stated $1.5–$1.8 billion plan. The preview anticipated a possible increase but did not indicate an increase of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The five-year capital plan was upgraded, now expecting to exceed $2.2 billion from 2024 through 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “within a 2024–2028 plan of $1.5–$1.8B”; the preview asked whether that range would be raised.

surprises.description: Despite the expectation that management would detail refreshed long-term capital expectations on the call, it deferred new 2027–2031 capital and earnings-growth guidance until February 2027. It reaffirmed the 2028 EPS target, but provided no new longer-term growth framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed its 2028 EPS guidance of $7.75 to $8.00 but deferred issuing new 2027-2031 capital and earnings growth guidance until the February 2027 call.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “management has publicly committed to detailing the $1.2B Florida Energy Pathway and refreshed long-term capital expectations on this call”; the preview also identified a possible “new 2027–2031 plan.”

surprises.description: The company clarified that it expects to fund and own at least 51% of the Florida Energy Pathway, implying roughly $600 million of company-side capital. However, the call facts identify no partner or partnership process timeline; partner funding of up to 49% remains only a possibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PPC will fund and own at least 51% of FEP, with partners potentially funding up to 49%, building to roughly $600 million of capital on the company's side.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “a partner [would be] identified or a process timeline given” and what “CPK's net share of the $1.2B” would be.

surprises.description: The Florida City Gas rate case also faces an explicit opposing position from the Office of Public Counsel, a challenge the preview did not flag while focusing on the requested increase and interim-rate timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FCG rate case requests a ~$47 million base rate increase and an 11.25% ROE”; “the Office of Public Counsel has taken an opposing position.”

in_line: The Florida Energy Pathway’s approximately $1.2 billion scale, 2030 in-service timing, and nearly 250,000 dekatherms/day of investment-grade shipper commitments matched the preview’s description.
The rate case request of approximately $47 million and an 11.25% ROE were close to the preview’s $46.9 million request and 11.25% ROE; interim rates were approved around the expected Q3 2026 timing.
The Worcester Resiliency Upgrade remained on track for early 2027, as expected.
The company reaffirmed its 2028 EPS guidance of $7.75–$8.00.
The 7.3% dividend increase was already reported in the preview.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.88 versus the preview’s $0.63 consensus, a much larger beat than expected. About $0.19 came from a one-time tariff refund; even excluding that amount, EPS would be approximately $0.69.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS jumped 47% year-over-year to $0.88, boosted by roughly $0.19 from a one-time $15.6 million IEEPA tariff refund that was not in prior guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus: $0.63; the preview also described a buy-side bar closer to “$0.66–0.68.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted gross margin reached 45%, far above the 39.9% expected. The gap was largely explained by the unexpected tariff refund: 393 of the 524 basis points of expansion came from the refund, with 131 basis points from operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 524 basis points to 45%, but only 131 bps came from operations while 393 bps came from the tariff refund.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put Q2 adjusted gross margin at “~39.9%” and said tariff refunds were not assumed in guidance.

surprises.description: Full-year gross-margin guidance moved well above the preview’s 38.8%–39.0% range, to approximately 40.6%; Q3 was guided to approximately 40.8%. Management tempered that improvement by saying Q4 margin would decline year over year as raw-material costs flow through.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 gross margin to approximately 40.8% and full-year to approximately 40.6%, with Q4 expected to decline year-over-year due to timing of raw material cost flow-through.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 adjusted gross-margin guidance of “38.8–39.0%.”

surprises.description: Healthcare billings accelerated to 19%, exceeding the preview’s latest reported pace of 11% growth, despite a 28% comparison from the prior year. The preview did not specify a Q2 forecast for the segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Healthcare was the standout segment with global billings up 19% on top of 28% growth a year earlier, driven by nora and combined selling teams.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 Healthcare billings growth of “+11%.”

surprises.description: Corporate Office billings grew only 5%, well below the preview’s double-digit continuation scenario for the segment. This was notable because Corporate Office represents about 44% of year-to-date billings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Corporate Office, which represents about 44% of year-to-date billings, grew 5% on broad-based global demand tied to return-to-office and flight-to-quality trends.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 Corporate Office billings were “+16%” and its bull case required that Corporate Office “sustains double-digit billings.”

surprises.description: Education billings rose 5%, below the high-single- or double-digit Q2 inflection the preview was looking for after management attributed Q1’s weak result to seasonal timing. Growth improved from Q1’s 1%, but did not reach that expected rebound.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Education billings rose 5% on top of 11% prior-year growth, supported by approachable price-point carpet tile, LVT and nora share gains in K-12.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 was where the “timing” explanation would be tested and asked whether Education would inflect to “high-single/double-digit growth.”

surprises.description: Orders grew 5% in currency-neutral terms, short of the preview’s 7% threshold for a strong demand signal and automatic guidance raise. Backlog was stronger than anticipated, however, rising 22% year-to-date versus the preview’s cited 18% at Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog was up 22% year-to-date and consolidated currency-neutral orders grew 5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Orders holding ≥7% CN makes a guidance raise nearly automatic,” and cited Q1 backlog growth of “+18% YTD.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $395.7 million exceeded both the $391.3 million consensus and the $395 million high end of company guidance, though the beat over the guidance ceiling was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 5.4% as reported to $395.7 million and 3.8% on a currency-neutral basis, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus net sales of “$391.3M” and company guidance of “$385–395M.”

surprises.description: Q2 repurchases were $8.8 million, below the $12 million repurchased in Q1 rather than accelerating. The company still bought back about $21 million year to date, while generating strong operating cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interface repurchased $8.8 million (about 310,000 shares) in Q2 and roughly $21 million year-to-date, while generating $38.4 million operating cash flow against $12.2 million capex.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “buyback acceleration” as something to watch and noted that Q1 repurchases were “$12M.”

in_line: Full-year net sales guidance was raised modestly to $1.455–$1.485 billion, consistent with the preview’s base case of a reaffirmation or a nudge toward the high end of the prior $1.450–$1.480 billion range.

Management continued to cite tariffs on 15–20% of COGS and low-single-digit raw-material inflation, while saying it had taken proactive pricing to offset the inflation—consistent with the preview’s discussion of tariff exposure and pricing pass-through.
Q2 operating cash flow was $38.4 million; the preview had described Q2 and Q3 as cash-generative quarters.

surprises.description: Oklo raised 2026 operating cash-use guidance to $120–150 million from $80–100 million, a substantial increase over the preview’s baseline range. The company attributed the higher spending to accelerated first-of-a-kind project work at Aurora-INL.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oklo raised its 2026 operating cash use guidance to $120–150 million (from $80–100 million), driven by accelerated first-of-a-kind project spending at Aurora-INL.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 operating cash use **$80–100M**”; the preview also said to watch “Cash burn, capex guidance, and dilution.”

surprises.description: Oklo disclosed $400–500 million of 2026 PP&E capex and raised that guidance by $50 million at both ends, to fund accelerated Aurora-INL spending. The preview anticipated that a capex bracket could be provided, but did not anticipate this higher revised range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PP&E capex guidance to $400–500 million (from $350–450 million), driven by accelerated first-of-a-kind project spending at Aurora-INL.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said an “explicit FY2026 capex bracket” would be worth watching and modeled “~$40–60M capex” for Q2.

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash and marketable securities reached $3 billion, well above the preview’s estimated $2.44–2.48 billion. But the higher balance came alongside $1.9 billion raised through 2026 ATM programs, making the liquidity upside come with substantial share issuance rather than simply lower-than-expected spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $3 billion in cash and marketable securities, including $1.9 billion raised via ATM programs in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2-end liquidity at roughly $2.44–2.48B, unless further ATM issuance offsets it”; the preview also warned that “continued heavy ATM issuance at $42” would be a real negative.

surprises.description: Oklo said Aurora-INL remains on track for a planned 2028 startup, whereas the preview’s reference schedule was late 2027/early 2028 and flagged a move into 2028 as a downside risk. The call also reported DOE safety-analysis approval, an unexpected project milestone that partially offsets the less favorable timing wording.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aurora-INL received DOE approval of its Preliminary Documented Safety Analysis and remains on track for a planned 2028 startup.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Aurora-INL schedule reaffirmation (late 2027 / early 2028 operations)” and “Any softening of language … or a slip into 2028” was identified as a downside risk.

surprises.description: Oklo was selected for advanced negotiations over surplus plutonium that could be blended into HALEU-equivalent bridge fuel. The preview highlighted fuel supply as a key constraint, but this specific potential source was not anticipated; timing remains outside the company’s control.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DOE selected Oklo for advanced negotiations on surplus plutonium … that could be blended at 10–13% plutonium content to create HALEU-equivalent bridge fuel, though timing remains outside Oklo's control.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Fuel supply” and said a “fuel contract or facility authorization” could be an underrated catalyst.

surprises.description: A Centrus letter of intent contemplated enough domestic HALEU for initial cores and reloads for up to five Aurora powerhouses over multiple years. This is a concrete potential supply source, although it is an LOI and deliveries are not expected to begin until 2029.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Centrus letter of intent contemplates domestic HALEU supply sufficient for initial core and reload needs of up to 5 Aurora powerhouses for multiple years, with deliveries expected to begin in 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified HALEU sourcing as a key issue and said a fuel contract or facility authorization could be a catalyst.

surprises.description: Oklo acquired ARMEC and Creative Engineers to bring more engineering and manufacturing capability in-house. The preview did not flag either acquisition; ARMEC was already contributing to Aurora-INL procurement, while CEI adds sodium and alkali-metal systems experience.
surprises.fact_evidence: “During the quarter Oklo acquired ARMEC and Creative Engineers (CEI) to strengthen in-house engineering and manufacturing,” with ARMEC contributing to Aurora-INL procurement and CEI adding “~30 years of sodium/alkali metal systems experience.”

surprises.description: Oklo signed an MOU with Kiewit for EPC planning for the Ohio campus and is advancing PJM interconnection applications, an incremental development step not specified in the preview. The call did not report a binding, priced power contract or provide full project-cost guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oklo signed an MOU with Kiewit to support EPC planning for the initial phase of its planned 1.2-gigawatt Ohio clean energy campus and is advancing multiple PJM interconnection applications, though full project cost guidance has not yet been provided.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “binding, priced PPA with a delivery date” was what would move the market and called for watching grid interconnection progress.

in_line: Groves achieved first criticality in early August, consistent with the preview’s note that criticality had already been achieved on August 5 and announced August 6.
Oklo expects first isotope revenue in 2027, consistent with the preview’s view that a credible 2027 isotope-revenue date would be important; the call specified early 2027.

No binding, priced PPA was reported. The Ohio update was planning and interconnection progress rather than customer-contract conversion, consistent with the preview’s distinction between pipeline activity and a binding deal.

surprises.description: National's leverage ratio improved to 21:1, better than the preview's Q1 level of 23:1 and below the sub-22:1 threshold it identified as a positive surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: National's leverage ratio (gross par to statutory capital) improved to 21-to-1 from 24-to-1 at year-end 2025, with insured gross par declining ~$1.5 billion to about $20.8 billion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: National insured portfolio runoff & leverage: $21.5B gross par and leverage 23:1 from 24:1; “Sub-22:1 leverage would be a positive surprise.”

surprises.description: National's statutory capital reached $968 million, above the preview's expected range of $940–960 million and its Q1 level of $950 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: National's statutory capital rose $31 million to $968 million versus year-end 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “National stat cap $940–960M”; Q1 level: “$950M stat cap (+$13M q/q).”

surprises.description: National's PREPA exposure fell by $35 million from the preview's $425 million baseline after claims were paid on bonds maturing July 1; the call also said only $20 million payments are due in each of 2027 and 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: National's PREPA exposure fell by $35 million to $390 million of gross par value following insurance claims paid on bonds that matured July 1, 2026, with only $20 million payments due in each of 2027 and 2028.
surprises.expectation_evidence: PREPA Q1 level: “$425M gross par, unchanged”; the preview also said “~$35M of PREPA-related debt service remained payable across the rest of 2026.”

surprises.description: MBIA Insurance Corp. reported $27 million of statutory net income after the preview described its capital as flat and flagged Zohar as a legacy exposure, but did not anticipate a large reserve benefit from reassessing Zohar recoveries.
surprises.fact_evidence: MBIA Insurance Corp. posted statutory net income of $27 million in Q2 2026 (up from $4 million a year earlier), driven by a large loss reserve benefit tied to Zohar CDO recovery reassessments.

surprises.description: Management put the rejected PREPA offer at roughly $0.30–$0.40 per dollar while recent market indications were about $0.75, highlighting a larger gap between the offer and bondholder value indications than the preview had quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimated the rejected settlement offer valued bonds at roughly $0.30 to $0.40 on the dollar, versus recent market indications of about $0.75.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was one cent worse than the preview's $0.13 loss-per-share consensus, though it fell within the preview's broader base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted net loss was $7 million (negative $0.14 per share) in Q2 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) consensus: “–$0.13”; base scenario: “–$0.13 to –$0.18.”

in_line: Book value per share was negative $45.58, within the preview's expected range of negative $45.00 to negative $45.75.
Holding-company cash and liquid assets were $337 million, within the preview's expected $335–350 million range.
The $71 million of remaining share-buyback capacity matched the preview's reported $71 million authorization.
The PREPA offer remained rejected, as the preview had already said the approximately $3 billion offer was formally rejected by the bondholder group.

surprises.description: ARKO reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $72 million, below the preview’s guidance-implied $80–85 million bogey. Management said the decline was largely driven by $3.3 million of higher same-store credit card fees as fuel prices rose.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA declined to $72 million from $76.9 million”; the decline was “largely driven by $3.3 million of higher same-store credit card fees tied to elevated fuel prices.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA bogey math” put Q2 at “roughly $80–85M”; the base case also expected “$80–85M.”

surprises.description: Same-store merchandise sales ex-cigarettes fell 0.9%, rather than reaching the preview’s expected 1% or better. The preview had identified a second positive quarter as an important test of whether the merchandise turnaround was continuing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store merchandise sales ex-cigarettes declining a modest 0.9%”; lower SNAP EBT sales pressured comps by approximately 75 basis points.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “What good looks like” was “≥ +1.0%”; the preview said the market wanted “a second positive quarter with an acceleration.”

surprises.description: Same-store retail fuel gallons fell 5.7%, weaker than the preview’s expectation that the decline improve to better than 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store retail fuel gallons fell 5.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “SS gallons better than −3%” would be a key signal.

surprises.description: Retail fuel margin reached 48.7 cents per gallon, above the preview’s 46-cent threshold, and management raised the full-year outlook to 45.5–47.5 cents from the 41.5–43.5-cent range cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Same-store fuel cents-per-gallon margin “rose 6.5% to $0.487,” and management “raised its full-year retail fuel margin outlook to $0.455–$0.475 per gallon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s key-metric threshold was “≥46¢”; it cited a FY guide of “41.5–43.5¢.”

surprises.description: ARKO reported a 5% quarterly increase in loyalty enrollment and said enrolled members spend more than twice as much as non-enrolled members; the preview did not identify loyalty as a metric to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loyalty enrollment grew by over 100,000 members (5%) in the quarter,” and enrolled members spend “more than 2x” that of non-enrolled members.

surprises.description: ARKO disclosed that it repurchased $38 million of its senior notes for $35 million in cash, an unanticipated capital-allocation action that reduced long-term debt. The preview had instead highlighted a possible step-up in equity buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $38 million of its 5.18% senior notes for $35 million cash”; long-term debt was $675 million, down $29 million from Q1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s capital-returns watch item listed “Buyback step-up.”

in_line: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $245–265 million, as the preview’s base case expected; the preview also anticipated management continuing to cite uncertainty.
Merchandise margin expanded to 34.7%, above the preview’s threshold of 34.0% or higher.

The USPP acquisition’s scale and expected contribution were already disclosed in the preview: approximately 280 million gallons, around $30 million of annual adjusted EBITDA, and pro forma leverage of 3.0–3.5x.
The lower year-over-year net income comparison was not unexpected: the preview had flagged that Q2 2025 included a one-time gain and cautioned that EPS comparisons were noisy.

surprises.description: Wendy’s withdrew its full-year 2026 outlook instead of reaffirming or narrowing it, and said continued traffic headwinds mean it does not expect year-over-year system-wide sales growth in either Q3 or Q4. That is a more severe reset than the preview’s base case of narrowing the outlook and its stated possibility of a cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management withdrew its full-year 2026 financial outlook, citing a comprehensive turnaround assessment, and expects continued traffic headwinds preventing year-over-year system-wide sales growth in Q3 or Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A cut or a narrowing to the low end is a live possibility”; the base case expected the FY guide to be “narrowed to the low end.”

surprises.description: Wendy’s cut its quarterly dividend in half, from the preview’s cited $0.14 per share to $0.07, to fund turnaround investments. The preview flagged dividend-cut risk, but the actual reduction was a concrete and substantial cut rather than just softer dividend language.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its quarterly dividend to $0.07 per share” to “create flexibility for turnaround investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the dividend as “$0.14/qtr” and said “the market is partly pricing a cut.”

surprises.description: Traffic remained sharply weak: U.S. traffic fell 12.5%, with negative double-digit declines in each period, while new products and promotions lifted average check but did not bring in the expected traffic. The preview’s base case expected comps to be roughly flat versus April, and its bull case expected the launches to drive traffic.
surprises.fact_evidence: U.S. same-restaurant sales were driven by a “12.5% traffic decrease,” with “negative double-digit traffic in each period”; launches “boosted average check but failed to drive expected traffic.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected U.S. SRS to be “−6% to −7%, roughly flat vs. April”; the bull case said “Biggie Deals + Pretzel Bacon Pub / Minions LTOs drive traffic.”

surprises.description: U.S. company-operated restaurant margin reached 13.8%, well above the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly 11.5%–12%. That strength came despite commodity inflation running around 9%, above the preview’s cited 8% level, and labor inflation remaining around 4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. company-operated restaurant margin was 13.8%,” pressured by “roughly 9% commodity cost increases” and “about 4% labor rate inflation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “margin ~11.5–12%”; the preview cited “8% commodity and 4% labor inflation.”

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow reached $120.3 million, up $10.8 million year over year. Against the preview’s full-year guide of $190–205 million and its expectation that cash flow would be back-half weighted, this leaves substantially less of the annual target to generate in the second half than the preview implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow rose $10.8 million to $120.3 million for the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 free cash flow guidance of “$190–205M” and described it as “Back-half weighted.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.18, two cents above the preview’s $0.16 consensus estimate. The beat was positive but modest in absolute terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.18 for the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus EPS of “$0.16.”

in_line: U.S. same-restaurant sales declined 7%, within the preview’s expected range of roughly −6% to −7%.
Global system-wide sales declined 6.5% on a constant-currency basis, broadly consistent with the preview’s mid-single-digit decline expectation.
Adjusted EBITDA of $124.1 million was within the preview’s implied range of approximately $120–125 million.

surprises.description: Post said preliminary FY2027 adjusted EBITDA should be roughly flat against a comparable base of about $1.48 billion. The preview framed the market as looking for a path back to growth in FY2027, so flat guidance points to a weaker recovery trajectory than investors were hoping to hear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Preliminary FY2027 guidance is for EBITDA roughly flat” versus a “comparable adjusted EBITDA base of approximately $1.48 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus is not asking POST to grow this quarter; it is asking management to defend the FY guide and articulate a path back to growth in FY27.”

surprises.description: Although Post bought back 4% of its shares in Q3 and reduced the year-to-date share count by about 17%, management said it is shifting from aggressive buybacks toward debt reduction. The preview treated Q3 repurchases as a key signal of conviction and highlighted the new authorization, but did not anticipate a move away from buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post repurchased 4% of outstanding shares in Q3,” bringing the year-to-date reduction to “approximately 17%”; management is “shifting capital allocation from aggressive share buybacks toward debt reduction,” despite “no bond maturity for four years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buyback pace in Q3 is a direct read on management's own conviction. An aggressive number is the strongest available signal”; the preview also cited the new $600 million authorization.

surprises.description: Post attributed roughly 60% of the year-over-year pet business decline to value brands, mostly 9Lives, which is facing promotions from two rivals pricing below it. The preview focused on whether 9Lives distribution losses had stopped compounding, so the reported competitive pressure suggests the pet weakness remained a live issue rather than a clear stabilization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 60% of the year-over-year pet business decline is attributable to value brands, mostly 9Lives,” which “faces competitive promotions with two rivals pricing below its brand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged whether “9Lives distribution losses from prior price increases have stopped compounding” and whether pet food’s decline was “decelerating from −14.1%.”

surprises.description: Post disclosed that it has reached about 30% pet market share and sees substantial cost savings still available through portfolio simplification and formula harmonization, beyond footprint changes. The preview emphasized pet volume and the Nutrish and 9Lives outlook, but did not flag this additional cost-savings opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pet business has reached approximately 30% market share,” with “substantial untapped cost-savings opportunities in pet beyond footprint, including portfolio simplification and formula harmonization.”

surprises.description: Post said FY2027 cereal volume is expected to decline about 2.5%, but that its underperformance gap versus the category is narrowing as assortment adjustments take effect. The continuing decline is not a return to growth, though the narrowing gap is more encouraging than the preview’s concern about a further cereal step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cereal volume is expected to decline about 2.5% in FY2027,” while Post is “narrowing its underperformance gap to category” as assortment adjustments take effect.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited tracked-channel data showing a “further ‘step-down’ in PCB” and warned that cereal could join pet food “in accelerating decline”; it also sought an FY2027 path back to growth.

surprises.description: Post plans to close two peanut butter plants following the AW integration, using the cost-optimization approach previously applied to three cereal plants. This is a newly disclosed opportunity for efficiency improvement that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post is closing two peanut butter plants following the AW integration,” applying “the same cost-optimization playbook used to close three cereal plants.”

surprises.description: Post described refrigerated retail pressure from fuel and freight costs and egg prices falling below its grain-based procurement costs, in addition to timing and HPAI comparisons. The preview anticipated HPAI-related normalization and modeled a weaker refrigerated retail quarter, but did not flag this unfavorable procurement-cost mismatch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 refrigerated retail was pressured” by “higher fuel/freight costs and unfavorable egg market dynamics where market prices plummeted below the company's grain-based procurement costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Refrigerated Retail at about $40 million of EBITDA and cited the Crystal Farms divestiture as a likely source of lower sales; it also highlighted lapping peak HPAI-related economics elsewhere.

surprises.description: Management expects FY2027 pricing actions mostly later in the year, concentrated in PCB/pet, with inflation toward the high end of prior expectations and pricing lagging inflation because of retailer negotiations. The later-year timing was consistent with the preview, but the higher inflation pressure and lagged pricing imply a less favorable near-term recovery in those costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Most FY2027 pricing actions” are expected “later in the year,” concentrated in “the PCB/pet segment where inflation is running toward the higher end of prior expectations,” with “pricing lagging inflation due to retailer negotiation timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected fuel-surcharge inflation to be absorbed in FY2026 “with pricing deferred to FY2027.”

in_line: Foodservice normalized EBITDA run rate: Post estimated about $500 million annually, consistent with the preview’s approximately $125 million quarterly run-rate expectation.

surprises.description: RGCO cut FY2026 EPS guidance to $1.29–$1.32, below the preview’s expected $1.31–$1.37 range and its expectation that guidance would be reaffirmed or narrowed toward the upper end. Management attributed the revision to unusual May weather and associated gas delivery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management narrowed its full-year fiscal 2026 EPS forecast to a range of $1.29 to $1.32, citing unusual May weather patterns and associated gas delivery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management either reaffirms $1.31–$1.37, narrows to the upper half, or trims”; the ranked checklist said “Narrow to $1.35–$1.37.”

surprises.description: The Roanoke Gas rate case settled for $3.85 million in incremental annual revenues, below the preview’s expectation of an outcome at or near the $4.3 million request. The roughly $450,000 shortfall is a meaningful reduction from the amount sought.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Roanoke Gas rate case settled at $3.85 million in incremental annual revenues, below the $4.3 million originally sought.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected a final order “at/near $4.3M.”

surprises.description: RGCO accrued $275,000 for customer refunds on rates collected since January 1, whereas the preview expected no material refund reserve. The settled lower rates took effect August 1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company accrued $275,000 for customer refunds as of June 30 related to rates charged since January 1, 2026, with lower settled rates taking effect August 1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s rate-case watch item said “no material refund reserve.”

surprises.description: The LNG peak-shaving facility is expected to remain without restored on-system storage capability until the 2027–2028 winter season, extending the outage beyond the preview’s stated expectation that it would be unavailable for winter 2026–2027. The company did establish a regulatory asset and expects recovery in a future proceeding, partly offsetting the longer outage concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: The 54-year-old facility “suffered structural/metal fatigue damage from Winter Storm Fern,” with restored capability “not expected until the 2027-2028 winter season”; outage costs were excluded from the rate case, but “the company established a regulatory asset and expects recovery in a future proceeding.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the facility was “unavailable for winter 2026-27” and identified reliability and capital risk; it expected SCC regulatory-asset treatment to be confirmed.

surprises.description: Q3 diluted EPS was $0.05 against the preview’s $0.06 consensus, a one-cent miss. Net income was approximately $550,000, also slightly below the preview’s roughly $0.6 million implied estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 net income was approximately $550,000, or $0.05 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q3 diluted EPS consensus of “$0.06” and net income of “~$0.6M implied.”

in_line: Year-to-date EPS was $1.37, matching the preview’s reported 9M EPS of $1.37.
Industrial gas usage increased, but the incremental volumes carried the company’s lowest margins; the preview anticipated increased interruptible industrial volumes at lower-tier margins.
The $15 million note was refinanced at a higher rate, as the preview expected; the disclosed 5.2% fixed rate and higher interest costs confirm the anticipated refinancing headwind.
Full-year capital spending guidance remained roughly $22 million, in line with the preview’s expectation that CapEx would remain on plan.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.52, well above the preview’s $0.42 consensus and even the lower $0.39 whisper estimate. The 40% year-over-year increase was substantially stronger than the growth implied by those estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew approximately 40% to $0.52 versus $0.37 in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $0.42”; the preview also cites a “Most Accurate Estimate (~$0.39).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $140.9 million, far above the preview’s estimated $125–127 million. The 23.3% margin also exceeded the preview’s estimated 21.3–21.5%, expanding nearly 240 basis points rather than the expected 40–60 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 22.5% to $140.9 million with margin expanding nearly 240 basis points to 23.3%, aided by roughly $4 million of eliminated Nova integration costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est.): ~$125–127M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin (my est.): ~21.3–21.5%” and “+40–60 bps.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to $485–495 million, above the preview’s anticipated buy-side range of $465–485 million. The new midpoint is about $20 million above the prior guide midpoint, as the preview expected a raise but not one reaching $495 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to … adjusted EBITDA of $485-$495 million (about $20 million higher at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side expects a raise to roughly … $465–485M EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $606 million, above the preview’s $591.7–592.5 million consensus range; growth was 10% rather than the 7.5% implied by consensus. Core revenue excluding Pivot also grew 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 10% year-over-year to $606 million, with core revenue (excluding Pivot) up 8% to $589.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $591.7M–$592.5M” and “Implied YoY | +7.5%.”

surprises.description: Daily patient visits topped 56,000, exceeding the roughly 55,500–55,800 implied by the preview and its expected 1–1.5% growth. The reported 2.6% increase was a better organic-volume result than the preview’s base expectation, though short of its 56,500-plus clean-beat marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total patient visits rose 2.6% to over 56,000 per day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue of ~$592M backs into roughly 55,500–55,800 visits/day (+1% to +1.5% YoY)” and “56,500+ is a clean beat.”

surprises.description: Employer services visits grew 1.8% instead of turning flat or negative amid the hiring slowdown highlighted in the preview. That was also above the preview’s cited Q1 ex-Nova growth of 0.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Employer services up 1.8%, both above long-term averages.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “employer services visits go negative YoY” was a key risk and listed “Employer services visits vs. flat”; it also noted Q1 ex-Nova visits grew “just +0.7%.”

surprises.description: Revenue per visit grew 4.6%, above the preview’s roughly 3.5% base expectation and its 3% threshold for avoiding a mix-driven concern. California and Tennessee rate increases and favorable initial-injury mix supported the stronger result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue per visit grew 4.6%, driven by 4.9% work comp and 3.2% employer services growth, boosted by California and Tennessee rate increases … and favorable initial-injury visit mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “RPV ~$151 (+3.5%)” and said “RPV growth below 3%” would signal a risk.

surprises.description: Onsite Health Clinics organic growth excluding Pivot was 27.9%, above the preview’s 20% organic-growth watch threshold and the 20.9% organic growth cited for Q1. The reported segment growth of 72.1% was boosted by Pivot, so the organic figure is the clearest comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Onsite Health Clinics segment grew revenue 72.1% to $38.8 million (27.9% excluding Pivot).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Onsite health organic growth ≥20%” and cited Q1 organic growth of “+20.9% ex-Pivot.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was already just under 3x in Q2, reaching the preview’s year-end target well ahead of schedule. The reduction also triggered a 25-basis-point Term Loan B spread step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage fell to just under 3x from 3.4x in Q1, reaching the year-end target well ahead of schedule and triggering a 25 basis point Term Loan B spread step-down to 175 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed net leverage “comfortably below 3.0x at year-end (3.4x at Q1).”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year free-cash-flow guidance midpoint by $5 million, to $230 million from $225 million. The preview gave the existing range but did not specifically anticipate a free-cash-flow raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to … free cash flow of $220-$240 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow $215M–$235M.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a CEO succession announcement. The company disclosed a planned transition in which Keith Newton becomes Executive Chairman and current President and CFO Matt DiCanio becomes CEO on November 1, 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Keith Newton will transition to Executive Chairman effective November 1, 2026, with current President and CFO Matt DiCanio becoming President and CEO as part of a multi-year succession plan.”

in_line: The revenue guidance range was raised to $2.325–$2.375 billion, broadly in line with the preview’s anticipated raise to roughly $2.30–$2.38 billion.
CapEx guidance remained $70–$80 million, matching the range in force before the release.

surprises.description: Spectrum Brands’ Q3 sales growth was stronger than the preview’s roughly 4.7% expectation: sales rose 7.7% year over year, or 6.6% organically excluding favorable FX.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales increased 7.7% year-over-year (6.6% organic excluding $7.5 million favorable FX) with all three business units delivering growth in Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Consensus $732.4M | +4.7%”; the preview’s segment model estimated total growth of about 4.8%.

surprises.description: Home & Garden substantially outperformed the preview’s estimate: sales rose 19% to $225 million, versus the preview’s model of about 9% growth to $206 million. The quarter also exceeded the preview’s seasonal framing, reaching demand levels above the pandemic-era peak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Home & Garden delivered a record quarter with net sales of $225 million, up 19%, surpassing even COVID-19 pandemic-era demand levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Home & Garden sales of “~$206M (+9%)” and described Q3 as the seasonal peak.

surprises.description: Global Pet Care organic growth fell short of the preview’s expected momentum: organic sales rose 2.9%, rather than the roughly 7% growth modeled or the mid-to-high-single-digit growth the preview said was needed. Its margin, however, expanded more than the preview modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global Pet Care organic net sales rose 2.9% with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 250 basis points to 19.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Global Pet Care sales growth of “~7%” and said organic growth “needs to hold mid-to-high single digits”; it estimated an 18.6% margin.

surprises.description: Home & Personal Care delivered better operating results than the preview modeled: all three business units grew, while HPC adjusted EBITDA excluding refunds rose to $14.4 million from $7 million in the year-ago quarter, above the preview’s $9 million estimate. Management also disclosed an impairment charge tied to the Oaktree partnership that the preview had not anticipated.
