surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | Not published (est. ~$5.5–6.0M)”; “A Q2 Adjusted EBITDA below ~$5.5M makes the FY guide arithmetically very hard”; “Sub-12% margin says the marketing spend isn't converting to operating leverage.”

surprises.description: Customer acquisition costs rose rather than stabilizing: CAC reached about $3,500 per case, above both the $3,400 Q1 level and the $2,900 level a year earlier. Marketing also increased to roughly 20% of revenue year-to-date from 18%, contrary to the preview’s hoped-for flat-to-down sequential CAC.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer acquisition cost rose to approximately $3,500 per case from $2,900 a year ago, with marketing spend increasing to roughly 20% of revenue year-to-date versus 18% last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flat-to-down sequentially is the tell that the CTV/influencer/digital-funnel rebuild is working.”

surprises.description: Management reported that sales softened in June and continued into July, and guided Q3 revenue to be down single digits on a comparable basis. That is weaker near-term momentum than the preview’s base case of comps improving, although management said it expects revenue and Adjusted EBITDA to return to year-over-year growth in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sales trends softened in June and continued into July”; “Management guided Q3 revenue to be down single digits on a comparable basis, but expects Q4 to return to year-over-year growth in both revenue and adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base-case scenario: “comps improving but not accelerating”; preview described Q2 as “seasonally the strongest quarter.”

surprises.description: The company addressed the looming loan maturity by extending the term loan to November 2027 and reported substantial debt reduction, rather than leaving the refinancing question unresolved. The preview had identified an update at the release as a key event and treated silence or punitive terms as a major downside risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced gross debt by over $30 million since the start of 2025, ending Q2 with approximately $44 million gross debt and $24 million total liquidity, and extended its term loan maturity to November 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said on the Q1 call they were ‘in process to refinance’ and would give details with Q2 results”; “silence or a punitive structure is the biggest downside tail.”

surprises.description: AirSculpt disclosed more than 200 skin excision procedures, a new Alloclay partnership, and a management estimate of a $100 million-plus long-term GLP-1 revenue opportunity. The preview anticipated that new-SKU traction could matter, but did not specify an opportunity estimate of this size; the near-term caveat is that these offerings are excluded from guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AirSculpt announced a new Alloclay partnership with Tiger Aesthetics and completed over 200 skin excision procedures”; “the company estimates a $100 million-plus long-term GLP-1 revenue opportunity”; guidance “excludes contributions from these early-stage new offerings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A disclosed case count and revenue/case for this cohort would be new, valuable information — this is the entire long-term bull narrative.”

in_line: Case growth was approximately +1%, consistent with the preview’s derived estimate of roughly +1–2% and its expectation that positive case growth could continue.

surprises.description: N-able cut its FY26 ARR outlook to $562–565 million from the preview’s $581–586 million, and revenue guidance to $539–542 million from $554–559 million. The new Q3 revenue range also implies only about 3% reported growth, signaling a much weaker near-term trajectory than the prior full-year outlook implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year 2026 guidance,” now expecting ARR of “$562-565 million (4-5% reported growth)” and revenue of “$539-542 million”; Q3 revenue guidance of “$134.5-135.5 million” implies approximately 3% reported growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance (set 5/7/26, unchanged): Revenue $554–559M (+8–9% reported, +7–8% cc); Total ARR $581–586M (+8–9%).”

surprises.description: Q2 ARR was $544 million, well below the preview’s $555–558 million estimate, with 6% constant-currency growth versus the preview’s expected roughly 6–7%. This was a weaker ARR result than the preview’s roughly 8% reported-growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 ARR was $544 million, growing 6% year-over-year in constant currency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total ARR” consensus “~$555–558M”; expected “~8% reported against ~6–7% cc.”

surprises.description: Renewals weakened sharply in N-able’s largest annual renewal cohort, concentrated in UEM and EDR, and management said this drove the net new ARR shortfall and guidance cut. The preview anticipated pressure around growth and the new CRO, but did not forecast this deterioration in renewal rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 renewal rates in the largest annual renewal cohort (concentrated in UEM and EDR) fell from the high-80s to the mid-80s during the quarter, driving the net new ARR shortfall and guidance cut.”

surprises.description: N-able plans to cut about 6% of its workforce, an unanticipated restructuring that will reduce annualized operating expenses but incur charges in the second half. The savings are helpful, but the need for the cuts adds a negative signal alongside the lowered outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reduce total headcount by approximately 6% (from ~2,000 employees), cutting annualized operating expenses by $11-13 million while incurring $4-6 million in restructuring charges in the second half.”

surprises.description: Growth in customers with at least $50,000 of ARR was about 7%, below the preview’s expected 13% growth. Their share of ARR was a little better than expected at about 63% versus 62%, so the cohort showed both slower growth and slightly higher concentration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers contributing $50,000 or more of ARR grew ~7% to 2,706 and now represent ~63% of total ARR.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$50K+ ARR customers grew 13% YoY and are 62% of total ARR”; the preview said to watch whether growth “holds double digits.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 80% from 82% a year earlier, a deterioration not flagged in the preview’s expectations. The reported 29% adjusted EBITDA margin was in line, but the gross-margin decline is an adverse operating detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 80% from 82% a year earlier.”

surprises.description: Data protection ARR exceeded $200 million, continued to grow faster than the company overall, and again led net new ARR growth. The preview highlighted new product launches but did not anticipate this specific business line’s scale or contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data protection ARR surpassed $200 million, continues to grow faster than the total company, and again led net new ARR growth this quarter.”

surprises.description: Management said the newly launched DRaaS product could become one of N-able’s fastest-growing SKUs and reach $10 million in ARR. The preview expected a back-half product ramp, but did not give this specific growth ambition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly GA-launched DRaaS product contributed no revenue in Q2 (launched July), but management expects it to become one of their fastest-growing SKUs to reach $10 million ARR.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H2 product ramp: DRaaS full launch + Google Workspace backup”; management had said FY26 ARR was back-half weighted “due to some of the new offerings we're bringing to market.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $40 million at a 29% margin, in line with the preview’s approximately $40 million and 29% expectations.
Dollar-based net revenue retention was 106% reported and 103% constant currency, matching the preview’s 106% / 103% estimate.
DRaaS launched in July, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a back-half launch; its lack of Q2 revenue is consistent with that timing.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was expected to be about $79.3 million, but Target reported approximately $86 million, about 8% above consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was approximately $86 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $79.3M”

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q2 adjusted EBITDA at $13–16 million; Target reported approximately $18 million, above even the top of that estimated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was approximately $86 million with adjusted EBITDA of approximately $18 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | no clean published consensus — my est. $13–16M”

surprises.description: The preview expected FY26 revenue of $370–380 million and adjusted EBITDA of $75–85 million. Target raised those ranges to $410–420 million and $85–95 million, respectively.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 outlook to total revenue of $410-$420 million and adjusted EBITDA of $85-$95 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance: Revenue $370–380M · Adj. EBITDA $75–85M”

surprises.description: The preview expected 2026 capital spending of $460–480 million, but Target now expects $490–510 million excluding acquisitions, an increase of $30 million at both ends of the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital spending of $490-$510 million excluding acquisitions.”

surprises.description: The preview’s 2027 exit-rate benchmark was above $680 million in annualized revenue and above $240 million in annualized adjusted EBITDA. Target raised those targets to above $700 million and above $260 million, based solely on its existing contract portfolio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Target projects exiting 2027 with annualized revenue exceeding $700 million and adjusted EBITDA above $260 million, based solely on the existing contract portfolio without pipeline contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2027 exit run-rate target: >$680M annualized revenue, >$240M annualized Adj. EBITDA”

surprises.description: The preview set a Q2 WHS revenue benchmark above $30 million; Target reported approximately $36 million, around 20% above that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The WHS segment generated approximately $36 million in Q2 revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “WHS revenue >$30M”

surprises.description: The preview said new WHS contracts carried 40–50% margins. Target reported WHS segment margins of around 53.5%, above the top of that expected range, alongside more than 700 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion versus Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of more than 700 basis points versus Q1, with WHS segment margins around 53.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New contracts carry 40–50% margins per management.”

surprises.description: Target reported more than $110 million of year-to-date operating cash flow, a cash-generation detail the preview did not flag; however, more than $100 million came from customer advance payments tied to recent WHS awards, so much of it reflects payment timing rather than recurring operating cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date operating cash flow exceeded $110 million, including more than $100 million of customer advanced payments tied to recent WHS contract awards.”

surprises.description: The preview described an active pipeline and expected further contract activity, but Target quantified a pipeline exceeding 20,000 beds, heavily weighted toward AI data centers and power generation, and said it was finalizing multiple definitive agreements for projects of 1,000-plus beds expected in coming quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The active pipeline exceeds 20,000 beds heavily weighted toward AI data centers and power generation, with management finalizing multiple definitive agreements for projects of 1,000-plus beds each expected in coming quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New contract award announced with the print”; the preview also described “additional awards in advanced negotiation” as a bull-case signal.

in_line: The preview noted that the $660 million ABL had already closed and that net leverage was 0.6x at Q1; the call reported the replacement facility and quarter-end net leverage of 0.6x.

surprises.description: Jerash reported Q1 revenue of $50.2 million, above both the preview’s $48.86 million consensus and the $48.3 million top of company guidance. That is a meaningful upside to an already high revenue bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 Q1 revenue grew 26.7% year-over-year to a record $50.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q1 revenue consensus of “$48.86M” and company guidance of “$47.5–48.3M.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.13, above the preview’s $0.09 consensus. The reported result exceeded the expected figure by about 44%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income advanced more than fivefold to $1.7 million ($0.13 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Diluted EPS $0.09.”

surprises.description: Operating income reached $2.6 million, exceeding the preview’s roughly $2.3 million estimate despite operating expenses being slightly higher than its modeled level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating income rose 174% to $2.6 million”; operating expenses “increased to $5.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case estimated “operating income ~$2.3M” and modeled “~$5.5M” of opex.

surprises.description: The preview expected the first capacity phase to add about 700 workers by year-end 2026; management instead described about 500 workers for the roughly 15% capacity addition. The stated timing and capacity increase remain consistent with the preview, but the worker count is lower.
surprises.fact_evidence: “~15% added by end of calendar 2026 (500 workers).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “Phase 1: +15% capacity / ~700 workers by end of calendar 2026.”

surprises.description: Management introduced Q2 revenue guidance of approximately $49–51 million, alongside a forecast gross-margin decline to roughly 14–15% because of higher raw-material transportation costs. The preview did not provide a Q2 margin expectation, so this is a newly disclosed outlook that signals lower margins than Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue to approximately $49 million to $51 million with gross margin declining to roughly 14%-15%, reflecting increased raw material transportation costs.”

surprises.description: The U.S.–Jordan duty-free trade announcement was already generating new purchase orders and inquiries, and Jerash’s largest customer projected orders about 15% above last year’s season. This added a concrete near-term demand signal beyond the preview’s discussion of Jordan’s existing duty-free status and geopolitical order risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: The agreement “has already generated new purchase orders and inquiries from new importers”; the largest customer “projected orders roughly 15% above last year's season following the zero-duty tariff announcement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Jordan’s U.S. FTA duty-free status “the structural moat” and flagged some key-customer orders as “partly contingent on a Middle East ceasefire/peace agreement.”

surprises.description: Jerash disclosed a new Urban Outfitters relationship with a forecast first-year order of $5 million, along with potential opportunities involving Lee, Wrangler, Reebok, and North Face. The preview anticipated watching for new brand names but did not identify this customer or an order of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New customer Urban Outfitters was onboarded with a forecasted first-year order of $5 million,” with the named brands representing additional potential opportunities.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any new brand names” but did not name Urban Outfitters or describe a $5 million order.

in_line: Q1 gross margin was 16.4%, within the preview’s approximately 16% expectation and the company’s 15–17% guidance range.
The second capacity phase remains in line with the preview: management described a 20–25% addition by mid-2027, compared with the preview’s expected 20–25% by mid-2027.
The quarterly dividend of $0.05 per share was continued, as the preview expected.
Management did not provide FY2027 full-year guidance, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it might remain withheld.

surprises.description: Telos raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $23.6–28.6 million from $20.6–28.0 million. The preview’s base case expected the range to be narrowed but not raised, so lifting the low end by $3 million was better than that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $23.6-28.6 million (up from $20.6-28 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY narrowed to upper half but not raised”; the preview also asked whether management would remove the $20.6M low end.

surprises.description: Telos plans to phase out a low-margin software resale stream and lowered the FY2026 revenue outlook by about $2.5 million, with the new range at $187–195 million. The preview’s base case anticipated narrowing the range but not a revenue-guide cut; the move trades some reported revenue for better margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Starting in Q4, the company will phase out a low-margin third-party software resale stream (single-digit gross margin) worth roughly $33 million in annual revenue, cutting the full-year revenue outlook by about $2.5 million to a new range of $187-195 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY narrowed to upper half but not raised”; the preview listed a trim toward $187–193M as part of its bear scenario.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $47.7 million, above the preview’s roughly $47 million whisper bar and the company’s $44–46 million guidance range. The beat was modest versus the preview’s already elevated expectation and came from stronger-than-forecast TELOS ID performance, including TSA PreCheck and DMDC.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 33% year-over-year to $47.7 million, exceeding the guidance range of $44 million to $46 million, driven by stronger-than-forecasted TELOS ID performance including TSA PreCheck and the Defense Manpower Data Center program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat ~$47M as the real bar.”

surprises.description: Management said phasing out the low-margin resale stream, together with completion of prior TSA PreCheck investment recognition, should lift cash gross margins by about 10 percentage points in the second half of 2027. The preview discussed the near-term margin outlook but did not anticipate this specific longer-term margin step-up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Eliminating the low-margin software plus completion of prior TSA PreCheck investment recognition is expected to boost cash gross margins by approximately 10 percentage points (600 bps + 400 bps) in the second half of 2027.”

surprises.description: Management expressed openness to a change-of-control transaction if it clearly offered a superior path to shareholder value, while also emphasizing continued organic value creation. The preview did not flag this strategic possibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management indicated openness to a change-of-control transaction if it clearly represented a superior path to shareholder value, while emphasizing continued organic value creation.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance implies a slight year-over-year decline, although revenue would grow 6% excluding prior-period non-recurring startup revenue. The preview anticipated a low-single-digit year-over-year growth outlook for the second half, so the Q3 headline is weaker, partly offset by the adjusted comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue is guided to $49.2-50.6 million with cash gross margin of 37.5-38.5%, reflecting a slight year-over-year decline due to prior-period non-recurring startup revenue, though implying 6% growth excluding that item.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CFO Mark Bendza explicitly guided 2H total revenue growth down to low-single-digit Y/Y.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $6.9 million was within the preview’s $6.5–7.5 million base-case range and close to its roughly $5.5 million guidance-midpoint estimate.
FY2026 cash gross margin guidance of 39–40% was broadly in line with the preview’s approximately 39% outlook.
Free cash flow of $6.6 million and a sixth consecutive quarter above a 12% free-cash-flow margin continued the trend the preview flagged as a fifth consecutive quarter above 12%.
The company repurchased more than 1 million shares for $4.7 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that buybacks would accelerate from Q1’s 0.5 million shares and $2.2 million.

The pipeline remained slightly above $500 million in total contract value, with award decisions expected in the second half of 2026, broadly matching the preview’s pipeline size and timing expectations.

surprises.description: Conduent reported $531 million of continuing-operations revenue, far below the preview’s $702 million consensus. The preview warned that a discontinued-operations reclassification could make revenue non-comparable, so the size of the gap is large but partly reflects a changed reporting basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue from continuing operations fell 11.9% year-over-year to $531 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $702M” and “A reclassification would produce an optical revenue ‘miss’ that is economically meaningless.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was only $16 million, well below the preview’s roughly $40–43 million estimate for a softer quarter. The 3% margin also compressed 80 basis points, rather than expanding as the preview estimated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $16 million from $23 million, with margins compressing 80 basis points to 3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2 adj. EBITDA estimate: $40–43M (5.6–5.9% margin)” and “+70–100bps margin expansion.”

surprises.description: Commercial revenue fell 13%, worse than the preview’s Q1 decline of 10.2% and beyond its stated bear-case threshold of a decline past 12%. The preview did not flag that the largest commercial client would end its contract in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Conduent's largest commercial client is ending its contract in Q3 2026, contributing to a 13% year-over-year commercial revenue decline to $316 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Deceleration of the decline to single digits is the bull case; acceleration past −12% breaks the FY revenue guide.”

surprises.description: Government revenue was $215 million, below the preview’s roughly $248 million estimate, and its adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 23.7% rather than holding near the Q1 level of about 26%. The call attributed the weakness partly to completed New Mexico Medicaid revenue recognition and prior-year favorable reserve releases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Government segment revenue fell to $215 million from $238 million with adjusted EBITDA margin down 150 basis points to 23.7%,” partly due to “the New Mexico Medicaid implementation completing revenue recognition and prior-year favorable reserve releases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Government revenue of “~$248M” and said “Government margin holds near 26%.”

surprises.description: The revised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA range is $140–170 million, $20 million below the previously stated $160–190 million range at both endpoints. The revenue range also moved from $2.80–2.90 billion to $2.15–2.25 billion, though the company says the new guidance reflects discontinued operations and is therefore not directly comparable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revised its full-year 2026 guidance to reflect discontinued operations, targeting revenue of $2.15–$2.25 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $140–$170 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 Revenue (guide) | $2.80B – $2.90B” and “FY2026 Adj. EBITDA (guide) | $160M – $190M”; the preview also flagged “cut/restate for divestitures (ambiguous).”

surprises.description: The qualified ACV pipeline was $3 billion, below the preview’s approximately $3.5 billion reference. However, it was up 11% year over year, and the commercial pipeline had grown 48% since the start of 2026, tempering the shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The qualified ACV pipeline stands at $3 billion, up 11% year-over-year, with the commercial segment pipeline growing 48% since the start of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 ACV $114M (+$5M YoY), qualified pipeline ~$3.5B (up from $3.2B).”

surprises.description: Q2 new-business ACV was $99 million, down from $111 million a year earlier, although it improved sequentially and first-half signings were flat year over year with a higher recurring-revenue mix. The preview flagged ACV as a key metric but did not provide a Q2 target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed $99 million of new business ACV in Q2 (down from $111 million a year ago but up sequentially), with $188 million signed in the first half—flat versus 2025 but with 12% more recurring revenue signings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New business ACV / pipeline” was a key metric to watch; the preview cited Q1 ACV of “$114M (+$5M YoY).”

surprises.description: Conduent said the divestiture proceeds would be used primarily to reduce debt, resolving the allocation question more decisively than the preview’s expectation that management was still considering alternatives. The businesses also transacted at a mid-teens adjusted EBITDA multiple, described as well above Conduent’s current trading multiple.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The transportation divestitures transacted at a mid-teens adjusted EBITDA multiple … well above Conduent's current trading multiple, with proceeds earmarked primarily for debt reduction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said allocation was ‘under discussion with bondholders’ — options span debt reduction, buybacks, and reinvestment.”

surprises.description: Adjusted net leverage improved to 2.1x from the 2.8x level cited in the preview, and management gave a target of roughly 1x within 18–24 months. That is a stronger balance-sheet update than the preview’s starting leverage suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net leverage improved to 2.1x this quarter, with management targeting roughly 1x within 18–24 months as transformation benefits materialize.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Net leverage (Q1'26) | 2.8x” and described the proceeds allocation as still under discussion.

surprises.description: Management supplied more detail on the $100 million annualized savings program than the preview had: most savings are headcount-driven, more than half are identified, and the company aims to eliminate outside consultants by year-end. This is evidence of execution progress, though it does not quantify the program’s in-year EBITDA contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The $100 million annualized cost savings program is roughly 60–70% headcount-driven and 30–40% technology-related, with more than half already identified and management aiming to eliminate all outside consultants by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “$100M cost-reduction program (18-month horizon) needs a quantified in-year contribution.”

in_line: The approximately $234 million of gross divestiture proceeds was already described in the preview as contracted; the call’s expected proceeds amount is broadly in line with that expectation.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag SpaceX as a driver, but GCM Grosvenor said its roughly $150 million investment was valued at about $3.5 billion, its largest single-issuer gain in firm history. The gain is unrealized and subject to lockup, but SpaceX also lifted ARS returns to about 14% for the quarter versus about 10% excluding it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The firm's ~$150 million investment in SpaceX (average cost of $6.37 per share) was valued at approximately $3.5 billion as of last week,” with “gains remain unrealized and subject to lockup.” The ARS composite returned “~14% gross returns for the quarter including SpaceX and ~10% excluding it.”

surprises.description: AUM and fee-paying AUM came in above the preview's ranges: AUM was $97 billion versus an estimate of $93–95 billion, and fee-paying AUM was $78 billion versus $75–77 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: GCM Grosvenor ended Q2 with “$97 billion in AUM and $78 billion in fee-paying AUM, both up approximately 13% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “AUM $93–95B” and “Fee-paying AUM $75–77B.”

surprises.description: Fee-related earnings modestly exceeded the preview's $48–49 million estimate, reaching $50 million. The 45% margin was at the top of the expected 44–45% range rather than a material margin surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-related earnings grew 21% to $50 million (45% FRE margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “FRE $48–49M” and a “44–45%” margin.

surprises.description: Management gave a specific positive outlook for ARS fees: strong Q2 performance is expected to lift Q3 ARS management fees about 10% sequentially and nearly 20% year-over-year. The preview highlighted ARS inflows and returns but did not anticipate this fee-growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Because ARS fees are billed in advance on beginning-of-quarter AUM, “strong Q2 performance is expected to drive Q3 ARS fees up ~10% sequentially and nearly 20% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: The fundraising mix showed unusually strong contributions from individual investors and insurers relative to their starting share of AUM. The preview discussed wealth-channel momentum, but did not anticipate these proportions.
surprises.fact_evidence: Individual investors and insurance channels drove “23% and 18% of year-to-date fundraising despite representing only 5% and 4% of AUM at the start of the year.”

in_line: Q2 fundraising was $2.3 billion, within the preview's $2.0–2.5 billion estimate and above the management bar of exceeding Q1's $1.5 billion; management's second-half fundraising outlook also matched the prior expectation that the back half would outpace the front half.
Fee-related revenue of $111 million was at the top of the preview's $109–111 million estimate.

The estimated $35–40 million of unrealized annual performance fees was broadly consistent with the preview's roughly $35 million run-rate expectation; most fees crystallizing in Q4 also fits the preview's note that ARS fees predominantly crystallize then.

The $0.12 quarterly dividend was maintained, as expected. The preview described the remaining buyback authorization as $64 million and said silence on an increase was defensible; the reported $55 million remaining after about $17 million of repurchases does not indicate an authorization increase.

surprises.description: RadNet reported Q2 revenue of $622.7 million, $12.7 million above the preview’s $610 million consensus estimate and also above its $620 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total company revenue rose 25% year-over-year to a record $622.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $610.0M”; the bull case called for “≥$620M.”

surprises.description: Same-center advanced imaging growth came in above the preview’s roughly 8% base case and 9% bull-case marker, with a favorable shift in procedure mix toward advanced imaging.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-center advanced imaging volumes grew 9.6% (MRI +10%, CT +8.6%, PET-CT +8.8%), driving a 238 basis point favorable mix shift toward advanced imaging, which reached 29.9% of total procedure volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Same-center advanced imaging ≥8%” was a key metric, with “same-center ~8%” in the base case and “≥9%” in the bull case.

surprises.description: RadNet raised imaging-center EBITDA guidance by $5 million at both ends and raised free-cash-flow guidance by $3 million at both ends, rather than holding those ranges flat as the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 imaging center guidance, lifting … adjusted EBITDA to $345–$358 million, and free cash flow to $115–$125 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated a “Modest imaging revenue raise, EBITDA/FCF trimmed to reaffirmed.” The prior ranges were $340–$353 million for adjusted EBITDA and $112–$122 million for free cash flow.

surprises.description: Management’s initial estimate for the proposed 2027 Medicare rates was nearly neutral for RadNet, as RVU increases offset most of the conversion-factor cut; the preview flagged the proposal but did not forecast this offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management's initial analysis of proposed 2027 Medicare rates indicates a net-neutral impact (less than $1 million negative) on roughly $2.4 billion in revenue, as RVU increases offset the 1.68% conversion factor cut.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “any read on the CY2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule proposal” as something to watch, but gave no expected impact.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a proposed 2027 site-neutrality provision that could sharply reduce hospital reimbursement for certain non-contrast studies and said it could accelerate health-system partnership discussions; this policy detail was not in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A proposed 2027 site-neutrality provision would cut hospital reimbursement 30%–50% on certain non-contrast studies, which management expects to accelerate health system partnership discussions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed reimbursement commentary, including Medicare rates, but did not mention this site-neutrality provision.

surprises.description: Management gave a specific, aggressive deployment trajectory for AI-powered draft reporting, including productivity gains and adoption across a large share of RadNet volumes; the preview noted the breast-ultrasound clearance but did not anticipate this rollout guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “With expanding draft reporting delivering 20%–30% productivity gains, management expects about 15% of RadNet volumes through AI-powered draft reporting by year-end 2026, rising to over 50% by mid-2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the July 30 FDA clearance for DeepHealth Breast Ultrasound and flagged its monetization path, but gave no draft-reporting adoption or productivity targets.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $99.7 million was at the upper end of the preview’s roughly $95–$99 million estimate, consistent with the expected seasonal step-up.
Imaging-center revenue guidance was raised to $2.370–$2.421 billion from $2.355–$2.405 billion, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a modest imaging revenue raise.
Digital Health ARR of $105.5 million was within the preview’s $105–$112 million base-case range, and management remained on track to exceed the already-stated $140 million year-end target.

Digital Health adjusted EBITDA increased sequentially to $2.5 million from $1.3 million in Q1, in line with the preview’s expectation of modest sequential margin improvement; the segment guidance was reaffirmed as expected.

Adjusted EBITDA margin was approximately 16.0% ($99.7 million divided by $622.7 million), roughly 30 basis points below the prior-year 16.3%, within the preview’s expected flat-to-60-basis-point decline.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $117 million, well below the preview’s $134 million estimate, with international sales down 18% rather than showing the anticipated catch-up after Q1’s decline. The international weakness was the main driver of the roughly 10% year-over-year sales drop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales fell approximately 10% year-over-year to $117 million from $129 million, driven primarily by an 18% decline in international sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales … My estimate: $134M”; international: “If the ‘timing’ explanation was correct, Q2 should show catch-up.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $6.6 million, far below the preview’s $11.5–12.5 million estimate; it fell 40% year over year instead of coming in around or above the prior-year $11 million. First-half adjusted EBITDA was also $17 million, short of the preview’s roughly $22 million expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA dropped 40% to $6.6 million from $11 million a year earlier”; “First-half 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose more than 20% to $17 million from $14 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … My estimate: $11.5–12.5M (vs. $11M LY)”; “H1 FY26 adj. EBITDA will land near $22M.”

surprises.description: Cash and net debt moved the wrong way for a quarter the preview expected to be a source of cash: cash fell to $43.9 million and net debt increased to $224.7 million. The preview had flagged a cash balance materially below about $60 million as a concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt increased sequentially to $224.7 million from $194.7 million, while cash fell to $43.9 million from $70.9 million at the end of Q1 due to peak seasonal working capital needs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is a US-crop collection quarter and should be a source of cash”; “A Q2 cash balance materially below ~$60M … would raise real covenant-headroom questions.”

surprises.description: U.S. crop sales fell 9%, rather than continuing the growth the preview’s base case expected, although management attributed much of the decline to cotton portfolio sales shifting into Q3. U.S. specialty growth of 11% partly offset the crop decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. specialty business grew 11% in the quarter and 10% in the first half, offsetting a 9% decline in U.S. crop sales driven largely by cotton portfolio sales shifting into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “US Crop was +17% to $67.0M in Q1”; the base scenario expected “US Crop growth moderates from +17%.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a longer-term growth roadmap that the preview did not anticipate: more than $600 million of annualized run-rate revenue by the second half of 2028, alongside a goal of 50 product launches generating $100 million in annualized revenue by 2030. R&D and regulatory spending was already up 12% to support that pipeline, making the announcement promising but also involving higher investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company set a longer-term target of exceeding $600 million in annualized run-rate revenue by the second half of 2028, roughly 20% above 2025 levels, with double-digit EBITDA margins”; “R&D and regulatory spending rose 12% year-over-year to support a goal of 50 new product launches over five years generating $100 million in annualized revenue by 2030.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of $44–48 million adjusted EBITDA on sales of $530–550 million, as the preview expected.

The LA plant rationalization and headquarters relocation are expected to save at least $4 million annually, consistent with the preview’s expectation that $4 million-plus of annualized savings would be on track.

surprises.description: Sonida’s same-store community NOI grew 16.9% and its NOI margin reached 32.6%, 10 basis points above the preview’s 31.5–32.5% range; growth also accelerated from 14% in Q1. Labor costs fell 130 basis points to a portfolio-low 40.4% of revenue, stronger than the preview’s expectation of a stable cost profile.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store community NOI grew 16.9% year-over-year with NOI margin expanding 250 bps to 32.6%, accelerating from 14% NOI growth in Q1”; “labor costs fell 130 bps to a portfolio-low 40.4% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected same-store NOI margin of “31.5–32.5%” and said “outsized rate increases plus a stable cost profile” would drive margin gains.

surprises.description: The six communities transitioned to Sonida in early May posted NOI improvement exceeding 60% and 850 basis points of margin expansion. The preview looked for early margin lift on these communities but did not anticipate an improvement of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Six communities transitioned to Sonida management in early May delivered year-over-year NOI improvement exceeding 60% and 850 bps of NOI margin expansion versus Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch completion count and any early margin lift on the first six” as proof of concept, without forecasting the size of the lift.

surprises.description: The preview expected the $170 million bridge loan to be refinanced with property-level mortgage debt. Instead, Sonida completed a $380 million five-year Ally Bank term loan that refinanced the bridge loan and prior debt, with 97% of maturities pushed to 2029 or later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A post-quarter $380 million five-year term loan with Ally Bank refinanced the $170 million bridge loan and prior debt, pushing 97% of total debt maturities to 2029 or later.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to refinancing the bridge “with property-level mortgage debt” by the end of Q2 or early Q3.

surprises.description: The 2025 acquisition cohort’s NOI margin recovered from negative 1% in Q4 2025 to 15% this quarter, while occupancy remained just 70.4%. The preview highlighted acquired-portfolio operating performance as a key debate but did not forecast this sharp margin recovery or the remaining occupancy gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2025 acquisition cohort saw NOI margin swing from -1% in Q4 2025 to 15% this quarter, with occupancy still at 70.4% (up 1,400 bps in occupancy since Q4).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for a “first clean look” at the acquired communities’ operations and highlighted the gap between total SHOP occupancy and same-store occupancy, but gave no expectation for this cohort’s margin or occupancy.

surprises.description: Sonida had approximately $88 million of assets under contract with projected mid-teens unlevered IRRs and expected accretion to normalized FFO and NAV per share once stabilized. The preview did not flag a specific acquisition pipeline transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is under contract to acquire approximately $88 million of assets expected to generate mid-teens unlevered IRR and be accretive to normalized FFO and NAV per share on a stabilized basis.”

surprises.description: Sonida issued approximately 672,000 ATM shares in July to fund near-term acquisitions. The preview identified equity funding as a potential bear-case signal, but did not expect a specific share issuance in the reported facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company issued approximately 672,000 shares via its ATM program in July at an average price of $41.05 for net proceeds of $27.3 million to fund near-term acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “a first-time reference to equity as a funding source” as a bear-case signal.

surprises.description: Management did not provide full-year 2027 normalized FFO guidance now; it said guidance would begin after CHP and pipeline integrations are complete. The preview viewed a guidance framework initiated this quarter as a possible positive surprise, so the timing is later and more conditional than that upside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to begin issuing full-year normalized FFO guidance for 2027, deferring guidance until CHP and pipeline integrations are complete.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that “initiating” a guidance framework would be a “genuine narrative shift” and a possible underpriced positive surprise.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $50 million versus the preview’s approximately $47 million estimate. The reported figure is stated on a total-portfolio basis, whereas the preview labeled its estimate at-share, which limits the comparability of the apparent beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $50 million on a total portfolio basis for Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA (at-share)” at “~$47M.”

in_line: Same-store occupancy was 87.8%, within the preview’s 87.6–88.0% estimate range.
Same-store RevPOR growth of 4.9% was within the preview’s +4.5–5.5% expectation.
The near-term leverage target of 6.0x–6.5x was consistent with the preview’s expectation of a mid-6x target.

surprises.description: Revenue was $8.2 million, above the preview’s expectation of results near the $7.5–$7.8 million guided range. That is a clear upside beat against the company’s guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $8.2 million” and was “above the guided range of $7.5 to $7.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue will almost certainly land in or near the $7.5–7.8M guided range.”

surprises.description: Consumables growth and flow-cell sales were stronger than the preview’s already-positive operating expectations: consumables grew 30% rather than roughly 20%, and flow-cell sales exceeded the 9,000-unit watch level. The result reflects faster utilization growth than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumable revenue grew 30% year-over-year to $4.3 million”; “Flow cells sold hit a record 9,219 units, up 27% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for >9,000 flow cells and continued 20%-ish consumables growth”; the catalyst checklist also specifies “Consumables growth ≥18% and flow cells ≥9,000.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 53%, well above the preview’s roughly 49% base-case expectation. That is a substantial improvement on the anticipated margin level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin reached a record 53% in Q2 2026,” compared with 52% a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “GM ~49%.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of full-year revenue guidance to $31 million from $30 million, rather than narrowing toward the preview’s base-case range of about $30–$31 million. The $33 million top end was retained rather than cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance had its low end raised to $31-$33 million (9%-16% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called narrowing to “~$30–31M” the base case and said the $33 million high end was “not credible on current trajectory.”

surprises.description: Demand is exceeding manufacturing capacity, leaving a flow-cell backlog expected to take until mid-to-late Q4 to clear. The preview anticipated strong flow-cell demand but did not anticipate that production limits would constrain fulfillment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Demand continues to outpace manufacturing capacity, creating a backlog expected to clear by mid-to-late Q4 2026”; the full-year top end was held back due to capacity constraints.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview looked for “>9,000 flow cells” and described utilization as compounding, but did not flag manufacturing capacity or a backlog.

surprises.description: Despite the Q2 revenue beat, Q3 guidance implies only flat-to-modest sequential growth, with management citing large orders that could slip between quarters. The preview did not provide a Q3 expectation, but this is a cautious near-term outlook alongside the stronger Q2 result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $8.2-$8.6 million” implies “roughly flat-to-modest sequential growth,” reflecting “conservatism around large orders at risk of slipping quarters.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash and securities were slightly above the preview’s $8–$10 million estimate, and the company said runway extends into at least Q1 2027. This is somewhat better than the cash estimate, though it does not remove the financing concern: the company still signaled potential future financing needs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with only $10.4 million in cash and securities, with runway extending into at least Q1 2027, signaling potential future financing needs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$8–10M exiting Q2” and described management’s prior runway claim as “into 2027,” while warning of “well under two quarters of runway.”

in_line: The full retirement of the senior secured convertible debt was already known before the release: the preview said the company had retired the debentures in full on May 26.

The preview expected continued utilization-led growth even as instrument placements stayed soft; the reported 5% growth in the installed base alongside deeper use by existing clinical customers is consistent with that outlook.

surprises.description: CRC’s operating update pointed to only about 1% gross entry-to-exit production growth, rather than the preview’s roughly 175,000 BOE/day exit target. The full-year average guide is approximately 153,000 BOE/day, but the reported growth outlook signals a much flatter production trajectory than the preview had highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year guidance is approximately 153,000 BOE/day and roughly 1% gross entry-to-exit production growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~175 MBoe/d exit target.”

surprises.description: CRC cut the expected H2 California rig count to five while keeping production nearly flat, reducing 2026 D&C and workover capital by $10 million. That is a sharper move toward lower spending than the preview’s 7-rig peak plan and its expectation that the H2 program might be defended.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Improved drilling efficiency cut time-to-market by ~25%, allowing California operations to run 5 rigs in H2 2026 instead of 6 while keeping production nearly flat, reducing 2026 D&C and workover capital by $10 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The May raise added $100M and 3 rigs (2 California, 1 Uinta) to reach a 7-rig peak”; “Whether CRC defends or trims this program at $85 Brent”; base case: “H2 rig program defended on efficiency gains.”

surprises.description: CRC also lowered its normalized California maintenance requirement to six rigs—one fewer than previously projected—and cut the associated D&C and workover capital estimate by about 5%, with a $450–475 million go-forward range. This adds a lasting capital-efficiency improvement beyond the near-term H2 rig reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Normalized California maintenance now requires 6 rigs (one fewer than previously projected) and ~5% lower D&C and workover capital, with go-forward maintenance capital range of $450-475 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY capex $520–560M”; the preview also noted the earlier plan had “<$400M of D&C/workover capital” as a contrast to the expanded rig program.

surprises.description: Berry integration savings were further along and larger than the preview’s estimates: CRC said it had exceeded the 2026 target six months early, with about $103 million of annualized savings, and raised cumulative synergies and structural cost reductions through 2028 to as much as $470 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Berry integration synergies were delivered at over 100% of the 2026 target six months ahead of schedule,” representing “~$103 million of annualized savings”; cumulative synergies and structural cost reductions were raised “to up to $470 million through 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Berry synergies at $90–100M annually, >80% of original target captured, ~$460M cumulative through 2028.”

surprises.description: A temporary pipeline-operator dispute and takeaway constraints created unexpected operating headwinds. CRC said the takeaway constraints reduced Q2 EBITDAX and operating cash flow by about $25 million each, while the marketing dispute pressured differentials; CRC limited the differential impact to roughly $2/barrel and expects Q3 realizations of about 93% of Brent before recovering to its 94% full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Temporary takeaway constraints reduced EBITDAX and operating cash flow by approximately $25 million each”; marketing disputes pressured differentials, but CRC “limited its impact to roughly $2/barrel,” guided Q3 realizations to “~93% of Brent” as the year’s low point, and maintained full-year realizations of “~94%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch 2027 exposure” and “Realized oil price with hedges,” but did not flag a pipeline dispute or takeaway constraint.

surprises.description: CRC reported substantially better-than-expected well results: about 80% of wells drilled year to date beat the type curve, with average initial production more than 10% above expectations. The company also put new California production costs at roughly $2,000–7,000 per flowing barrel, far below the $28,000–30,000 paid in the Era and Berry acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 80% of wells drilled year-to-date outperformed the type curve with average initial production more than 10% above expectations,” and California drilling delivers new production at “roughly $2,000-7,000 per flowing barrel versus $28,000-30,000 paid in the Era and Berry acquisitions.”

surprises.description: CRC announced an all-cash purchase of Crimson’s approximately 2,000-mile California crude pipeline network at about 4.4 times estimated 2027 EBITDA, which it described as below prevailing midstream multiples. The preview did not anticipate this acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced an all-cash acquisition of Crimson's ~2,000-mile California crude pipeline network at approximately 4.4x estimated 2027 EBITDA, below prevailing midstream valuation multiples,” with tentative PUC approval received.

surprises.description: CRC completed no share repurchases in the quarter, despite the preview identifying accelerated buybacks as a potential signal of conviction and noting that the prior quarter’s $10 million repurchase was small. The preview did not make a buyback an unconditional base-case expectation, so the gap is limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Executed no share repurchases this quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 FCF was −$32M … with only $10M of repurchases”; “the cheapest bullish surprise available to management … [is] an accelerated buyback”; “Buyback pace — $10M in Q1 was negligible.”

surprises.description: Management described the Uinta as a non-core asset unlikely to receive long-term capital, a firmer capital-allocation stance than the preview’s description of the asset as still under evaluation with development and monetization both live options.
surprises.fact_evidence: CRC “viewed the Uinta as a non-core asset unlikely to receive long-term capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Uinta remains ‘evaluation stage’ — 4 wells by year-end, with full development or monetization both live.”

surprises.description: CRC said its Elk Hills CCS project had begun capturing about 270 tonnes per day and had recorded first revenue. The preview noted that injection had already occurred but identified first revenue recognition as something still to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CRC commenced CO2 injection and achieved first revenue at California's first CCS project at Elk Hills, capturing ~270 tonnes/day (targeting ~100,000 tons/year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “First CO₂ injection at CTV I / Elk Hills achieved (May–June 2026)”; “Watch: 45Q monetization mechanics, first revenue recognition.”

surprises.description: CRC refinanced its remaining 2029 notes with debt due in 2035, extending weighted-average maturities and lowering annual interest expense. The preview did not flag a refinancing as an expected event.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refinanced its remaining 2029 senior notes with notes due 2035, extending weighted average debt maturity from 5.5 to 8 years and cutting annual expense by $5.5 million.”

in_line: Q2 net production averaged 149,000 BOE/day, within the preview’s cited 148,000–150,000 BOE/day company guide.
Q2 adjusted EBITDAX was $338 million: below the company’s $370–410 million guide, but within the preview’s $335–360 million base-case estimate, which anticipated a result modestly below the guide.

The Golden Valley data-center hub remained at an early development stage. The preview identified hard lease or PPA economics as the potential catalyst; the call reported co-developer funding for early-stage development, not lease or PPA terms.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $28.1 million, about 3% above the $27.29 million consensus, and growth accelerated to 33%. That was a modest beat against consensus, though it was within the preview’s $27.8–28.2 million buy-side whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $28.1 million, up 33% year-over-year, accelerating from 29% growth in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $27.29M”; “Revenue vs. $27.29M consensus / ~$27.8–28.2M buy-side whisper.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 92%, above the preview’s high-80s expectation. Even excluding the $1.6 million tariff refund, the 89% margin was at or slightly above the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin hit a record 92%, or 89% excluding a $1.6 million tariff refund.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~87–88% (guided ‘high-80s’)”; “guided high-80s all year.”

surprises.description: The company raised its 2026 revenue range to $114–117 million, but the increase was smaller than the preview’s more bullish buy-side bar of roughly $115–118 million and its expectation for a roughly $3 million raise. The new range matched the preview’s base case, so the shortfall is against the higher bar rather than its central scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $114-$117 million … from prior guidance of $112-$116 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side bar is a raise to roughly $115–118M”; “anything less than a ~$3M raise reads as H2 caution.” The preview’s base case was “guide to $114–117M.”

surprises.description: The delirium commercial launch was brought forward to Q4 2026, rather than remaining as late as early 2027 under prior guidance. The preview focused on launch detail and potential 2027 economics but did not flag this timing pull-forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Delirium will launch commercially in Q4 2026, pulled forward from prior guidance of Q4 2026/early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “pulled forward from prior guidance of Q4 2026/early 2027.”

surprises.description: The GAAP loss per share was $0.51, four cents worse than the $0.47 loss consensus. This was at the lossier end of the preview’s base-case range, while adjusted EBITDA was better than its stated threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $19.3 million ($0.51 per share) from $13.6 million ($0.38 per share) a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP net loss/sh) | ($0.47).”

surprises.description: Management said account growth relied less on VA accounts than in prior quarters, suggesting sales-force maturation beyond simply meeting the expected account-add count. The preview anticipated strong adds but did not identify this change in account mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added 32 active accounts to reach 712 total, with growth relying less on VA accounts than in prior quarters, indicating organic sales force maturation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net new accounts ≥30”; the preview described whether Q1’s adds reflected “a step-function in sales-force productivity.”

surprises.description: The refinancing adds access to up to $60 million of committed capital, lowers interest expense beginning in Q4, and extends repayment into 2031. The preview raised cash-burn and financing concerns but did not anticipate this facility refinancing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company held $129.3 million in cash and marketable securities and refinanced its credit facility to access up to $60 million committed capital, reducing interest expense starting Q4 and extending repayment into 2031.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any wobble on that commitment reopens the financing question”; the preview cited “cash and marketable securities $141.2M, net cash ~$119M.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted that less than 4% of the core seizure market is penetrated and that top accounts use the product at roughly three times the rate of similarly sized average accounts. This offered a specific adoption and utilization runway that the preview had not quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cited less than 4% penetration in its core seizure market, with top accounts using the product at roughly three times the rate of average accounts of similar size.”

in_line: The 32 net account adds and 712 total active accounts were within the preview’s estimate of roughly 708–712 accounts and its expectation of 28–32 adds.
Adjusted EBITDA loss of $9.8 million was within the preview’s expected threshold of $11 million or less.
The CMS NTAP payment, its up-to-$2,171 amount, and its October 1, 2026 effective date were already disclosed and highlighted in the preview.
The two seizure-algorithm clearances were already anticipated: the preview noted the FDA clearance for epileptiform abnormality detection and artifact reduction.

surprises.description: Total revenue was $243.7 million, well above the preview’s $218.7–$222.2 million consensus range and its $232 million estimate. That is roughly a 10% beat versus the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues were $243.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $218.7M – $222.2M (commonly cited $220.9M)” and “My Est.: $232M.”

surprises.description: Attruby revenue reached $222.4 million, above the preview’s $214 million estimate, and increased $41.8 million sequentially. The preview expected about a $35 million sequential addition, with consensus implying only about $25 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Attruby net product revenue reached $222.4 million in Q2” and marked “another quarter with a sequential increase of at least $35 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied Attruby US net … ~$205M (+13% q/q)” and “My Est.: $214M (+18% q/q)”; the preview also said “Holding [the sequential dollar add] flat gets you to ~$214M” and consensus implied “~+$25M q/q.”

surprises.description: The market commentary was stronger than the preview’s category-deceleration concern: the ATTR market grew 19% in the quarter and 51% year over year, while Attruby was the fastest-growing brand and gained an estimated 2–3 percentage points of first-line share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Attruby was the fastest-growing brand in the ATTR space at 23%, with overall market growth of 19% in the quarter (up 51% year-over-year) and first-line share gains estimated at 2-3 percentage points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the “bear read” that “the whole category is decelerating” and said “BBIO’s category commentary is the arbiter.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was only $72.2 million, far below the preview’s expected $780–$850 million. The July 1 preferred investment raised cash to about $1.7 billion, but that was also below the preview’s roughly $1.8 billion pro forma expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The preferred investment “closed … on July 1, lifting cash to approximately $1.7 billion, up from just $72.2 million at quarter end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect reported Q2 cash of roughly $780–850M with ~$1.8B pro forma.”

surprises.description: New kidney-protection data turned a previously perceived acoramidis drawback into a potential advantage: among patients with acute eGFR dips at or above the median, outcomes favored acoramidis with a hazard ratio of 0.42.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In patients with acute eGFR dips at or above the median, acoramidis favored survival/CV-hospitalization outcomes with a hazard ratio of 0.42 (p=0.006), reframing a previously perceived drawback as a differentiator.”

surprises.description: New real-world evidence reported substantially better outcomes for Attruby than tafamidis, including fewer diuretic intensifications, heart-failure hospitalizations, and deaths, with differences appearing early.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New real-world evidence associated Attruby with a 34% reduction in diuretic intensification, heart failure hospitalization and mortality versus tafamidis, with separation observed as early as 30 days.”

surprises.description: Management gave a substantial portfolio revenue outlook not specified in the preview, projecting more than $10 billion in risk-adjusted revenue and saying acoramidis should reach worldwide blockbuster status in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management projected the portfolio supports over $10 billion in risk-adjusted revenue ($8 billion post-Phase III), [and] guided to acoramidis reaching worldwide blockbuster status in 2026.”

surprises.description: Management described chronic hypoparathyroidism as a potential additional blockbuster opportunity for encaleret, adding commercial upside beyond the preview’s focus on the ADH1 regulatory timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management framed encaleret’s chronic hypoparathyroidism opportunity as “a potential additional blockbuster,” citing “~200,000 patients in U.S. and EU.”

surprises.description: Management supplied a path to breakeven by late 2027, after several quarters of stable operating results. The preview highlighted rising launch spending and asked whether management would outline operating leverage, but did not give a breakeven timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects stable operating results for several quarters before trending toward breakeven by late 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “whether management frames any path to operating leverage” and described a base case of “EPS miss on launch spend.”

in_line: Gross-to-net stayed within the 30%–40% range, consistent with the preview’s concern about possible softening in gross-to-net.

The expected regulatory cadence was broadly confirmed: the preview already cited the encaleret PDUFA of May 8, 2027 and expected infigratinib’s NDA to be on track for Q3 2026; the call reported the NDAs submitted and encaleret’s Phase III trial screening underway.

The competing cardio transform trial’s failure was already known before the call; management’s view that this reinforces stabilizers as first-line treatment aligned with the preview’s focus on the post-failure positioning debate.

surprises.description: Revenue was well above both the $44.64 million consensus and the preview’s roughly $44 million base estimate. The $48.4 million result also represented 25% growth on a continuing-business basis, above the preview’s roughly 19% implied growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $48.4 million” and was “up 25% year-over-year on an aggregate continuing business basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$44.64M”; the preview’s base estimate was “~$44.0M” and said it implied “~+19% YoY on continuing operations.”

surprises.description: Commerce Media Solutions revenue exceeded the preview’s estimate, reaching $30.5 million rather than the modeled $28.5 million. Its 90% growth was also above the preview’s modeled 75–85% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commerce Media Solutions revenue grew 90% year-over-year to $30.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled CMS at “$28.5M” and “~+77% YoY,” with its key-metrics section giving a “~+75–85% YoY” model.

surprises.description: CMS exited the quarter above the preview’s $120 million run-rate bogey, with an annual revenue run rate exceeding $125 million. That was stronger than the preview’s base-case $115–120 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commerce Media Solutions exited Q2 with an annual revenue run rate of over $125 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected a “run rate $115–120M”; its ranked metric said “>$120M = thesis intact.”

surprises.description: Owned and operated revenue held up substantially better than the preview modeled: $16.3 million versus an estimate of $12.5 million. Its 24% decline was also much less severe than the historical decline rates highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owned and operated revenue declined 24% year-over-year to $16.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s estimate build modeled Owned & Operated at “$12.5M”; its key-metrics section cited recent declines of “-49% (Q2'25) → -50% (Q1'26).”

surprises.description: Profitability and monetization metrics improved more strongly than the preview’s margin discussion suggested. Gross profit rose 36% and reached 28.9% of revenue, while CMS media margin expanded to 34% from 20%; the preview had expected improving CMS margins but identified 21–23% as its Q2 estimate. The reported media-margin and CMS gross-margin measures are not identical.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit rose 36% year-over-year to $14 million (28.9% of revenue), a 650 basis point improvement from Q1 2026”; CMS “media margin expanded to 34% from 20% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “CMS gross margin” at “21–23%” and said “≥22% = credible.”

surprises.description: Fluent reported a major CVS partner launch in Q3, adding a large retail pharmacy chain and a path toward in-store expansion in 2027. The preview flagged the existing in-store proof of concept but did not anticipate this specific large pharmacy partner win.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CVS, one of the largest retail pharmacy chains, went live in Q3 as one of Fluent's largest partner wins,” expanding Fluent into pharmacy, with “a roadmap for in-store expansion in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Fluent In-Store/Bilt/Beyond proof of concept and said “Any signed conversion, second retailer, or revenue timeline” would extend the narrative.

surprises.description: The Beyond-linked in-store offering is not expected to contribute meaningful revenue in 2026, with material impact anticipated in 2027. That limits the near-term financial contribution from a proof of concept the preview identified as a possible source of upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: The new in-store offering “is not expected to contribute meaningful revenue in 2026, with material impact anticipated in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the proof of concept was “slated mid-July–August 2026” and that a “revenue timeline” would be an upside narrative extension.

surprises.description: Cash fell to $6.9 million, below the $10.3 million cash balance cited for Q1 in the preview, even as debt was reduced. First-half operating cash flow was only about $0.3 million, so cash generation did not provide much cushion after the preview highlighted the Q1 cash-flow boost as partly one-time.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and equivalents fell to $6.9 million” and “operating cash flow was approximately $300,000 in the first half”; short-term debt was reduced to “$26.8 million from $30.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Cash $10.3M” and “OCF +$5.1M in Q1,” while noting that the Q1 cash-flow increase was “partly AR liquidation” and advising investors to watch whether OCF held up.

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year guidance for double-digit consolidated revenue growth on aggregate continuing businesses and improved adjusted EBITDA, matching the preview’s base case that guidance would be reaffirmed.
The adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $1.8 million from $2.8 million a year earlier, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of improvement and its estimate of roughly a $2.0 million loss.
The preview expected continued high CMS growth and improving margins; those broad trends occurred, although CMS revenue and the reported margin developments were stronger than its estimates.

surprises.description: The preview modeled quarterly operating cash use of about $18–20 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $17–19 million. Management reported about $16 million of operating cash use and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $16.3 million, both better than modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash used in operations was approximately $16 million in Q2,” and adjusted EBITDA improved to “negative $16.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “adjusted EBITDA loss $17–19M” and cash at June 30 of “$43–47M (from $63.2M, less ~$18–20M operating use).”

surprises.description: The preview expected the company to have enough cash to reach the pivotal readout, but management said $47.1 million would fund operations beyond pivotal data and through a potential de novo submission, with no raise planned before pivotal data. That is stronger runway and financing reassurance than the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with “$47.1 million in cash,” funding operations “beyond pivotal data and through a potential de novo submission,” with “no planned raise before pivotal data.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “cash at 6/30/26 of $43–47M” and described the base case as runway “into early 2027” repeated, “no financing detail.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated R&D expense of $14–16 million; reported R&D was slightly below that range, at $13.8 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 R&D expenses fell to $13.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimates: R&D $14–16M.”

surprises.description: The preview implied a net loss of about $24 million, while the reported loss was $25.5 million. The shortfall was modest, though the preview cautioned that earnings were affected by warrant marks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowing to $25.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss: ~($24M) implied.”

surprises.description: The preview discussed durable weight-loss maintenance but did not anticipate that no patients in the midpoint cohort would restart GLP-1 therapy. That adds a favorable treatment-persistence detail to the reported durability result.
surprises.fact_evidence: Patients maintained “more than 80% of their prior GLP-1-induced weight loss at one year versus 46% in the sham arm, with no patients reinitiating GLP-1 therapy in the midpoint cohort.”

surprises.description: The preview cited responder rates and the FDA threshold but did not state an expectation for statistical power. Management’s estimate that both pivotal co-primary endpoints are powered above 95% is an additional favorable indication of the study’s anticipated ability to meet its endpoints.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company estimates both co-primary pivotal endpoints are powered above 95%,” with a midpoint responder rate of 73% in MITT and above 90% in complete-ablation patients versus the FDA’s 50% threshold.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a CMS transitional pass-through payment expectation. Management now expects Revita to qualify, potentially enabling reimbursement from launch through a targeted center-of-excellence model.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects Revita to “qualify for CMS transitional pass-through payment as a breakthrough device,” enabling “reimbursement from day one of launch” through a targeted center-of-excellence model.

in_line: The preview highlighted the one-year durability data; the reported Reveal One maintenance of approximately 78% of prior weight loss and the midpoint-cohort retention result were broadly consistent with that expectation.
The preview noted no device- or procedure-related serious adverse events in the earlier clinical data; the call again reported zero such serious adverse events over a full year.

The preview expected REMAIN-1 Pivotal to be fully randomized since February and flagged early-Q4 six-month topline data and late-Q4 De Novo timing. The call reported randomization completed in February and reaffirmed those catalyst windows.

surprises.description: GCT reported just $1.0 million of Q2 revenue, far below the preview’s $3.30 million consensus and its $2.6–$3.3 million base-case range. Service revenue fell by $0.2 million, and management said delayed customer deployments caused revenue to fall meaningfully short of internal expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenues declined 18% year-over-year to $1 million (from $1.2 million), driven by a $0.2 million drop in service revenues”; delayed deployments were “causing revenue to fall meaningfully short of internal expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 revenue | Consensus | $3.30M”; the base scenario expected “Revenue | $2.6–3.3M.”

surprises.description: Several key customer deployments moved back by one to two quarters, weakening the expected near-term ramp and helping explain the revenue shortfall. The preview emphasized H2 shipments and warned that rollout delays would undermine the ramp, although management said demand and engagement were unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Several key customer deployments slipped by one to two quarters due to corporate restructuring and evolving deployment schedules”; management said “demand and engagement are unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said satellite initial shipments were guided to “begin H2 2026,” and that any timing slip or hedging about rollout plans would be a concern.

surprises.description: Gross margin turned negative instead of tracking toward the preview’s expected mid-30s initial product margin and high-30s/low-40s blended range. Costs rose even as shipment volume increased, while management said margins should improve as 5G sales scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin turned negative in Q2 2026 versus 32% a year earlier,” as “cost of revenues rose 49% to $1.2 million on higher unit volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided product gross margin to “35% initially, growing into the low 40s,” with blended margin “high-30s/low-40s.”

surprises.description: The $20.4 million net loss was materially worse than the preview’s realistic EPS-loss band implied, but much of the gap came from a $12.3 million non-cash warrant-liability revaluation. Adjusted EBITDA loss was essentially flat year over year at $6.6 million, indicating that the headline loss worsened far more than this supplemental measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened by $8.1 million year-over-year to $20.4 million,” including “$12.3 million in non-cash losses from fair value changes in common stock warrant liabilities”; adjusted EBITDA loss was “essentially flat year-over-year at $6.6 million (versus $6.7 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Treat −$0.12 to −$0.18 as the realistic band” for EPS.

surprises.description: GCT raised the maximum gross proceeds allowed under its ATM program from $75 million to $120 million, expanding potential future equity issuance beyond the program referenced in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GCT amended its ATM equity program to raise maximum gross proceeds from $75 million to $120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to the “$75M ATM” and described ATM issuance as “persistent overhead supply.”
