surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $60 million, exceeding the preview’s expected $35–55 million range. The result was above even the top of the company’s prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $60 million (8% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 adj. EBITDA vs. $35–55M guide”; the preview also estimated “~$45M (guide midpoint).”

surprises.description: The company raised FY26 revenue guidance to $3.1–3.3 billion from $2.8–3.0 billion. The new midpoint is about 10% higher than the previous midpoint, a material upward revision.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $3.1-$3.3 billion (32-41% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management nonetheless raised FY26 revenue guidance to $2.8–3.0B”; the preview described the key debate as whether the EBITDA guidance would be “reaffirm[ed], narrow[ed], or cut.”

surprises.description: Hims added 300,000 net subscribers and reached nearly 3 million, above the preview’s implied Q2 range of roughly 2.65–2.75 million. The reported total is also well ahead of the preview’s base-case expectation of about 2.70 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company [added] 300,000 net new subscribers to reach nearly 3 million total.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscribers: ~2.65–2.75M (implied)”; the base case expected “subs ~2.70M.”

surprises.description: The company issued Q3 guidance of $880–900 million in revenue and $75–95 million in adjusted EBITDA. The preview focused on Q2 and the FY26 back-half bridge and gave no Q3 estimate, so this outlook was not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Guided] Q3 revenue to $880-$900 million (47-50% growth) with adjusted EBITDA of $75-$95 million.”

surprises.description: The preview expected GAAP results to be substantially worse than adjusted EPS because of amortization and integration costs, and flagged a possible FTC accrual. The reported $86 million GAAP loss included approximately $81 million of nonrecurring costs, quantifying a substantial one-quarter burden across the Eucalyptus acquisition, restructuring, and FTC legal accruals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $86 million, impacted by approximately $81 million of nonrecurring costs including Eucalyptus acquisition, restructuring, and FTC legal accruals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP will be well below [the adjusted EPS estimate] given amortization and integration costs”; the preview also called for watching “any accrual, reserve” related to the FTC.

surprises.description: Management said the FTC case would be defended vigorously rather than settling on terms it disagreed with. The preview highlighted the case and asked about management’s posture, but the call made its stance explicit after settlement negotiations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FTC filed a complaint against the company on July 29 after settlement negotiations, and management stated it intends to defend the case vigorously rather than accept terms it disagreed with.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FTC litigation — quantification and operational impact” as a key metric to watch and also flagged “consent-decree posture.”

surprises.description: International revenue reached $131 million, with Eucalyptus contributing about $40 million and the U.K., Australia, and Germany each exceeding $100 million in annualized revenue. The preview expected an Eucalyptus contribution disclosure but did not anticipate these reported scale figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International revenue grew over 17-fold year-over-year to $131 million, with the newly acquired Eucalyptus contributing approximately $40 million and the U.K., Australia, and Germany each already exceeding $100 million in annualized revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “disclosure that separates organic from acquired growth” and described this as the “first quarter with the asset (~one month).”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow and free cash flow turned negative, with management attributing the outflow to working-capital needs in branded weight loss. The preview supplied no expectation for a Q2 cash outflow; management expects free cash flow to resume in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow turned negative $36 million and free cash flow was negative $68 million in the quarter due to working capital demands from branded weight loss, though the company expects to resume free cash flow generation in the second half.”

surprises.description: The company added a $400 million receivables facility and raised more than $400 million through convertible debt, ending with more than $840 million in cash and short-term investments despite the Eucalyptus upfront payment. The preview did not flag these financing actions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company shored up its balance sheet with a $400 million receivables facility and a $400 million+ convertible debt offering, ending the quarter with more than $840 million in cash and short-term investments after a $225 million Eucalyptus upfront payment.”

surprises.description: TRT is scaling faster than any specialty outside weight loss and is expected to become the company’s sixth U.S. specialty with a $100 million annual run rate; injectable and oral launches are planned before year-end. The preview did not identify this as an opportunity to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Testosterone/TRT is scaling faster than any specialty outside weight loss and is expected to become the company's sixth U.S. specialty to reach a $100 million annual run rate, with injectable and oral TRT launches planned before year-end.”

surprises.description: Management reported large AI-related workflow changes—33x higher patient-care team messaging engagement and 50% fewer non-clinical support tasks—and expects the investments to pay back within 12–18 months. The preview did not anticipate these operating metrics or the payback estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-native rollouts drove 33x higher patient-care team messaging engagement and a 50% reduction in non-clinical support tasks, with management expecting AI investments to pay back within 12 to 18 months.”

in_line: Gross margin was 64%, within the preview’s expected 62–64% range. Management’s expectation that margins remain structurally lower with the branded weight-loss and international mix shift was consistent with the preview’s expectation of further compression from the branded pivot.
Management reaffirmed the 2030 targets of $6.5 billion in revenue and $1.3 billion in adjusted EBITDA, as the preview specifically flagged reiteration of those targets as an important check.

surprises.description: Hallador’s results were materially weaker than the preview’s base case of $7–13 million in adjusted EBITDA: adjusted EBITDA was negative $2.9 million, alongside a $15.2 million net loss and negative $23.9 million of operating cash flow. The preview expected a loss, but this was a much deeper shortfall, with management attributing it to outage-related downtime and high purchase-power costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss of $15.2 million”; “Adjusted EBITDA turned negative at -$2.9 million”; “operating cash flow swung to -$23.9 million”; driven by “outage-related downtime and high purchase power costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%)” scenario: “Adj. EBITDA $7–13M”; Q2 EPS consensus “–$0.10.”

surprises.description: Despite the expected post-outage improvement in Merom availability, the quarter still suffered from outage-related downtime, and average delivered energy price fell substantially even as energy sales volume increased. That combination suggests the recovery did not translate into stronger realized energy economics in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “outage-related downtime and high purchase power costs”; average delivered energy price “fell to $41.69/MWh from $52.66/MWh despite a 17% increase in energy sales volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Q2 “the proof point” for Merom’s return with “higher availability” and highlighted realized energy price and hedge position, noting management had called itself “well hedged for 2026.”

surprises.description: The Turtle Creek gas project’s estimated cost moved below $800 million from below $900 million last quarter, and commercial operations were pulled forward to the second half of 2028. The preview focused on the roughly $450 million turbine-related commitment and September FID, but did not anticipate a lower total-cost estimate or an accelerated operating schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “estimated total cost has been lowered to below $800 million (roughly $1,700/KW), down from below $900 million last quarter, with commercial operations pulled forward to the second half of 2028.”

surprises.description: Management said it aims to fund Turtle Creek with little to no equity dilution, using equipment financing and structured or traditional debt. That is reassuring against the preview’s concern that equity could be part of the funding stack, although the financing plan is described as an aim rather than completed financing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management aims to finance Turtle Creek with little to no equity dilution using equipment financing and structured/traditional debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified financing framed as “project debt/partner-funded” as the most bullish outcome and warned that management signaling equity in the funding stack would be a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: Hallador’s forward sales book grew to about $2.4 billion, and two 2026 capacity agreements total about $1.1 billion in contracted revenue, including a three-year deal priced at roughly twice historical contracted capacity pricing. The preview already flagged the long-term capacity agreement and a book above $2.1 billion, so the surprise is the additional scale and the disclosed three-year deal rather than the existence of the 12-year contract.
surprises.fact_evidence: “total forward sales book reached approximately $2.4 billion”; “Two landmark capacity agreements signed in 2026 (a 3-year and a 12-year deal) total approximately $1.1 billion in contracted revenue, with the 3-year deal priced at about 2x historical contracted capacity pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a forward book of “>$2.1B” and highlighted the “12-year NIPSCO capacity agreement” at “~2x historical capacity pricing.”

in_line: Energy sales volume rose 17%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Merom availability would improve after the outage, even though outage-related downtime and lower realized prices weakened the overall result.

The preview anticipated substantial project spending ahead, including roughly $450 million of turbine-related spend; Q2 capex rose to $26.3 million from $13.1 million, reflecting Merom reliability upgrades and Turtle Creek development.
The preview expected the 12-year capacity agreement and emphasized its roughly 2x historical pricing; the reported capacity agreements and strong contracted book broadly fit that expectation.

surprises.description: Kopin now expects second-half results to exceed its prior full-year revenue guidance of $52–60 million, a much stronger outlook than the preview’s base case of reiterating guidance and requiring roughly $15–18 million per quarter in H2.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “now anticipates second-half results exceeding prior full-year guidance of $52-60 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the most likely outcome was to “reiterate” guidance and described H2 as implicitly roughly “$16M/qtr.”

surprises.description: Management expects GAAP profitability and positive free cash flow to begin in Q4 2026, whereas the preview described Kopin as a loss-maker and did not anticipate a near-term turn to both measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects to “begin generating GAAP profitability and positive free cash flow in Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear-case description referred to “a loss-maker,” and its scenarios anticipated Q2 EPS between –$0.01 and –$0.04, with breakeven only in the bull case.

surprises.description: Product gross margin was positive at 14%, a sharp improvement from the preview’s concern that product costs had exceeded product revenue in Q1 and might remain above 90% of sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product gross margin improved to 14% (cost of product revenue fell to 86% of sales from 94%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 “cost of product revenue ran 103% of product revenue” and warned that if COGS “still exceeds ~90%,” the ramp story loses earnings leverage.

surprises.description: Q2 reached net income of $0.9 million, or $0.00 per share, versus the preview’s –$0.01 EPS consensus. The improvement was substantially aided by investment gains and a tax benefit, so the reported profit was less operationally strong than the headline suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income of $0.9 million ($0.00 per share)” was aided by “~$2.3 million of investment gains and a $2.1 million income tax benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 FY26 EPS consensus of “–$0.01.”

surprises.description: Sentinel FPV volume orders are now expected to start in late Q4 2026, later than the preview’s expectation of volume production beginning in late August after Drone Dominance Program evaluations and awards.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Volume orders [are] expected to begin in late Q4 2026 and 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management expected volume production to begin “in late August, immediately following DDP Phase 2 evaluations and awards.”

surprises.description: Neural I/O’s disclosed 2027 revenue opportunity is more limited and later-weighted than the preview’s $25–50 million 2027 scaling expectation: management says $20–30 million of development revenue is possible, with production revenue not expected until 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Development revenue of $20-30 million possible in 2027,” with “production revenue not expected until 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “at least $15M” of Neural I/O revenue in 2026, “scaling to $25–50M in 2027,” and flagged the year-end demonstrable-chipset date.

surprises.description: Kopin reported more than $45 million in orders year-to-date and set a $100 million revenue target for 2028, adding concrete order and longer-term growth figures the preview had identified as missing or worth watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has received over $45 million in orders in 2026 year-to-date” and management is “targeting $100 million in revenue for 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors wanted “a dollar backlog figure” and discussed FY2027 revenue consensus, but gave no comparable 2028 target.

surprises.description: Kopin’s color microLED program exceeded the IBAS brightness threshold, reporting more than 150,000 nits of single-panel full-color brightness and a target transition to product manufacturing in mid-2027; the preview flagged program milestones but gave no such achievement or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: The program achieved “over 150,000 nits of single-panel full-color brightness, exceeding the IBAS program threshold,” and “targets transition to product manufacturing in mid-2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Army MicroLED milestones” as existing narrative but did not specify an expected brightness result or manufacturing timeline.

in_line: Q2 revenue was $12.7 million, within the preview’s estimated vendor range of $11.5–13.8 million and its $11–13 million base case.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $3.6 million, well above the preview’s modeled loss of $8 million, even though it remained sharply below the year-ago quarter. This was a substantial positive gap against the preview’s operating estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA” was “$3.6 million in Q2 2026” versus $25.9 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimates: … adj. EBITDA −$8M”; the base scenario also expected “adj. EBITDA ~−$8M.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $87.3 million was close to the preview’s $85 million estimate and within its $78–92 million base range, but it fell well short of the preview’s stated stale consensus of about $103.2 million. A $2.7 million tariff refund recorded as a revenue reduction partly explains the reported figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $87.3 million,” down 4.5% year over year, “partly reduced by a $2.7 million tariff refund issued to a customer and recorded as a revenue reduction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “~$103.2M (likely stale)”; the preview’s own estimate was “$85M,” and it said “a $90M+ print may clear the real bar.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 29.5%, above the preview’s 26% estimate and its 25% watch threshold, despite falling from 34.7% a year earlier. The decline from last year was attributed to higher raw-material prices and lower utilization, but the reported level was better than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross margin fell to 29.5% from 34.7% in Q2 2025,” driven by “higher raw material prices and lower production utilization reducing fixed cost absorption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimates: … adj. gross margin 26%”; the preview said “Below ~25%” would break the resilient-margin thesis and flagged “adjusted gross margin ≥25%” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: The six-month volume total implies roughly 443 MWh in Q2 after Q1’s 274 MWh, above the preview’s expected recovery to roughly 350–400 MWh and its 425 MWh bull-case threshold. That inferred quarterly recovery contrasts with the steep first-half year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Six-month sales volume was “717 MWh,” down 24.3%; subtracting the preview’s Q1 volume of 274 MWh implies approximately 443 MWh for Q2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a recovery toward “~400 MWh” would validate the timing narrative and described “Volumes >425 MWh” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: European sales rose 35% and reached 61% of quarterly revenue, a notable counterpoint to the preview’s concern that demand weakness could extend across EMEA. The preview did not anticipate this regional growth or mix shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “European sales rose 35% in the quarter and now account for 61% of quarterly revenue (up from 43%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that volume below 325 MWh would indicate “structural demand loss in India/Korea/EMEA.”

surprises.description: Liquidity remained under pressure: six-month operating cash flow was negative $33.3 million and cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash fell by $26.2 million to $143.1 million. The preview highlighted liquidity and going-concern risk, but did not give a forecast for this period’s cash burn or ending cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow deteriorated to negative $33.3 million for the six months,” a $77.6 million swing year over year; cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash “fell by $26.2 million,” ending at $143.1 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview ranked “Liquidity and the going-concern language” first and cited Q1 operating cash flow of “−$22.8M,” but gave no Q2 or first-half cash-flow forecast.

in_line: APAC sales weakness was consistent with the preview’s concern about demand loss in India and other markets: quarterly sales fell 23%, and year-to-date sales fell 45% amid a shift toward lower-cost products in India.

Clarksville construction remained contingent on additional financing or strategic partnerships, as the preview explicitly expected; the pack line was reported on schedule for initial output by year-end.
The adjusted net loss was consistent with the preview’s expectation of negative adjusted earnings, although the preview did not provide a comparable adjusted net-income estimate.

surprises.description: OppFi cut its FY26 outlook well below the preview’s stated company guidance: revenue is now $600–625 million versus $650–675 million, and adjusted EPS is $1.34–1.51 versus $1.76–1.84. Management cited delays in the line-of-credit launch and Lola system migration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OppFi cut its full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $600-625 million, adjusted net income of $115-130 million, and adjusted EPS of $1.34-1.51, citing delays in its line of credit launch and Lola system migration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue (co. guide) $650–675M”; “FY26 adj. EPS (co. guide) $1.76–$1.84.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted earnings were materially below the preview’s estimates: adjusted EPS was $0.33 versus $0.42–0.45 expected, while adjusted net income was about $29 million versus the preview’s implied $36–39 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income fell 27% to approximately $29 million and adjusted EPS declined to $0.33 from $0.45.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: Consensus $0.42 – $0.45”; “Adjusted net income (implied) ~$36–39M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue missed the preview’s consensus range: OppFi reported $145 million, versus expected revenue of $155.9–159.0 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue rose only 1.9% year-over-year to $145 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: Consensus $155.9M – $159.0M.”

surprises.description: Credit losses were somewhat worse than the preview’s Q2 estimates: net charge-offs were about 52% of receivables versus an estimated ~50%, and about 40% of revenue versus an estimated ~39%. The preview had identified the sequential charge-off trend as the central debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net charge-offs as a percentage of receivables jumped to approximately 52% from 43%, and as a percentage of revenue rose to about 40% from 32%, though management attributed part of the increase to a denominator effect from slower growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 estimate was “NCO % of revenue … ~39%” and “NCO % avg receivables (ann.) … ~50%.”

surprises.description: Originations came in below the preview’s Q2 estimate: OppFi originated about $212 million versus an estimated ~$225 million, and reported a 9% year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Originations declined approximately 9% year-over-year to $212 million as the company tightened underwriting in segments with less attractive risk-adjusted returns.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net originations … Q2'26E ~$225M.”

surprises.description: The line-of-credit launch was pushed back to September, a two-month delay that the preview did not flag. It will initially serve net-new customers in three new geographies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The line of credit product launch has been pushed to September, effectively a two-month delay, and will initially open three new geographies to net-new customers.”

in_line: The preview expected OppFi to reaffirm a Q4 2026 close target for the BNC transaction and highlighted regulatory progress as a key item to watch. Management still targets a Q4 2026 close and reported that regulatory applications had been submitted to the OCC.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $320.1 million, about 8% below the $348.7 million consensus and below the company’s prior $330–360 million guidance range. The preview expected a trim to full-year guidance but treated the Q2 midpoint as the relevant benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $320.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$348.7M (Investing.com) | $330–360M”

surprises.description: The full-year outlook was cut below the preview’s anticipated range: revenue guidance now starts at $1.28 billion rather than the expected $1.35 billion, and adjusted EPS guidance is $0.70–$0.90 rather than the anticipated $0.80–$1.00. This is a deeper reset than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut full-year revenue guidance to $1.28-$1.35 billion and adjusted EPS to $0.70-$0.90.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base = … FY range trimmed to roughly $1.35–1.42B and adj. EPS to $0.80–1.00”; “A trim of the FY range is the base case; the question is whether the low end holds at $1.35B or breaks below it.”

surprises.description: Despite positive adjusted EPS, reported Q2 EPS was deeply negative because of large non-cash charges; the company also guided to negative reported EPS for the full year, versus the preview’s positive GAAP EPS guidance. These accounting charges were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported EPS was negative $5.14, driven by a $78.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment on the RISE manufacturing unit and a $167.5 million non-cash deferred tax valuation allowance, while adjusted EPS was a positive $0.20”; reported EPS guidance was “negative $4.90 to negative $4.73.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance to be tested: … GAAP EPS $0.70–1.10”; Q2 consensus was “Adj. EPS $0.20.”

surprises.description: Nu Skin delayed India’s formal launch to the first half of 2027, later than the preview’s expected year-end 2026 timing. That pushes out a launch the preview described as central to the recovery narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “India's formal market launch has been delayed to the first half of 2027 to further refine the business model and operational readiness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “India formal launch guided to year-end 2026”; the preview said “Any slip in India timing … removes the 2027 recovery story.”

surprises.description: Prism.io device placements and scans grew strongly during the quarter: placements rose to over 39,000 and scans to 2.5 million. This is positive evidence of product adoption against a preview that treated acceleration in the device and subscription opportunity as a key uncertainty, although the call facts do not report subscription-volume growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prism.io device placements reached over 39,000, up nearly 30% quarter-over-quarter, with 2.5 million scans up 25%, and the company targets 50,000-60,000 devices by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1: ~2M scans, 30,000+ devices, subscription volume +5% YoY”; the preview identified whether “subscription volume [would] accelerate past +5%” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Management disclosed an East-West operating-model transition expected to produce meaningful savings starting in the second half of 2026, but with $5–$10 million of transition costs this year. The preview anticipated possible cost actions, but not this specific plan, timing, or implementation cost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is transitioning to an East-West operating model expected to generate meaningful cost savings starting in the second half of 2026, with $5-$10 million in transition costs anticipated this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether management pulls forward cost actions.”

surprises.description: Foreign exchange was a modest headwind rather than neutral: it reduced Q2 revenue by about $4 million, or roughly 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $320.1 million, including a roughly 1% ($4 million) foreign currency headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FX impact … ~0% (neutral).”

in_line: Adjusted Q2 EPS was $0.20, matching consensus and the midpoint of prior company guidance.

Overall gross-margin pressure remained consistent with the preview’s concern about mix and manufacturing drag: gross margin was 68.2% versus 68.8% a year earlier, while core Nu Skin gross margin improved to 77.7% from 76.9% in Q1, in line with the preview’s view that core margin was holding up.
The dividend was paid, consistent with the preview’s base case that it would be maintained; the reported cash and debt figures do not, by themselves, establish a surprise about covenant headroom.

Management’s statement that recruiting and leadership development remain below the levels needed for sustainable growth reinforces the preview’s concern about the customer-count trajectory and lack of evidence of an operating inflection.

surprises.description: RUM Group reported Q2 revenue of $40.4 million, above the preview’s estimated $33–37 million build and the roughly $30.7 million consensus-implied figure. That is a clear upside gap, not just the expected contribution from the short Quake AI consolidation period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 61% year-over-year to $40.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated total Q2 revenue of “~$33–37” million and cited “~$30.7M” implied consensus.

surprises.description: The first formal revenue guidance was for Q3 only, at $87–93 million; the preview’s central guidance question was whether management would provide a credible FY2026 revenue range. The Q3 range signals a substantial ramp, but the stated guidance does not answer that annual-guidance question.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company issued its first-ever formal revenue guidance, projecting Q3 2026 revenue of $87 million to $93 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Delivering a credible FY26 revenue and adj. EBITDA range is the single highest-variance item”; the preview also said the company would “initiate formal financial guidance concurrent with the Q2 release.”

surprises.description: Management newly quantified a much higher-value monetization model for AI-compute-as-a-service: about $11 million per megawatt annually on Blackwell versus $1.5–2 million for power-and-shell. The preview discussed the 250MW and $3B-plus opportunity but did not provide this per-megawatt comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-compute-as-a-service monetizes at roughly $11 million per megawatt per year on Blackwell versus $1.5–2 million for the power-and-shell model.”

surprises.description: RUM said it will stop using MAU and ARPU as headline metrics from Q3 and instead report by Rumble Video and Quake AI. The preview expected MAU and ARPU to remain key measures to watch, although it also anticipated the move toward segment reporting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Starting Q3, RUM Group will drop MAU and ARPU as headline metrics … in favor of segment reporting for Rumble Video and Quake AI.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “MAU … ARPU” among the key metrics to watch and separately asked whether RUM would “break out Quake AI separately.”

in_line: The Northern Data acquisition closed on June 17, as the preview already described; Q2 was expected to include only a short Quake AI consolidation period.
GPU utilization was reported at over 85%, broadly matching the preview’s expectation that utilization near 85% would hold.
The Together AI agreement to deploy NVIDIA HGX B300 capacity is consistent with the preview’s focus on further B300 wins and new contracts.
The 250MW power roadmap and $3B-plus annual revenue opportunity were already described in the preview as management’s ambition.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $7.6 million, well below the preview’s implied $9.5–10.5 million, and the roughly 6.9% margin was below the company’s 8–10% guide. Management attributed pressure to higher fuel and driver costs incurred before customer payment cycles.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $7.6 million in Q2 2026 from $11.3 million in Q2 2025,” pressured by “higher fuel and driver costs incurred ahead of customer payment cycles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (not formally polled): ~$9.5–10.5M implied”; company guidance was an “8–10% adjusted EBITDA margin.”

surprises.description: PAL announced a $130 million enterprise-value acquisition of Hansen & Adkins, a much larger transaction than the preview’s general possibility of a bolt-on. H&A’s more than $400 million of revenue and $27 million of EBITDA would make the combined company over $800 million in revenue and roughly $60 million in adjusted EBITDA, with a leading North American market position and entry into Canada.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company agreed to acquire Hansen & Adkins at an enterprise value of $130 million”; H&A generated “over $400 million in revenue and more than $27 million in EBITDA,” making the combined entity “over $800 million in revenue and roughly $60 million in adjusted EBITDA.” The combined company is expected to be “the largest auto hauler in North America.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a bolt-on” was one possible catalyst and noted that “seven acquisitions in five quarters” made integration credibility important; it did not anticipate this transaction or its scale.

surprises.description: The standalone Q3 revenue outlook was flattish versus Q2, short of the preview’s expectation of at least $110 million. Management did expect improved profitability, so the outlook was not uniformly negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “Q3 standalone revenue flattish versus Q2 with improved profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side wants ≥$110M revenue and adj. OR below 96%” for Q3.

surprises.description: The preview’s share-taking test was not met: units fell 8% year over year, slightly worse than the preview’s roughly 7% decline threshold for continued share gains. Deliveries were still within its broad estimated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Units delivered down 8% to 580,962.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 units at “~575–620k” and said “down less than ~7% YoY” would indicate continued share gain.

surprises.description: Quarter-end net debt and leverage were higher than the preview’s starting figures: net debt was $62.3 million and leverage 2.1x, versus approximately $59.3 million and 1.6x in the preview. This adds to the balance-sheet burden alongside the announced acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt stood at $62.3 million at quarter-end for a 2.1x leverage ratio” on trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of $30.3 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “net leverage at 1.6x (net debt ~$59.3M on TTM adj. EBITDA $36.3M).”

surprises.description: The deal financing introduced a substantial convertible and equipment-facility structure that the preview had not anticipated. A capped call is intended to reduce dilution, but the financing adds a capital-structure consideration beyond the preview’s discussion of buybacks and possible M&A.
surprises.fact_evidence: The deal is being financed with “a $75 million 7-year convertible bond” plus “a capped call to reduce dilution,” and “a syndicated equipment facility of up to $120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the “$15M buyback authorized” and possible “bolt-on” M&A, but did not describe convertible or equipment-facility financing.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in above the primary published consensus but just below the preview’s roughly $110 million whisper. It was within the company’s $105–110 million guide, making the headline a modest beat against the primary estimate rather than a clear beat against the higher expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total operating revenue was $109.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$106.78M” primary consensus, company guidance of “$105–110M,” and a whisper “at the high end of guidance, ~$110M.”

surprises.description: The monthly operating-ratio trend improved more than the preview’s key threshold by June: June reached 95.7%, and management called it the best month of the calendar year. This is a positive monthly data point, though it does not establish that the full-quarter ratio met the target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Monthly operating ratios “improved sequentially through Q2, ending with June at 95.7%, the best month of the calendar year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “anything ≤96%” as evidence of improvement and identified adjusted OR as the key metric.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $109.4 million was within the company’s $105–110 million guidance range.
Revenue per unit was up 2.9%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of flat-to-up year-over-year revenue per unit.
Q2 deliveries of 580,962 were within the preview’s broad estimate of roughly 575,000–620,000 units.
Year-to-date equipment CapEx was under $5 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of less than $10 million for full-year 2026.

surprises.description: TCMD reported diluted EPS of $0.34, well above the preview’s $0.14 consensus. That is a substantially larger earnings beat than the preview’s base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net income increased 142% to $7.8 million, or $0.34 per diluted share, up from $0.14 per share in the prior-year period.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) $0.14”; the base scenario also expected “$0.14–0.16.”

surprises.description: Airway clearance revenue fell to $12.1 million, rather than reaching the preview’s roughly $14 million and 9% growth bogey. Management also lowered its full-year airway outlook to roughly flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Airway clearance down 7% to $12.1 million”; the outlook was “more conservative” and now expected to be “roughly flat year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s airway bogey was “~$14M (+9% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $11.4 million, above the preview’s estimated $9–10 million range. The full-year EBITDA outlook was maintained rather than raised, as the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 49% to $11.4 million”; full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was “maintained at approximately $49–$51 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The quarterly estimate was “~$9–10M”; the preview said the FY26 guide was “$49–51M (maintained, not raised).”

surprises.description: The top of full-year revenue guidance was lowered by $2 million, to $366 million from the previewed $368 million. The reduction was tied to a weaker airway clearance outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “lowered the top end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $360–$366 million,” driven by a more conservative airway clearance outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected the company to “reaffirm $360–368M.”

surprises.description: Lymphedema revenue slightly exceeded the preview’s $72–73 million estimate, reaching $73.6 million and growing 12% rather than the expected 10%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lymphedema up 12% to $73.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s lymphedema bogey was “~$72–73M (+10% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was below the preview’s approximate net-cash figure, with the decline attributed partly to upfront payments for distribution rights and share repurchases. The company still had no debt.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash fell to $69.9 million from $83.4 million at year-end 2025,” reflecting “upfront payments for the Elastomed/MyoSleeve distribution rights and share repurchases, with no outstanding debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Net cash: ~$75M, no debt.”

surprises.description: TCMD disclosed an expanded Lymphatech diagnostic-aid indication filing and a push for a Category 3 CPT code, neither of which the preview flagged. These could open a larger market, but the indication is expected in 2027 and Lymphatech remains a small part of lymphedema revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lymphatech, still a small portion of lymphedema revenue, has submitted for an expanded FDA diagnostic-aid indication expected in 2027 and is pursuing a Category 3 CPT code to unlock a market of 20 million undiagnosed U.S. patients.”

surprises.description: The MyoSleeve distribution agreement was an unflagged development in the preview. Management said it should contribute incrementally over time, but is not expected to add material revenue under current guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MyoSleeve distribution agreement is expected to contribute incrementally over time but is not assumed to add material revenue in current guidance, leveraging existing VA sales infrastructure.”

in_line: Global revenue was $85.7 million, essentially matching the preview’s $85.5 million consensus and within its $85–87 million base-case range.
Gross margin was 76.3%, within the preview’s ~76–77% estimate and above its 76% minimum bogey.
The Medicare prior-authorization requirement shifted some lymphedema orders from Q2 into Q3, with normalization expected; the preview had anticipated Q2 timing friction and a larger Q3 step-up.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance remained approximately $49–51 million, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: WEBTOON’s Q2 constant-currency revenue growth was 5.2%, above the 1.7%–4.6% range in its prior guide, even though reported revenue of $338.5 million was essentially in line with the $338.8 million consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $338.5 million,” down 2.8% reported but “growing 5.2% on a constant currency basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave the company’s Q2 constant-currency guide as “+1.7% to +4.6%” and consensus revenue as “$338.8M.”

surprises.description: The reported-versus-constant-currency gap was wider than the preview’s roughly 6-percentage-point implied FX headwind: Q2 reported revenue fell 2.8% while constant-currency revenue grew 5.2%, an approximately 8-point gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue declined “2.8% year-over-year on a reported basis” and grew “5.2% on a constant currency basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated an “implied ~6pp FX headwind” from the company’s guide and said to reconcile that bridge.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA exceeded the top of the company’s guide and the preview’s consensus range. The beat was modest in absolute terms, while EBITDA margin still contracted as marketing investment increased.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA came in at $5.5 million, exceeding the high end of guidance,” compared with the prior-year $9.7 million; margin fell to 1.6% from 2.8% due to increased marketing investment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$0.0–5.0M” and consensus of “~$2–3M.”

surprises.description: Advertising turned into a much stronger growth contributor than expected: it grew 11.5% in constant currency, versus the preview’s expectation of a year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advertising was a bright spot with 11.5% constant currency growth,” including rest-of-world ad revenue growing “over 20%” in constant currency.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed advertising consensus as “$43.0M” and “-4.8% Y/Y,” and described Q1 advertising as down 0.5%.

surprises.description: Japan deteriorated rather than improving toward the preview’s hoped-for stabilization: revenue fell 6.7% in constant currency and MPU fell 9.5% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Japan revenue declined 6.7% on a constant currency basis with MPU down 9.5% year-over-year,” and remained the key weak spot to stabilize.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Japan “inflecting to flat-or-better cc” was the key proof point and expected the base case to be “still -2% to -4% cc,” versus Q1’s -3.4%.

surprises.description: The Q3 constant-currency revenue outlook is weak relative to the acceleration the preview was watching for. Although the $358–$368 million range is above the preview’s roughly $355 million consensus in nominal dollars, the guided 0.7%–3.3% constant-currency growth is below the preview’s expected 4%–6% range and its roughly 5% threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance calls for constant-currency revenue growth of “0.7% to 3.3% ($358–$368 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Q3 cc guide +4–6%”; it also said anything implying “<+5% cc” would break the acceleration thesis.

surprises.description: Korea was a notably strong growth market, with double-digit constant-currency revenue and user-monetization growth; the preview did not identify this market-specific upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: Korea had “20% constant currency revenue growth, 5.9% MAU growth, 10.4% MPU growth, and 14.8% ARPU growth year-over-year.”

surprises.description: WEBTOON announced a 60% ownership stake in RI Games Holdings across two closings, a move into off-platform IP ownership not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company made a “60% ownership stake in RI Games Holdings (across two closings).”

surprises.description: WEBTOON also co-established a $100 million IP Adaptation Fund with Naver, a specific new capital commitment beyond the preview’s discussion of capital allocation and Naver ownership.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company announced a “$100 million IP Adaptation Fund co-established with Naver.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “capital allocation / strategic” developments and commentary around “Naver’s majority stake,” but did not anticipate this fund.

in_line: Q2 revenue was essentially in line with the preview’s $338.8 million consensus: actual revenue was $338.5 million.

Management reaffirmed its expectation to return to double-digit revenue growth by exiting Q4 2026, consistent with the preview’s focus on whether that commitment would remain; management clarified it is a run-rate target, not full-quarter guidance.
Gross margin expanded nearly 100 basis points to 26%, meeting the preview’s stated 26% threshold for a positive gross-margin result.

surprises.description: The preview considered a cut to FY2026 revenue guidance the most likely outcome because of the large second-half ramp required. Instead, SRFM reaffirmed the $128–138 million range, despite Q3 guidance that does not fully meet the implied quarterly pace at its midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $128-138 million revenue (20-30% growth)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A trim to the low end (or below $128M) paired with a maintained or improved EBITDA guide is a very plausible — arguably the most likely — outcome.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $35.5–37.5 million is below the preview’s implied $37–42 million quarterly pace needed in the second half to meet the annual range, at the midpoint and especially at the low end. That leaves more of the annual target dependent on a stronger Q4, even though full-year guidance was reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $35.5-37.5 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied 2H26: $74M – $84M, or $37M – $42M per quarter.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in at the top of guidance and slightly above the preview’s consensus estimate, whereas the preview’s base case put revenue at or just below consensus. The beat was modest in dollar terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue was $29.5 million, at the high end of guidance”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Street Consensus ~ $29.3M”; the base case expected “$28.0M – $29.5M (in guide, at/just below consensus).”

surprises.description: Surf On Demand showed stronger momentum than the preview’s deceleration concern: departures rose about 67% and revenue per departure about 25%, and first-half revenue nearly doubled year over year. The preview warned that growth below roughly 40% would weaken the segment’s growth story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Surf On Demand private charter posted record Q2 revenue of $12.1 million with departures up ~67% and revenue per departure up ~25% year-over-year, nearly doubling first-half revenue versus the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Deceleration below ~40% would remove the one line that is clearly working.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed an enterprise SurfOS pipeline it says could be worth tens of millions of dollars annually, a scale of potential opportunity the preview did not quantify. This remains pipeline, not signed revenue; management’s stated goal is at least one additional enterprise contract by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management describes an enterprise SurfOS pipeline potentially worth tens of millions annually, targets at least one additional enterprise contract by year-end.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $10.5 million was within the guided loss range and within the preview’s expected range.
The Wheels Up deal was already known as SRFM’s first enterprise SurfOS customer; the preview described its two-year value and optional extension as up to about $12.2 million.
Scheduled service continued to decline following deliberate exits from unprofitable routes, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the airline business would keep shrinking by design.

The refinancing and asset-backed financing fit the preview’s discussion of the debt restructuring and funding bridge; the preview also flagged the NYSE deficiency and shareholder-approved reverse split.
The Q4 OperatorOS launch timing and progress toward the 100-broker target were consistent with the preview’s stated 2H launch plans and broker-count target.

surprises.description: Alico reported Q3 revenue of $9.0 million, far above the preview’s roughly $2.75 million consensus estimate. The preview expected a quiet quarter without a material land closing, so the reported top line was substantially stronger than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue rose 7.7% to $9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY26 Consensus” revenue was “$2.75M”; the preview estimated “revenue $2.5–3.0M” and expected “No material closing.”

surprises.description: Instead of the expected quarterly loss, Alico reported net income attributable to common stockholders of $2.1 million, or $0.29 per diluted share. The turnaround was mainly due to completed citrus tree accelerated depreciation, so the positive earnings result does not necessarily indicate stronger recurring operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net income attributable to common stockholders was $2.1 million ($0.29 per diluted share)”; the result was “driven mainly by completed citrus tree accelerated depreciation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q3 diluted EPS consensus was “$(0.73)”; the preview’s estimate was “EPS $(0.68)–$(0.75)” and net loss “$(5.0)–$(5.5)M.”

surprises.description: Alico raised fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $15 million rather than reaffirming the $14 million outlook the preview treated as the baseline. The raise is favorable against an expectation that a reaffirmation would be neutral.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $15 million from prior guidance of approximately $14 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance (~$14M) — reaffirm or cut”; the base case expected “FY26 guidance reaffirmed ($14M EBITDA / $40M cash / $45M net debt).”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was $55.6 million, above the preview’s expected $46–49 million range and its stated positive-surprise threshold of more than $49 million. Cash had increased since fiscal year-end rather than showing the anticipated second-half consumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alico ended Q3 2026 with $55.6 million in cash, up $17.5 million since fiscal year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “cash $46–49M” and said “Anything above ~$49M is a positive surprise.”

surprises.description: The company’s year-end outlook is stronger than the preview’s expected $40 million cash and $45 million net debt: Alico now expects roughly $48 million in cash and $37 million net debt. This points to a better year-end liquidity position than the anticipated baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Alico “now expects to end the year with roughly $48 million in cash and $37 million net debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “$40M cash / $45M net debt” at fiscal year-end.

surprises.description: Management said available liquidity should fund operations through at least fiscal 2029 without further asset sales. The preview focused on the near-term cash balance and expected year-end cash burn, but did not anticipate this longer-term assurance of operating liquidity.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management stated that liquidity, including “$92.5 million of available borrowing capacity,” is “sufficient to fund operations through at least fiscal 2029 without any additional asset sales.”

surprises.description: Management explicitly valued Alico’s roughly 47,300-acre Florida portfolio at about $9,000 per acre and said it carries substantially more value than the current market capitalization reflects. The preview identified the gap between conservative portfolio assumptions and recent transaction pricing as a key debate, but the call supplied a broad portfolio valuation at the higher per-acre mark.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said the “roughly 47,300-acre Florida portfolio, valued at ~$9,000 per acre consistent with recent sales, carries substantially more value than reflected in the current market capitalization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management’s portfolio value used “$4,000–5,000/acre” while recent sales were around “$9,100/acre,” and called an updated per-acre disclosure that closes that gap “a bullish narrative shift.”

surprises.description: Alico acquired the remaining 49% of Citree for $2 million in cash and assumed approximately $3.3 million of debt, a capital-allocation transaction the preview did not identify as an expected event. The transaction adds ownership but also uses cash and adds assumed debt.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “acquired the remaining 49% of Citree for $2 million in cash while assuming its ~$3.3 million debt.”

surprises.description: Q3 EBITDA was $4.6 million, whereas the preview estimated adjusted EBITDA of negative $3.5–4.5 million. The measures are not identical, but the reported positive EBITDA contrasts sharply with the preview’s expected quarterly loss; the call attributed the year-over-year decline to lower insurance proceeds and reduced gains on asset sales rather than operational weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 EBITDA fell to $4.6 million from $19.2 million a year earlier, primarily due to lower crop insurance proceeds and reduced gains on property/equipment sales rather than operational weakness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “adj. EBITDA $(3.5)–$(4.5)M.”

in_line: The Hendry County lease covering approximately 3,280 acres, including a purchase option near $9,000 per acre, was already disclosed and described in the preview.
Completion of the $10 million share repurchase program was broadly expected: the preview stated that the $10 million program and 245,399 shares had been completed through April 2026.
The substantial citrus wind-down and resulting decline in nine-month revenue were consistent with the preview’s description of the planned transition away from citrus.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $22.7 million, above both the $21.45 million consensus and the $22.5 million top of company guidance. That is 11% year-over-year growth, well ahead of the preview’s implied 4.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $22.7 million, up 11% year-over-year … and exceeded the company's guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus (Aug 2026) $21.45M”; company Q2 guide “$20.5M – $22.5M”; implied y/y “+4.6%.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 3%–5% from 2%–4%, rather than merely reaffirming the range as the preview’s main checklist contemplated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 3%-5% (from 2%-4%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: revenue growth +2–4%”; the preview asked whether it would be “reaffirmed, raised, or trimmed” and identified reaffirmation as a possibility.

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted gross margin guidance was cut to 57%–59% from 58%–60%. The preview had highlighted a margin level of at least 59% as an important watchpoint, so the cut is a clear deterioration from the expected margin trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted gross margin guidance was cut by 100 basis points to 57%-59% (from 58%-60%) due to product mix shift toward lower-margin CMT products and higher China sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … adj. gross margin 58–60%”; catalyst checklist: “Adjusted gross margin ≥59%.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted gross margin was 57%, below the preview’s roughly 58% consensus and its ≥59% watchpoint, landing at the bottom of the company’s 57%–59% guide. Management attributed the pressure to higher CMT and China sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted gross margin declined to 57% … pressured by higher CMT and China sales carrying lower margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted gross margin consensus at “~58%” and said to watch for “Adjusted gross margin ≥59%.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $1.7 million came in above the roughly $1.5 million consensus and at the high end of the outlook range. EBITDA margin nevertheless remained flat at 7.3%, so the upside was in the amount rather than margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA came in at $1.7 million, up 11% year-over-year and at the high end of the outlook range, though EBITDA margin remained flat at 7.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EBITDA consensus at “~$1.5M” and company guidance at “$1.0M – $2.0M.”

surprises.description: APAC revenue growth was much stronger than the preview’s China discussion suggested: APAC rose 24% and China rose 29%, compared with the preview’s reference to China growth of 3% in Q1. The reported China growth was partly helped by a weak prior-year base.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC revenue rose 24% year-over-year to $4.6 million, with China up 29% to $3.1 million, though partly benefiting from a weak prior-year base impacted by retaliatory tariffs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted, “China grew 3% in Q1 on CRO activity,” and described China as “the only geography with a specific new catalyst attached.”

surprises.description: Cash generation was weaker than the preview’s base case of cash being roughly flat: first-half operating cash flow was negative, and quarter-end cash was $6.5 million versus $7.1 million at Q1. The balance remained above the preview’s bear-case trigger of less than $6 million, but the reported figures show continued liquidity pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash used in operations was $0.3 million in the first half (versus $5.7 million generated a year earlier), with the company ending the quarter with only $6.5 million in cash and net debt of $33.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “cash roughly flat”; it flagged cash and operating cash flow as a key risk and described cash below $6 million as a bear-case signal.

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA growth guidance was reaffirmed at 6%–10%, consistent with the preview’s stated full-year guidance.
Project Viking remains on track with $3 million of savings expected in 2027 and $4 million annually thereafter, matching the preview’s outlined savings targets.

surprises.description: The preview expected the pivotal-trial and interim-analysis milestones to be the main update, but Bicara also announced that CEO Claire Mazumdar will become Vice Chair and Strategic Adviser at the start of next year, with President/COO Ryan Cohlhepp succeeding her ahead of pivotal data. The company also announced January promotions for Tanya Green and Jenna Cohen.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Claire Mazumdar will transition to Vice Chair and Strategic Adviser at the start of next year, with current President/COO Ryan Cohlhepp succeeding her as President and CEO ahead of pivotal data”; “additional January promotions of Tanya Green to COO and Jenna Cohen to Chief Business Officer.”

surprises.description: The preview noted CFO Ivan Hyep’s prior stock sale but did not anticipate his departure; the call said he is being replaced by Jenn Larson effective the day after the call. The immediate CFO change adds to the leadership transition announcements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Ivan Hyep is being replaced by Jenn Larson effective the day after the call.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned that “CFO Ivan Hyep sold ~$808K of stock” under a pre-arranged plan, but did not mention a CFO transition.

surprises.description: Q2 cash was slightly above the preview’s expected range: Bicara reported approximately $497 million versus the preview’s $485–495 million estimate. The expected runway into the first half of 2029 was unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bicara ended Q2 2026 with approximately $497 million in cash and marketable securities, providing runway into the first half of 2029.”

surprises.description: Management identified a specific new competitive catalyst: Genmab’s LiGeR-HN1 frontline head-and-neck readout is slated for Q4 2026, with overall response rate data expected to be an early indication of durability. The preview flagged competitive read-through generally but did not identify this trial or its timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Competitor Genmab's LiGeR-HN1 frontline head and neck readout is now slated for Q4 2026,” with “overall response rate data as an early indicator of durability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned “any competitive 1L HNSCC read-through” as a risk, but did not name LiGeR-HN1 or give a Q4 2026 timing.

in_line: FORTIFI-HN01 remains on track for substantial enrollment by year-end and a mid-2027 interim analysis, matching the preview’s central milestone expectation.
FORTIFI-FLEX was initiated, as the preview expected for Q3; the call also said site overlap with the pivotal study is limited and enrollment is staged to keep FORTIFI-HN01 the priority.

The reported approximately one-in-three three-year survival at the 1,500 mg weekly dose is consistent with the preview’s cited 31% three-year survival and roughly twofold comparison with standard care.
The cash runway into the first half of 2029 was reaffirmed, as expected.
Management said operating expenses rose year over year and are expected to increase further, in line with the preview’s expectation of a Phase 3 spend ramp and commercial build-out.

surprises.description: LWLG added a fifth Stage 3 customer in Q2, ahead of the preview’s expectation that one or two additional customers would reach Stage 3 by the end of Q3. The new customer is an unnamed Fortune Global 500 company focused on scale-across transceivers using coherent modulation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expanded to five stage-three customers this quarter, adding a new unnamed Fortune Global 500 customer focused on scale-across transceivers using coherent modulation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Stage 3 customer count (currently 4). Management guided on the Q1 call to 1–2 additional tier-1 customers reaching Stage 3 by end of Q3 2026. A fifth named at this print = ahead of schedule.”

surprises.description: The company reported that one material supply and licensing agreement is already in place, although the preview expected the lead-customer agreement to remain under negotiation and said no commercial agreement was expected in the base case. A second agreement is still being negotiated with the most advanced customer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One material supply and licensing agreement is already in place, and a second is being negotiated with the most advanced customer, targeting volume production beginning in the second half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Under negotiation as of the Q1 call. Execution of this converts the story from prototypes to contracted economics”; the base case anticipated “no commercial agreement yet.”

surprises.description: Net loss was lower than the preview’s modeled estimate, though the reported four-cent loss per share was within the preview’s expected range. This was a modest improvement rather than a major earnings surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $6.6 million (4 cents per share) from roughly $5 million (4 cents per share) in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss … Q2 FY2026 est. ~$7.0M”; EPS estimate was “$(0.04)–$(0.05).”

surprises.description: R&D expense was slightly higher than the preview’s model, at about $3.9 million versus an estimate of roughly $3.7 million. The call attributed the increase to scale-up investments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expense increased to about $3.9 million (from $2.6 million) … reflecting scale-up investments.”

in_line: Revenue of approximately $33,000 was close to the preview’s ~$35,000 estimate; the preview also cautioned that revenue was small and lumpy.
Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $95.9 million were within the preview’s expected $95–105 million range.

Foundry wafers were expected from two foundries in August and a third in Q4, while another foundry was targeting a tape-out later in the year; this is broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of multiple foundry devices in Q3–Q4, though no measured 200G/400G results were reported.
The company continued to target volume production beginning in the second half of 2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the 2027 target would be maintained.

surprises.description: INVINCIBLE-3 was expected to be resuming enrollment in April, but management now says new enrollment should begin only within the next couple of months and at limited U.S. sites. That points to a later and narrower restart than the preview’s April-resumption framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New patient enrollment in the Phase 3 INVINCIBLE-3 study is expected to begin within the next couple of months at limited U.S. sites.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With INVINCIBLE-3 resuming (April 2026)” and “patients enrolled since April restart.”

surprises.description: Q2 net loss was $3.0 million, above the preview’s implied consensus range of about $2.3–2.4 million. The miss came alongside the expected R&D ramp, so the financial result was worse than expected while the higher clinical spending was consistent with trial restarts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss for Q2 2026 rose 19% year-over-year to $3.0 million,” with R&D expense “climbing 19% to $1.8 million on higher clinical trial costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss | ~$2.3–2.4M implied” and diluted EPS consensus of “$(0.87).”

surprises.description: INVINCIBLE-4 reported a 71% pCR rate with INT230-6 plus standard of care versus 42% with standard of care alone in a harder-to-treat group. The treatment-arm result is strong, but the 42% control rate makes the observed treatment-control gap less pronounced than a low control response would imply; the preview had flagged uncertainty in the pCR figures and denominators.
surprises.fact_evidence: “71% of Cohort A patients (INT230-6 plus standard of care) achieved pathologic complete response versus 42% for standard of care alone,” in a population with “median tumor size over 2.4 cm.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preliminary pCR figures have been presented inconsistently across releases … so watch the denominators.”

in_line: Q2 ending cash of $9.5 million was within the preview’s approximately $8.5–10.0 million estimate.
R&D increased from Q1 as expected while the trials restarted; the preview specifically said R&D should step up and that rising R&D would validate the restarts.

The need for additional financing remained apparent: the preview already warned that cash might not cover the trial timelines and that further dilution could be needed. The call quantified the need, saying completion of INVINCIBLE-3 would require another $30 million and current cash was insufficient to restart all sites.

The preview anticipated ATM use and treated partnering progress beyond discussions as the key potential catalyst; the call reported ATM proceeds and ongoing partnership discussions supported by BIO meetings, but no new agreement or named deal.

surprises.description: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $9.8 million, below the preview’s $12.5 million estimate and the $12–13 million base-case range. Its 9.5% margin was also below the preview’s 11% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 22% year-over-year to $9.8 million, with margin expanding 240 basis points to 9.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ... My estimate: $12.5M (11.0% margin)” and the base scenario projected “$12–13M.”

surprises.description: Net sales were $102.9 million, below the preview’s $114 million estimate and below even its $105–110 million bear-case range. The preview cautioned that published consensus of $84.9 million was stale and unusable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales declined to $102.9 million from $113.1 million a year earlier, primarily reflecting the closure of the U.K. cast roll facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate: $114M”; the bear scenario projected “$105–110M.” The preview said to “Treat the published revenue consensus as unusable.”

surprises.description: Forged and Cast Engineered Products adjusted EBITDA recovered to $7.8 million, but remained below the preview’s roughly $9 million base expectation for a reversal of Q1 timing pressures. The reported year-over-year and sequential gains show improvement, but less than the preview’s key threshold implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Forged and Cast segment adjusted EBITDA rose 15% year-over-year and 36% sequentially to $7.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “FCEP EBITDA lands ≥$9M” would keep the thesis intact and modeled “FCEP EBITDA ~$9M” in its base case.

surprises.description: Forged and Cast segment sales were $67.3 million, below the preview’s $74 million estimate. The company attributed nearly all of the decline to the U.K. facility exit and AUP distribution business, but the preview’s estimate was still higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Forged and Cast Engineered Products segment net sales fell to $67.3 million from $77.9 million, with nearly all of the decline attributed to exiting the U.K. facility and AUP distribution business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s segment estimate was “FCEP revenue ... $74M.”

surprises.description: The Air & Liquid segment reported its highest-ever adjusted EBITDA, up 34% in the quarter, with manufacturing efficiencies and product mix contributing. That is stronger than the preview’s expectation that margins would merely hold as volume and capacity increased.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Air & Liquid segment delivered its highest adjusted EBITDA in its history, up 34% in Q2 ... driven by manufacturing efficiencies and positive product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “ALP margin durability at record volume” as a key issue and said to watch “whether incremental margins hold as headcount and capacity step up.”

surprises.description: Total backlog reached $385.4 million, about $10 million above the preview’s roughly $375 million estimate and above its base-case range of $370–380 million. Orders themselves were approximately $144 million, in line with the preview’s calculation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer orders of approximately $144 million were up 50% versus the prior year, and total backlog grew $39.9 million from Q1 to $385.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Backlog (6/30) ... ~$375M” and modeled “backlog ~$370–380M” in its base case; it derived Q2 orders of “roughly $144M.”

surprises.description: Management said the second half would be significantly stronger than the first half, a more emphatic recovery statement than the preview’s base-case expectation of ongoing improvement as the year progressed. The outlook was qualified by normal seasonal maintenance outages.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects the second half of 2026 to be significantly stronger than the first half despite normal Q3 seasonal maintenance outages in the U.S. and Europe.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated that “trends support ongoing improvement as 2026 progresses”; it also said the call would be watched for “any FY2026 EBITDA framing.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was $0.07, a penny below the preview’s $0.08 consensus and five cents below its $0.12 estimate. The return to positive net income was a year-over-year turnaround, but the reported EPS still missed the stated expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $1.5 million ($0.07 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “EPS (GAAP) ... $0.08” consensus and “My estimate: $0.12.”

in_line: Customer orders were approximately $144 million, matching the preview’s estimate of roughly $144 million.

surprises.description: NGS reported GAAP EPS of $0.30, below the preview’s $0.37 consensus estimate and its $0.38–$0.42 model range. The preview anticipated transaction costs of about $2–3 million; the call cited approximately $3.3 million, while adjusted EPS was $0.47, close to the preview’s ~$0.48 estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported net income fell to $3.8 million ($0.30/share) from $5.2 million ($0.41/share) a year earlier, impacted by ~$3.3 million in Flat Rock transaction costs; adjusted net income was $6.1 million ($0.47/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS $0.37” consensus; the preview’s model was “GAAP diluted EPS $0.38–0.42” and “Adjusted EPS ~ $0.48.” It also estimated “Transaction costs (~$2–3M pre-tax).”

surprises.description: Flat Rock contributed about $1.9 million of Q2 rental revenue in roughly half a month, above the preview’s $1.4 million stub estimate. The preview cautioned that actual stub revenue could vary by ±40%, so the upside was limited relative to that uncertainty.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Flat Rock contributed only ~half a month (~$1.9 million) of that revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flatrock stub: 86,000 rented HP × ~$27.50/HP/month × ~0.6 month ≈ $1.4M revenue”; the preview noted, “Actual stub revenue could be ±40%.”

surprises.description: Post-acquisition leverage was 2.77x, below the preview’s approximately 3.0x pro forma expectation, with more than $170 million of unused facility capacity. That indicates somewhat more financial headroom than the preview had modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post-acquisition leverage was 2.77x against a 3.5x covenant, with over $170 million of unused facility capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma leverage was guided to ~3.0x at close.”

surprises.description: NGS raised its organic deployment target to at least 55,000 horsepower, above the preview’s expectation that the company would reaffirm a 50,000-horsepower target. This provides a higher stated deployment floor than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised organic 2026 deployment guidance to at least 55,000 horsepower from 50,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market needed “confirmation that ≥50,000 HP of organic deployment” remained intact and described “≥50k HP reaffirmed” in its base scenario.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $25.1 million, close to the preview’s ~$25.0 million estimate.
The FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance raise to $103–108 million was broadly in line with the preview’s mechanical expectation of ~$103–108 million.
Horsepower utilization of 88.3% was close to the preview’s expectation of roughly 88%.
Rental revenue per average horsepower rose to $28.06 from $27.51 in Q1, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would continue climbing.
Rental revenue of $49.4 million was close to the preview’s $49.6 million rental-revenue estimate.
The quarterly dividend remained at $0.15 per share, the level the preview identified as already having been raised and as a key capital-allocation consideration.

surprises.description: MASS said the AVCAD contract has run its course and excluded any AVCAD contribution from FY2026 guidance, rather than retaining the preview’s expected $2–3 million 2H contribution. Management still described AVCAD as a $10 million-plus long-term opportunity, but gave no current contribution to rely on.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AVCAD military program's current contract has run its course and remains excluded from guidance,” while management views it as “a $10 million-plus long-term opportunity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said AVCAD was “guided at $2–3M in 2H” and called for watching whether that line was “held intact”; it also said the contribution was contingent on an anticipated Smiths Detection award.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $16.1 million, above the preview’s roughly $15.4–$15.5 million expectation, with reported year-over-year growth of 23% versus the preview’s expected 18–19%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $16.1 million, up 23% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 revenue consensus of “$15.37M” and a base-case estimate of “$15.5M (+19% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: MASS secured a previously unanticipated $6 million Protector order from an Asia Pacific corrections agency, with deliveries expected to contribute revenue in both Q3 and Q4. The preview highlighted the value of a named large order but did not anticipate this order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $6 million Protector order from an Asia Pacific corrections agency was secured in July and will be split across Q3 and Q4 2026 revenue.”

surprises.description: NearLab’s expected second-half revenue contribution was put at about $1.25 million, below the preview’s estimate of roughly $1.7 million for 2H. The company also reported brisk sales—more than 35 devices in about 60 days, each with a multi-year subscription—so the update combines a lower near-term revenue contribution with encouraging sales traction.
surprises.fact_evidence: NearLab “sold more than 35 devices within ~60 days each with a multi-year subscription” and is “expected to contribute ~$1.25 million in second-half revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated that “NIRLAB (~$1.7M of its ~$2.5M eight-month contribution lands in 2H).”

surprises.description: MASS raised the low end of its full-year revenue range by $1 million, to $68–$70 million, instead of simply reiterating the $67–$70 million range expected in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised the low end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $68-$70 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected FY guidance to be “reiterated at $67–70M.”

in_line: Adjusted gross margin was approximately 57%, matching the preview’s 57% base case and 56–58% expected range.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $1.9 million, close to the preview’s $2.0 million loss estimate.
U.S. state and local customers generated more than half of Q2 revenue, consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued state and local demand.
The Viper placement outlook of more than 100, potentially approaching 150, for the year was consistent with the preview’s expectation of 2–3x the 2025 placement level.
