surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $41.6 million, above the $40.17 million consensus and the preview’s roughly $39.9 million base case. Its 9.1% year-over-year growth also exceeded management’s “mid-single-digit” Q2 guide cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $41.6 million, up approximately 9.1% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus” revenue: “$40.17M”; “My Base” revenue: “$39.9M”; management guided Q2 to “mid-single-digit” revenue growth.

surprises.description: Profitability was much better than the preview’s expected loss: adjusted EBITDA was positive, while the preview estimated about a $4.0 million adjusted EBITDA loss. The $0.05-per-share net loss was also substantially narrower than the $0.11 consensus loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.3 million versus negative $5.6 million a year ago”; “net loss narrowed to $3.4 million ($0.05/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA ~$(4.0)M” and listed consensus EPS of “$(0.11).”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 51.1%, well above the preview’s roughly 48% consensus implication and 47.5% base estimate. This went against the preview’s concern that the revenue mix would drag margins lower.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 51.1% from 46.6% year-over-year, driven by favorable mix and improved revenue cycle management.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put gross margin at “~48% implied” by consensus and “47.5%” in its base case, and said shifting toward Greenbrook “mechanically drags GM.”

surprises.description: Greenbrook clinic revenue was $26.9 million, well above the preview’s $24.5–25.0 million estimate. Its 16.8% growth also ran faster than the preview’s expected 6–9% growth and anticipated deceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Greenbrook clinic revenue reached $26.9 million, up 16.8% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Clinic revenue ~$24.5–25.0M” and “+6–9% y/y,” describing growth as “decelerating.”

surprises.description: Neurostar treatment-session revenue declined by double digits, worse than the preview’s expected low-to-mid-single-digit decline. This weakness left total Neurostar revenue down 2.7% despite capital sales growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Neurostar revenue was $14.7 million, down 2.7% year-over-year, as double-digit capital sales growth was offset by double-digit declines in treatment session revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected treatment sessions of “~$10.3–10.6M (down low-to-mid single digits y/y).”

surprises.description: Capital sales grew at a double-digit rate, stronger than the preview’s roughly flat-to-modest-growth system-sales build of $3.5–3.8 million versus $3.5 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Double-digit capital sales growth” at Neurostar.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “US NeuroStar systems ~$3.5–3.8M” versus Q2 FY25 actual US systems revenue of “$3.5M.”

surprises.description: The company narrowed FY26 revenue guidance to $160–164 million rather than reaffirming the prior $160–166 million range; the floor stayed the same, but the ceiling fell by $2 million. This was less severe than the preview’s feared guide-down scenario, but not the base case of a reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company narrowed full-year revenue guidance to $160–164 million (from $160–166 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the guidance question was “reaffirm, raise, or cut,” and its base case required the “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: FY26 gross-margin guidance moved up to 48–50% from 47–49%, above the prior range and consistent with the much stronger Q2 margin result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised gross margin guidance to 48–50% (from 47–49%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited company guidance of “GM 47–49%” and emphasized the need to demonstrate H2 expansion to meet that range.

surprises.description: Cash rose to $25 million from $19 million, whereas the preview’s liquidity bridge implied a Q2 cash burn. However, the increase was aided by $7.6 million of ATM proceeds, so it came with equity issuance rather than demonstrating stronger operating cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total cash rose to $25 million as of June 30 from $19 million at March 31, aided by $7.6 million in net proceeds from an at-the-market equity offering.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY guidance implied “Q2 burn of ~$4–8M” and flagged quarter-end cash and ATM usage as key issues; it noted “$41.7M of ATM capacity remained at Q1.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new Neurostar sales model: customers can buy systems outright or use lease financing with a la carte support. The company said the mix will shift toward capital, consumables, and service and away from session revenue, with second-half revenue potentially choppier before management expects renewed, sustainable growth entering 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The new model allows customers to purchase systems outright or use “lease financing with a la carte support,” shifting revenue “toward capital, consumables, and service and away from session revenue”; management said “second-half revenue may be choppier” but positions the company for “renewed and sustainable growth entering 2027.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted Greenbrook as a potential delivery site for Compass Pathways’ psilocybin therapy, using existing Spravato REMS infrastructure and roughly 40% unused clinic capacity. The preview did not identify this as a potential growth opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: Greenbrook has “roughly 40% unused capacity” and is positioning to deliver Compass Pathways’ psilocybin therapy, which requires “~6 hours of observation,” by leveraging existing Spravato REMS infrastructure.

surprises.description: Revenue was $662 million, below the preview’s $668.9 million consensus and below its $665–672 million base-case range; the year-over-year decline was 1.8% versus the preview’s 0.8% consensus decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue was approximately $662 million, down 1.8% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $668.9M”; the base case expected “$665–672M (−0.3 to −1.3% YoY).”

surprises.description: Pounds processed fell 4.5%, substantially more than the preview’s base-case expectation of a 1%–2% decline. Management attributed the decline to exiting volume generating only $0.55 per pound against a $1.24 cost per pound, so the larger volume drop was linked to removing deeply unprofitable business rather than simply unexplained account losses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 4.5% decline in pounds processed” was driven by exiting “low-quality volume averaging only $0.55 revenue per pound versus the business's $1.24 cost per pound.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “volume −1% to −2% framed as deliberate mix exit”; the bear case described a decline “past ~2.5%” as signaling real account losses.

surprises.description: Revenue per pound rose 3% to $1.42, stronger than the preview’s minimum bar of $1.37 and flat-to-up year over year. The increase marked the first actual year-over-year rise since Vestis became public, rather than merely another quarter without a decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue per pound rose $0.04 or approximately 3% year-over-year to $1.42,” the “first year-over-year increase in revenue per pound since Vestis became a public company.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview set a bar of “Revenue per pound (≥$1.37, flat-to-up YoY)” and said a second clean quarter would show the trend was continuing.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in at $80.9 million, just above the preview’s $78–80 million bar, with a 12.2% margin versus the expected 11.7%–12.0%. The result was somewhat stronger than the expected range, though not a major gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA reached approximately $80.9 million,” up “23% year-over-year,” with margin “expanding to 12.2% from 9.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s key bar was “~$78–80M, ~11.7–12.0% margin”; it also said Q3 needed “roughly $79–80M.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year free cash flow guidance to $160–170 million from $120–150 million, a much larger increase than the preview’s already-surprising possibility of a raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year free cash flow guidance to $160-$170 million … a 22% increase from the prior $120-$150 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a maintained FCF guide would be “a modest positive and a raise is a genuine surprise,” with the existing range at “$120–150M.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was tightened to $310–315 million: the midpoint rose only $2.5 million from the prior midpoint, while the former $325 million upper end was removed. That is less expansive than the preview’s bull case of a raised range to $310–330 million and leaves a narrower ceiling despite the strong Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was tightened to $310-$315 million (midpoint $312.5 million), up $2.5 million from prior, implying Q4 EBITDA of $84-$89 million while the prior top end of $325 million was removed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the existing guide as “$295–325M” and described the base case as “FY26 guide reaffirmed”; its bull case anticipated “FY26 EBITDA raised to $310–330M.”

surprises.description: Transformation savings were already about $30 million in-year, versus the preview’s estimate of roughly $15 million realized YTD. That leaves about $20 million for Q4 to reach the approximately $50 million target, rather than the preview’s anticipated $35 million still needing to land in H2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Transformation initiatives have delivered roughly $30 million of in-year cost savings toward a ~$50 million target, with the remaining $20 million expected in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$15M realized YTD against a raised $50M in-year target” and said “~$35M in H2” was required.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new estimated $15–20 million management incentive bonus expense embedded in fiscal 2026 EBITDA, which was not present last year. The preview did not flag this new expense when discussing the expected EBITDA trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 marks the first year Vestis has accrued a management incentive bonus at this level, estimated at $15-$20 million of new expense embedded in EBITDA that was not present last year.”

surprises.description: A new outsourcing agreement is expected to save about $10 million annually beginning in fiscal 2027, an additional future cost-saving opportunity not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new third-party outsourcing agreement for back-office finance, IT, and customer service functions is expected to generate approximately $10 million in annualized cost savings beginning in fiscal 2027.”

surprises.description: Management identified the bottom roughly 30 market centers as a significant drag on results and plans to direct about 42% of plant CapEx to them in 2026–2027 to address a material margin gap. The preview did not anticipate this specific concentration of underperforming centers or the planned allocation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said the “bottom ~30 market centers (quadrant 4) significantly drag results” and plans to allocate “about 42% of plant CapEx to these centers in 2026-2027” to close a margin gap described as “material.”

surprises.description: Brookdale said occupancy has not inflected as quickly as anticipated and lowered its full-year occupancy expectation to roughly 83%. That is a weaker demand outlook than the preview’s focus on the known 82.4% Q2 occupancy and ongoing recovery, even though management said new cost efficiencies would offset the lower occupancy in its EBITDA outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Occupancy growth has not inflected as quickly as anticipated”; management lowered full-year consolidated occupancy expectation to “roughly 83%,” offsetting the lower occupancy with new cost efficiencies.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 occupancy was already known and described the demand story as “off the table as a surprise variable”; it focused on rate realization, expense control, and the EBITDA bridge.

surprises.description: Management gave a specific, back-loaded H2 growth profile: low-double-digit adjusted EBITDA growth in Q3 and growth above its mid-teens target range in Q4. The preview stressed that the full-year guide required steep H2 acceleration and that a lack of a sharper bridge would disappoint; the quarterly outlook provides some of the requested detail, though Q3 growth is below the overall H2 growth rate needed by the preview’s arithmetic.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company expects Q3 year-over-year adjusted EBITDA growth in the “low double-digit range” and Q4 growth “above its mid-teens target range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview calculated that the FY guide required “~$249–263M for H2 2026 vs. ~$217M in H2 2025 — 15–21% growth,” and said management needed to “sharpen the H2 bridge” with specifics.

surprises.description: Brookdale reported a new Houston acquisition and closure of a negative-NOI skilled nursing operation, neither of which was identified in the preview. The $23.4 million purchase was under $100,000 per unit, while closing the negative-NOI operation supports repositioning the property.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company acquired the 244-unit Brookdale Galleria in Houston for approximately “$23.4 million (under $100,000 per unit)” and closed its negative-NOI skilled nursing operations to reposition the property.

surprises.description: Leverage and liquidity improved more than the preview’s stated starting figures: annualized leverage fell to 8.4x from 8.8x and liquidity rose to $566 million from $369 million. The preview discussed deleveraging and liquidity as key issues but did not anticipate these specific improvements; the mortgage refinancing itself was already expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annualized leverage improved to 8.4x from 8.8x” and “total liquidity rose to $566 million from $369 million”; the company also refinanced all remaining 2027 mortgage maturities, leaving no debt maturities until 2028.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Leverage 8.8x annualized, liquidity $369M (3/31/26)” and expected the July refinancing to “clear[] all mortgage maturities to 2028.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $122.1 million, within the preview’s roughly $121–124 million consensus range and consistent with its low-to-mid-single-digit growth framing.
Q2 occupancy of 82.4%, up 230 basis points year over year, matched the already-released figure; July’s 30-basis-point sequential increase also matched the preview’s occupancy setup.
Consolidated RevPAR growth of 8.2% was within the preview’s approximately 8%–9% full-year guidance range.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $502–$516 million, the preview’s base case, rather than raised or cut.
Same-community labor expense improved to 45.2% of revenue from 46.1% a year earlier, consistent with the preview’s expectation of better Q2 flow-through.
The planned Q4 acquisition of 17 leased communities for approximately $157 million and its roughly $11 million 2027 adjusted EBITDA benefit were already described in the preview.
Refinancing the remaining 2027 mortgage maturities and leaving no debt maturities until 2028 matched the preview’s expectation for the July refinancing.

surprises.description: Revenue was $23 million, below the $24.88 million consensus. It also fell short of the preview’s expectation for roughly 3–7% core growth: the reported $23 million compares with about $24.8 million on a Q2 2025 pro forma basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $23 million”; it was “$24.8 million on a pro forma basis excluding divested businesses and nonrecurring license revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus was “$24.88M”; continuing-operations product revenue was estimated at “roughly $23–24M in Q2'25,” implying “~+3–7% core growth.”

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was substantially worse than expected: diluted EPS was -$0.07 versus the preview’s -$0.02 consensus. This was a larger loss than the preview’s base and bear scenarios anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 swung to a net loss of $9.4 million ($0.07 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 EPS consensus was “−$0.02”; the bear scenario projected “−$0.03 to −$0.04.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss was worse than expected and below even the preview’s bear-case threshold: the company reported a $2.7 million loss versus an estimated loss of $0.8–$1.2 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA turned to a $2.7 million loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~−$0.8M to −$1.2M”; its bear case was “adj. EBITDA worse than −$2M.”

surprises.description: The key biologics and wound-care lines remained weaker than the preview’s expected second-half pickup: management said legacy workhorse products and Amnio underperformed expectations and drove the biologics revenue miss. This challenges the recovery that the preview identified as an important H2 assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy ‘workhorse’ product lines (OsteoSelect, OsteoSponge, 3Demin) and the Amnio wound-care line underperformed expectations and were the main drivers of the biologics revenue miss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided to a “pickup again in the second half”; the preview called Q2 “the first checkpoint” for Amnio/advanced wound care and stem-cell recovery.

surprises.description: Liquidity was more constrained than the preview’s cash-decline warning alone suggested: cash fell below $10 million, while debt was $23 million and revolver availability was nearly exhausted. The preview had cited $12.2 million of debt and $11.8 million of revolver availability at Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash and equivalents were “$9.9 million” at June 30, with “total debt of $23 million and only $0.7 million of revolver availability remaining.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 cash of “$12.2M,” “$12.2M total debt,” and “$11.8M revolver availability”; it flagged a second cash decline as reopening the financing question.

surprises.description: Operating costs included a $5 million exclusive distribution fee to Dilon, a substantial reported expense alongside the preview’s estimate of roughly $2.5 million per quarter for the Dilon sales team. The fee contributed to the higher operating expenses and weaker profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses rose to $22.5 million from $19.7 million, largely due to a $5 million exclusive distribution fee paid to Dilon recorded as an operating expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “~21-person Dilon sales team adds roughly $2.5M per quarter in S&M.”

in_line: FY2026 revenue guidance was cut to $99–103 million from $101–105 million, matching the preview’s base-case expectation of a narrowing to approximately $99–103 million.
Gross margin of 57.9% was around the preview’s estimated 58% floor, though it was at the bottom of the expected range.

surprises.description: The preview modeled Q2 revenue of $254–258 million, implying 2.5–4% growth; reported revenue instead fell about 8% to $229 million. That is a large shortfall from the modeled range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue declined to $229 million from $248 million a year earlier,” roughly an 8% decrease.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Q2 FY2026 Model (base) … 254–258” and “Y/Y +2.5–4%.”

surprises.description: Mechanical Services was expected to be roughly flat, but revenue fell 11%. Turnaround revenues were down more than 50% as refining customers deferred maintenance, and the Middle East conflict and deferred work reduced first-half revenue by more than $20 million—far worse than the preview’s slippage debate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mechanical Services revenue dropped 11% to $97 million”; “Turnaround revenues are down more than 50% versus the prior year as refining customers deferred maintenance to capture strong crack spreads”; the Middle East conflict and deferred turnaround activity “negatively impacted first-half 2026 revenue by more than $20 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The model put Mechanical Services at “116–118” and “~flat”; the preview described turnaround work as “pushed later into 2026” and framed whether delays would land in 2H or be cancelled as a key debate.

surprises.description: Inspection and Heat Treating was modeled to grow 6–8%, but instead declined 5%, a clear reversal of the expected segment growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inspection and Heat Treating segment declined 5% to $131 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The model forecast IHT revenue of “138–141” and “+6–8%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was modeled at $26–27 million, but came in at $13.7 million, down sharply year over year. The shortfall is especially stark given the preview’s warning that below $24.5 million would put the full-year guide in question.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell sharply to $13.7 million from $24.5 million” because of weaker mix and fixed-cost deleveraging.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The model forecast “Adj. EBITDA … 26.0–27.0”; the preview also said “Below $24.5M (flat Y/Y) the FY guide is in question.”

surprises.description: The company reaffirmed its full-year ranges, as the preview’s base case anticipated, but said it now expects results toward the lower half. That is weaker positioning than the preview’s preference for a raise or a range narrowed toward the top half.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance” for revenue of $920–945 million, gross profit of $240–260 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $68–73 million, “but expects results toward the lower half of these ranges.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a reaffirm is neutral-to-slightly-negative” and that “the buy-side wants the revenue range nudged up or the EBITDA range narrowed to the top half.” Its base scenario assumed the FY guide would be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: The new cost program was larger on an annualized basis than the preview’s base-case estimate, with a stated full run-rate date and quantified second-half benefit. The preview had expected an $8–12 million run-rate in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: The new structural cost improvement program targets “$20 million to $35 million of annualized savings,” with full run-rate expected by 2027 and “$8 million to $15 million of benefit in the second half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected a “cost program $8–12M run-rate”; the preview also said the program was expected to be quantified in this release.

surprises.description: The preview looked for positive Q2 operating cash flow, but the company used cash instead. The use was small, while reported liquidity was above the preview’s stated level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow slightly negative at $0.7 million used”; quarter-end total liquidity was approximately $51.2 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Look for positive Q2 operating cash flow” and cited “~$49.2M total liquidity.”

surprises.description: Stellex became the company’s largest common-equity shareholder in a negotiated transaction at a significant premium, buying out CORE Partners. The preview did not anticipate this ownership change, and the facts provided do not establish its broader implications for shareholders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stellex Capital Management became Team’s largest common equity shareholder through a negotiated transaction at a significant premium, buying out prior shareholder CORE Partners.”

surprises.description: Management set a target of more than 10% year-over-year growth in several newer verticals and described additional senior operational and people leadership appointments to support the transformation. The preview did not flag these targets or appointments.
surprises.fact_evidence: Team is “targeting more than 10% year-over-year growth in new verticals including LNG, aerospace, commercial nuclear power, and pulp and paper,” with an incoming COO, CHRO, and SVP of Operational Excellence supporting the transformation.

in_line: Management reaffirmed the existing FY2026 guidance ranges rather than raising or cutting them, consistent with the preview’s base-case expectation of a reaffirmation; the lower-half outlook was a negative qualification.

surprises.description: JBI cut its 2026 revenue outlook to $925–$945 million, below the preview’s $940–$980 million company guidance range and below its $957.4 million consensus estimate. The cut also puts the new range below the prior guidance floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $925–$945 million, citing weaker-than-expected demand.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 guide: Rev $940–980M”; FY26 revenue consensus was “$957.4M.” The preview said a cut below “$940M revenue” was the bear trigger.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was below the preview’s estimated $42–$45 million range, and the 17.2% margin fell short of the expected roughly 17.6%–18.7% range. This left the quarter’s profitability weaker than the already reduced consensus outlook implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 18% to $40.2 million, compressing margin by roughly 430 basis points to 17.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (my est. of Street): ~$42–45M”; implied margin “~17.6–18.7%.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in below the preview’s roughly $238.8 million consensus, with 2.4% year-over-year growth instead of the expected 4.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $233.5 million, up 2.4% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue estimate was “~$238.8M” with expected YoY growth of “+4.7%.”

surprises.description: The company now expects North American organic self-storage revenue to decline high single digits, worse than the preview’s expectation of a mid-single-digit decline. That is also weaker than the preview’s stated confirmation threshold that results not be tracking worse than mid-single digits down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North American organic self-storage revenue is now guided to decline high single digits versus 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had “guided NA organic self-storage down mid-single digits”; the preview said to confirm it was “not tracking worse.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was well below the preview’s roughly $40 million watch level. The strong trailing conversion and full-year conversion outlook temper the shortfall, but do not change that the quarter missed the preview’s cash-flow expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was $21.6 million”; trailing-12-month free cash flow conversion of adjusted net income was 129%, and full-year conversion was guided to the higher end of the 75%–100% range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “FCF ≥ ~$40M” and described sustained FCF conversion as keeping the balance sheet out of the debate.

surprises.description: Commercial and other revenue fell sharply rather than returning to growth as the preview said was guided for 2026. The 21.2% decline was a substantially weaker outcome than the preview’s hoped-for inflection from Q1’s slight decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The commercial and other segment revenue dropped 21.2% year-over-year,” primarily from continued softness in commercial sheet doors.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Commercial & Other was “guided to return to growth in 2026” and called Q2 “the proof point.”

surprises.description: The expected contribution from the KB2/Kiwi construction acquisition was lowered by about $10 million because projects were delayed and timelines extended. The preview had treated the acquisition as roughly $90 million annualized and used an estimated $22–$25 million of Q2 inorganic revenue in its organic-versus-inorganic framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: The acquisition’s inorganic revenue contribution was lowered to “approximately $80-$90 million (about an $10 million cut) due to project delays and extended timelines, though no cancellations occurred.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Kiwi II as “~$90M annualized” and estimated Q2 inorganic revenue at “~$22–25M.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted that Nokia smart entry had passed 500,000 installed units and said this scale should support recurring revenue and better profitability over time; it also set Q4 factory availability for Nokia Infinity on roll-up and swing doors. The preview had noted installed-unit growth and new SKUs but did not flag this installation milestone or the specific factory-install timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company surpassed 500,000 installed Nokia smart-entry units,” an inflection point management expects to support recurring revenue and improved profitability over time. “Nokia Infinity” is expected to be available for factory install starting in Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Installed units +24.2% YoY in Q1; new Infinitē and Ion SKUs” and said the business was “Small financially.”

in_line: Net leverage was 2.7x, matching the preview’s stated 2.7x level and remaining within the company’s 2–3x target range.

surprises.description: Helios raised FY2026 sales guidance to $880–$900 million and adjusted EPS to $3.05–$3.25, above the preview’s base-case raise to $855–$875 million and $2.90–$3.05. The new ranges reached the preview’s bull-case threshold, with the EPS high end exceeding its bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 sales guidance to $880-$900 million” and “adjusted EPS to $3.05-$3.25.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the FY guide to be “$855–875M / $2.90–3.05”; its bull case called for “$880–900M / $3.05–3.20.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.88 was materially above both the $0.80 consensus and the preview’s $0.85 estimate, and beat the top of company guidance by five cents. This was a stronger earnings beat than the preview’s expected “good” quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.88 grew 49% and exceeded the high end of guidance by $0.05.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted diluted EPS consensus at “$0.80” and its estimate at “$0.85”; guidance was “$0.78–0.83.”

surprises.description: Profitability exceeded the preview’s margin expectations: adjusted EBITDA margin reached 21.2%, above both its 20.4% consensus and 20.8% estimate. Gross margin also expanded 280 basis points, with only about $1 million of net tariff refunds contributing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 280 basis points to 34.6%” and “adjusted EBITDA margin reached 21.2%, up 260 basis points”; gross-margin expansion was “aided by roughly $1 million of net IEEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated adjusted EBITDA margin at “20.8%” versus consensus of “~20.4%.” It also said to strip out any IEEPA refund if recognized, noting “~$4M of potential IEEPA refunds excluded from guidance.”

surprises.description: Electronics underperformed the preview’s Q2 expectations: sales were $86 million rather than about $88 million, and operating income was $11 million rather than consensus of $12.9 million or the preview’s $13.7 million estimate. The 13.1% operating margin was also below the 14.7% consensus margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Electronics sales grew 19% to $86 million with operating income nearly doubling to $11 million and operating margin expanding 490 basis points to 13.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put Electronics consensus at “$87.8M” and its estimate at “$88M”; consensus operating income and margin were “$12.9M (14.7% mgn)” and its estimate was “$13.7M.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook points to a sharper near-term slowdown than the preview’s bullish H2-reset scenario: adjusted EPS is guided to just 2% growth at the midpoint and adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to fall 30 basis points. Electronics growth is also expected to slow to about 5% as comparisons get tougher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance implies decelerating momentum, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.8%-20.6% (down 30 bps at midpoint) and adjusted EPS of $0.70-$0.77 (up only 2% at midpoint)”; management guided Q3 Electronics growth of “only ~5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case required management to break H2 conservatism, with “H2 to be roughly in line with H1”; its electronics watch item identified “holding $89M+ and 15.5%+” as a beat vector.

surprises.description: Data-center cooling interest appears unusually large and close to an initial order, but the timing is later than the preview’s anticipated H2 2026 ramp: management included no 2026 revenue and described only a gradual ramp from 2027. The scale and customer activity are encouraging, while the revenue schedule is a setback to the preview’s timing expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management called data-center thermal-management couplings “the single largest opportunity across Helios,” potentially larger than combined ag and construction markets; samples are out to “about a dozen customers” and an order is expected “imminently,” but “no 2026 revenue is included in guidance” and only a gradual ramp is modeled from 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described an “H2 2026 ramp expected” and said quantification of the pipeline or design wins would be a key upside signal.

surprises.description: Order momentum did not soften: double-digit year-over-year intake continued for a fourth consecutive quarter, and July set a company record for both monthly revenue and order intake. That is stronger than merely avoiding the deceleration the preview identified as its main bear trigger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Order intake grew double digits year-over-year for the fourth straight quarter, with July marking the best-ever monthly revenue and order intake.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called months 13–15 of order data “the single best leading indicator” and said softening from “double-digit” to “solid” or “normalizing” would be a bear trigger.

surprises.description: The balance sheet improved beyond the preview’s Q1 baseline, with net leverage falling to 1.4x from 1.6x and below the company’s target range. Management consequently shifted priorities away from debt reduction toward organic growth, buybacks, and M&A; the company had returned $18 million year-to-date, including $6 million of buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt fell to $264 million, the lowest since Q3 2020,” leverage improved to “1.4x from 2.6x a year ago,” and the company is “shifting capital priorities away from debt paydown toward organic growth, buybacks and M&A.” It returned “$18 million to shareholders year-to-date,” including “$6 million of buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 net debt of “$284.2M,” leverage of “1.6x,” and said “M&A capacity is real” with “~$82M remaining on buyback.”

in_line: Q2 sales of $232 million landed at the high end of the $227–$232 million guidance range and were close to the preview’s $230.4 million consensus and $233 million estimate.

The preview expected order-intake commentary to remain a key indicator after 12 months of double-digit growth; management confirmed double-digit growth continued, even though the record July activity was an additional positive.

surprises.description: TONX generated only about $0.5 million of operating income, far below the preview’s estimate of roughly $9–10 million. The call attributed part of the gap to a $5.5 million accelerated non-cash stock-compensation charge and a $2.9 million non-cash Kingsway-related charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company achieved positive operating income of approximately $0.5 million despite absorbing a $5.5 million accelerated non-cash stock compensation charge and a $2.9 million non-cash Kingsway-related charge.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating income ~+$9–10M, the company's first positive operating quarter.”

surprises.description: The fair-value gain and pre-tax earnings were materially below the preview’s mark-driven forecast: TONX reported an $82.8 million non-cash gain and $83.5 million of pre-tax income, versus a preview estimate of about $115 million for the gain and $110–135 million for GAAP net income. The preview’s estimates depended on an estimated June 30 Gram price, so the comparison is uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income before taxes was approximately $83.5 million … largely due to an $82.8 million non-cash gain from fair value changes in gram holdings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP net income (+$110M to +$135M)” and “unrealized gain ≈ +$115M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $15 million, slightly below the preview’s $16–18 million estimate, although it was far above the $2.14 million consensus figure the preview warned was unreliable. The preview expected $1–1.5 million of residual legacy revenue in addition to staking revenue, while the call said the revenue increase was entirely driven by higher staking rewards.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose to $15 million in Q2 from $3 million in Q1, entirely driven by higher staking rewards.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … My Estimate: $16–18M”; “$15–16M staking revenue, plus ~ $1–1.5M residual legacy revenue.”

surprises.description: The wind-down savings appear later than the preview’s Q2 cost assumptions suggested: the company expects $4–5 million of annual operating-cost savings, with most of the benefit not visible until Q4. That timing leaves less cost reduction in the near term than the preview’s modeled Q2 operating-cost decline implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The wind-down of legacy VERB operations is expected to remove approximately $4-5 million of annual operating costs, with the majority of savings becoming visible in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating: ~$16–17M revenue … less ~$6–7M opex (down from ~$7.9M in Q1 on the wind-down).”

in_line: The June 30 holding of approximately 230.5 million Gram matched the figure the preview identified as already disclosed.

The approximately 17% annualized Q2 staking yield was broadly consistent with the preview’s estimate of about 16% for June; management’s warning that current staking economics may not persist also addressed the sustainability risk the preview had flagged.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $60.7 million, above the preview’s $56–58 million estimate. That was a stronger quarter than expected and a 12% sequential increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached $60.7 million, a 12% sequential increase driven by growth in both the Rockies and Mid-Con segments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … my estimate $56–58M.”

surprises.description: Management tightened full-year EBITDA guidance to $235–255 million while keeping the $245 million midpoint. The preview expected the range to be held, so narrowing it around the midpoint was more reassuring than the base case’s softened midpoint language.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management tightened full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $235-255 million (midpoint $245 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … guidance range held with midpoint language softened to ‘within the range’”; the preview also said the midpoint was $245 million.

surprises.description: Full-year capital expenditure guidance rose to $100–120 million, above the preview’s $85–105 million range. That is a meaningful increase in planned spending, even though the facts provided do not specify what drove the revision.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Raising] capital expenditure guidance to $100-120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY capex vs. the $85–105M guide.”

surprises.description: Rockies activity was stronger than the preview’s five-rig expectation: the rig count rose to eight, including six in Williston, and the company secured about 30 additional Williston connections beyond original guidance. Those connections are weighted to Q4 and are expected to add roughly $10 million of EBITDA in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rig count behind the Rockies system rose to 8 (6 in Williston, 2 in DJ) from 5 in the prior quarter, the highest Williston activity in several years”; “approximately 30 new Williston well connections not in original guidance … expected to contribute roughly $10 million of EBITDA in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~80 DUCs behind the systems and 5 rigs running”; the preview also described a Q2 guide of about 40 connects.

surprises.description: The Double E expansion was assigned a sub-6x build multiple, providing a favorable economic marker that the preview said had not been publicly framed. The preview had anticipated an FID discussion but highlighted the absence of project economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The mainline compression expansion open season [was] extended through August and an FID [is] expected in the coming weeks at a sub-6x build multiple.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The number that has never been publicly framed is the expansion capex and SMC's share of the JV funding”; the preview also called for FID ‘by end of summer.’

surprises.description: Piceance faces a more clearly quantified near-term cash-flow decline than the preview’s general flat-to-down outlook: MVC shortfall payments of about $4 million per quarter expire starting in Q4, leaving an expected 2027 run-rate of roughly $4–4.5 million per quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Piceance segment faces a cash flow step-down starting Q4 as ~$4 million/quarter in MVC shortfall payments expire, implying a normalized run-rate of about $4-4.5 million per quarter for 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Piceance … Structural decliner. … Assume flat-to-down.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased only about $1 million of shares, roughly 3% of the $35 million authorization, while management said debt reduction and dividend reinstatement take priority over buybacks. The preview flagged whether buybacks would occur but did not anticipate such limited use of the authorization or this explicit ranking.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased ~35,000 shares for $1 million under its $35 million buyback authorization, leaving ~$34 million remaining, with management prioritizing debt reduction and dividend reinstatement over buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether any buyback was actually executed in Q2”; the preview also listed deleveraging, Double E growth capex, buybacks, and dividend initiation as capital-allocation priorities to watch.

in_line: Double E contracted volume reached just over 1.9 Bcf/day, in line with the preview’s expectation of approximately 1.9 Bcf/d; an FID expected in the coming weeks is also consistent with the preview’s end-of-summer timing.
Management expects to resume a common dividend in the near future, consistent with the preview’s expectation that a dividend was achievable in the near term.
The $245 million full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint was maintained, as the preview identified that midpoint as the central test.

surprises.description: KLX announced a $125 million backstopped equity rights offering, which the preview did not anticipate. It is expected to guarantee at least $94 million of deleveraging and reduce net leverage to about 2.7x; management also said the balance-sheet actions and lease roll-off should improve 2027 free cash flow by about $20 million, including $11–14 million of annual interest savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “KLX announced a $125 million backstopped equity rights offering that guarantees at least $94 million of deleveraging and would cut net leverage to approximately 2.7x”; the actions plus lease roll-off are projected to improve 2027 free cash flow by about $20 million.

surprises.description: Against expectations of a flat market and a preview that sought a quantified Q3 growth outlook, KLX guided to $176–188 million of revenue, with a midpoint of $182 million. Management characterized this as mid-single-digit base-business growth, a clearer and stronger outlook than a non-committal seasonal recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $176-188 million (midpoint $182 million) implies a $15 million sequential increase and mid-single-digit base-business growth against flat market expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bull case requires ... explicit Q3 sequential growth guide”; the preview also described the base case as “H2 language constructive but non-committal.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $18.7 million slightly exceeded the preview’s $16–18 million estimate range, and the 11.2% margin was just above its implied 10–11% range. This was a modest beat rather than the larger recovery implied by the preview’s bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 68% sequentially to $18.7 million, expanding margins ~350 basis points to 11.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$16–18M (implied, est.)” and “Adj. EBITDA margin ~10–11% (implied).”

surprises.description: Reported diluted loss per share was $0.41, better than the preview’s $0.82 loss estimate, but the improvement was partly attributable to a nonrecurring bargain-purchase gain rather than adjusted operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $8 million ($0.41 per share) ... aided by a nonrecurring $6.5 million bargain purchase gain excluded from adjusted results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: –$0.82.”

surprises.description: Northeast/Mid-Con profitability was stronger than the preview’s expectation that the segment would hold around a 20–21% margin: its adjusted EBITDA margin reached 24%, with EBITDA up 74% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Northeast/Mid-Con segment posted the strongest profitability at 24% adjusted EBITDA margin with EBITDA up 74% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Northeast/Mid-Con was at “~21% margin” in Q1 and the bull case required it to “hold ~20% margins.”

surprises.description: KLX reported that WolfPack, acquired during the quarter, contributed $3.4 million in June—about a $41 million annual run rate—and raised its synergy target to roughly $2.5 million. The preview discussed M&A only as a possible wildcard and did not anticipate this acquisition’s contribution or updated synergy target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The WolfPack acquisition, closed June 2, contributed $3.4 million in June (implying a ~$41 million annual run rate) and its synergy target was raised to ~$2.5 million.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s emphasis on structurally strong gas basins and improving Haynesville activity, KLX said natural gas had fallen to about 15% of revenue after losing a Haynesville customer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Natural gas fell to about 15% of revenue due to a lost Haynesville customer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Gas basins are structurally strong (Haynesville rigs +35% YoY; Western Haynesville wells are service-intensive).”

surprises.description: Management identified Q3 as the expected liquidity low point, tempering the preview’s expectation that cash generation would normalize in the second half. Quarter-end liquidity was $53.3 million, above the preview’s $50 million watch threshold, but the call did not report the positive free cash flow the preview was looking for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarter-end total debt stood at $288.9 million against total liquidity of $53.3 million ... with Q3 now expected to mark the liquidity low point.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “cash generation normalizes in H2 as receivables convert” and called for “liquidity ≥$50M and positive FCF.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $167.3 million, near the $167 million midpoint of company guidance and the preview’s $167.5 million consensus estimate.
KLX elected to PIK 100% of interest in Q2 and expected to do so in Q3 before moving to a 50-50 cash/PIK mix in Q4, matching the preview’s description of management’s plan.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 EBITDAX of $170–180 million. First-half EBITDAX was about $281 million; subtracting the preview’s Q1 actual of $133.5 million implies Q2 EBITDAX of roughly $147.5 million, materially below that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: HighPeak generated “approximately $281 million of EBITDAX in the first half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 base case estimated “EBITDAX” at “$170–180M.”

surprises.description: The preview modeled Q2 capital spending of about $84 million, but the reported first-half total implies Q2 spending of roughly $107.5 million after subtracting Q1’s $78.4 million. Management said spending was front-loaded and expects a meaningful decline in the second half, so the higher Q2 spend reflects timing rather than necessarily an increase to the annual budget.
surprises.fact_evidence: First-half capital spending “totaled $185.9 million,” with management expecting capital to “decline meaningfully in the second half” after front-loading “roughly mid-to-upper 60% of the annual budget.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 capex at “~$84M.”

surprises.description: The preview said management had prioritized debt reduction and expected about $60 million of quarterly free cash flow to move gross debt lower. Instead, management cautioned against prepaying the term loan above its required $30 million per quarter, emphasizing a cash cushion because prepaid amounts cannot be re-borrowed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management signaled “caution on prepaying the term loan above $30 million per quarter because the loan cannot be re-borrowed,” prioritizing “a cash cushion for 2027 and beyond”; mandatory amortization of “$30 million per quarter begins at the end of Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “explicitly prioritized debt reduction” and expected “a ~$60M FCF quarter” to take gross debt toward “~$1.12–1.14B.”

surprises.description: The preview modeled oil at about 30.5 thousand barrels per day, roughly 68% of expected production, and described HPK as a 68%-oil-weighted producer. Q2 oil weighting was only 64%, although management attributed the dip to fracing high-oil-cut wells and reactivating older, higher-gas-cut wells and expects it to return near 67%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oil weighting fell to 64% in Q2 from the guided 67%-68% range” due to fracing high-oil-cut wells and reactivating higher-gas-cut older wells; management expects to return near 67% for the rest of the year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described HPK as “a 68%-oil Midland Basin pure-play” and estimated Q2 oil production at “~30.5” thousand barrels per day.

surprises.description: The preview questioned whether Q1’s unusually low LOE was sustainable or a favorable-timing artifact. First-half LOE remained about 13% below the midpoint of full-year guidance even with an expanded workover program, offering evidence that costs stayed below guidance, though the first-half average was higher than Q1’s $6.53 per BOE.
surprises.fact_evidence: First-half unit LOE “averaged $7.56 per BOE, approximately 13% below the midpoint of full-year guidance, despite an expanded workover program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 LOE of “$6.53/BoE” raised the question of whether it was “a structural run-rate or a favorable-timing artifact.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated gas pricing but did not anticipate the improvement in Waha differentials. Management reported that pipeline expansions had moved Waha from roughly negative $3–$5 per MCF to near negative $1, pointing to better gas realizations through the first half of 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Waha gas differentials improved from roughly negative $3-$5/MCF to near negative $1/MCF following pipeline expansions,” versus HighPeak’s negative $1.50 realized in Q2, with better realizations expected through the first half of 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled gas at “~$2.00” and noted that Waha gas pricing was estimated, without flagging the pipeline-driven differential improvement.

in_line: Q2 production was essentially flat with Q1 and above the formal guidance range, broadly matching the preview’s estimate of about 45 MBoe/d and its expectation of another quarter above the 41–44 MBoe/d guide.

Net cash hedge losses of approximately $55 million were within the preview’s $45–55 million estimate; the reported mid-$60s oil-hedge positioning was also consistent with its expectation of capped oil prices and substantial hedge losses.

surprises.description: Q2 spending and cash burn came in well below the preview’s estimates: R&D was $1.5 million versus an expected $2.4–3.0 million, G&A was $1.3 million versus $1.9–2.1 million, and operating cash burn was $3.0 million versus $3.8–4.5 million. The lower burn is favorable for near-term cash needs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 R&D expenses rose to $1.5 million”; “G&A fell about 20% to $1.3 million”; “quarterly operating cash burn dropped to $3.0 million from $4.0 million in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 R&D of “$2.4–3.0M,” G&A of “$1.9–2.1M,” and operating cash burn of “$3.8–4.5M.”

surprises.description: Management said the $6.9 million cash balance only funds operations through year-end and that additional capital will be needed to complete the Phase 3 trial and support G&A. This makes the future financing and dilution need explicit, though the preview had already highlighted solvency risk and the financing overhang.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company had “only $6.9 million in cash and cash equivalents” at June 30, providing runway “only through the end of the year”; management “will need additional capital to fully execute the Phase 3 trial and support G&A needs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called June 30 unrestricted cash and going-concern language “the single binary for the day,” and described the base case as financing “bridging to a partnership with no date.”

surprises.description: The disclosed June financing structure was less dilutive than the preview’s unresolved terms left open: it used non-redeemable, non-convertible preferred stock and secured notes with no warrants. That reduces the immediate dilution concern, even though the company still expects to need future capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: The financing was structured with “non-redeemable, non-convertible preferred stock and secured promissory notes with no warrants to minimize shareholder dilution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the full financing terms were “not fully disclosed” and specifically identified possible “warrant coverage, share-settlement features, redemption triggers” as matters to confirm.

surprises.description: The call said Phase 3 interim analyses are event-driven and will begin only after full enrollment. That is a less near-term catalyst setup than the preview’s discussion of two planned interim analyses and its hope for timing guidance on the first one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Phase 3 interim analyses are event-driven and will begin only after full enrollment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Two pre-planned interims with potential for early BLA filing” and said “Timing guidance for the first interim would give the equity a datable catalyst.”

surprises.description: The call added a favorable safety update not covered in the preview: across the clinical programs, including Phase 3, the company reported no cytokine release syndrome, systemic toxicities, or serious immune-related adverse events, and the IDMC found no new safety concerns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Across all clinical programs, including the Phase 3, no cytokine release syndrome, no systemic toxicities, and no serious immune-related adverse events have been observed,” and an IDMC review found “no new safety concerns.”

in_line: Ovation 2’s reported overall-survival improvements matched the preview’s cited final data: 14.7 months in the all-comers population and 24.2 months among patients receiving PARP inhibitor maintenance.
The MRD-trial results matched the preview’s cited figures, including 44% versus 67% MRD positivity and 87.5% versus about 62.5% ctDNA clearance.
Ovation 3 enrollment of approximately 0.5 patients per site per month was consistent with the preview’s report that enrollment was ahead of plan and running above the 0.3 planned rate.
The Phase 3 full-enrollment timeline extending into the first half of 2029 was broadly consistent with the preview’s Q2 2029 completion estimate.

surprises.description: Absci reported $201.1 million of cash, equivalents, and marketable securities, slightly above the preview’s $190–200 million estimate, and said runway now extends into the second half of 2028 rather than the preview’s base-case expectation of into the first half of 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash, equivalents, and marketable securities were $201.1 million as of June 30, 2026, and the strengthened balance sheet extends operating runway into the second half of 2028.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2-end cash of ~$190–200M” and the base case expected runway “into 1H 2028.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the planned Q4 endometriosis Phase 2 start but did not anticipate an expansion of the trial. Absci said the stronger balance sheet supports expanding the planned study, although it did not specify the added scope.
surprises.fact_evidence: The strengthened balance sheet “supports an expansion of the planned endometriosis trial.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “Phase 2 endometriosis initiation (guided Q4 2026)” and described the Q4 start, but did not mention expanding the trial.

surprises.description: The preview said quantitative prolactin suppression or target-engagement data were still outstanding. Absci now says modeling indicates that two to three doses over six months could achieve greater than 90% prolactin-receptor occupancy, which management contrasts with a competitor’s modeled 60–70% occupancy; this is a model-based claim, not reported clinical occupancy data.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New modeling suggests 2 to 3 doses over 6 months can achieve greater than 90% prolactin receptor occupancy”; management said HMI-115 reached only “60-70%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that the June release gave “no quantitative prolactin suppression or target-engagement data” and that “the pharmacodynamic proof is still outstanding.”

surprises.description: The preview characterized Lilly’s $40 million investment as passive equity with no option rights. The call confirmed Lilly has no rights to ABS-201, but disclosed that Lilly will place a representative on Absci’s Endometriosis Advisory Board, adding a limited advisory connection that the preview did not describe.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Eli Lilly partnership does not confer any rights to ABS-201,” but Lilly “will place a representative on Absci’s Endometriosis Advisory Board.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the $40 million was “an equity investment, not a partnership with option rights” and described the investment as “currently priced as passive capital.”

surprises.description: Absci gave a specific U.S. total-addressable-market estimate of more than $25 billion for Pattern Hair Loss, a figure not provided in the preview. The preview did discuss ABS-201 market potential through analyst sales estimates, so this is a new company market-sizing disclosure rather than evidence of a changed indication.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Absci estimates a U.S. total addressable market greater than $25 billion for Pattern Hair Loss.”

in_line: The interim 13-week Pattern Hair Loss proof-of-concept readout remained expected in the second half of 2026, with full 26-week proof-of-concept data expected in early 2027.
The Phase 2 endometriosis study was still anticipated to begin in Q4 2026, consistent with the preview.
Q2 R&D of $22.6 million and SG&A of $9.2 million were within the preview’s respective estimates of $21–23 million and $9–10 million.
The $100 million financing, including Lilly’s $40 million equity investment, had already been disclosed and was expected by the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $7.9 million, well below the preview’s roughly $13 million base estimate and even slightly below its $8–11 million bear-case range. The preview already expected a large miss against $23.03 million consensus, but the reported result was weaker than its low-end central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell approximately 25% year-over-year to $7.9 million” and “rose 17% sequentially from Q1's $6.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 base estimate: ~$13M”; the base scenario was “Revenue $12–15M,” and the bear scenario was “$8–11M.”

surprises.description: Management cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $60–75 million, far below the preview’s suggested possible reset to about $90–100 million. The preview focused on delivery and feedstock timing as the main risks, whereas management attributed the reduction entirely to lower antimony prices.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $60 million-$75 million, attributing the reduction entirely to lower antimony prices rather than delivery delays.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A clean cut to ~$90–100M with a credible shipment schedule may actually be received better than another unbacked reaffirmation”; the preview also said the guide might be cut or withdrawn and highlighted Bolivian feedstock delays.

surprises.description: Antimony gross margin fell to 7%, below the preview’s base-case 15–20% range and its stated Q1 margin of 16%. Selling prices fell much faster than costs, squeezing profitability despite higher pounds sold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Antimony average selling prices dropped roughly 52% year-over-year to $13.70 per pound,” while “average cost per pound fell only 33% to $13.34,” compressing “gross margin to 7% from 27% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called gross margin a key metric, citing “Q1 was 16%” and a base case of “GM 15–20%.”

surprises.description: The first DLA shipments did not contribute their expected roughly $2.6 million to Q2 revenue: although delivered in June, they were accepted only in July, shifting recognition to Q3. The preview had highlighted the June invoice and included approximately $2.6 million of DLA revenue in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The first two DLA shipments (~82,000 pounds, ~$2.6 million) were delivered in June but only accepted in July, pushing recognition into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the 82,000 pounds were “generating ~$2.6M invoiced in June,” and its base scenario assumed “~$2.6M DLA.”

surprises.description: Physical volumes were stronger than the preview’s concern that the Bolivia feedstock disruption would clip volumes: antimony pounds sold rose, and zeolite sales and tonnage more than doubled. That volume strength contrasts with the revenue decline, which was driven mainly by lower antimony prices.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Antimony pounds sold rose 26% year-over-year to 428,425 pounds and zeolite revenue grew 110% to $1.9 million on a 114% increase in tons sold.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Bolivian feedstock deliveries were delayed during the quarter by diesel shortages” and its base scenario said “Bolivia delay clips volumes.”

surprises.description: Despite an approximately $7 million operating loss, UAMY reported about $0.1 million of net income because of a $6.8 million unrealized gain on its Larvotto investment. The preview expected a large Larvotto mark-to-market hit in Q2 and modeled a net loss in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted an operating loss of about $7 million” but “reported positive net income of about $0.1 million thanks to a $6.8 million unrealized gain on its Larvotto Resources investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a $4.1M mark-to-market loss on the Larvotto equity stake” was among items expected to recur in Q2; its base scenario projected EPS of “–$0.04 to –$0.02.”

surprises.description: The company built inventory substantially, using $20.7 million of operating cash to stockpile feedstock. The preview considered liquidity ample but did not flag this level of inventory accumulation or operating cash use.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory built intentionally to $21.6 million from $6.4 million a year earlier, driving $20.7 million of cash used in operations,” as the company stockpiled low-cost feedstock for DLA and commercial demand.

surprises.description: The first $9.9 million DLA delivery order is now expected to be completed nearly a year ahead of schedule, a faster contract conversion timeline than the preview anticipated. The preview highlighted the $57.3 million of cumulative orders and the need for shipment cadence, but did not forecast this accelerated completion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The first $9.9 million delivery order expected to complete nearly a year ahead of schedule.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “total DLA orders received since contract inception … $57.3M” and asked for a “dated 2H DLA shipment schedule”; it did not state that the first delivery order would finish ahead of schedule.

in_line: Cumulative DLA orders of approximately $57.3 million matched the preview’s cited total order value.
Liquidity remained ample, consistent with the preview’s assessment that near-term liquidity was not the risk; it had already noted substantial post-quarter financing.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $14.9 million, above the preview’s roughly $13.8 million consensus and contrary to its expected year-over-year decline: revenue was roughly flat versus $15.3 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $14.9 million, roughly flat versus $15.3 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue ~ $13.8M”; the preview said this implied “−10%” year over year.

surprises.description: The net loss narrowed to $12 million, better than the preview’s roughly $13 million implied loss. The reported reductions in R&D and SG&A accompanied the improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $12 million from $13.3 million a year earlier”; R&D fell to $11.7 million from $13.8 million and SG&A to $10.9 million from $12.3 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied net loss ~$13M”; Q2 EPS consensus was “~$(0.12).”

surprises.description: Product gross margin reached 73%, above the preview’s roughly 70% sustainability benchmark, and management raised its full-year gross-margin outlook to the high 60s.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product gross margin reached 73% in Q2 2026” and management raised full-year 2026 gross-margin guidance “to the high 60s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sustainability at or near 70% supports the ‘stable and profitable core’ framing”; the bull case called for product gross margin “held ≥70%.”

surprises.description: The cash runway was extended through 2028, beyond the preview’s expectation that the company was funded through the end of 2027. The roughly $79.8 million pro forma cash balance itself was within the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: The $25 million net equity financing lifted pro forma cash to “approximately $79.8 million” and extended the runway “through 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the prior “through end-2027” runway language and expected pro forma cash of “~$75–80M.”

surprises.description: A CDMO partner has advanced beyond the small-scale transfer stage: its assessment is complete and long-term commercial contract negotiations are expected to wrap up soon. The preview identified conversion to a commercial arrangement as a key catalyst but did not report negotiations this advanced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The most advanced has finished its assessment and is now in long-term commercial contract negotiations expected to wrap up soon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market needed “paid, revenue-generating conversions” and called for watching for a partner “converting from evaluation to license”; its bull case required a partnership “signed or imminent.”

surprises.description: The biocatalysis business reported four product approvals in 2026 plus a label expansion, ending a multi-year drought of new approvals—an additional development beyond the preview’s description of a stable legacy business.
surprises.fact_evidence: The business supports 14 commercial products, “including four that received approval in 2026 plus one label expansion, ending a multi-year drought of new approvals.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a substantial clinical pipeline and a longer-term growth outlook: 15 Phase 2 or 3 programs, seven expected trial readouts over two years, and projected high-single-digit growth over five to seven years. The preview did not include this pipeline-based outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The clinical pipeline includes 15 programs in Phase 2 or 3 development with data readouts expected on seven trials over the next two years, supporting projected high-single-digit growth over five to seven years.”

surprises.description: Management added a particularly bullish siRNA manufacturing-demand and cost-efficiency case not covered in the preview: it expects demand to grow 30-fold by 2035, sees a bottleneck within three years, and says Ecosynthesis is roughly 70% more capital efficient than solid-phase synthesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “siRNA demand to grow 30-fold by 2035,” projects “a manufacturing bottleneck within three years,” and claims Ecosynthesis is “roughly 70% more capital efficient than solid-phase synthesis.”

surprises.description: The permit had not yet been submitted by the time of the call: management said submission was imminent, whereas the preview expected the building permit to be filed in Q2. Equipment had already been ordered, but that does not change the permit timing difference.
surprises.fact_evidence: The facility had “permit submission imminent and equipment already ordered.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “building permit filed in Q2” as a scale-up target.

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $72–76 million, as the preview expected, and reiterated that the year is heavily weighted to the second half.
The July financing and pro forma cash balance were broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of a completed raise and roughly $75–80 million of pro forma cash.
The year-end half-kilo scale target was consistent with the preview’s 0.5 kg production-scale target.

surprises.description: GrowGeneration raised its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook from roughly breakeven to $2–3 million, a substantial improvement over the preview’s baseline expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $2-3 million, up from a prior expectation of roughly breakeven.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA — ~breakeven.”

surprises.description: The company said an AIPA tariff refund exceeding $2 million is expected to boost Q3 and back-half EBITDA. The preview did not anticipate this benefit, so the improved EBITDA outlook includes a material, apparently one-off contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Back-half EBITDA is being boosted by an AIPA tariff refund exceeding $2 million expected to be recognized in Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $44–46 million implies a year-over-year decline, whereas the preview said reaffirming the full-year revenue guide would imply flat-to-up second-half comparisons. Management attributed the Q3 decline to unusually large durable-goods sales a year ago and expects higher margins this year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $44-46 million implies a year-over-year decline,” attributed to “unusually large durable-goods sales in Q3 2025” rather than weakening demand, with “higher margins this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirm means management sees flat-to-up 2H comps.”

surprises.description: Proprietary brands reached 39.7% of cultivation and gardening revenue by Q2, hitting the company’s roughly 40% full-year target halfway through the year. The preview expected that level before Q4, so the target was reached ahead of schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Proprietary brand sales reached approximately 40% of cultivation and gardening revenue (39.7%), up from 32% a year earlier, hitting the company's full-year target halfway through the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “37.0% in Q1, targeting ~40% before Q4.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 28.5%, above the preview’s 27–28% base-case range and at the preview’s 28.5% bull-case threshold. It was also within the company’s 27–29% guidance, so the recovery was better than the base case rather than outside the guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 28.5%, a 310 basis point sequential improvement from 25.4% and slightly above 28.3% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base ... GM 27–28%”; “Bull ... GM ≥28.5%”; company guidance was “27–29%.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $43.2 million exceeded the preview’s cited $42.41 million consensus, though it remained within the preview’s expected in-line range of $42.5–43.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $43.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $42.41M (Investing.com)”; the base scenario expected “$42.5–43.5M (in line).”

surprises.description: The GAAP loss was $0.03 per share, one cent better than the preview’s cited $0.04-per-share consensus and also better than its expected roughly $0.05-per-share outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss narrowed to $2 million (-$0.03 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted): –$0.04”; the preview said the “most likely single outcome is revenue in line/above and EPS a penny light” and its base case was “–$0.05.”

surprises.description: MMI storage solutions revenue was $8.3 million, slightly below the preview’s illustrative expectation of about $8.5 million for storage while the company targeted roughly $43 million in total Q2 revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MMI storage solutions segment generated $8.3 million in revenue, up from $8.1 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “To hit $43M with storage at ~$8.5M, C&G must do ~$34.5M.”

surprises.description: Store and other operating expenses fell about 21.9% year over year and total operating expenses fell 13.1%. The preview anticipated closure charges tapering but did not forecast reductions of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Store and other operating expenses fell approximately 21.9% year-over-year to $6.1 million and total operating expenses declined 13.1% to $14.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management explicitly promised the snapback and said closures taper from here.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA returned to positive $0.3 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a return to positive EBITDA and its base-case range of roughly $0 to $0.5 million.
FY2026 revenue guidance of $162–168 million was reaffirmed, as the preview expected.

The company repurchased shares under its $10 million authorization, matching the preview’s expectation that investors would look for visible buyback execution; the preview did not set an expected repurchase amount.
Q2 revenue growth was the third consecutive year-over-year increase, consistent with the preview’s expectation of another quarter of year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $78.7 million, far above the preview’s roughly $42 million estimate. The 120.7% year-over-year increase was driven by both 40.4% volume growth and an 80.2% increase in average blended price.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue surged 120.7% year-over-year to $78.7 million,” driven by “40.4% volume growth and an 80.2% increase in average blended price.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026E (my base)” revenue: “~$42M”; the preview says its estimates are its “own build,” as there is no credible published sell-side consensus.

surprises.description: Instead of the expected quarterly losses, FutureFuel reported $11.4 million of net income and $11.8 million of adjusted EBITDA. That is a large upside gap versus the preview’s estimates of a $9.7 million net loss and a $7 million adjusted EBITDA loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company swung to net income of $11.4 million in Q2 2026 from a net loss of $14.2 million,” with “adjusted EBITDA of $11.8 million versus a prior-year loss of $11.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 net income/(loss) of “~($9.7)M” and adjusted EBITDA of “~($7)M.”

surprises.description: Cash was $34.3 million, well above the preview’s expected $18–25 million range, and the company had not borrowed on its revolver. This was materially better than the cash trajectory the preview identified as the key risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company held $34.3 million in cash with no borrowings on its $35 million revolver.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash & equivalents (EOP)” at “~$18–25M” and said cash above “~$20M with the revolver still untouched” would defer the runway concern.

surprises.description: Biofuel gross profit reached $10.1 million, while the preview warned that another adverse hedge mark could weigh heavily on the quarter and framed positive biofuel gross profit excluding derivatives as a bull-case condition. The reported result also included a $9.1 million benefit from selling physical inventory above hedge levels, which offset a prior-quarter hedging loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Biofuel segment gross profit reached $10.1 million versus a $13.5 million gross loss a year earlier,” aided by “a $9.1 million benefit from selling physical inventory above hedge levels that offset a prior Q1 hedging loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “If Q2 brings another large mark, the headline EPS will look far worse than the underlying business,” and listed “biofuels gross profit positive ex-derivatives” as a bull-case requirement.
