surprises.description: Chemicals delivered $5 million of gross profit on $25.8 million of revenue, stronger than the preview’s roughly $22 million revenue estimate and base-case expectation of a small gross loss. Utilization was 65%, above the preview’s 60% marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chemical segment gross profit rose to $5 million,” with segment revenue “up to $25.8 million from $16.6 million”; “Chemical capacity utilization improved to 65%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated chemicals revenue of “~$22M,” expected the segment gross loss to narrow to “~($1M)” in its base case, and flagged utilization “above ~60%” and crossing into gross profit as key markers.

surprises.description: FutureFuel expects $22 million in gross proceeds from Section 45Z credit monetization in the second half of 2026, compared with the preview’s approximately $19 million FY2026 credit commitment. The call also described the proceeds as recurring annually through 2029, adding visibility beyond the preview’s stated FY2026 benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects $22 million in gross proceeds from monetizing Section 45Z clean fuel credits in H2 2026 (about $3 million in Q3 and $19 million in Q4), recurring annually through 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “FY2026 45Z credit monetization” of “~$19M” and said FF had “committed its estimated $19M of 2026 credits” to Freepoint.

surprises.description: The call reported that the 45Z credit was extended through 2029 and that the SAF credit was cut from $1.75 to $1.00 per gallon, which management said leveled competition for biodiesel. The preview discussed 45Z monetization and higher RFS mandates but did not flag these additional policy changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 45Z credit was extended through 2029 while SAF's credit was cut from $1.75 to $1.00 per gallon, leveling competition for biodiesel.”

surprises.description: Management described a customer-funded agreement involving more than $40 million over three years to double or triple capacity. The preview had cited customer funding for Batesville expansion, but did not describe this capacity-doubling or -tripling scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management secured a customer-funded agreement to invest more than $40 million over three years to double or triple capacity,” reflecting its “capital-light contract manufacturing model.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Batesville expansion funding | Customer commitment | $25M in 2026, up to $17M in 2027” and expected “>$27M” in customer deposits.

surprises.description: The biodiesel plant had an outage lasting more than three weeks, contrary to the preview’s expectation of a clean quarter after the storm-related shutdown was behind the company. Production still increased 26% overall, including 21% in biofuels, so the outage did not prevent year-over-year production growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total production increased 26% year-over-year,” with “biofuel production up 21% despite a more than 3-week biodiesel plant outage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “The storm quarter is behind them” and that “Q2 should be clean.”

in_line: The EPA’s higher RFS blending requirements were directionally anticipated: the preview cited the final RFS rule setting “materially higher 2026–2027 RVOs.”

surprises.description: Evolv reported Q2 revenue of $43.8 million, about 2.8% above the $42.6 million consensus estimate and ahead of the preview’s implied 31% year-over-year growth. The expected sequential decline still occurred.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 34% year-over-year to $43.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $42.6M” and “Implied Y/Y | +31%”; the preview also said management had “explicitly pre-announced a sequential revenue decline in Q2.”

surprises.description: Evolv raised its full-year revenue range to $180–185 million from $175–180 million, rather than merely reaffirming or slightly nudging the prior range. This is a positive revision, though the preview had already described a possible nudge as a base-case outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Evolv raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $180-185 million … from prior $175-180 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FY guide reaffirmed or nudged”; it also listed a bull-case revenue raise to “$182M+.”

surprises.description: The year-end ARR range was tightened upward at the low end, to $148–150 million from $145–150 million, improving the floor and lifting the growth range. The preview had identified an ARR guide raise as a particularly important positive outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised year-end ARR guidance to $148-150 million (23-25% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed standing ending ARR guidance of “$145–150M (+20–25%)” and said “an ARR guide raise is worth far more than a revenue guide raise.”

surprises.description: Q2 ending ARR of $132.7 million was just below the preview’s approximate $133–135 million expectation and its stated $133 million glide-path threshold. The shortfall was slight, and management raised the year-end ARR range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annual recurring revenue reached $132.7 million, up 20% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ending ARR | ~$133–135M” and “Need ≥$133M to stay on the $145–150M glide path.”

surprises.description: The full-year deployment mix is now expected to be 60% purchase subscription, versus the preview’s 55% assumption. Management also outlined about 2.5 percentage points of 2026 gross-margin headwinds, including refurbishment and supply costs, which is a more pressured margin outlook than the preview’s hoped-for stabilization or trough.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now forecasts 60% of new full-year deployed units via purchase subscription (up from 55% prior)” and “Gross margin faces roughly 2.5 points of combined 2026 headwinds,” including Gen1 refurbishment and component/supply-chain costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the mix was “Guided ~55/45 for the year” and described the bull case as requiring the margin drag to prove transitory, with management explicitly calling a trough.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 10.1% in Q2, above the preview’s estimate of roughly $3–4 million of adjusted EBITDA, which implies a margin below that reported level on Q2 revenue. The full-year $15–16 million guide, however, was broadly consistent with the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 10.1% in Q2 from 6.5% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA ~$3–4M” for Q2 and expected full-year adjusted EBITDA of about “$14–16M.”

surprises.description: Evolv added 70 customers, its strongest quarter for additions in two years, exceeding the preview’s cited Q1 pace of 48 additions and its bear-case concern about falling below 40. This was a stronger new-customer result than the preview’s downside scenario contemplated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added 70 new customers, its strongest quarter for additions in two years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “48 added” in Q1 and said the bear case involved “new logo adds decelerate below ~40.”

surprises.description: eXpedite reached over 100 customers, about 8% of the customer base, ahead of the preview’s cited 75-plus customers and roughly 6% penetration. Management also said price increases are planned to bring eXpedite ARPU closer to Express, adding a monetization lever.
surprises.fact_evidence: “eXpedite adoption expanded to over 100 customers (~8% of base, up from 2% a year ago)” and “price increases planned to align eXpedite ARPU closer to Express.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said eXpedite had “75+ customers, ~6% of base” and highlighted attach-rate improvement as a bull signal.

surprises.description: RPO grew sequentially and was more than 1.7 times full-year revenue guidance, with an estimated gross margin well above the company’s current reported margin. The preview did not call out RPO as a specific expected result, so this adds an unanticipated backlog and future-economics data point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligation grew 4.5% sequentially to $312.6 million, exceeds 1.7x full-year revenue guidance, and carries an estimated ~66% gross margin versus current 51% reported gross margin.”

in_line: The sequential revenue decline occurred as management had pre-announced, so that direction was not a surprise.
ARR grew 20% year over year, within the preview’s expected 20–22% growth range, notwithstanding the slightly low ending ARR figure.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $15–16 million was broadly in line with the preview’s implied $14–16 million range.
The target of over 10,000 deployed units by year-end was consistent with the preview’s cited year-end target.

surprises.description: The preview expected FY2027 adjusted EPS of $5.86, with the tax rate normalizing to roughly 23–25%. H&R Block guided to $6.04–$6.24 while projecting an effective tax rate of approximately 23%, putting even the low end above consensus despite the expected tax normalization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for” adjusted diluted EPS of “$6.04-$6.24” and an effective tax rate “rising to approximately 23%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 adj. EPS (initial guide vs.) $5.86”; the preview also described a normalized rate of “~23–25%.”

surprises.description: The preview put FY2027 revenue at $4.05 billion and considered a guide around $4.03–$4.08 billion in-frame. H&R Block guided to $4.11–$4.16 billion, above that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue of $4.11-$4.16 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 revenue (initial guide vs.) $4.05B”; the scenario analysis described a base range of “$4.00–4.06B.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a new or upsized buyback authorization, with at least $1.5 billion cited in its bull case. Instead, H&R Block said about $600 million remains on the existing authorization and plans approximately $400 million of buybacks for FY2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plans about $400 million in buybacks for fiscal 2027 with roughly $600 million remaining on authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A new/upsized authorization plus a high-single/low-double-digit dividend raise is expected”; the bull case specified “buyback re-upped to ≥$1.5B.”

surprises.description: FY2026 revenue and adjusted EPS both exceeded the preview’s expectations and the company’s prior-year guidance ranges. Revenue was about 1% above the preview’s $3.91 billion estimate, while adjusted EPS was about 3% above its $5.16 estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 revenue of $3.95 billion” and “adjusted EPS up 13.9% to $5.31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue $3.91B”; “FY26 adj. EPS $5.16”; the preview listed FY26 guide ranges of “$3.910–3.920B” revenue and “$5.10–5.20” adjusted EPS.

surprises.description: FY2026 EBITDA growth was stronger than the preview’s operating-growth framework implied: EBITDA grew faster than revenue, at about 1.7 times the revenue growth rate, versus the preview’s roughly 1.5-times framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA up 8.3% to $1.06 billion” as revenue “was up 4.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management reaffirmed “EBITDA at ~1.5x” revenue growth.

surprises.description: H&R Block reported unusually large gains in conversion and retention that the preview did not identify as expected outcomes: conversion had its largest single-year improvement in company history, and retention also rose.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Conversion improved 200 basis points this season (the largest single-year gain in company history) and retention rose 190 basis points.”

surprises.description: The client mix has shifted substantially toward the $50,000–$200,000 household AGI range, a strategic change toward more complex, higher-lifetime-value clients that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The percentage of clients in the target household AGI range of $50,000-$200,000 has risen from 38% to 50%,” reflecting a mix shift toward “more complex, higher-lifetime-value clients.”

surprises.description: Management now expects industry growth below the historical roughly 1% norm, attributing the moderation to slowing job growth. The preview focused on the company’s growth algorithm and competitive dynamics but did not flag this industry slowdown.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects moderated industry growth below the historical ~1% norm due to slowing job growth.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed an $8.3 million severance charge in Q1 FY2027 tied to changes in office leadership and support functions. The preview did not anticipate this near-term restructuring cost, although the charge is excluded from guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The transition to a year-round office leadership model plus streamlining of support functions triggered an $8.3 million severance charge in Q1 fiscal 2027 that is excluded from guidance.”

in_line: The FY2026 effective tax rate was 14% because of the disclosed $84.1 million one-time noncash IRS examination benefit, adding $0.65 to EPS; the preview had already identified that benefit and expected the rate to normalize toward roughly 23–25% in FY2027.
The quarterly dividend increase was in line with expectations: the dividend rose 10% to $0.46 per share, within the preview’s expected 8–12% range and its estimated $0.45–$0.47 quarterly payout.

Assisted volume rose 2% and net average charge rose 4.1%, broadly consistent with the preview’s recent assisted volume growth of 2.1% and NAC growth of 3.9%; the preview had specifically flagged assisted trajectory and pricing as issues to watch.

surprises.description: Peraso reported gross margin of 63.7%, well above the preview’s expected 50–55% range and guidance into the 50s. Management attributed the improvement to favorable millimeter-wave mix and sales of previously written-down inventory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 63.7% in Q2 2026,” boosted by “favorable millimeter wave product mix and sales of previously written-down inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~50–55%”; Q1 guidance was “into the 50s” as product mix rises.

surprises.description: Management provided no quarterly guidance, rather than a Q3 revenue outlook investors could assess; it cited irregular FWA order patterns and limited visibility. The preview already warned that Q3 guidance was likely to disappoint, but did not anticipate that management would withhold guidance altogether.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management declined to provide quarterly guidance, citing limited near-term visibility due to irregular fixed wireless access order patterns” and elevated memory prices.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 guidance” was a key metric to watch; the preview said the sell-side “explicitly warns that Q3 guidance is likely to disappoint” and called for listening for a specific Q3 revenue number.

surprises.description: Cash ended at $3.3 million, above the preview’s expected $1.5–2.5 million range, but the increase was supported by substantial ATM equity sales. That improves near-term liquidity while also indicating dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash rose to approximately $3.3 million” from $2.7 million, “aided by $2.4 million in net proceeds from at-the-market equity sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “cash ~$1.5–2.5M pre-CEF”; the preview also said to watch for ATM usage during Q2.

surprises.description: The call disclosed that Peraso had already generated seven-figure revenue from its Israeli defense IFF partner and expected increasing volume as the application shifts to drone use. The preview discussed the defense opportunity and possible future orders, but did not anticipate revenue already being generated from this partner.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Peraso has generated seven-figure revenue from its Israeli defense IFF (identification friend or foe) partner” and expects “increasing volume over the coming quarters” as it transitions to drone-based use.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Intact drone-identification win, August field trials, and volume targeted for Q3/Q4’26; it said to watch for “a named, quantified purchase order.”

surprises.description: Management flagged elevated DDR4/DDR5 memory prices as likely to persist into Q4, a forward cost and visibility headwind not raised in the preview. This contributed to the decision not to provide quarterly guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “elevated third-party memory (DDR4/DDR5) prices expected to persist into Q4.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $1.3 million was within the preview’s $1.2 million company guide and $1.25 million consensus; the delayed FWA order shipment that the preview identified as a key test drove much of the sequential improvement.

Adjusted EBITDA of negative $2.0 million was close to the preview’s approximately negative $2.1 million estimate, and non-GAAP operating expenses of approximately $2.9 million matched the preview’s $2.9–3.0 million expectation.
The PRM2145 drone module’s Q4 2026 evaluation timing and anticipated production shipments in 2027 were consistent with the preview’s stated timing.

surprises.description: Total Q2 revenue was $5.5 million, far above both the $2.21 million consensus and the preview’s $2.4–2.7 million model. The beat came from license revenue, not from stronger-than-expected US product sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue was $5.5 million,” including “$3.8 million in ex-US license revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus: “$2.21M”; preview model: “$2.4–2.7M.”

surprises.description: Product volume came in below the preview’s growth expectations: about 27,000 monthly packs were sold, up only 9% from Q1, versus an estimate of 32,000–34,000 paid scripts and a roughly 30,000-script hurdle. This is a weak Q2 result against the expected lift from expanded territories, TV advertising, and direct dispensing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over $1.7 million in product revenue (~27,000 monthly packs sold, up 9% from Q1).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “32,000–34,000” paid scripts, “(+28–36%),” and said “Anything below ~30,000 scripts (+20%) says the commercial investment isn't converting.”

surprises.description: License revenue was dramatically higher than expected, accounting for most of the revenue beat. The quarter included both a first regulatory milestone from the TEA/Health Canada submission and a first sublicense milestone connected to Everest’s sale of Greater China rights to Cork Cell, whereas the preview modeled only $0.2–0.5 million and did not assume material revenue from the Everest transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$3.8 million in ex-US license revenue,” including “the first regulatory milestone from the TEA/Health Canada submission” and “the first sublicense milestone tied to Everest Medicine's asset sale of Greater China rights to Cork Cell.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “License revenue” of “$0.2–0.5M” and said the Everest/Corxel China upfront “may not accrue to LENZ this period.”

surprises.description: The net loss was substantially smaller than the preview expected, and the reported loss per share was better than both consensus and the preview’s own estimate. LENZ reported a $1.02 loss per share against consensus of $1.21 and the preview’s estimated range of $1.44–$1.56 loss per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss was $31.9 million ($1.02 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed GAAP EPS consensus of “−$1.21” and its own estimate of “−$1.44 to −$1.56.”

surprises.description: Adjusted SG&A fell rather than rising with the Q2 TV campaign and expanded commercial footprint. It was down 14% sequentially, a notably lower spending trend than the preview’s $48–52 million SG&A estimate, though the reported $34.9 million figure excludes stock-based compensation and is therefore not directly comparable to an unqualified SG&A estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted SG&A (excluding stock-based comp) fell 14% quarter-over-quarter to $34.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “SG&A” of “$48–52M,” noting that national TV was “the swing factor” and expected a step-up in spending.

surprises.description: The call provided encouraging repeat-purchase evidence that had not previously been disclosed: more than 60% of e-pharmacy buyers purchased multiple packs, and the mature Q4 cohort had bought slightly more than five packs on average before a full year. That is positive evidence on persistence despite the weaker Q2 volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “More than 60% of e-pharmacy patients who purchased VIZ since launch have bought more than one monthly pack”; the mature Q4 2025 cohort “has purchased slightly more than five monthly packs on average (before reaching a full year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said LENZ “has not disclosed patient refill rates or daily-dose consumption per patient” and identified refill/persistence disclosure as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Despite high physician awareness and a broad prescriber base, management said retail uptake remained poor and prescribing was not consistently recurring, prompting a pivot toward consumer-driven demand. That is a concern about the existing ECP and retail channel even as the company pursues telehealth and advertising.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail uptake tracked through Symphony or IQVIA has been described as poor and limited”; despite “more than 75% prescribing multiple times,” high awareness “has not translated into consistent recurring prescribing, prompting a pivot toward consumer-driven demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the July telehealth launch as an option that “bypasses the ECP bottleneck entirely” and highlighted the commercial trajectory and refill/persistence as key debates.

surprises.description: Early July momentum was stronger than the preview’s qualitative watch item suggested: prescriptions rose more than 45% month over month, with management attributing the increase to telehealth and national TV advertising lifting all channels. This is a promising post-quarter signal, though it does not undo the weaker Q2 product-volume result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July prescriptions grew over 45% month-over-month versus June,” driven by the telehealth option and national TV campaign, which “lifted all sales channels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called telehealth a “Q3 item, commentary only” and said early conversion anecdotes would shape Q3 expectations, without anticipating a specific growth rate.

surprises.description: Management did not announce the explicit quarterly spending ceiling or breakeven quarter the preview identified as the most important capital-allocation signal. Instead, it said it would use Q3 data to reallocate commercial investment toward the best-performing initiatives, leaving the size of future spending and a cash-flow timeline unspecified.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management plans “to use Q3 data to reallocate commercial investment toward the highest-performing initiatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market wanted a “peak-spend statement” and described an SG&A cap as the “print's real catalyst”; it also said a named breakeven quarter would be especially powerful.

in_line: Quarter-end cash and securities were approximately $220 million, at the top of the preview’s $212–220 million estimate.
R&D expense was zero, within the preview’s $0–2 million estimate.

surprises.description: Energy Vault raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $270–310 million, above the prior $225–300 million range and above the preview’s bull-case threshold of guidance above $300 million. The increase to the lower end of the range is especially notable against the preview’s base case of reaffirmed guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $270–310 million from the prior $225–300 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … FY26 guide reaffirmed at $225–300M”; “Bull (25%): FY26 guide raised above $300M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $17.4 million exceeded the preview’s approximately $14.2 million consensus estimate, though the preview cautioned that Q2 revenue estimates were unreliable and not the main focus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $17.4 million.”

surprises.description: The Q2 GAAP loss per share was $0.17, worse than the preview’s consensus estimate of a $0.13 loss. The narrower year-over-year net loss does not change the miss against that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP net loss narrowed to $29.7 million (loss of $0.17 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 EPS: –$0.13”; the preview also cited an alternative estimate of “–$0.14.”

surprises.description: FY2026 GAAP gross-margin guidance improved at the low end, moving from 15–25% to 20–25%. That is better than the preview’s concern that a low-end margin outcome could undermine the profitability narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 GAAP gross margin guidance was narrowed to 20–25% from 15–25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY guide is 15–25% GAAP”; “Any print at the low end while revenue disappoints breaks the ‘scale into profitability’ narrative.”

surprises.description: Q2 margins were strong: GAAP gross margin was 31% and adjusted gross margin was 38.6%, with adjusted margin up about 900 basis points year over year. This was a favorable result against the preview’s focus on margin pressure after adjusted gross margin had fallen to 27.9% in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP gross margin at 31% (up 140 bps) and adjusted gross margin at 38.6% (up ~900 bps year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin: 27.9%, down from 57.1%”; “Any print at the low end while revenue disappoints…”

surprises.description: The company raised the lower end of its year-end cash guidance to $160 million from $150 million, and reported $148 million of cash and equivalents including restricted cash at June 30. This is ahead of the preview’s base-case cash expectation, although the reported cash increase was partly supported by an AR facility draw.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-end 2026 cash guidance was raised to $160–200 million from $150–200 million”; “Total cash and equivalents including restricted cash were $148 million on June 30th, up ~$31 million sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … cash mid-$90Ms–$110M”; the preview also flagged “Cash and liquidity vs. the $150–200M year-end target.”

surprises.description: Management projected nearly $3 billion of backlog by year-end, an additional forward target beyond the preview’s discussion of the current backlog and its $2.5 billion-plus level as a clean beat. The actual backlog reported at about $2 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s current-backlog expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management projects backlog approaching nearly $3 billion by year-end.”

surprises.description: Management outlined a path to roughly 5 gigawatts online by 2030, above the 4-gigawatt installed-by-2030 target cited in the preview, and added a target of approximately $2 billion in annualized EBITDA. This raises the stated scale ambition, though it remains a long-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Outlined a path to roughly 5 gigawatts online generating approximately $2 billion in annualized EBITDA by 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Asset Vault platform expansion (4 GW installed by 2030 target).”

in_line: The reported backlog of approximately $2 billion was in line with the preview’s expectation of roughly $2.0–2.4 billion and its warning that a figure below about $2.0 billion would look light.
The preview expected the 1.25-gigawatt agreement’s revenue to be mostly in 2027; the call likewise said the majority would be in 2027, with a portion in Q4 2026.
The preview anticipated a back-end-loaded year with most revenue in Q4; management said the vast majority of second-half FY2026 revenue was expected in Q4.
The preview noted that the low $8.5 million year-earlier Q2 revenue base would produce a very large year-over-year growth rate; the reported 104% growth was consistent with that expectation.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $19.7 million, below the preview’s $23.5 million estimate and even below its $21–26 million base-case range. The preview expected a content-gap quarter, but the reported decline was worse than its central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue declined 11% year-over-year to $19.7 million,” driven by drops in ASA and ASE sales, partly offset by Bellwright.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate: $23.5M (range $21–26M)” and the base case projected “$22–25M.”

surprises.description: Bookings were $21.8 million, below the preview’s roughly $25 million estimate and just under its $22–29 million range. That is a weaker demand read than the preview’s central expectation, even though bookings remained above revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 bookings fell to $21.8 million from $27.1 million,” reflecting lower ASE and ASA sales, partly offset by Bellwright.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bookings: $25M (range $22–29M)” and the base case projected “$24–27M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Fantastic Tames to be the only material new paid content contribution inside Q2, but some Fantastic Tames content was deferred for recognition into Q3 and Q4. This meant less of that content’s revenue was recognized in the quarter than the preview’s framing implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Current deferred revenue rose to $28.5 million as phased DLC content releases for the Fantastic Tames pack and Dragontopia defer recognition into Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Fantastic Tames Season 1 (May 2026) contribution. The only material new paid content inside the quarter.”

surprises.description: The reported $3 million net loss was materially worse than the preview’s roughly break-even estimate and its stated -$0.50 to +$0.30 EPS range. The year-over-year narrowing in the loss was largely due to the absence of a prior-year tax provision, rather than stronger underlying results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss narrowed sharply to $3 million from $16.6 million a year earlier,” primarily because the prior-year quarter included a $14 million income tax provision.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “EPS (post-split): -$0.05 (range -$0.50 to +$0.30).”

surprises.description: A reduced ARK licensing fee structure generated roughly $1.5 million of quarterly savings and boosted gross profit, an offset to the revenue decline that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The reduced fee structure effective April 2026 “saved roughly $500,000 monthly (about $1.5 million per quarter), boosting gross profit even as revenue fell.”

surprises.description: Management said R&D and G&A should stay consistent quarter-over-quarter and that R&D spending is nearing its peak, a more reassuring expense trajectory than the preview’s expectation that operating costs were more likely to rise.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management indicated “R&D and G&A expenses should remain consistent quarter-over-quarter” as investment in three in-development AAA titles nears completion, with R&D spend “approaching its peak.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Opex was $9.6M in Q1 and is more likely to rise than fall,” and estimated Q2 operating expenses at about $10.0 million.

surprises.description: Bellwright’s console launch reached the top five paid games on Xbox, adding a specific sign of console traction that the preview did not forecast, though it had described Bellwright as potentially durable.
surprises.fact_evidence: Bellwright’s PlayStation and Xbox launch “reached the top five paid games list on Xbox,” building on over 1 million lifetime units sold and 46.4 million playtime hours.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Bellwright durable” as a possible bull-case driver but did not forecast a console launch ranking.

in_line: The preview expected Genesis Part 1 Ascended and Tides of Fortune revenue to shift out of Q2 and the roughly $11 million deferred-revenue recognition to land in Q3; the call said the July launch and shifted Tides sales support approximately $11 million of Q3 recognition.
Unrestricted cash of $13.3 million was within the preview’s $12–15 million estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $7.7 million, about 10% below the $8.52 million consensus and below the preview’s $8.0–8.7 million base case. The quarter had no robotic system deliveries, making the result weaker than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue totaled $7.7 million,” declining year-over-year “due to the absence of any robotic system delivery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $8.52M”; the preview’s base case was “$8.0–8.7M.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue miss, recurring revenue appears to have been a strong positive: with no system deliveries, the $7.7 million total was above the preview’s >$6.0 million recurring-revenue bogey. Robotic catheter revenue also exceeded $1 million after the MAGIC launch, indicating a sharper near-term ramp than the preview’s threshold implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue totaled $7.7 million” with “absence of any robotic system delivery”; robotic catheter revenue “surpassed $1 million,” growing “roughly 270-300% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bogey: >$6.0M and up sequentially.”

surprises.description: The H2 outlook fell short of the preview’s expected revenue shape: guidance implies about $10 million in Q3 and $11 million in Q4, or roughly $35 million for 2026 including Q1 and Q2—not the prior >$40 million target. Q3 is no longer guided above $10 million, and Q4 is well below the preview’s roughly $14.2 million consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided recurring revenue to “approximately $7 million in Q3 and $8 million in Q4 2026” and system revenue to “approximately $3 million in each of Q3 and Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had previously guided to “>$40M with Q3 and Q4 each above $10M”; the preview’s consensus shape was “Q3 ~$11.0M” and “Q4 ~$14.2M.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted a 500-catheters-per-month exit-2026 target and said the absence of a quantified production rate would be a negative tell. The call facts report strong catheter growth but no monthly production run-rate, and say sales remain supply-constrained with only about a dozen U.S. sites approved to purchase MAGIC in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: Catheter sales “remain supply-constrained with a customer backlog”; “only about a dozen U.S. sites received hospital approval to purchase MAGIC in Q2.” No monthly production run-rate is reported in the call facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management targeted “500/month exiting 2026”; “If they don't quantify it at all, treat that as a negative tell.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed an internal cash-flow-profitability target for the first half of 2027, a more constructive milestone than the preview’s emphasis on Robocath being dilutive to the P&L for roughly three years. The company expects incremental recurring revenue to carry through to operating profit under its lean cost structure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Internally modeling cash flow profitability in the first half of 2027,” with “the majority of incremental recurring revenue flowing to operating profit under its existing lean cost structure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Robocath “is not breakeven until year three” and would be “dilutive to the P&L for ~3 years.”

surprises.description: The preview cited a $3 million Synchrony revenue target for 2026; management now expects Synchrony to contribute over $1 million in system revenue per quarter at an ASP near $200,000. That run-rate would be materially higher than the stated 2026 target if sustained, though the timing is not specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects synchrony to contribute over $1 million in system revenue per quarter at an ASP near $200,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided to $3M in 2026 revenue.”

surprises.description: The company reported its first U.S. GenesisX purchase from an academic medical center, with installation expected this fall. The preview was looking for GenesisX proof points and order-book conversion, but had not identified a U.S. academic-center purchase as an existing expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced its first U.S. GenesisX purchase from an academic medical center (install expected this fall).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for named ‘pioneering accounts’ demonstrating GenesisX compatibility” and evidence of GenesisX orders converting to installations.

in_line: Overall gross margin was 58%, essentially matching the preview’s approximately 58.1% FY2026 estimate.
Cash ended the quarter at $10.5 million with no debt, within the preview’s modeled $9.5–11 million range; Q2 free-cash-flow burn of $3.7 million was close to the modeled roughly $3.5 million.
Adjusted operating expenses were $6.6 million, roughly flat year-over-year, consistent with the preview’s expectation of adjusted opex around $6.9 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $3.1 million, about 13% below the $3.55 million consensus and below the preview’s $3.2–3.6 million base-case range. The year-over-year decline was roughly 24%, materially steeper than the preview’s expected 12% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $3.1 million,” down roughly 24% from $4.1 million in Q2 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus: $3.55M”; implied year-over-year “−12%.” The base scenario expected “$3.2–3.6M.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue shortfall, Seer reaffirmed its $16–18 million full-year revenue guidance rather than narrowing it to the low end, as the preview’s base case anticipated. That keeps in place a demanding second-half recovery after a roughly 30% first-half decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $16-18 million,” implying “second-half growth north of 20% after a roughly 30% first-half decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected guidance to be “narrowed to ‘low end of $16–18M’”; it also described the 2H bridge as “very stretched.”

surprises.description: Gross margin came in at 49%, above the preview’s estimated 40–46% range and its 38–44% base case. It also rebounded sharply from Q1, although it remained below the year-ago margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 49%,” down from 52% in Q2 2025 but “up 1,300 basis points sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “40–46%” and gave a base-case range of “38–44%.”

surprises.description: The quarter-end cash balance was above the preview’s estimate, with a smaller-than-expected decline from the prior-quarter balance. Cash still declined and the company continued to burn cash, but the reported balance was modestly better than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: Seer ended the quarter with “approximately $209.5 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments”; six-month free cash flow was “approximately negative $25.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 cash at “$204–207M,” from $219.5 million at March 31, and cited a burn estimate of “~$14.6M/qtr.”

surprises.description: Seer bought back about 1.4 million shares during Q2 while the two proposals were outstanding. The preview specifically identified whether the company repurchased shares during this period as an open question; the purchases also continued the reduction in shares outstanding.
surprises.fact_evidence: Seer repurchased “about 1.4 million Class A shares at an average of $1.68 in Q2,” bringing cumulative buybacks to 13.4 million shares and reducing net shares outstanding by “~15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked: “Whether the company bought stock in Q2 — while two bids were outstanding — is a live governance question.”

surprises.description: The net loss was narrower year over year, but at $16.9 million it exceeded the preview’s approximately $15 million estimate. Lower operating expenses helped limit the loss, but did not bring it down to that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $16.9 million from $19.4 million,” while operating expenses were $18.3 million versus $22.6 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s estimated Q2 net loss was “~$15M.”

surprises.description: Seer reported substantially more validation evidence for the Proteograph platform, including head-to-head studies showing broader coverage than Olink and SomaLogic. The preview discussed competitive and moat concerns but did not anticipate this specific body of platform evidence.
surprises.fact_evidence: Validating publications “surpassed 95,” an “approximately 80% increase over the prior 12 months,” including head-to-head studies showing broader proteome coverage than Olink and SomaLogic.

surprises.description: The PRECISE SG100K team had completed running 10,000 samples and planned to present preliminary data in September. The preview identified the cohort as a potential program but did not report that this sample milestone had been completed or that data were due so soon.
surprises.fact_evidence: The PRECISE SG100K team “completed running 10,000 samples from the 100,000-sample cohort in May” and will present preliminary data at HUPO in September.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “PRECISE SG100K (10,000 participants, expanding toward 100,000)” as a population-scale biobank program.

surprises.description: Seer disclosed that shipments were coming from both prior STAC customers and the SIP program, with some SIP placements converting into owned instruments. This provides evidence of instrument-placement channels and conversion, though the preview had no specific expected shipment mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: In the first half, “one-third of instrument shipments came from prior STAC customers and one-third from the SIP program,” with some SIP placements converting into owned instruments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “instrument placements and consumables pull-through” as a metric to watch, including “evidence the reorder cycle is actually converting.”

in_line: Academic and government funding headwinds and elongated sales cycles continued to pressure revenue, consistent with the preview’s expectation of macro and academic-funding headwinds.
Management again said its capital was sufficient to reach cash-flow break-even, consistent with the preview’s description of that existing management claim.
The year-over-year reduction in operating expenses and narrower year-over-year net loss were consistent with the preview’s expectation that cost cuts would narrow losses.

surprises.description: The preview focused on the pending FCC PNT notice but did not flag that the lower 900 MHz band could be left out of the final direct-to-device NPRM. The final NPRM excluded the band even though the draft had proposed allowing unlicensed space-to-first transmissions there, a negative change in the regulatory picture for NextNav’s spectrum proposal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NextNav's lower 900 MHz band was ultimately not included in the FCC's final direct-to-device NPRM despite the draft proposing to permit unlicensed space-to-first transmissions in the band.”

surprises.description: The preview said the final derivative and warrant mark would likely swing in NextNav’s favor and could produce a GAAP beat. Instead, the company reported a $33.8 million net loss, including a roughly $32 million noncash loss on the fair-value change in derivative and warrant liabilities.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss of approximately $33.8 million for Q2 2026, driven by a ~$32 million noncash loss on the change in fair value of derivative and warrants liability, partially offset by a ~$21 million gain on debt extinguishment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The derivative mark likely swings in NextNav's favor, meaning a headline GAAP ‘beat’ that means nothing.” The preview also gave a base EPS range of “-$0.10 to -$0.16.”

surprises.description: NextNav reported 15.2 million shares issued to convert all debt, slightly above the preview’s estimate of about 14.9 million conversion shares. The difference is small, and the conversion itself—and becoming debt-free—was expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company became debt-free by converting all its debt to 15.2 million shares, with all debt holders electing shares over cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated that converting the notes would issue “~14.9M shares” and expected “zero convertible debt.”

surprises.description: NextNav reported approximately 20-nanosecond timing accuracy across outdoor, indoor, and GPS-denied settings, a concrete performance result not anticipated in the preview. Management said it exceeds critical-infrastructure requirements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Demonstrated approximately 20 nanoseconds of timing accuracy over its operational 5G PNT network across outdoor, indoor and GPS-denied environments,” which management says “exceeds critical infrastructure requirements.”

surprises.description: NextNav disclosed a new Tier 1 partner arrangement to put its Z-access software and reference data on devices for 911 vertical-location services. The preview discussed commercial opportunities but did not anticipate this device-based partnership.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new partnership brings NextNav's Z-access software and reference data onto a Tier 1 partner's devices for 911 vertical location services,” advancing its device-based strategy and “creating incremental revenue opportunities.”

in_line: Liquidity was approximately $300 million, within the preview’s expected $290–315 million range; the preview also expected roughly $170 million of warrant proceeds and no debt.
The 14.8 million public warrant exercises and nearly $170 million of proceeds matched the preview’s estimate of about 14.8 million warrants and $170 million.
The FCC draft PNT-focused NPRM remained in interagency review, with timing still subject to ongoing reviews, as the preview expected.

The SpaceX letter citing NextNav’s 900 MHz proposal was already known and highlighted in the preview; management’s view that it validated demand for scarce low-band spectrum was consistent with that setup.

The Safran interoperability partnership was already identified in the preview as a commercial proof point to track; the call facts describe integration and demonstrations, not a revenue-bearing contract.

surprises.description: Revenue was $260 million, above the preview’s $245–250 million company range and $245.98 million consensus. That is a clear quarterly beat, rather than the in-range result expected in the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $260 million, up 27% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $51.5 million at a 19.8% margin, well above the preview’s roughly $42–44 million and 17% estimate, and above its 17.5% “clean pass” threshold. The margin result was stronger than even the preview’s ≥18% bull-case marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin hit a modern-day high of 19.8% ($51.5 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (est.) | ~$42–44M / ~17%”; “≥17.5% consolidated is a clean pass”; bull case: “≥18%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was approximately $0.70 versus the preview’s $0.53 consensus, a substantially larger beat than the preview’s base-case range of $0.55–0.58. The preview cautioned that share-count restatement made the consensus uncertain, but the reported figure still exceeds the stated estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of approximately $0.70.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $0.53”; base case: “$0.55–0.58.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.02–1.04 billion, above the preview’s prior $970 million–$1.0 billion range and even above its bull-case range of approximately $1.00–1.02 billion. The new range also takes the company above $1 billion for the first time.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year guidance to $1.02-$1.04 billion, crossing the $1 billion threshold for the first time.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 Revenue … Company Guidance: $970M – $1.0B”; bull case: “Raised to ~$1.00–1.02B.”

surprises.description: Bookings reached $306 million, extending the sequence of quarterly increases and exceeding the preview’s $250–270 million range for holding visibility and its >$270 million bull-case marker. Rather than normalizing from Q1’s record, bookings set another all-time high.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 bookings reached an all-time high of $306 million,” following $210M, $257M, and $290M over the prior three quarters.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A number in the $250–270M range … keeps the visibility story intact”; bull case: “> $270M.”

surprises.description: Aerospace operating margin was 21.4%, materially above the preview’s 18%+ bull-case marker for the segment. The segment also reported record sales and backlog, adding strength beyond the preview’s focus on margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aerospace segment sales grew 22.6% to a record $237.3 million with adjusted operating margin of 21.4% (up 510 bps), while backlog hit a record $657.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Aerospace operating margin prints 18%+” in the bull-case operational description.

surprises.description: The call added a sizable, previously unflagged program contribution: MV-75 FLRAA generated a $27.4 million booking and is expected to provide about $35 million of 2026 revenue, with management describing it as potentially the company’s largest military program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MV-75 FLRAA program generated a $27.4 million booking in Q2, is expected to contribute roughly $35 million in revenue in 2026, and is described as potentially the largest military program in company history.”

surprises.description: The $44.7 million Army radio production order itself was already expected, but management now anticipates similar annual orders for the next four to five years. That adds a longer stream of expected demand than the preview’s stated $40–50 million annual run-rate framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $45 million (specifically $44.7M) production order for the U.S. Army 4549/T radio test program, expected to support deliveries over 18 months with similar annual orders anticipated for the next 4-5 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $44.7M full-rate production order landed in July 2026”; “a $40–50M annual run rate.”

surprises.description: Astronics recognized a $2 million IEEPA tariff refund in Q2, adding about 70 basis points of margin, whereas the preview said no refunds had yet been recognized. The preview noted tariff-refund upside generally, but not a refund already benefiting this quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Results benefited from a $2 million IEEPA tariff refund (about 70 bps of margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tariffs were a ~$2M Y/Y headwind with no refund benefit yet recognized.”

surprises.description: Management described an ongoing tariff burden of $3–4 million per quarter before mitigation. The preview reported a roughly $2 million year-over-year tariff drag in Q1 but did not flag this larger recurring quarterly run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects an ongoing tariff run rate of $3-$4 million per quarter before mitigation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tariffs were a ~$2M Y/Y headwind” in Q1.

surprises.description: Long-term debt fell to $310.3 million and available liquidity rose to $253.2 million, compared with the preview’s Q1 snapshot of $334.9 million of total debt and $231.8 million of liquidity. The preview highlighted cash flow as a risk to watch but did not anticipate this balance-sheet improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Long-term debt decreased $24.1 million from year-end to $310.3 million, with $253.2 million in available liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total debt / liquidity | $334.9M / $231.8M.”

in_line: The $44.7 million Army 4549/T production order itself was anticipated: the preview said the full-rate production order had landed in July. The added expectation of similar annual orders for four to five years is captured separately above.

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was far below the preview’s estimate: Intrusion had just $0.2 million, versus an expected $2.0–2.5 million. The company also said it raised $3.3 million through Streeterville notes and plans further public or private financings, underscoring greater-than-expected funding pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents stood at just $0.2 million as of June 30, 2026,” and the company raised “$3.3 million via Streeterville notes” and plans further public/private financings, including its ATM program.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I model ~$2.0–2.5M cash at 6/30.” The preview also anticipated a possible equity raise or ATM, but not cash this low.

surprises.description: Revenue was $1.5 million, above the preview’s own $1.25–1.35 million estimate, though it matched the stated $1.50 million consensus. The result was therefore better than the preview’s modeled quarter, but not a consensus beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $1.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate: revenue $1.25–1.35M”; the preview also listed Q2 consensus revenue of “$1.50M.”

surprises.description: The reported loss was smaller than the preview’s operating estimate, but still wider than consensus. Intrusion lost $0.13 per share, versus the preview’s modeled loss of $0.16–0.18 and consensus of $0.10.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $2.6 million ($0.13 per share) in Q2 2026 from $2.0 million ($0.10 per share) in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate: ... EPS $(0.16)–$(0.18)” and Q2 consensus EPS of “$(0.10).” The preview said the EPS bar “looks too low to clear on operations.”

in_line: The Department of War contract-funding delay continued to weigh on the quarter, consistent with the preview’s base case that the extension might still be pending and there might be no catch-up revenue.

VigilAigent contributed approximately $3.5 million of ARR from multiyear customer contracts; the preview expected the acquired business to be reaffirmed at about $3.5 million ARR and specifically sought confirmation that it was contracted.
The company reported over $350,000 in annualized new business and renewals and MSP partners with potential to generate over $1 million ARR each, matching the preview’s stated figures to watch.
Management identified more than $3 million of annualized cost synergies, as previewed; the facts provided do not report a realization schedule or quarterly opex exit rate.

The Texas contract was described as a $4 million annual contract with revenue recognition beginning in Q2, broadly matching the preview’s approximately $3.9 million annual contract and expectation of partial-quarter revenue.
The cash-flow-positive goal moved to Q1 2027, consistent with the preview’s base case that the year-end 2026 target could be pushed into 2027.
A shareholder vote on Proposal 3 relating to the acquisition’s issuance of shares was anticipated in the preview, which noted that the second closing was subject to shareholder/Nasdaq approval.

surprises.description: After quarter-end cash of $10.8 million came in slightly above the preview’s $9.5–10 million estimate, cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments had fallen to about $5.6 million by July 31. The company also issued a going-concern warning, making the post-quarter liquidity deterioration worse than the preview’s roughly $4 million monthly burn assumption suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “~$5.6 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments as of July 31, 2026, down from $10.8 million unrestricted cash at quarter end,” and “issued a going-concern warning.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Straight-lining puts June 30 liquidity at ~$9.5–10M”; the preview also described cash depletion at roughly “$4.0M/month.”

surprises.description: ESS disclosed a nonbinding business-combination LOI with an implied combined enterprise value of about $515 million, but ESS shareholders would own only 5%–10% of the combined company. The preview anticipated a possible strategic or non-dilutive financing structure, but not a transaction that would leave existing shareholders with such a small stated stake.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ESS signed a nonbinding LOI for a business combination implying a combined enterprise value of ~$515 million, with ESS shareholders expected to own only ~5% to 10% of the combined company at close.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any strategic investor, project finance, or partner-funded structure would be the genuine bull catalyst.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating expenses rose 19% year over year, rather than approaching the preview’s desired $4–5 million quarterly level after the restructuring. The first-half total was down 12%, but Q2 was pushed higher by a largely nonrecurring legal accrual and increased R&D spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 opex rose 19% year-over-year driven by a $1.5 million largely nonrecurring legal contingency accrual and higher R&D spending”; first-half operating expenses were “$14.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Opex needs to approach ~$4–5M/quarter to make the remaining cash meaningful,” and the preview sought “proof the June restructuring is real.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $73,000, below even the preview’s lower estimate of about $0.1 million, although the preview cautioned that the estimates were highly inconsistent and revenue was a very small base.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue collapsed to just $73,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue | ~$0.1M (Stocktwits) / $404K (ChartMill).”

surprises.description: The reported loss per share of $0.46 was slightly worse than the preview’s $0.44 loss estimate. The absolute net loss, however, remained within the preview’s expected $13–16 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $15.6 million ($0.46/share).”

surprises.description: ESS had repaid $37 million of the original $40 million Yorkville promissory note, a substantial debt reduction not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of financing options. The deleveraging is favorable, though it comes amid sharply reduced cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has repaid $37 million of the original $40 million principal on its Yorkville promissory note, prioritizing deleveraging.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on the ATM, possible strategic or project financing, and the risk of relying on ATM issuance; it did not anticipate repayment of nearly all the Yorkville principal.

in_line: The $15.6 million Q2 net loss was within the preview’s expected $13–16 million range.

The preview expected the Juniper and Alsym arrangements to remain LOIs unless converted into binding orders. The call still described them as LOIs, and management said the nearly $1 billion of sodium-ion opportunities were early-stage, unbooked and uncontracted.
First-half operating cash burn of $22.4 million works out to about $3.7 million per month, broadly in line with—and slightly better than—the preview’s roughly $4 million-per-month assumption.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was approximately $64,000, far below the preview’s $300,000 estimate and even below its $150,000–$700,000 range. The preview expected a small, lumpy quarter, but not revenue this low.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $64,000.”

surprises.description: Pixelworks signed its first major device licensee ahead of the planned 2026 timeline: a multi-year certification agreement with a global manufacturer. The preview focused on whether title work and royalties would emerge, and did not anticipate this device-licensing milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed its first major device licensee—a multi-year device certification agreement with an unnamed global manufacturer—ahead of its planned 2026 timeline following a six-month evaluation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for the first disclosure that splits services revenue vs. per-title license/royalty revenue.”

surprises.description: Operating costs were higher than the preview’s modeled level: GAAP operating expenses were $3.4 million, versus a preview build of about $2.35 million. Management’s cash operating expense target of less than $2.5 million per quarter through year-end also sets a higher ceiling than the preview’s roughly $2.0 million framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP operating expenses fell to $3.4 million in Q2 from $5.2 million in Q1”; management “targets cash operating expenses of less than $2.5 million per quarter through the remainder of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$2.35M GAAP opex”; “Cash opex ~$2.0M”; “My Estimate: $2.0–2.4M incl. SBC.”

surprises.description: The company spent $3.2 million on repurchases in Q2, a substantial execution of the buyback program rather than the token or no repurchase contemplated in the preview’s base case. This was the quarter’s largest cash use, with $1.8 million still authorized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pixelworks repurchased $3.2 million of common stock during Q2, its single largest cash use, with $1.8 million remaining on the buyback authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … token or no buyback”; “Shares repurchased in Q2 … vs. an expectation of something.”

surprises.description: Management said Q3 revenue should increase sequentially based on business already booked, giving a more constructive near-term revenue signal than the preview’s expectation of a small, lumpy business with no formal guidance. Management still cautioned that revenue will remain lumpy until the business scales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 2026 revenue to increase sequentially based on currently booked licensing and motion grading business, though revenue will remain lumpy until scale is achieved.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Formal guidance: None — company does not guide”; the base case anticipated “revenue lumpy and small.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was $53 million, below the preview’s estimated $55.0–$56.5 million. The preview also expected a buyback, and the reported $3.2 million of repurchases was the largest cash use, so the shortfall came alongside meaningful capital return.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pixelworks ended Q2 2026 with $53 million in cash and cash equivalents and zero debt”; it “repurchased $3.2 million of common stock during Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Quarter-end cash … My Estimate: $55.0–56.5M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 60.9%, slightly above the preview’s estimated 55–60% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin improved to 60.9% in Q2 2026 from 56.7% in the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … My Estimate: ~55–60%.”

surprises.description: Pixelworks added an endorsement from Kannapolis Group, which the preview did not mention, while also reporting a CINITY partnership that fits the preview’s already-described exhibitor ecosystem.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expanded its exhibitor ecosystem by securing endorsements from Kannapolis Group and a partnership with CINITY, adding to existing relationships with Marcus Theatres, Odeon, and VIEW.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described exhibitor partnerships including “CINITY, Marcus Theatres, Odeon, Vue, and Kinepolis,” but did not mention Kannapolis Group.

in_line: Management’s expected quarterly interest income of $400,000–$500,000 was in line with the preview’s $0.4–$0.5 million framework.

surprises.description: SES reported Q2 revenue of $5.1 million, below the preview’s $5.84 million consensus and below the stated $5.4–5.9 million range. That was also short of the preview’s $5.5–7.0 million base scenario, though not below its bear-case threshold of $4.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $5.1 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $5.84M (range ~$5.4–5.9M)” and “Base … Revenue | $5.5–7.0M”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 22.6%, above the preview’s estimated 15–19% range and its 18% level described as supportive of the business narrative. The sequential improvement was stronger than the preview’s expected margin trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin improved to 22.6% in Q2 2026 from 18.1% in Q1”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … my est. 15–19%” and “Sustained ≥18% supports the ‘this is a real business’ narrative”

surprises.description: The preview described the Korea NDAA-compliant line conversion as complete and cited capacity of 1 million or more cells a year. The call instead said production is currently 200,000 cells a year and is expected to scale to 1 million by about September, reaching full speed in Q4—indicating the capacity ramp is still ahead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “scale its Korea NDAA-compliant cell production five-fold from 200,000 to 1 million cells per year by about September, running at full speed in Q4”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Korea line conversion to NDAA-compliant cells is complete, with stated capacity of 1M+ cells/year”

surprises.description: SES disclosed that annual drone-cell demand from its top five large customers already exceeds 1.5 million cells, against deliverable capacity of roughly 700,000–800,000, with order visibility into 2028. The preview anticipated a ramp but did not describe demand at this scale; the capacity shortfall tempers the positive demand signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Drone demand from its top five large customers already exceeds 1.5 million cells annually against roughly 700,000-800,000 deliverable capacity, with order visibility into 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NDAA drone cells convert from samples to purchase orders” and “A hard dollar number for Q2 drone revenue is the swing factor”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP net loss was $0.04 per share, wider than the preview’s alternative compiled estimate of $0.02 per share in losses. The call also cited a bad-debt provision on a legacy EV service contract as a contributor to the wider quarterly loss, an item the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net loss was $13.1 million ($0.04/share) in Q2, wider than Q1's $11.1 million loss, hurt by lower revenue and a bad debt provision on a legacy EV service contract.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (alt. compile) | –$0.02 … (likely non-GAAP / stale)”

surprises.description: SES announced Solark certification as a battery partner and said new restrictions on foreign-produced inverters helped reduce the residential ESS competitive field from roughly 20 players to about three. The preview did not anticipate this channel or competitive-position development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company was certified by Solark as a battery partner, reducing residential ESS competition from roughly 20 players to about three (alongside Enphase and Tesla), aided by new restrictions on foreign-produced inverters.”

in_line: SES reaffirmed its FY2026 revenue guidance of $30–35 million, as the preview’s base case expected.
GAAP EPS of –$0.05 matched the preview’s consensus estimate.
Q2-end cash of approximately $163 million was broadly in line with the preview’s expected $158–162 million range.
ESS remained the majority of revenue, consistent with the preview’s expectation that ESS would carry the quarter.

surprises.description: Management said R&D expense is expected to double in the second half of 2026 versus the first half and rise again in 2027. The preview discussed the study ramp but did not flag this scale of planned spending increase, which could weigh on profitability as the pipeline expands.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expense in the second half of 2026 is expected to double first-half levels and increase again in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “10 ongoing studies across YUTREPIA and L606, including new indications” and Re-Spire’s ramp, but did not state an expectation for this degree of R&D spending growth.

surprises.description: The call disclosed dose-related improvements in the ASCENT PH-ILD study without worsening cough scores, a clinical result not anticipated in the preview. The reported gains increased from 21.5 meters at week 8 to 41 meters at week 24.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Progressively higher YUTREPIA doses at weeks 8, 16, and 24 produced 6-minute walk improvements of 21.5, 31.5, and 41 meters respectively without worsening cough scores.”

surprises.description: Management said a ruling in the 327 patent litigation could come “any day now,” with possible outcomes including a royalty or adjunctive relief if the ruling goes against Liquidia. The preview emphasized the separate '782 litigation and did not flag this near-term 327 ruling, adding a new, immediate legal uncertainty.
surprises.fact_evidence: A ruling before Judge Andrews could come “any day now,” with outcomes ranging from “an unimpeded win to a royalty or adjunctive relief” if adverse.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the '782 patent litigation “the dominant variable in the equity” and urged questions about the case timeline, but did not mention an imminent 327 ruling.

in_line: Management reaffirmed confidence in reaching more than $1 billion in 2027 revenue, matching the preview’s expectation that it would reiterate “at least $1 billion in annual revenue by 2027.”
YUTREPIA sales of $170.4 million, up 31% quarter over quarter, were consistent with the preview’s stated sales and sequential-growth setup.

The July 31 prescription, patient-start, and physician counts, including more than 5,000 patient starts and more than 1,100 prescribing physicians, were in line with the commercial metrics laid out in the preview.
Four consecutive quarters of increasing profitability were consistent with the preview’s expectation of a fourth straight profitable quarter.
Ten studies underway or planned and Re-Spire already enrolling matched the preview’s discussion of ten studies and Re-Spire enrollment having begun.
SG&A rising as commercial scaling continues was consistent with the preview’s flagged expectation that field-force expansion could keep SG&A growing.
The inhaled prostacyclin market expanded while YUTREPIA growth exceeded category growth, consistent with the preview’s market-expansion framing rather than a purely share-shift story.

surprises.description: Q2 Symbest sales were $0.4 million, below the preview’s roughly $0.7 million product estimate. Sales grew from the prior year, but the reported amount fell short of the expected commercial ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 commercial sales of Symbest were $0.4 million” versus “$0.1 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Product (Symvess) … est. ~$1.0M”; “My Estimate … ~$0.7M (~40 units).”

surprises.description: Q2 net loss was substantially larger than the preview’s estimate, despite the preview cautioning that GAAP results could be distorted by earn-out remeasurement. The six-month comparison was also affected largely by a non-cash remeasurement of the contingent earn-out liability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss was $36.8 million in Q2 2026”; the “six-month net loss of $54.4 million compared to net income of $1.5 million a year prior, driven largely by non-cash remeasurement of the contingent earn-out liability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss … ~$(23)M.”

surprises.description: R&D expense came in far below the preview’s expected post-restructuring level: $8.1 million versus an estimate of about $16.5 million. Management attributed the drop to reduced non-commercial manufacturing runs and lower clinical-trial costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses fell sharply to $8.1 million in Q2 2026 from $22.0 million in Q2 2025 due to reduced non-commercial manufacturing runs and lower clinical trial costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&D … ~$16.5M”; the preview also expected R&D to step down “toward ~$16M.”

surprises.description: The company reported a new $0.7 million inventory reserve and unused-capacity costs, contributing to $1.2 million of cost of goods sold even though only $0.2 million was tied to units sold. The preview had flagged any new inventory reserve as a downside signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost of goods sold rose to $1.2 million in Q2 2026, including a $0.7 million inventory reserve and unused production capacity costs, with only $0.2 million tied to actual units sold.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “any new inventory reserve” as a bear tell and noted that “Q1 took $1.6M.”

surprises.description: ATEV’s infection rate in the dialysis trial was much lower than AV fistula’s, a favorable clinical finding not identified in the preview’s discussion of the already-reported efficacy win.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ATEV showed a substantially lower infection rate of 6 infections per 100 patient-years versus 23 per 100 patient-years for AV fistula in the V012 dialysis trial.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that at least 20 major U.S. healthcare systems are working toward Symbest adoption in the second half of 2026 and described a national-account strategy aimed at roughly 1,000 additional hospitals. This adds a specific account pipeline and broader reach beyond the preview’s discussion of units, VAC approvals, and ordering conversion; it does not establish that those systems have begun ordering.
surprises.fact_evidence: “At least 20 major U.S. healthcare systems are in the process of adopting Symbest in the second half of 2026,” and “a new national account strategy targets access to roughly 1,000 additional hospitals.”

surprises.description: The FDA accepted the IND for the CTEV coronary bypass program, with a 10-patient Phase 2a study expected to open this quarter. The preview did not identify this program milestone as an expected catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA accepted the IND for the CTEV coronary bypass program, with a 10-patient Phase 2a study expected to open this quarter.”

surprises.description: SG&A was slightly above the preview’s estimate: $8.0 million versus about $7.0 million, while management characterized it as roughly flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A remained roughly flat at $8.0 million.”

in_line: The V012 interim analysis met the primary efficacy endpoint, consistent with the preview’s statement that the Phase 3 dialysis interim had already hit on superiority.
The planned November 2026 supplemental BLA filing remains within the preview’s expected H2 2026 submission window.
Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash of $80.3 million was around the high end of the preview’s roughly $75 million estimate and its roughly $80 million estimate if the greenshoe was exercised.

surprises.description: Q2 spending and loss were modestly below the preview’s estimates: R&D was $18.7 million versus an estimated $19–21 million, G&A was $7.6 million versus $8.0–8.7 million, and the $22.8 million net loss ($0.12 per share) was better than the expected $23–26 million loss and $0.13–0.15 per-share loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss was $22.8 million ($0.12/share)”; “R&D rising to $18.7 million and G&A rising to $7.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied net loss ~($25)M”; “My Estimate ($23)–($26)M”; “EPS … ($0.13) – ($0.15)”; “R&D expense … $19–21M”; “G&A expense … $8.0–8.7M.”

surprises.description: A new exploratory RECLAIM analysis showed a liver-risk improvement not called out in the preview: after 24 weeks, 50% of pemvidutide patients with baseline FIB-4 above 1.3 fell below 1.3, compared with 17% on placebo. This adds a potential liver-benefit signal to the AUD results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “50% of pemvidutide patients with baseline FIB-4 above 1.3 dropped below 1.3 after just 24 weeks, versus only 17% on placebo.”

surprises.description: The cash runway covers the MASH Phase 3 readout, but not a potential AUD Phase 3 trial. Management said it intends to pursue non-dilutive funding for AUD—such as royalties, debt, or strategic partnerships—after FDA End-of-Phase-2 feedback, so that funding is not yet secured.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The cash runway does not include a potential AUD Phase 3 trial”; management intends to fund it via “royalty, debt, or strategic partnerships after obtaining FDA end-of-Phase-2 feedback.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company’s $535 million “funds operations through the 2029 Phase 3 52-week readout” and highlighted partnership commentary as a key issue, but did not flag that a potential AUD Phase 3 would sit outside that runway.

surprises.description: RESTORE’s protocol was amended to assess liver stiffness hierarchically at both week 48 and week 24, a trial-design detail not anticipated in the preview. The update does not move the stated top-line timing, which remains the second half of 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amended the protocol to assess liver stiffness hierarchically at both week 48 and week 24”; “top-line data expected in the second half of 2027.”

in_line: PERFORMA’s Phase 3 MASH trial had already been reported as initiated, with a 2029 52-week readout expected; the call reaffirmed that the $519 million cash balance funds operations through that readout, consistent with the preview’s $510–520 million cash estimate and runway expectation.
RECLAIM’s primary endpoint, WHO risk-level reduction, zero-heavy-drinking-days result, and 9.1% placebo-adjusted weight loss matched figures already reported in the preview.
RESTORE enrollment completion was consistent with the preview’s expectation that enrollment would finish in Q3 2026.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $19.9M, far above the preview’s $13.06M consensus and even above its $17–19M bull-case range. The preview described at least $13M of goods revenue as a good outcome; goods revenue instead reached $19.8M, mainly on higher Elfabrio sales through Chiesi.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues rose to $19.9 million”; “Q2 2026 revenues from selling goods grew to $19.8 million”; growth was “driven mainly by higher El Fabrio sales through Chiesi.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus: “$13.06M”; bull scenario: “$17–19M”; good outcome for goods revenue: “≥$13M.”
