surprises.description: Q2 net income was $3.8M, or $0.05 per share, versus the preview’s consensus expectation of a $0.01-per-share loss. The result also exceeded the preview’s bull-case EPS range of $0.01–$0.02.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income increased sharply to $3.8 million (5 cents per share) from just $164,000 (breakeven per share) in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 FY2026 consensus EPS: “$(0.01)”; bull scenario EPS: “$0.01 – $0.02.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for evidence that Pfizer ordering had normalized after lower purchases, but the call said lower Pfizer sales partially offset higher sales to Chiesi and Fiocruz. Thus, the strong overall goods-revenue result did not reflect a broad-based recovery across the partners.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 cost of revenues reflected “higher sales volumes to Chiesi and Fiocruz partially offset by lower Pfizer sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Good outcome: “explicit confirmation Pfizer/Fiocruz ordering has normalized”; the preview also noted lower Elelyso purchases by Pfizer and Fiocruz in Q1.

surprises.description: Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term deposits were $40.7M at quarter-end, below the preview’s expected minimum of $47M. The preview had expected the cash balance to show that the milestone had not been consumed by an operating quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company holds $40.7 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term deposits as of June 30, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Cash-at-quarter-end good outcome: “≥$47M — confirms the milestone wasn’t consumed by an operating quarter.”

surprises.description: The company reported no outstanding debt, whereas the preview listed $8.5M of debt at Q1 and described the balance sheet as having debt. That is a better debt position than the preview’s starting point suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company had “no outstanding debt or warrants.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “debt $8.5M” at March 31, 2026.

surprises.description: R&D expense was $4.4M, below the preview’s expected $5.5–6.5M range. The call attributed the reduction in part to $2.1M of grants being recorded as a reduction of R&D expense under a new law, which management said is available on an ongoing basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses fell to $4.4 million from $6 million a year earlier,” aided by “$2.1 million in grants now recorded as a reduction of R&D expenses under a new R&D law available on an ongoing basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: R&D expense good outcome: “$5.5–6.5M”; the preview noted Q1 R&D had stepped up to $5.4M.

surprises.description: Management offered a long-term market and share projection not discussed in the preview: it estimated the global Fabry market at about $3.2B by 2031 and said El Fabrio could capture 15–20% of it. This is new potential upside commentary, though the preview provides no comparable market-share expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management projected “the global Fabry market to reach approximately $3.2 billion by 2031, with El Fabrio positioned to capture 15-20% of that market.”

in_line: The $25M Chiesi milestone was recognized in Q1 and boosted first-half revenue, as the preview had already stated.
Cost of revenues was about 39% of goods revenue ($7.8M on $19.8M), below the preview’s roughly 48% favorable-mix threshold.

Management said strong Chiesi purchases largely reflected inventory management and that quarterly revenue is lumpy; the preview had warned that partner shipment and inventory timing can make a single quarter misleading.
The expected timing for PRX115 RELEASE topline results remained the second half of 2027, as the preview stated.

surprises.description: Kontoor raised full-year adjusted gross margin guidance to 49.8%–50.0% from 48.3%–48.5%, a much larger upward revision than the preview anticipated, which had focused on whether margins would reach the high 46% to 48% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raising full-year adjusted gross margin guidance to 49.8%-50% from 48.3%-48.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin ~46.5–48.0% (my est.)”; FY guidance in force was “48.3–48.5%.”

surprises.description: Kontoor raised its full-year adjusted EPS range by $0.10 at both ends, rather than merely reaffirming the prior range as the preview's base case expected. The revised range is also below the preview's bull-case range of $5.35–$5.45.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $5.25-$5.35 … from the prior $5.15-$5.25.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “FY range reaffirmed”; bull case: “FY cont.-ops EPS raised to $5.35–5.45.”

surprises.description: Helly Hansen reached roughly $2 million of operating profit in its seasonally smallest quarter, which management said may be the first time the brand has done so. The preview highlighted Q2 seasonality and growth deceleration, but did not anticipate this quarterly profitability milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Helly Hansen delivered positive operating profit of roughly $2 million in Q2, its seasonally smallest quarter,” possibly “the first time ever the brand achieved this.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is explicitly HH's smallest revenue quarter”; the preview expected seasonal deceleration but gave no Q2 operating-profit expectation.

surprises.description: The Lee divestiture comes with about $0.55 per share of stranded or unmitigated costs in addition to $0.90 of lost operating earnings, and Kontoor expects it to take 12–18 months to offset them. The preview cited Lee's expected earnings contribution but did not flag these costs or the mitigation period; management nevertheless sees a $6.70–$6.80 pro forma run-rate EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Lee divestiture leaves ~$0.55 of stranded/unmitigated costs and ~$0.90 of lost operating earnings,” expected to be “fully offset within 12-18 months” to make the deal EPS-neutral, bridging to “~$6.70-$6.80 pro forma run-rate EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Lee at “~$0.90 EPS” and described the deal as a divestiture, but did not mention stranded costs or a 12–18 month offset period.

surprises.description: Kontoor is putting about $25 million of incremental brand-building spending into the updated outlook, an estimated $0.36 per-share drag, rather than allowing all of the gross-margin improvement to flow through to earnings. The preview did not anticipate this investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The updated outlook incorporates approximately $25 million of incremental brand-building investment (a ~$0.36 EPS drag)” to support growth “for 2027 and beyond.”

surprises.description: Wrangler's female business grew 20% in the first half, with Q2 trends accelerating. The preview identified the business as a growth priority and noted it was about 10% of revenue, but gave no expectation of growth at this pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wrangler's female business, currently ~10% of total revenue … grew 20% in the first half with accelerating Q2 trends.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called out “the women's business (~10% of Wrangler revenue, a stated growth priority)” but gave no growth-rate expectation.

surprises.description: Helly Hansen's China JV revenue grew nearly 70% in Q2, and the brand plans to debut at Dick's House of Sport in 18 doors in October. The preview noted the JV's contribution to prior-quarter pro forma growth and discussed fall/winter orders, but did not anticipate this JV growth rate or the specific retail rollout.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Helly Hansen's China JV revenue (excluded from consolidated results) grew nearly 70% in Q2” and “the brand debuts at Dick's House of Sport in 18 doors in October.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 growth was “>20% pro forma with the China JV” and flagged the fall/winter order book, but gave no Q2 JV growth-rate or Dick's rollout expectation.

in_line: Wrangler U.S. wholesale was flat for a second consecutive quarter, consistent with the preview's concern that a second flat quarter could occur after Q1's +1%.
Kontoor's approximately $450 million cash-from-operations outlook matched the preview's ~$450 million expectation.
The reported plan to close the Lee divestiture and begin the associated repurchase in Q4 remained within the preview's stated 2H26 target window.

surprises.description: Cash ended Q1 at approximately $116 million, above the preview’s $85–90 million base-case range for the quarter-end balance. The call attributed part of the balance to $20 million from stock-option exercises, an additional cash source not included in the preview’s cash-bridge discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Anterix ended the quarter with approximately $116 million in cash and no debt,” bolstered by “$16 million in customer payments and $20 million from stock option exercises.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario projected “cash ~$85–90M”; the preview also framed the FY27 cash bridge around “roughly $30–45M of net cash burn in FY27 absent new signings.”

surprises.description: Management forecast at least single-digit-million-dollar broadband license gains in the following quarter, suggesting gains could arrive sooner than the preview’s description of FY27 revenue recognition as heavily back-end loaded into the CPS Energy Q4 delivery. This is a forecast of gains, not a change to the expected Q1 revenue annuity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects at least single-digit-million dollar broadband license gains in the following quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the entire FY27 revenue ramp to $20.8M consensus is back-end loaded into a single delivery event” and identified “$13M of revenue recognition in Q4 FY2027” on CPS Energy delivery.

surprises.description: The call did not provide a newly signed agreement or contracted-proceeds figure, leaving the preview’s central question about whether utility discussions had converted into deals unanswered. Management instead described active opportunities and accelerating conversations, so the facts do not establish that no agreements were signed.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call cited “nearly a dozen active utility opportunities” and accelerating conversations, but no newly signed agreement or added contracted-proceeds amount is reported in the call facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called new agreements and “dollars of contracted proceeds added” the “entire print,” and said the bar was “roughly $25M+” while “zero new agreements would be a genuine problem.”

surprises.description: Management described nearly a dozen active utility opportunities spanning 7-, 8-, and 9-digit deal sizes, with conversations accelerating over the past two months. That is more specific and more clearly accelerating pipeline commentary than the preview’s base case of constructive pipeline discussion without pricing disclosure, though it is not evidence of signed deals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nearly a dozen active utility opportunities” span “7-digit, 8-digit, and 9-digit deal sizes,” and “conversations [have been] accelerating over the past two months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “pipeline commentary constructive but no pricing disclosure,” and cautioned that “the pipeline is strong” was “the price of admission, not a catalyst.”

surprises.description: Management did not commit to renewing the expiring buyback authorization, but the CFO said she would not be surprised if it were renewed and kept buybacks in the capital-allocation toolkit. That is a more constructive signal than a quiet lapse, while leaving the actual decision unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: The “$226 million buyback authorization expires in late September,” and the CFO “would not be surprised if the program is renewed” while keeping buybacks “in the capital allocation toolkit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had to address “renewal, lapse, or use” of the authorization and described renewal as part of its bull scenario.

surprises.description: Management said 40% of counties had been cleared in the full 10 MHz broadband configuration and expressed confidence it could monetize the entire country. This adds a concrete nationwide-clearing progress measure to the preview’s concern about the pace of 6-to-10 MHz conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has cleared 40% of counties in the full 10 MHz broadband configuration” and expressed “confidence it can monetize 100% of the country.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any hedging … on 6→10 MHz conversion pace” as a bear-case concern and noted that conversion was “in progress across the 219 exchanged / 155 delivered county base.”

in_line: Q1 GAAP revenue was approximately $2 million, essentially matching the preview’s $1.97 million consensus and the expected roughly $2 million quarterly lease-amortization baseline.

The approximately $11 million broadband license-exchange gain was consistent with the preview’s expectation that non-cash spectrum gains could produce a noisy, mechanically strong GAAP earnings headline.
Q1 spectrum-clearing spend of approximately $7 million was broadly consistent with the preview’s annual clearing-cost frame of slightly above FY26’s approximately $27 million.

Management reiterated the valuation-discount argument the preview expected it to address: executed utility transactions averaged approximately $1.40 per MHz POP, compared with $2.50 for the recent AWS-3 auction, while the market capitalization implied approximately $0.60 per MHz POP.

The estimate that approximately 85% of spectrum remained available to monetize was consistent with the preview’s statement that only about 15% was contracted. The SpaceX filing and Anterix’s supportive letter were also anticipated in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q2 EBITDA of about $1.25 million, but Stran reported $551,000. That was a substantial shortfall despite the quarter remaining profitable.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 EBITDA fell to $551,000 from $929,000 in the prior-year quarter; net income was $309,000.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2 2026 estimate: … EBITDA ~$1.25M”; the base scenario also estimated “EBITDA ~$1.25M.”

surprises.description: SLS revenue came in well above the preview’s $8.8 million base estimate and its $9.5 million upside-surprise threshold, although it remained below the $10.8 million year-ago peak.
surprises.fact_evidence: SLS revenue was $10.1 million, compared with $10.8 million in the prior-year quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario estimated “SLS $8.8M”; the preview said “Anything ≥$9.5M is a genuine upside surprise.”

surprises.description: Consolidated revenue exceeded the preview’s estimate and grew faster than its roughly flat-growth base case. The preview had cautioned that the SLS decline would likely keep total growth near zero.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue rose 2.4% year-over-year to $33.4 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2 2026 estimate: revenue $32.7M (+0.4% YoY)”; the base scenario likewise forecast “$32.7M (+0.4%).”

surprises.description: SLS gross margin was well below the preview’s assumed 28.7%, and management now sees a normalized run rate of roughly 26%. The margin still improved year over year, but the reported level and outlook were lower than the preview’s model.
surprises.fact_evidence: SLS gross margin was 24.3%, up from 21%; management guided to a normalized run rate of roughly 26%, citing competitive pricing pressure on larger orders.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “SLS ~28.7% after +690bps of Gander integration gains” and said sustained “31%+” consolidated gross margin would validate the repair.

surprises.description: Core Stran grew, but more slowly than the preview’s base estimate: revenue was $23.3 million versus an estimate of about $23.9 million, and growth was 6.9% rather than the forecast 9.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Stran segment’s Q2 revenue increased 6.9% to $23.3 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario forecast “Core Stran $23.9M (+9.6% YoY).”

in_line: The preview expected a second consecutive profitable quarter; Q2 net income was positive at $309,000.
The preview anticipated a resumed buyback with actual Q2 repurchases; the company repurchased about 131,000 shares for roughly $272,000.
The preview identified the grocery uniform program and nearly seven-figure construction materials contract as expected enterprise wins; management reported both.
The preview flagged the Q4 2026 warrant expiry and its potential to remove overhang and simplify the capital structure; management reiterated that expectation.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $16.1 million, below both the preview’s realistic buy-side bar of $16.8–17.5 million and the approximately $18.0 million published consensus. The shortfall was notable even though revenue reached a company record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue reached a record $16.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: ~$18.0M”; the preview also says the “realistic buy-side bar” was “$16.8–17.5M.”

surprises.description: GAAP results were substantially weaker than expected: the company reported a $0.05-per-share loss rather than the preview’s consensus of positive $0.01 per share, and the operating loss widened. The call attributed the higher operating loss primarily to stock-based compensation in G&A.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss was $1.6 million, or negative $0.05 per share,” versus “$1.1 million, or negative $0.04 per share” a year earlier; “Operating loss widened to $1.6 million from $1.1 million,” primarily due to “higher stock-based compensation within G&A.”

surprises.description: PodcastOne reported portfolio additions through acquisitions of named shows and original launches. The preview discussed possible network M&A, but did not anticipate these specific content additions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expanded its content portfolio through acquisitions including The Magnificent Others with Billy Corgan and Life Happens with Barb and Michelle, plus original series launches.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “a strong pipeline” of potential network acquisitions and listed M&A as a catalyst, but did not identify these content acquisitions or launches.

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $1.6 million was within the preview’s modeled $1.2–1.5 million range and at the top of its $1.2–1.6 million base-case range.
The company’s #6 Podtrac ranking was consistent with the preview, which already cited a #6 position in June and noted that it was ahead of Disney.
The call’s description of summer as slower and calendar Q4 as seasonally strongest aligned with the preview’s characterization of Q1 as the seasonally softest advertising quarter.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $11.9 million, about 9.8% above the $10.84 million consensus estimate, despite the expected year-over-year decline from the completion of large contracts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $11.9 million,” down approximately 31% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $10.84M” consensus.

surprises.description: Management gave a stronger and more specific H2 outlook than the preview’s base case of an unquantified recovery: it expects second-half revenue to be more than 50% above the first half, with profitability building in both Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects second-half 2026 revenue to increase by more than 50% compared to the first half, with profitability building through Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated that “H2 recovery [would be] reiterated but not quantified”; the Q1 commitment was for H2 results to “significantly improve.”

surprises.description: Aerospace growth was markedly stronger than the preview’s cited Q1 growth rate: aerospace revenue rose 71% year over year and volumes rose 79%, versus the preview’s Q1 revenue growth figure of 31%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aerospace LNG volumes sold rose 79% year-over-year and 87% sequentially, with aerospace revenue up 71% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described aerospace as “the one genuinely compounding end market” and cited “+31% Y/Y in Q1.”

surprises.description: Non-power-generation industrial volumes delivered substantial growth, an end-market result the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-power-generation industrial business volumes grew more than 67% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Management projected a high-teens adjusted EBITDA margin for 2027, adding a profitability target to the expected data-center revenue ramp that the preview had not forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management projects 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin “expanding to the high teens,” though no formal 2027 guidance was provided.

surprises.description: The six-month commissioning project was expected to start in late Q2, but LNG deliveries are now set to begin in August 2026, a modest timing slip. Equipment is deploying now, and the project could extend beyond six months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new six-month behind-the-meter LNG data center commissioning contract was executed, with equipment deploying now and LNG deliveries beginning in August 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the commissioning project was “starting late Q2 2026” and running through year-end.

surprises.description: The expected customer-funded equipment build is now fully covered by $25 million of prepayments, with no further payments expected. The preview anticipated customer advances to fund equipment capex but did not specify this full amount or that all prepayments had been received.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has received the full $25 million in customer prepayments for the 2027 data center contract,” funding equipment and mobilization “with no further payments expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “a further $10–12M of equipment capex, funded by customer advance payments.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $0.1 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of breakeven or better.
The 2027 revenue projection of more than $100 million broadly matches the preview’s expected $200 million, two-year data-center contract, or approximately $100 million annually.

surprises.description: Organic independent restaurant case growth was 5.8% in Q4, just below the preview’s 6% bar and below the 6–7% base-case range. The gap was slight, but it fell short of the level the preview said would sustain the share-gain narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 organic independent restaurant case growth was 5.8%; full-year independent case growth was 5.9%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Sub-6% organic at PFG” would “break the share-gain narrative” and listed base-case cases of 6–7%.

surprises.description: Fiscal 2027 guidance came in above the preview’s central EBITDA range: the $2.125–$2.225 billion range has a $2.175 billion midpoint, above the preview’s $2.05–$2.15 billion base case. Sales guidance of $72.5–$73 billion also exceeds the preview’s $71 billion bull-case threshold, although the outlook includes roughly a 2% benefit from the 53rd week.
surprises.fact_evidence: Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for sales of $72.5–$73 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $2.125–$2.225 billion; midpoint growth is 7.2% and 12.7%, respectively, including roughly 2% benefit from a 53rd week.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case called for FY27 EBITDA of “$2.05–2.15B”; its bull case specified FY27 EBITDA “≥$2.15B and sales ≥$71B.”

surprises.description: Management supplied quantified procurement-synergy and margin targets, while the preview said a hard number on Cheney-related synergy or cost relief was needed. Management was confident of reaching or exceeding the high end of the synergy target by FY28.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company targets $120–$125 million in procurement synergies, with management confident it will meet or exceed the high end by fiscal 2028, and expects 50–60 basis points of EBITDA margin enhancement over its three-year plan.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Quantified Cheney synergy/cost relief in Q4 and FY27” was needed and that it “needs a number, not adjectives.”

in_line: Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $587.5 million was at the upper end of guidance, consistent with the preview’s $558–$588 million implied band and expectation for a result in the upper half.
Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.59 was essentially in line with the preview’s $1.60 consensus and within its $1.55–$1.64 estimate range.
The preview expected a modest Q4 revenue miss as its base case; reported sales growth of 6.4% was below the preview’s consensus growth estimate of 7.2%, consistent with that expectation.

surprises.description: LiveOne’s Q1 revenue of $19.3–19.4 million fell short of the $21.23 million consensus and the preview’s roughly $20.7 million base case. The miss was about 9% against consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LiveOne reported Q1 FY2027 consolidated revenue of $19.3-19.4 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue **$21.23M**” and “**~$20.7M**” total in the base case.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was much stronger than the preview’s roughly $1.2 million consolidated base case: consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $4.3 million and audio-division adjusted EBITDA reached a record $6.3 million. That outperformance was partly offset by the fact that Slacker’s result included unusual benefits that management said would not recur at the same level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “record adjusted EBITDA of $6.3 million for its audio division, though consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $4.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “**Adj. EBITDA consolidated** … **~$1.2M**” in the base case; the preview also said it expected the first clean positive consolidated quarter.

surprises.description: PodcastOne’s $16.1 million of quarterly revenue was below the preview’s roughly $17 million base case and the cited $18.03 million Street estimate, despite being a record. This was a notable contributor to the weaker-than-expected consolidated revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PodcastOne delivered record quarterly revenue of $16.1 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “PodcastOne” base case “**~$17.0M**”; the preview also cited “Street has PODC at **~$18.03M** for Q1.”

surprises.description: Slacker’s $4.7 million adjusted EBITDA was not a clean indication of recurring profitability: it was boosted by stock-for-service deals and the elimination of about $1.5 million in past liabilities, and management said margins would return to normal without more such deals. That qualifies the apparent EBITDA beat against the preview’s expectation of a genuinely positive consolidated quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Slacker's Q1 adjusted EBITDA of $4.7 million was heavily boosted by non-recurring stock-for-service deals and elimination of ~$1.5 million in past liabilities, with management indicating margins will revert to normal levels absent further such deals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “**~$1.2M**” consolidated adjusted EBITDA and described it as the “first clean positive quarter”; it also flagged further stock-for-service conversions.

surprises.description: LiveOne disclosed that Amazon represented over $20 million and Paramount more than $27 million in revenues, giving concrete scale to existing partnerships. The preview focused on the need for B2B relationships to convert into quantified dollars but did not anticipate these figures for these partners.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Key existing partnerships are scaling rapidly, with Amazon now representing over $20 million and Paramount surpassing $27 million in revenues.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “B2B pipeline converting to dollars” and “A named, dollar-sized contract is the bull catalyst”; the preview said existing opportunities had “not yet been quantified in revenue.”

surprises.description: The company reported signing a new four-year agreement with a major global retailer, an additional concrete commercial partnership beyond the pipeline opportunities discussed in the preview. The deal was not quantified, so it did not provide the dollar-sized contract detail the preview identified as the strongest catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed a new 4-year retail agreement with a major global retailer”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the B2B opportunities as not yet quantified and said “A named, dollar-sized contract is the bull catalyst.”

surprises.description: LiveOne announced a podcast-only distribution partnership with Netflix and its 700 million members, a new distribution channel the preview had not flagged. The facts do not state the deal’s financial terms or expected revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a podcast-only distribution partnership with Netflix and its 700 million members.”

surprises.description: AI licensing moved from general interest to discussions with 17 companies, with a stated price range and monetization expected to begin next quarter. However, the facts describe discussions rather than a signed licensing deal, so the report stopped short of the signed deal the preview called a genuine catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LiveOne is in discussions with 17 AI companies to license its 500,000+ hours of audio and 250,000+ hours of video content at $100-$500 per hour on a non-exclusive basis, with monetization expected to begin next quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An actual signed deal would be a genuine narrative unlock”; the preview also warned that another quarter of “imminent” without a deal would be a discount.

surprises.description: Management set a new aspirational target of more than $250 million in revenue within three years, alongside a nearer-term goal of exceeding $100 million. The preview discussed the FY2027 guide but did not anticipate these longer-range targets; they are ambitions rather than reported results or a quantified near-term revision.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management set an aspirational target of over $250 million in revenue within three years, with a nearer-term goal of surpassing $100 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY2027 revenue guidance of “**$85–95M+**” and did not state a longer-term revenue target.

in_line: The quarter’s balance-sheet actions were consistent with the preview’s flagged expectation of reduced liabilities and increased equity: management had highlighted those items before the release, and the call reported $5 million of liabilities eliminated and a $7 million increase in stockholders’ equity.

Buyback activity was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation that management would continue repurchases: the call said $7 million of the $12 million program was completed and management intended to keep buying shares.

surprises.description: The preview said the commercial debate centered on whether bem-rusosvir could compete with generic Epclusa and called for specific payer or pricing evidence. Instead, management presented a sizable opportunity—more than $700 million in potential peak U.S. net revenue, a market that could reach $2.5 billion, and strong prescriber-interest survey results—without the supplied facts giving a specific net-price or payer answer.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management projected peak annual U.S. net revenue potential in excess of $700 million and a total U.S. market potentially expandable up to $2.5 billion annually. Market research found 76% of high-volume DAA prescribers would be extremely likely to prescribe bem-rusosvir, while only 6% of surveyed physicians reported no unmet need in current therapies.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The question is net price against a generic incumbent”; “A credible, specific answer on payer conversations ... is what would begin closing the EV gap.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was above the preview’s estimated range: Atea reported $219.5 million, versus an estimate of $208–215 million. The runway through 2027, however, matched the preview’s expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$219.5 million in cash and marketable securities as of June 30, 2026, with a projected cash runway extending through 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash + marketable securities (6/30): $208–215M” and identified runway “through 2027” as an expected outcome.

surprises.description: Management set an NDA target of Q2 2027, contingent on positive C-FORWARD results. That provides a date for a previously unguided filing strategy, but means the filing depends on the second trial rather than the more bullish possibility of filing on C-BEYOND alone in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An NDA submission [is] anticipated in Q2 2027 pending positive results” from C-FORWARD.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “never given an NDA date” and asked whether Atea would file “on C-BEYOND alone, or wait for C-FORWARD”; it called a “2026 filing on C-BEYOND” the most bullish possibility.

surprises.description: For AT-587, management now targets proof of concept in 2027, later than the preview’s expectation of a proof-of-concept milestone around year-end 2026. The Phase 1 start itself was expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Atea initiated the first-in-human Phase 1 trial in July 2026, completed the first cohort, and is “targeting proof of concept in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Phase 1 initiation was guided for mid-2026 and “proof-of-concept was guided for around year-end.”

in_line: C-BEYOND met its endpoints and demonstrated non-inferiority, with 93.9% SVR overall versus 94.8% for Epclusa and an 8-week course for non-cirrhotic patients; the preview had already reported these topline results and the same treatment-duration comparison.
The reported favorable safety profile was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of no drug-related serious adverse events or early discontinuations.
C-FORWARD’s top-line results are expected in early Q1 2027, in line with the preview’s expectation of results in early 2027.
The projected cash runway through 2027 matched the preview’s expectation.

The planned focused sales force of approximately 75–100 personnel and launch anticipated in mid-2028 were consistent with the preview’s discussion of a roughly 75-representative commercial model and a revenue story extending toward 2028.
AT-587’s Phase 1 initiation in mid-2026 was consistent with the preview’s expectation that the trial would start around that time.

surprises.description: The preview estimated June 30 stockholders’ equity at roughly $1.3–2.0 million, below Nasdaq’s $2.5 million minimum. BioCardia instead reported $2.7 million in equity and said it was maintaining Nasdaq compliance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BioCardia ended Q2 2026 with $5.4 million in cash and $2.7 million in equity (maintaining NASDAQ compliance)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Stockholders' equity (6/30/26) … ~$1.3–2.0M — likely below the $2.5M threshold”

surprises.description: The preview estimated cash of about $3.5–4.0 million and expected runway into Q1 2027. BioCardia reported $5.4 million in cash and runway into 2027, a materially stronger cash position than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ended Q2 2026 with $5.4 million in cash … providing runway into 2027”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash (6/30/26) … ~$3.5–4.0M”; “Does the ‘into Q1 2027’ runway survive?”

surprises.description: The preview estimated a quarterly net loss of $2.2–2.4 million, but the reported loss was $1.6 million. That is a substantially smaller loss than expected, even though operating cash use rose slightly year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $1.6 million in Q2 2026 from $2.0 million a year earlier, while cash used in operations rose slightly to $1.7 million from $1.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss … My estimate: −$2.2M to −$2.4M”

surprises.description: The preview estimated R&D expense at about $1.3 million; actual expense was $0.9 million. BioCardia attributed the reduction primarily to closing out the original CARDiAMP heart failure trial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expense decreased $0.5 million to $0.9 million in Q2 2026, primarily due to the closeout of the original CARDiAMP heart failure trial.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the Japan Shonin submission timing to be reaffirmed, but did not anticipate PMDA support for moving toward submission or its assessment that the CARDiAMP trial outcomes were credible. The company also said submission is expected in Q4 2026 and approval is anticipated about 12 months later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PMDA supported BioCardia's advancement to Shonin pre-market regulatory submission … deeming the CARDiAMP trial outcomes credible,” with “submission expected next quarter (Q4 2026) and approval anticipated approximately 12 months after submission.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Japan Shonin submission timing … Company guided Q4 2026”; “Reaffirm Q4 2026”

surprises.description: The preview cited Japanese precedent reimbursement of about $124,000 per procedure. The call cited a comparable cell therapy approved for reimbursement at $326,000 per treatment, a much higher price reference, though the units described are not identical.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Heartseed/ReHeart … approved for reimbursement in July at $326,000 per treatment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Japan precedent reimbursement is cited at $124,000/procedure”

surprises.description: The preview expected CARDiAMP Heart Failure II enrollment to remain slow but estimated 5–8 sites, up from four activated at Q1. The call said only four sites were actively enrolling and management described the pace as resource-driven and “not going at blazing speeds,” with no total enrollment disclosed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only four clinical sites are currently actively enrolling patients”; management described the pace as “resource-driven” and “not going at blazing speeds,” and declined to disclose total enrollment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “4 activated sites at Q1”; “5–8 sites; enrollment still slow”

surprises.description: The preview had noted FDA feedback around the CardiAMP PMA pathway, but the call reported a specific favorable development: FDA meeting minutes say the ongoing Heart Failure II trial may serve as a confirmatory study, reversing prior FDA reluctance to accept a single trial for this indication.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FDA meeting minutes confirmed the ongoing CARDiAMP Heart Failure II trial may support premarket approval as a confirmatory study,” a “shift from prior FDA reluctance to accept a single trial for this indication.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “the stock … rallied ~12% in early June on FDA feedback around the CardiAMP PMA pathway”

surprises.description: The preview mentioned Helix as a potential partnering opportunity but did not anticipate FDA feedback on its regulatory path. The call reported no FDA concerns about safety, performance, or compatibility and agreement on two possible clearance pathways, including de novo approval that could make Helix the first FDA-approved transendocardial biotherapeutic delivery catheter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FDA raised no concerns on Helix catheter safety, device performance, or compatibility, and agreed to two potential pathways for marketing clearance,” with de novo approval “potentially making Helix the first FDA-approved transendocardial biotherapeutic delivery catheter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Partnering (Helix/Heart3D, CardiALLO) … No signed deal; ‘active discussions’”

surprises.description: Management introduced a favorable peer comparison not raised in the preview: it said two Japanese cell-therapy peers each have roughly $250 million market capitalizations despite BioCardia having performed more than 20 times as many clinical procedures as the two peers combined. This is a management valuation argument, not a new deal or financing announcement.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “noted two Japanese cell-therapy peers each carry roughly $250 million market caps despite BioCardia performing over 20 times as many clinical procedures as both combined.”

in_line: The Japan Shonin submission remained expected in Q4 2026, as the preview anticipated.
The initial Japan indication targets approximately 20,000 patients, consistent with the preview’s estimate of an initial approximately 20,000-patient subgroup.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $2.9 million, above the preview’s base case of $1.0–1.5 million and its bull case of $2.0–2.5 million. GAAP net loss also narrowed to $0.01 per share, versus the preview’s consensus loss estimate of $0.05 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company turned EBITDA positive with $1.4 million and adjusted EBITDA of $2.9 million.” GAAP net loss was “$300,000 ($0.01/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” was forecast at “+$1.0–1.5M” in the base case and “+$2.0–2.5M” in the bull case; “Q2 FY26 EPS consensus | $(0.05).”

surprises.description: Emrosi’s calculated average selling price rose about 10% sequentially, exceeding the preview’s expectation of flat-to-slightly-up revenue per prescription. Management also expects further sequential ASP gains in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Emrosi's calculated average selling price increased in Q2 over Q1 (about a 10% boost) after also rising in Q1, with management expecting continued sequential ASP gains in the back half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “net price/Rx flat-to-slightly-up”; the preview said strong Rx growth with “flat/down revenue-per-Rx is a bear print.”

surprises.description: Emrosi revenue reached $8.1 million, modestly above the preview’s $7.5–7.9 million base case, though short of the $8.5 million level the preview identified as a bullish catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Emrosi generated $8.1 million in net revenue in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case forecast “Emrosi” at “$7.5–7.9M”; the catalyst checklist said “above $8.5M” would restore credibility to the FY26 ramp.

surprises.description: High-quality formulary coverage improved to about 38%, up from the 34% level cited in the preview, and a large national plan added Emrosi in early August. The preview had noted no new payer win announced through August 5.
surprises.fact_evidence: “High-quality formulary coverage (single-step edit or better) rose from 34% in Q1 to approximately 38% currently”; “A large national health plan added Emrosi to its formulary in early August.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “only ~60M lives (34%)” had single-step-or-better access and that there was “no new payer win announced in the quarter.”

surprises.description: Journey launched Eurax Cream, a niche anti-itch product, in July despite the preview saying the anticipated niche products had not yet landed and that no new product news had emerged. This is a positive product launch, although the facts do not quantify its expected or actual revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ... launched a niche anti-itch product, Eurax Cream, in July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the two niche products haven't landed yet” and noted “No pre-announcement, no in-licensing deal.”

surprises.description: Emrosi’s dermatology prescriber count rose to more than 4,500 from 3,700 at the end of Q1. The preview highlighted the prior increase to 3,700 but did not set an expectation for another increase of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unique Emrosi dermatology prescribers grew to over 4,500 ... up from 3,700 at the end of Q1.”

in_line: Total revenue of $18.5 million was at the top of the preview’s $17.5–18.5 million buy-side whisper range, rather than clearly above it.
Emrosi prescriptions of approximately 36,000 matched the top of the preview’s 34,000–36,000 base-case range.
The five additional dermatology sales representatives were deployed in July, as the preview expected.
QBREXZA was described as slightly light, but the preview had already flagged base-business erosion and QBREXZA’s access-tier change as risks.

surprises.description: QUELIMMUNE revenue was $615,000, about 12% above the preview’s $550,000 point estimate, and year-over-year growth accelerated to 82% versus the modeled roughly 63%. The result remained within the preview’s $420,000–$720,000 range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 QUELIMMUNE net revenue reached $615,000, an 82% year-over-year increase and an acceleration from the 69% growth rate in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Q2 FY26 QUELIMMUNE net revenue at “$0.55M (range $0.42–$0.72M)” and year-over-year growth at “~+63%.”

surprises.description: The adult AKI trial was slightly below the preview’s 225-patient progress marker, and management now gives completion timing as around year-end 2026 or in Q1 2027 rather than simply around year-end. Enrollment of 8–12 patients per month is also below management’s new 15–20-per-month target, though more sites are expected to come online.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The neutralize AKI adult pivotal trial has enrolled 223 of a targeted 339 patients, with enrollment expected to complete around year-end 2026 or in Q1 2027”; current enrollment is “roughly 8-12 patients per month,” with management targeting “15-20 per month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “A Q2 number below ~225 puts the YE2026 completion target — and the 2027 PMA — at risk,” and described enrollment completion as “~YE2026.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was approximately $7 million, above the preview’s expected $6.0–$6.6 million range. The company still reported ongoing cash burn, so the surprise is the higher balance rather than an improvement in the funding outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash fell to approximately $7 million at June 30, 2026 from $12 million at December 31, 2025, reflecting an ongoing quarterly cash burn.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Cash (period end)” at “$6.0–6.6M.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses reached $4.4 million, slightly above the preview’s implied combined R&D and G&A estimate of $3.8–$4.3 million. The increase was driven by trial R&D and higher G&A, although the reported net loss remained within the preview’s forecast range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 operating expenses more than doubled to $4.4 million from $2.1 million a year earlier, driven by increased clinical trial R&D and higher G&A costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated R&D of “$2.2–2.5M” and G&A of “$1.6–1.8M.”

in_line: Six-month net revenue was $1.1 million and management said the company remained on track for its $2 million FY2026 target, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the target would be reaffirmed.
The PMA submission timeline remained late 2027, in line with the preview’s expectation of a 2027 PMA.
Gross margin remained above 90%, within the preview’s 88–91% estimate.
Net loss of $3.7 million and EPS of -$0.91 were within the preview’s respective $3.3–$3.7 million and -$0.83 to -$0.93 ranges.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $2.05 billion, about 3% above the preview’s $1.98–$1.99 billion consensus, and reached the top of company guidance. This was a clear beat, though it was below the preview’s bull scenario of $2.05–$2.10 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue was a record $2.05 billion”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus ~ $1.98–1.99B”; Q4 guidance was “$1.91B – $2.05B.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 exceeded the preview’s working consensus of $1.62 and its stated effective buy-side bar of $1.72, although it was only slightly above that higher bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $1.74”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Model against $1.62 as the working number and $1.72 (guide high) as the effective buy-side bar.”

surprises.description: The data center and communications segment appears to have delivered about $1.62 billion of Q4 revenue—79% of the $2.05 billion total—versus the preview’s roughly $1.50 billion estimate. The data center business also grew 56% year over year and 24% sequentially, stronger than the preview’s expected roughly 10% sequential increase for the segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The data center and communications segment, 79% of Q4 revenue, grew 59% year-over-year”; “the data center business alone [was] up 56% year-over-year and 24% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Datacenter & Comms revenue: ~$1.50B”; “Another ~10% sequential step puts it at ~$1.50B.”

surprises.description: The Q1 FY27 revenue outlook was stronger than the preview’s roughly $2.15 billion reference point: the range is $2.2–$2.4 billion, with a $2.3 billion midpoint. The range clears the preview’s $2.25 billion bull-case threshold at its midpoint, though not at its low end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q1 FY27 revenue to $2.2–$2.4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue guide vs. ~$2.15B”; “>$2.25B validates the street’s $9.66B FY27.”

surprises.description: Management added a target to reach its first $3 billion revenue quarter by the end of FY27, a stronger stated exit-rate ambition than the preview’s discussion of FY27 growth exceeding FY26 and its $9.66 billion full-year model.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects to reach its first $3 billion revenue quarter by the end of fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sell-side FY2027 modeling sits at $9.66B revenue (+36.9%)”; management had said FY27 growth would “exceed” FY26’s roughly 21%.

surprises.description: Management expects data center revenue growth to exceed 80% year over year in the current quarter, a particularly strong near-term growth rate not specified in the preview’s Q1 expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects data center revenue growth to exceed 80% year-over-year in the current quarter.”

surprises.description: Q4 capex reached $556 million, well above the preview’s $350–$400 million quarterly step-up framework. The stated roughly 18-month payback on data center investments helps explain the spending, but the outlay is still substantially larger than the preview contemplated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 capital expenditures surged to $556 million (from $131 million a year ago) with a roughly 18-month payback on data center investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A capex step to $350–400M/qtr is demand confirmation but pressures FCF.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated leverage of 0.5x, while management reported 0.7x, modestly above that expected level despite substantial debt payments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Debt leverage was cut to 0.7x from 2.0x a year earlier via $513 million in debt payments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Balance sheet supports either: ~$3B cash post-NVIDIA, leverage down to 0.5x from 2.1x a year ago.”

surprises.description: Management outlined additional product ramps, including ultra-high-power CW lasers beginning in the December quarter and ThermaDit thermal management in the second half of calendar 2027; these specific revenue streams were not in the preview’s roadmap discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New revenue streams are set to ramp, including ... ultra high-power CW lasers beginning in the December quarter ... and thermal management (ThermaDit) in the second half of calendar 2027.”

in_line: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 40.2%, close to the preview’s roughly 40.0% consensus; it did not deliver the 41%+ print identified as the strongest bull signal.
The InP capacity expansion was broadly as previewed: the company remained on track to double output a quarter ahead of plan and to expand capacity further by the end of 2027.

Bookings and customer commitments matched the preview’s expectation of demand visibility into 2028 and long-term supply agreements: the call cited purchase orders into calendar 2028 and take-or-pay LTAs through the end of the decade.
The multi-rail systems ramp in the first half of calendar 2027 was consistent with the preview’s expectation that multi-rail revenue would begin in 2027.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was only about $243,000, well below the preview’s roughly $600,000 floor for keeping the FY26 target math credible and the $500,000–$900,000 base-case range. First-half adjusted EBITDA was a loss of about $224,000, making the preview’s expectation of year-over-year improvement in Q2 and its FY26 ambition materially harder to achieve.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to about $243,000 in Q2 2026 from roughly $628,000 a year earlier, and first-half adjusted EBITDA was a loss of about $224,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything below ~$0.6M in Q2 puts the ‘surpass $2.9M’ ambition mathematically under strain”; the base case expected “$0.5–0.9M” of adjusted EBITDA.

surprises.description: GAAP results were worse than the preview’s EPS estimate: DLPN reported a $0.13 loss per share versus an expected $0.07 loss. Net loss also widened year over year to $1.6 million from $1.4 million, rather than showing the improvement implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loss per share was $0.13 in Q2 2026 on ~12.8 million weighted average shares, up from ~11.2 million shares a year earlier”; “net loss of $1.6 million versus $1.4 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS | $(0.07)” versus Q2’25 actual “$(0.12)” and described as “improving.”

surprises.description: The quarter included roughly $720,000–$800,000 in retention bonuses and litigation-related legal fees that the preview had not anticipated. Management said both costs are expected to roll off in Q3, so the reported burden is unusually high but temporary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $360,000-$400,000 of one-time retention bonuses and another ~$360,000-$400,000 of litigation-related legal fees, both expected to roll off in Q3.”

surprises.description: Cash was $7.7 million at June 30, above the $6.3 million reported at March 31 and therefore a build over the quarter, despite being below the $8.8 million year-end balance. That is better than the preview’s cash-draw concern and matches its stated positive signal for cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents declined to $7.7 million as of June 30, 2026, from $8.8 million at year-end 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash at 6/30/26 vs. $6.3M at 3/31/26 — direction of travel matters more than the level: a build supports the FCF claim, a draw revives the raise risk.”

surprises.description: Management identified an additional roughly $1 million of annual savings when the New York and Los Angeles leases roll off late next year, a source of future free-cash-flow improvement that the preview did not flag. The preview had already noted the expected $2.2 million annual debt-service savings, so that portion is not new.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects meaningfully improved free cash flow from bank debt maturing in about two years (freeing ~$2.2 million annually in principal and interest) and NY/LA leases rolling off in late next year (saving ~$1 million annually).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “payoff saves $2.2M/yr in principal and interest,” but did not mention savings from the NY/LA leases.

surprises.description: Management highlighted approximately $127 million in NOLs, saying they would let nearly all future cost savings flow directly to the bottom line. The preview did not discuss this potential tax benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company holds approximately $127 million in NOLs, allowing nearly all future cost savings to flow directly to the bottom line.”

surprises.description: The CEO said he expects to own more than 5% of DLPN within a week or two under his 10b5-1 buying plan, a stronger ownership signal than the preview’s description of small, immaterial regular purchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Bill O'Dowd expects to own over 5% of DLPN common stock within the next week or two under his 10b5-1 buying plan, signaling insider alignment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described recent purchases as “small, regular open-market blocks” and said “the dollar amounts are immaterial.”

surprises.description: Beyond the expected first DealMaker venture deal before year-end, management said it had identified two candidates and aspired to complete three to four capital-light equity-plus-fee ventures annually within a few years. That adds pipeline detail and a longer-term scale ambition not stated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects its first Dealmaker venture deal in market before year-end, with two candidates identified and an aspiration to complete 3-4 capital-light equity-plus-fee ventures annually within a few years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “targeted a first deal announcement by YE2026” and described an “~six-figure annual marketing fee per deal.”

in_line: Revenue was $14.4 million versus $14.5 million consensus, with 2.5% year-over-year growth versus the preview’s 2.8% implied growth—essentially in line with the modest-growth expectation.
The expected first DealMaker deal before year-end remained the stated timing; the preview had identified YE2026 as management’s target.

surprises.description: GO reported adjusted EBITDA of $65.7 million and adjusted EPS of $0.20, well above the preview’s roughly $56 million and $0.12 consensus estimates and above company outlook. The earnings beat was substantially larger than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $65.7 million” and “adjusted EPS was $0.20, both above outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$56M” and “Diluted adj. EPS $0.12”; company outlook was “$55–58M” EBITDA and “$0.11–$0.13” EPS.

surprises.description: Comparable sales fell just 0.3%, far better than the preview’s roughly 1.5% decline expectation and the company’s 1.5%–2.0% decline outlook. The decline also improved 70 basis points sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable store sales down 30 basis points, a 70bp sequential improvement from Q1 and beating the outlook for a 1.5%-2% decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 comps were expected at “~−1.5%” with company guidance of “−1.5% to −2.0%”; the preview’s functional bar was “comps no worse than −1.5%.”

surprises.description: GO raised the low end of its full-year outlook, including comps from −2.0% to −0.5%, and lifted the low end of EBITDA guidance from $220 million to $225 million. This was stronger than the preview’s central concern that the existing FY26 range might only be reaffirmed or trimmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised the low end of full-year guidance to comps of -0.5% to 0.0%, net sales of $4.7-$4.72 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $225-$235 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.51-$0.55.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY guidance of “−2.0% to 0.0%” comps and “$220–235M” adjusted EBITDA, and flagged whether it would be “reaffirmed vs. trimmed.”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $1.19 billion, about $23 million above the preview’s $1.167 billion consensus, and grew 1% rather than declining year over year as expected. This was a clear top-line beat alongside the stronger comps.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 1% to $1.19 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 net sales consensus was “$1,167M”; the preview listed Q2 FY25 sales of “$1,180M” and expected “−1.1%” year-over-year.

surprises.description: The opportunistic assortment gained momentum faster than the preview’s turnaround test required: its comps accelerated about 500 basis points from Q1’s start, and total company comps turned positive in May and June. The preview identified rebuilding opportunistic units per transaction as a key condition for recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Opportunistic comp sales accelerated about 500bp from the start of Q1 and op mix expanded over 300bp, lifting total company comps into positive territory in May and June.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case required “units-per-transaction to stop deteriorating” through “the opportunistic branded closeout assortment genuinely rebuilding.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 30.2%, above the preview’s 29.8%–30.0% outlook range, and its year-over-year decline was only 30 basis points rather than the roughly 70-basis-point contraction expected. Promotions and closure markdowns still weighed on the year-over-year result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin of 30.2% exceeded the 29.8%-30.0% outlook but declined 30bp year-over-year due to promotions and store-closure markdowns.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “29.8%–30.0%” and expected gross margin down “~−70bp YoY.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the closed-store savings to be visible in Q2, but the call said most of the $12 million annualized EBITDA benefit from the 36 closures is expected in 2027. The closures remain on track, but the timing of most of the benefit is later than the preview suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The closure of 36 underperforming stores completed in April remains on track to eliminate a $12 million annualized adjusted EBITDA drag, with most benefit expected in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the closures were completed by April, cited the “~$12M annualized EBITDA benefit,” and said “Q2 is the first quarter where it should be visible in SG&A and four-wall margin.”

surprises.description: A multi-state cyclospora outbreak is expected to reduce Q3 company comps by about 100 basis points, an unanticipated headwind for the quarter the preview identified as the most important guidance issue. The company said its products were not involved in any recalls.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A multi-state cyclospora outbreak is expected to create a roughly 100bp headwind to total company comps in Q3, though products were not involved in any recalls.”

in_line: The basket decline was about 2.1%, close to the preview’s bull-case threshold of less than 2% and better than its base-case expectation of a 2.5%–3% ticket decline; it also improved roughly 100 basis points sequentially.
The $20 million incremental promotional investment is set to taper fully by the end of Q3, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that promotions would wind down in the second half.
All 36 planned store closures were completed by April, as the preview expected.
The CFO transition to Ian Ferry was anticipated in the preview; the call reported Chris Miller’s retirement and Ferry’s replacement.

surprises.description: Yartemlia net sales reached $28.5 million in its first full quarter, far above the preview’s $15.5 million base case and even its $18–21 million bull range. Sequential net sales growth of 188% also substantially exceeded the preview’s roughly $12–13 million “no-acceleration” benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026, its first full quarter on the market,” generated “$28.5 million in net sales”; “net sales grew 188%” quarter over quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s “My base case” was “$15.5M”; its bull scenario was “$18–21M,” and it called roughly “$12–13M” the “no-acceleration” number.

surprises.description: The launch reached 73 ordering accounts by June 30, well above the preview’s 50-plus account level that it said would feel good. P&T approval had also reached roughly 55–60% across tracked top-center cohorts, supporting strong breadth of adoption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “73 unique accounts had ordered Yartemlia (up 143.5% since March 31),” with P&T committee approval at “roughly 55-60% across tracked top transplant center cohorts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “I’d want 50+ to feel good,” compared with 30 unique ordering accounts at Q1 exit.

surprises.description: The company reported $1.8 million of adjusted net income, or $0.02 per share, rather than the adjusted loss the preview expected. The reported $13.2 million GAAP profit was partly a $12.1 million non-cash derivative gain, but the adjusted result was still positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP net income was $13.2 million ($0.18/share), but non-GAAP adjusted net income was only $1.8 million ($0.02/share) after excluding a $12.1 million non-cash mark-to-market derivative gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s adjusted EPS “My base case” was “–$0.20”; it also said a second large non-cash gain and headline GAAP profit were likely, while cautioning not to read that as an operating beat.

surprises.description: Company-wide operations generated positive cash flow in Q2, much earlier than the preview’s expected timeline for company-wide breakeven. The mid-2027 target itself is broadly consistent with the preview’s expected Q3 2027 timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Company-wide operations generated $4.1 million of positive cash flow in Q2,” supporting guidance to reach company-wide cash flow positivity “by mid-2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management targeted “company-wide positive cash flow within 18 months (~Q3 2027)” and expected $115–125 million of cash at June 30.

surprises.description: Cash and investments ended Q2 at $132 million, above the preview’s expected $115–125 million range. This is a positive cash-position surprise separate from the quarter’s positive operating cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $132 million in cash and investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I’d expect ~$115–125M cash at June 30.”

surprises.description: Omeros disclosed a substantial July repurchase of its 9.5% 2029 convertible notes, reducing principal outstanding by 43% and eliminating future interest expense. The preview discussed the notes and earlier capital actions but did not anticipate this transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In July, Omeros repurchased $30.5 million of its 9.5% 2029 convertible notes for $60.2 million,” cutting outstanding principal “43% to $40.3 million,” eliminating “$8.6 million in future interest,” and reducing conversion shares from 11.4 million to 6.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the 2029 notes as having “$70.8M principal” and discussed retiring the 2026 converts and buying back shares, but did not forecast a 2029-note repurchase.

surprises.description: Adult utilization was much more dominant than the preview’s discussion of a higher-than-expected pediatric mix suggested: adults represented about 95% of sales, versus the historical 85% adult share. Faster adult growth is favorable to the adult launch, but the much smaller pediatric share makes the current mix less favorable to pediatric-market expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adult utilization grew at more than twice the rate of pediatric utilization, with adults now representing approximately 95% of Yartemlia sales,” approaching the historical “85%/15% adult-pediatric split.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Omeros “already sees a higher-than-expected pediatric mix vs. the historical 85/15 adult-pediatric split.”

in_line: Gross-to-net was 11.5%, close to the preview’s Q1 11% and its bull-case expectation of roughly 11–13%; it did not drift above the high teens the preview flagged as a concern.
The company’s mid-2027 cash-flow-positivity guidance is close to the preview’s expected timing of roughly Q3 2027.
The EMA re-examination request was already known in the preview; the call facts say Omeros requested re-examination, with no reported change in status.
The permanent J-code and NTAP were already described in the preview, including the July 1 and October 1 effective dates and the up-to-$287,079 payment amount.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case anticipated advanced discussions with multiple parties and a term sheet expected before the October 30 deadline. Instead, Spruce reported no committed refinancing arrangements at quarter end and only preliminary lender discussions for SP1, leaving the debt maturities unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “No committed refinancing arrangements were in place at quarter end”; “only preliminary lender discussions underway for SP1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “advanced discussions with multiple parties, term sheet expected before Oct 30.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $30.3 million, below the preview’s $31.5 million estimate, and fell 9% year over year rather than the preview’s modeled 5% decline. The call attributed the weakness partly to lower SP5 SREC production and a slower-than-expected Spruce Pro revenue ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 9% year-over-year to $30.3 million”; drivers included “lower SP5 SREC production” and “a slower-than-expected Spruce Pro revenue ramp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 revenue of “$31.5M” and a “-5%” year-over-year change.

surprises.description: Operating EBITDA reached $26.5 million, exceeding the preview’s $24.0 million estimate and the $23–25 million base-case range. This was stronger than the preview’s expected solid but broadly in-line operating quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating EBITDA rose to $26.5 million from $24.6 million a year earlier”; core operating expenses fell 21% to $13.8 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Operating EBITDA $24.0M” and gave a base-case range of “$23–25M.”

surprises.description: Spruce reported net income of $3.3 million, or $0.14 per diluted share, instead of the preview’s expected $3.5 million net loss and $0.19 loss per share. The call said favorable non-cash interest-rate-swap valuation changes partly aided the reversal, consistent with the preview’s warning that EPS could be affected by swap marks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to stockholders of $3.3 million ($0.14 per diluted share)”; results were “partly aided by favorable non-cash interest rate swap valuation changes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss attrib. to stockholders -$3.5M” and “EPS -$0.19.”

surprises.description: Unrestricted cash ended the quarter at $44.7 million, below the preview’s expected $46–50 million range. It remained above the preview’s roughly $42 million level identified as a particularly concerning cash threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$81.5 million in total cash (including $44.7 million unrestricted).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Unrestricted cash $46–50M” and said cash below “~$42M” would compress the runway meaningfully.

in_line: The going-concern qualification remained in place, as the preview’s base case expected the language to be unchanged; the reported negative working capital also followed from the debt reclassification described in the call.
Full-year guidance was reaffirmed, consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would keep FY2026 operating expectations generally consistent with prior guidance.
The expected second-half O&M activity shift remained part of the outlook: management said first-half O&M favorability was expected to reverse with higher second-half service activity.

Underlying contracted performance showed the sort of Q2 generation strength the preview anticipated: combined PPA and lease revenue rose 2% year over year and portfolio generation increased to about 196,000 MWh from 187,000.

surprises.description: SKYX reported Q2 revenue of $25.3 million, about 5% above the published $24.07 million consensus, though slightly below the preview’s ~$25.4 million whisper estimate. That makes the result a modest beat against published consensus, not a clear beat against the broader expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 14% sequentially to a record $25.3 million, up 10% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $24.07M (Investing.com)” and “Treat $24–25.4M as the real goalpost band.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 29%, below the preview’s roughly 30% expectation, as sales mix held back gross profit growth despite revenue growth. Management expects higher-margin products and B2B supply to help in the back half, but the current-quarter margin result was weaker than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 29% in Q2 2026 from 30% in Q1, with only 4% year-over-year gross profit growth to $7.3 million, lagging revenue growth as sales mix weighed on margins.” Management said higher-margin products are expected to improve margins in the back half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~30% (no formal consensus)” and “Gross margin vs. the 30% line.”

surprises.description: The announced B2B pipeline has not yet produced meaningful revenue: project shipments are only beginning this quarter and are expected to continue into later periods. The preview sought evidence of B2B conversion, including shipped-unit figures, so the lack of quantified current contribution leaves that conversion less established than a bullish outcome would have implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “B2B project shipments are only beginning this quarter and will continue into Q4, Q1, and 2027, meaning meaningful revenue from the announced pipeline remains largely ahead.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “B2B conversion — does the pipeline show up as revenue?” and “A specific number is bullish; another qualitative list is not.”

surprises.description: Gen 3 appears less certain and potentially later than the preview’s expectation that production would be landing around mid-to-third quarter. Production samples are testing well, but mass production still depends on regulatory approvals and management gave only a hoped-for next-quarter launch, without a firm timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Gen 3 monitoring product has working production samples testing well but remains dependent on FCC and other regulatory code approvals before mass production, with no firm timeline beyond a hoped-for next-quarter launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guided to ‘mid-to-third quarter 2026’ production — meaning it should be landing now.”

in_line: Operating cash use fell to $3.7 million from $6 million in Q1, consistent with the preview’s view that Q2 burn needed to be below roughly $4 million.
Management reaffirmed the goal of becoming cash flow positive as it exits 2026, as the preview’s base case expected.
Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash of $27.7 million was within the preview’s expected $26–28 million ending-cash range.
The company reaffirmed its target of delivering over 100,000 units by the end of 2026, consistent with the preview’s stated target.
The Europhase licensing agreement and the Group OTT, France, and Prague hotel activity were already identified in the preview as existing pipeline developments.

surprises.description: KOMZIFTI recorded 115 new patient starts, above the preview’s 95–110 base-case range and its 100+ threshold for meaningful demand. That suggests a stronger quarter of new-patient demand than the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 115 new patient starts”; new patient starts grew “about 35% quarter-over-quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New patient starts” base case of “95–110”; the preview said “100+ starts into a soft class quarter” would be genuine share capture.

surprises.description: Kura said KOMZIFTI captured a majority of new patient starts in the relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant menin inhibitor market, a stronger share claim than the preview’s roughly 40% Q1 figure. This is a favorable resolution of the preview’s debate about Kura’s share relative to Syndax’s broader market-share claim.
surprises.fact_evidence: KOMZIFTI was “capturing a majority share of new patient starts” in the relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant AML menin inhibitor market.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Kura claimed ~40% share of R/R NPM1 new starts in Q1” and “Tonight’s new-start number adjudicates it.”

surprises.description: Prescription growth outpaced new-start growth, and management said the results were not driven by inventory or one-time stocking. That is stronger evidence of ongoing use than a quarter whose sales were boosted by channel fill, and addresses a central concern in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New patient starts grew about 35% quarter-over-quarter while total prescriptions grew about 60%,” with “no meaningful inventory or one-time stocking effects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether Q1 was “a stocking-and-switching pop or a real launch curve” and called a “rising scripts-per-start ratio” the “single most bullish quiet datapoint.”

surprises.description: KOMZIFTI had preferred status requiring step-through before other menin inhibitors for approximately 16 million covered lives, while more than 95% of covered lives had no label restrictions. The preview did not flag this access position, so it adds a favorable commercial detail beyond the launch metrics it highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 95% of covered lives” had “no label restrictions,” and “approximately 16 million lives carry preferred status requiring patients to step through KOMZIFTI before other menin inhibitors.”

surprises.description: Komet-007 data showed high response and survival figures, including 94% overall survival at 12 months and median overall survival not reached after 17.6 months. The preview did not identify this data as an expected catalyst or provide an efficacy benchmark for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: In 99 patients, “96% ORR” was reported in relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant AML, with “94% overall survival at 12 months” and “median OS not reached at 17.6 months follow-up,” versus historical 12-month OS of “45%-80%.”

surprises.description: Darlifarnib showed a 44% response rate in cabozantinib-exposed RCC, compared with the 17%–22% historical range cited on the call, and reported 33%–50% ORR with 13-month median PFS in cabo-naive RCC. The preview mentioned pending KCRS RCC data but did not set expectations for these efficacy results.
surprises.fact_evidence: Darlifarnib demonstrated a “44% objective response rate and 94% disease control rate in cabozantinib-exposed RCC (versus 17%-22% historical),” and “33%-50% ORR with 13-month median PFS in cabo-naive RCC.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any darlifarnib (KO-2806) development decision after the July 24 KCRS RCC data,” without giving an expected efficacy result.

surprises.description: About 40% of new patient starts involved physician-initiated combinations with venetoclax/azacitidine or FLT3 inhibitors, despite promotion being limited to the approved monotherapy indication. The preview mentioned combination use as a possible bull-case signal but did not anticipate this level of physician-initiated use.
