That is progress beyond a general opportunity pipeline, but it was still under negotiation rather than a signed, dated H2 contract—the kind of conversion the preview said was needed to de-risk the ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In active negotiation on an eight-figure hyperspectral microwave sounding contract tied to its HIMSS payload, expected to be awarded within about a month and confirmed to be a US government (NOAA pipeline) opportunity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side needs a production-scale award, not another pilot extension”; “Bull needs a dated, contracted H2 backlog — not ‘$150M+ of NOAA opportunity.’”

surprises.description: Spire reported RFGL awards from four new international customers and said it had increased RFGL capacity roughly tenfold year-to-date, operational traction the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Spire won RFGL awards from four new international customers in Q2 (on top of five US and three international awards in Q1), increased RFGL capacity roughly 10x year-to-date.”

surprises.description: Spire reported an approximately $12.4 million award in the dismissed Northstar arbitration, an unanticipated positive item not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Was awarded approximately $12.4 million in the dismissed Northstar arbitration.”

in_line: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $75–85 million, as the preview’s base case expected.
Adjusted EBITDA of negative $8.6 million was within the preview’s approximately negative $8–9 million estimate.
Break-even timing remained late 2026 to early 2027, consistent with the preview’s Q4 2026–Q1 2027 expectation.

surprises.description: Total adjusted EBITDA reached a record $249 million, well above the preview’s $224 million estimate and the company’s roughly $223 million guidance midpoint. The $27 million tariff refund, which the preview did not anticipate, more than accounts for the gap: excluding it, EBITDA was about $222 million, roughly in line with the estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA grew 19% to a record $249 million and included a favorable $27 million of tariff refunds, primarily received by ADI, which will not recur for the remainder of 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj EBITDA $224M”; company guidance midpoint “$223M.” The preview also said, “Section 232 tariffs were assessed as non-material.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.83, above the preview’s $0.75 estimate and the company’s $0.71–$0.75 guidance range. That is a clear upside beat, though the call facts do not specify how much the tariff refund contributed to EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total adjusted EPS grew 26% year-over-year to $0.83.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj EPS $0.75”; company guidance was “$0.71–0.75 adj.”

surprises.description: The new standalone FY2026 revenue guide of $2.9–$2.95 billion is below the preview’s $3.0–$3.05 billion bogey. The $605–$625 million EBITDA guide overlaps the preview’s $610–$630 million bogey, but has a lower midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 stand-alone revenue is guided to $2.9–$2.95 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $605–$625 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bogey: ~$3.0–3.05B revenue, ~$610–630M adj EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Management now expects a large OEM security customer’s vertical integration to reduce second-half revenue by $40–$50 million versus the prior year. The preview did not flag this customer-specific volume loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reduced volumes from a large OEM security customer pursuing vertical integration are expected to cut second-half revenue by $40 million to $50 million versus the prior year.”

surprises.description: Products & Solutions revenue grew 4%, below the preview’s 7% growth estimate. The segment’s growth therefore fell short even as its margin performance was better than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Products & Solutions segment posted 4% revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Products & Solutions revenue of “$712M” versus “$666M” a year earlier, or “+7%.”

surprises.description: Products & Solutions gross margin rose to 43.6%, up 70 basis points year over year, exceeding the preview’s 43.2% estimate and 30-basis-point expansion forecast. The 13th consecutive quarter of expansion itself was expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin reached “43.6% (up 70 bps YoY, up 100 bps sequentially)” and it was the “13th consecutive quarter of year-over-year gross margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “P&S gross margin” at “43.2%,” up “+30bp,” and said it “Would be 13th straight quarter of expansion.”

surprises.description: The preview expected price and cost to still be lagging but to cross over in the second half. Management instead warned that rising input costs will pressure Q3 gross margin and said another consecutive quarter of gross profit growth is uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged rising costs for “memory, metals, PCBs, semiconductors, shipping” as a Q3 gross-margin headwind, and warned that a 14th consecutive quarter of gross profit growth is uncertain as price increases lag cost inflation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was that “price/cost still lagging but crossing over in H2”; it also identified price/cost crossover as a key issue.

surprises.description: Total Q2 revenue was just under $2 billion, above the preview’s $1.935 billion estimate and the company’s guidance ceiling of $1.940 billion. It was nevertheless roughly in line with the preview’s approximately $1.98 billion MarketScreener consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 2% year-over-year to just under $2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Total revenue” at “$1,935M” and cited company guidance of “$1,916–1,940M”; it also listed MarketScreener consensus at “~$1.98B.”

in_line: The 13th consecutive quarter of year-over-year Products & Solutions gross-margin expansion occurred as the preview expected, although the margin increase was larger than forecast.
The $900 million Term Loan B repayment and an additional roughly $200 million repayment in Q3 were broadly in line with the preview’s expected deleveraging plan.
Q2 revenue was roughly in line with the preview’s approximately $1.98 billion MarketScreener consensus, despite exceeding the preview’s own estimate and the company’s guidance range.

surprises.description: June-quarter revenue was $1.8 million, flat year over year and sequentially, rather than the preview’s roughly $2.0 million estimate and expected modest growth. It was also about 22% below the $2.30 million consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 revenue ... was $1.8 million, effectively flat both year-over-year and sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus: $2.30M”; “My estimate: $2.0M”; the preview projected “+28%” year-over-year and “+21%” sequentially at consensus, and “+11%” and “+5%” in its own estimate.

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 13%, well above the preview’s 6–8% estimate and above its bull-case threshold of 10%. The company also recorded its third consecutive quarter of positive gross profit, strengthening the margin trend beyond the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 13% in the quarter versus 9% a year earlier, marking the third consecutive quarter of positive gross profit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “6–8%” gross margin and described “GM > 10%” as part of its bull case.

surprises.description: Cash and marketable securities at quarter-end were $15.2 million, above the preview’s $11.5–12.5 million estimate, even before adding the recently announced financing. That leaves the pre-financing balance roughly $2.7–3.7 million higher than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “As of June 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities totaled only $15.2 million, which does not include the recently announced financing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash @ 6/30/26” at “$11.5–12.5M” and said that estimate “excludes July placement.”

surprises.description: Management reported that the commercial pipeline had doubled over five to six months and that several opportunities had already been won in the current quarter, with expected H2 revenue benefit. The preview highlighted conversion of hospital access into accounts as a key uncertainty but did not anticipate this pipeline growth and near-term wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated the commercial pipeline has doubled over the last five to six months, with several opportunities already won in the current quarter expected to boost H2 revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the gap between ‘access to 7,000 hospitals’ and ~$2M of quarterly revenue is the entire bear thesis” and called for watching whether GPO agreements convert into installed accounts.

surprises.description: The company reported that its international partnerships cover more than 40 countries, a concrete measure of commercial reach that the preview did not identify or quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its international partnerships now cover more than 40 countries.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed calendar 2026 revenue guidance of $8 million, as the preview’s key watch item expected.
Management reaffirmed 2027 revenue guidance of $16–18 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation; Gen 2 approval remains expected in H2 2026, with Q4 still within that window.

The $7.9 million net loss was close to the preview’s approximately $7.8 million consensus-implied loss and $8.0 million estimate; the split-adjusted $11 loss per share was also close to its $11.20 estimate.
The up-to-$30 million financing, including $10 million upfront and additional proceeds contingent on warrant exercises, matched the financing structure already described in the preview.
The third major national GPO agreement was anticipated in the preview, which noted the existing Premier and Vizient relationships and the addition of a third agreement.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $2.9 million, well below the preview’s $3.9–4.5 million base case. The company attributed the sequential decline to the intentional wind-down of contract manufacturing, but the preview had already anticipated CMO exits and still expected higher revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined approximately 29% sequentially to about $2.9 million from $4.1 million in Q1 2026, reflecting the intentional wind-down of contract manufacturing volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue” base case: “$3.9–4.5M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was a $3.5 million loss, worse than the preview’s expected $2.3–2.7 million loss. This was also worse than the preview’s bear-case range of a $2.8–3.4 million loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA worsened to negative $3.5 million in Q2 2026 from negative $2.6 million in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA” base case: “$(2.3)–(2.7)M”; bear case: “$(2.8)–(3.4)M.”

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter at $6.1 million, below the preview’s $7–10 million range and below its cited $6.5 million level of particular concern. The supplied facts do not state whether a financing was announced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $6.1 million in cash and cash equivalents and no outstanding debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Cash base case: “$7–10M”; the preview also said, “Below ~$6.5M and the next financing is imminent, not theoretical.”

surprises.description: Management acknowledged that price increases are driving some customers to lower-cost suppliers and that gross-margin improvement has been slower than planned. That is a setback relative to the preview’s expectation that CMO exits and repricing would produce a gross-margin inflection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acknowledged that pricing increases have caused some customers to leave for lower-cost suppliers and that gross margin improvement has been slower than planned.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “gross margin inflection from the contract-manufacturing exit” and said, “gross loss narrows toward breakeven on CMO repricing.”

surprises.description: The reported gross loss was within the preview’s expected range, but its improvement included a substantial one-time excise-tax recovery, partly offset by a one-time inventory write-off. That makes the reported narrowing less clearly indicative of recurring margin progress than the preview’s CMO-exit thesis implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross loss narrowed to $0.3 million from a $0.6 million gross loss in both Q1 2026 and Q2 2025”; the result “benefited from a one-time $692,000 MSA NPM excise tax recovery, partially offset by a $196,000 one-time write-off of aged inventory, both deemed non-recurring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Gross profit/(loss) base case: “$(0.3)–(0.6)M.”

surprises.description: Operating loss was $3.3 million, just outside the preview’s expected $2.8–3.2 million loss range. The preview had anticipated a roughly flat-to-slightly-improved loss versus Q1, rather than a sequential increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating loss and net loss from continuing operations each rose to $3.3 million in Q2 from $3.0 million in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Operating loss base case: “$(2.8)–(3.2)M.”

surprises.description: Management said second-half branded-product shipments should be significantly larger than first-half shipments, positioning the company for a stronger 2027. The preview anticipated expansion efforts but did not specify this shipment ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects second-half branded product shipments to be significantly larger than the first half of 2026, positioning for a stronger 2027.”

in_line: Gross loss narrowed to $0.3 million, within the preview’s expected $0.3–0.6 million loss range, although the reported improvement included non-recurring items.

Management continued to target expansion from approximately 2,000 stores across 20 states to roughly 5,000 stores across 35 states by year-end 2026; the preview had flagged the 5,000-store year-end target.
The planned wind-down of legacy contract-manufacturing volume was consistent with the preview’s expectation that exiting low- or no-margin CMO contracts would reduce revenue.

surprises.description: Cellectar now targets its Waldenström’s NDA submission for March–April 2027, later than the preview’s expectation of an early-2027 filing. The call also describes an approximately six-month review, consistent with the preview’s Breakthrough-based timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “submit its NDA ... in mid-2027 (targeting a March-April timeframe), with an approximate six-month review expected due to breakthrough designation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 call framed NDA submission early 2027, potential approval 2H 2027 under Breakthrough (6-month review).”

surprises.description: The company’s expected CLR-125 interim data have moved later: the preview said early dosimetry, safety and efficacy data were expected mid-year 2026, while management now expects initial data later in 2026 or early 2027. The first patients have been dosed, but the data timing is delayed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “dosed the first patients in its Phase 1B trial of CLR-125 in triple-negative breast cancer, with initial dosimetry, safety, and efficacy data expected later in 2026 or early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guided as ‘early dosimetry, safety and efficacy data expected mid-year 2026.’”

surprises.description: Phase 3 first-patient timing is less firm and may be later than the preview’s late-Q4 2026 initiation expectation: management expects first dosing in late 2026 or early 2027. It did provide an operational target of 10–20 sites open and a couple of patients enrolled by NDA submission.
surprises.fact_evidence: “open the first Phase 3 confirmatory trial sites in the coming months, with first patient dosing anticipated late 2026 or early 2027, targeting 10-20 sites open and a couple of patients enrolled at NDA submission.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “initiation late Q4 2026”; the preview also flags Phase 3 FPI timing as “Q4'26.”

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was somewhat worse than expected: net loss was $6.9 million and loss per share was $0.57, versus the preview’s roughly $6.0–6.5 million pre-warrant-mark loss estimate and EPS estimate of -$0.50 to -$0.55 (with -$0.52 consensus).
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss widened to $6.9 million ($0.57 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS -$0.52”; “My estimate: -$0.50 to -$0.55”; “Net loss ... ~$6.0–6.5M pre-warrant marks.”

surprises.description: R&D spending was materially above the preview’s estimate, at $4.6 million versus an expected $3.3–3.8 million, as clinical activity increased. G&A, by contrast, was within the preview’s $2.6–2.9 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses nearly doubled to $4.6 million from $2.4 million due to increased clinical activity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&D expense ... My estimate: $3.3–3.8M.”

surprises.description: The warrant call terms include a minimum average daily liquidity requirement that the preview did not flag, in addition to the stock-price and duration hurdle. This makes access to the potential warrant proceeds subject to an extra condition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “callable only if the stock's VWAP reaches at least $3.45 for 20 consecutive trading days with minimum $500,000 average daily liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “forced-call rights only when the milestone hits and the stock trades above 130% of $2.65 = ~$3.45 for 20 consecutive sessions.”

surprises.description: The call reported strong full 12-month Clover-WM follow-up results, including 17.8-month median durability and approximately 62% major response, plus high response rates in patients treated immediately after BTK inhibitors. The preview discussed the CLOVER-WaM follow-up as a catalyst but did not specify an expected result for these measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “full 12-month Clover-WM follow-up showed a median durability of 17.8 months, approximately 62% major response rate”; immediately post-BTK patients had “a 79.2% major response rate, 87.5% overall response rate, 100% clinical benefit rate, and 16-month median duration of response.”

in_line: Cash was approximately $34.0 million at June 30, within the preview’s expected $32–34 million range.
G&A expense was $2.6 million, within the preview’s $2.6–2.9 million estimate.
The six-month NDA review expectation associated with Breakthrough designation was consistent with the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 18%, below the preview’s consensus-implied 19–20% and short of its ≥20% bullish trigger. It was nevertheless at the low end of the preview’s own 18–19% base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 18% in Q2 2026,” up from 16% a year earlier and 17% in Q1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: ~19–20% (implied)” and “≥20% validates the liquid-line payoff”; the preview’s base case was “a gross margin nearer 18–19%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $200,000, below the preview’s expectation of breakeven to positive $300,000. The preview did allow for an EPS miss, but its EBITDA expectation was still for a result around breakeven or better.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $200,000, consistent with the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~breakeven to +$0.3M (implied).”

surprises.description: Management explicitly said the reverse split would not be followed by a capital raise and that a new medical-device opportunity would be funded within the existing operating plan, addressing the preview’s dilution concern with a more reassuring financing stance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The reverse split was “undertaken solely to regain Nasdaq minimum bid price compliance and will not be followed by a capital raise”; the new opportunity is “being financed within the existing operating plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Cash / dilution posture” and advised listening for “any ATM or financing language,” noting that reverse splits frequently precede raises.

surprises.description: Management described incremental western U.S. volume as carrying margins above the company average, with higher-margin liquid concentrate products contributing to the mix. This was a favorable margin driver beyond the preview’s focus on whether the new automated liquid lines would contribute immediately.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Incremental western U.S. volume growth carries margins consistently higher than the corporate average, aided by a mix skewed toward higher-margin liquid concentrate products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on the new automated liquid lines activating in Q2 and said their benefit was “weighted to 2H.”

in_line: Q2 net sales were $17.8 million, at the bottom of the preview’s $17.8–18.2 million consensus range and consistent with its $17.8–18.3 million base scenario.
Management reaffirmed the $70–75 million full-year sales, 18–22% gross-margin, $1–2 million adjusted-EBITDA, and positive-operating-cash-flow guidance, matching the preview’s base case.
Q2 operating cash flow was positive at approximately $2.1 million, in line with the preview’s expectation that positive Q2 cash flow would de-risk the balance-sheet narrative.
The preview anticipated updates on Heritage Dialysis and Aqua Dialysis; the call reported a new Heritage agreement and an Aqua renewal.

surprises.description: LUNR reported $206 million of Q2 revenue, below the preview’s $216.3–$219.3 million consensus range by about 5–6%. It also fell well short of the preview’s “>$250M” level for a strong result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $206 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $219.3M (Zacks) / $216.3M (Street, TipRanks)” and “What Good Looks Like | >$250M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was a $14 million loss, rather than the preview’s expected breakeven-to-positive range. The preview’s hoped-for result was at least $8 million, and the company cited a $14.7 million IM-4 estimate-at-complete adjustment as a partial offset to the year-over-year improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved to negative $14 million from negative $25 million a year earlier, partially offset by a $14.7 million estimate-at-complete adjustment on IM-4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | Not formally consensus; buy-side ~breakeven to +$8M” and “adj. EBITDA >$8M.”

surprises.description: The company’s stated backlog-conversion schedule implies much less conversion in 2026 than the preview’s 60–65% figure: management expects just 25–30% in 2026, with more pushed into 2027 and beyond.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects backlog conversion of 25%-30% to revenue in 2026, 35%-40% in 2027, and the remainder thereafter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed backlog as “60–65% converts in 2026.”

surprises.description: Backlog reached $1.8 billion, above the preview’s target of more than $1.4 billion. Record bookings helped drive the result, and management also anticipated another $300 million of ATP bookings in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company exited the quarter with a record $1.8 billion backlog”; “generated $1.7 billion in bookings year-to-date, including $1.2 billion in new bookings in Q2 through the call date, marking the highest quarterly bookings in company history”; “additional $300 million in ATP bookings anticipated in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s backlog target was “>$1.4B”; it also said to look for Andromeda/CLPS bookings and asked whether the L3Harris award was in backlog.

surprises.description: Cash deployment was heavier than the preview’s desired burn level, while the reported ending cash balance was supported by substantial ATM proceeds. This means the $367 million cash balance exceeded the preview’s threshold, but came alongside $235 million in net ATM proceeds and $84 million in total cash deployment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash used was $60 million and total cash deployment was $84 million, with the company ending the quarter with $367 million in cash including $235 million in net ATM proceeds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Cash >$220M, FCF burn <$40M” and flagged that disclosure of “heavy ATM issuance during Q2” would offset operational strength.

surprises.description: The company disclosed three GEO communications satellite wins valued at more than $600 million over 30 months, a sizable commercial award not specifically anticipated in the preview. It also said more than 70 IM-300 spacecraft are under contract, beyond the preview’s discussion of L3Harris selecting it for 18.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recent commercial wins include three GEO communication satellites valued at over $600 million over 30 months, while the company now has more than 70 IM-300 spacecraft under contract.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “L3Harris selects LUNR for 18 IM-300 spacecraft” and said to ask for the booking value; it did not identify the three GEO satellite award.

surprises.description: The lunar communications constellation plan was described as accelerated: Altus-1 is slated for Mission 3 in Q1 2027, and the other four satellites are now planned to deploy together in 2028 to reach full operational capability ahead of schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The lunar communications constellation is being accelerated, with Altus-1 launching on Mission 3 in Q1 2027 and the remaining four Altus satellites now planned to deploy together in 2028 to reach full operational capability ahead of schedule.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $900 million to $1 billion and continued to expect positive adjusted EBITDA for the year, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: The preview cited preliminary ARDS data in H2 2026 as the earlier guidance, while MiNK now expects a preliminary randomized readout in H1 2027. The preview noted that an early-2027 checkpoint was circulating, but still flagged a move beyond H2 2026 as a negative timeline slip.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a preliminary randomized readout in the first half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “versus the ‘H2 2026 preliminary data’ guided on the Q1 call. A slip in that timeline is itself a bear signal.”

surprises.description: MiNK says it has launched its first paid named-patient access program in Brazil, with revenue from the initial patients expected in the Q3 update. The preview treated whether the program would generate revenue as an open question and put first revenue in its bull case, so this is a concrete step toward monetization, though no Q2 revenue is reported here.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MiNK launched its first paid named-patient access program for agent 797 in Brazil, with revenue from initial patients to be reported in the Q3 update.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Key questions: which jurisdictions, is it cost-recovery or free-of-charge, is revenue recognized” and “First-ever revenue on the P&L would be a genuine narrative change.”

surprises.description: MiNK gave a near-term regulatory step for the ARDS program: it plans to seek an FDA meeting in the coming weeks to discuss converting the randomized Phase 2 into a seamless Phase 3, with 28-day mortality as the FDA-driven primary endpoint. The preview described a seamless Phase 3 pathway as designed, but did not anticipate this specific meeting timing or endpoint detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management plans to seek an FDA meeting in the coming weeks to convert the randomized phase 2 into a seamless phase 3 study, with 28-day mortality as the FDA-driven primary endpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “a seamless Phase 3 pathway designed.”

in_line: Cash ended the quarter at $8.8 million, above the preview’s roughly $7.8 million estimate but within its $7.0–$9.5 million range.

Net loss of $3.1 million and EPS of -$0.62 were broadly in line with the preview’s approximately $2.9 million net-loss estimate and EPS range of -$0.51 to -$0.72; the preview also cautioned that a beat against stale -$0.89 consensus would carry little information.
Operating cash use rose to $2.1 million from $1.6 million a year earlier, consistent with the preview’s expectation that burn would step up as the randomized ARDS study launched.

The initial ARDS observations were not a material expansion of the dataset the preview said had already been presented: the preview noted first treated patients alive and afebrile at Day 28 and said the bar was more patients or control-arm information.
The 77% disease control rate in PD-1-refractory gastroesophageal cancer was already cited in the preview.

surprises.description: NUWE ended June with about $3.9 million in cash, below the preview’s estimated $4.2–4.8 million range and below its $4.0 million downside threshold. That is a modest shortfall from the expected cash balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “As of June 30, 2026, the company held only about $3.9 million in cash and cash equivalents with no debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash (period end) … $4.2–4.8M”; the preview also said, “If the actual 6/30 balance prints below $4.0M, the below-net-cash thesis collapses immediately.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 76%, well above the preview’s 65–69% estimate and even above its bullish-scenario threshold of 70%. The margin improvement was stronger than expected despite the sequential revenue decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded dramatically to 76% in Q2 2026 from 56% a year earlier,” driven by “higher selling prices, favorable product mix, and the shift to contract manufacturing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … Q2 FY2026 est. 65–69%”; the preview described “holding ≥68% on lower revenue” as the bullish tell and set its bull case at “≥70%.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses were $4.7 million, below the preview’s $5.0–5.5 million estimate. The preview expected burn-reduction efforts to begin, but the expense figure came in better than its modeled range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses of $4.7 million rose year-over-year from $3.9 million but declined sequentially from $6.3 million in Q1 2026 as management aligned spending with priority programs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating expense … Q2 FY2026 est. $5.0–5.5M.”

surprises.description: The net loss was about $4.8 million, slightly worse than the preview’s estimated range of $3.8–4.5 million. The reported loss included $1.7 million of warrant valuation expense tied to the June financing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed sharply to approximately $4.8 million from $12.6 million in the prior-year quarter, though it included $1.7 million of warrant valuation expense tied to the June 2026 financing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss … Q2 FY2026 est. $(3.8)–(4.5)M”; the preview noted “warrant fair-value / deemed-dividend noise from June financing.”

surprises.description: NUWE disclosed plans to submit an FDA label expansion in Q4 2026 that would lower Aquadex’s patient-weight threshold from 20 kilograms to 5 kilograms. The preview discussed pediatric franchise metrics but did not anticipate this specific regulatory step.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to submit an FDA label expansion in Q4 2026 to broaden Aquadex use to patients weighing 5 kilograms and above (from the current 20 kilograms), potentially expanding its pediatric market.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $1.97 million, consistent with the preview’s $1.90–1.95 million estimate and the pre-announced 14% year-over-year growth.
The preview expected fewer console placements than Q1’s 15; NUWE sold 9 consoles in Q2.
The preview expected the acquired kidney-monitoring product to launch in 2027; the call likewise said ClarityPrime is expected to launch in 2027.
The preview estimated roughly $12.5 million of gross capital raised YTD; the call reported roughly $12.7 million through mid-2026.

surprises.description: Revenue was $49 million, about $3.1 million or 6.8% above the preview’s $45.9 million consensus, and growth was 13% rather than the expected 6.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $49 million, up 13% year-on-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $45.9M” and “+6.7%” year-on-year.

surprises.description: The preview worried that organic growth could be flat to down once Waqoo was excluded; the call reported 6% same-clinic revenue growth and 9% higher average spend per visit. The call did not provide an ex-Waqoo revenue figure, but these same-clinic results point to stronger underlying clinic performance than the preview feared.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-clinic revenue grew 6% and average spend per visit rose 9% in the quarter”; revenue growth also came “despite a weaker yen headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that if Waqoo’s contribution repeated, “the core franchise network is flat to down organically,” and described the base case as “organic roughly flat-to-LSD.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded the preview’s approximate $19 million estimate, but the 41% margin was slightly below its roughly 42% estimate. The margin nevertheless cleared the preview’s key 40% threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 32% to $20 million with a 41% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$19M / ~42% margin” and flagged “EBITDA margin ≥40%.”

surprises.description: Management quantified roughly $15 million of annual revenue from service-fee increases, with most expected to flow directly to profit because the services have a fixed-cost base. The contribution is staged: only about half its value is expected in Q3 and Q4 of this fiscal year, with the full contribution beginning next fiscal year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Planned service fee increases—roughly $11 million per year from enhanced call center functions and $4 million from Gorilla/Lise clinic support—are expected to add about $15 million annually, mostly flowing directly to profit”; “only about half its value in Q3 and Q4” and “full contribution beginning next fiscal year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No formal company guidance exists. SBC has never issued quantitative FY guidance. Anything numeric from management on the call is a new datapoint by definition.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a longer-term goal of reaching 1,000 clinics by 2035 while keeping indirect-department headcount flat through AI. The preview watched near-term clinic additions but did not anticipate this long-range scale-and-efficiency target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SBC targets 1,000 clinics by 2035 (up from close to 300 currently) while aiming to keep indirect department headcount flat by leveraging AI for operational efficiency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed clinic count as a metric to watch, noting “284 → 290+?”, but did not set a 2035 target or discuss flat indirect headcount through AI.

surprises.description: Management said it wants to substantially increase the share of non-aesthetic business over the next decade; the current transaction-value mix is still about 84% aesthetic and 16% non-aesthetic. This adds a longer-term mix-shift ambition that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's transaction value mix remains roughly 84% aesthetic and 16% non-aesthetic, with management targeting a substantial shift toward non-aesthetic categories over the next decade.”

surprises.description: SBC is considering increasing its ownership in OrangeTwist, a potential capital deployment not specified in the preview. This is only under consideration, rather than an announced transaction or completed increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OrangeTwist operates 24 U.S. locations across 6 states with recurring revenue exceeding 40% of sales, and the company is considering increasing its ownership stake.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said buybacks had been de-prioritized and that a buyback or “a named accretive deal” would be a catalyst; it described OrangeTwist as an 18.2% equity-method stake.

in_line: The 41% adjusted EBITDA margin cleared the preview’s stated 40% threshold, even though it was slightly below the preview’s approximate 42% margin estimate.
Trailing 12-month activity grew 10%, broadly matching the preview’s +10% benchmark for trailing 12-month customer growth; the call reported visits, while the preview cited customers.

surprises.description: Wolverine reported Q2 revenue of $506 million, above the preview’s $500.7 million consensus and the company’s $495–500 million guidance range. The beat was modest relative to the expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 6% in constant currency (7% reported) to $506 million, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus **$500.7M**”; “Company Guide … **$495–500M**.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.40, above both the preview’s $0.38 consensus and the top of company guidance. That was a clearer beat than the preview’s baseline, which treated $0.38 as the effective bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 14% year-over-year to $0.40, beating the company's $0.35-$0.38 outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS … Consensus **$0.38**”; “the buy-side bar is effectively the **top end of company guidance ($0.38)**.”

surprises.description: Wolverine raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $1.55–1.65 from $1.43–1.58, taking the midpoint to $1.60. The increase exceeded the preview’s base case of reaffirming or narrowing guidance and landed in its anticipated bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 … adjusted EPS to $1.55-$1.65 (from $1.43-$1.58).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … **FY guide reaffirmed / narrowed to upper half**”; “Bull … **FY EPS raised toward $1.55–1.65**.”

surprises.description: Wolverine raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.98–2.00 billion from $1.96–1.985 billion, rather than merely reaffirming or narrowing the prior range as the preview’s base case expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.98-$2.0 billion (from $1.96-$1.985 billion).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … **FY guide reaffirmed / narrowed to upper half**”; prior FY guide was “revenue $1.96–1.985B.”

surprises.description: Wolverine raised Saucony’s full-year growth outlook to mid-teens, while the preview expected the brand to decelerate to low- to mid-single-digit growth through its toughest comparison. Q2 growth was 9%, and management noted that some second-half acceleration reflects easier comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Saucony's full-year growth outlook was raised to mid-teens (from low-to-mid-teens), building on 40% growth in the year-ago quarter, though second-half acceleration partly reflects easier comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … **Saucony decelerates to LSD-MSD as flagged**”; the preview also called Q2 “the toughest comp of the year for Saucony.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted operating margin reached 10%, above the roughly 9.5% level cited in the preview. The 80-basis-point year-over-year expansion was driven by SG&A leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS … [was] driven by SG&A leverage and 80 basis points of adjusted operating margin expansion to 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin … **~9.5%** (+30bps) — Q1'26 call.”

surprises.description: Wolverine raised full-year gross-margin guidance to about 46.9% from 46.4%. The preview highlighted a possible tariff-driven improvement; management attributed most of the increase to structural factors such as healthier inventories and more full-price sales, with only about $2 million from tariff relief.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin guidance was raised to approximately 46.9% (from 46.4%), with management attributing most of the improvement to structural factors like healthier inventories and more full-price sales rather than the modest ~$2 million tariff relief.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If the realized 2H rate lands near 10–12.5% … the **$50M unmitigated 2026 tariff figure comes down and creates room for a margin/EPS raise**.”

surprises.description: Wolverine raised operating free cash flow guidance to $115–130 million from $105–120 million, lifting both ends of the range rather than leaving the prior outlook unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating free cash flow guidance was raised to $115-$130 million from $105-$120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating FCF $105–120M” in the FY2026 guide.

in_line: Q2 gross margin was close to the preview’s approximately 46.4% expectation: the reported 46.5% was only 10 basis points higher. The preview also expected a roughly 310-basis-point unmitigated tariff headwind to be largely offset, which management said was the case.

Near-term DTC softness associated with Wolverine’s strategic shift was anticipated: the preview said moving away from promotion toward full-price DTC “depresses near-term DTC revenue.” The call reported Merrell DTC revenue declined as marketing shifted to upper-funnel brand building.

surprises.description: ONDAS reported Q2 revenue of about $83.8 million, roughly 22–26% above the preview’s $66.7–68.5 million consensus range. The preview’s bull case included $75–85 million, but the actual result still substantially exceeded the buy-side reference point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record ~$83.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” was “$66.7M (Zacks) – $68.5M (Street)”; the preview also said to “Treat ~$68M as the buy-side reference point.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY2026 guidance to $525–550 million rather than merely reaffirming the expected $525 million floor. The upper end adds $25 million of revenue potential beyond the preview’s central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $525-550 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “FY26 revenue guide ≥$525M” as the key test and said the base case was “FY26 reaffirmed at ≥$525M.”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue range of $140–155 million is below the preview’s expectation that consensus needed about $160 million or more; its midpoint is roughly 8% below that reference. This leaves more of the annual revenue ramp to Q4 than the preview’s illustrative Q3/Q4 split.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue is guided to $140-155 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Consensus needs ~$160M+” and used a “40/60 H2 shape” implying “roughly $163M in Q3 and $244M in Q4.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss was about $51 million, far worse than the preview’s expected peak-loss range of roughly $13–18 million and its stated bear threshold of a loss greater than $20 million. Management still called it the peak loss, but the reported loss was nearly three times the preview’s $18 million upper base-case figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of ~$51 million, which management characterized as the peak loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “loss $13–18M (‘the peak’)” in its base case and flagged “loss >$20M” as a bear scenario.

surprises.description: Despite the much larger-than-expected current loss, management moved its operating-platform profitability target forward to Q4 2026 and its company-wide adjusted EBITDA profitability target to Q4 2027. Both dates are one quarter earlier than the preview’s stated expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating platform profitability now pulled forward one quarter to Q4 2026 and company-wide adjusted EBITDA profitability targeted for Q4 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “OAS adj. EBITDA-positive by Q1 2027” and “company-wide by Q1 2028.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin was 50.4%, above the preview’s 45–49% base-case range and its 50% threshold for the bull case. This was stronger than expected even though management warned of second-half pressure from acquired excess capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 50.4%, down slightly from 51.5% prior quarter, with management warning of second-half margin pressure from acquired excess capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “GM 45–49%,” while its bull case required “GM ≥50%.”

surprises.description: Pro forma backlog reached about $757 million, around $94 million or 14% above the preview’s expected level of roughly $663 million. The preview’s bull case had identified backlog above $700 million as an upside signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma backlog grew ~66% sequentially to ~$757 million at June 30.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected backlog “around ~$663M” and listed “backlog >$700M” in its bull case.

surprises.description: The reported order intake showed continued momentum beyond the preview’s expectation of more than $150 million of quarter-to-date orders: ONDAS said it captured $175 million during Q2 and another roughly $105 million quarter-to-date in Q3. The added Q3 intake was not part of the preview’s stated order expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company captured $175 million in new orders during Q2 and ~$105 million more quarter-to-date in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Q2 order intake ... >$150M quarter-to-date” and “a further ~$70M of defense orders in the four weeks since.”

surprises.description: ONDAS disclosed a strategic pipeline above $11 billion, which had expanded 2.5 times since May; the preview discussed backlog and conversion timing but did not anticipate this pipeline figure or its expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2-year strategic pipeline expanded to over $11 billion, up 2.5x since May.”

surprises.description: The release highlighted a $140 million combat engineering vehicles program and very high year-over-year organic growth at several subsidiaries. These program and subsidiary-growth details were not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $140 million combat engineering vehicles program” and “strong subsidiary organic growth (Centrix +298%, 4M +258%, Airobotics +112%) year-over-year.”

in_line: The FY2026 revenue guidance retained the preview’s expected floor of at least $525 million, although the company raised the range’s upper end.
The preview expected cumulative Mistral LUS awards above $240 million; the call cited $240+ million of orders under the U.S. Army’s lethal unmanned strike IDIQ.

surprises.description: The preview expected gross margin of roughly 43–44% and said it needed to reach at least 42%; reported gross margin was only 38.6%. Hardware margin fell to 17.2% from 25.1%, and management said a return to 40%+ blended margins is not expected until 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin held roughly flat at 38.6% versus 38.5%, but hardware margin fell to 17.2% from 25.1% and service margin declined to 50.1% from 54.4%, with a return to 40%+ blended margins not expected until 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: ~43–44% (implied)” and “Gross margin — must print ≥42%.” The preview said Q1’s compression was largely a “one-time CDM legacy subcontractor termination.”

surprises.description: The common-shareholder net loss was substantially worse than the preview’s estimated loss, even allowing for its warning that GAAP results could be distorted by fair-value marks. The reported loss was $4.6 million, or $0.43 per share, versus the preview’s estimated $2.5–$3.0 million loss and $0.25–$0.30 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss attributable to common shareholders widened to $4.6 million ($0.43 per diluted share) from $1.8 million ($0.17 per share) in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My GAAP EPS estimate: –$0.25 to –$0.30”; the preview also estimated a “–$2.5M to –$3.0M net loss.”

surprises.description: The auditors concluded the going-concern qualification was no longer needed, a positive outcome against the preview’s base case, which anticipated that the qualification might be retained. The preview had identified removal as a possible positive scenario, but not its expected base outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The auditors concluded the going concern qualification is no longer needed and it will be removed from the Q2 10-Q.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said removal was a “genuine shot,” but its base case described “going-concern retained but with improved liquidity narrative”; it called removal a “discrete, high-impact positive.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was inside the company’s pre-announced range but came in below sell-side consensus and the preview’s base-case range. At $21.5 million, it was also below the preview’s $22.3 million consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 65% year-over-year to $21.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue — sell-side consensus: $22.3M”; the preview’s base case was “$21.8–22.5M.” It also noted company preliminary revenue of “$21.0–23.0M.”

surprises.description: ARR reached $20.5 million, below the preview’s estimated Q2 exit range of $21–22 million. The additional SaaS backlog may support future ARR and margins, but it is not yet reflected in the reported ARR.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annual recurring revenue rose modestly to $20.5 million from $20.1 million last quarter, with an additional $3.5 million–$5 million in SaaS backlog set to turn on January 1, 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARR (exit Q2): ~$21–22M”; the preview also noted “$4M contracted to begin at year-end.”

surprises.description: Management described a strong Q3 and Q4 revenue ramp, but did not explicitly reaffirm the preview’s $100 million-plus FY26 framing. The Q3 target of north of $25 million is below the roughly $31.5 million quarterly H2 pace the preview calculated would be needed for the $101.6 million consensus, although Q4 is expected to exceed Q3 significantly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 will be the company's largest revenue quarter ever, with Q4 expected to significantly exceed Q3,” and management targets quarterly revenue “north of $25 million approaching or exceeding $30 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “FY2026 revenue guidance — reaffirm ‘>$100M’ or not,” cited “$101.6M” consensus, and calculated that this implied “~$63M in H2 (~$31.5M/quarter).”

surprises.description: The CEO personally bought 5% of the shares in the follow-on offering, a management commitment not anticipated in the preview. The offering itself and its liquidity purpose were already known, so the surprise is the CEO’s participation rather than the capital raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A follow-on offering raised roughly $12 million in net proceeds—in which the CEO personally purchased 5% of the shares.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $2.0 million, at the low end of the company’s pre-announced $2.0–$2.2 million range.
Revenue remained within the company’s pre-announced $21.0–$23.0 million range, despite coming in below sell-side consensus.
The preview had flagged the roughly $8.5 million Tennessee Titans/Nissan Stadium project; the call reported that it was secured and mostly expected to be recognized in 2026.
The preview expected roughly $4 million of SaaS backlog to begin at year-end; the call cited $3.5–$5 million scheduled to turn on January 1, 2027.

surprises.description: While the preview emphasized three consecutive quarters of overall gross-margin compression, the call reported that Product gross margin rose to 48.5% from 29.3% a year earlier, helped by price increases and product mix. This segment-level improvement was not apparent from the preview’s focus on overall margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product gross margin expanded dramatically to 48.5% from 29.3% year-over-year due to price increases and favorable product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin has now compressed three quarters running (44.3% → 40.9% → 37.8%).”

surprises.description: Services margin faced an unexpected hit from about $300,000 of one-time costs, including a catastrophic electric chiller failure, reducing the margin by roughly 7 percentage points. That complicates the preview’s expectation that service-territory cost reductions would begin showing up by Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Service margin was reduced roughly 7 percentage points by about $300,000 in one-time costs including a catastrophic electric chiller failure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Service-territory cost reductions were promised to show up ‘by Q3.’”

in_line: The reported revenue decline, Product revenue collapse, net loss, adjusted EBITDA loss, and overall gross margin matched figures already disclosed in the preview.
Services revenue growth of about 10% matched the preview’s reported actuals and description of a growing services business.
The preview’s expected sequential decline in operating expenses was confirmed: expenses fell about $400,000 from Q1, following service-center headcount reductions.

Backlog above $8 million and another $2 million to $3 million of projects expected to close were broadly in line with the preview’s roughly $8 million backlog and expectation of $2 million or more in additional projects.
The 12 demonstrations, including six in person and six virtual, and the data-center capacity represented were consistent with the preview’s account of the pipeline.

The preview said Q3 Product revenue was expected to be higher than Q1 and Q2; the call pointed to anticipated Q3 revenue growth supported by backlog, without providing a quantified Product revenue target.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS grew 65% year over year, well above the 30%–39% growth implied by the Q1 guide. The result included an unexpected $31 million tariff refund ($0.63 per share) and $9 million of expanded 45X benefits, so the headline beat was partly driven by those benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS increasing 65% over the prior year”; results included “a one-time $31 million tariff refund ($0.63/share)” and “$9 million of expanded 45X benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q1 guide was “Adj. diluted EPS (incl. 45X) $2.70M – $2.90M” versus prior-year actual of $2.08, implying “+30% to +39%.”

surprises.description: The Q2 adjusted EPS guide of $3.15–$3.25 is above the preview’s $2.90-or-higher expectation. The company also gave an ex-45X range of $1.95–$2.05, clarifying the outlook excluding credits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 guidance calls for … adjusted diluted EPS of $3.15-$3.25,” or “$1.95-$2.05 excluding 45X.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side wants Q2 revenue ≥ $960M and adj. EPS ≥ $2.90.”

surprises.description: Gross margin excluding the tariff refund and 45X benefits rose 110 basis points year over year, despite the preview’s concern about tariff and inflation pressure and the possibility of another year-over-year decline. The reported 510-basis-point increase was much larger because it included those benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 gross margin reached 33.5%, up 510 basis points year-over-year, but excluding tariff refunds and 45X benefits, gross margin was 25.2%, up 110 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “gross margin and net tariff impact” and identified “gross margin down Y/Y again” as a bear-case outcome.

surprises.description: Data-center orders surged more than 80% year over year, a stronger order signal than the preview’s expectation that the prior order momentum would hold. However, deliveries are scheduled 12–36 months out, while current data-center revenue growth was only low-teens.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center orders surged over 80% year-over-year with deliveries extending 12-36 months, while data center top-line grew low-teens.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q4 Energy Systems orders were “+36% Y/Y” and said the bar was for NIS book-to-bill to be “held at or above 1.0x.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow was $218 million, boosted by a $115 million U.S. federal tax refund; the preview had not identified this refund or a comparable cash-flow contribution. The 187% conversion rate falls to 140% excluding 45X, underscoring the effect of the benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $218 million (versus negative $32 million in prior-year Q1), boosted by a $115 million U.S. federal tax refund,” with “free cash flow conversion to 187% (140% excluding 45X).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed capital allocation, including “cash $440M, net debt $684M,” but did not anticipate a federal tax refund or give a Q1 free-cash-flow expectation.

surprises.description: Industrial Mobility’s material-handling orders declined by high single digits, contrary to the preview’s focus on whether orders would inflect after sequential order growth. Transportation orders nearly doubled, making the order picture uneven rather than a broad recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Material handling orders declined high single digits while transportation orders nearly doubled (up 91% year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “sequential orders +19%” and said to “watch Y/Y order growth, not revenue.”

surprises.description: Net debt fell by more than $160 million from fiscal year-end and leverage declined to 0.8x EBITDA, a stronger balance-sheet position than the preview’s cited $684 million of net debt and 1.1x leverage. The call also reported $531 million of cash and nearly $900 million of remaining buyback authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt fell over $160 million since fiscal year-end to $522 million, leaving leverage at just 0.8x EBITDA, with $531 million cash on hand and nearly $900 million remaining in buyback authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “cash $440M, net debt $684M, leverage 1.1x EBITDA” and said an accelerated repurchase “would be read as a confidence signal.”

in_line: Q1 net sales of $936 million were within the company’s $915–$955 million guide and close to its $935 million midpoint.
Industrial Mobility revenue fell 3%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of softness through mid-FY27.
Data-center top-line growth was low-teens, consistent with the preview’s full-year high-single-digit to low-teens growth expectation.
The Q2 sales-guide midpoint was $975 million, above the preview’s $960 million threshold, although the $955 million low end was slightly below it.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $670.5 million, about 3.6% above the $647.1 million consensus and near the preview’s bull-case range, rather than the more modest beat in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 13.7% year-over-year to approximately $670.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $647.1M”; base case: “$655–665M”; bull case: “$672–685M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $95.4 million exceeded the preview’s derived $86–89 million range and landed in its bull-case range. Growth was 8% year over year, but the prior-year quarter included roughly $9 million of favorable non-recurring PDS items; the preview had anticipated an approximately $11 million timing benefit and expected clean growth in the high teens.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA increased 8% year-over-year to $95.4 million, though the prior-year period included roughly $9 million of non-recurring favorable items in the PDS division.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$86–89M”; bull case: “$95–99M”; and “clean EBITDA +18–20% ex-timing.”

surprises.description: Aveanna raised its full-year revenue and EBITDA outlook well beyond the prior guidance range, with management attributing the increase to core organic performance rather than the already-contemplated Family First acquisition. The EBITDA floor of $365 million also exceeds the preview’s bull-case threshold of $348 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue greater than $2.68 billion and adjusted EBITDA greater than $365 million, driven by core organic performance rather than the already-contemplated Family First acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY2026 guidance … Revenue $2.63–$2.65B, Adj. EBITDA $338–$342M”; bull case: “FY26 EBITDA guide raised to $348M+.”

surprises.description: The company raised its long-term organic growth targets for both PDS and home health and hospice, beyond the preview’s emphasis on near-term volume growth and moderating rate increases. The new targets are 5–6% for PDS and 8–10% for home health and hospice.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its long-term organic growth targets, increasing private duty services from 3-5% to 5-6% and home health & hospice from 5-7% to 8-10%, while keeping medical solutions at 8-10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Volume, not rate, is the 2026 growth engine” and “rate enhancements moderate to mid-single-digits after three years of outsized Medicaid increases.”

surprises.description: PDS spread per hour reached $12.88, above the preview’s $12.30–$12.40 reference points, and PDS gross margin was 28.9% versus 27.9% in Q1. That is stronger than the preview’s highlighted concern about PDS margin pressure, although cost per hour rose faster than revenue per hour.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PDS Q2 gross margin was 28.9% with revenue per hour up 1.7% to $44.62, cost of revenue per hour up 7.8% to $31.74, and spread per hour of $12.88 reflecting wage normalization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided to ‘low $12 range’ going forward”; “A spread holding $12.30+ … neutralizes” the bear point; bull case: “spread holds $12.40+.”

surprises.description: Home health episodic mix reached 81%, above the preview’s expected high-seventies range and the 75% goal, while episodic volume grew 18.5% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Home health episodic mix reached approximately 81% (above the 75% goal) with episodic volume growth of 18.5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Home Health & Hospice episodic mix (80% in Q1, management says ‘high seventies’).”

surprises.description: PDS had 37 preferred payer agreements, one short of the 38 year-end target, and had added seven since Q1. That falls slightly short of management’s previewed expectation to exceed eight new agreements, although preferred payers’ share of PDS MCO volume rose to 64%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PDS preferred payer agreements reached 37 of a 38 target, with preferred payers now representing approximately 64% of PDS MCO volumes, up from 60% at the end of Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “PDS: 30 at Q1 end, 60% of MCO volume, target 38 by year-end (management already said they expect to exceed eight new agreements).”

surprises.description: Medical Solutions grew 9.4%, above the preview’s expectation of mid-single-digit near-term growth, though short of its anticipated double-digit growth by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medical solutions +9.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Medical Solutions growth (mid-single-digits near-term, management promises double-digits by year-end post-modernization).”

surprises.description: California’s 2027 budget provides a significant pediatric private-duty nursing rate increase effective January 1, 2027. The preview did not flag this rate increase, which follows roughly nine years without an increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “California's 2027 budget includes a significant pediatric private duty nursing rate increase effective January 1, 2027, the state's first rate increase in roughly nine years after four years of advocacy.”

surprises.description: Credit upgrades from all three major agencies enabled a term-loan repricing that cuts annual interest expense by about $10 million, a financing benefit not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received credit rating upgrades from all three major agencies and repriced its term loan 75 basis points lower, cutting annual interest expense by approximately $10 million.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date free cash flow was already positive $75.4 million, and management expects a similar amount in the second half. That points to roughly $151 million for the year if achieved, above the preview’s approximately $131 million FY expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow was positive $75.4 million with similar expected in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guide is ~$131M FCF, consistent with 2025”; “Q1 was seasonally negative (OCF $4.3M, FCF –$3.8M).”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the sub-three-times leverage target and expected timing: it said the target remains achievable in 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated sub-3.0x target.

surprises.description: ISSC reported $26.7 million of Q3 revenue, above the $26 million top end of its own guidance and well above the preview’s consensus range. The beat was meaningful but not enormous relative to the guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 revenue grew approximately 11% year-over-year to $26.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company revenue guidance: $24M – $26M”; consensus was “$22.6M – $24.0M.”

surprises.description: Even excluding both F-16 revenue and acquisitions, the organic business grew over 40% in Q3. That was stronger than the preview’s concern that FY26 organic growth was expected to be essentially flat because of the F-16 pull-forward, though the preview had noted 69% non-F-16 growth in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding F-16 revenue and new acquisitions, the organic business grew over 40% year-over-year in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 organic growth was guided ‘essentially flat’ purely because of this pull-forward”; the preview also noted “non-F-16 growth as the true organic signal (+69% in Q2).”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 51.7%, above the preview’s expected path toward the mid-40s and even above the preview’s 47–51% base-case range. Management attributed the strength to favorable mix and lower Honeywell transition costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 51.7% from 35.6% a year ago, marking the fourth consecutive quarter above 50%, aided by favorable mix and reduced Honeywell transition costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided to “mid-40s% long-term” and set a base case of “GM 47–51%.”

surprises.description: F-16 revenue was $5.7 million, modestly above the preview’s normalized $3–5 million quarterly range. Management described roughly $5 million per quarter as sustainable long term, consistent with the upper end of that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “F-16 revenue was $5.7 million this quarter versus $12.6 million a year ago (which was inflated by pull-forward), with management viewing roughly $5 million per quarter as sustainable long-term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Normalized to $3–5M/quarter from an elevated ~$10M in Q2 FY25.”

surprises.description: The Liberty flight deck moved beyond the development-agreement stage: ISSC won its first OEM contract with a Japanese eVTOL developer, associated with over 400 aircraft orders. The preview had flagged development and forward-fit potential, but not a first OEM award.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company won its first OEM contract for the Liberty flight deck with a Japanese eVTOL developer, holding over 400 aircraft orders, with production targeted for late 2027 and full production in 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted an “eVTOL display/avionics development agreement announced Aug 12 (reported forward-fit potential >$50M).”

surprises.description: Backlog was approximately $83 million, below the prior-quarter $87 million level and weaker than the preview’s base case of roughly flat backlog. It was still up $5.5 million year over year, so the shortfall is relative to the near-term expectation rather than an annual decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog at approximately $83 million, up $5.5 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 backlog at “$87.0M” and its base scenario expected “backlog roughly flat.”

surprises.description: GAAP diluted EPS was $0.25, slightly above the preview’s $0.23–$0.24 consensus range. The beat was narrow and remained within the preview’s base-case EPS range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income rose to $4.5 million ($0.25 diluted EPS) from $2.4 million ($0.14) a year ago.”

in_line: Q4 revenue guidance of $28–30 million was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q4 could land near $30 million.
Management reaffirmed the long-term $250 million revenue objective, which the preview had already identified as the company’s target.

surprises.description: BFRI reported Q2 revenue of $12 million, above the preview’s $10.71 million consensus and its own $10.4–10.6 million estimate. Year-over-year growth was 33%, versus the preview’s 19% consensus-implied growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net product revenue grew 33% year-over-year to $12 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 consensus **$10.71M**”; “My estimate: **$10.4–10.6M** (+16–18%).”

surprises.description: Ameluz unit growth was materially faster than the preview’s expected 14–17%: the call reported approximately 30% growth. That exceeds the preview’s >30,000-tube marker for stronger-than-expected demand, although the call did not give an exact tube count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “~30% growth in Ameluz unit volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “29–30k tubes (+14–17%)”; “>30k = the inside-sales program and lower rep turnover are working.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was near breakeven at negative $0.2 million, far better than the preview’s expected loss of $3.0–3.6 million. The roughly $5 million year-over-year improvement was not just a continuation of the preview’s modeled improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached negative $0.2 million (near breakeven), a roughly $5 million improvement from a negative $5.1 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … My estimate: **$(3.0)–$(3.6)M**.”

surprises.description: The ITC exclusion order unexpectedly bars import and sale of the current Rodolet XL lamp and restricts Ameluz use with it, affecting 243 of 801 installed lamps. A modified, non-infringing lamp has FDA clearance, but customs/border approval is still pending and remediation is estimated at about $500,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An ITC exclusion order effective July 7 bars import and sale of the current Rodolet XL lamp and restricts Ameluz sales for use with it, affecting 243 of the 801 installed lamps”; “Remediation cost for a modified, non-infringing XL lamp is estimated at ~$500,000 (unchanged), with FDA clearance obtained but customs/border approval still pending.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was $4.7 million, below the preview’s expected $5.5–6.5 million base-case range and below its roughly $5 million risk threshold. The going-concern qualification remained, as the preview had expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents fell to $4.7 million as of June 30, 2026 … prompting a going-concern qualification.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … cash ~$5.5–6.5M”; “Anything that puts cash below ~$5M pulls forward a raise”; “Going-concern language … retention is expected.”

surprises.description: The preview referred to $7.7 million of debt, while the call described only $4.6 million of convertible notes, maturing in November 2027, and no bank debt. That indicates a lower and later-maturing debt burden than the preview figure suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only $4.6 million of convertible notes maturing November 2027 and no bank debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$6.3M at 3/31/26 against $7.7M of debt.”

surprises.description: Management maintained its full-year 2026 revenue goals despite the ITC order and characterized the impact as a shift in order timing rather than a reduction in total demand, citing that most installed lamps are unaffected. The preview expected revenue to be achievable but did not anticipate this specific guidance in response to an ITC restriction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management maintains full-year 2026 revenue goals, expecting the ITC order to shift order timing rather than reduce total demand since the majority of the installed base is unaffected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY consensus looks beatable on revenue”; the preview did not discuss an ITC order or its effect on demand.

surprises.description: The preview anticipated the September 28 sBCC PDUFA date, but the call added a full-launch expectation of Q1 2027, providing a concrete launch timeframe that the preview did not specify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA accepted the sNDA for Ameluz PDT to treat superficial basal cell carcinoma with a PDUFA date of September 28, 2026, and a full launch anticipated in Q1 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “sBCC PDUFA — September 28, 2026”; the preview asked for launch detail but did not give a launch-timing expectation.

surprises.description: The planned AK label-expansion filing in Q3 matched the preview, but management also gave an expected Q3 2027 approval timeframe and described a potential U.S. target population of about 58 million adults—details not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A second sNDA to expand the AK label to extremities, neck, and trunk (up to 240 square centimeters) is planned for around end of Q3 2026, with FDA approval anticipated in Q3 2027, targeting ~58 million U.S. adults with AK lesions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AK extremities/neck/trunk sNDA — guided for Q3 2026 filing”; no approval timing or target-population estimate was stated.

in_line: Gross margin was approximately 80%, in line with the preview’s expected ~79–81% and its view that the post-October-2025 earn-out structure should support that level.
The sBCC PDUFA date of September 28, 2026, matched the preview.
The AK label-expansion sNDA remained on track for a Q3 2026 filing, as the preview expected.
The going-concern qualification remained, which the preview expected.

surprises.description: Southland reported revenue of $113.3 million, far below the preview’s live estimate of about $177 million, and a $1.55-per-share loss versus an expected loss near $0.29. A $102.3 million non-cash revenue reversal and $93.6 million unfavorable legacy claims adjustment drove a $71.2 million gross loss and negative $73.4 million EBITDA; management called the reassessment one-time but said recovery timing and resolution remain uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell to $113.3 million” due to a “$102.3 million non-cash revenue reversal”; the company recorded a “$71.2 million” gross loss, primarily from a “$93.6 million unfavorable legacy claims adjustment,” and a “$1.55 per diluted share” net loss. EBITDA was “negative $73.4 million.” Management characterized the reassessment as “a one-time adjustment,” though “timing and ultimate resolution of recoveries remain uncertain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The live bar is therefore closer to ~$177M revenue / ~-$0.29 EPS”; the preview also said it was “skew[ing] slightly below the mechanical build because SLND has taken an adverse legacy adjustment in three of the last four quarters,” and its bear case included “a fresh legacy dispute charge.”

surprises.description: The financing situation became more concrete than the preview’s base case of financing being advanced but not closed: Southland set a deadline to convert approximately $151 million of surety financing into perpetual, non-convertible senior preferred shares and amended its credit facility to provide about $27 million of cash debt-service relief over the next year. Surety repayment is also deferred until at least August 13, 2027, later than the preview’s stated May 13, 2027 date, although the preferred-share conversion remains prospective.
surprises.fact_evidence: Southland expects to convert “approximately $151 million” into senior preferred shares “no later than September 30, 2026.” The credit facility now has “a fixed 4% PIK interest rate with suspended amortization and early-termination premium,” delivering “roughly $27 million of cash debt service relief over the next 12 months.” Surety advances totaled $209.8 million, with “repayment not required before at least August 13, 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called whether the financing “closed” the “single most important disclosure,” while its base case assumed financing was “advanced but not closed.” It said surety principal and interest were waived “until at least May 13, 2027.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects bidding activity to ramp up now that surety bonding support is formalized. The preview focused on whether financing had closed, but did not anticipate this specific near-term bidding outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Southland “expects bidding activity to ramp up now that surety bonding support is formalized.”

in_line: Backlog was $1.68 billion, close to the preview’s stated ~$1.7 billion burn-off case; 38% was expected to convert to revenue over the next 12 months, matching the 38% figure cited for Q1.
The $190 million Winnipeg project share was booked in Q3, consistent with the preview’s warning that the Winnipeg award would not count in Q2 backlog and was expected to enter Civil backlog in Q3.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $278.7 million, above the preview’s $242 million base case and $246 million sell-side high; full-year revenue of about $1.15 billion also exceeded the cited $1.10 billion FY26 consensus. The Q4 result was roughly 13% above the preview’s highest considered estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 total revenues jumped to $278.7 million”; “MSG Sports generated fiscal 2026 full-year revenues of approximately $1.15 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My base case: $242M”; “Revenue (sell-side high) $246M”; “FY26 $1.10B.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted operating income was $39.6 million, substantially above the preview’s $12–18 million base case and even above its $30 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted operating income swung to a positive $39.6 million from an adjusted operating loss of $16.8 million in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating income … My base case: +$12M to +$18M”; bull scenario: “AOI $30M+.”

surprises.description: Management now expects the Rangers-Knicks spin-off to be completed by the end of October, earlier and more specific than the preview’s baseline expectation of an on-track process with no timetable.
