surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to complete the spin-off of its Rangers business from its Knicks business by the end of October”; it plans to publicly file an updated Form 10 this week.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … spin-off ‘on track, no timetable’”; the preview said no timetable had been set and framed calendar Q4 2026 / early 2027 as a bullish possibility.

surprises.description: Management disclosed an estimated $16 million of additional income tax expense in FY2028 from new tax-law changes, and said combined tax expense is expected to be higher after the separation—an unanticipated future earnings headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New tax law changes are estimated to add approximately $16 million in additional income tax expense in fiscal year 2028 (excluding spin-off effects), with combined tax expense across the two companies expected to be higher post-separation.”

in_line: The nine Knicks home playoff games had the higher-value conference-finals and NBA-finals mix the preview expected to drive a sharp increase in playoff revenue; playoff revenue was $182 million versus $115.2 million a year earlier.

The preview anticipated strong ticket and sponsorship economics from the championship run; the Knicks set playoff per-game gate revenue records and postseason sponsorship revenue more than doubled year over year.

The preview flagged FY27 pricing as a key issue and expected Knicks price increases; management reported raising Knicks season-ticket prices, while Rangers prices were unchanged after the team missed the playoffs.
The preview highlighted roster compensation and luxury-tax costs; management expects higher team compensation and luxury tax in FY27.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was a $0.01 loss, far below the preview’s $0.38–$0.40 expectation, because the effective tax rate jumped to 67.8% when two dividend-withholding matters were resolved. The preview’s earnings math assumed a tax rate around 30%, although it noted that tax could cause a miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Q4 effective tax rate spiked to 67.8% due to resolution of two dividend withholding matters, driving an adjusted loss of $0.01 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 adj. EPS: $0.38–$0.40”; the preview also said “$375M × 4.5% adj. op margin = $16.9M; less ~$2.5M interest, taxed at the guided ~30% → ~$0.42.”

surprises.description: Q4 sales were slightly below the $373.4 million consensus estimate, though they remained within the company’s $370–$380 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 net sales were $371.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 revenue | Consensus: $373.4M | Company Guidance: $370–380M.”

surprises.description: Q4 operating margin reached 4.9%, above the preview’s roughly 4.5% expectation and the prior 4.4%–4.6% company guide; gross margin also reached 8.9%, above the preview’s 8% threshold. This margin strength came despite operating income declining year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin improved 90 basis points year-over-year to 8.9%”; “Q4 adjusted operating income was $18.1 million (4.9% of sales), down from $19.6 million (5.2%) a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 adj. operating margin | ~4.5% | 4.4%–4.6%”; the preview described “Q4 at 4.6% with GM ≥8%” as the setup.

surprises.description: The FY2027 sales outlook includes 3%–5% organic growth in addition to Helvoet, stronger than the preview’s concern that a $1.50 billion guide would amount to roughly flat organic sales. Total guidance is within the preview’s base-case range, but its organic component is a favorable distinction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance projects net sales of $1.535 billion to $1.56 billion, a 7% to 9% increase, comprised of 3% to 5% organic growth plus $60 million in Helvoet revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A $1.50B guide is ~flat organic; buy-side wants organic growth, not acquired growth”; the preview’s base case was FY27 revenue of “$1.50–1.56B.”

surprises.description: FY2027 operating-margin guidance reaches 4.7% at the high end, above the preview’s 4.6% base-case ceiling; even its 4.4% low end is above the preview’s bear-case concern of 4.0%–4.3%. The Indianapolis drag was quantified at a level close to the previously anticipated 40–50 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 operating margin guided to 4.4%-4.7%”; the Indianapolis ramp is expected to create “a drag of roughly $6.5-$7 million in fiscal 2027 that is offset by Helvoet’s accretive benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case had FY27 adjusted operating margin at “4.3%–4.6%,” and its bear case at “4.0%–4.3%”; it flagged a “40–50 bp gross margin headwind from the Indianapolis ramp.”

surprises.description: Medical is expected to approach 35% of company sales in FY2027, above the preview’s roughly 32% mix marker. Full-year medical growth above 10% was consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued double-digit growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medical sales grew over 10% for the full fiscal year (normalized for last year's consigned inventory sale) and are expected to approach 35% of total company sales in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said medical crossing “~32% of mix” was the re-rating narrative and described “three straight double-digit quarters.”

surprises.description: Automotive is expected to be roughly flat in FY2027 despite a 7% full-year decline and weaker EV program volumes, offering a clearer stabilization outlook than the preview’s concern that pressure on awarded programs could extend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Automotive sales fell 7% for the full year (down 3% in Q4) driven by weaker EV program volumes, and are guided to be roughly flat in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked “Automotive — has it troughed?” and said pressure on “already-awarded programs” was “harder to fix than a bookings problem”; its bear case included auto weakness extending into FY27.

surprises.description: Borrowings were down to $116.6 million and leverage was near 1x EBITDA after the Helvoet acquisition, easing the preview’s concern that acquisition financing and pro forma leverage could be a major risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Borrowings fell to $116.6 million, the lowest level in over 4 years, down 21% year-over-year, leaving leverage near 1x EBITDA with management targeting a 1.5x-2x range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called “pro forma leverage” the bear’s lever and asked for confirmation against “$163M net debt plus ~$103M cash consideration.”

surprises.description: Cash conversion days improved to 82, the best reading in 17 quarters, an additional working-capital improvement beyond the expected continuation of positive operating cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash from operations was a robust $42.4 million in Q4, marking the tenth consecutive quarter of positive cash, with cash conversion days improving to 82, the best in 17 quarters.”

in_line: FY2027 total sales guidance of $1.535–$1.56 billion is within the preview’s $1.50–$1.56 billion base-case range.

The Indianapolis ramp drag was quantified at roughly $6.5–$7 million, close to the preview’s anticipated 40–50 basis-point headwind; new-program production is still expected by the end of calendar 2026.
Helvoet’s benefit was described as accretive, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the acquisition would be accretive to FY2027 adjusted EPS.
Operating cash flow was positive for a tenth consecutive quarter, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: MPTI’s diluted EPS was $0.43, below the preview’s lowest cited consensus estimate of $0.47 and its $0.60 base case. The preview flagged dilution as a headwind, but the reported figure also included a $1.0 million non-cash expense for accelerated vesting of the 2025 bonus, which the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS fell to $0.43 from $0.53 due to a higher share count following the April 2026 rights offering”; net income “included a $1.0 million non-cash stock compensation expense tied to accelerated vesting of the 2025 annual bonus, absent in prior-year periods.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) $0.47” to “$0.54”; “Working consensus… EPS ~$0.50”; base-case EPS “$0.60.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 41.2%, materially below the preview’s 45.0% base case and below its stated 43–46% target range. The preview highlighted sub-43% as a break from the framework; the reported margin was also weighed down by roughly $0.5 million of non-cash stock compensation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margins declined to 41.2% from 43.6% a year earlier,” weighed down by “roughly $0.5 million of non-cash stock-based compensation not expected to recur at comparable levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin… 43–46% long-term target”; “Sub-43% would break the Investor Day framework”; base case gross margin “45.0%.”

surprises.description: Management provided a second-half gross-margin outlook even though the preview said formal guidance was not expected. The indicated 41.5–43.5% range, likely near its midpoint, remains below the preview’s 43–46% target framework, with rapid program ramping expected to reduce margins by about one point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guided second-half gross margins to a range of roughly 41.5% to 43.5%, likely landing near the middle, with a ~1-point drag from rapid ramping of new programs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Do not treat as a catalyst: formal guidance. MPTI does not issue quarterly or annual guidance”; the preview also cited a “43–46% long-term target.”

surprises.description: Although the $84 million backlog was within the preview’s forecast range, the call added stronger-than-expected visibility commentary: backlog exceeded near-term production capacity, more than half of next year’s production was already booked, and orders extended through 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog jumped… to $84 million”; “over half of next year's production already booked and orders extending through 2028”; backlog was “exceeding near-term production capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case backlog: $78–84M”; backlog was described as the forward-visibility number to watch, with sequential growth keeping the story intact.

surprises.description: Recently introduced products had secured $12 million in orders for 2026–2027 production despite generating only about $200,000 of sales in 2025. The preview discussed likely unannounced bookings generally but did not anticipate this specific level of orders for new products.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recently introduced products generated $12 million in new orders for 2026-2027 production despite selling only about $200,000 in 2025.”

surprises.description: The newly signed seven-year defense framework agreements carry a longer conversion timeline than near-term growth commentary might suggest: first purchase orders are expected in Q1 2027, for production in 2028, with more meaningful revenue impact anticipated that year. The preview did not flag this timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The first purchase orders from newly signed 7-year defense framework agreements are expected in Q1 2027 for 2028 production, with more meaningful revenue impact anticipated in 2028.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $15.1 million modestly exceeded the preview’s cited consensus estimates of $14.7–$15.04 million, although it matched the preview’s own $15.1 million base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 total revenues rose 13.8% year-over-year to $15.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue estimates of “$14.7M,” “$14.8M,” and “$15.04M”; the base case was “$15.1M.”

in_line: Revenue was $15.1 million, matching the preview’s $15.1 million base case and clearing its $14.7 million threshold for a fifth consecutive record revenue quarter.
Backlog reached $84 million, the top of the preview’s $78–84 million base-case range.
Adjusted EBITDA grew to $3.4 million, matching the preview’s $3.4 million base-case expectation.

surprises.description: AudioEye reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $3.0 million, above the preview’s expected $2.6–$2.7 million range. The roughly 11% beat over the high end was a stronger profitability result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $3 million (28% margin), up 54% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | $2.6M – $2.7M | n/a (guide = consensus).”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to at least $12.7 million from at least $12 million and raised adjusted EPS guidance to at least $0.98 from at least $0.96. It also expects Q4 2026 run-rate adjusted EBITDA to exceed $15 million, versus the preview’s $15 million exit target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from at least $12 million to at least $12.7 million”; “adjusted EPS guidance of at least $0.98”; “expects to reach over $15 million run-rate adjusted EBITDA by Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance to be reaffirmed or revised: revenue $43.25M–$44.25M; adjusted EBITDA ≥$12M; adjusted EPS ≥$0.96; $15M adjusted EBITDA run-rate exiting 2026.”

surprises.description: Enterprise revenue was flat year-over-year and enterprise ARR growth slowed to 5%, rather than showing the reacceleration the preview identified as the clearest evidence of regulatory demand converting. The shift from nonrecurring to recurring revenue offers context but does not change the weaker reported growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise revenue was flat year-over-year (5% ARR growth) due to a shift from nonrecurring to recurring revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Enterprise re-accelerating above ~12% would be the cleanest evidence that the Title II/EAA regulatory funnel is converting.”

surprises.description: Partner and marketplace growth accelerated to 16% year-over-year, compared with 8% growth in the preview’s Q1 baseline. The channel now accounts for 59% of ARR, as expected, but its growth was much stronger than that baseline suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The partner and marketplace channel grew 16% year-over-year and now represents 59% of ARR.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1: … Partner/Marketplace 59% (+8% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: The company generated $2.6 million of adjusted free cash flow in Q2 and expects substantial cash generation in H2. The preview focused on the EBITDA ramp and litigation costs, but did not anticipate this reported free-cash-flow result or explicit cash-generation outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 generated $2.6 million of adjusted free cash flow”; management expects litigation expenses to continue declining in H2, “driving substantial cash generation.”

surprises.description: Litigation expenses were already down 40% from Q1, with further declines expected in H2. That is favorable progress for the margin ramp, although the call did not provide the dollar amounts or post-trial run-rate the preview said investors needed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Litigation expenses—down 40% from Q1—to continue declining in H2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tonight needs a quantified number — dollars of legal expense in Q2, expected in Q3/Q4, and post-trial run-rate.”

surprises.description: R&D fell to 12% of revenue from 17% a year earlier, which management attributed to AI-driven headcount efficiencies. The preview did not anticipate this specific cost-efficiency development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D spend fell to 12% of revenue from 17% a year earlier due to AI-driven headcount efficiencies.”

surprises.description: Management is evaluating buybacks, dividends, and M&A as uses for excess cash. The preview cited cash on hand but did not flag these possible capital-allocation actions, and no decision or commitment was reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is evaluating deployment of excess cash including potential share buybacks, dividends, and M&A,” with $8.7 million cash and net debt-to-adjusted-EBITDA of approximately 0.6.

surprises.description: Customer count reached approximately 129,000, up 9,000 year-over-year, modestly ahead of the preview’s Q1 baseline of about 127,000 customers and 8,000 annual additions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total customer count reached approximately 129,000, up 9,000 year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~127,000 customers at Q1 (+8,000 Y/Y).”

surprises.description: Europe made its strongest contribution to ARR growth to date amid early enforcement of the European Accessibility Act, a more concrete sign of European demand than the preview’s general discussion of the EAA opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 marked the strongest EU contribution to ARR growth to date amid early European Accessibility Act enforcement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The EAA is live in the EU.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $10.7 million was in line with the preview’s ~$10.71–$10.73 million consensus and the $10.65–$10.75 million company guidance range.
ARR of $42.3 million was within the preview’s estimated $42.3–$42.5 million range; the $1.1 million sequential increase was close to the expected roughly $1.2 million add.
The Q3 revenue guidance midpoint of $10.95 million was broadly in line with the preview’s approximately $11.0 million baseline, though below its ≥$11.1 million bull-case validation level.
Full-year revenue guidance was tightened to $43.5–$44 million while maintaining the midpoint, consistent with the preview’s expected $43.25–$44.25 million range and midpoint.

surprises.description: The preview made a signed, named licensing agreement the key strategy milestone. The reported facts identify no such partner or deal; instead, management described a concierge target of about 1.9 million patients across four U.S. geographies and estimated breakeven at roughly 30,000 patients, leaving the licensing pivot without the concrete commercial proof the preview sought.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company estimates it needs roughly 30,000 patients (or fewer given the reduced cost profile) to reach cash-flow breakeven, targeting a concierge market of approximately 1.9 million patients across four U.S. geographies. No named licensing partner or signed agreement is identified in the reported call facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A signed, named agreement with disclosed economics … is the single highest-value disclosure.” The preview also said that without a named counterparty, the pivot would have “nothing to show by August.”

surprises.description: The preview said a quarterly burn target below about $2.5 million would materially improve runway, but its Q2 model assumed about $3.4 million of operating burn. Management now expects baseline operating cash flow to fall below $2.5 million per quarter by Q4, though an MI pivotal study could push spending above that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided baseline Q4 2026 operating cash flow to step down to below $2.5 million per quarter,” with MI pivotal-study spending potentially taking it above that level. Q2 net cash used in operations was $3.3 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything under ~$2.5M/qtr materially changes the runway math”; the Q2 cash bridge assumed “~$3.4M burn.”

surprises.description: The preview discussed MI detection as a major potential expansion and expected ALIGN-ACS results, but the reported facts add a regulatory step: HeartBeam submitted an FDA 510(k) pre-submission for MI detection on the call date, with a pivotal study potentially starting before year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: HeartBeam submitted a “510(k) pre-submission to the FDA for heart attack (MI) detection” on the day of the call; the FDA response window is 75 days, and a pivotal trial could start before year-end 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called heart-attack detection “the large indication expansion” and listed ALIGN-ACS data as a key catalyst, but did not anticipate a 510(k) pre-submission or possible pivotal-trial timing.

surprises.description: The preview expected ALIGN-ACS enrollment of 120 patients to be complete. The study instead enrolled 134 chest-pain patients in under four months, and its results were accepted for full presentation at TCT in October or November.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ALIGN-ACS pilot study completed enrollment of 134 chest-pain patients in under 4 months and its results were accepted for full presentation at the TCT conference in October/November 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Enrollment of 120 chest-pain patients completed ahead of schedule (June 30); analysis underway.”

surprises.description: The preview modeled a Q2 net loss of about $4.3 million. The reported loss was $5 million, worse on the headline, but management attributed about $0.9 million to one-time leadership-transition costs and said the underlying loss was about $4.1 million, below the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss was $5 million,” including “~$0.9 million of one-time leadership transition costs”; the stated underlying loss was “~$4.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss ~$4.3M, partly offset by interest income on post-raise cash”; the preview also allowed for a possible severance/restructuring charge.

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a government-supported study progressing this quickly: HEADSTART-ACS had passed 50% enrollment in under three months, alongside a smaller patch pilot.
surprises.fact_evidence: The “Indonesian government-supported HEADSTART-ACS 500-patient study surpassed 50% enrollment in under 3 months,” alongside a “~50-patient patch pilot study.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on cash and runway but did not anticipate employees and executives taking shares instead of cash for bonuses. That election reduced operating cash outflow by more than $1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Executives and employees elected to take shares instead of cash for the 2025 bonus program, reducing operating cash outflow by over $1 million.”

surprises.description: The reported facts describe product extensions beyond the core ECG and licensing discussion: two new patents cover acoustic heart-valve sensing and impedance-based fluid monitoring for congestive heart failure, and a 12-lead patch prototype is aimed at a stated $2 billion patch market.
surprises.fact_evidence: HeartBeam “recently added two new patents for acoustic sensing (heart valve monitoring) and impedance-based fluid monitoring for congestive heart failure”; its “12-lead patch prototype targets a $2 billion patch market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed patch makers among the potential licensing channels and described the existing clearance as covering non-life-threatening arrhythmias; it did not flag these additional sensing technologies or the 12-lead patch prototype.

in_line: June 30 cash of $8.8 million was close to the preview’s ~$9.0 million estimate and within its stated $8.3–9.7 million range.
The preview expected runway to be framed into 2027; the call facts say the April raise extended runway further into 2027.

surprises.description: CODX reported a $6.3 million net loss, well below the preview’s estimate of $8.6–9.0 million, and loss per share was $1.46 versus the preview’s roughly $2.00 estimate. The preview expected operating expenses of $8.4–9.0 million; actual expenses were $6.3 million, mainly reflecting lower costs after a headcount reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $6.3 million ($1.46 per share)” and “Total operating expenses fell to $6.3 million from $8.2 million year-over-year,” reflecting reduced costs “following a completed headcount reduction.”

surprises.description: The call said NGO partners are largely funding validation-study costs for the TB ERPD assessment, reducing CODX’s cash burden. The preview identified TB as a possible non-dilutive funding path but did not anticipate this specific partner support.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Certain TB validation study costs for the ERPD assessment are largely being funded by NGO partners, reducing the company's cash burden for that program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The only credible non-dilutive funding path” was described as “CoSara monetization, partnership, or grant”; the preview did not mention NGO partners funding ERPD study costs.

surprises.description: CODX reported completing a blood-based, direct-from-plasma Ebola proof-of-concept assay and fulfilling a request for 200 Bundibugyo tests. The preview did not flag either development, which extends reported activity beyond the swab-based testing it discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed its first blood-based (direct-from-plasma) Ebola proof-of-concept assay and fulfilled an Indian government-related request for 200 Bundibugyo tests.”

in_line: Revenue was $166,000, within the preview’s $150,000–$190,000 estimate and close to its roughly $170,000 consensus figure.
Quarter-end cash was $3.6 million, at the top of the preview’s estimated $2.4–$3.6 million range.

The company’s broad pursuit of equity, debt, strategic transactions, partnerships, and grants was consistent with the preview’s expectation of generic financing alternatives rather than a named, specific funding event.
The dual 510(k) and CLIA waiver submission was not new relative to the preview, which said the application had already been submitted and that the submission itself was not news.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $17.8 million, well above the preview’s $15.2–$15.6 million likely upside range. The $2.1 million of unregulated ICFA revenue from the first wastewater plant entering service was not anticipated, while regulated revenue alone reached $15.7 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 24.8% year-over-year to $17.8 million,” partly driven by “$2.1 million of unregulated ICFA revenue”; “Regulated revenue, excluding ICFA revenue, grew” 9.9% to $15.7 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue upside to $15.2–15.6M is the most likely positive surprise”; consensus revenue was “$14.99M.”

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS was $0.10, far above the $0.03 consensus and even above the preview’s bull-case range of $0.05–$0.07. The quarterly result was particularly strong given the reported D&A pressure, although year-to-date EPS remained flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income rose to $2.7 million ($0.10 per diluted share) from $1.6 million ($0.06)”; “year-to-date EPS was flat at $0.08 versus prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 GAAP EPS consensus was “$0.030”; the preview’s bull scenario projected “$0.05–0.07.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $7.9 million, exceeding the preview’s modeled $7.0–$7.2 million and growing faster than expected. The preview had modeled roughly 2–4% year-over-year growth, versus the reported 15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 15% to $7.9 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “~$7.0–7.2M” of Q2 adjusted EBITDA and “~+2–4%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: The Santa Cruz settlement’s contemplated net revenue increase is about $1.9 million, below the roughly $2.3 million increase the preview expected. The November 1 effective date remains the stated target, but final Commission approval is still pending.
surprises.fact_evidence: The settlement “contemplates net increased revenues of approximately $1.9 million effective November 1, 2026, pending final Commission approval later this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “~$2.3M annual revenue requirement increase” effective “November 1, 2026.”

surprises.description: Organic growth showed recent acceleration: the latest three-month pace was 3.2%, above the preview’s cited 2.6% year-over-year organic growth baseline. The full-quarter organic figure of 2.6%–2.7% was closer to that baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said “organic growth accelerated to 3.2% over the last three months”; organic growth excluding the acquired systems was “2.6%-2.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited organic growth of “2.6% Y/Y” and described Q1 organic growth as “1.9% annualized.”

surprises.description: Phoenix-area building permits declined only 4.7% year over year, much less than the preview’s concern that another double-digit decline—around 19%—would challenge the growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Single-family building permits in the Phoenix MSA were “declining 4.7% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said permits fell “18.8% in Q1'26” and warned that “a second consecutive double-digit permit decline” would undermine the growth thesis.

in_line: Total active service connections were 69,429, within the preview’s modeled range of approximately 69.3–69.6 thousand.
The Santa Cruz rate case still targets November 1, 2026 for the increase to take effect, consistent with the preview’s timing expectation, though final approval remains pending.
The preview expected no Santa Cruz rate relief in Q2; the stated effective date means the settlement would not yet contribute Q2 revenue.
Palo Verde’s new rates are not expected until 2028, consistent with the preview’s expectation of implementation in 2028.

surprises.description: The preview expected adjusted EBITDA of about +$50,000 and a net loss of about $300,000. Bridgeline instead reported adjusted EBITDA of -$102,000 and a net loss of $500,000, a clear shortfall on both profitability measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved to negative $102,000 from negative $330,000” and “Net loss narrowed to $500,000 from $800,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: ~+$50K” and “Net loss: ~-$0.30M.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for $700,000–$900,000 of new ARR. Bridgeline reported 19 subscription contracts, but their combined annual recurring revenue was only over $370,000, well below that range despite the strong contract count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Closed 19 subscription contracts worth $1.7 million in total contract value and over $370,000 in annual recurring revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New ARR booked: $700–900K.”

surprises.description: Bridgeline’s Core mix was 62% of total revenue in Q3, still well short of management’s stated goal to exceed 70% of overall revenue this fiscal year. Management now projects exceeding 70% next year, suggesting the goal has shifted out.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core product revenue…now represents 62% of total revenue”; management projects “core revenue exceeding 70% of total…next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Kahn said Core/HawkSearch would reach ‘over 70% of overall revenue this year.’”

surprises.description: Management gave a positive growth outlook for next year, projecting double-digit overall revenue growth as double-digit Core growth translates into a larger share of revenue. The preview flagged FY27 framing as a potential upside scenario but did not establish this outlook as its base expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management projects…double-digit core CAGR to translate into double-digit overall revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Explicit FY27 growth framing” appeared as a bull-scenario condition; the preview also listed “any FY27 framing” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Management said it had cut quarterly advertising spend from roughly $500,000 to about $350,000 and expects to maintain that level without significant cash burn. The preview highlighted financing and cash-runway concerns but did not anticipate this specific spending reduction or assurance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reduced quarterly ad spend from roughly $500,000 to about $350,000 and expects to sustain that level going forward without significant cash burn.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With $1.4M cash at Mar 31” and “the financing runway is finite and visible.”

surprises.description: HawkSearch received a new competitive endorsement not anticipated in the preview: it was ranked #1 for B2B search in Gartner’s 2026 Critical Capabilities report for a second consecutive year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HawkSearch was ranked #1 for the B2B search use case in Gartner's 2026 Critical Capabilities report for the second consecutive year.”

in_line: Total revenue of $3.9 million was close to the preview’s $3.90–$4.00 million base estimate.
Core net revenue retention of 106% was within the preview’s expected 106–109% range.
Cash of $1.5 million exceeded the preview’s $1.4 million watch threshold.

surprises.description: Applied guided Q4 revenue of $10.25 billion, above the preview’s $10.0 billion whisper line and far above published consensus of $9.3–9.4 billion. It was slightly below the preview’s $10.3–10.5 billion bull-case range, but still cleared the high whisper bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $10.25 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat $10.0B as the whisper line for the Q4 guide”; consensus was “~$9.3–9.4B.”

surprises.description: The Q4 Semiconductor Systems outlook of about $7.9 billion was well above the preview’s bull-case threshold of roughly $7.1 billion. This added substantial segment strength to the already-strong total revenue guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Semiconductor Systems expected at ~$7.9 billion (up 62% YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Semi Systems above ~$7.1B with explicit leading-edge and DRAM strength.”

surprises.description: Management raised its calendar-2026 Semiconductor Systems growth outlook above the prior “greater than 30%” level, rather than merely maintaining that outlook. The preview specifically identified another increase as a possible upside development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its Semiconductor Systems growth outlook to above the prior ‘greater than 30%’ guidance for calendar 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Raising the ‘>30%’ CY2026 equipment growth figure again” was listed as a potential bull-case signal.

surprises.description: Applied now expects to gain market share during the year. That contrasts with the preview’s warning that an in-line guide could imply relative share loss, and is a more favorable competitive outlook than the preview’s concern suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects to gain market share during the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An in-line AMAT guide reads as relative share loss.”

surprises.description: DRAM revenue, including HBM packaging, reached a record after growing 52% year over year, and management expects a very significant second-half increase as customers add clean-room capacity. The preview anticipated DRAM upside, but did not specify growth of this scale or this second-half ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DRAM revenue (including HBM packaging) grew 52% year-over-year to record levels,” with a “very significant second-half-weighted increase” expected.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case cited “leading-edge + DRAM upside.”

surprises.description: The calendar-2026 advanced-packaging growth outlook rose to more than 70%, above the preview’s expectation of more than 50% and some framings of 50–60%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advanced packaging revenue is now expected to grow more than 70% in calendar 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Advanced packaging was “Guided to grow >50% in CY2026 (some framings >50–60%).”

surprises.description: The process diagnostics and control business is expected to grow more than 50%, a specific strong growth outlook the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The process diagnostics and control business is expected to grow more than 50%.”

surprises.description: Applied Global Services reached record revenue of $1.8 billion, modestly above the preview’s roughly $1.75 billion estimate, and management now expects more than 20% calendar-2026 growth with a sustainable mid-teens long-term rate. The preview gave a quarterly estimate but did not anticipate this longer-term growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Applied Global Services grew 22% year-over-year to a record $1.8 billion and is now expected to grow more than 20% in calendar 2026, with a sustainable long-term mid-teens growth rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Applied Global Services ~$1.75B”; it provided no calendar-2026 or long-term AGS growth outlook.

surprises.description: Management expects China revenue to grow not only this year but also next year, led by 28-nanometer foundry-logic investment. The preview’s stated outlook was flat to slightly higher for the calendar year, so the next-year growth outlook extends beyond what it described.
surprises.fact_evidence: China represented 26% of semiconductor systems plus AGS revenue, and management “now expects China revenue to grow this year and next, led by 28-nanometer foundry logic investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said CFO Brice Hill guided China and global ICAPS to “flat-to-slightly-higher for the calendar year.”

surprises.description: Applied expects to double quarterly system-output capacity by 2028, alongside substantial recent hiring and manufacturing-space expansion. The preview did not anticipate this scale or timing of capacity expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to double its quarterly system output capacity from current levels by 2028,” after adding over 1,500 manufacturing and support staff in Q3 and nearly doubling manufacturing space in recent years.

in_line: Q3 revenue of $9.1 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $3.50 were around the preview’s modeled base case of $9.05–9.15 billion and $3.42–3.50, despite being above the published consensus estimates.
Q3 non-GAAP operating margin of 34% was consistent with the preview’s derived expectation of roughly 33–34%.

The preview’s central gross-margin expectation was around 50%; the reported Q4 gross-margin guide of about 50.4% stayed near that level, although it did not reach the preview’s 51%+ bull-case outcome.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be about $26.0 million, and Q2 revenue came in at $26.5 million. That was a modest beat, although the preview also described roughly flat sequential revenue as the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 65% year-over-year to $26.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $26.0M”

surprises.description: The preview expected gross margin around 38% and modeled a base range of 37.5%–38.5%, with improvement from Q1. Instead, gross margin fell to 37.0% from 37.6% in Q1, as Irwin's lower-margin mix weighed on the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 37.0% from 42.8% a year earlier, reflecting Irwin's structurally lower margins (32.8%) versus Legacy FitLife (41.7%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~38% (no formal consensus)” and “margin grinds up ~50bps”; the bear case flagged “≤37%.”

surprises.description: The preview hoped Legacy FitLife's year-over-year decline would moderate toward the low teens. Instead, revenue fell 23%, slightly worse than Q1's 22% decline, although it was roughly flat sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy FitLife revenue declined 23% year-over-year to $12.4 million, with wholesale down 31% (largely GNC) and online down 19% (largely MRC), but was roughly flat sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the decline moderates toward the low teens.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was expected at about $3.4–$3.6 million in the estimate table; the reported $3.7 million came in just above that range. It also exceeded the preview's Q1-based comparison of $3.3 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 10% to $3.7 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | ~$3.4–3.6M (no formal consensus)”

surprises.description: The preview did not identify a further sequential SG&A reduction as an expected Q2 result. Management reported a 3.8% sequential decline to $4.8 million, or roughly $0.8 million of annualized savings, and said further reductions were planned.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A fell 3.8% sequentially to $4.8 million, equivalent to roughly $0.8 million annualized savings, with further reductions planned for the rest of the year.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted Amazon algorithm changes and a slowing growth pace, but did not anticipate the reported subscriber recovery. Amazon subscribers rose from a mid-April bottom above 90,000 to approximately 94,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amazon subscriber count bottomed above 90,000 in mid-April and has since recovered to approximately 94,000.”

surprises.description: The preview expected ongoing deleveraging but did not forecast a specific interest-savings figure. Management said the debt reduction since the Irwin acquisition now saves about $0.6 million in annual interest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid down approximately $8.6 million of debt since the Irwin acquisition, cutting the term loan to $36.1 million and the revolver to $2.0 million, saving about $0.6 million in annual interest at a 6.5% weighted rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect ~$38–39M net debt” and “deleveraging ahead of schedule ($1.9M in Q4, $2.9M in Q1) is the underappreciated bull point.”

in_line: Irwin's Amazon business was near $1 million per month in June, with July comparable even without Prime Day, broadly matching the preview's base-case expectation of about $1.0 million per month.

The reported approval of three-year shelf-life formulas for 85% of Irwin products was consistent with the preview's stated reformulation plan to reduce roughly $2 million of annual inventory obsolescence.
Lost revenue from out-of-stock situations fell by over 50% sequentially, consistent with the preview's expectation that inventory recovery would provide a Q2 tailwind.

surprises.description: The preview flagged an explicit Q4 revenue figure as the key test of the recovery, but the reported facts say management only reaffirmed a record year in revenue and profitability, without giving a Q4 number. That leaves the scale of the expected Q4 rebound unquantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed guidance for a record year in both revenue and profitability.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Explicit FQ4 revenue guidance — a number, not an adjective.”

surprises.description: Cash and marketable securities were $3.1 million at quarter-end, below the preview’s cited $4.0 million minimum-liquidity covenant. The facts do not say whether the company was in compliance or had a waiver, but the balance is weaker than the preview’s base case of tight cash with the covenant met.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, equivalents and marketable securities fell to $3.1 million as of June 30, 2026”; the company extended the term loan maturity to July 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “$4.0M minimum liquidity covenant” and described its base case as “cash still tight but covenant met.”

surprises.description: Software revenue accelerated to 21% year-over-year growth, from the preview’s cited 6% year-over-year growth in Q2, and rose 12% sequentially. The preview had described software as decelerating; quarterly bookings of approximately $2.5 million also support the stronger showing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Software revenue rose 21% year-over-year and 12% sequentially to $2.7 million, with approximately $2.5 million in software bookings during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only $2.4M in FQ2 (+6% y/y) — decelerating.”

surprises.description: A California utility’s LRAD 950NXT orders reached $4.4 million this fiscal year, including a recent $2.4 million order, versus about $1 million the prior year. The preview did not anticipate this customer or the scale of its orders, which point to a growing critical-infrastructure business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A single California utility ordered $4.4 million of LRAD 950NXT critical infrastructure systems this fiscal year (including a recent $2.4 million order), up from about $1 million the prior year.”

in_line: Q3 revenue was $7.3 million, within the pre-announced $7.0–$7.5 million range and matching the preview’s $7.3 million model.
Q3 gross margin was 57.1%, within the preview’s expected 55–58% range.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $3.1 million, within the preview’s expected $3.0–$3.3 million loss range.
GAAP loss was $0.10 per share, matching the preview’s modeled range of $0.10–$0.12 per share.
The 12-month backlog was approximately $69 million, as the preview expected.

Puerto Rico collections resumed after quarter-end, with approximately $2.9 million collected over four weeks. This is consistent with the preview’s base case of partial collections, rather than its bear case of collections stalling.
Management reaffirmed a record year in revenue and profitability, consistent with the preview’s report that management had already reaffirmed that outlook.
Genasys Protect coverage of approximately 15% of the U.S. population is consistent with the preview’s cited milestone of coverage for more than 50 million U.S. residents.

surprises.description: The preview treated the plan to launch three to five companies a year as a possible operating approach; MDB said it is scaling that plan back and returning to a selective “rifle-shot” strategy because microcap market conditions are unfavorable. That is a setback to the previously promoted launch pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scaling back its previously announced plan to launch three to five new companies per year, reverting to a selective ‘rifle-shot’ approach due to unfavorable microcap market conditions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described management’s framing as “AI lets us launch 3–5 companies a year” and said the base case was “Marlett repeating” that framing; it also flagged that approach as an operational tell.

surprises.description: The preview expected a thin Q2 fee slate and described a signed self-clearing-platform partnership as a possible upside catalyst, but MDB reported active discussions with four to five parties and letters of intent, targeting a deal within the next quarter. This is meaningful progress, although no deal or named counterparty was announced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In active discussions with four to five parties regarding a partnership or sale” of Public Ventures, “received letters of intent,” and is “aiming to close a deal within the next quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “signed strategic partnership for the self-clearing platform” was the “single highest-value surprise available,” while its base case anticipated timelines being reiterated “not advanced.”

surprises.description: Paulex’s IPO timing appears later than the preview’s September target: management described the registration filing as close and the offering as expected in the fourth quarter. The update preserves an IPO catalyst but indicates a timing slip from the anticipated September window.
surprises.fact_evidence: Paulex is “close to filing its IPO registration statement” with an “expected fourth-quarter offering.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Paulex’s IPO was “targeted September 2026” and identified a September IPO date as a bull-case catalyst.

surprises.description: eXoZymes raised only about $6 million in its recent financing, well below its target. The preview identified the offering but did not flag a financing shortfall, making the amount raised a negative portfolio-company update beyond the modeled MDB fee estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “eXoZymes recently completed a financing that raised only around $6 million, well short of its target.”

surprises.description: eXoZymes is nearing a strategic contract-manufacturing partnership, an operational development the preview did not identify among its expected catalysts. It is a potentially positive development, but the facts do not say that an agreement has been completed.
surprises.fact_evidence: eXoZymes is “nearing a strategic contract manufacturing partnership.”

in_line: Management’s target of approximately $5–6 million in annual MDB operating expenses is broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of fixed operating expenses falling to about $6 million after the PatentVest spin-out and platform partnership.

surprises.description: Cash ended at $13.1 million, below the preview’s $16–18 million estimate and below its $15 million bear-case threshold. That is a larger shortfall than expected from the starting balance of $21.4 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $13.1 million in cash and no debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash (period end) … My Base Estimate: $16–18M”; the bear case flagged “cash <$15M.”

surprises.description: Net sales were $41 million, below the preview’s $43.5–45.0 million base estimate. The 19.9% year-over-year decline was also worse than the expected 12–15% decline, and sales fell sequentially rather than making the expected seasonal step up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 2027 net sales declined 19.9% year-over-year to $41 million”; Q4 FY26 sales were $42.82 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … My Base Estimate: $43.5–45.0M (–12% to –15% YoY)”; “I model a modest sequential step up off $42.82M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 27.6%, well short of the preview’s 30–31% estimate and below the 30% level it identified as important to confirm. The preview’s bear case contemplated margin below 28%, which the reported figure narrowly reached.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 27.6% from 28.1% year-over-year, mainly due to lower manufacturer rebates partially offset by lower freight costs per order.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … My Base Estimate: 30–31%”; “Gross margin ≥30%” was a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss was $3.4 million, slightly worse than the preview’s estimated loss range of $2–3 million. This indicates underlying operating performance weakened even as the reported net loss narrowed year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $3.4 million from a $2.7 million loss in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … My Base Estimate: –$2M to –$3M.”

surprises.description: The diluted loss per share was $0.28, larger than the preview’s expected loss of $0.14–$0.17 per share. Although the net loss narrowed sharply from last year, the preview had already noted that last year’s EPS included a large impairment charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed sharply to $6.1 million ($0.28 per diluted share) from $34.2 million ($1.65 per diluted share) a year ago, largely due to the absence of last year's goodwill and trade name impairment charge.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) … My Base Estimate: –$0.14 to –$0.17”; the prior-year EPS “included the $26.7M goodwill impairment.”

surprises.description: PETS acquired approximately 70,000 new customers while cutting customer acquisition cost to $60, down 15% year over year. The preview called for early funnel data but did not anticipate these specific customer and acquisition-cost results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired approximately 70,000 new customers in Q1 while reducing customer acquisition cost 15% to $60 from $71 a year earlier.”

in_line: The $37 million Delray Beach sale-leaseback was still expected to close within roughly 120 days, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it remained on track.

The $3-per-share Silver Cape proposal was still non-binding, with no determination or assured transaction; the preview had already described the live $3 proposal and board resistance as the key M&A debate.

The Rural King white-label pharmacy launch was noted in July, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it had launched shortly before the quarter ended and would contribute negligibly to Q1 revenue.
Recurring sales, including autoship and membership revenue, rose to 61.5% of total gross sales from 57.6%; the preview had flagged improving AutoShip as a potential source of green shoots.

surprises.description: Quantum-Si had been expected to launch Proteus at the end of 2026, but moved the launch to Q2 2027 after adding an instrument-design cycle. The early-access program has also not begun and is now expected in early 2027 rather than at the sites the preview expected to be live that summer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Delayed its Proteus platform launch from end of 2026 to Q2 2027,” adding “an additional integrated instrument design cycle”; the “early access program has not yet begun” and is “now expected to shift to early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management was committed to putting instruments into sites “this summer,” and described “a commercial launch at the end of 2026” as the expected timeline. It identified a slip into 1H27 as a bear case.

surprises.description: Proteus is now expected to detect 19 or 20 amino acids at launch, above the preview’s stated launch requirement of 18. The expected demonstration of all 20 amino acids during 2026 remains unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management now expects launch detection of “either 19 or 20 amino acids,” up from 18 previously planned, with “all 20 to be demonstrated in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said launch “requires 18” and that “all 20” were to be demonstrated during 2026.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $344,000, above the preview’s $302,000 consensus and $270,000 base estimate, despite falling year over year. The preview expected the revenue line to remain depressed by customers deferring purchases ahead of Proteus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell to $344,000 from $591,000 a year earlier,” reflecting weak Platinum capital purchasing ahead of Proteus.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 consensus revenue of “$0.30M” and a base estimate of “$0.27M.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a reduction in force of about 20% of headcount, with roughly $12 million in annualized operating expense savings. The preview did not anticipate a workforce reduction; the savings are positive for costs, while the size of the cuts makes the news mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reduction in force of approximately 20% of total headcount,” expected to generate “roughly $12 million in annualized operating expense savings” starting in the second half of Q4 2026.

surprises.description: After the cost cuts, management expects cash to fund operations into Q4 2028, later than the preview’s expected runway into Q2 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company had “$169.9 million in cash and investments” at June 30, providing runway “into Q4 2028 after the cost-cutting actions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 guidance was expected to reaffirm “runway into Q2 2028.”

surprises.description: The reported net loss was slightly narrower than the preview’s approximately $24 million estimate. The call also reported improved adjusted EBITDA year over year, but the preview did not provide an adjusted EBITDA estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss narrowed to $23.5 million from $28.8 million a year earlier, with adjusted EBITDA of negative $21.2 million versus negative $22.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated net loss at “~$24M.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a large potential Proteus market and disclosed broad institutional and biotech/pharma interest. These are potential applications and stated interest, not reported orders or launched evaluations, but the preview did not anticipate these specific figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimated the non-human proteomics opportunity at “more than $4 billion annually”; it had qualified “more than 250 unique institutions with stated interest in Proteus” and identified “over 150 biotech and pharma companies developing AAV gene therapies” as a potential market.

in_line: The company reiterated FY2026 guidance of approximately $1 million in revenue, adjusted operating expenses of $98 million or less, and total cash usage of $93 million or less, matching the preview’s expected guidance.
The $169.9 million cash-and-investments balance was within the preview’s expected range of approximately $167–169 million.
Management still expects to demonstrate all 20 amino acids in 2026, as the preview anticipated.
The explanation that Platinum purchasing was weak as customers waited for Proteus was consistent with the preview’s expectation that prospects were deferring purchases ahead of the platform.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted recurring mix as something to verify but gave no expected growth rate. Rekor reported recurring revenue up 14% in Q2 to $6.7 million, while total revenue grew only 2%, indicating stronger growth in recurring business than the headline revenue figure suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue grew 14% in the quarter to $6.7 million,” outpacing total revenue growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “verify: recurring mix (64% in Q1)” but did not give a Q2 recurring-revenue growth expectation.

surprises.description: The preview centered the balance-sheet risk on roughly $10 million of cash versus the December note maturity, but did not state an expectation for cash burn. Rekor reported quarterly operating cash burn of $2.4 million and first-half cash used from operations down 61%, an improvement in cash consumption not captured by the cash-balance estimate alone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cut quarterly operating cash burn to $2.4 million” and “improved first-half cash used from operations by $9.6 million (61%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “~$10M” of period-end cash and framed the print as a balance-sheet and financing event, but gave no cash-burn estimate.

surprises.description: The preview treated the operating print as largely settled and did not flag a one-time gain. Rekor said Q2 operating income was aided by a $2.8 million non-cash lease-liability remeasurement gain, so reported operating income included a material benefit unrelated to recurring operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating income was aided by a one-time, non-cash $2.8 million gain from the remeasurement of a lease liability tied to operational realignment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the P&L is essentially a non-event” and did not mention a one-time gain.

in_line: Revenue of $12.7 million was broadly in line with the preview’s operative expectation of about $12.6 million; the preview cautioned that published consensus of $13.32 million was stale.
Adjusted gross margin of 56% was in line with the preview’s expectation of about 55% and its stated 55%+ effective whisper.
The adjusted EBITDA loss of approximately $1.2 million was in line with the preview’s expected loss of about $1.3 million or less.
Cash slightly above $10 million was in line with the preview’s roughly $10 million expectation.
Management reiterated adjusted EBITDA profitability during H2 2026 without naming Q3 as the target quarter, consistent with the preview’s base case.

Several million dollars of additional savings from non-workforce efficiencies were in line with the preview’s expectation of “several million more”; the call added that execution is planned for Q3, with noticeable impact in Q4 and into 2027.
Refinancing remained pending, consistent with the preview’s base case that it would still be in progress rather than signed or committed.
GoSecure’s initial launch-partner commercial terms are targeted for Q3, broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of Q3 commercial activity and partnerships.

surprises.description: The preview pointed to FY2026 revenue of $24.55 million, up 8.3%, but management now expects full-year revenue to be slightly below 2025 if the large customer completes its planned volume reduction. That is a sharp reversal of the expected growth and H2 acceleration narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assuming the large customer completes its planned volume reduction, management expects total 2026 revenue to be slightly lower than 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue | $24.55M (+8.3%)”; the preview also said the “H2 acceleration narrative” was the key bar for the print.

surprises.description: A customer that generated about 29% of first-half revenue is evaluating a multi-vendor approach, creating substantial revenue risk the preview did not flag. The immediate situation is less severe than the customer's communicated “doomsday scenario,” however: it has signed a new purchase order and plans to migrate to Intellicheck's newest API.
surprises.fact_evidence: The customer “represent[s] approximately 29% of first-half revenue” and “has begun evaluating a multi-vendor IDV approach”; volume reduction so far has been “far less severe than the ‘doomsday scenario’ communicated,” and the customer “recently signed a new purchase order and intends to migrate to Intellicheck's newest API.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call said results so far “track ahead of the customer's warnings,” and described the warning as a “doomsday scenario.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $5.9 million exceeded both the preview's $5.67 million consensus and its $5.55–$5.60 million base case, and was stronger than the expected flattish sequential result. But the reported 7% year-over-year increase was below the preview's implied 10.7% growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $5.9 million, up 7% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” revenue was “$5.67M” with “Implied Y/Y” of “+10.7%”; the preview's base case was “$5.55–5.60M” and described the expected quarter as “flattish.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $1.1 million, above the preview's roughly $0.9–$0.95 million expectation, and the company recorded a fifth consecutive positive quarter. This was a stronger operating-profit result than the preview's already-positive baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $1.1 million, marking the fifth consecutive positive adjusted EBITDA quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA” at “~$0.9M” consensus and “$0.95M” in its base case.

surprises.description: Excluding the large concentrated customer, the rest of the business grew about 19% in the first half across all verticals—an encouraging sign of broad-based underlying growth not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the large concentrated customer, the rest of the customer base grew approximately 19% year-over-year in the first half across all verticals.”

surprises.description: Banking and lending rose to 48% of Q2 revenue from about 40% a year earlier, with three new clients signed, but it did not reach the preview's watchpoint of more than 50% of revenue. The mix was therefore slightly below the flagged threshold despite solid year-over-year progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Banking and lending grew to about 48% of Q2 revenue from roughly 40% a year earlier, with three new clients signed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's catalyst checklist called for “Banking mix >50% and new-logo count.”

surprises.description: A previously dormant large social media customer resumed activity, with more than 99% of its data now processable. The preview did not identify this development, although management is not counting any revenue from the customer in its current forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A previously dormant large social media customer has resumed activity with over 99% of data now processable, but the company includes zero revenue from them in its current forecast.”

surprises.description: Title-related mortgage loan originations rose 14% year over year, an unanticipated positive operating datapoint alongside the preview's focus on retail and auto weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Title-related mortgage loan originations rose 14% year-over-year.”

in_line: Gross margin was 91%, in line with the preview's expected range of roughly 91–92%.
Retail declined about 2% year over year, consistent with the preview's expectation that retail would remain under pressure and that a mid-single-digit decline would be manageable.

surprises.description: The preview’s house estimate was $8.3 million in revenue, and it highlighted $8.5 million as the run-rate test. TPCS reported $9.1 million, exceeding both the estimate and the nine-million-dollar threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 consolidated revenue rose 23% year-over-year to $9.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The house estimate was “$8.3M”; the preview also said “Revenue ≥ $8.5M” validates the run-rate step and noted the CEO’s goal to get into “nine-plus.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a 17.5% consolidated gross margin and $1.45 million of gross profit. Reported gross profit was about $1.4 million on $9.1 million of revenue, implying a margin of roughly 15.4%—below the margin expectation despite the revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross profit up 36% to $1.4 million” on revenue of “$9.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The house estimate listed “Gross profit” of “$1.45M” and “Gross margin” of “17.5%.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Ranor to carry the quarter at about a 35% margin. Its reported $1.6 million of gross profit on $5.5 million of revenue implies a margin of about 29%, below that expectation, even though management cited favorable project mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ranor segment revenue grew 27% to $5.5 million and generated $1.6 million in gross profit, driven by favorable project mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Ranor carries the quarter at ~35% margin.”

surprises.description: The preview made Stadco crossing into positive gross profit the key test and said gross profit above roughly $0.3 million would validate the turnaround. The call reported a 65% increase in Stadco gross profit, but also said the segment was still not profitable, so it did not establish the expected turnaround into profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stadco revenue increased 22% to $4.1 million with gross profit up 65% (a $300,000 increase), though the segment remains not yet profitable.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called “Stadco gross profit sign” “the whole ballgame,” said “a Stadco gross profit above ~$0.3M” would validate the turnaround, and described FY27 as the year Stadco should cross into positive gross margin.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted liquidity pressure and possible financing needs. Instead of merely preserving debt, TPCS cut total debt by $2 million, but cash also fell from $431,000 to $279,000, leaving liquidity tighter; the combined balance-sheet outcome was therefore mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt was cut from $7 million to $5 million,” while “Cash balance declined to $279,000” from $431,000; the call also cited “$2 million in financing activity paydowns.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Liquidity and the balance sheet,” citing “$431K cash against $6.9M of debt,” and said management wanted to invest while paying down debt; it raised the possibility of “a facility, a raise, or customer-funded equipment.”

surprises.description: The preview cited about $25 million of unfunded orders to watch. The reported amount was approximately $22 million, below that reference point, although funded backlog remained within the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Funded backlog stands at $52 million … plus approximately $22 million in unfunded purchase orders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “the ~$25M unfunded” and said to watch whether any of it converted to funded backlog.

surprises.description: The call gave a more specific account of Stadco’s turnaround actions than the preview anticipated: less than half of its business was still under legacy loss-making contracts, with price-adjustment requests and new estimate-to-complete gates in use. This offers concrete evidence of remediation, though it does not by itself establish profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Less than 50% of Stadco's business is now operating under legacy loss-making contracts,” with management using “price adjustment requests and new estimate-to-complete gating processes to improve margins.”

in_line: FY2027 guidance was reaffirmed, as the preview described reaffirmation as table stakes.
Funded backlog was $52 million, within the preview’s $50–54 million expected range around the prior $52.1 million level.
The reported net loss of about $153,000, or $0.02 per share, was better than the house net-loss estimate of $220,000 but matched the expected loss per share of $0.02.
The Navy grant total remained above $24 million, consistent with the preview’s statement that the company already had more than $24 million in fully funded grants.

surprises.description: SRTS reported Q2 revenue of $2.3 million on 11 units, far below the preview’s $4.6–5.0 million revenue range and its estimate of roughly 16–18 units. Management said eight units were held out of Q2 because a third-party bank had not completed financing approval by June 30; those units have since been approved and sold and are expected to be recognized in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue dropped approximately 68% to $2.3 million”; the company sold “11 units”; financing approval timing “prevented recognition of 8 units in Q2,” which “will be recognized in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $4.60M” and an alternate “$5.03M”; the model showed “~16–18 needed” units.

surprises.description: The reported loss was much larger than the preview’s expected per-share loss, largely because SRTS recorded a $5.7 million valuation allowance against net deferred tax assets. The preview had flagged a valuation allowance as a risk to the tax benefit supporting reported EPS, but the actual loss was substantially beyond the consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss of $8.7 million ($0.53 per share)”; the loss was “driven largely by a $5.7 million valuation allowance against net deferred tax assets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS consensus was “−$0.115” and an alternate “−$0.13”; the preview also warned, “If Sensus books a valuation allowance against its deferred tax assets, that cushion disappears and headline EPS gets structurally worse.”

surprises.description: Despite the weak Q2 unit count, management guided to more than 20 units in each of Q3 and Q4. That is a stronger near-term unit outlook than the preview’s roughly 16–18-unit Q2 model and its general expectation of sequential improvement, and the delayed eight units are expected to contribute to Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “reaffirmed expectations of sequential unit growth,” guiding to “20-plus units in each of Q3 and Q4”; the eight delayed units are expected to be recognized in Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “~16–18” Q2 units and said management had “committed publicly to sequential improvement every quarter.”

surprises.description: Management said the overall revenue mix is running roughly 50/50 between outright purchases and recurring-revenue models, and it is expanding higher-margin CensusLink subscriptions to nearly all new customers and existing installed systems. The preview described recurring revenue as building but small and highlighted attach-rate disclosure as an open question, so the stated breadth of the subscription rollout is more encouraging than that setup implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management indicated the “overall revenue mix is running roughly 50/50 between outright purchases and recurring-revenue models” and is expanding CensusLink subscriptions to “nearly all new customers and existing installed systems.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario described “recurring revenue building but small”; it flagged “Sensus Link attach rate” and said “Any quantified ARR/attach data” would be notable.

surprises.description: Management cited a proposed 26% increase in Level 1 radiation hospital reimbursement as support for SRT economics. The preview emphasized the January 2026 CPT-code increase but did not mention this additional proposed reimbursement increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A proposed 26% increase in Level 1 radiation hospital reimbursement supports SRT economics.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described dedicated CPT codes taking effect January 1, 2026, with “roughly a 300% increase in the per-fraction delivery code,” but did not mention the proposed 26% increase.

in_line: Gross margin was 34.8%, close to the preview’s roughly 35% implied expectation.
Cash and equivalents were $15.2 million, broadly in line with the preview’s estimate of about $15 million.
The former largest customer placed no Q2 orders and no second-half units are expected, as the preview said this customer was excluded from the 2026 model and any return would be upside.

surprises.description: SoundThinking cut its 2026 revenue outlook by roughly $10 million, from $109–111 million to $99–100 million. The cut was larger than the preview’s bear-case range of about $104–107 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance from $109-111 million to $99-100 million, a roughly $10 million reduction”; about 70% was attributed to timing/pushouts into 2027 and 30% to slower sales growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue (guide) | $109.0–$111.0M”; the bear case described “FY cut to ~$104–107M.”

surprises.description: The company lowered its full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 8–9%, far below the preview’s expected 16–18% range. This is a substantial reset to expected profitability, not just a weaker-than-expected quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was reduced to 8-9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adj. EBITDA margin (guide) | 16–18% — reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $23.9 million, well below the $25.76 million consensus and the preview’s $25.5–26.2 million base-case range. It also fell 7.7% year over year, rather than tracking roughly flat to slightly down as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell to $23.9 million from $25.9 million a year earlier”; it missed the company’s “$25.9 million half-year pacing target by about $2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue | $25.76M (~flat to -0.5% YoY)”; base case revenue was “$25.5–26.2M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was just $1.2 million in Q2, below the preview’s base-case expectation of $2–3 million. The sequential improvement from Q1’s roughly negative $100,000 was a positive detail, but it did not make the quarter meet the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $1.2 million from $3.4 million in Q2 2025, though it improved sequentially from roughly negative $100,000 in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “adj. EBITDA $2–3M.”

surprises.description: GAAP loss per share was $0.37, materially worse than the preview’s consensus estimates of a $0.177–$0.20 loss. The net loss also widened year over year, unlike the preview’s prior-year EPS comparison of a $0.24–$0.25 loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss widened to $4.8 million ($0.37 per diluted share) versus a $3.1 million loss ($0.24 per share) in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS (GAAP) | -$0.177”; the alternative estimate was “-$0.20.”

surprises.description: Management said ShotSpotter performance was weakening in both bookings and go-lives, and acknowledged internal sales execution problems. The preview anticipated budget pressure and ARPA funding wind-down as attrition risks, but did not flag weak bookings and sales execution as additional problems.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged “deteriorating ShotSpotter performance driven by both weak bookings and go-lives,” citing “elongating sales cycles, ARPA funding wind-down, and admitted internal sales execution underperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said guidance assumed “higher attrition than historical, tied to budget pressure and the end of ARPA funds.”

surprises.description: The Puerto Rico ShotSpotter recapture was removed entirely from 2026 guidance, rather than being a signed deal that supported the planned second-half ramp. This was one of the specific contracts the preview said the H2 plan depended on.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Puerto Rico ShotSpotter contract recapture (originally ~$1.5 million) was removed entirely from 2026 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Puerto Rico was “positively engaged” but timing uncertain, and that “Signed = FY guide is live; slipped to 2027 = guide is arithmetically broken.”

surprises.description: SoundThinking did win the Texas statewide Crime Tracer deal, worth about $2.5 million in annual recurring revenue. The preview treated signing the state deal as an unresolved H2 catalyst, so the award is a positive result against the base-case expectation that deals could remain in pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Won a fourth statewide Crime Tracer deal in Texas worth approximately $2.5 million in annual recurring revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Puerto Rico and the “~$2.5M CrimeTracer state contract” were “explicitly embedded in the H2 ramp”; its base case had H2 deals “still described as pipeline.”

surprises.description: SafePointe deployment delays reduced expected revenue by about $2 million, despite nearly 90 new lanes being booked in Q2. The preview expected a substantial SafePointe drag, but also described revenue scaling from $3.6 million toward $6.5 million or more, rather than this specific deployment-related reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SafePointe deployment delays reduced expected revenue by about $2 million despite nearly 90 new lanes booked in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said SafePointe had a “>$8M annualized drag in 2026” and that “Revenue should scale $3.6M → $6.5M+.”

surprises.description: The company recognized $900,000 of restructuring costs in Q2. The preview anticipated about $4 million of annualized workforce savings and raised the question of how much was in the run-rate, but did not flag this quarter’s restructuring charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$900,000 in restructuring costs recognized in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “$4M annualized workforce savings ($2.5M in-year)” and asked whether the savings were “fully in the Q2 run-rate.”

surprises.description: Cash fell from $14.2 million at Q1-end to $6.4 million at Q2-end, while the company still had $4 million drawn on its credit facility. The preview flagged liquidity as a concern if the quarter brought cash burn and a guidance cut, but did not anticipate this specific cash balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with only $6.4 million in cash, $4 million drawn on its credit facility.”
